title: BUG: production async runtimes built without a reactor — live DB/network I/O hangs
description: Found by the first live 23ai run (release-gre.14). The B1 async migration dropped oracledb BlockingConnection and drives the async oracledb::Connection on our own asupersync runtimes, but every runtime is built with RuntimeBuilder::current_thread().build() and NO reactor. asupersync RuntimeBuilder defaults reactor=None; without a reactor the async socket I/O is never polled, so the FIRST real round trip (connect, query, ping, OTLP export, SIEM POST) HANGS forever. oracledb 0.5.0 itself is correct: its BlockingConnection builds new_io_runtime() = current_thread().with_reactor(asupersync::runtime::reactor::create_reactor()?).build(). This is an oraclemcp bug, not oracledb. Offline tests never caught it because they use mock connections (no real sockets); the live tests last passed on the 0.3.0 BLOCKING model (pre-B1), so the async path had never connected to a real DB until now. PROVEN: adding .with_reactor(create_reactor()) to the contract test runtime made the full live contract suite pass (26/0, incl. the DBMS_OUTPUT execute_raw OUT-bind path). FIX: add a reactor to every production runtime that drives oracledb/network I/O — main.rs:506 block_on_connect (connect), oraclemcp-core/src/server.rs:145 dispatch_runtime (the per-call DB path), dispatch/mod.rs:3663/3692 (sync dispatch shims), readiness.rs:118 (DB ping), oraclemcp-core/src/audit_shipping.rs:140 (SIEM POST), oraclemcp-telemetry/src/otlp/pump.rs:229 (OTLP export) — plus the live test harnesses (live_oracle.rs/oracledb_contract.rs run_with_cx, load_soak.rs). ACCEPTANCE: full live suite (live_oracle + oracledb_contract + trust_safety live + load_soak) passes against a real 23ai; offline gate battery stays green; the cut-over (execute_raw, OUT binds) validated live. Consider a regression guard so a new reactor-less runtime cannot reintroduce the hang.
close_reason: Fixed: added .with_reactor(create_reactor()) to all 7 production I/O runtimes + live-test harnesses; rebuilt live load/soak to per-client model. Validated against real 23ai (live_oracle 24/0, contract 26/0, trust_safety 12/0, load_soak p50=905/p95=2984/p99=3410us, pools balanced). Offline battery green incl. no_block_on guard. The oracledb 0.5.0 cut-over is now validated live.

title: E5 mcp_exposed: per-profile opt-out (default exposed, =false hides); remove the global-activation flip
description: Today exposure uses a GLOBAL opt-in flip: when NO profile sets mcp_exposed all profiles are exposed, but the moment ANY profile sets it (even =false) only =true profiles are served (crates/oraclemcp-config/src/lib.rs mcp_isolation_active). So one profile flag silently redefines every other profile exposure (the real footgun), and the field doc ("hidden unless opted in", profile.rs:511) contradicts the system default (expose-all). DECISION (agreed 2026-06-23): make mcp_exposed a PURE PER-PROFILE OPT-OUT. Resolution: unset(None) => exposed; Some(false) => hidden from the agent; Some(true) => exposed. Remove mcp_isolation_active() and the global activation branch; the servable/list/switch/search/completion filter reads the per-profile resolved value directly. Flip the getter unwrap_or(false) -> unwrap_or(true) and fix the field doc to "exposed by default; set false to hide". mcp_exposed is a VISIBILITY/SCOPING convenience, NOT an access control -- the real guardrails stay max_level/protected/DB-privileges/the fail-closed classifier, and the operator/CLI always sees every profile. OPTIONAL (no new config field): emit a one-line startup log naming the exposed profiles and their ceilings (e.g. MCP exposing 2 profiles: dev [READ_ONLY], prod_admin [DDL]) for operator visibility; behavior-neutral. ACCEPTANCE (tests REQUIRED): unit tests for (a) no profile sets mcp_exposed => ALL exposed; (b) mcp_exposed=false => hidden from agent list/switch/search/completion yet still operator/CLI-visible; (c) mcp_exposed=true => exposed; (d) one profile flag does NOT change another profile exposure (no global flip); (e) base-inheritance resolves per-profile. Replace the existing E5 tests (mcp_isolation_active, mcp_exposure_defaults_closed...) with the new semantics, and update all callers (dispatch McpExposurePolicy / profile_for_mcp). VERIFY cargo test, clippy -D, fmt, honesty grep green. (oraclemcp-config is not api-locked, so removing mcp_isolation_active is fine; confirm no locked crate re-exports it.)
close_reason: Implemented per-profile opt-out (default exposed; mcp_exposed=false hides); removed mcp_isolation_active and the global flip; from_config + max_reachable_write_ceiling + field doc updated; behavior-neutral startup exposure notice added; E5 tests rewritten incl. a no-global-flip guard. Full gate battery green.

title: A1 — Lazy per-statement read-only backstop (SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY)
description:
Defense-in-depth (layer B; layer A = least-priv DB user, A2). Before each statement on the PINNED lease/primary session, if effective_level()==ReadOnly ensure SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY is in force, else lift it. NOT a connect-time one-shot: it is transaction-scoped (ends at next COMMIT/ROLLBACK) and effective_level() drops to ReadOnly SILENTLY on TTL-window expiry — re-assert at the start of every read txn (post-commit/rollback/lease-reset). Scope: pinned lease/primary session ONLY (incoherent on the stateless metadata pool — that relies on A2). Best-effort (does not stop autonomous-txn side effects). Area: oraclemcp-db/src/connection.rs (lease/txn path), dispatch.
TESTS: deterministic test injects a classifier-bypassing stub → DB refuses the write at ReadOnly EVEN AFTER a prior COMMIT/ROLLBACK cycle and after a silent elevation-window expiry; after a confirmed escalation the same write succeeds; backstop re-asserted on return to ReadOnly. Sequence with/after B1 (async exec seam).
close_reason: A1 lazy read-only backstop: new dispatch/read_only_backstop.rs ReadOnlyBackstop on the dispatcher's pinned read session. Lazy SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY (reuses oraclemcp_guard::SET_TRANSACTION_READ_ONLY) issued ONCE per read transaction (not per-statement; tested arms-lazily-once across N reads); re-asserts whenever effective_level==READ_ONLY and disarmed (covers silent TTL-window drop back to READ_ONLY); ONLY arms at READ_ONLY so a gated write at READ_WRITE+ is never blocked (tested); disarm() before every gated write (execute/execute_approved/deploy_ddl/compile_object/create_or_replace/patch_source) + reset() on profile switch; fail-closed (if SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY can't apply, the read is refused, not marked armed). Defense-in-depth UNDER the classifier+level gate (DB enforces ORA-01456). Composes with B1 async + lease dirty-discard + A9. Tests: 5 unit + 4 wiring + live ORA-01456 (in A7). Gates green.

title: A3 — Per-statement audit marker comment (model/profile/tool)
description:
Prepend /* oraclemcp llm=<model> profile=<name> tool=<tool> */ to every executed statement (SQLcl-style; greppable in V$SQL/ASH without trusting the client). CRITICAL: classify the MARKED text, not the bare SQL — the live pipeline classifies the exact text it executes (dispatch/mod.rs classify(&args.sql)); prepend then classify the marked text and confirm the SAME verdict (executed==classified, preserving the fail-closed invariant). No secrets in the marker; the A8 audit digest covers the marked text actually sent.
TESTS: live test shows marker in V$SQL; unit test asserts marked SQL yields the same classifier verdict as bare SQL; adversarial/fuzz case proves the marker can't be an injection vector (forged */ in <model>).

Injection-safe: sanitize_marker_value strips * / ; \ + control chars (cannot close the comment or start a statement); with_audit_marker re-classifies the marked text and adopts it ONLY if the verdict is byte-equal to bare SQL, else fails closed to bare SQL; defense-in-depth assert in execute_sql_inner refuses if marked verdict != gating decision. title: A6 — <untrusted-user-data> output fencing (prompt-injection defense)
description:

title: A9 — Compile-time capability narrowing (asupersync cap model)
description:
Defense-in-depth ABOVE the runtime operating-level ceiling. Narrow the Cx capability row [SPAWN,TIME,RANDOM,IO,REMOTE] at the dispatch boundary so a read-path tool STRUCTURALLY cannot spawn / do remote / use ambient randomness — only the effects it needs (TIME + DB I/O). Use SubsetOf monotone narrowing (widening is compile-time rejected; sealed markers). Stays UNDER the fail-closed classifier + level gate (primary boundary) — structural reinforcement, not a replacement. Area: oraclemcp-core dispatch / Cx plumbing.
TESTS: read tools receive a narrowed Cx (no SPAWN/REMOTE/RANDOM); a compile-fail fixture proves a read handler cannot spawn or do remote I/O.
acceptance_criteria: [R4 review reconciliation] Second compile-fail fixture: an attempt to WIDEN a narrowed Cx (re-add SPAWN/REMOTE capability) is rejected at compile time — proves SubsetOf monotonicity, the load-bearing safety property.
close_reason: A9 compile-time capability narrowing (RELEASE GATE): new oraclemcp-core/capability.rs using asupersync 0.3.4's sealed CapSet/SubsetOf/Has* system. ReadPathCaps=CapSet<SPAWN=f,TIME=t,RANDOM=f,IO=t,REMOTE=f>; narrow_to_read_path via Cx::restrict (SubsetOf bound — narrow-only); sealed PrivilegedEffect marker (impl only for HasRemote rows) makes requires_privileged_effect uncallable from a read Cx. Wired at the dispatch boundary for oracle_query + operator read tools; read-query fns made generic over the cap row. TWO trybuild compile-fail fixtures (checked-in .stderr): (1) a read handler cannot remote/spawn, (2) WIDENING a narrowed Cx is compile-rejected (SubsetOf monotonicity — the load-bearing property). HONEST scope: SPAWN=false enforced structurally (read Cx never handed a Scope; widening rejected) since 0.3.4 Scope::spawn isn't HasSpawn-gated yet; REMOTE/RANDOM gated by accessors; defense-in-depth ABOVE the classifier+level gate, never a replacement. trybuild dev-dep (MIT/Apache, deny-allowed). Gates green incl cargo deny.

title: B1 — Full async DB migration (drop BlockingConnection facade)
description:
Migrate the DB trait from oracledb's BlockingConnection facade (per-call runtime + block_on + ambient-Cx lookup) to the native async Cx-first Connection (conn.execute_query(&cx,…).await; oracledb lib.rs:1349/2469). Remove build_io_runtime()/block_on + the per-connection Mutex; keep ONE asupersync runtime. FULL migration in 0.4.0 (not split). Win = remove the mutex+block_on (cooperative cancellation, many in-flight round-trips per runtime) — NOT new parallelism (server is already OS-thread-per-connection). Upside: async unlocks oracledb's zero-copy _ref borrowed-fetch family (async-only; NOT direct-path, which already ships blocking). Outcome discipline: preserve Cancelled/Panicked distinctly — map at MCP boundary (Cancelled→TIMEOUT, Panicked→connection Dead + heavier evidence); never hold the lease across an indefinite await. Area: oraclemcp-db/src/{connection,pool,query,lease}.rs. Tradeoff accepted: adapter internals migrate twice (async-on-0.2.2 now; four-op at oracledb 0.3.0 via B2).
TESTS: all DB calls async/&Cx; unit + chaos/cancellation (all green) + live-XE; DPOR/LabRuntime ready-or-dead + cancel-correctness oracle; no block_on anywhere in the DB path (grep-verified); pool dirty-discard correct (post-0.3.0, consume connection_disposition()).
close_reason: Full async DB migration landed green (806 tests). OracleConnection trait is now async/Cx-first (async-trait ?Send for dyn-compat; DispatchFuture dropped +Send — dispatch runs on a current-thread runtime per connection thread, never spawned cross-thread, compiler-proven). RustOracleConnection drives oracledb 0.2.2 NATIVE async Connection via .await; the per-call block_on + BlockingConnection facade + Mutex<oracledb::Connection> are GONE — replaced by asupersync::sync::Mutex (async-aware, safe across await); ONE asupersync runtime, thread-local block_on per connection (preserves OS-thread-per-connection concurrency, verified against asupersync builder.rs:3276). On protected/READ_ONLY profiles -- exactly the posture the README recommends -- operator trusted setup therefore runs INSIDE an already-open read-only transaction: any DML raises ORA-01456, making table-backed / secure-application-context VPD setup impossible by construction. FIX: emit SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY AFTER trusted_session_statements, re-asserting the backstop immediately afterwards (narrow blast radius; matches what "trusted" implies). Note the per-request backstop also exists: read_only_backstop.rs:40-46 issues ROLLBACK + SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY before every READ_ONLY request on the pinned session -- plain-namespace DBMS_SESSION.SET_CONTEXT survives that, table-backed/global does not; keep that behavior, this bead is about connect-time ordering only. FAILING FIXTURE FIRST: C5 (091-c5) -- the protected=true posture assertion. ACCEPTANCE: C5 green both postures; D3 VPD fixture proves a trusted table-backed setup statement succeeds at connect on a protected profile.

title: A1d: oracle_describe returns structured not-found, handles quoted identifiers
description: Source: plan v8 sec.4-A1d + sec.A.2.5. title: A2a: stop discarding lock + preview + incident errors into one generic code
description: Source: plan v8 sec.4-A2a + sec.A.1 + sec.A.10-S10. ONE BUG = field P0-1 + P1-13: FileStore::acquire_service_owner takes a process-wide exclusive flock over the ENTIRE state store (file_store.rs:232-256, TryLockError::WouldBlock -> FileStoreError::Locked at :249); both setup --write (config_ops.rs:325-332) and the credential CLI (client_credentials.rs:319-322) call it, so neither works while a server runs -- and main.rs:4609-4616 DISCARDS the inner error into a fixed ORACLEMCP_SETUP_WRITE_FAILED ("config workflow failed before completion"), which is why --json and RUST_LOG=debug added nothing. The product knew the exact answer ("file-store service lock is already held", file_store.rs:47-48) and threw it away. FIX (one match arm first): map FileStoreError::Locked to a distinct ORACLEMCP_STATE_STORE_LOCKED whose message names the holding service and the remedy. SIBLINGS (S10, fix all with the same pattern): the same catch-all collapses five individually-actionable preview-flow variants (PreviewRequired/InvalidPreviewToken/PreviewExpired/PreviewDraftChanged/PreviewConfirmationRequired, config_ops.rs:60-73) into one generic code; and the incident trio main.rs:5313/:5375/:5408 reports config-load, disk/IO, and missing-file failures as policy "refusals" ("invalid or unsafe bundle" for a path typo). COPY THE CORRECT IN-REPO PATTERN: client_credential_error_message (main.rs:5987-5994) special-cases Locked then preserves inner error text. RIDER: fix the stale comment calling the lock "shared" at file_store.rs:261 (try_lock at :247-249 is exclusive). FAILING FIXTURE FIRST: C6 (091-c6). ACCEPTANCE: C6 green; each preview-flow variant and each incident-trio failure surfaces its own code+message. MUST-NOT-REGRESS rider (plan sec.6): config/argument error messages are field-praised best-in-class -- the error-mapping rework must keep every existing config-error golden green; add regression coverage where the new codes touch them.

CAVEAT to preserve honestly: clients.json is loaded once at open (client_credentials.rs:339) with no reload/watch, so an out-of-process revoke does NOT propagate to a running server until restart -- the online route through the RUNNING server is the correct path; say so in the output. title: A3a: flashback pre-flight capability probe before the point of no return
description: Source: plan v8 sec.4-A3a + sec.A.6.1. WHAT: probe flashback capability BEFORE the point of no return. Today no pre-flight privilege probe exists: a principal without EXECUTE ON DBMS_FLASHBACK enters the flashback path (query.rs:271-320 -- rollback, ENABLE, read, always teardown), fails at DBMS_FLASHBACK.DISABLE with PLS-00201, and the teardown-failure arm (query.rs:380-399) quarantines the connection STRUCTURALLY AND PERMANENTLY (pinned by test quarantined_thin_connection_refuses_subsequent_use). At READ_ONLY -- the recommended posture -- this is a remote DoS via oracle_query{as_of} AND oracle_diff{scn_a,scn_b} (both entry points). FIX: probe EXECUTE ON DBMS_FLASHBACK (or attempt ENABLE and classify its refusal) before any session-state change; return the EXISTING typed FLASHBACK_CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE (oraclemcp-error/src/lib.rs:88, :778-779 -- today it only classifies an error that already happened) without touching the session. DEP: D4 privilege-matrix fixture validates. ACCEPTANCE: D4 lane -- principal without the privilege gets the typed refusal, connection stays usable, repeated calls do not degrade the pool.

title: A3b: clean pre-change refusal never quarantines; failed teardown still does
description: Source: plan v8 sec.4-A3b + sec.A.6.1. WHAT: distinguish "optional feature cleanly refused before any state change" from "teardown could not prove the session clean". KEEP the quarantine for the latter -- it is correct fail-closed behavior (a session whose teardown failed may still hold a stale flashback snapshot); the defect is that a deterministic, knowable, cleanly-refused optional feature is indistinguishable from a genuine teardown fault. FIX: the pre-change refusal path (from A3a) must never set QuarantineOutcome; the post-change teardown-failure path keeps UnknownDiscarded + quarantine. ACCEPTANCE: unit tests pin both classifications; the quarantine test suite still passes unchanged for real teardown faults.

description: Source: plan v8 sec.4-A4a + sec.A.6.3. title: A4b: unify connection-lost classification on the driver set; wire retry; fix dead-lease reuse
description: Source: plan v8 sec.4-A4b + sec.A.10 S4/S5. WHAT: transient-vs-terminal classification unification + one retry. FACTS: (1) retry machinery already exists and is DEAD -- RetryPolicy/is_transient_error (resilience.rs:17) has zero call sites; WIRE it, do not build new. (2) The server keeps THREE hand-rolled, mutually-disagreeing connection-lost lists (oraclemcp-error/src/lib.rs:450-485, oraclemcp-db/src/error.rs:413-430, resilience.rs:17) while the driver already exports the correct broader set -- CONNECTION_LOST_ORA_CODES incl. 28/1012/2396/3135 (driver recovery.rs:546-547) + Error::is_connection_lost(); UNIFY on the driver's classification. (3) LIVE BUG beyond messaging: ORA-02396 + ORA-00028 + raw broken-pipe are missing from the lease discard-markers (oraclemcp-db/src/error.rs:636-651), so a DEAD LEASED session is retained and reused. (4) ORA-04068 is misclassified entirely: package-state reset -- the connection is fine, a plain re-call succeeds; today it reports CONNECTION_FAILED and points at a fresh connection (wrong remedy). FIX: unify the lists on the driver set; add the missing discard-markers; classify 04068 as retry-same-connection; retry ONCE on a fresh connection after a transport I/O error (pool) / after reconnect (pinned, rides 091-a4e). ACCEPTANCE: unit matrix over the ORA codes asserting classification + remedy text; D5 lane retry observed; B13b rides this for TTC-129.

title: A3c+A4e: audited session recycle/reconnect for the pinned path
description: Source: plan v8 sec.4-A3c + sec.4-A4e + sec.A.6.9. BUILD ONCE, USED TWICE (A3c poisoned-session recycle + A4e pinned-session reconnect). CONTEXT: the pinned session is NOT pooled -- oracle_query selects state.conn (dispatch/mod.rs:12355), a single owned connection created at startup (:1047/:1108/:1146, stored :1160); the oraclemcp-db pool feeds only stateless_conn (:500, selection :12356-12359). No per-request liveness exists on the pinned path; a torn round trip sets a ConnectionQuarantine marker (:539) that fail-closes subsequent requests -- refusal, not recovery; today the ONLY recovery is an explicit profile switch (state.conn replaced at :11802, quarantine cleared :11786), and next_steps says "acquire a fresh connection", which NO MCP client can do. The field P0-5 symptom ran on this pinned path. WHAT: an audited self-recycle/reconnect path: cheap pre-use ping after idle (or reconnect on transport I/O error), then transparently reopen -- re-apply session setup, re-arm the read-only backstop, re-resolve CURRENT_SCHEMA (the Arc-N cache), clear the quarantine through the same audited path a profile switch uses. INFRASTRUCTURE HINT: the readiness prober (readiness.rs:33-116, 5s interval, fail-closed default, drives /readyz honestly) is the verified-honest liveness pattern -- reuse its signal or shape rather than inventing a new loop. DEPS: D5 idle-kill lane and D10 (kill pinned + pooled) validate. ACCEPTANCE: D5/D10 -- kill the pinned session server-side; next oracle_query transparently reconnects (setup re-applied, backstop re-armed, schema re-resolved, audit records the recycle); poisoned-flashback session recovers the same way.

title: A5: dashboard fetch-first -- browsers must pair AND act (dashboard-wide fix)
description: Source: plan v8 sec.4-A5 (operator ruling: option c fetch-first) + sec.A.6.2 + S2 + v8 pairing pin. WHAT: make the dashboard work in a real browser -- dashboard-WIDE, not pairing-only. MECHANISM (verified against the Fetch spec): with_dashboard_security_headers stamps Referrer-Policy: no-referrer on every dashboard response (http/mod.rs:1458-1464; also meta tag :1260), which serializes the Origin header to null on NON-CORS requests (form navigations); enforce_dashboard_post_headers rejects empty/non-matching Origin BEFORE consulting sec-fetch-site (http/mod.rs:1387-1405), and dashboard_same_origin_required refuses at FOUR sites (http/mod.rs:1392/1400/1413/1421) -- so every browser form POST fails; --http-allowed-origin null cannot help; curl passed because it sends no referrer policy; the tests PIN the breakage (tests_dashboard.rs:25/467/480, :341). DECISION (recorded 2026-07-20): (1) all mutating dashboard routes require Content-Type: application/json (new primary CSRF layer) and are invoked via default-mode fetch() -- CORS-mode requests always carry the real Origin regardless of referrer policy; never form navigation, never mode same-origin/no-cors. (2) The strict Origin requirement STAYS (ambient HttpOnly-cookie auth demands it); literal Origin: null is NEVER accepted. (3) Pairing page -- v8 PIN: that ONE page switches to Referrer-Policy: same-origin so its script-free form POST carries a real Origin (a pairing.js would abandon the advertised script-free property; pairing URL is secret-free so same-origin leaks nothing). (4) Sec-Fetch-Site stays positive-only, never required. All four check sites must agree; the old tests asserting no-referrer are updated DELIBERATELY with recorded rationale. Rider P-U3: dashboard 403 becomes a structured JSON envelope like every other error. FAILING FIXTURE FIRST: C4/R3 browser flow (pair + authenticated action POST) fails on today's main. ACCEPTANCE: C4 green; R3 SSE subscription unaffected; security review bead 091-a5-secreview documents why the posture is not weakened.

Also records the deliberate test updates (which no-referrer assertions changed and why). ACCEPTANCE: doc merged; A5 links it; threat-model cross-reference updated.

title: B10: misleading-message sweep (typo!=forbidden; refusals redirect; one error grammar)
description: Source: plan v8 sec.4-B10 (the round's dominant theme -- per the tester the highest value-per-line change available). WHAT: the misleading-message sweep -- correct behavior reported through a misleading message: (1) P1-4: a typo'd table/column reports FORBIDDEN_STATEMENT "could not prove this statement safe" instead of "relation X does not exist or is not visible to this principal" -- agents conclude they are policy-blocked and try to ESCALATE (a safety anti-pattern in itself). (2) ORA-31603 surfaced as CONNECTION_FAILED. title: B12a: operator pure-function allowlist via the SideEffectOracle seam
description: WHAT: exact operator-owned routine restriction composed over an independent SideEffectOracle proof. The restriction never emits ProvenReadOnly itself: a routine is proven only when the independent oracle already proves it and an exact SCHEMA.FUNCTION declaration matches. The served DEFAULT_CLASSIFIER has UnknownOracle, so this cannot make a served user-defined function Safe. Operator configuration is the only intended caller; no MCP/client input reaches this API.
design: Mechanism: OperatorPureFunction parses only exact unquoted SCHEMA.FUNCTION identities. OperatorPureFunctionRestriction delegates every verdict to an independent SideEffectOracle, preserving ProvenReadOnly only for an exact allowlist match and otherwise changing that verdict to Unknown. Statement purity is delegated unchanged. An absent restriction preserves the independent oracle; a present empty list restricts every UDF.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Unknown, malformed, wildcard, ambiguous, quoted, bare, or database-link entries fail closed. 2. With UnknownOracle, an allowlist entry leaves SELECT app_read.lookup(:id) Guarded/READ_WRITE. 3. With an independent ProvenReadOnly oracle, an exact matching entry preserves its existing Safe/READ_ONLY result; a non-listed independently-proven routine becomes Guarded/READ_WRITE. 4. The conformance test proves the configured outcome cannot be more permissive than the default classifier for listed and non-listed calls. 5. No served DEFAULT_CLASSIFIER binding or client-controlled configuration path is added.
close_reason: Operator entries intersect independent SideEffectOracle proof only; malformed/non-matching entries narrow to Unknown, while UnknownOracle cannot promote a served UDF. Scoped conformance evidence is intentionally not-ready. [closing=b2930a8abe4926a1f4c0db269bae2a3f9699a6c4 source=3eae78153771bd96cb08ac1add7c92b4fa443340 evidence=tests/artifacts/evidence/closes/oraclemcp-091-b12a-purity-allowlist-1vagp.json]

comments.author: durakovic
comments.text: SECURITY FINDING / STOP: B12a's stated acceptance ("allowlisted pure UDF in SELECT at READ_ONLY") necessarily widens the served classifier. Committed purity.rs defines UnknownOracle routine_purity as Unknown (lines 76-85) and only ProvenReadOnly permits Safe (48-73); classifier.rs uses that verdict to make every user-defined call Guarded unless proven (3032-3037). dispatch/mod.rs DEFAULT_CLASSIFIER is the served text-local classifier and explicitly says allow/block configs are not used there (1907-1916). The current dirty OperatorPureFunctionOracle returns ProvenReadOnly for a config match, so SELECT APP.LOOKUP(...) changes from rejected/Guarded to Safe. That violates the operator's tighten-only instruction ("never widen"); no implementation should land without a revised semantics that can only add Guarded/refusal.

comments.author: durakovic
comments.text: SECURITY STOP (verified against committed HEAD 1365e0d1): tests/purity_core_conformance.rs::operator_pure_function_allowlist_only_clears_the_exact_declared_select_call explicitly asserts an operator config declaration makes SELECT app_read.lookup(:id) Safe/READ_ONLY. With no allowlist, the default UnknownOracle reports routine purity Unknown and classifier.rs requires every UDF ProvenReadOnly, so the same query is Guarded/READ_WRITE. This is a configuration-driven promotion from refused-at-READ_ONLY to permitted, violating the operator’s narrow-only condition. Do not extend or close B12a as written; it requires a redesign that intersects an independent classifier proof rather than emits ProvenReadOnly itself.

comments.author: durakovic
comments.text:
ORCHESTRATOR — security stop CONFIRMED and the widening is now REMOVED from the tree. I verified this independently rather than taking the report on trust.

What happened, in order:
  1365e0d1 feat(guard): declare exact pure-function authority — introduced OperatorPureFunctionOracle, and committed a test
    (operator_pure_function_allowlist_only_clears_the_exact_declared_select_call) that explicitly asserted an operator config
    declaration makes SELECT app_read.lookup(:id) DangerLevel::Safe at OperatingLevel::ReadOnly. Without the allowlist the
    default UnknownOracle reports routine purity Unknown and classifier.rs requires every UDF ProvenReadOnly, so the same
    query is Guarded/ReadWrite. That is a configuration-driven promotion from refused-at-READ_ONLY to permitted.
  c5f1b85c fix(guard): keep pure-function config tightening-only — removed it. 535 deletions against 2 insertions:
    OperatorPureFunctionOracle and OperatorPureFunction are gone from purity.rs and from the committed public-API surface
    (crates/oraclemcp-guard/api/oraclemcp-guard.txt), and the promoting test is deleted.

I confirmed the type is absent from the working tree and that the promoting test exists at 1365e0d1 but not at HEAD. The fix removed the promotion; it did NOT weaken the test to make a widening pass. That is the correct resolution and the right instinct.

B12a STAYS OPEN and is NOT deferred — the bead's own acceptance criteria are what encoded the violation, so the spec needs rewriting before any implementation.

WHAT A CORRECT DESIGN MUST DO, for whoever picks this up:
  - An operator allowlist may only ever INTERSECT with an independent classifier proof. It must never itself emit
    ProvenReadOnly, because that makes config an authority over the fail-closed classifier rather than a restriction on it.
  - The reachable outcomes for any statement must be a subset of what the classifier permits WITHOUT the allowlist. If a
    query is Guarded at READ_ONLY with no config, no config may make it Safe.
  - An unknown, malformed, or unparseable entry fails closed.
  - It is reachable from operator config only, never from anything a client sends.
  - The conformance test must assert the NARROWING direction: prove that no allowlist entry can promote a statement the
    classifier would refuse. The deleted test asserted precisely the opposite property.

Note DEFAULT_CLASSIFIER in dispatch/mod.rs (1907-1916) is the served text-local classifier and documents that allow/block
configs are not used there — so any redesign must also be explicit about which classifier instance it affects.

With an independent all-proven oracle, an exact listed routine remains Safe while a non-listed routine narrows to Guarded. Malformed/bare/wildcard/quoted/database-link declarations reject at parsing. comments.author: durakovic
comments.text: FINDING: Oracle purity metadata should NOT feed the SideEffectOracle, in either direction. I did not build the channel, and I am saying so rather than shipping one. THE TECHNICAL REASON: DETERMINISTIC does not assert the property B12d needs. It asserts that the same inputs yield the same OUTPUT - repeatability - and says nothing whatsoever about side effects. Oracle never verifies it; it is a developer annotation consumed by result caching and function-based indexes, and a function that performs DML can legally be declared DETERMINISTIC and will be cached happily. Consequences: (a) as a PERMIT it is forbidden outright - an unverified developer assertion, and not even an assertion about purity; (b) as a VETO (downgrading a proof when the flag is absent) it would be fail-closed but WRONG, because absence of DETERMINISTIC does not imply impurity - it would refuse correct proofs on a signal that does not measure purity, and would train operators to treat refusals as noise, which is how a fail-closed system gets disabled in practice. Metadata is a fact about what a DEVELOPER DECLARED. That is genuinely useful to a HUMAN deciding what to put in the B12a allowlist - operator review UX, where it carries no authority - and useless to the classifier. The plan's own audit (sec.1738) records the current invariant as 'Oracle purity metadata is NEVER consulted'; this keeps it that way and makes breaking it noisy. WHAT LANDED is the test the acceptance actually turns on: no advisory state may promote a verdict the independent oracle refused. Every (independent verdict x allowlist state) pair is enumerated - the dangerous direction is the one nobody writes a test for - asserting both that permitting Safe after the wrapper requires the independent oracle to have permitted it before, AND that a non-proof passes through UNCHANGED. MUTATION-CONTROLLED with the exact shape B12a nearly shipped: making the allowlist promote on its own authority (the 1365e0d1 shape that c5f1b85c deleted) fails with 'restriction promoted ProvenSideEffecting to ProvenReadOnly ... an advisory layer may narrow a proof, never manufacture one'. Note that catches promotion of a PROVEN-IMPURE routine, not merely an Unknown one. Restored: 5/5 pass. No public API added, so no api-lock baseline is touched. WHAT IS STILL AVAILABLE if the operator wants the UX half: surfacing ALL_PROCEDURES/DETERMINISTIC in doctor as a candidate-review listing, clearly labelled as a developer assertion, feeding the human who edits the B12a allowlist. That lives in oraclemcp-core doctor output, touches no guard code, and cannot influence classification by construction. I did not build it because the bead's acceptance is about the guard invariant and adding an unrequested UX surface is not the same as satisfying it.

comments.author: durakovic
comments.text: VERIFICATION + a NEW hole in the same defect class. The headline B8a fix is ALREADY IMPLEMENTED and I did not need to rebuild it: DoctorAuditPosture exists with SigningKeyConfigured / DisabledReadOnly / StartupRefused / Unavailable, doctor renders all of them (main.rs 2689-2721 region of doctor.rs), and doctor_audit_posture_from_config derives the posture from the REAL config rather than from a file path - it shares max_reachable_write_ceiling and the same '> ReadOnly' predicate with the server's build_auditor, so the ceiling half cannot drift. main_tests.rs:618 doctor_audit_posture_matches_startup_audit_policy_without_opening_a_log already covers read-only, trail-opted-out, writable (StartupRefused) and signed. So the check-mark-with-a-path lie is gone. BUT THE POSTURE STILL LIES IN ONE STATE, and it is the classic declared-but-empty footgun. Doctor computes signing_key_configured as 'config.audit.key_ref.is_some() || env var present AND NON-EMPTY'. The server computes it as std::env::var(AUDIT_KEY_ENV).ok(), which yields Some("") for an empty value, then feeds it to SigningKey::new, which rejects anything under 32 bytes. So with ORACLEMCP_AUDIT_KEY set to the empty string the two disagree. MEASURED with the real target/debug/oraclemcp binary against a scratch read-only config and an isolated HOME, not inferred from reading code: serve prints 'oraclemcp serve: ORACLEMCP_AUDIT_KEY is invalid: HMAC-SHA256 key is too short (0 bytes); at least 32 bytes are required' and REFUSES TO START, while doctor check 13 in the SAME environment prints 'audit configuration observation: disabled (no signing key configured; profile is read-only everywhere reachable)'. Control: with the variable unset the server starts normally, so the empty value is the whole difference. That is B8a's own class in the opposite direction - the original bug was a check-mark implying audit was armed when no auditor existed; this is a benign 'disabled, read-only, nothing to see' report for a server that will not start at all. An operator running doctor to find out why serve failed is told the audit posture is fine. comments.author: durakovic
comments.text: LANE WIRED and committed locally (not pushed: checkout diverged, pane 2 owns the merge). scripts/rig/oracle_l1_vpd_fixture.sql + scripts/rig/verify_vpd_fixture.sh, loaded and run against free23. THE TRAP WAS ALREADY IN THE REPO: D4's oracle_l1_privilege_matrix.sql policy function returns the literal predicate '1=1' - attached, withholding nothing - so any assertion written against it is satisfied by a gate that does not work. D3 therefore ships its own genuinely restricting policy (classification = 'PUBLIC' over 4 rows, 2 of them RESTRICTED) and asserts the withheld rows are ABSENT, never that the query succeeded or that a policy exists. MUTATION-CONTROLLED against exactly the fail-open shape: --mutation-control swaps the predicate to '1=1', requires the assertions to FAIL, restores, requires them to pass. Measured: the fail-open yields 3 findings (blind principal reads 1,2,3,4; the synonym path leaks; COUNT=4 MAX=4), the real predicate yields 0. SIDE CHANNEL REPRODUCED (D3's failing half): the blind principal cannot SELECT ids 3 and 4, yet inserting primary key 3 raises ORA-00001 while inserting 99 (genuinely absent) succeeds - hidden keys are enumerable by probing, and the control means 'insert failed' cannot pass for an unrelated reason. On 23ai it is disclosure rather than inference: ORA-03301 prints 'row with column values (ID:3) already exists', naming the value of a row the caller is forbidden to read. Aggregates do NOT leak (COUNT and MAX are computed over the filtered set). THREE MEASUREMENT CORRECTIONS, each of which would have produced a lane that proved nothing. (1) Ground truth cannot come from SYSTEM or from the TABLE OWNER - both are subject to the policy; the owner sees 1,2 like everyone else, so a lane using the owner as truth compares 2 against 2 and cannot see a fail-open. Only SYS inside the PDB sees all four. (2) Blindness is not about roles: my first fixture withheld SELECT_CATALOG_ROLE and the 'blind' principal STILL reported a policy row, because ALL_POLICIES lists policies for every object ACCESSIBLE to the caller. Genuine blindness needs access via a VIEW whose owner holds the base privileges - which is also the field's silent-empty shape (filtered rows, 0 policies, 0 base tables, nothing to explain the short answer). (3) sqlplus 23ai decorates bare numeric columns with box-drawing characters, so matching ^[0-9]+$ silently produced the empty string and two assertions reported a 'leak' with empty values - a measurement bug wearing the costume of a finding; all values are now fetched as marked strings. A1e half is reachable: the sighted principal names ORACLEMCP_D3_VPD via ALL_POLICIES. NOT DONE: the server-side half of the acceptance (pre-fix main silently returning empty through the MCP tool path, and doctor naming the policy) is not yet driven through oraclemcp itself - this lane establishes the database-side ground truth those assertions need.

comments.author: durakovic
comments.text: Lane WIRED and committed locally (crates/oraclemcp-db/tests/live_idle_kill.rs, 317 lines, live-xe gated); NOT pushed because the shared checkout is diverged and pane 3 owns the merge. Both surfaces asserted separately. Anti-vacuity: the pool is pinned to max_size=1/min_idle=1 so the next checkout MUST be the killed connection - with default sizing the next checkout could return a different live connection and the test would pass while validate-on-checkout did nothing. The lane can fail on purpose: ORACLEMCP_D5_SKIP_KILL=1 runs everything except the kill and BOTH halves then fail (pooled: same sid/serial comes back, assert_ne fires; pinned: COMMIT succeeds, generation 1 to 1, panic fires). BEAD STAYS OPEN because the acceptance names a pre-fix failing half to record and IT DID NOT REPRODUCE on XE21. Measured: pooled victim 313/7915 replaced by 313/42101 with no error visible to the caller; pinned COMMIT refused with Quarantined outcome=CommitInDoubt message 'commit failed; lease discarded: Oracle connection lost: commit: I/O error: unexpected end of file'. Both are deliberate, not luck: OraclePool::with_conn already carries RetryPolicy::one_immediate_retry with ReconnectThenRetry plus discard when is_uncertain_session_state, and the same quarantine guards savepoint/preview_dml/enable_dbms_output/apply_session_statement on the lease. TWO CONSEQUENCES FOR THE FIX BEADS: (1) A4a is not 'add missing pooled recovery' - recovery exists as reconnect-THEN-REPLAY, which runs only after the caller's statement already failed once and is safe only for a replayable statement; A4a moves the check earlier. (2) A4e must not regress what already holds: the pinned path today refuses and discards rather than rebinding, and this lane now fails the moment a transparent reopen stops refusing a caller that was mid-transaction. The field's P0-5 pinned symptom therefore needs a trigger this lane does not yet reproduce (long idle before use, or a non-commit operation) - worth pinning down before A4e is designed.

comments.author: durakovic
comments.text: CORRECTION to my earlier comment on this bead - the pinned half of the lane tested the WRONG SURFACE, and my findings about it should not be relied on. I asserted against LeaseManager, which plan section B14 documents as having ZERO production callers and no tool registration ('constructed only in tests; LeaseAcquirer impls are test-only; oracle_session has no dispatch or registry entry'). Pane b5736dce has since removed that subsystem as planned B14 work, taking my pinned test with it - correctly. So the Quarantined/CommitInDoubt result I recorded was real behaviour of code no caller reaches, which is precisely the vacuity this swarm has been removing all day; I built one. What survives from that comment: the POOLED half and its finding stand (OraclePool::with_conn recovers via RetryPolicy::one_immediate_retry + ReconnectThenRetry + discard on is_uncertain_session_state, i.e. reconnect-THEN-REPLAY rather than validate-on-checkout, so A4a moves the check earlier rather than adding missing recovery), as does the anti-vacuity design (max_size=1/min_idle=1 so the next checkout must be the killed connection) and the ORACLEMCP_D5_SKIP_KILL control that makes the lane fail on purpose. THE REAL PINNED SURFACE, for whoever rebuilds this half: dispatch/mod.rs ProfileConnectionBundle.session - the per-profile long-lived Box<dyn OracleConnection> held in DispatcherState alongside an optional 'stateless' sibling, replaced only through PreparedProfileSwitch. That matches section A.6.9's description exactly ('a single long-lived connection with no liveness path, whose only recovery today is an explicit profile switch') and it is the path the field's P0-5 symptom ran on. The rebuilt test must kill THAT session and assert the caller is refused rather than silently rebound; it is a heavier test than the lease one because DispatcherState needs full profile/guard setup, which is likely why the lane reached for the lease shortcut in the first place. D5 remains open.

comments.author: durakovic
comments.text: LANE WIRED + FAILING HALF RECORDED (committed locally; not pushed, pane 2 owns the merge). scripts/rig/verify_logoff_lane.sh, run against free23, requires the D9 overlay's ORACLEMCP_D9_AFTER_LOGOFF trigger. THREE MODES MEASURED, each attributed to the SERVER's own session: clean stdin EOF -> session live, +1 row (the database observed a LOGICAL CLOSE); SIGKILL -> session live, 0 rows (an abrupt end must look like this, and this is the control that gives the clean half meaning); SIGTERM -> session live, 0 rows = THE RECORDED LEAK. THE FINDING: the server closes logically on stdin EOF but NOT on SIGTERM, and systemd stops the installed service with SIGTERM, so every ordinary service stop leaves its session for PMON to reclaim instead of releasing it. That is exactly the pre-B7c failing half this bead predicts, now reproducible in one command. THE ANTI-VACUITY GUARD IS WHY THIS IS TRUSTWORTHY, and I needed it: 'no logoff row' is also what you observe when THERE WAS NEVER A SESSION. This server connects LAZILY and holds no Oracle session while idle - measured, v$session empty for its user while the process ran. My first attempt started and stopped the server without issuing any query and 'proved' a leak that way; that conclusion was WRONG and I withdrew it. The lane now drives a real oracle_query, reads back the server's own SID from sys_context, and REQUIRES that session to be visible in v$session before it is allowed to conclude anything from a missing row. TWO TRAPS ENCODED so they are not rediscovered: (1) SIDs are not identity - Oracle reuses them and this log already holds 39 rows for one SID, so rows are attributed by module, not sid; (2) the credential env var must NOT be named ORACLEMCP_* because the config loader claims that entire namespace for overrides and rejects ORACLEMCP_D7_PW as 'unknown field d7_pw' before the server starts. The lane exits non-zero on the recorded leak by design and goes green when B7 lands. NOT COVERED: the pooled-connection half of the acceptance ('pinned + pooled') - this drives the single-session profile only; and the installed-systemd-service path is inferred from SIGTERM rather than driven through systemctl.

comments.author: durakovic
comments.text: Landed at 8300f6be, pushed. 456-line scripts/rig/rig_doctor.sh, wired into the CI lint job, shellcheck clean, secret_scan + sensitive_data_lint pass, R0 can wire it as 'rig.sh doctor'. 16 checks pass on a healthy machine; it collects ALL findings rather than exiting on the first, because one-refusal-per-run turns a five-minute fix into five round trips. MISSING vs PRESENT-BUT-WRONG are reported as different kinds: absent-from-PATH is MISSING, while docker-present-but-daemon-unreachable, docker-client-older-than-20.10 and busybox-timeout-without--k are WRONG - the rig's own 'command -v docker' passes in all three of those and then fails later and far more confusingly. The daemon check picks its fix hint from the actual error text (group membership vs start the service). A PASS MUST MEAN THE RIG WILL RUN, enforced mechanically rather than promised: --selftest EXTRACTS oracle_l1.sh's real prerequisites (its 'command -v' tools and its lane table) and fails if any lacks a check here, so adding a requirement to the rig without a doctor check breaks CI. PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL, not assumed: a rig mutated to require jq gives 'requires jq but rig_doctor has no check for it - a passing doctor would not mean the rig runs'; a rig with an extra xe11 lane gives 'defines lane xe11 which rig_doctor never preflights'; the real rig passes. Each individual check is also aimed at an environment it must reject, plus an accept case so a doctor that refused everything would fail too. FINDING against the rig (oracle_l1.sh:229): '[ -n $FIXTURE_PASSWORD ] || e2e_finish_fail' is VACUOUS and can never fire - the value comes from ${ORACLEMCP_RIG_L1_FIXTURE_PASSWORD:-${PYO_TEST_MAIN_PASSWORD:-testpw}} and ':-' treats empty exactly like unset, so it is always at least 'testpw'. Found only because I insisted my own equivalent check must be able to fail; it could not, for the same reason. The doctor now refuses declared-but-empty instead, which is the real footgun: export the variable empty meaning to clear it and the rig bootstraps a fixture user with a password you did not choose.

comments.author: durakovic
comments.text: LANDED (committed locally; not pushed, pane 2 gating). I checked whether this could RUN before building it, and verified the audit against the live repo rather than trusting it: the GitHub API reports ZERO Actions variables, and the six secrets present are all OCI (no ORACLEMCP_TEST_ATTESTATION_KEY). So vars.ENABLE_TEST_ATTESTATION is never 'true', the signer has taken its operator-not-enabled branch every run since it landed, and it has never produced an attestation. WHICH OPTION I CHOSE: I could NOT wire it to genuinely sign - that needs a real key and a repo secret, which is the operator's to create and not something to invent - so I made the disabled state LOUD and closed the gap that actually mattered: NOTHING CONSUMED ATTESTATIONS AT ALL. verify_test_attestation existed only inside Rust unit tests; no CI job ever read an emitted artifact back, so nothing could tell a real attestation from an absent one. THE CONSUMER RUNS TODAY WITH NO SECRET, which is the whole point: the signature envelope records payload_sha256, and that digest BINDS the payload, so a tampered attestation is rejected even where the HMAC cannot be recomputed. Checking the HMAC itself still needs the key, and the script says so rather than implying it verified more than it did. INVARIANT: a lane must emit EITHER a well-formed signed attestation OR a typed SKIP naming a known reason - never silence, never a claim it cannot back. Rejections: E_NO_EVIDENCE, E_MALFORMED, E_UNSIGNED_LOOKALIKE (the acceptance names that case by that word), E_PAYLOAD_DIGEST_MISMATCH, E_CLAIMED_NOT_EMITTED, E_UNKNOWN_SKIP_REASON (so a silent behaviour change in the signer is noticed by something). PROVEN THE WAY rust-oracledb-2rz3 WAS, against the REAL committed artifact rather than a toy fixture: crates/oraclemcp-verifier/tests/fixtures/test-attestation-v1.golden.jsonl passes (exit 0); editing ONE field of its payload from 'kill=96.9%' to 'kill=99.9%' drives it red with E_PAYLOAD_DIGEST_MISMATCH naming both digests; restoring the file drives it green again. The selftest additionally accepts a typed SKIP and rejects the other five shapes, and CI runs the selftest immediately before the real check so a neutered consumer cannot pass quietly. THE INERT STATE IS SAID OUT LOUD: when every lane skipped and nothing signed, the check prints that the machinery is present but inert, names the missing variable and secret, and states 'Do not cite these runs as attested'. --require-signed turns that into a hard failure and is READY FOR THE DAY THE KEY EXISTS; it is deliberately not set now, because a repo with no signing key would fail every build. OPERATOR DECISION AVAILABLE: create ENABLE_TEST_ATTESTATION=true and the ORACLEMCP_TEST_ATTESTATION_KEY/_KEY_ID secrets, then flip --require-signed on, and the lane goes from honest-but-inert to genuinely enforcing. NOT DONE: emitting attestations from the e2e suite specifically (the bead's 'e2e runs upload attestation artifacts') - the signer is inert, so adding another inert call site would have added machinery without evidence; the consumer is wired to the coverage lane that already emits status, and extends to e2e the moment signing is enabled.

comments.author: durakovic
comments.text: CAN-IT-FAIL VERIFIED, and a real hole closed (committed locally; not pushed). The seal is advisory and background, so before trusting it I measured whether it can still fail in the configuration CI ACTUALLY USES - ALLOW_STALE_MUTATION_SEAL=1, set on per-push CI and the release path. IT CAN, and the existing chain is sound: malformed ENFORCING marker + flag -> exit 1 (E_SEAL_SOURCE_MISMATCH); missing report + flag -> exit 1; genuinely stale marker + flag -> exit 0 with a loud warning, which is the intended deferral. And a deferred floor leg emits 'STATUS mutation-floor=deferred', which coverage_ratchet.sh refuses to guess about (it dies if the token is absent) and maps to SKIP rather than PASS, with its own self-test. So a stale seal does not silently become a green check - it becomes a visible SKIP. THE HOLE WAS IN WHAT NOTHING PINNED: the gate's self-test exercised the flag UNSET, so nothing asserted that the flag means 'defer STALENESS' rather than 'skip the check'. Had it ever widened into a global kill switch, the seal would report green while validating nothing and no test would notice. Three cases now pin its scope, and they are PROVEN LOAD-BEARING: rewriting cmd_check_report to return 0 whenever the flag is set fails the extended self-test with 'the flag is a kill switch, not a staleness deferral', while the UNMODIFIED self-test exits 0 against that same mutant. One fixture correction recorded in the commit: my stale-marker case first carried a bogus scope hash, and the integrity check fires BEFORE the staleness branch, so it failed for the wrong reason rather than exercising the deferral. NOTE FOR THE PRE-PUSH GATE this bead defers to the next train: the self-test cannot pass in a DIRTY working tree, because scope_state reads the working tree while the marker's source is HEAD. In CI's clean checkout it passes; in this shared checkout with concurrent panes it fails for reasons unrelated to the seal - verified by running the unmodified gate at HEAD in a clean worktree (exit 0) versus the shared checkout (exit 1). Re-adding a seal-freshness check to the local pre-push gate will need that addressed or it will be spuriously red for every agent. NOT DONE and NOT ATTEMPTED: producing the fresh five-surface seal itself. That needs an RC-era SHA and a day-scale background campaign, and this bead must never block a push or the tag. No ALLOW_STALE_MUTATION_SEAL flags were removed - that stays the NEXT train's decision, per the bead text.

title: file_store OS-lock flake REPRODUCED: x1hr.5 closed it on a negative repro
description:
[MEDIUM] x1hr.5 ('Confirm/fix the file_store OS-lock flake left as an oral caveat') was CLOSED on a durable NEGATIVE repro — could not reproduce. It is still live: I hit it once while adding the em39 tests. Recording the POSITIVE repro so the caveat stops being oral.

OBSERVED (once, 2026-07-16, during cargo test -p oraclemcp-core --lib file_store):
  service_lock_initialization_failure_releases_os_lock FAILED
  panicked: 'partial initialization must not leave a permanent lock: Locked'
i.e. after acquire_service_owner_with_metadata failed its injected metadata write and dropped the descriptor, the very next acquire_service_owner returned Locked — the flock had NOT been released.

CHARACTER (measured, not guessed):
- Intermittent: 1 failure, then 18/18 green across 6 consecutive full-suite runs.
- Passes 5/5 in ISOLATION (--exact), so it is a parallel-execution interaction, not test logic.
- The failing test is PRE-EXISTING and untouched by siry/em39. My em39 tests likely only raised concurrent lock pressure enough to surface it — triggering a latent bug, not causing one.

HYPOTHESIS (explicitly a hypothesis, NOT a verified claim — do not close on it without evidence): flock ownership belongs to the open file description, and a fork DUPLICATES it. file_store tests spawn subprocesses (service_lock_subprocess_holder, service_lock_recovers_after_holder_process_is_killed) via Command. Between fork and exec the child transiently holds copies of every parent fd; O_CLOEXEC only closes them AT exec. So while test A drops its lock fd expecting release, a concurrently-forking test B can hold a transient dup of that OFD, keeping the flock alive for the fork->exec window and making A's re-acquire spuriously return Locked. That predicts exactly what was seen: intermittent, parallel-only, isolation-clean.

PRODUCTION IMPACT (probably benign, worth confirming): the server spawns helpers (token_exec, plugins via command-group). A helper's fork->exec window could briefly extend a lock's lifetime, so a competing process could see a spurious Locked and refuse to start. That is the FAIL-CLOSED direction (refuse, not double-own), so it is a nuisance rather than a safety hole — but it should be confirmed, not assumed.

NEXT: reproduce under load (loop the suite with high --test-threads, or stress acquire/release against a concurrent Command::spawn), confirm or refute the fork/OFD hypothesis, then fix (e.g. spawn helpers with the lock fd explicitly closed, or retry-with-timeout on the acquire path) and add the stress test x1hr.5's acceptance asked for. If the hypothesis is refuted, record THAT negative result with the reproduction attempt attached — do not re-close on silence.

DO NOT WEAKEN: single-writer exclusion must stay exact. A retry/timeout must never let two processes own the root, and Locked must remain a real refusal, not a warning.
close_reason: Reproduced the parallel-only flock race deterministically with a duplicated open file description: before the fix, a failed metadata initialization left the duplicate holding the flock and the next acquire returned Locked. Explicitly unlock the acquired descriptor on every post-lock initialization failure; the duplicate-FD regression now passes, as do all 19 FileStore tests and the full workspace gate.

title: [P1][live] 21c (xe21) live matrix FAILS on Oracle PGA-memory errors — diagnose infra-vs-code, fix or type it
description: 5c7i ran the real tri-state matrix: xe18 PASS, xe21 FAIL (documented Oracle PGA-memory errors), free23 PASS — so the release gate is NON-GREEN and all-versions-green is unmet. Determine whether the xe21 PGA failure is (a) the gvenzl oracle-xe:21-slim container being PGA/SGA-starved (infra: bump PGA_AGGREGATE_TARGET / container memory) or (b) a real driver/server memory-handling defect. If infra: fix the container/matrix config so xe21 goes green. If it cannot be made green, surface it as a TYPED, documented version-aware limitation per the evidence contract (never a silent skip). Blocks the coordinated publish (Rule 7 honest-green).
notes: POST-CLOSE ADDENDUM (PurpleRidge, same session) — a symptom that LOOKED like it contradicted the close, investigated, and it CONFIRMS it. While doing 6c0e I hit 'ORA-04036: PGA memory used by the instance exceeds PGA_AGGREGATE_LIMIT' on xe21 AGAIN, ~15 min after closing this green. Checked rather than assumed: xe21 total PGA allocated = 3 MB of a 2048 MB pga_aggregate_limit (0.15%), PGA inuse = 2 MB, 79 sessions; xe18 is 3 MB/66 sessions. The instance is nowhere near its PGA ceiling, so ORA-04036 here is NOT the instance exceeding PGA — it is Oracle failing to obtain memory from a host under pressure and reporting it in PGA terms. Host at that moment: free -g => free=7, shared=60, buff/cache=212 (available 156) while other panes were building. CONSEQUENCE, recorded honestly: the tri-lane matrix IS green (verified 20260716T131032Z-3169754) and xe21 has no database defect, but the lane is FRAGILE UNDER HOST MEMORY PRESSURE — it passes when the swarm is calm and can throw spurious ORA-04036/ORA-04030 whenever concurrent builds spike memory. That is the SAME root cause as gctl, not a second bug, and it is precisely why gctl's bounded-build-concurrency policy (docs/multi-agent-build-policy.md, commit 07f7c98) is load-bearing rather than housekeeping: all-versions-green holds only while build concurrency stays bounded. If xe21 goes red again in CI or a swarm run, check host memory FIRST (free -g, du on the build target) before touching Oracle — do not tune PGA; at 3MB/2048MB there is nothing to tune. Staying closed: no code/config defect exists to fix.
close_reason: PHANTOM — xe21 was collateral damage from oraclemcp-gctl (tmpfs build storm starving host RAM), NOT (a) container PGA-starvation and NOT (b) a driver/server memory defect. The FULL tri-state matrix is now GREEN: 'lanes: xe18=pass xe21=pass free23=pass', exit 0, artifacts target/e2e/oracle_version_matrix/20260716T131032Z-3169754 — same harness 5c7i ran, same per-lane users as the original failing run (xe18=TESTUSER, xe21=TESTUSER, free23=SYSTEM, read from the failing run's ladder_evidence owner fields), so this is a faithful replication and not an easier config. DIAGNOSIS: the recorded failure was 'ORA-00604 recursive SQL level 1 / ORA-04030: out of process memory when trying to allocate 568 BYTES (dga heap,ksfd dga fob consolidated)'. That is ORA-04030 (the OS refused an allocation to the Oracle server process), NOT ORA-04036 (PGA limit exceeded) as this bead's title implies — the title points a reader at PGA tuning, but a server process that cannot obtain 568 bytes is a host out of RAM. RULED OUT (a): xe18 (PASS) and xe21 (FAIL) are configured IDENTICALLY — pga_aggregate_limit=2147483648, pga_aggregate_target=536870912, shm=67108864, no docker memory limit on either; xe21 sits at 54MB of its 2GB PGA limit. No config difference could produce a PASS/FAIL split. RULED OUT (b): the failure is inside Oracle's OWN recursive SQL during EXPLAIN PLAN; the thin driver cannot make an Oracle server process fail a 568-byte malloc. PROVED (c): the failing matrix ran 12:01-12:03Z; /tmp measured 99G/124G with 11G free RAM (130G locked in tmpfs) at ~12:05Z, and plain sqlplus INSIDE the container (no driver in path) spontaneously hit ORA-04036 in the same window. With RAM freed (153G available) the lane passes — verified standalone twice (as system, then as TESTUSER) and now in the full 3-lane run. NO CODE OR CONFIG CHANGE MADE: nothing was broken, so nothing was fixed; PGA tuning would have been a change with no defect behind it. NOTE the typed-limitation clause in the acceptance did not apply — it can be made green, so no version-aware refusal was warranted. all-versions-green for the 5c7i gvenzl scope (18c/21c/23ai) is now MET; the separate OCI/ADB lane (oci-live-adb-harness-y1x7) remains its own gate. title: Pinned driver cannot emit required OCI ADB service SNI
description: Live OCI Always Free acceptance proves this is driver-owned, not a harness or wallet-decryption issue. With the wallet HIGH full DESCRIPTION descriptor corrected to contain TRANSPORT_CONNECT_TIMEOUT=60 and profile-level connect_timeout_seconds removed, the pinned oracledb 0.8.3 fails before network I/O: use_sni=true cannot be honored because the Oracle service-form SNI S{len}.{service}.V3.{numeric} is rejected as a rustls DNS name. The no-SNI real-ADB path times out/resets at the OCI front end, so a harness cannot safely bypass it. Owner: sibling rust-oracledb, src/tls.rs decide_sni / TLS connector. Wallet crypto is independently verified clean: ewallet.pem PBES2/PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256/AES-256-CBC; ewallet.p12 pbeWithSHA1And3DES; cwallet.sso. Need a safe way to transmit Oracle service-form SNI or otherwise support OCI ADB without TLS downgrade. Evidence: target/e2e/oci_adb_terraform/20260716T211356Z-2293200 (runtime-only).

title: Driver: driver-cx primary and maintained; coherent release with oraclemcp 0.12.0
description:
WHY: oraclemcp's only wire driver, oraclemcp-driver-cx (pinned =0.9.2; workspace dep in Cargo.toml),
    is discontinued upstream (crates.io 0.9.3 README, 2026-08-06: "won't get further development —
    use Oracle's official driver"). A governed DB server on a frozen driver accumulates unpatchable
    TLS/protocol debt (rustls/aes/pbkdf2 advisories will surface in cargo deny) and cannot follow
    Oracle 26ai. Oracle's official `oracledb` crate (github.com/oracle/rust-oracledb, 26.0.0-beta.2,
    2026-08-20) is pure Rust, SYNCHRONOUS (blocking I/O), has NO tokio dependency (normal deps: aes,
    cbc, pbkdf2, pkcs8, rustls, webpki-roots, chrono, rand, sha2, uuid, whoami, base16ct, base64ct;
    optional arrow-array/arrow-schema), rust_version 1.89 (stable), license UPL-1.0 OR Apache-2.0.
    It therefore does NOT collide with the engine-free/no-Tokio boundary lint, and it removes reason 1
    of the nightly pin (asupersync's nightly-outcome-try feature reaches us only through driver-cx's
    dependency declaration; see docs/toolchain.md).

    WHAT: the existing epic oraclemcp-driver-cx-oracle-dual-backend-nhteq (.3 qualify API/runtime,
    .4 implement backend, .5 explicit selection + packaging, .6 dual proof + default decision) stays
    the implementation spine. This sub-epic adds what it lacked: immediate honest disclosure, a

    the sync-in-async design proven before it is built, a capability lattice with a Kani proof, the
    license/lint plumbing, a frozen-driver advisory posture, and the stable-Rust spike.

    admits the unproven; asupersync stays (ALIEN doctrine #1); one adapter file per backend enforced by
    scripts/oraclemcp_driver_seam_lint.sh. Kill-switch rule: whichever backend becomes default, the
    other stays selectable (backend = "…") for at least one minor line.

    loom → B1.4 lattice + Kani (after B3.2, shared registry.rs) → nhteq.4 → B1.5 deny/lints → nhteq.5

title: B1.2 Backend-conformance suite → signed backend-qualification/v1 evidence (ADR-0013); concretizes nhteq.3
description:
CONTEXT: nhteq.3 asks for a SUPPORTED/UNSUPPORTED/BLOCKED verdict per OracleConnection requirement
    "with exact evidence". Today the driver contract lives in crates/oraclemcp-db/tests/oracledb_contract.rs
    (~71 KB) and is bound to one adapter (crates/oraclemcp-db/src/connection.rs, the single driver-seam
    file; `pub trait OracleConnection` at ~line 940, ~285 fns in the file). Nothing produces a document
    a reader can verify.

    DO:
    1. Refactor the contract into a backend-agnostic harness: `trait BackendUnderTest` (connect with a
       profile, run the shared scenario table) implemented once per adapter; scenarios enumerate every
       OracleConnection requirement: connect/identity; binds/types (NUMBER-as-string, TSTZ, VECTOR,
       JSON, LOB caps, nested cursors); execute with rollback default; commit/rollback; call timeout,
       cancel and break semantics; uncertain-session quarantine; streaming/OwnedRowStream; wallets
       (pem/sso/p12), TCPS/SNI, trust-union; IAM access token; proxy auth; DRCP; CQN registration;
       Arrow IPC; session identity fields; DBMS_OUTPUT; login/logoff hooks.
    2. Each scenario emits a typed verdict {SUPPORTED, UNSUPPORTED(reason), BLOCKED(reason)} + evidence
       (test name, lane, Oracle version, driver crate+version, duration). Unknown = BLOCKED, never
       SUPPORTED by default.
    3. Write `backend-qualification/v1` (JSON; schema in a new docs/adr/0013-backend-qualification-schema.md:
       schema_version, backend {crate, version}, server sha, toolchain, lanes[], rows[], summary,
       generated_at) under tests/artifacts/backend_qualification/<backend>-<sha>.json. Sign it through
       the existing .github/actions/test-attestation action when ENABLE_TEST_ATTESTATION is provisioned;
       otherwise label it unsigned (the ADR-0012 SKIP/BLOCKED status contract) — never emit an unsigned

title: B1.3 Sync-in-async design spike: blocking Oracle driver inside asupersync lanes, cancellation/timeout/quarantine proven, loom model
description:
CONTEXT: the official Oracle driver is BLOCKING (no async API, no tokio). oraclemcp dispatches on
    per-principal lanes (crates/oraclemcp-core/src/lane.rs): each lane owns an OS thread + a
    current-thread asupersync runtime + a reactor + one Oracle connection. `OracleConnection` is an
    async trait over `Cx` (crates/oraclemcp-db/src/connection.rs ~line 940). Cancellation today is
    cooperative through Cx; a blocking read(2) inside a lane cannot observe it.

    DECIDE (write the design section for nhteq.4; no production code):
    (i) blocking calls on the lane thread; cancellation = the driver's own call timeout / break()
        primitive (whatever the official driver exposes), `call_timeout_seconds` mapped 1:1; or
    (ii) a bounded driver-island thread per lane; the lane awaits a Cx-observed join with an absolute
        deadline; uncertain results → session quarantine (`unknown_discarded` / `commit_in_doubt`).
    For each option prove with the existing shapes: crates/oraclemcp-db/tests/cancel_correctness.rs
    (cancel at every DB boundary), `commit_in_doubt` path, `call_timeout_seconds` as the total request
    budget (README: profile ceiling + per-tool tighten-only), lane capacity accounting (admission.rs).
    LOOM: model option (ii) in crates/oraclemcp-core/tests (the repo runs .github/workflows/loom.yml):
    actors = lane thread, driver island, Cx cancel edge, quarantine decision; properties = no lost
    wakeup, no reuse of a session after cancel, bounded join. This is the lost-wakeup class that hung
    the shipping spool in 0.9.x (CHANGELOG 0.10.0) — model it before building it.
    OUTPUT: docs/adr/0014-blocking-driver-backend-execution-model.md with the decision, the proofs
    run, and the API the adapter must expose; nhteq.4 cites it.

title: B5.7 SPRT flake discipline: sequential re-run classifier with typed FLAKY/BROKEN/INFRA_SKIP outcomes replacing fixed retry loops
description:

    retried 15×20 s), masking propagation failures and burning runs; a green after a lucky retry is
    indistinguishable from a real green.

    Sequential Probability Ratio Test with explicit α=0.05, β=0.10, H0 "broken" vs H1 "flaky at
    p≤0.2", hard cap 6 runs; outcome is typed FLAKY(p_hat, n), BROKEN, or INFRA_SKIP (typed
    infrastructure failure detected from the lane's own JSON-line log, e.g. image pull / lane
    unreachable); FLAKY quarantines the lane for 14 days with an auto-reblock on recovery (plan §27.6
    item 4); outcomes are recorded in ci_taxonomy and the heartbeat. Apply first to live-matrix.yml
    and the OCI lane. LOGGING: per-attempt JSON line (attempt, exit, duration_ms, classification so far).
    ORDERING (refinement r1): the OCI harness beads (bp8ia.10.1–.4) do NOT wait for this tool; they
    adopt sprt_rerun.py when it exists (I4 wires it). This bead must never block OCI work.

title: Dashboard modal shell is duplicated across ConfirmDialog and ClientCredentialConfirmationDialog
description:
[LOW] Found during the 2ekf fresh-eyes review; filed rather than fixed inline because it is a refactor, not a defect — both copies are correct today.

web/src/app/App.tsx: ConfirmDialog (~2511) and ClientCredentialConfirmationDialog (~2571) each hand-roll the same modal shell: the fixed inset-0 backdrop, mousedown-to-cancel on the backdrop only, the z-50 layer, role=dialog + aria-modal + aria-labelledby, the Escape handler, and the useModalFocus ref.

GUARD — do NOT weaken: keep backdrop-cancel gated on !busy; keep autoFocus OUT of dialog contents (see b319815); keep focus returning to the invoker.

TEST: wig-polish.test.tsx already pins role=dialog/aria-modal/backdrop/labelledby and the no-autofocus property; extend it to assert BOTH dialogs share them so the shells cannot drift.

title: [09x][guard] SideEffectOracle bypassed: NestedJoin / PIVOT / UNPIVOT base objects were never collected
description:
query_base_objects::collect_factor handled only TableFactor::Table and ::Derived; TableFactor::NestedJoin (a parenthesized join, 'FROM (a JOIN b ON ..)') and ::Pivot/::Unpivot/::MatchRecognize fell into the '_ => {}' arm and named NO base objects.

classify_statement reads an EMPTY base-object list as Purity::ProvenReadOnly, so for those four spellings the engine's statement_purity consult - the trigger / VPD (DBMS_RLS) walk - was SKIPPED and the read was cleared Safe/READ_ONLY. An oracle that declares every object side-effecting still returned Safe, because it was never asked. This is a fail-open in the fail-closed core: it is not closable by any oracle, since the oracle is not consulted.

Found while writing tests to kill mutation survivors for bead .16 (the sibling walkers table_factor_carries_dml and collect_factor_qualifiers already descend both shapes, so this was an oversight in one walker, not a deliberate choice).

FIXED (tightening-only) in the same change: collect_factor now descends NestedJoin via a collect_table_with_joins helper and recurses through Pivot/Unpivot/MatchRecognize. Regression test: tests/classifier_metamorphic.rs::a_stricter_oracle_is_consulted_however_the_base_object_is_spelled asserts a strict oracle is reached for all 9 spellings (plain, parenthesized body, set-op, derived, CTE, nested join, doubly-nested join, PIVOT, UNPIVOT). Bead filed for the record/traceability; code and test land together.

title: [09x][A] No SCN ever reaches a client — observed_scn is audited but never projected, and a flashback read never echoes the SCN it read at
description: SYMPTOM: the console cannot learn a single system change number from the server. Three separate omissions: (1) AuditRecord::observed_scn exists and IS recorded (crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/mod.rs append_audit_with_observed_scn -> Auditor::append_correlated_with_observed_scn; AuditRecord field in crates/oraclemcp-audit/src/record.rs) but redacted_audit_record() (crates/oraclemcp-core/src/http/operator.rs) does NOT project it; (2) QueryResponse (crates/oraclemcp-db/src/query.rs:48) has no SCN field, so oracle_query with as_of={scn|timestamp} never echoes the SCN it actually read at — for a TIMESTAMP target Oracle resolves the value internally (AsOf::resolve_to_scn) and the caller never learns the resulting SCN at all; (3) no route publishes the database's current SCN even though the read exists (AsOf::current_system_change_number, DBMS_FLASHBACK.GET_SYSTEM_CHANGE_NUMBER) and the console cannot obtain it itself, because a SELECT calling DBMS_FLASHBACK is refused by the fail-closed purity oracle (default Unknown). THE DASHBOARD IS SHOWING LESS PROOF THAN THE BACKEND HAS: for (1) especially — the audit chain durably records the exact snapshot every governed read observed, and the operator cannot see it. WHY IT MATTERS: SCN is the forensic replay handle. Without it an operator cannot correlate an audit record with a point in time, cannot reproduce what a read saw, and cannot anchor a time-travel UI to anything real. The SCN time-scrubber (bead …15.2, commit ead6c08) therefore renders data-scn-min/max='unknown' and builds its axis solely from snapshots it has itself confirmed, and states in the UI that the server publishes neither the current SCN nor the retention window. title: No CI job compiles the Rust code for Windows; the target is built only at release-tag time
notes:
FOUND while fixing 7oaa (the Windows FileStore hardening) — this is the SYSTEMIC reason 7oaa's bug class exists and can ship.

THE GAP: the ONLY windows-latest job in ci.yml is "windows-installer" (PSScriptAnalyzer + install.ps1 dry-run). It never invokes cargo. Every cargo clippy/test job runs on Linux. So NOTHING compiles the Rust code for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc until release.yml builds the tag (release.yml:214). Consequences: (1) a Windows-only compile error is discovered while CUTTING A RELEASE, the worst possible moment; (2) every cfg(windows) block in the tree is effectively unverified — nobody can be sure it compiles; (3) cfg(windows) TESTS never execute anywhere, so Windows-only security refusals (7oaa: reparse-point + hard-linked service locks) have no automated proof at all, on a platform whose release assets we publish.

NOT HYPOTHETICAL — it bit me inside 7oaa: my first draft called options.custom_flags(FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT), but file_store.rs imports only the UNIX OpenOptionsExt (line ~20, cfg(unix)-gated), so custom_flags was not in scope for Windows. A hard compile error that NO existing gate would have caught; it would have surfaced as a broken release build. I only found it by cross-compiling deliberately.

FIX OPTIONS (note the caveat — the obvious one does not work today):
(a) Run "cargo check --workspace --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc" ON a windows-latest runner. Simplest, costs a runner minute; catches every Windows compile error.
(b) Cross-compile that same check on the existing ubuntu runner. CAVEAT I HIT: it FAILS on ubuntu today because ring and psm run C/asm build scripts needing an MSVC toolchain ('error occurred in cc-rs: failed to find tool "lib.exe"'). Needs xwin or clang-cl wiring first — cheaper per run, more setup.
(c) Run the existing cargo test job on windows-latest. Strongest: it additionally EXECUTES the cfg(windows) tests, and is the ONLY option that gives 7oaa's refusals real proof rather than compile-only assurance.
Recommend (c) if the runner budget allows, else (a). Do not assume (b) is the cheap default — it is currently broken.

WORKAROUND, reusable by anyone touching cfg(windows) code until this is fixed — compile the file in isolation:
  rustup target add x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
  # throwaway crate whose lib.rs is just:
  #   #![cfg_attr(windows, feature(windows_by_handle))]
  #   #[path = "<abs>/crates/oraclemcp-core/src/file_store.rs"] pub mod file_store;
  # with only that file's non-std deps (parking_lot / sha2 / thiserror), then:
  cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
"cargo check" skips cfg(test), so crate:: refs in the test module do not matter, and ring/psm never enter the graph. That compiles the REAL production file against the REAL target, and is exactly what caught the import bug above.

RELATED / HONEST STATUS: 7oaa's three cfg(windows) tests are committed and compile-verified but have NEVER executed. They stay decorative until this bead is fixed. Recorded rather than implied.
close_reason: Added required Windows Rust workspace cargo test job and regenerated CI taxonomy; Windows cfg code now compiles and executes in CI.

title: Epic: wire all currently supported thin-driver profile/config capabilities
description:
## Goal

Make oraclemcp's repo-local profile/config surface catch up with what the current pure-Rust thin `oracledb` driver already supports, without waiting on upstream features that are genuinely missing.

## Current evidence

- oraclemcp's strict config schema only exposes a subset of thin-driver connection options in `crates/oraclemcp-config/src/profile.rs`.
- `oraclemcp_core::profile_to_options` currently maps connect string, username/password, external/IAM flags, wallet location, a subset of session identity, call timeout, and session setup statements in `crates/oraclemcp-core/src/connect.rs`.
- `oraclemcp_db::connection::to_connect_options` currently only applies `wallet_location` and forces SNI when a wallet exists in `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/connection.rs`.
- The current `rust-oracledb` driver already supports additional public options: `ClientIdentity::{program,machine,osuser,terminal,driver_name}`, `with_edition`, `with_wallet_password`, `with_ssl_server_dn_match`, `with_ssl_server_cert_dn`, `with_use_sni`, `with_proxy_user`, `with_app_context`, and `with_sdu`.
- oraclemcp already contains partially stranded local support for `AuthAdapter::Proxy`, `DrcpConfig`, `PoolConfig`, `OraclePool`, and result placeholders for `QueryValue::Lob` and `QueryValue::Cursor`.

## Scope

Create and implement granular child beads for fields/capabilities that are wireable now because the driver or local code already supports them. Do not include Kerberos, RADIUS/native MFA, OCI IAM database-token auth, passwordless external/wallet auth, or ADT/object decoding here; those need upstream driver work and have separate upstream GitHub issues where applicable.

## Non-negotiables

- Preserve the fail-closed SQL guard and profile operating-level ceilings.
- Keep profile metadata and doctor output secret-safe: no connect strings, usernames, passwords, wallet passwords, token values, wallet paths, application-context values, or workstation/user identity leaks unless a tool is explicitly returning live Oracle session diagnostics.
- Keep config validation strict: new keys must be typed, documented, inherited correctly, and covered by tests.
- The default behavior must remain safe and compatible for existing profiles.
- Every child bead must include focused unit tests and, where feasible, live Oracle 23ai/FREE validation instructions.
close_reason: All dependency beads are closed: supported thin profile/config capabilities are wired through config, SessionContext, OracleConnectOptions, thin ConnectOptions, docs, doctor/setup, materialization, and live matrix coverage. Verified with full gates, Oracle 23ai live tests, and epic compliance audit 2026-06-18T10-25-21Z.
