title: [09x][L] Cost badge under-reports: the profile max_query_cost is already on the operator wire and the dashboard ignores it
description:
SYMPTOM: the cost/gas badge (bead 15.1, commit eaab5e2) renders data-cost-ceiling="undisclosed" for any statement that was not refused, because it learns the ceiling only from a cost refusal (structured_reason.query_cost_refusal.max_query_cost). That was wrong about the wire. GET /operator/v1/config ALREADY returns each profile ceiling: ConfigOps::status() (crates/oraclemcp-core/src/config_ops.rs:513) fills ConfigOpsStatus.profiles from OracleMcpConfig::list_profiles(), whose element type ProfileMetadata (crates/oraclemcp-config/src/profile.rs:1037) is Serialize and carries max_query_cost: Option<u64> (line 1047), alongside call_timeout_seconds, cumulative_query_cost_budget and max_level. The dashboard type ConfigProfileMetadata in web/src/app/operator-client.ts simply does not declare the field, so the badge never reads it.

THE DASHBOARD IS SHOWING LESS PROOF THAN THE BACKEND ACTUALLY HAS, and this one is entirely the fault of the dashboard: the backend has published the ceiling all along.

WHY IT MATTERS: an operator cannot see how close a statement is to the ceiling until the gate has already refused it, which is exactly the moment the information stops being useful. With the config ceiling in hand the badge can render within_ceiling with a real ratio BEFORE the statement runs.

FIX (web/ only, Arc L lane): (1) add max_query_cost to ConfigProfileMetadata; (2) have the Workbench cost panel read the active profile ceiling from the config query and pass it as the ceiling input; (3) keep a refusal-disclosed ceiling as the authority when the two disagree, because a per-call max_query_cost meets the profile ceiling with min(), so a refusal can legitimately report a LOWER ceiling than the profile.

A FIX MUST PROVE: a test asserts the badge renders a numeric data-cost-ceiling from config alone with no refusal in play, and that a lower refusal-disclosed ceiling still wins over the config value.
close_reason:
Fixed in commit 42acae2 (web/ only, no Rust touched). The badge now learns the ceiling from the operator wire.

ROOT CAUSE (my own bug from bead 15.1): GET /operator/v1/config already publishes every profile max_query_cost — ConfigOps::status() fills ConfigOpsStatus.profiles from list_profiles(), whose ProfileMetadata (crates/oraclemcp-config/src/profile.rs:1047) serializes max_query_cost — but the dashboard type ConfigProfileMetadata never declared the field, so the badge could only learn the ceiling from a cost refusal, i.e. after the gate had already refused, which is exactly when the number stops being useful.

FIX: operator-client.ts adds max_query_cost (and call_timeout_seconds) to ConfigProfileMetadata; new profileCostCeiling(config, activeProfile) reads the ceiling for the active profile (falling back to default_profile) and new parseActiveProfile() reads connection.profile from oracle_connection_info. presentation-model.ts: CostBadgeInput gains ceilingSource ("refusal" | "config" | "unknown") and ungated; toCostBadgeViewModel now distinguishes THREE states that were previously collapsed into one — a numeric ceiling in force (from config or refusal), UNGATED (the config positively says the profile declares no max_query_cost, so oracle_query is not cost-gated: a fact, not a missing reading), and UNKNOWN (the console could not identify the active profile, so it claims nothing). A refusal-disclosed ceiling always wins, because the server has already met the profile ceiling with any per-call one via min(), so the refusal number is the effective ceiling and may legitimately be LOWER than the configured one. skin.tsx emits data-cost-ceiling-source and renders data-cost-ceiling="none" for ungated vs "undisclosed" for unknown. App.tsx CostGatePanel adds the config + connection useQuery consumers and feeds the configured ceiling in.

PROVEN: 7 new cost-gate.test.ts cases (ceiling read from config for the active profile; default-profile fallback; ungated vs unknown kept distinct; a numeric data-cost-ceiling with NO refusal in play; an estimate judged within_ceiling against the config ceiling BEFORE the gate refuses; a lower refusal-disclosed ceiling winning over the configured one; ungated reported as ungated) plus 2 rewritten conformance it() (renders data-cost-ceiling="50000" + data-cost-ceiling-source="config" with no refusal; never invents a ceiling and never confuses ungated ("none") with unknown ("undisclosed")). The two older tests that asserted the WRONG claim — that the ceiling is only ever disclosed on refusal — were corrected rather than left passing.

Gate green: tsc --noEmit clean, vitest 106/106 (10 files), npm run build + dashboard-bundle-check OK.

title: Wire driver-level application context triples from profiles
description:
## Current gap

`rust-oracledb` exposes `ConnectOptions::with_app_context(Vec<(namespace, key, value)>)`, and the protocol layer applies those triples during auth. oraclemcp currently has no profile schema for driver-level application contexts. Operators can sometimes approximate this with `trusted_session_statements`, but that is broader, later, and less structured than the driver-supported logon app-context path.

## Required change

Add a strict profile config section for driver-level application context triples and map it through:

- `ConnectionProfile`
- `profile_to_options`
- `OracleConnectOptions`
- `RustOracleConnection::to_connect_options`
- `oracledb::ConnectOptions::with_app_context(...)`

## Design requirements

- Use a typed list of triples, not string parsing.
- Validate that namespace/key are non-empty and bounded.
- Treat values as potentially sensitive tenant/session context: do not include them in profile metadata or ordinary debug output.
- Preserve `trusted_session_statements` for cases that really need arbitrary operator-authored session setup.

## Acceptance criteria

- TOML examples can express at least two app-context triples.
- Config inheritance merges or replaces the app-context list according to the documented profile inheritance rule; tests must pin that behavior.
- The mapped `OracleConnectOptions` preserves ordering.
- Unit tests prove config parsing, validation failures, metadata redaction, and final driver option mapping.
- A live test or documented 23ai/FREE script verifies the context through `SYS_CONTEXT(namespace, key)` when the database has an application context available.
close_reason: Implemented typed profile app-context wiring and verified with full Rust gates plus single-bead compliance audit 2026-06-18T08-14-08Z; deterministic missing-test item manually calibrated as false positive against concrete test evidence.

title: Fail closed on Windows reparse-point and hard-linked FileStore service locks
description: [HIGH] Cross-review finding after 8c26968. The Unix hardening correctly opens .service.lock with O_NOFOLLOW and validates the opened descriptor as one regular inode. On Windows the cfg(unix) protections are absent: std::fs::OpenOptions follows an existing symlink/reparse point, and no nlink check rejects hard links. A same-user actor who can modify the FileStore state directory can therefore redirect acquire_service_owner() and its set_len(0)+metadata write into another writable file. Windows symlink privilege defaults are not a security boundary (Developer Mode and reparse points exist), and Windows release assets are published. Implement a safe no-follow/reparse-point open using a maintained safe abstraction or a platform-specific safe API while preserving #![forbid(unsafe_code)], reject non-regular/reparse and multi-link sidecars atomically where the platform permits, add Windows-gated adversarial tests, and return UnsafePath before any truncate/write. Do not weaken Unix behavior, crash recovery, or replacement-lock semantics.
close_reason:
FIXED in 1df04ae. Windows half of siry/em39: both Unix defences were cfg'd out on Windows, so a same-user actor able to write the FileStore state dir could still redirect acquire_service_owner's set_len(0) — or the JSONL append carrying audit-chain records — into any file that user can write.

FIX (mirrors the Unix shape, does not invent one):
1. FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT is the O_NOFOLLOW analogue and is what makes the refusal possible AT ALL: it returns a handle to the reparse point ITSELF. Without it the open silently follows, authenticate_private_file then stats the VICTIM — a perfectly ordinary lone regular file — and we truncate it. The flag is ignored for non-reparse files, so the normal path is unaffected.
2. authenticate_private_file also rejects FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT and number_of_links() != 1, stat'ing THE HANDLE WE HOLD, never the path — no inspect-then-use window. is_file() covers neither: a file symlink opened no-follow still reports as a file, and a hard link IS a regular file, just the victim's.
Both run before try_lock and before any truncate/append, and refuse as UnsafePath, not Io.

SCOPE WIDER THAN THE BEAD TEXT, deliberately: 7oaa was filed before em39 landed and names only .service.lock, but em39 added two MORE unix-only-no-follow opens (tail-recovery set_len at ~line 367, and open_append_private_file) with the identical Windows gap. Fixing only the lock would have left those live. All three now carry the flag. create_new_private_file needs none — create_new is O_EXCL and refuses any existing path, link included. (4 open sites audited, 3 needed it.)

WINDOWS-SPECIFIC INSIGHT worth keeping: a HARD LINK NEEDS NO PRIVILEGE on Windows, unlike a symlink (SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege / Developer Mode). So the hard link, not the reparse point, is the REACHABLE attack, and its test does not skip. The reparse test skips when the runner cannot create a symlink — that privilege default is NOT the boundary, which is exactly why the hard-link test carries the load. This also refutes siry's parting note ("Windows symlink creation requires privilege by default"), which was true but not the whole surface.

number_of_links() is unstable (windows_by_handle, rust-lang/rust#63010) so lib.rs gains a cfg_attr(windows)-gated feature. Adds NO nightly requirement — the line is already nightly-pinned for asupersync. None => REFUSE: File::metadata documents Some, so None means the descriptor could not be authenticated, and an unverifiable sidecar must not be written.

CONSTANTS are documented literals, a deliberate DEPARTURE from siry's libc precedent: O_NOFOLLOW genuinely differs per Unix (0x20000 Linux vs 0x100 macOS/BSD) so hardcoding it there is fragile; the Win32 flags are one frozen ABI identical on every Windows target, and windows-sys already sits at TWO versions in the lock — a third copy for two integers is the worse trade. std's OpenOptionsExt/MetadataExt remain the platform-specific safe API the bead asked for. forbid(unsafe_code) holds; zero unsafe added; no new dependency.

VERIFIED: the REAL file_store.rs cross-compiles clean for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc (via a #[path] include probe — the full crate cannot be checked here because ring/psm need an MSVC toolchain). That caught a GENUINE BUG IN MY OWN FIRST DRAFT: the file imports only the UNIX OpenOptionsExt, so custom_flags was not in scope for Windows and would have broken the RELEASE build — the only place it could have surfaced. Linux untouched: fmt clean, clippy -p oraclemcp-core --all-targets -D warnings clean, file_store 18/18 green.

HONEST LIMIT — the reason this is not as strong as siry: the three cfg(windows) tests are compile-verified but have NEVER EXECUTED. This box has no Windows and, as I discovered doing this, NO CI JOB COMPILES OR TESTS THIS CRATE FOR WINDOWS AT ALL (filed as oraclemcp-6fyp; the only windows-latest job is the installer PSSA). siry proved its tests load-bearing by mutation; I cannot. The tests mirror the unix ones that do pass, and both Windows-only primitives they use (fs::hard_link, os::windows::fs::symlink_file) were compile-checked against the real target. Until 6fyp lands, the Windows refusals rest on code review + cross-compilation, not on execution. Stated rather than implied.

NOT WEAKENED: Unix behaviour, crash recovery, and replacement-lock semantics untouched — no cfg(unix) path changed; 18/18 file_store tests green including service_lock_recovers_after_holder_process_is_killed and old_lock_drop_does_not_unlink_replacement_lock.

title: [BUG][P0] A READ_ONLY lane is frozen at the snapshot of its first read
description:
FOUND LIVE by the Arc I e2e (scripts/e2e/reversible.sh) against Oracle 23ai Free: an independent READ_ONLY MCP session never observes commits made after its first read.

MECHANISM. The A1 read-only backstop (crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/read_only_backstop.rs) is LAZY BY DESIGN: ensure_armed() issues ROLLBACK + SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY once and then no-ops while 'armed' (its own test pins 'issued exactly once across many reads', and its doc calls this 'repeated reads in the SAME read-only transaction pay no extra round trip'). Nothing on the pure-read path ever ends that transaction. But Oracle gives a READ ONLY transaction TRANSACTION-LEVEL read consistency: 'all queries refer to the same snapshot of the database' (Database Concepts, Read-Only Transactions). The transaction ends only at COMMIT/ROLLBACK. So a lane that only reads keeps one read-only transaction open forever and is pinned to the snapshot taken at its FIRST read.

IMPACT. Any read-only agent - the default and recommended posture, and the whole monitoring/inspection use case - sees stale data indefinitely. oracle_query, the dictionary tools, and oracle_db_health all serve the frozen snapshot. The staleness is silent: no error, no label. A write-capable lane is unaffected (its writes end the transaction), which is why the deterministic tests never caught it: they assert the statement is issued once, which is exactly the bug.

REPRO (live, 2 sessions on one DB): session W = READ_ONLY MCP lane; run oracle_query 'SELECT V FROM T WHERE ID=1' (arms the backstop). From another session, commit an UPDATE to that row. Re-run the same oracle_query in W: it still returns the OLD value, forever.

FIX SPACE (needs a deliberate call - this is a security control, so the A1 property must be re-proved by whatever lands): (a) end the read-only transaction after each read (ROLLBACK) so the next read arms a FRESH read-only transaction and a fresh snapshot - costs one extra round trip per read, which is precisely what the lazy design was avoiding; (b) keep laziness but re-arm on a staleness bound (time / on demand); (c) drop SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY for a per-statement mechanism that does not carry a snapshot. Whatever lands must keep layer B intact (a MISCLASSIFIED write must still hit ORA-01456) and must come with a live test that proves a read-only lane observes a commit made by another session.

Not an Arc I regression: the reversible workspace neither introduced nor worsened it. The Arc I e2e worked around it by making its witness session READ_WRITE-but-never-writing (statement-level consistency), with a pointer to this bead.
close_reason: Fixed the READ_ONLY snapshot freeze by starting a fresh engine-enforced READ ONLY transaction before each guarded read; added unit and two-session Oracle 23ai regression coverage. Scoped fmt, clippy, and tests passed; live Oracle credentials were unavailable locally.

title: Refresh profile docs, setup templates, and doctor for thin-supported fields
description:
## Current gap

The README, setup templates, profile examples, profile metadata, and doctor output still describe a thin profile surface that is behind the current driver capabilities. For example, the README says `os_user` and `program` remain backend-reported unless the driver exposes setters, but the current driver does expose `ClientIdentity` setters. Profile docs also need to reflect that thin edition selection is now driver-supported through `ConnectOptions::with_edition(...)`, while unsupported IAM/external auth paths remain explicit unsupported diagnostics.

## Required change

Refresh user-facing profile/config documentation and diagnostics after the supported thin-driver fields are wired.

## Must cover

- Explicit driver identity fields vs DBMS session attributes.
- Edition selection through the thin driver, including connection-time failure behavior for invalid/unauthorized editions.
- Username/password over TCPS wallet vs unsupported passwordless external/wallet auth.
- Wallet password references and TLS DN/SNI options.
- Proxy auth as supported, distinct from unsupported Kerberos/RADIUS/external auth.
- Application context triples.
- SDU and DRCP routing knobs.
- `[profiles.pool]` behavior after it is either wired or made explicitly non-operative.
- Result materialization improvements for LOB locators and REF CURSORs.

## Security requirements

- `oracle_list_profiles` remains non-secret and does not leak identity values, connect strings, usernames, credential references, wallet paths, wallet passwords, app-context values, proxy target details, or arbitrary edition names unless explicitly justified.
- `oraclemcp --json setup --profile ...` must generate safe templates with placeholders, never real local secret values.
- `doctor` should classify unsupported auth separately from malformed profile config and real connection/auth failures.

## Acceptance criteria

- README profile section is accurate for the thin-only driver.
- `oraclemcp --json setup --profile demo` includes safe examples for the newly wired fields.
- Doctor output reports actionable next steps for supported vs unsupported thin profile modes.
- Tests cover profile metadata redaction and setup template contents.
- Search for stale claims such as "driver lacks setters", unsupported edition selection, or unsupported wallet/password statements and update them.
close_reason: Refreshed thin-only profile docs, setup templates, and doctor guidance for supported fields, safe examples, redaction, pools, and LOB/REF CURSOR materialization; verified focused tests, full gates, and compliance audit 2026-06-18T10-15-36Z.

title: [CI-RECOVERY-2026-07][installer] Preserve npm dispatch outputs under GitHub Actions
description:

title: Classifier: WITH-CTE-smuggled DML body tiered READ_ONLY (sqlparser SetExpr::Update/Delete/Merge/Insert)
description:
CONFIRMED live on READ_ONLY lane (xe18, plain TCP lab container) via oracle_preview_sql, then FIXED with tests.

SYMPTOM: On a READ_ONLY profile, oracle_preview_sql for
  WITH a AS (SELECT 1 x FROM dual) UPDATE t SET x=1
  WITH a AS (SELECT 1 x FROM dual) DELETE FROM t
  WITH a AS (SELECT 1 x FROM dual) MERGE INTO t USING a ON (1=1) WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET x=1
returned gate_decision=allow, required_level=READ_ONLY (Safe). A statement whose text carries a top-level UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE must never be tiered READ_ONLY (fail-closed invariant).

ROOT CAUSE: sqlparser 0.62 parses WITH <cte> {UPDATE|DELETE|MERGE|INSERT} ... as a single Statement::Query whose query.body is SetExpr::Update/Delete/Merge/Insert (the trailing DML is absorbed as a query body, not surfaced as Statement::Update). classify_statement's Statement::Query arm assumed the body is always a read and fell through to Safe/ReadOnly. Verified by dumping the sqlparser AST (body: Update(...) / Delete(...)). The comment at classifier.rs ~886 already noted DML SetExpr bodies exist but wrongly assumed they are 'classified separately'.

EXPLOITABILITY: none in practice — Oracle rejects the syntax with ORA-00928 (WITH cannot precede UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE), confirmed via oracle_query on the live lane (isError, error_class=SYNTAX_ERROR, no write). This is a fail-closed-SPIRIT / defense-in-depth verdict bug, not a live write bypass. The genuinely dangerous variants were already blocked: WITH FUNCTION autonomous-transaction DML (blocked), WITH cte DROP/TRUNCATE/GRANT (parse-fail -> buried/leading-verb scan -> blocked).

FIX (crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/classifier.rs): added set_expr_carries_dml() that recurses query.body through SetExpr::Query and SetExpr::SetOperation and returns true on Insert/Update/Delete/Merge. The Statement::Query arm now returns guarded_rw (Guarded/READ_WRITE) when it fires. Purely STRUCTURAL AST inspection - NOT text scanning - so it has zero false-positive surface (unlike the buried-verb scan, which would false-positive on non-reserved identifiers like purge/audit/flashback and on FOR UPDATE lock clauses). Match is exhaustive (SetExpr is not non_exhaustive) so a future sqlparser bump that adds a body variant breaks the build and forces review.

TESTS added: cte_smuggled_dml_body_is_never_read_only (4 variants -> not Safe, not READ_ONLY); legitimate_cte_reads_stay_safe_after_dml_body_tightening (legit CTE read, SELECT purge/audit/flashback identifiers, UNION ALL body stay Safe; SELECT ... FOR UPDATE stays Guarded/READ_WRITE not over-tightened to Forbidden). Post-fix live re-verify: WITH cte UPDATE now blocked/READ_WRITE; legit CTE read still allow/READ_ONLY. cargo test -p oraclemcp-guard green (93 lib tests), fmt+clippy clean.
close_reason: Fixed in classifier.rs (set_expr_carries_dml structural guard in Statement::Query arm) + 2 tests; verified live on xe18 READ_ONLY lane pre/post; guard suite + fmt + clippy green

title: Workspace test in a fresh target dir is refused by the build guard: nested unleased cargo fetch at the rustc probe
description:
Observed 2026-09-24 by BlackCondor (.11.8). In a fresh worktree CARGO_TARGET_DIR, 'scripts/build_lease.sh --slots 2 -- timeout 1800 cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast' exited 101 at the rustc probe twice, because the repo compiler wrapper refused a nested, un-leased 'cargo fetch'. Leased 'cargo deny check' failed the same way. The orchestrator's gate in a warm target dir passes, probably because the cached rustc probe skips the wrapper. So every agent with a new worktree target cannot run the mandatory pre-push workspace test, and the swarm pushes without it.

Find the nested cargo invocation (a test or build script spawning cargo with the lease env stripped or cleared, e.g. env -u CARGO_SWARM_BUILD_LEASE_* or Command::env_clear) and make it inherit the live lease identity. Or make the wrapper accept a nested cargo whose ancestor holds the lease. Do not weaken the refusal of genuinely un-leased builds.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: in a brand-new CARGO_TARGET_DIR, 'scripts/build_lease.sh --slots 2 -- cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast' completes and 'cargo deny check' under the lease completes.
- [ ] Negative: a plain un-leased 'cargo test --workspace' is still refused (existing selftest stays green).
- [ ] Tests: a check_build_lease selftest case for a nested cargo under a live lease.
- [ ] No-claim: does not change slot count or target-dir rules.
close_reason: Nested cargo inherits a verified live ancestor lease; fresh-target workspace test + cargo deny pass [closing=60e87315776ee543c19972d99664007e67326af4 source=1c5f13716124efd53a762a04390f1749d0bc551c evidence=tests/artifacts/evidence/closes/oraclemcp-ax7ru.json]

title: [P1][oci-harness] wallet SSL_SERVER_CERT_DN extraction fails on real free-tier ADB wallet
description: OCI-live re-run 21:29: provision+wallet-download+DESTROY all PASSED (zero cost, ADB destroyed), but the harness FAILED extracting SSL_SERVER_CERT_DN from the downloaded ADB wallet ('downloaded ADB wallet has no SSL_SERVER_CERT_DN'), so the TCPS probe could not configure ssl_server_dn_match. This is a HARNESS wallet-parsing bug, NOT the driver's OCI code nor creds. Modern ADB wallets carry the DN in tnsnames.ora (ssl_server_cert_dn / ssl_server_dn_match=... in the connect descriptor) and/or sqlnet.ora, not always as a separate metadata field. FIX: extract the server cert DN from the wallet's tnsnames.ora connect descriptor (parse ssl_server_cert_dn="...") with a fallback, and only require it when the probe needs strict DN match; verify against the wallet fixtures + a live re-run. Keep the exit-trap destroy + free-tier guard intact. Do NOT apply to cloud yourself; fix + validate + wallet-fixture test only.
close_reason: Fixed by 198f00c: parse explicit wallet SSL_SERVER_CERT_DN with sqlnet fallback; modern no-literal wallets keep strict host/SAN matching. Fixture and Terraform harness checks pass.

notes:
SCOPE ESCALATED — this is CROSS-REPO, do not fix it from one repo. New evidence since filing:

(1) ALL THREE implicated files are MIRRORED in rust-oracledb: .github/workflows/_quality.yml, scripts/ci_taxonomy.py, scripts/verify_required_local.py. Both candidate fixes therefore change a mirrored contract, so this needs the .2/.8 owners plus whoever owns the mirror (GoldenGorge). NOTE: _quality.yml already DIFFERS between the two repos (cmp), so the mirror has drifted already — worth checking whether that drift is intentional before anyone edits either copy.

(2) I RETRACT the 'check the Actions tab' suggestion from my earlier note as currently untestable: _quality.yml is NOT PUSHED. origin/main does not contain it and there are 45 unpushed commits. 'gh workflow list' shows 7 registered workflows (ci/docker/kani-safety/mutation-safety/publish-mcp/publish-npm/release) and _quality.yml is absent — but that proves NOTHING, because GitHub has never seen the file. Whether GitHub reports 'Invalid workflow file' for an on:-less yml in .github/workflows/ stays UNVERIFIED until the orchestrator pushes. Do not treat its absence from the list as evidence it is ignored. Re-check after the next push: if GitHub does flag it, option (a) becomes clearly correct rather than merely tidier.

(3) OPTION ANALYSIS, refined. (a) move _quality.yml out of .github/workflows/ and re-point verify_required_local.py: fixes the taxonomy false positive AND any invalid-workflow risk, but changes a mirrored path in BOTH repos. (b) teach ci_taxonomy that a workflow is a file GitHub would actually run (has an 'on:' trigger): contained and arguably the more honest definition, BUT it silently stops flagging a REAL workflow that lost its 'on:' by mistake — such a file is dead and should be reported as 'not runnable', not skipped; so (b) done naively trades one blind spot for another. Prefer (b) implemented as a distinct 'not a runnable workflow' classification rather than a skip. (c) add timeout-minutes/permissions to _quality.yml: still recommend AGAINST — it greens the gate while asserting nothing true about a file GitHub never runs.

title: Materialize generic LOB locator cells with thin driver reads
description:
## Current gap

`rust-oracledb` already exposes public LOB locator reads through `Connection::read_lob` / blocking `read_lob`, and oraclemcp already has capped LOB-reading logic for explicit `oracle_read_clob` style workflows. Generic query serialization still emits placeholders for `QueryValue::Lob` in `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/connection.rs`:

`<unsupported LOB locator size=...>`

That makes ordinary `SELECT clob_col FROM ...` or PL/SQL output returning LOB locators less useful to agents even though the driver can read the locator.

## Required change

Materialize LOB locator cells during generic query/result conversion when the driver returns `QueryValue::Lob`, using the driver's public locator-read API and the existing oraclemcp caps/serialization policy.

## Safety requirements

- Preserve hard caps for text characters and binary bytes.
- Preserve type-specific output: CLOB/NCLOB as capped text, BLOB/BFILE as capped binary/base64 or existing binary representation, with truncation metadata.
- Do not read unbounded LOBs by default.
- Respect call timeout/cancellation handling where available.
- Keep errors structured: unsupported LOB subtype or failed locator read should be explicit, not silently replaced with null.

## Acceptance criteria

- Generic query rows no longer emit unsupported placeholders for supported LOB locators.
- Existing explicit LOB tools keep working.
- Unit tests cover CLOB, BLOB, null LOB, truncation, and locator-read failure paths.
- Live 23ai/FREE tests cover selecting CLOB/BLOB values through `oracle_query` with caps.
- Performance is bounded: tests or benchmarks prove a large LOB cannot force unbounded allocation.
close_reason: Implemented bounded generic LOB locator materialization for CLOB/BLOB/BFILE, wired oracle_query serialization caps through the backend, added unit tests and bound live 23ai coverage; gates, full workspace tests, cargo deny, and single-bead audit passed.

title: [P1][cqn] public EMON receiver opening bypasses subscription caps
description:
Confirmed CQN subscription-cap bypass.

After one privileged CqnRegistrationGate::register_query succeeds, the public CqnRegisteredQuery::open_emon_receiver(&self, cx, connection) may be called repeatedly. It takes no SubscriptionRegistry, owner, URI, reservation token, or cap proof. Each invocation directly calls OracleConnection::open_cqn_notification_receiver and can create another independently authenticated EMON connection.

The C1.3 registry's documented invariant is that every admitted owner/URI pair consumes one EMON connection and total active connections never exceed the profile/database ceiling. That invariant is not enforced at the actual EMON effect point: a caller can register once, skip SubscriptionRegistry::subscribe, and open unbounded receivers. This is an availability/resource-governance fail-open, not a cosmetic API concern.

Acceptance: make an atomically acquired registry reservation (or opaque capability) mandatory for each EMON open, bind it to the server-derived owner and registered query/URI, and release it exactly once on receiver teardown/failure. Add a regression that attempts open_emon_receiver without admission and then beyond both principal and DB ceilings; no driver receiver call may occur.
close_reason: Closed P1 CQN EMON cap bypass: every receiver open now requires an atomically acquired registry reservation bound to the server-derived owner, registered URI, and query identity; reservations release on driver failure and receiver teardown. Regression covers no-admission, principal/DB caps, N+1 refusal, and release.

title: FileStore JSONL append and tail-recovery follow links (same class as siry)
description:
[HIGH] Found by fresh-eyes review immediately after fixing siry: siry hardened .service.lock, but the SAME link-following class survives on the FileStore DATA path, one function over in the same file.

TWO SITES (crates/oraclemcp-core/src/file_store.rs):
1. append_jsonl -> open_append_private_file: OpenOptions.append(true).create(true) FOLLOWS an existing link. Path segments are validated (no traversal), but a same-UID actor who can write the state dir can pre-plant <root>/<collection>/<id>.jsonl as a symlink (or hard link) to any file this UID can write, and the store then APPENDS to it. This is the audit / write-intent / metrics append path, so it is both an arbitrary-append primitive AND a way to divert the audit chain off its own file.
2. recover_jsonl_tail (the OpenOptions::new().read.write.open(&path) near the repair block): same follow, and it then calls set_len(valid_len) — an arbitrary file-shortening primitive.

WHY nlink==1 IS SAFE FOR DATA FILES (checked, not assumed): no production code hard-links store files (only tests do); store files are created via create_new_private_file (O_EXCL, nlink 1); and service restore ALREADY refuses a hard-linked bundle (ORACLEMCP_SERVICE_RESTORE_INVALID_BACKUP). The house posture already treats a hard link here as invalid.

FIX (reuse the siry pattern, do not reinvent): O_NOFOLLOW on both opens so a symlinked target is refused IN THE OPEN (no inspect-then-open window), then authenticate the OPEN DESCRIPTOR via fstat (file.metadata(), never the path) for is_file() + nlink()==1. Generalize siry's authenticate_lock_file into one shared authenticate_private_file(file, path). Refuse as UnsafePath, not Io — ELOOP is an attack signal. OpenOptionsExt::custom_flags is a safe API so forbid(unsafe_code) holds; libc is already a unix-gated dep of this crate after siry.

TESTS: mirror siry's discipline — assert the VICTIM'S BYTES SURVIVE, not merely that an error came back (refusing while still appending or shortening would be a passing test and a live bug). Cover symlinked append, hard-linked append, and symlinked tail-recovery. Mutation-verify: reverting the defence must make them fail.

DO NOT WEAKEN: append_jsonl's created/fsync_dir semantics, the torn-tail repair contract, or the InvalidJsonlRecord line-terminator guard.
close_reason:
FIXED in 2942e7c. Same class as siry, found by reviewing the siry fix itself.

BOTH SITES HARDENED (crates/oraclemcp-core/src/file_store.rs):
1. append_jsonl / open_append_private_file — appended service records (audit chain, write-intents, metrics) through a planted link into an attacker-chosen file.
2. recover_jsonl — followed a link then set_len(valid_len), an arbitrary file-shortening primitive.

FIX: O_NOFOLLOW refuses a symlinked target IN THE OPEN (no inspect-then-open window), then the OPEN DESCRIPTOR is authenticated by fstat (file.metadata(), never the path) for is_file() + nlink()==1. siry's authenticate_lock_file/lock_open_error were GENERALIZED to authenticate_private_file/private_open_error, so all THREE sites (lock + append + recovery) now share ONE contract instead of three hand-rolled ones. 3x O_NOFOLLOW + 3x authenticate, verified by grep.

nlink==1 CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED, for data files: no production code hard-links store files (only tests), store files are created via create_new_private_file (O_EXCL, nlink 1), and service restore already refuses a hard-linked bundle (ORACLEMCP_SERVICE_RESTORE_INVALID_BACKUP). The house posture already treats a hard link here as invalid, so requiring nlink==1 breaks nothing.

TESTS (3 new, unix-gated): symlinked append, hard-linked append, symlinked tail-recovery. Each asserts the VICTIM'S BYTES SURVIVE, not merely that an error was returned.

MUTATION-VERIFIED (and the first attempt caught my own sloppiness): my initial mutation was imprecise — it stripped O_NOFOLLOW from the LOCK opener (byte-identical text) instead of the APPEND opener, so the symlink-append test passed and looked non-load-bearing. Re-mutated precisely against the unique  anchor: BOTH append tests then FAIL at the Ok(...) branch, i.e. the record was appended THROUGH the link into the victim. Recovery test fails the same way. All three are load-bearing. Fix restored and re-verified (18/18 file_store green).

NOT WEAKENED: append_jsonl's created/fsync_dir semantics, the torn-tail repair contract (jsonl_recovery_repairs_torn_tail_and_rebuilds_index still green), and the InvalidJsonlRecord line-terminator guard.

GATE (scoped): fmt clean; clippy -p oraclemcp-core --all-targets -D warnings = 0 warnings; cargo test -p oraclemcp-core --lib file_store = 18 passed; forbid(unsafe_code) intact (custom_flags is a safe API); no new package (libc already unix-gated here from siry).

title: F-LOW DC5: reject sub-minute FixedOffset loss
description: Repo/site: /home/durakovic/projects/rust-oracledb/crates/oracledb/src/sql_convert.rs:1233-1250, DateTime<FixedOffset>::to_sql computes offset_minutes with local_minus_utc() / 60. comments.author: durakovic
comments.text: PARKED - driver-side, and CONFIRMED STILL UNFIXED at rust-oracledb origin/main today, so this is not a stale finding. crates/oracledb/src/sql_convert.rs:1247 still computes 'let offset_seconds = self.offset().local_minus_utc();' and builds BindValue::TimestampTz with 'offset_minutes: offset_seconds.div_euclid(60)'. SHARPENING THE FINDING while I was in there: div_euclid does not merely truncate, and the two signs fail DIFFERENTLY. +00:00:30 gives div_euclid(60) = 0, so the offset silently becomes +00:00 - the truncation the bead describes. But -00:00:30 gives div_euclid(60) = -1, so the offset silently becomes -00:01:00: the represented instant moves by 30 seconds in one direction and 30 in the other, and a caller sees neither an error nor a consistent rounding rule. The bead's narrow fix (reject a FixedOffset whose seconds are not divisible by 60, since Oracle TSTZ offsets have minute precision) remains the right one, and its negative acceptance should assert BOTH signs for exactly this reason. Hand this to the driver pane with the sign asymmetry noted.

comments.author: durakovic
comments.text:
CONSUMER ENUMERATION DONE (read-only, against HEAD 153c9d08 content — the bead's line refs 4281/11590/14082 have drifted, so this maps by semantics not line number). NOT YET FIXED: dispatch/mod.rs, dispatch/args.rs and tests.rs are carrying another pane's ~1081 uncommitted lines, and a pathspec commit takes the file's WORKING-TREE content, so editing now would land their WIP under this bead and their next commit would silently revert mine.

THE TWO ZERO-SEMANTICS THAT ALREADY DISAGREE, both live at HEAD:
  profile_request_timeout(mod.rs:340) — Some(0) => None, i.e. profile call_timeout_seconds=0 means NO TIMEOUT / wait forever (documented opt-out; doctor warns on that posture).
  call_timeout_duration(mod.rs:4283)  — seconds==0 => InvalidArguments 'timeout_seconds must be at least 1 when provided'.
Different inputs (profile config vs per-call arg) so this is defensible, but it is the exact wait-forever-vs-reject split the finding warns about and any fix must not blur them.

VALIDATING PATHS — only two functions ever reject zero:
  with_call_timeout() (mod.rs:4553), 11 call sites
  prepare_query_stream_delivery() (mod.rs:14461), the streaming path
HANDLERS THAT READ timeout_seconds (13 total). Validate: compile_object, create_or_replace, deploy_ddl, dispatch_with_cx_inner, execute_sql, patch_source, prepare_query_stream_delivery, preview_dml, run_prepared_query. Forward WITHOUT validating: create_or_replace_inner, deploy_ddl_inner, execute_approved_args, semantic_search_as_query_args — but the first three are called from validating parents (create_or_replace, deploy_ddl, execute_sql via ExecuteArgs), so they are likely covered transitively; semantic_search_as_query_args(mod.rs:3471) rewrites into query args and needs its downstream confirmed.

THE WIDER GAP, which the bead does not name: registry.rs advertises timeout_seconds_prop() on 20 tools (JSON Schema minimum:1, maximum:3600) while only 13 arg structs carry the field. args.rs uses deny_unknown_fields on exactly ONE struct (args.rs:123). So for the ~7 tools that advertise the property without a field to parse it into, a supplied timeout_seconds — including 0 — is accepted and silently IGNORED. That is a third semantics ('accepted, no effect') alongside wait-forever and reject, and it is invisible to any test that only exercises a representative path.

WHEN THE FILE FREES: validate an explicitly-present timeout_seconds once before canonical dispatch on BOTH the normal and streaming paths, keep 1..=3600 clamping, and assert the identical InvalidArguments envelope on EVERY advertised tool rather than one representative — the 20-vs-13 mismatch above is why a representative test would pass while the gap remained.

title: F-LOW DI6: preserve successful checkpoint and undo across late deadlines
description: Repo/site: /home/durakovic/projects/oraclemcp/crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/mod.rs:8232-8307 and response_reports_terminal_effect at 11147-11170. Current verification: successful oracle_checkpoint and oracle_undo_to execute SAVEPOINT or ROLLBACK state changes, but the outer late-deadline policy does not classify their responses as terminal effects. Risk: the client receives a retryable timeout after Oracle and the workspace state already changed, so retry can duplicate or mis-sequence transaction operations. Narrow fix: classify only successful checkpoint/undo responses as terminal at the post-body deadline boundary; previews and pre-body cancellation remain cancellable. This complements, but is independently scoped from, the landed DI1 held-execute branch. Negative acceptance: an injected deadline after DB success returns the successful response and exactly one audit/state transition for checkpoint, rollback-to, and full rollback. Positive acceptance: a deadline before DB success still cancels and an invalid checkpoint remains an error.
close_reason: DI6 preserves successful checkpoint and undo across late failures [closing=cae92527790bf793c630101e1be1ee7bfc997fb3 source=332c2c658d259babcd976e32084313b045d3b8b7 evidence=tests/artifacts/evidence/closes/oraclemcp-eng-program-bp8ia.7.11.9.json]

comments.author: durakovic
comments.text: DI6 LANDED (committed locally; not pushed, pane 2 owns the merge). response_reports_terminal_effect now classifies successful oracle_checkpoint and oracle_undo_to as terminal: both have already changed transaction state on the pinned session when they return Ok, so a deadline expiring after Oracle answered was reporting a RETRYABLE cancellation for completed work - and a caller retrying after Cancelled would re-establish a savepoint or re-roll-back a workspace that had already moved. BOTH UNDO SHAPES COUNT, and one is a trap I nearly walked into: a FULL rollback reports undone_to=null because it targets no named checkpoint, and it is the call that discarded the MOST state. Keying terminality on undone_to being non-null would wave through precisely the largest effect, so the undo arm keys on the executed 'statement' field instead. MUTATION-CONTROLLED against exactly the two most natural wrong implementations: setting the checkpoint arm to false, and re-keying undo on undone_to, both fail successful_checkpoint_and_undo_are_terminal_effects; restoring passes. The widening is bounded in the other direction too - previews stay cancellable (they roll themselves back and leave nothing behind), and a body missing the field the handler sets on success is not treated as an effect, so a call that never reached the database keeps no effect it does not have. 361 lib tests pass. NOT COVERED: the end-to-end deadline-injection acceptance ('an injected deadline after DB success returns the successful response and exactly one audit/state transition') is asserted at the classifier seam rather than by driving a real late deadline through the dispatcher against a live session.

title: F-WIN-E2E: dashboard_readonly.sh e2e fails on Windows Git-Bash (empty stderr, early exit)
description:

Diagnosis leads: (1) PASSES on Linux (0.30s). (2) --dry-run SKIPS the heavy commands (npm/tsc/dashboard_skin_lint/bundle_check) via e2e_run_command E2E_DRY_RUN=1 branch (lib.sh:146), so the web toolchain is NOT the cause. (3) Empty stderr with E2E_LOG=1 means the script died BEFORE emitting e2e_log_event scenario_start (dashboard_readonly.sh:34) - during early setup: source lib.sh, ROOT computation, or the arg-parse loop. (4) Sibling bash-e2e binaries installer_e2e and e2e_harness PASS on the same Windows job, so bash + lib.sh work under Git-Bash generally; the failure is specific to dashboard_readonly.sh setup path or an arg it parses (--dry-run). This is the LAST blocker to a fully-green Windows lane; F-VZUI durable-state scope itself is DONE and validated.

Scope grew far beyond dashboard_e2e: (1) WSL-bash trap -> Git-Bash resolver (bash_bin/coreutil/sh_bin); (2) Linux release/distribution/installer tooling -> Unix-scoped; (3) CRLF -> .gitattributes (*.sh/json/toml/ts/...); (4) 34 oraclemcp-core unit tests (Git-Bash coreutils for iam_token exec, TOML literal/forward-slash paths for connect+inject, .ts LF for operator_protocol, sh_bin for plugin, http accept-nonblocking PRODUCTION bug [7.16], file_store fsync, shipping_spool timing); (5) CI infra: rust-cache cache-on-failure + --lib --bins + CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 cut the job ~2h->~6min (risk-aligned: Windows-specific behaviour is all in unit tests; integration tests run on Linux + the windows-installer job). dashboard_e2e WSL-bash fix stands for cross-platform correctness.

title: F-WIN-HTTP: native HTTP/HTTPS server could not complete a TLS handshake on Windows
description: Found while greening the Windows lane (7.14). PRODUCTION bug: the serve loops (serve_http_until/serve_https_until/serve_control_https_until in crates/oraclemcp-core/src/http/serve.rs) set the LISTENER non-blocking for shutdown polling. On Windows (Winsock), a socket returned by accept() INHERITS the listeners non-blocking mode (on Unix accepted sockets are always blocking). The per-connection code is blocking-with-timeout (SO_RCVTIMEO/SO_SNDTIMEO), which a non-blocking socket silently ignores while returning WouldBlock immediately -> every TLS handshake aborted instantly (mapped to TimedOut) and transport worker permits released before ever being observed held. Net: the MCP HTTP/HTTPS/control server was non-functional on Windows. Fixed f9f00b0: restore_accepted_socket_blocking() (set_nonblocking(false)) on every accepted socket in all three loops; no-op on Unix; continue-on-error is fail-safe; mTLS/capacity fail-closed gating unchanged. Linux http 155/0; confirmed on the Windows lane (run 5219cb8, 0 fail).
close_reason: Fixed f9f00b0 (restore blocking on accepted sockets). Confirmed green on the Windows CI lane.

title: 0.6.0 Interactive & Always-On — release train 0.6.0→0.6.1→0.6.2
description:
# Epic: oraclemcp 0.6.0 "Interactive & Always-On" (release TRAIN 0.6.0 → 0.6.1 → 0.6.2)

Source of truth at beading time: PLAN_0_6_0_INTERACTIVE_ALWAYS_ON.md v3.18 (2787 lines). These beads
elaborate that plan and are intended to be SELF-CONTAINED — you should not need to reopen the markdown.

## What we are building (TL;DR)
oraclemcp becomes ONE guarded always-on service + ONE versioned schema-first protocol + MANY front-ends,
with a first-class per-principal HTTP **LaneRuntime** as the internal security & concurrency boundary.
Two access modes, decoupled:
- **stdio — UNCHANGED.** Each agent spawns its own process → own connection/level/DB. Single-principal
  per process, already correct. DO NOT TOUCH IT (non-goal N10).
- **http — UPGRADED** to true per-lane concurrency. One persistent service; each caller resolves to a
  **lane** bound to a **verified Subject** (never caller-supplied), with its own DB/profile, operating
  level, single-use grant store, request budget, audit context, cancellation. Many agents + a human →
  many databases at once, isolated. The **web dashboard** is the human face.

## The release train (decision D1 — one plan, beaded together, built continuously, NO deferral)
- **0.6.0 — Foundation (safety core + usable product):** driver 0.5.1 validation (WP-A), #4/#3/#2
  (WP-B/C/R), **WP-N lane foundation**, WP-P protocol, WP-S service, WP-E/F installer/distribution,
  WP-G core + `om doctor`, WP-H release. Dashboard = the READ-ONLY control plane (Overview/Sessions/
  Audit/Doctor; 2D first; skinnable seam in place).
- **0.6.1 — Interactive dashboard:** full views + the governed Workbench (Safe SQL, governed edit loop,
  live compile, schema browser, global search) + plsql-intelligence wiring + version history.
- **0.6.2 — Advanced/wow:** Change-Review board ("PR for PL/SQL") + the 3D Orrery skin + migration export.
Train membership is carried as a label (train:0.6.0 / train:0.6.1 / train:0.6.2) on every bead.

## Throughline (NON-NEGOTIABLE safety invariant — AGENTS.md "do not weaken")
Every face goes through the SAME fail-closed core: classifier → per-lane ceiling → preview/confirm →
rollback-by-default → audit. Identity is a verified Subject (dashboard login / OAuth sub / mTLS fp /
local pairing / OS user) — NEVER self-supplied in tool args. Loopback hub; dashboard requires local
pairing/auth even on loopback; no foreign-config mutation; no raw PTY/free-SQL terminal; secrets are
external refs; uncertain DB outcomes poison/quarantine the connection. Ladder: READ_ONLY < READ_WRITE
< DDL < ADMIN. Never bypass the classifier, never exceed a profile max_level, never make a protected
profile writable, never auto-commit DML, never admit an unproven statement.

## Ground truth that shapes the work (verified — §1, §4-GT)
- Repo at 0.4.1; `oracledb = "=0.5.1"` ALREADY pinned (WP-A = validation, NOT a version bump).
- The fail-closed GUARD ALREADY SHIPS in crates/oraclemcp-guard (classifier 104KB, OperatingLevel
  ladder + DangerLevel, 3-valued purity.rs with a SideEffectOracle port, stepup.rs confirm-token,
  token.rs AllowOnceStore single-use grants). **WP-N builds the per-lane LANE layer OVER the existing
  guard — it does NOT re-implement the classifier.**
- `#4` timeout_ms is already threaded through collect_all_rows/fetch_cursor/read_lob (WP-B = verify +
  shared-layer default + bounded ROLLBACK, not re-plumb).
- plsql-intelligence v0.7.0, ~21 PURE engine crates (no tokio/net) → bake in via (1) the SideEffectOracle
  purity port [safety core, 0.6.0-eligible] and (2) the Workbench IDE [0.6.1].
- Runtime: asupersync 0.3.4 (pinned nightly-2026-05-11 for try_trait_v2). Appendix A of the plan is the
  SOURCE-VERIFIED asupersync API reference every WP-N bead must cite by id; Appendix B is the per-WP
  acceptance-test spec (incl. B.13 edge cases). Pure-Rust, #![forbid(unsafe_code)], no tokio/axum/hyper
  (boundary-linted).

## Sub-epics (one per work package, matching plan §10)
WP-A driver validation · WP-B timeout/poison (#4) · WP-C non-lossy serialization (#3) · WP-R routine
exec (#2) · WP-N per-principal LaneRuntime (THE FOUNDATION) · WP-P operator protocol · WP-S persistent
service · WP-W web dashboard · WP-E installer · WP-F distribution · WP-G hardening/docs · WP-H release.

## Phase-0 release-blockers for 0.6.0 (gate the whole train)
CX-I6 capacity spike (justify 16/8/64 lane caps; lane ≈ 2 OS threads), CX-I7 panic-isolation prototype
(catch_unwind/drop/quarantine/audit), CX-C1 durable write-ahead idempotency (no double-execute across
restart). All under WP-N.

## How to work these beads
Front-load WP-N (N8 → N0a → N0 → …) + the Phase-0 spikes. Every implementation bead names its
applicable D15 cheap-change rule in its DoD and carries an Appendix-B test companion. Use `br ready`
to find unblocked work; `bv --robot-next` to pick. Do NOT weaken the safety invariant.
close_reason: 0.6.x RELEASE TRAIN COMPLETE 2026-07-02: v0.6.6 live on all four channels with the full 0.6.0+0.6.1+0.6.2 scope incl. the one-line install/update UX. npm excluded; H5 operator-owned; deferred (OUT) items remain deferred. Endeavour wrapped up.

title: WP-B — Timeout hardening + poison/quarantine (#4)

Poison: any timeout/network-error/cancel-deadline/rollback-failure/CLOSE-WAIT/unknown-COMMIT → conn poisoned, dropped, never pooled, grants revoked, audit outcome class (rolled_back|discarded_uncommitted|commit_in_doubt|unknown_discarded). oracledb signals: connection_disposition()→Reusable|Dead, is_connection_lost(), CallTimeout/ConnectionClosed. The driver per-op deadline is Query::timeout/Execute::timeout (one deadline spanning continuation fetches + LOB reads). doctor warns when a timeout is 0/unset. Why: #4 is a hang/timeout bug; the budget algebra unifies the three knobs #4 treated separately. DoD: budget threaded; doctor warn; B.2 budget_meet_replaces_three_timers. Edits connection.rs.

title: B1c — poison/quarantine contract (uncertain outcome → never reuse)
description: THE safety contract for uncertain DB outcomes. Any timeout / network error / cancellation-deadline / rollback-failure / CLOSE-WAIT / unknown-COMMIT marks the lane connection POISONED → dropped, never pooled, OPEN GRANTS REVOKED, and the audit records the outcome class: rolled_back | discarded_uncommitted | commit_in_doubt | unknown_discarded. Use the driver signals: error.connection_disposition() → Reusable|Dead, is_connection_lost(), CallTimeout vs ConnectionClosed (drain-fail = lost). Run rollback + the audit append as masked/commit_section finalizers (Appendix A.9) so cleanup completes deterministically under shutdown/cancel. Why: prevents a half-known session from leaking state into the next caller (invariant N5/B1c). DoD: B.2 poisoned_conn_is_never_reused + commit_in_doubt_marks_quarantine. Ties to WP-N N5 + B1c lane teardown.

Transport = MT asupersync runtime; conn ops marshaled to the owning lane thread. Verified against asupersync 0.3.4 (Appendix A): channels A.3, cancel A.4, supervision/AppSpec A.7, name-leases A.8, combinators A.9 (bulkhead per-DB ceiling — NO asupersync Pool exists), Send/!Send seam A.10. title: N5 — lane lifecycle + MCP Streamable-HTTP semantics
description: Distinguish: RESPONSE-STREAM DISCONNECT (does NOT cancel — the call continues to completion / explicit CancelledNotification / budget expiry), EXPLICIT cancellation, HTTP DELETE MCP-Session-Id (terminate the lane: rollback if dirty, revoke grants, release/discard conn — as a MESSAGE to the owning lane thread, C-3), idle TTL, service shutdown (bounded drain). Dropped SSE can reconnect/resume or get a typed expired result. Failed/cancelled/uncertain → quarantine (B1c), never reuse. Record the structured CancelReason/CancelKind (Appendix A.4) in the audit chain (User=DELETE/disconnect, Timeout=B1, Shutdown=drain). DoD: N9-E1..E5 + N9-J (MCP compliance). Depends N1, N4.
notes: N5 implementation complete. Streamable HTTP DELETE invalidates the session, clears buffered replay events, invokes the stateful lifecycle hook, and terminates the lane via an owning-lane Close mailbox command. Listener shutdown drains request workers and then closes all stateful lanes with server_shutdown; runtime drop closes with runtime_drop; lifecycle close releases N4 capacity permits. OracleDispatcher cleanup drops elevation, increments grant generation, clears execute grants/compat grants/patch previews, resets the read-only backstop, rolls back the primary session, and discards the connection by lane exit. Lifecycle audit is structured: audit schema v2 includes hash-covered cancel.kind/cancel.reason, lane_lifecycle records use SQL preview LANE_CLOSE, and close reasons map to User/session_delete, Timeout/idle_timeout, Shutdown/server_shutdown, or Shutdown/runtime_drop. GET replay detects cursors older than the retained per-session ring and returns typed 410 stream_cursor_expired. C-6 proof is implemented: an initialized idle lane parked between mailbox commands wakes and closes from another OS thread; docs record the split between idle mailbox wake and in-flight Oracle call timeout/driver break/socket close plus quarantine/discard. C-1 is implemented: stateful HTTP idle TTL reaping updates last_seen on activity, removes expired replay buffers, and sends Timeout close messages through the lifecycle hook without touching the Oracle connection. title: N6 — stop serializing reads on a global lock (read-worker lanes)
description: Stateless reads run CONCURRENTLY via bounded read-worker lanes (each its own reactor+conn) / per-reactor shards — NOT one shared cross-reactor OraclePool (reactor-affine, CX-1). A read lane is per (Subject, profile, DB) — never a cross-principal pool (CX-C4). Stateful work serializes only within its own lane. DoD: N9-C1 (readers no head-of-line). Depends N0a runtime.
close_reason: Routed served stateless generated metadata reads through bounded per-principal/profile read-worker lanes with profile-switch invalidation; HTTP startup no longer opens the unused shared stateless pool while stdio/direct pool behavior remains intact.

title: N7 — per-Subject audit identity + DB evidence
description: Every action records its VERIFIED Subject (no generic HumanOperator); NO caller-supplied identity (agent_identity/operator_name/label) can change it. Live DB records also capture the redacted DB fingerprint (db_unique_name/service/instance), Oracle username/proxy user, and session evidence (sid, serial#, client_identifier, module, action) when visible; absence → db_evidence_unavailable, not a failure. Depends on FN2 (Subject-aware audit rebuild). DoD: N9-G1..G4 + the headline negative test (a fake agent_identity cannot change the audit subject). Depends N0.
close_reason: Threaded audit records to server-derived subjects, attached best-effort DB evidence under audit schema 3, rejected caller-supplied identity spoofing, and verified full gates.

title: FN2 — Subject-aware audit rebuild (+DB evidence, schema bump)
description: FOUNDATION (before N7). Extend AuditRecord with a structured Subject{kind,stable_id,authn_method,client_id,thumbprint} + DB-evidence columns; preserve/upgrade verify; bump the audit schema_version (additive/format-versioned, never rewrite — DOC-5). Background §4-R: today audit is a free-form agent_identity:String + a single global chain (also a cross-lane p99 serialization point). The audit-chain writer must be transaction-style (build entry in a local, append-and-swap) so a panic mid-append can't corrupt the chain (DL-5). DoD: structured Subject in records; verify still passes across the bump; concurrent appends → valid chain (N9-G2). Prereq for N7/N-S2/W5/G9.
close_reason: Added audit schema_version=2 with structured AuditSubject and optional DbEvidence, kept signed v1 verification compatible, hash-covered v2 subject/evidence fields, hardened audit append buffering/poison handling, and added concurrent append chain verification.

title: FN3 — per-lane telemetry (before W3)
description: FOUNDATION (before W3). Add a per-lane/per-subject label dimension across counters + histograms; a 'blocked' counter; an 'active_lanes' gauge; a per-lane MCP-request latency histogram. Background §4-R: telemetry is process-global bare atomics today. Metrics = a live in-memory ring + append-only per-day history files (FORK-2/D14 — NO TSDB; OTLP export optional). DoD: per-lane metrics emitted; W3 consumes them. Feeds W3/W4 + doctor (DL-10).
close_reason: Implemented per-lane request, blocked, latency, and active-lane telemetry across operator JSON, Prometheus, and OTLP with redacted subject hashes.

title: N-S1 (CRITICAL) — retire the legacy deterministic confirm-MAC
description: CRITICAL. Remove confirmation_mac / verify_commit_confirmation (HMAC over (profile,level,sql), NO caller/lane/nonce — dispatch/mod.rs::confirmation_mac + the compat {sql,token} acceptance, CX-5). The single-use server-side grant (N3) becomes the ONLY confirm path. Why: any lane can recompute another lane's token today → a forgeable cross-lane channel survives even when N9-A4 passes. DoD: confirmation_mac removed; B.5 confirm_mac_retired_cross_lane_recompute_rejected (a lane cannot recompute another's confirm). Depends N3.
close_reason: Retired legacy deterministic confirmation MAC path; session/execute/compile/patch confirmations now use single-use lane-bound grants, with cross-lane rejection tests and docs updated.

title: N-S2 (CRITICAL) — audit ALL committing tools (compile/patch) + classify in compile
description: CRITICAL. Thread AuditCtx into oracle_compile_object + oracle_patch_source and run the classifier in compile. Why: today these commit DDL with NO audit → 'audit = durable record' (N3) is false and W5/W8b/G9 are empty. SEC-3: audit-write failure ⇒ FAIL-CLOSED (refuse the privileged action; the audit sink already fsyncs BEFORE execute — state the contract so no future change makes it best-effort). DoD: every committing tool (execute/compile/patch) appends an audit record; B.5 every_committing_tool_audits; SEC-3 negative test (audit-write-fail refuses). Depends FN2.

description: In handle_tls_connection read peer_certificates(), SHA-256 the leaf DER → CertFingerprint; thread it + peer_addr through HttpRequest→DispatchContext→Subject; require a leaf-fp→registered-client map (any CA-signed cert != identity). Why: today the 'mTLS-fp Subject' source does not exist (http.rs never reads peer_certificates). Enables one of the D11 Subject sources. title: N-S5 — lease stamps server-derived Subject + re-asserts ALTER SESSION allowlist
description: When N0 wires the lease, agent_identity→v$session MUST be the SERVER Subject stable_id (never a tool arg), and the new path RE-CHECKS is_allowed_alter_session itself (do not inherit the lease's trust-the-caller contract, lease.rs:427-437). Why: the dormant oracle_session takes agent_identity as an arg — it must never become the HTTP trust source (D11). title: N0a(i) — lane runtime/thread ownership (tear out shared dispatch_runtime)
description: STRUCTURAL long-pole. Replace today's single shared current-thread dispatch_runtime (server.rs) with THREAD-PER-LANE: each lane = its own OS thread running its own asupersync current-thread Runtime + reactor + pinned !Send Oracle conn (the proven load/soak pattern; non-Send dispatch futures become a non-issue). Transport = a MT asupersync runtime (Appendix A.1; current_thread()=worker_threads(1) so a lane ≈ 2 OS threads — budget that in CX-I6). C-arch: the LaneRuntime is a REGISTRY OF SEND HANDLES (mailboxes), NOT a map of connections — registry-capability NAME LEASES (Appendix A.8), the leased entry is the Send LaneHandle {mpsc::Sender, generation:u64, cancel, JoinHandle, status}, never the conn. Read path = bounded read-worker lanes / per-reactor shards (NOT one shared OraclePool — reactor-affine, CX-1; and asupersync has NO Pool, A.11). Why: Oracle state is per-session; one shared executor funnels everything. DoD: no HTTP/operator stateful dispatch receives process-global DispatcherState; two blocked lanes don't block a third (N9-C1); LeaseManager reached only via LaneRuntime. Cite Appendix A.1/A.8/A.10.
close_reason: Implemented N0a lane ownership: removed OracleMcpServer's shared dispatch_runtime, added core LaneRuntime as a Send mailbox handle around a dedicated OS-thread/current-thread asupersync runtime+reactor, cloned owned DispatchContext across the mailbox, and wired served HTTP stateful dispatch through served-http-stateful while leaving stdio on the direct dispatcher. Added blocked_lane_does_not_block_another_lane proof that a blocked lane does not block an independent lane; DL-1 prototype/ADR remains as Phase-0 decision evidence. Verification: cargo check -p oraclemcp-core; cargo check -p oraclemcp; cargo test -p oraclemcp-core lane::tests::blocked_lane_does_not_block_another_lane -- --nocapture; cargo test -p oraclemcp --test e2e_http_oauth -- --nocapture; focused core server tests; cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test --workspace; cargo deny check; driver/honesty/boundary/api-lock scripts; git diff --check.

title: N-S6 — allow-list-first redaction newtypes for every new surface
description: Allow-list-first redaction for every new surface. (1) BEHAVIOR (0.6.0 default): bind values are REDACTED BY DEFAULT everywhere (audit timeline, proof bundle, logs, telemetry, protocol, UI); an operator REVEAL is explicit and AUDITED (I3 operator-confirmed, supersedes the old FORK-1 operator-sees-everything). There is NO default-off redaction of binds. (2) MECHANISM: redacting newtypes for OracleBind + OracleConnectionInfo; proof bundle/timeline use sql_sha256 NOT sql_preview (or scrub inlined literals, which enter the SIGNED chain today); classify raw ORA- text into a safe envelope; config diff over PARSED allow-listed fields; redact other sessions' v$session; HTML-escape labels/message at render. (3) The configurable RedactionPolicy SEAM (custom per-field/per-role policies, D15) is a future extension and is NOT built for 0.6.0; its absence does not make binds visible (binds stay redacted-by-default regardless). Why: the audit chain is signed, so a leaked literal is permanent. Foundation for N7/W5/W8b/G9/A3/A4. DoD: redaction newtypes; binds redacted by default on EVERY surface; reveal is operator-gated + audited; a test asserts no bind/secret reaches any surface unredacted without an audited reveal. B.11/B.8.

Added protocol/type regression tests proving bind and connection sentinels do not reach rendered surfaces; extended sensitive-data lint and docs; refreshed the intentional oraclemcp-db API baseline. title: N-S7 (CRITICAL) — bind MCP-session-id to the verified Subject
description: CRITICAL. Every stateful request must assert lane.subject == request.subject; NEVER select a lane by session-id alone. Why: today HttpSessionStore is a bare HashSet<String> and the bearer is validated independently of session membership → any valid bearer can present ANOTHER principal's mcp-session-id and both checks pass = cross-principal lane HIJACK (R2). DoD: B.5/B.6 session_id_bound_to_subject (a valid bearer presenting another principal's session-id is rejected). Depends N0.
close_reason: Bound stateful MCP session ids to the server-derived principal key in HttpSessionStore: initialize records the owner, POST and DELETE validate the current principal before accepting a known mcp-session-id, cross-principal replay returns a generic 403 without leaking subject/token material, and the OAuth stateful E2E now covers the hijack case.

title: C-1 — idle/abandoned-lane reaping via a watchdog (message, never touch the conn)
description: reap_expired (lease.rs:447) has ZERO production callers; expiry is lazy. With N5 (disconnect!=cancel), an abandoned dirty lease holds its txn + row locks until process exit. Design: a WATCHDOG sends a terminate/timeout MESSAGE to the lane's mailbox (a lane parked in a DB call is unblocked by call-timeout/OCI-break per B1; a lane parked idle wakes on its mailbox). A central reaper touching the conn is the C-2 bug — forbidden. DoD: abandoned dirty lane reaped via mailbox, row locks released; B.13#3 abandoned_dirty_lane_reaped_via_mailbox. Depends N5, N0aH.
notes: Implementation landed: stateful HTTP now has a configurable stateful_idle_ttl_seconds defaulting to 900 seconds, with 0 disabling reaping. The HTTP accept loop runs a lightweight reaper on a fixed interval, updates session last_seen on activity, removes expired replay/result buffers, and asks the registered HttpSessionLifecycle to close the session with DispatchCloseReason::Timeout. StatefulLaneDispatch implements that lifecycle by removing the lane and sending the timeout close message to the owning lane; the reaper never touches an Oracle connection directly. Timeout close reasons are propagated into structured lifecycle audit metadata as Timeout/idle_timeout. Config docs and the example TOML describe the new setting and the message-only safety rule. Tests cover idle reaper timeout closure plus buffer cleanup, cross-thread idle mailbox wake, timeout audit metadata, and config loading. Verified by cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo test -p oraclemcp-core --lib stateful_idle_reaper_closes_by_timeout_and_clears_buffers, cargo test -p oraclemcp-core --lib idle_lane_mailbox_wakes_for_cross_thread_close, cargo test -p oraclemcp --lib lifecycle_timeout_close_audits_timeout_reason, cargo test -p oraclemcp-config --lib http_oauth_config_loads_and_validates, cargo test -p oraclemcp-core --lib, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace --quiet, cargo deny check, scripts/oraclemcp_api_lock.sh, scripts/oraclemcp_boundary_lint.sh, scripts/sensitive_data_lint.sh, and git diff --check.
close_reason: Implemented idle/abandoned stateful-session reaping by mailbox message: configurable idle TTL, activity tracking, replay-buffer cleanup, Timeout close through HttpSessionLifecycle/StatefulLaneDispatch, and structured Timeout/idle_timeout audit metadata. Reaper never touches the Oracle connection. Verified with focused reaper/wake/audit/config tests, core lib tests, clippy, workspace tests, deny, lints, and diff check.

title: C-4 — Lease/lane epoch (generation u64) + bind grants to it
description: Add a monotonic GENERATION (u64) + lane/subject id to the lane/lease (Lease has none today, lease.rs:144). NOTE (Appendix A.11): this is a PLAIN atomic u64 (published Release, read Acquire — DL-6), NOT asupersync epoch_tracker (which is a scheduler health monitor) and NOT asupersync::epoch (the ATP data layer). Grants (N3) bind to this generation → closes the check-vs-use window on the ceiling (A6/K2/K3). DoD: generation increments on switch_profile/level change; stale grants invalidated; N9-K2/K3. Feeds N3.
close_reason: Added monotonic lane/lease generation primitives and generation-bound execution grant validation. ExecGrantBinding now binds session/lane/subject/generation; stale generation/lane/subject/session mismatch rejects without consuming; LaneRuntime exposes bump_generation; LeaseInfo exposes monotonic generation. Tests: exec_grant, query_execute, lane_generation, acquire_assigns_monotonic_lease_generation. Gates: fmt, affected-crate all-target clippy, api_lock, sensitive_data_lint, boundary_lint, git diff --check.

title: C-5 — switch_profile = atomic conn-swap state machine
description: A lease pins one non-optional conn for life; N1's per-lane switch must ACQUIRE THE NEW profile's permit/conn BEFORE releasing the old (or represent a 'switching' lane state), rolling back to the old on AtCapacity — NEVER strand the lane connection-less. Aligns with K1 'permit released exactly once'. DoD: B.13#3 switch_profile_at_capacity_keeps_old_conn; N9-K1/K2. Depends N1.
close_reason: Made profile switching an explicit prepared-then-commit ownership swap: new connection/stateless/catalog/response preparation completes before dispatcher state is overwritten, commit-side fallible updates run before the infallible swap, and an AT_CAPACITY regression proves the old pinned connection/profile remain usable after a prepared replacement is refused.

title: C-6 — cross-thread cancel of a parked block_on (capability proof)
description: CONFIRM + prove: asupersync can wake a lane parked in block_on on mpsc::recv from another thread (mpsc::Sender::wake_receiver — Appendix A.10, verified for IDLE lanes). A lane INSIDE a blocking Oracle call can only be interrupted by driver OCI-break/call-timeout/socket-close (then treat the conn as suspect → rollback/discard, B1/B1c). asupersync handles idle/async; B1/B1c handle in-flight. DoD: a deterministic test waking an idle parked lane cross-thread; documented in-flight path. Depends N0aH, N5.
notes: Implementation landed while N5 remains in progress: added a deterministic core lane test showing an initialized idle lane parked between mailbox commands wakes and closes from another OS thread via close_with_reason(ServerShutdown), records the close hook reason, and reaches Stopped without external timeout. Documented the split: mailbox wake handles idle lanes; lanes inside Oracle round trips are handled by DB call timeout/driver break/socket close plus quarantine/discard. Verified cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo test -p oraclemcp-core --lib idle_lane_mailbox_wakes_for_cross_thread_close, cargo test -p oraclemcp-core --lib, cargo clippy -p oraclemcp-core --all-targets -- -D warnings, and git diff --check. br close is currently blocked by dependency oraclemcp-epic-060-f4xo.5.10 (N5), so close this bead after N5 closes or after intentionally relaxing that dependency.
close_reason: Implemented the cross-thread idle wake proof: an initialized idle lane parked between mailbox commands wakes and closes from another OS thread via close_with_reason(ServerShutdown), records the close hook reason, and reaches Stopped. Documented the in-flight Oracle path as call timeout/driver break/socket close plus quarantine/discard. Verified with focused wake/core tests, clippy, workspace tests, deny, lints, and diff check.

title: N-M7 — cross-restart exactly-once (consult durable audit before commit)
description: Execute consults the durable AUDIT CHAIN (sql_sha256 + grant id) BEFORE commit to prevent double-execute across restart; document at-least-once where unavoidable. Ties to CX-C1 (durable write-ahead intent). Why: the in-memory ledger doesn't survive a crash — 're-preview is safe' is FALSE for already-committed DML. DoD: B.6 idempotency_key_dedup_and_no_cross_restart_double_execute. Depends N3.

Run a measured Phase-0 spike that derives the shipped defaults from real Oracle sessions + fds + systemd TasksMax + per-thread stack memory (remember: a lane ≈ 2 OS threads — current_thread()=worker_threads(1)+the block_on driver, Appendix A.11) + tail latency. The SHIPPED defaults MUST cite this measurement. DoD: B.5 phase0_capacity_spike (--ignored, measured); defaults justified in code + docs. Gates the whole train. Depends N4, N0aR.

title: CX-I7 (Phase-0 RELEASE-BLOCKER) — panic-isolation prototype
description: RELEASE-BLOCKER. D12 reverses 0.4.0 panic=abort → unwind + per-lane catch_unwind (Cargo.toml still aborts today). PROTOTYPE + PROVE containment BEFORE relying on it: catch_unwind + Drop + quarantine + audit around the lane block_on loop; a lane panic does NOT abort siblings; the conn is dropped/quarantined; unknown_discarded is audited (CX-2: NO rollback promise after panic). DL-5: use parking_lot/asupersync Mutex (non-poisoning), never std::sync::Mutex, since unwind reintroduces poisoning. DoD: B.5 phase0_panic_isolation (E, real cross-OS-thread). Gates the train. Depends N0aR.
