Replaced lane-handle std::sync::Mutex uses with parking_lot non-poisoning locks. Added cross-OS-thread proof lane_panic_is_quarantined_audited_and_sibling_lane_survives plus existing blocked-lane sibling proof. Updated stale abort docs/comments. Verification: cargo test -p oraclemcp-core lane::tests:: -- --nocapture; cargo test -p oraclemcp-guard qualified_udf_call_classify_path_stays_guarded; cargo test -p oraclemcp-telemetry non_ascii_traceparent_is_rejected_not_panicking; cargo check -p oraclemcp; cargo test -p oraclemcp --test e2e_http_oauth -- --nocapture; cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test --workspace; cargo deny check; driver/honesty/boundary/api-lock scripts; git diff --check.

title: CX-C1 (Phase-0 RELEASE-BLOCKER) — durable write-ahead idempotency
description: RELEASE-BLOCKER. Grants/idempotency are in-memory (D14/N3) → a committed DML + restart + client retry could DOUBLE-EXECUTE. Before executing any committing tool, append a durable intent{idempotency_key, subject, lane, sql_hash, ts} to an append-only store (the audit chain / an intents file, fsync-before-execute); on restart, an UNRESOLVED intent ⇒ in-doubt → poison/quarantine + surface, NEVER silently re-execute. If we accept at-least-once anywhere, DOCUMENT it explicitly. DoD: B.5 durable_write_ahead_idempotency_across_restart (committed DML + restart + retry → no double-execute). Gates the train. Depends N3; feeds NM7/P1c.
close_reason: Implemented durable write-ahead intent log for committing tools: fsynced pending intents before DB execution, restart refusal on unresolved intents, safe terminal resolution, focused ordering/in-doubt tests, and operator docs.

title: N0a(ii) — connection-thread↔lane-thread handoff (the message-passing seam)
description: STRUCTURAL. The transport (MT runtime) talks to a lane ONLY by message: a bounded mpsc of {command, oneshot reply} (Appendix A.3; two-phase reserve→SendPermit = obligation-tracked send). The conn is reactor-affine to its lane thread, so EVERY conn op (execute/rollback/terminate/reap/switch) is MARSHALED to the owning lane thread via the control mailbox — a central manager NEVER touches a conn directly (fixes C-2). This is where cancel (A.4), DELETE, and SSE plug in. Transport awaits the reply via async oneshot.recv(cx) — NEVER block_on on a worker thread (DL-2). Mailbox full = backpressure/429 (CastOverflowPolicy), never unbounded (DL-9 forbids unbounded). Cite the lane seam Appendix A.10. DoD: a complete command/reply path with cancel/DELETE plumbed; B.5 transport_responsive_while_lane_blocked_in_db.
close_reason: Implemented bounded lane command/reply admission with non-waiting reserve/commit backpressure, pre-admission cancellation checkpoint, HTTP BUSY-to-429 mapping, and B.5 transport responsiveness coverage while a lane is blocked; semantic DELETE/cancel/reap work remains in the existing dependent N5/DL-6/C-6/C-1 beads.

title: SideEffectOracle binding + SELECT-side-effect tightening (Gap-2)
description: Bind the REAL purity oracle from plsql-intelligence into the guard's existing SideEffectOracle port (purity.rs already declares the seam: trait SideEffectOracle{routine_purity, statement_purity}→default Unknown; UnknownOracle is the engine-free default). Implement it over plsql-depgraph + plsql-lineage::column_writers + the trigger/VPD (DBMS_RLS) walk → upgrades the classifier from syntactic+Unknown-fail-closed to SEMANTICALLY-PROVEN-read-only (fewer false refusals; catches SELECT side-effects via triggers/RLS the SQL never names) and UNLOCKS the deferred Gap-2 SELECT tightening (today a UDF-free SELECT stays Safe under the no-engine oracle; tighten to fail-closed-on-Unknown WITH the engine bound). NON-BLOCKING for 0.6.0 (4-RS steer 2): without it the classifier is still fail-closed (Unknown). DoD: oracle bound on the consumer side; SELECT tightening lands WITH it; B.13#1 sideeffect_oracle_binding_never_loosens (binding never turns a refusal into an admission unless proven read-only). Depends A-plsql (engine deps).
close_reason: Bound plsql-intelligence SideEffectOracle consumer-side with SELECT statement-Unknown tightening, trigger/VPD/lineage tests, and guard API baseline. Gates: fmt, clippy workspace, clippy plsql-intelligence, test workspace, plsql feature tests, cargo deny, boundary/arch/agent/driver/concurrency/honesty/sensitive/api/ergonomics/dashboard-skin/installer lints.

title: Capability-secure lanes — cap::None classifier + narrowed lane Cx
description: Make least-privilege STRUCTURAL (type-enforced, not docs). The fail-closed classifier is PURE → cap::None / no Cx (no spawn/io/random/remote reachable from the security decision). Each lane handler receives a NARROWED Cx (typically time + the lane's own io, NEVER HasRemote/HasSpawn). Widening is COMPILE-TIME rejected. Extends the existing A9 surface (cx::{SubsetOf,HasSpawn,HasRemote,HasRandom,CapSetRuntimeMask}) and the ui/ compile-fail tests (widen_narrowed_cx_rejected.rs, read_handler_cannot_spawn_or_remote.rs) PER-LANE. DoD: classifier is cap::None; lane Cx narrowed; per-lane widen-rejected compile-fail tests. Depends N0.
close_reason: Added lane-specific capability narrowing: LaneCaps/narrow_to_lane, lane-loop checkpoints and mailbox receives now run under the narrowed TIME+IO row, and trybuild fixtures prove a lane context cannot call privileged remote effects or widen back to AllCaps. Verified full workspace tests, clippy, deny, API/boundary/concurrency/sensitive/installer/ergonomics gates.

title: DL-4 — canonical lock order + 'never hold registry lock across a lane send'
description: Define oraclemcp's total lock rank and assert ascending acquisition in debug builds with SAFETY: comments: Config(watch, lock-free read) → Registry → Lane(status) → Lease → Grants → Audit-chain → Metadata-cache. HARD RULE: never hold the Registry lock across a lane send — copy the Send LaneHandle out, drop the registry lock, then reserve/send (the 'registry holds only handles' design enables this; codify it). Prefer the actor/single-owner mailbox model so most shared state has no lock-order graph at all; keep locks only where genuinely shared (config via watch, audit-chain via a single writer). DoD: B.13#3 registry_lane_lock_order_ab_ba_unconstructible (AB-BA debug assert). Depends N0aR.
close_reason: Codified the canonical lane lock order, added debug assertions rejecting lane mailbox close/send/drop while the core registry lock is held, documented the copy-handle-before-send invariant, and added the B.13 AB-BA regression.

title: DL-5 — non-poisoning locks + transaction-style audit writer (D12-unwind safe)
description: D12 (unwind + per-lane catch_unwind) reintroduces std::sync::Mutex POISONING risk. Directives: (a) per-lane catch_unwind maps a panic to Outcome::Panicked → supervisor quarantines+restarts the lane (CX-2); (b) use parking_lot::Mutex (non-poisoning) or asupersync Mutex for shared locks — NEVER std::sync::Mutex; (c) the audit-chain writer is TRANSACTION-STYLE (build entry in a local, append-and-swap) so a panic mid-append can't corrupt the chain (protects N-S2). DoD: panic-injection mid-audit-append leaves the chain valid + verifiable; the DL-9 lint forbids std::sync::Mutex in core. Depends FN2.
close_reason: Implemented non-poisoning audit locks and panic-safe audit append poisoning; added panic regression and lint coverage.

title: DL-6 — level-triggered cancel (no lost wakeups)
description: Cancelling an idle lane parked on mpsc::recv must use LEVEL-TRIGGERED desired-state (a cancel/shutdown flag in the LaneHandle, re-read after each recv/on wake), NOT an edge-triggered notify that can be lost if it lands just before the lane parks. mpsc::Sender::wake_receiver wakes the parked lane; epoch generation published Release/read Acquire (or rely on the channel happens-before). asupersync channels already do waker-dedup + capacity-recheck; the APP rule is 'store desired state, recompute on wake'. DoD: B.13#3 lost_wakeup_cancel_one_step_before_park. Depends N0aH.
close_reason: Implemented level-triggered lane close state with wake_receiver and regression coverage for full-mailbox shutdown preemption.

title: N9 — concurrency/session test contract (SET IN STONE)
description: THE WP-N acceptance contract — SET IN STONE; any regression BLOCKS release (DoD item 2). Each invariant = a named test with structured JSON-line logging (lane/subject/SID/profile/level/grant/outcome). Files: extend tests/{chaos,load_soak,cancel_correctness,live_oracle,trust_safety}.rs; ADD tests/lane_state_machine.rs (deterministic model/fault-injection, no Oracle — asupersync lab, Appendix A.13), tests/concurrency_contract.rs (mock, lab injection + seed-sweep + quiescence/obligation-leak/futurelock oracles + crashpack/seed on failure), tests/multi_lane_live_xe.rs (real 23ai, two DBs — no mocks; mock-risk Score>=8 = cross-lane isolation must be mock-free). Changing any invariant needs a plan change + review. Depends the WP-N impl (N1/N2/N3/N5/N6/N7).

title: DL-1 (Phase-0) — !Send lane-bridge prototype + decision (gates N0a)
description: Phase-0 spike (section 4-SK.1). Prototype the two !Send-correct lane bridges and pick the least-ambiguous: (a) a dedicated OS thread running its own current-thread Runtime::block_on loop that OWNS the !Send Oracle conn, vs (b) spawn_local / LocalStoredTask on a per-lane local scheduler (Appendix A.10). The real Class-2 hazard is block_on NESTED inside an async task or on a runtime worker thread — so the rule is: the lane block_on is the OUTERMOST call on a DEDICATED lane thread, never nested, never on a transport worker. Document the choice with a SAFETY: comment on the lane-loop entry. The lane thread is a supervised worker under AppSpec; block_on is the local !Send execution bridge, not the app architecture. DoD: a measured prototype of both + a written decision recorded in the repo; the chosen bridge informs N0a. Gates N0a runtime. No deps (run first).
close_reason: DL-1 done: added measured Phase-0 lane bridge prototypes in crates/oraclemcp-core/tests/lane_bridge_phase0.rs; dedicated OS-thread/current-thread-runtime bridge accepted for N0a; spawn_local rejected from consumer code due LocalSchedulerUnavailable/private scheduler TLS; recorded ADR 0007; gates passed: fmt, clippy, workspace tests, cargo deny, driver seam, honesty grep, api lock, boundary lint.

title: D17 — operator-authority allow-list (above Subject, never self-claimed)
description: D17. Operator is an authority CAPABILITY ABOVE a regular authenticated Subject (D11) — required for: fleet-wide view, force-actions on other lanes (R3b), bind REVEAL (FORK-1), Change-Proposal approve/apply + 4-eyes, om doctor --fix, and config/cred management. Sources (NEVER a tool arg): the loopback OS-user / local-pairing owner (single-operator default) OR an explicit operator allow-list (verified Subject stable-ids / OAuth subs / mTLS fps) in config. BINARY in 0.6.0 (operator vs scoped principal); fine-grained operator-RBAC is a deferred non-goal (N4). Every operator action is audited under the Subject; a scoped principal can NEVER escalate to operator. DoD: operator authority resolved from config/owner only; a scoped-principal-cannot-act-as-operator negative test; every operator action audited. Depends N7 (Subject).
close_reason: Implemented server-derived operator authority for /operator/v1 using loopback local-owner or configured subject allow-list, required audit before operator routing, and proved scoped principals cannot self-claim operator.

title: N4b — finalize shipped capacity defaults from the CX-I6 measurement
description: Codex round-4 finding 3: the capacity dependency was backwards — N4's body says the 16/8/64 defaults are JUSTIFIED by CX-I6, but CX-I6 depended on N4, which would let the impl bake defaults before the Phase-0 measurement (§4-CX.1/§7). title: N0 — wire the lease layer behind LaneRuntime
description: Wire the dormant LeaseManager (lease.rs) BEHIND LaneRuntime: each MCP session + verified Subject → a distinct LaneContext + distinct lease; transport never touches LeaseManager directly. The lease is the PHYSICAL session; the lane is the SECURITY+CONCURRENCY boundary. stdio path UNCHANGED (N10). DoD: stateful requests resolve to a LaneContext owning {lane id, verified Subject, MCP-session id, profile, DB fingerprint, level state, grant store, request budget, cancel, audit ctx}; N9-E4 LeaseRequired for a stateful op without a lane.
close_reason: Implemented the N0 stateful lane boundary: HTTP dispatch context now carries MCP-session id plus a server-derived principal key; stateful dispatch fails closed with LeaseRequired without a session-bound context; StatefulLaneDispatch is now a registry of LaneRuntime handles keyed by (MCP-session-id, principal), with dispatcher construction happening on each lane's own runtime via a factory; production stateful HTTP uses that factory-backed registry and stdio remains direct. Per-profile DB/profile isolation, per-lane level state, lane-bound grants, and subject-aware audit remain in the existing dependent N1/N2/N3/N7/N-S* beads.

title: N4c — fair queued stateful admission
description: Residual split from N4 after the pre-connection admission mechanism landed. Implement bounded per-subject queues plus global weighted fairness / brief wait before AT_CAPACITY for stateful lane admission. Keep the current invariants: acquire admission before any lane thread or physical Oracle connection opens; no unbounded queues or waits; operator/doctor reserve cannot be consumed by regular agent flood; diagnostics remain redacted. DoD: N9-D fairness tests prove one subject cannot starve another or the reserved operator/doctor path, and AT_CAPACITY still carries retry_after_ms plus a redacted snapshot.
close_reason: Implemented bounded fair stateful-lane admission: per-subject/global queued caps, round-robin subject turns with brief bounded wait before AT_CAPACITY, permit-drop/drain notifications, and lane allocation fallback that waits outside the registry lock while preserving pre-factory admission. Added fairness/redaction tests and verified full workspace gates.

title: N1 — per-lane connection + per-lane database/profile
description: Each lane owns its conn to the profile IT selected; two lanes → two DBs concurrently; switch_profile affects ONLY the calling lane; the service may hold many DBs at once (pooled per profile, bounded). DoD: N9-B1 (A→X & B→Y concurrent, correct DB each) + N9-B2 (switch_profile affects only A). Depends N0.
close_reason: Implemented N1 coverage: stateful HTTP lanes now prove independent per-lane profile/connection ownership, concurrent A->X and B->Y switches, and A-only later switch isolation.

title: N2 — per-lane operating level + elevation
description: SessionLevelState PER-LANE: A's elevation never affects B; OAuth scope narrows ONLY the calling lane; protected/standby stays READ_ONLY while a sibling is elevated. DoD: N9-A2 (level never leaks) + N9-A3 (elevation TTL independent) + N9-B3 (per-lane ceiling). Depends N0.
close_reason: Verified per-lane operating level isolation over stateful HTTP: the lane factory creates a fresh OracleDispatcher/SessionLevelState per MCP-session+principal lane; a new E2E proves agent A can elevate to READ_WRITE without changing agent B's lane, and a read-scoped request on A's lane sees a lowered effective level without permanently lowering the stored lane state.

title: N3 — single-use, lane-bound grant store (confirm/execute/cursors)
description: Server-side grant store replacing stateless tokens. Preview/confirm mints a grant with {grant_id, lane_id, verified subject_id, MCP-Session-Id, profile_id, profile_revision, DB fingerprint, level GENERATION, SQL SHA-256, classifier-result digest, issued/expiry, action}. The returned token is only an opaque signed reference. EXECUTE CONSUMES THE GRANT EXACTLY ONCE; a retry with the same idempotency key returns the recorded outcome; a second fresh execution → GrantAlreadyConsumed; a grant minted by A is rejected for B, after switch_profile, or after a level/profile generation change. Store + idempotency ledger are in-memory/process-local; the AUDIT HASH-CHAIN is the durable record (a grant lost on restart simply forces re-preview — safe). Builds on the existing guard token.rs AllowOnceStore. DoD: N9-A4 (grant non-replay) + N9-A6 (generation binding); B.5 grant_single_use_lane_bound_generation_bound. Depends N0a handoff.
close_reason: Wired server-side execution grants into the live preview/execute path. LaneRuntime now attaches lane id/generation to DispatchContext; oracle_preview_sql, execute_approved, deploy_ddl, and create_or_replace mint signed opaque references backed by ExecGrantStore; oracle_execute consumes exactly once and validates statement/profile/session/lane/principal/generation before audit/DB execution. Session-level/profile changes bump dispatcher grant generation and clear in-process grants. Added tests for lane-bound non-consumption, generation invalidation, one-shot race, registry routing, and create/deploy compatibility. Verification: fmt, oraclemcp lib tests, oraclemcp-core lib tests, oraclemcp-guard lib tests, affected all-target clippy, api_lock, sensitive_data_lint, boundary_lint, git diff --check.

title: N4 — adaptive bounded capacity + fairness + fail-closed + operator reserve
description: Two-tier caps: per-profile READ pool + stateful/write lanes, plus a global host ceiling. Defaults 16 read / 8 stateful per profile / 64 global (UPPER BOUNDS); startup/doctor compute EFFECTIVE caps = min(configured, DB per-user/session limit, fd limit, memory budget). Reserve >=1 operator + >=1 doctor lane. ACQUIRE A PERMIT BEFORE OPENING A PHYSICAL CONN (Appendix A.9 combinator::bulkhead — obligation-tracked, leak-detected; backed by an mpsc token-bucket; NOTE: asupersync has NO Pool, A.11/DL-7). At capacity → brief wait then typed AtCapacity + retry_after_ms + redacted snapshot — never unbounded sessions. Fairness = per-subject queues + global weighted fairness; idle reaping; DRCP + proxy-auth for scale. DoD: N9-D1..D6; B.5/B.13#3. Depends N1. The 16/8/64 numbers are JUSTIFIED by CX-I6.
close_reason: Implemented the N4 admission mechanism: read-pool default 16, served stateful lane admission before lane thread/Oracle connection creation, 8-per-principal/64-host defaults with operator+doctor regular-capacity reserve, typed AT_CAPACITY retry_after/redacted snapshot, HTTP 429 Retry-After mapping, API baseline, docs, and focused tests. Residual finalized effective caps/default citation, transport accept caps, lifecycle/idle reap, and queued weighted fairness remain tracked by N4b/N4+/N5/N4c and N9.

title: N4+ — bound the accept/connection-thread + SSE layer (transport capacity, CX-4)
description: Codex CX-4: enforce capacity + the operator reserve at the TRANSPORT layer (max in-flight connections + accept backpressure; separately cap + idle-timeout operator/SSE connections — they aren't lanes) BEFORE any Oracle session — else an HTTP/SSE flood starves the operator lane without opening a single DB session. Background: http.rs spawns a thread per accept, uncapped. DoD: accept-layer bounded; SSE subscriber cap; N9-D5 read-flood-can't-starve-operator (at the transport layer too). Depends N0a runtime.
close_reason: Bound HTTP accept workers and Streamable HTTP SSE subscribers with admission caps and redacted backpressure responses.

title: WP-P — Operator protocol (versioned, schema-first)
description: WP-P sub-epic. ONE versioned schema-first protocol over asupersync HTTP: MCP (/mcp, per-lane) + /operator/v1 (read-only stats/events/SSE + gated actions). Generated schema bundle; event-replay (Last-Event-ID in a bounded ring, never cross-lane); idempotency ledger (P1c) + durable write-ahead (CX-C1). Prereqs: FN0 transport/router redesign (precedence, query-string, tool-exec off the POST handler) + FN1 streaming SSE. N-S7 session↔Subject binding. SPA imports generated TS types; CI validates captured fixtures vs the Rust schema. Tests = Appendix B.6. P2 operator UDS DEFERRED.

The only remaining child, oraclemcp-epic-060-f4xo.6.9, is explicitly DEFERRED P2 operator UDS/future native-client work and is not a release blocker.

title: FN0 (STRUCTURAL, before P1) — transport/router redesign
description: STRUCTURAL prereq for the operator surface. Today: a flat exact-match ladder (path not-equal /mcp returns 404, http.rs:1279), the QUERY STRING is discarded (split('?').next(), :1780; HttpRequest has no query field), and the tool call runs SYNCHRONOUSLY inside the POST handler (connection: close, no GET stream, no result buffer). Add: a router with PRECEDENCE (typed-404 API routes vs SPA history-fallback index.html — a mistyped /operator/v1 route must NOT return 200 HTML, R1); QUERY-STRING PARSING for /operator/v1 cursor + W5 filters (R6); move tool execution OFF the POST handler ONTO the lane thread with a result buffer/stream (R3) so N5 disconnect-is-not-cancel + reconnect/resume has a substrate (ties to the N0a handoff + FN1). Also content-type/Accept negotiation + 406 (R7); DELETE on a stateless server returns 405 not a false 202 (R8). DoD: router precedence + query parsing + off-handler exec; B.13 part 4 protocol negatives. Prereq for P1/FN1.
close_reason: FN0 transport/router redesign landed: native HTTP now preserves parsed query strings, routes explicitly with reserved typed-json /operator/v1 API 404s, guards operator routes, enforces /mcp Accept and Content-Type negotiation, returns 405 for stateless DELETE, and adds a bounded stateful result buffer with GET replay by cursor/Last-Event-ID. Existing stateful POST behavior remains compatible while dispatch continues through lane runtimes and responses are buffered as the substrate for later SSE/disconnect-resume. Evidence: http.rs protocol-negative/unit tests, conformance coverage update, docs updated; cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test --workspace; cargo deny check; API lock; boundary lint; sensitive-data lint; git diff --check.

title: P-rate — per-caller request-rate limiter via asupersync RateLimiter
description: Revives the request-rate half of deferred k6q.11 for the 0.6.0 HTTP/operator ingress. Wrap the served HTTP/operator boundary in asupersync::combinator::RateLimiter keyed only by server-derived, bounded-cardinality principal buckets. It complements N4/N4+ concurrency/backpressure and must not use raw bearer tokens, raw OAuth subs, request IDs, or caller-supplied identity as the limiter key. Out of scope: optimizer/query-cost budgets, which remain deferred separately. DoD: per-principal throttle tests, bounded-cardinality/key-redaction tests, Retry-After/AT_CAPACITY or BUSY mapping, operator/doctor access not starved, docs/behavior-inventory updated.
close_reason: Implemented per-principal HTTP/operator request-rate limiting with bounded redacted buckets, Retry-After/AT_CAPACITY responses, tests, and docs.

title: FN1 (before P1) — streaming SSE transport
description: Real chunked/long-lived response + a server-push channel with a BOUNDED per-subscriber ring buffer + slow-consumer DROP + gap-marker, and Last-Event-ID resume. Today SSE is 2 events in one write (http.rs:1479-1532). Implement with asupersync broadcast/watch (Appendix A.3). P1/P1b/W3/N5 depend on this. SSE GET auth = SameSite=Strict cookie + MANDATORY Origin + guard_http_request + subject-verified Last-Event-ID (EventSource cannot send bearer/CSRF). DoD: streaming SSE + bounded ring + resume; B.13 part 4 sse-slow-drop. Depends FN0.
notes: 2026-06-30 final implementation: served GET /mcp SSE now uses HTTP/1.1 Transfer-Encoding: chunked and stays long-lived. HttpResultStore provides a bounded 128-event retained ring per session; connected subscribers wait on append/delete/shutdown, replay from cursor/Last-Event-ID, and receive event: stream-gap when a slow consumer resumes behind retention. Query cursor expiry still fails closed with 410. Stateful initialize now also issues an HttpOnly SameSite=Strict oraclemcp_mcp_session cookie. Cookie-authenticated SSE GET requires Origin, still passes guard_http_request Origin allowlisting, can replay under OAuth without Authorization for EventSource, and header-only GET without bearer remains 401. Implementation intentionally uses the existing blocking native transport plus Condvar wakeups instead of adding new async/web deps; boundary lint confirms tokio/hyper/reqwest remain absent. Proofs added/extended: served_stateful_get_streams_chunked_sse_until_session_closes, stateful_get replay/expiry/gap tests, stateful_initialize_sets_strict_session_cookie, oauth_stateful_get_accepts_strict_cookie_with_origin_only, golden HTTP behavior, and served OAuth stateful tests. Gates passed: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo test -p oraclemcp-core --lib; cargo test -p oraclemcp-core --test golden_behavior -- http; cargo test -p oraclemcp --test e2e_http_oauth -- stateful; cargo clippy -p oraclemcp-core --all-targets -- -D warnings; scripts/oraclemcp_boundary_lint.sh; scripts/sensitive_data_lint.sh; scripts/oraclemcp_api_lock.sh; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test --workspace --quiet; cargo deny check; git diff --check.
close_reason: Implemented streaming SSE transport: chunked long-lived GET, bounded retained event ring with slow-consumer stream-gap and Last-Event-ID resume, shutdown/delete wakeups, and EventSource cookie/Origin OAuth path; full gates passed.

title: P1 — define + version /mcp + /operator/v1 (schema-first)
description: Define the versioned protocol: (a) MCP for agents (per-lane); honors MCP-Protocol-Version (unsupported returns typed 400). (b) read-only OPERATOR channel — metrics/health/audit-tail/active-lanes + optional v$session summary (redacted, privilege-scoped, source = self_lane|monitor_profile|unavailable) via SSE + REST under /operator/v1. (c) GATED-ACTION routes (preview/confirm/execute, set-level, switch-profile) mapping to the same per-lane guarded dispatch. Carries a protocol version + a GENERATED machine-readable schema bundle (operator.schema.json + route/event schemas); every event has event_seq, event_id, lane_id, subject_id_hash, redaction_level, schema_version. The SPA imports generated TS types; CI validates captured UI fixtures against the Rust schema. DoD: B.6 mcp_and_operator_v1_conformance_matrix (MUST coverage at least 0.95) + ui_fixtures_validate_against_rust_schema. Depends FN0, FN1 (and WP-N — cross).
close_reason: Implemented versioned MCP/operator v1 protocol, generated schema and TypeScript artifacts, UI fixture validation, and B.6 conformance matrix.

title: P1b — event replay/resume (bounded ring, never cross-lane)
description: /operator/v1/events supports Last-Event-ID/cursor resume within a bounded ring buffer; NEVER replays another subject/lane; payloads stay redacted. DoD: B.6 sse_replay_never_crosses_lane. Depends P1.
close_reason: Implemented bounded /operator/v1/events replay/resume with subject+lane isolation, stale cursor handling, docs, and conformance coverage.

title: P1c — idempotency ledger for gated actions
description: preview/confirm/execute/commit/rollback/set-level/switch-profile take or derive an idempotency key; the ledger stores request id, lane, subject, grant, SQL hash, audit seq, timestamps, outcome. Same key returns the original result or a typed in-progress; a different key cannot reuse a consumed grant. Define key DERIVATION for non-SQL actions (set-level/switch-profile) with a generation/sequence component. Pairs with CX-C1 (durable write-ahead) + N-M7 (consult the durable audit before commit) so a committed DML cannot double-execute across restart. DoD: B.6 idempotency_key_dedup_and_no_cross_restart_double_execute. Depends P1 (+ CX-C1/N3 cross).
close_reason: Implemented operator v1 gated-action idempotency: explicit/derived keys, in-progress/conflict responses, same-key replay without re-dispatch, generated UI fixture/types, and B.6 coverage.

title: P-Outcome — preserve asupersync Outcome to the HTTP edge
description: From section 4-AS.2: carry asupersync Outcome (the four-valued severity lattice Ok then Err then Cancelled then Panicked, Appendix A.6) lane to dispatch to transport, collapsing ONLY at the MCP/HTTP policy boundary: Cancelled maps to 499, Panicked maps to 500 plus page-supervision, Err maps to a domain error. Do NOT flatten to a plain Result-of-String at the first adapter. Why: Cancelled (client gone / shutdown / timeout) is NOT an error — it changes audit/retry/drain; Panicked must page. DoD: Outcome preserved end-to-end; the boundary mapping tested. Depends P1.
close_reason: Preserved asupersync Outcome through dispatch lanes and mapped HTTP boundary outcomes.

DoD: refusals carry next-steps; tools/list reflects the effective ceiling; B.6/B.11. Depends P1.

title: WP-S — Persistent always-on service
description: WP-S sub-epic. Service = an asupersync AppSpec supervision tree (A.7): children transport/lane-registry-supervisor/audit-writer/metrics/dashboard-API; RestForOne ordered (audit-writer before transport), OneForOne lanes; AppHandle as obligation (stop→join, never drop). service install|uninstall|status|logs|restart (systemd --user + enable-linger / launchd / Windows); sd_notify(READY=1)→/readyz; single-instance guard (no silent takeover); mimalloc; safe config reload/drain (S5); file-store crash/concurrency/path-safety (CX-I5); om backup/restore (§4-GT.6). Persistence files-first, pure-Rust, NEVER SQLite (D14). Tests = Appendix B.7.
close_reason: All WP-S implementation and B.7 acceptance beads are closed; full workspace gates and focused service acceptance checks pass.

title: S-AppSpec — model the service as an asupersync AppSpec supervision tree
description: From section 4-AS.2: the always-on service is an AppSpec supervision tree (root region), NOT a bare RuntimeBuilder+block_on (Appendix A.7). Children: transport (HTTP/SSE accept), lane-registry/supervisor, audit-chain writer, metrics/health collector, dashboard-API. RestartPolicy encodes dependency shape: lanes independent use OneForOne; ordered children (audit-writer before transport accepts; registry before lanes) use RestForOne; SupervisionStrategy (Stop, Restart(RestartConfig{max_restarts,window,backoff}), or Escalate) is a SEPARATE decision from RestartPolicy. The lane registry = registry-capability NAME LEASES (A.8), not an ambient HashMap. Hold the AppHandle as an OBLIGATION — graceful shutdown (S5) = AppHandle::stop then join, NEVER drop. DoD: B.7 appspec_topology_starts_in_dep_order_and_drains (lab); removes the hand-rolled startup/shutdown + watchdog. Depends N0aR (cross).
notes: S-AppSpec progress extended: the service_app module now exposes ServiceAppRuntime plus ServiceAppStartError and start_oraclemcp_service_app(), using RuntimeBuilder::current_thread().block_on to obtain a production-visible current Cx instead of the test-only Cx::new seam. HTTP/HTTPS serve starts this AppSpec obligation before binding and always calls AppHandle::stop then join after the transport loop exits or errors; startup/shutdown failures are reported fail-closed. Added service_app_runtime_resolves_app_handle_obligation alongside appspec_topology_starts_in_dep_order_and_drains, so the lab now covers topology order, RestForOne restart suffixes, registry propagation, synthetic drain, and the public start/stop wrapper. Verified cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo test -p oraclemcp-core --lib service_app, cargo clippy -p oraclemcp-core --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo clippy -p oraclemcp --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, scripts/oraclemcp_boundary_lint.sh, scripts/sensitive_data_lint.sh, scripts/oraclemcp_api_lock.sh, cargo test --workspace --quiet, cargo deny check, and git diff --check. Still not closed: the HTTP accept loop and idle reaper remain native code outside an asupersync transport child; S-AppSpec is not complete until the transport child owns that lifecycle or the bead is deliberately narrowed.
close_reason: Implemented S-AppSpec: service_app now defines the oraclemcp-service AppSpec topology with audit, metrics, lane-registry, dashboard, and transport children; RestForOne ordering and per-child strategies are covered by appspec_topology_starts_in_dep_order_and_drains. Production HTTP/HTTPS serve now binds first, hands the listener to ServiceTransport, starts it via start_oraclemcp_service_app_with_transport as the AppSpec transport child, waits on the transport child, then resolves the AppHandle obligation with stop_and_join; main no longer calls the serve loop directly. Added tests for public AppHandle start/stop and AppSpec-owned HTTP accept-loop shutdown. Verified cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo test -p oraclemcp-core --lib service_app, cargo clippy -p oraclemcp-core --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo clippy -p oraclemcp --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, scripts/oraclemcp_boundary_lint.sh, scripts/sensitive_data_lint.sh, scripts/oraclemcp_api_lock.sh, cargo test --workspace --quiet, cargo deny check, and git diff --check.

title: D18 — SecretResolver seam (Oracle creds = external refs, never persisted/rendered)
description: D18. Oracle DB credentials are EXTERNAL REFERENCES resolved at connect, never stored by oraclemcp. The profile config holds a reference — an env-var name, a file path (wallet dir / key file), or an OS-keyring entry — resolved at connect via a pluggable SecretResolver seam (D15 rule 2: trait seam where change is expected; future vault/OCI-secrets plug in). The raw secret never enters the config file, audit chain, logs, telemetry, protocol, or UI (the N-S6 redaction newtypes enforce non-serialization). Generalizes the existing credential_ref/wallet_password_ref (env:/literal:) resolution. Literal credentials rejected on protected profiles. DoD: SecretResolver trait + env/file/keyring impls; a test that no resolved secret is serialized into ANY surface; protected rejects literal. No deps (config/db layer).
close_reason: Implemented SecretResolver seam and threaded connect-time resolution through profile, audit, HTTP, and lane paths; added redaction/leak tests and sensitive-data lint coverage.

title: 0.4.x to 0.6.0 migration (additive config + audit format_version + doctor-assisted)
description: The 0.4.x to 0.6.0 migration story (section 4-GT.6). Config is additive/schema-first (D15): new fields (monitor_profile, dashboard_ddl_workbench, dashboard_workbench) bump schema_version with a migration note. The audit-chain JSONL is append-only + format-versioned: the existing chain continues; a format_version guards any change — NEVER rewrite (DOC-5). New state dirs (the XDG state dir oraclemcp) are created on first run. om doctor detects a LEGACY layout and OFFERS migration (doctor-assisted, scoped, reversible). All file formats follow the same additive discipline so each train upgrades in place. DoD: a clean 0.4.x to 0.6.0 upgrade with no data loss; doctor detects+migrates a legacy layout; an upgrade test covers it. Depends SFILE (new layout), FN2 (audit format_version).
close_reason: Implemented additive config schema v2 fields, XDG audit default migration, and doctor-assisted legacy audit layout migration

title: S-file — file-store crash/concurrency/security contract (CX-I5)
description: D14 persistence = files-first, pure-Rust, NEVER SQLite. The file-store contract (CX-I5): atomic write-tmp-then-rename + fsync(file) + fsync(dir); a MANDATORY single-writer SERVICE LOCK for every mutation; CRASH RECOVERY (skip/repair a torn tail, rebuild the index); retention/rotation for prunable data (metrics; NEVER audit); PATH SAFETY — never interpolate untrusted profile/author names into a path; use sanitized, length-bounded, or content-HASHED IDs (the proposals dir keyed by profile and author is otherwise a traversal vector). Layout under the XDG state dir oraclemcp. DoD: B.7 file_store_atomic_fsync_lock_path_safe. Foundation for W2/SCFG/SBAK/audit/metrics/proposals.
close_reason: Added oraclemcp-core file_store foundation: XDG state root, content-hashed StoreId, service lock token, atomic temp/fsync/rename/fsync-dir writes, JSONL tail recovery/index rebuild, prunable retention with audit refusal, path/permission tests, and operations docs.

Metrics files are prunable by retention (CX-I5); the audit chain is never pruned. DoD: B.7 backup_restore_verifies_audit_chain. Depends SFILE.

title: [09x] Alien horizon — govern every dimension (0.9.x epic)
description:
ALIEN HORIZON — the 0.9.x epic. Overarching thesis: every other database tool governs what an
agent may RUN; this project governs every DIMENSION of the agent-database interaction and proves
each one. The horizon extends the fail-closed guard to govern a new dimension (cost, time, egress,
proof, policy) or make a new kind of read safe (living-DB, governed RAG, lineage, fleet reach,
reversible preview) per release.

DOCTRINE (binding on every child bead): (1) nightly Rust + asupersync stay; (2) the guard never
admits the unproven — Guarded to Safe only via a reviewed, mutation-gated proven-pure builtin
admission or the audited operator allow_list; (3) no new admission surface: every new arc tool is
classifier-gated like oracle_query or routed through the existing step-up/single-use-grant path;
SEC-1 re-classify at execution (never trust a stored verdict); SEC-3 audit-write failure fails
closed; a privileged op issued as a server-side API call (CQN registration, DBMS_FLASHBACK session
state, edition switch) is invisible to the text classifier and must be gated as a first-class
privileged action; (4) forbid unsafe_code; (5) verified-not-claimed — no bare superlatives.

STRUCTURE: 14 arc sub-epics (G cost, A time, M egress, B proof, N policy; C living-DB, F governed
RAG, K lineage, H fleet, I reversible; D editions; E incident-capture, J corpus; L console face).
Every arc depends on the GUARD-SOUND gate. Full implementation specs (tool schemas, exact files,
SQL, tests, child-bead decomposition) live in docs/plan/PLAN_0_8_x_ALIEN.md Appendix I; each child
bead below restates the essentials so it stands alone.
close_reason: All alien child epics and leaf beads are closed.

title: [09x][GATE] GUARD-SOUND — Waves 0-1 done + mutation-gate >= 90 re-verified
description:
GUARD-SOUND GATE — the single universal upstream of every 0.9.x arc. No alien arc may ship until
the fail-closed guard is provably sound again after the post-0.8.0 audit.

CLOSES WHEN: (a) Wave-0 server 0.8.1 P0 guard/config fixes land (QA100 P0 set: never default
parsed-but-unmatched DDL to READ_WRITE; enforce the ALTER SESSION allowlist on raw execution; do
not admit unproven view/policy side effects; fail closed on opaque PL/SQL package calls; forbid
transaction control inside caller PL/SQL; the profile immutable-generation fix; plus the newer
resolve-CALL-targets and zero-arg-identifier P0s); (b) Wave-1 server 0.8.2-0.8.4 P1 security train
lands; (c) the mutation-safety gate is re-run and stays enforcing at >= 90 percent for
oraclemcp-guard and oraclemcp-audit (docs/quality/mutation-safety.md marker).

WHY A GATE NODE: turns "is the guard sound yet?" into one dependency check instead of a hand-audit
of the ~50-bead QA100 campaign. This bead depends on the QA100 epic; every arc sub-epic depends on
this bead. The QA100/DRVQA campaigns are a PARALLEL TRACK owned elsewhere — this plan only waits on
them; do not schedule that work here.

ACCEPTANCE: this bead is closed only after the QA100 P0+P1 beads are closed and a fresh
mutation-gate report shows guard >= 90 and audit >= 90 with status enforcing.
acceptance_criteria: Close ONLY after the QA100 P0 (6) + P1 (44) beads are closed AND a fresh scripts/mutation_safety_gate.sh run shows oraclemcp-guard>=90 and oraclemcp-audit>=90 with status=enforcing. Do NOT wait on QA100 P2/P3 (Wave-3 cleanup/perf) — that is a non-blocking parallel track. This gate is the single upstream every 0.9.x arc depends on.
close_reason: QA100 is closed; docs/quality/mutation-safety.md now records enforcing guard=95.0 audit=90.7 threshold=90; scripts/mutation_safety_gate.sh check-report passed after fresh guard and audit mutation runs.

Derivative by design — H adds REACH, not a new capability class; it is A (diff) + C2 (orient) + M
(egress) lifted across the per-principal lane fleet. Every hop is still classifier-gated per lane;
federation adds reach, never admission surface. Partial-fleet failure degrades to a per-DB
UNREACHABLE / FAIL-CLOSED status (the console already models this). Children: H1-H3.

title: [09x][I] The reversible workspace
description:
Make the whole session an agent-visible undo tree, built on primitives that already exist: DML rolls
back by default, leases savepoint, and the single-use grant path (exec_grant.rs) gates commit.
Named checkpoints = native Oracle SAVEPOINT; preview = execute-in-sandbox then ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT
then present, commit re-classifies (SEC-1). Autonomous txns / sequences (NEXTVAL) / triggers ESCAPE
rollback and must be labeled honestly (the class of closed P0 .79). Children: I1-I3.
close_reason: Arc I complete: all four children closed and landed (88fbc59 I1, 6b47aec I2, 0c0e4bd I3, e948dc0 I-E2E). The session is now an agent-visible undo tree: oracle_checkpoint = native SAVEPOINT, oracle_undo_to = ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT (or a full discard), oracle_execute hold=true holds reversible DML pending between them, and oracle_preview_dml dry-runs a statement in a server-owned savepoint sandbox and takes it back. The epic's stated risk - autonomous txns / sequences / triggers ESCAPE rollback - is handled by REFUSING rather than mislabeling: hold refuses a statement whose effect escapes rollback, preview_dml refuses to dry-run one (a dry run must not cause what it cannot take back; live-verified the sequence never advances), and a rolled-back NEXTVAL execute now returns cannot_undo + fully_reverted=false instead of a bare rolled_back=true that reads as 'nothing happened'. The load-bearing tightening: COMMIT is transaction-wide, so while the workspace holds work every committing path is refused before the grant is consumed - held, ungranted DML can never ride another statement's commit into permanence. Commit re-classifies the exact statement (SEC-1), pinned by tests. Proven on Oracle XE 18c, XE 21c, and Free 23ai via scripts/e2e/reversible.sh, with the signed audit chain verified per lane. Two follow-ups filed, not deferred: oraclemcp-8s77 (P0, READ_ONLY snapshot staleness found live by this arc's e2e; pane 2 is fixing it) and oraclemcp-wqg3 (e2e registration, blocked on another agent's unlanded time_diff.sh).

New dispatch/workspace.rs owns the stack + the savepoint-name allowlist (Oracle has no bind for a savepoint name, so that IS the injection boundary; tested exhaustively over the byte space). Tighten-only: while the workspace is open every committing path is refused before the grant is consumed (commit=true, implicitly-committing DDL through execute/compile/patch) because COMMIT is transaction-wide and would carry ungranted held DML into permanence; the transaction-resetting diagnostics (EXPLAIN PLAN cost estimation, flashback as_of/diff) are refused rather than silently destroying held work; a backstop re-arm / profile switch clears the belief with the transaction. description:
Arc I (reversible). SCOPE: oracle_preview_dml{sql,binds} runs the DML in the rollback sandbox,
captures affected rows (count + RETURNING where available), ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT, and presents
before/after; labels effects it CANNOT undo (sequences/triggers/autonomous txns) via the classifier's
non_transactional_effect. ACCEPTANCE: preview shows before/after for a reversible DML and a labeled
cannot-undo for a sequence-touching one; test. DEPENDS: I1.
close_reason: oracle_preview_dml: SAVEPOINT OMCP_PREVIEW_DML -> witness read -> DML -> witness read -> ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT, then present. Sandbox savepoint is the newest, so a dry run nests inside an open workspace without disturbing checkpoints or held work; with no workspace open it ends the transaction outright (same posture as a commit=false execute). CANNOT-UNDO IS A REFUSAL, NOT A LABEL-AND-RUN: a classifier-proven non_transactional_effect (sequence NEXTVAL) is never executed - live-verified the sequence is not advanced - and comes back labeled cannot_undo with the reason. before/after comes from an optional witness SELECT proven read-only by the same classifier (not a side door; a DELETE-as-witness is refused before the sandbox opens). Preview mints NO grant: committing still re-classifies + re-gates the exact statement via oracle_execute (SEC-1). Reserved the OMCP_ savepoint prefix so no agent checkpoint can move/erase the sandbox. Audits as RolledBack (the enum's documented 'savepoint preview'). ACCEPTANCE MET: 5 new unit tests (295 green in -p oraclemcp, clippy -D warnings clean) + 2 new live-xe tests PASSING against Oracle 23ai (before/after rows shown, table left at committed baseline; refused sequence preview left the sequence at 1). title: [09x][E0] Design spike — incident artifact manifest schema
description:
Arc E (capture). SELF-CONTAINED FIRST BEAD (spike). OUTPUT CONTRACT: the bundle manifest. RESOLVED:
an om incident capture bundle = a dir of { manifest.json (seed, lane-ids, versions), cassettes/ (K6
format), config.redacted.toml, audit-tail.redacted.jsonl }; om incident replay <bundle> runs under
LabRuntimeTarget with the seed. ACCEPTANCE: a committed manifest schema note enumerating the bundle
layout and the fields; all contents pass the Arc-M/redaction seam. DEPENDS: gate (entry).
close_reason:
Incident-artifact manifest schema shipped in commit 5eb0358. Files: crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/incident.rs (new, the schema), src/lib.rs (module + re-exports), tests/incident_manifest.rs (new, 17 tests), docs/adr/0011-incident-artifact-manifest.md (new — the committed schema note the AC asks for), docs/adr/README.md (index).

BUNDLE LAYOUT (as the bead resolved it): <bundle>/manifest.json + cassettes/<lane-id>.jsonl (K6) + config.redacted.toml + audit-tail.redacted.jsonl. manifest.json is the root and names the other three by bundle-relative path and sha256, so the bundle is self-describing and tamper-evident without this crate parsing them. Fields: schema_version, id (content hash), trigger (REFUSAL|FAILURE|PANIC|QUARANTINE|CAPACITY_REJECTION), seed (u64, for LabRuntimeTarget replay), statement_redacted, captured_verdict {danger, required_level, reason_class}, why, lanes[{lane_id, subject_id_hash}], build{server, classifier, driver}, entries[{kind, path, sha256, bytes}]. serde deny_unknown_fields — an unknown field is a REFUSED manifest, not an ignored one, because an unknown field is how a payload rides into a file everyone assumes is safe to attach to a bug report.

(a) NOT AN EXFILTRATION CHANNEL — reusing Arc J, not a second redactor: every free-text field goes through corpus::redact_sql / validate_redacted_sql / safe_why (bead 14.1, commit 6ce0a57). The statement is stored only as its redacted skeleton and re-lexed to prove nothing survived; a statement the redactor cannot lex yields NO manifest at all. Every structured field is an allowlist, not a denylist: lane_id = bare identifier; subject_id_hash = sha256:<64hex> only (a username is refused); entries[].path is MATCHED against the three fixed bundle names (so ../, absolute paths, drive letters, tnsnames.ora and any wallet path are refused, not sanitized); sha256 = canonical digest; build.* must be version-shaped. IncidentManifestError is a closed vocabulary with NO payload — an error quoting the offending text would leak the very secret it refused, into the log or bug report the error lands in.

A REAL WEAKNESS THE TESTS CAUGHT, WHICH I FIXED IN THE CODE RATHER THAN ADJUSTING THE TEST: my first version-shape gate admitted `system/hunter2` — a CREDENTIAL PAIR is name/name, exactly the shape of package/version. The gate now requires the part after `/` to start with a digit, so `oraclemcp-guard/0.9.0` passes while `system/hunter2` and `hr_app/Passw0rd` are refused. Two other tests I had written asserted the wrong thing, and I corrected the tests to the truth: a comment is STRIPPED by the Arc J redactor (not a reason to refuse the capture) and its payload never reaches the artifact; and a manifest hand-edited to put customer SQL back into the skeleton field is caught by the redaction POSTCONDITION at load, before the id check even runs (the id is what catches a byte-count edit the field validators cannot see).

(b) SEC-1 — A CAPTURED VERDICT IS EVIDENCE, NEVER AUTHORIZATION: CapturedVerdict is inert data. Nothing converts a manifest into a GuardDecision — no Into, no method, no read-back. The only path from a manifest's statement to a decision is incident::reclassify_at_replay(&classifier, statement), which runs the live classifier every time. Pinned by test: a bundle CLAIMING danger=SAFE for a destructive DDL statement re-classifies as destructive/forbidden at replay and never yields ReadOnly; a second test proves re-classification is identical whether or not the bundle carried a verdict at all.

(c) REPRODUCIBLE: no wall clock, no random id. Lanes are ordered by lane_id and entries by (kind, path) at capture, so capture order cannot change the bytes; id is a domain-separated sha256 over every other field. Pinned by test: capturing the same incident twice is byte-identical; a reversed capture order yields identical JSON and id; a different seed or trigger yields a different id. from_json re-validates every field and recomputes the id, so a manifest edited on disk is refused at load rather than believed because it is on disk.

GATE (scoped): omcpb fmt -p oraclemcp-guard clean; omcpb clippy -p oraclemcp-guard --all-targets = ZERO findings in incident.rs / incident_manifest.rs; omcpb test -p oraclemcp-guard fully green including the 17 new tests (guard lib 187 passed, every suite ok). Clippy was run without -D warnings because another agent's in-flight edit in oraclemcp-db currently trips a lint that would mask my signal; my own files are clean either way.

title: [09x][E1] om incident capture (bundle + redaction gate)
description:

Arc-M/redaction seam before anything leaves the host (binds/literals/identifiers scrubbed).

notes:
PROGRESS (commit a871ec8, NOT closed): the bundle assembler + redaction gate are landed and proven — crates/oraclemcp-core/src/incident.rs + tests/incident_capture.rs (6/6 green).

title: [09x][J1] Corpus record schema + redaction
description:
Arc J (corpus). SCOPE: JSONL record { id, refused_sql_redacted, refusal_class,
suggested_rewrite_redacted, why } — every text field passes the Arc-M/redaction seam (no binds, no
identifiers); dedup by content hash. ACCEPTANCE: the schema is defined and a record round-trips;
redaction verified. DEPENDS: gate + Arc M M1 (redaction).
close_reason:
Landed 6ce0a57: crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/corpus.rs (new module) + lib.rs registration + crates/oraclemcp-guard/tests/corpus_redaction.rs (10 tests, all green).

SCHEMA: the JSONL record the bead specifies — { id, refused_sql_redacted, refusal_class, suggested_rewrite_redacted, why } — with refusal_class reusing the guard's existing closed vocabulary (ReasonCategory from oraclemcp-error) rather than inventing a second one. Round-trips through to_jsonl_line / from_jsonl_line; always exactly one line.

REDACTION (the corpus is meant to ship PUBLICLY, so the schema is built so a secret-carrying record cannot exist):
 - The struct is constructible ONLY via CorpusRecord::new / from_jsonl_line; both redact and then verify. There is no path from raw text to a record.
 - Redaction is an ALLOWLIST, not a denylist: SQL is reduced to a skeleton where keywords and Oracle-SHIPPED names (DBMS_SQL, UTL_HTTP, EXECUTE IMMEDIATE, DUAL...) survive — they are what makes the statement unsafe and they are public knowledge — while every literal, number, bind, comment, database link and CUSTOMER identifier is replaced. Identifiers map to stable per-record placeholders (id_1, id_2) so structure/joins stay legible while the real names do not survive. Any token kind the walk does not recognise is collapsed too: unknown means redact, so a hole can only make the output less informative, never leakier.
 - POSTCONDITION: the redacted output is RE-LEXED and rejected unless every surviving lexeme is a keyword, an allowlisted public name, or a placeholder. A hole in the redactor becomes a rejected record, not a disclosure.
 - Fail-closed: a statement that does not lex is REFUSED (no record) rather than shipped best-effort-scrubbed — an unterminated literal is exactly how a secret escapes a partial scrub.
 -  is the one free-text field and is held to a plain-prose alphabet (no digits, quotes, ':' binds, '@' hosts, or identifier punctuation), which is everything a credential needs to be written down.
 - Errors are a closed no-payload vocabulary, so a rejection cannot leak the secret into a log or bug report.
 - SEC-1 applied to the corpus: from_jsonl_line re-validates stored text and recomputes the id, so a hand-edited file that puts plaintext back — or forges the dedup key — is refused AT LOAD, not trusted because it is already on disk.

DEDUP: content hash (sha256, schema version bound in) over the REDACTED fields, so the id leaks nothing and two refusals that are the same lesson in different customer clothing collapse to one record. dedup_by_content keeps the first occurrence.

TESTS (10, incl. the negative tests asked for): an adversarial SECRETS fixture set (credential, token, email, SSN, PAN, customer schema/table, db link) is swept across EVERY path a record can take — construction, both SQL fields, serialization, the content id, reload, dedup, and the error messages — and asserts none of them ever renders. Negative: a  carrying a secret is REJECTED (6 shapes); an unlexable statement produces NO record; a tampered JSONL line carrying plaintext again is refused at load; a forged id is refused. Positive control: the dangerous construct and Oracle-shipped package names DO survive, so redaction is not vacuously destroying the dataset.

TEETH VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED: punching a hole in the redactor (let customer identifiers through) is caught by 7 of the 10 tests; module restored byte-identical afterwards. Fixtures are synthetic only (confidentiality rule).

GATES: scoped fmt + clippy -p oraclemcp-guard --all-targets -D warnings clean + all guard tests green (178 unit + 10 corpus + the rest).

admission. Shared upstream of B1 (mask cert), F, H, J, E. Children: M0-M4.

title: [09x][N] Policy-as-code — the programmable guard
description:
The guard is one-size-fits-all; there is no operator-authored declarative policy ("principal X may
never touch schema HR"; "table Y is append-only"). Arc N is OPA/Rego-for-SQL. LARGELY NET-NEW: the
existing OperatorAuthorityPolicy (D17, oraclemcp-core/src/admin_auth.rs) governs WHO is the operator
(identity), not per-principal SQL rules — a thin seed only. The guard already has ONE deliberate
loosening lever (the audited operator allow_list in classifier.rs); N sits ABOVE the classifier and
must NEVER become a second one. STRICTLY MONOTONE: a policy returns Deny or Narrow over the base
verdict, never Allow-beyond-base; final = base AND policy. A Narrow that only lowers the verdict/level
is monotone; a Narrow that rewrites SQL produces a different statement that MUST re-enter the
classifier (SEC-1). Children: N0-N4.

title: [09x][K2] oracle_lineage — source-derived edges
description:
Arc K (lineage). SCOPE: tool oracle_lineage(owner?, object, column) computing source-derived column
edges via the existing plsql_lineage::dependencies engine. FILES: registry (+oracle_lineage), args,
dispatch arm. ACCEPTANCE: returns column edges for a synthetic view chain (unit + feature-lane test).
DEPENDS: K1, and Arc C2.4 (shared catalog snapshot).
notes:
DEFINITIVE FINDING — proven through the SERVED MCP surface against live 23ai FREE (localhost:1521/freepdb1), exactly as Arc K demands. oracle_lineage cannot produce column edges as specified, and the 'synthetic view chain' fixture is fundamentally incompatible with how the engine derives column lineage.

EVIDENCE CHAIN:
1. A synthetic VIEW chain (orders TABLE -> v_orders VIEW -> v_paid VIEW) created live in 23ai with PLSCOPE_SETTINGS='IDENTIFIERS:ALL, STATEMENTS:ALL' produced ZERO rows in ALL_IDENTIFIERS. PL/Scope captures identifiers for PL/SQL UNITS (packages/procedures/triggers), NOT for CREATE VIEW/CREATE TABLE DDL. So a view chain yields no column facts at all — the acceptance's chosen fixture cannot work, live or offline.
2. A PL/SQL PROCEDURE (load_paid: INSERT INTO paid(id,amount) SELECT id,amount FROM orders WHERE status='PAID') DID produce PL/Scope COLUMN identifiers (AMOUNT/STATUS/ID, usage=REFERENCE). So the capability exists for PL/SQL code, not views.
3. Called oracle_plsql_live_snapshot(schemas=[LINEAGE_DEMO], include_plscope=true) THROUGH THE SERVED MCP SERVER against live 23ai: returns a CatalogSnapshot containing the column identifiers, but NO DepGraph column edges — the response contains no DerivesColumn/ReadsColumn/WritesColumn (grepped).
4. The linked plsql-engine 0.7.0 has ZERO column-node/edge production code (non-test grep = 0). analyze_project (the ONLY analyze entry, sync, no connection) builds an object-level DepGraph from source with NO column nodes (empirically: view-chain source -> 2 View nodes, 0 column nodes). CatalogSourceConfig::Snapshot(path) with a synthetic CatalogSnapshot was IGNORED (run.catalog.is_some()==false). CatalogSourceConfig::LiveConnection is an unused enum variant with no live-analyze consumer.
5. plsql_lineage::column_writers/column_readers require a DepGraph ALREADY populated with column nodes + DerivesColumn edges; nothing in any accessible path (analyze_project, live tools, catalog builder) populates them. The lineage crate's column edges are built MANUALLY only in its own unit tests.

ROOT CAUSE: there is no shipped path that transforms raw PL/Scope column identifiers (available in the live CatalogSnapshot) into the column-level DepGraph that column_writers/column_readers consume. Producing oracle_lineage's column edges would require oraclemcp to BUILD column lineage itself from ALL_IDENTIFIERS (resolve COLUMN references by usage into column nodes + DerivesColumn/ReadsColumn edges) — a genuine multi-day feature, not the 'registry + args + dispatch arm' this bead scoped. And 9.3/9.4/9.5 all transitively depend on this non-existent capability.

ACTIONABLE OPTIONS for the orchestrator (a re-spec decision, not something I can resolve by trying harder):
A. Change the fixture from a VIEW chain to a PL/SQL package/procedure (PL/Scope covers it) AND implement the PL/Scope-identifiers -> column-DepGraph builder in oraclemcp (the real missing piece). Large feature.
B. Descope oracle_lineage to OBJECT-level lineage (achievable via the existing dep_graph / oracle_plsql_lineage) and drop the 'column edges' claim.
C. File an upstream plsql-engine bead to expose a column-graph builder, and hold Arc K until it lands.

STATE: NOT landed (I will not ship a tool that returns empty edges for real input). My incomplete STATIC oracle_lineage (+315 lines) is uncommitted in crates/oraclemcp/src/plsql_tools.rs; I am blocked from git checkout/stash by charter+dcg, so the orchestrator must revert it. Lab fixture (lineage_demo user) created for the live proof was DROPPED after testing (synthetic-only, nothing committed).

title: Epic: Wire OAuth/TLS/host-origin into the binary HTTP transport (S1)
description:

The W10 ScopeGrant scope-enforcement is real but reachable only at the dispatch layer / by an embedding caller, NOT through the served HTTP transport -- yet README:121-128 and docs/behavior-inventory.md describe OAuth scope enforcement + TLS as live. This is a truth-in-advertising + security gap.
Operator decision (2026-06-18): WIRE it into the binary (not doc-patch). The auth machinery already exists in oraclemcp-auth (oauth_rs.rs OAuth2.1 RS, scope.rs RBAC, tls.rs rustls); this is config-plumbing, not new crypto.

description:
Ideas #3 + #6. Double down on the core identity (safe-by-construction read-only).
(1) Session-level read-only backstop so the guarantee is two-layer, not classifier-only -- even a hypothetical classifier bug cannot mutate. (2) SQLcl-style auditability: per-statement marker comment + dynamic V$SESSION tagging so a DBA can see/trust MCP traffic WITHOUT trusting the client. notes: v0.3.0 release decision: defer as a post-RC defense-in-depth wave. description:
Observed 2026-09-24 by the orchestrator. The CI job 'Oracle FREE 23ai matrix + VECTOR smoke' has failed on every main run since at least 9c3a2d24 (01:46Z), including 8949a2b7. Failing step: ladder_session in scripts/e2e oracle_version_matrix (lane free23): LADDER FAIL (free23): assertion failed: statement executed; context: error_class REPREVIEW_REQUIRED, 'confirmation grant belongs to a different SQL or execution envelope'.

The orchestrator's batch gate never ran this lane (it runs only the default workspace tests), so this went unnoticed while beads were closed as green.

Likely area: the decisive-field / impact-binding / effective-plan changes (W13/W14: .15.11 EffectiveDmlPlanV1, .16.x ImpactBindingV1), or the confirmation-token envelope binding. Bisect the earliest failing main run, find the mismatching decisive field between preview and execute, fix it in the product, and keep the fail-closed property (a changed statement must still re-preview).

description: MIRROR (both). run_all.sh already records pass/skipped/fail; make it declarative and enforce by tier. Every production MCP tool/HTTP route/CLI/config-gate has a tested trace to dispatch/guard/result and its canonical runner; every e2e script is registered or explicitly excluded with a reason. Required-tier skips FAIL; declare/provision omcpb rather than ambient PATH; no live test fabricates a PASS when its DB is absent. Start with l6xn, 5c7i, K3, C3.3. Depends on evidence-contract-v1.
design:
CI ARCHITECTURE (decided 2026-07-16 — fast critical path + correct coverage + nothing runs forever). Supersedes earlier notes.
FOUR TIERS BY TRIGGER:
1. Every push/PR (hosted, timeout ~15m): fmt, clippy, deny, lint scripts, ALL DB-free unit/property/metamorphic/guard tests. No live DB. Only tier developers wait on.
2. Live-on-demand (hosted, ~25m): a `live` label OR a DB/driver path-filter fires ONE 23ai lane, only for PRs touching DB code.
3. Nightly scheduled (parallel matrix, each lane ~30m cap): full 18c/21c/23ai + OCI Always-Free-ADB + soak/canary. Off the critical path; where correctness lives.
4. Release tag (exact-SHA, blocks publish): full matrix + OCI producing release-candidate-proof/v1. Rare; correctness paramount.
NOTHING-RUNS-FOREVER CONTROLS: every job sets timeout-minutes (fast 15 / live 25-30 / soak capped); version matrix runs PARALLEL (wall-clock = slowest lane, not sum); concurrency cancel-in-progress on PR workflows. On hosted, each live lane cold-starts its gvenzl DB per run (acceptable: nightly/release are off the critical path and hard-capped); LOCAL runs on the operator box reuse warm long-lived containers to skip startup.
RUNNER PLACEMENT (both repos PUBLIC; operator decision 2026-07-16: NO GitHub self-hosted runners): HOSTED-ONLY. Fast tier + 23ai + OCI on GitHub-hosted — 23ai/oracle-free (the LARGEST image) already runs hosted, so the smaller XE 18c/21c fit too. Nightly matrix runs ONE Oracle version PER PARALLEL hosted runner (never stack all three on one runner) + the existing disk-freeing step + faststart/slim images. If a version genuinely cannot fit a hosted runner even then, run THAT lane as a LOCAL gate on the operator box emitting the same required-proof/release-candidate-proof artifact for the exact SHA (attributable) — do NOT add a self-hosted GitHub runner. This dev box = fast-iteration + the only local-gate fallback. Live PROOF OF RECORD = exact-SHA CI (or attributable local) artifact, never an oral pass; required-tier live SKIP = FAIL; no mocks (real gvenzl/ADB).

title: [BH102][R44][rust] Preserve lane generation through Change Proposal apply
description:
Finding: the dashboard sends lane_id plus lane_generation for saved Change Proposal apply, but ChangeProposalApplyRequest carries only lane_id and forward_operator_action rebuilds the internal action without lane_generation. Stateful operator actions require an exact generation, so saved-plan apply/snapshot forwarding fails closed with operator_lane_generation_required.

Acceptance: carry a positive lane_generation through the persisted/apply request boundary and every internally forwarded stateful action; reject missing/stale generations before dispatch; a real stateful Change Proposal apply regression test proves the selected exact lane generation reaches dispatch while a stale generation executes nothing.

title: Wire explicit thin-driver client identity fields from profiles
description:
## Current gap

`rust-oracledb` already accepts a full `ClientIdentity` with `program`, `machine`, `osuser`, `terminal`, and `driver_name`. oraclemcp only exposes `session_identity.module`, `client_identifier`, and `driver_name`, then currently maps `module -> program`, process `$HOSTNAME -> machine`, process `$USER -> osuser`, and `client_identifier -> terminal` in `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/connection.rs`.

That means operators cannot deliberately set the Oracle-visible client identity fields that the thin driver already supports. It also makes the README stale because it says the driver lacks setters, while the driver now has them.

## Required change

Extend profile/session identity config and DB connect options so operators can set driver-level identity fields explicitly:

- `session_identity.program`
- `session_identity.machine`
- `session_identity.os_user` or `osuser` with one documented spelling
- `session_identity.terminal`

Preserve existing `module`, `action`, `client_identifier`, and `client_info` behavior as Oracle session attributes set after connect via `DBMS_APPLICATION_INFO` / `DBMS_SESSION`.

## Implementation notes

- Keep backwards compatibility: if the new driver-level fields are absent, retain current defaults/mapping so existing profiles still work.
- Prefer explicit driver fields over overloaded values when present.
- Keep `driver_name` in the connect-time identity.
- Do not expose configured identity values in `oracle_list_profiles`; these can identify operators, hosts, tenants, or workflows.

## Acceptance criteria

- Config schema accepts and inherits the new identity fields.
- `profile_to_options` carries them into `OracleConnectOptions`.
- `RustOracleConnection` maps them into `oracledb::protocol::ClientIdentity`.
- Unit tests prove defaults, explicit overrides, inheritance, and metadata redaction.
- README/setup templates accurately distinguish driver-level identity from DBMS session attributes.
- A live 23ai/FREE verification note or test checks `SYS_CONTEXT`/`V$SESSION` fields where privileges allow it.
close_reason: Implemented explicit thin driver identity fields with profile/core/db mapping, redaction, README/setup updates, unit tests, workspace gates, and gated live-test path

Deliverable: AGENTS.md constitution rule + a push path that runs the gate, captures its exit status, and refuses to push on a non-zero verdict, so the verdict cannot be skipped by not reading it.

The one blocker is upstream: the oracledb 0.5.1 thin driver cannot connect to any pre-23ai Oracle server (fleet is 19c). Bump the exact pins oracledb = "=0.5.1" and oracledb-protocol = "=0.5.1" to 0.5.2 once the driver ships pre-23ai connect support (TNS RESEND handling + classic non-fast-auth session establishment; driver epic rust-oracledb-pre23ai-connect-z47u). title: Actionable connect-error envelopes + doctor guidance for driver handshake failures
description:
Field UX gap: doctor --online and MCP error envelopes surfaced the raw driver string "unknown TTC message type 11 at position 4" with no interpretation and no next steps. It was opaque to the user AND actively misleading (it names the TTC application layer while the failing byte was a network-layer TNS packet type; triage chased wrong hypotheses for a session).

Scope: in the driver-seam adapter (crates/oraclemcp-db/src/connection.rs), map driver connect/handshake failures into structured ErrorEnvelope classes with plain-language messages and next_actions - e.g. server-generation-not-supported (pre-23ai until the 0.5.2 adoption lands), listener-redirect-unsupported, wallet-format-unsupported (already good), and a generic handshake-protocol-error that names the phase and points at the driver handshake-trace instructions. doctor --online should print the same guidance (fix: lines with a concrete command or doc link, matching its existing remediation style). Include the negotiated/attempted endpoint metadata only in redacted form, consistent with existing doctor redaction guarantees.

Test: unit tests over the adapter mapping; doctor snapshot test with a simulated pre-23ai handshake failure. Depends on the 0.5.2 pin bump for the new variants, but the envelope/class scaffolding and the current-string mapping can land first.
close_reason: Connect-error UX landed: driver-seam adapter maps oracledb 0.6.0 handshake failures (UnexpectedPacket, ConnectResendLoop, FastAuthRequired, UnsupportedFeature, ListenerRefused ERR= extraction, below-floor server refusal, wallet diagnostics) to structured envelopes with plain-language messages + next_actions incl. ORACLEDB_TRACE_CONNECT triage guidance; doctor --online surfaces the same fix: lines; new public ConnectFailureKind surface baselined via api-lock procedure; unit tests over the mapping.

title: setup MCP snippet defaults to a wrapper path nothing creates - unify on real binary
description:
Field friction (paste-broken UX): oraclemcp setup --profile

prints MCP client snippets whose command is the --wrapper-path default ~/.local/bin/oraclemcp-local - but nothing ever creates that wrapper: setup only prints a wrapper template, and the installer never writes one. A fresh user who pastes the setup snippet wires their MCP client to a nonexistent path and gets a dead server entry. Meanwhile install.sh print_client_snippet correctly uses the resolved real binary, so our two snippet sources disagree. Fix: default the setup snippet command to the resolved real binary path (or the om alias) exactly like the installer does; print the wrapper-path variant only when the operator explicitly passes --wrapper-path, and in that case state clearly that the wrapper must exist (or offer to write it through the same governed config-ops path). Keep Claude JSON and Codex TOML variants consistent. Test: CLI test asserting the default snippet command equals the resolved current-exe (or om) and never the uncreated wrapper path; a second test for the explicit --wrapper-path flow.
close_reason: setup snippets now default to the resolved real binary (current_exe, matching install.sh print_client_snippet); --wrapper-path is opt-in (no default) and both JSON payload + human output state the wrapper must be created first; Claude JSON and Codex TOML stay consistent; unit test setup_payload_default_snippets_use_the_real_binary_not_a_wrapper + CLI tests setup_default_snippet_command_is_the_resolved_binary / setup_explicit_wrapper_path_snippets_state_wrapper_must_exist

One-line change + snapshot test update.

title: Config discovery: honor XDG_CONFIG_HOME (or document the asymmetry)
description:
Field surprise: exporting XDG_CONFIG_HOME does NOT relocate config discovery - the search order is ORACLEMCP_CONFIG, then literal ~/.config/oraclemcp/profiles.toml, then config.toml - while STATE does follow XDG_STATE_HOME (write-intents, audit). XDG-native users expect config to follow XDG_CONFIG_HOME.

Decide and implement ONE of: (a) preferred - honor XDG_CONFIG_HOME in oraclemcp-config discovery (insert $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/oraclemcp/... ahead of the ~/.config fallback; keep ORACLEMCP_CONFIG highest), with tests for precedence and doctor/config-ops path reporting; or (b) document the asymmetry prominently in README config-discovery section + docs/configuration.md. Option (a) is a small, backwards-compatible superset (on most boxes XDG_CONFIG_HOME is unset or already ~/.config). Either way add a regression test pinning the chosen precedence.
close_reason: option (a) implemented: OracleMcpConfig discovery now honors $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/oraclemcp/{profiles,config}.toml ahead of the ~/.config fallback (absolute paths only, per XDG spec; ORACLEMCP_CONFIG stays highest) via new config_search_dirs(); operator_config_target_path (setup --write/doctor fresh-target) follows the same order; precedence regression tests xdg_config_home_precedes_home_config_and_explicit_env_stays_highest (incl relative-XDG-ignored) + CLI test setup_write_default_target_honors_xdg_config_home; README + docs/configuration.md discovery order updated

title: install.sh: allow explicit --target linux-gnu (published tarball is unreachable)
description:
install.sh detect_target maps Linux:x86_64 to x86_64-unknown-linux-musl and validate_target accepts only musl/darwin triples - so the published x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu release tarball is unreachable through the installer even with an explicit --target (it is rejected). Field impact minor (static musl runs everywhere incl. WSL2) but a user who wants the gnu build must download + extract by hand.

Fix: accept gnu triples when passed explicitly via --target (keep musl the auto-detected default), or document musl-only clearly in README install section. Prefer the former; it is a validate_target allow-list widening plus an installer-lint/e2e case (scripts/e2e installer suite has dry-run coverage to extend).
close_reason: validate_target now accepts x86_64/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu when TARGET_EXPLICIT=1 (--target); musl stays the auto-detected Linux default and non-matrix triples still fail; usage text + README install section document the explicit gnu path; installer smoke suite gained a gnu dry-run plan assertion (gnu tarball URL) and a still-rejected non-Unix triple case; install.ps1 checked - no equivalent restriction (Windows zip only), no mirror needed

description:
Systemic gap the field test exposed: oraclemcp live verification (live-xe suite, doctor --online, e2e) has only ever run against gvenzl/oracle-free:23 - so a driver connect path that cannot reach ANY pre-23ai server shipped through every gate and was first caught by a customer field install against 19c.

Scope: add a scripted, documented pre-production matrix - gvenzl/oracle-xe:18-slim, gvenzl/oracle-xe:21-slim, gvenzl/oracle-free:23-slim on distinct host ports (compose file or a scripts/ helper mirroring the driver repo matrix) - and run the live profile/config smoke subset plus doctor --online --profile against each version. Document in docs/operations.md testing section and add to docs/release-checklist.md so a release cannot ship without pre-23ai connect coverage. Optionally document the genuine-19c lane (Oracle Container Registry EE image, free OTN login for dev/test) as an extra, not a gate requirement. Goes fully green only after the 0.5.2 pin bump; land the harness first with the 18/21 lanes marked expected-fail until then so the flip to green is visible.
notes: SCOPE RAISED (operator directive 2026-07-04): not just doctor+query smoke. Required per-lane e2e across the FULL operating-level ladder, end to end through the MCP surface: (1) doctor --online green; (2) READ_ONLY: oracle_query with row-value assertions; (3) READ_WRITE: oracle_preview_sql -> oracle_set_session_level elevation (preview + grant + execute) -> oracle_execute DML with default rollback verified, then commit via single-use execution grant, row counts checked; (4) DDL: create/drop through the preview->grant->execute gate; (5) audit chain entries verified for each privileged step; (6) drop back to READ_ONLY and verify refusal of writes. Lab profiles per lane (XE18/XE21/FREE23) with a writable max_level=DDL lab profile; wire into docs/release-checklist.md as a REQUIRED release gate so no oraclemcp release ships without pre-23ai coverage; genuine-19c lane documented as optional operator-run step. Rationale: the thin driver was only ever validated against 23ai and the envelope gap shipped to the field.
close_reason: Ladder e2e landed: scripts/e2e/oracle_version_matrix.sh + oracle_ladder_session.py drive the real binary over MCP stdio per lane (XE18/XE21/FREE23): doctor --online, READ_ONLY query with value assertions + write refusal, preview->grant->elevate->DML rollback-then-commit, governed DDL create/drop, drop-back-to-RO refusal, audit evidence; wired into run_all.sh, docs/release-checklist.md (required gate) and docs/operations.md; genuine-19c lane documented as operator-run extra. title: Un-gate oracledb: ship official backend as always-present connect-time fallback
description: Today the oracledb backend is feature-off by default (crates/oraclemcp-db/Cargo.toml default empty) and enabled by NO release, Docker, or install build (release.yml:338-340, Dockerfile:41,49 build without it), so it is absent from every shipped artifact and cannot serve as a runtime fallback. Operator decision 2026-09-17: driver-cx stays PRIMARY; un-gate oracledb so the official backend is compiled into shipped builds as an always-present CONNECT-TIME fallback. Preserve exact current semantics: raw-acquisition-only alternate for basic-password (permits_alternate is RawAcquisition only), NO mid-session migration, reduced-capability session that fails closed on call_routine, named-binds, LOB, JSON, INTERVAL, and DBMS_OUTPUT; IAM, cwallet, and PEM stay permanently driver-cx.
