title: A2.2: cwallet.sso fallthrough (day-one linchpin)
description:
A2.2 — cwallet.sso fallthrough (the day-one linchpin). repo: oracledb. Top-ranked day-one risk. Blocks B2.1.

WHY: this IS the round-2 field failure. When a higher-precedence wallet file is present but undecryptable, the driver must fall through to the valid cwallet.sso auto-login credential — exactly as python-oracledb does. Today tls.rs:366 (load_wallet) has NO fallthrough: an undecryptable pem/p12 aborts the connect even when a perfectly good sso sits next to it.

CHANGE (decision tree): try pem -> on UnsupportedCipher FALL THROUGH to sso; on PasswordRequired / wrong-password WITH a valid auto-login sso present, ALSO fall through (sso is an independent valid credential) BUT log a warning naming the skipped wallet; if no sso, PRESERVE the original typed error. Precedence: pem -> p12(+pw) -> cwallet.sso.

DEPS: C1 (fixtures), A2.1 (3des decrypt).
TEST/DoD: a synthetic undecryptable legacy-3DES p12/pem PAIRED with the existing real cwallet.sso -> connect SUCCEEDS via sso (+ warning names the skipped wallet). NEGATIVE CONTROL (see sec via A2.3): undecryptable-pem-only, NO sso -> the exact typed error (UnsupportedCipher naming the OID) is preserved and MUST NOT mention sso fallthrough.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: undecryptable legacy-3DES p12/pem + a valid cwallet.sso -> connect SUCCEEDS via sso + a warning names the skipped wallet. AC2: undecryptable-pem-only, NO sso -> the exact typed error (UnsupportedCipher naming the OID) is preserved and the message does NOT mention fallthrough. AC3: precedence pem -> p12(+pw) -> cwallet.sso honored. AC4: all proven by autonomous C1-fixture tests, zero live OCI.
close_reason: A2.2 done — rust-oracledb 298cc97: cwallet.sso fallthrough (precedence pem->p12(+pw)->sso; only KeyDecrypt/Pkcs12/PasswordRequired/UnsupportedFormat are fallthrough-eligible; I/O + malformed-container NOT masked; WARN names skipped wallet; no-sso preserves original typed error). Verified compiling+tested.

title: sec1: re-classify-at-apply proof (SEC-1)
description:

WHY: the fail-closed guard must re-classify at the POINT OF ACTION; a stored verdict/grant is NEVER an authorization input. This bead is the explicit two-lane proof.

close_reason: SEC-1 PROVEN — no gap. Two-lane adversarial proof (5 tests, dispatch/tests.rs): a stored execute-grant is never honored after the ceiling is lowered on every dispatch-reachable path. title: Guard: block-wrapped WHERE-less DML floors at READ_WRITE (should require the interior statement tier — a TIGHTENING)
description: DISCOVERED during D6.1 (srv2). A benign balanced anonymous block floors at Guarded/READ_WRITE regardless of interior tier (oraclemcp-guard classifier.rs ~1344): a WHERE-less DML statement wrapped in BEGIN ... END classifies Guarded/READ_WRITE, whereas the bare unqualified form (an unconditional row-removal) is Destructive/DDL — block-wrapping WHERE-less DML LOWERS the required level (Ddl to ReadWrite). Same shape for a bare object-drop wrapped in a block (Oracle rejects that as invalid PL/SQL, so harmless; the WHERE-less-DML case is the real one). SEVERITY LOW (uncommitted DML rolls back by default; READ_ONLY and protected profiles cannot reach ReadWrite), but a genuine danger-tier inconsistency. FIX is a TIGHTENING (its own careful bead, do NOT loosen): a block should require at least max(interior statement tiers), not a flat ReadWrite floor. Validate against the guard corpora (adversarial_corpus.rs, admin_dcl_fail_closed.rs) plus the D6.1 MRs and the D6.4 mutation gate. NOTE D6.1 MR1 dropped block-wrap because block semantics are not currently monotone; this fix makes them monotone. Guard SOURCE change = highest scrutiny.
close_reason: Guard tightening DONE (TIGHTEN-ONLY) — 8c7333f: block-wrap now MONOTONE. Bare no-WHERE DML=Destructive/READ_WRITE; block-wrapped was Guarded (wrap lowered danger) -> now Destructive (==bare). Fix: body floor = max(current, interior_tier) on danger+level, interior_tier via REUSING the bare classifier (block_interior_segments + block_interior_floor re-run classify_statement, single source of truth), pure MAX (raise-only), parse==1 precheck prevents over-tighten; plsql_create floor also pure MAX; Forbidden branches untouched. Validation: MR6 block-wrap monotonicity MR (re-enables D6.1 MR1) mutation-validated (kills MUT-BLOCKWRAP); unit test; guard 104 lib + adversarial 8/8 + admin_dcl 2/2 + metamorphic 14/14 + proptest 6/6 + token 8/8; workspace green; secret_scan clean. title: WORKSTREAM C: autonomous secret-free OCI test harness
description:
WORKSTREAM EPIC C — the autonomous, secret-free OCI test harness. repo: oracledb (mostly) + oraclemcp.

Goal: the answer to "how do we test OCI autonomously?" A prerequisite for A2/A3/B2 and the single most reusable deliverable of the release. Everything committed, deterministic, secret-free.

Four OCI layers: (1) wallet parse/decrypt — 100% autonomous offline (C1); (2) TCPS handshake + DN/SAN + mTLS — 100% autonomous offline (C2 extends the existing tls_handshake.rs rustls listener); (3) token wire path + non-TCPS refusal — autonomous (C3 mock IAM); (3b) real DB query over TCPS — the local pre-tag gate (D3.2), not CI; (4) real-cloud IAM acceptance — operator manual smoke only.

Contains: C1 synthetic wallet generator+fixtures (FIRST — blocks A2/C2/C3); C2 local TCPS lane; C3 mock IAM; C4 confidentiality secret-scan lint (RELEASE BLOCKER); C6 doctor-output secret audit.

CONFIDENTIALITY: all fixtures are synthetic/throwaway with fictional DNs (CN=oracle-test.invalid). Validated live: OpenSSL 3.5.5 with -legacy produces the exact field-test OID 1.2.840.113549.1.12.1.3; orapki is absent so the cwallet.sso auto-login case reuses the existing real committed fixture.
close_reason: Workstream complete — all leaf beads closed; driver 0.8.2 + server 0.8.0 published.

title: C1: synthetic wallet fixtures + generator (FIRST prerequisite)
description:
C1 — synthetic wallet fixtures + generator (scripts/gen_test_wallets.sh). repo: oracledb. FIRST prerequisite — blocks A2/C2/C3.

WHY: the round-2 field failure was a stock OCI ADB wallet that would not connect (legacy-3DES PKCS12 key rejected). To test that autonomously and secret-free, we mint throwaway wallets ourselves. All fixtures use a fictional DN (CN=oracle-test.invalid) and a throwaway password; NO customer identifier ever appears.

VALIDATED LIVE (OpenSSL 3.5.5, orapki absent):
- modern PBES2/PBKDF2/AES-CBC ewallet.p12: `openssl pkcs12 -export` (default). Works.
- legacy 3DES ewallet.p12: `openssl pkcs12 -export -certpbe PBE-SHA1-3DES -keypbe PBE-SHA1-3DES -legacy ...`. Confirmed PBE-SHA1-3DES = pbeWithSHA1And3-KeyTripleDES-CBC = OID 1.2.840.113549.1.12.1.3 (the EXACT field-test OID). Requires the -legacy provider flag on OpenSSL 3.x.
- cwallet.sso auto-login: orapki is unavailable, so DO NOT try to generate one. Reuse the existing real committed fixture cwallet_orapki.sso already in the driver fixtures. The A2.2 fallthrough test pairs a synthetic legacy-3DES p12/pem with that existing sso.
- encrypted + plaintext ewallet.pem (note: openssl rsa -des3 on 3.x emits PBES2, already supported; the legacy case is the p12 above).

DETERMINISM (red-team R5): PKCS12 uses a random salt/IV so fixtures are NOT byte-reproducible. Commit the fixture bytes ONCE; tests assert the wallet DECRYPTS to the expected key/cert, never byte-identity. CI needs no openssl (only the regen script does).

Fixtures under crates/oracledb/tests/fixtures/tls/synthetic/. Extends the existing tls_wallet.rs set (~30 wallets). Drives A2.1/A2.2 + server B2.1 doctor wallet tests.

TEST/DoD: the generator script is committed + documented; offline decrypt tests pass over each minted wallet; PROVENANCE.md records exact openssl commands + version (D6.3).
close_reason: C1 landed in rust-oracledb e007839: gen_test_wallets.sh, synthetic fixtures (LFS), PROVENANCE.md, tls_wallet offline tests, TLS_SETUP doc.

title: C4: confidentiality secret-scan lint + self-test (RELEASE BLOCKER)
description:
C4 — confidentiality secret-scan lint (scripts/secret_scan.sh, both repos). RELEASE BLOCKER (p0).

WHY: the round-2 field test ran against a real confidential customer environment. Its identifiers (hostnames, DB/service/schema/user names, proxy identities, wallet OCIDs, IP ranges) must NEVER appear in any committed artifact. This lint is the technical enforcement of that rule so a future agent physically cannot leak them.

CHANGE: scripts/secret_scan.sh greps the ENTIRE tracked tree (code/tests/fixtures/cassettes/docs/beads JSONL) for forbidden confidential token patterns and fails CI on any hit. Wire into _quality.yml + the release preflight (release_preflight.sh). The exact pattern list lives in a GITIGNORED operator file the lint reads (so the patterns themselves are never published); it enumerates (1) every literal identifier under todelete/ and (2) the confidential customer-codename family (+ its *-prefixed schema/user variants), plus broad STRUCTURAL patterns that cannot match public content (e.g. CN=.*\.oraclecloud\.com, wallet-OCID shapes, RFC1918 ranges in fixtures).

SELF-TEST (required): a test that intentionally plants a forbidden pattern in a scratch file and asserts the lint FAILS — proving the gate actually catches leaks. Complements the driver cassette sanitization gate (which already refuses to write a cassette containing known auth-field names).

TEST/DoD: lint green over the current tree; self-test proves it fails on a planted secret; re-scan the tree + any new cassettes/fixtures/golden doctor outputs before cutting 0.7.3.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: scripts/secret_scan.sh greps the whole tracked tree (code/tests/fixtures/cassettes/docs/beads JSONL) and exits non-zero on any forbidden pattern. AC2: wired into _quality.yml + release_preflight.sh. AC3: a self-test plants a forbidden pattern -> the lint FAILS. AC4: the pattern list stays in the gitignored operator file, never published.
close_reason: secret_scan.sh structural+denylist+generic; self-test exercises full structural path; CI+preflight wired; rust-oracledb driver synced

title: C2: local TCPS lane (extend tls_handshake.rs with C1 wallets)
description:
C2 — local TCPS lane (extend the existing rustls harness). repo: oracledb. Covers OCI Layer 2 fully offline.

WHY: gvenzl Oracle images cannot do TCPS out of the box (no orapki/Java/openssl, only TCP 1521). So we prove the client TLS path against a local rustls listener we control — no external cloud, no infra.

CHANGE: extend crates/oracledb/tests/tls_handshake.rs (an existing rustls server on 127.0.0.1:0 that already proves handshake + DN/SAN match + mTLS + round-trip) with the C1 synthetic wallets and the token path. No new infra.

TEST/DoD: handshake + DN/SAN + trust-precedence + mTLS all pass against the synthetic wallets, fully offline and deterministic.
close_reason: C2 done — rust-oracledb 46b5827: local TCPS lane extends tls_handshake.rs over C1 synthetic wallets (offline). Verified: tls_handshake 20 passed/0 failed; compiles; secret_scan green.

title: C3: mock IAM token source (over the C2 lane)

CHANGE: a local provider returns a throwaway JWT-shaped token; drives A3 (TokenSource) and B2.2 (server IAM impl) over the C2 lane. Assert the AUTH_TOKEN framing on the wire AND that a token over a non-TCPS transport fails closed (AccessTokenRequiresTcps). No real IAM, no cloud creds.

TEST/DoD: mock token accepted over the C2 TCPS lane; the same token over plaintext is refused with the exact typed error.
close_reason: C3 done — driver: mock IAM AUTH_TOKEN over C2 lane + plaintext refusal. (drv3)

title: C6: doctor-output secret audit (RedactedSecret + golden)

title: WORKSTREAM D6: quality and test-hardening
description:
WORKSTREAM EPIC D6 — quality and test-hardening. repo: both.

Goal: every new feature ships with its STRONGEST available oracle (differential > metamorphic > round-trip > crash), and the safety core is proven, not asserted.

Contains: D6.1 metamorphic property tests (classifier + differentiators), mutation-validated; D6.2 fuzzing hardening (per-surface structure-aware targets + TSan campaign for cancel-safety + differential-fuzz-after-optimization); D6.3 conformance rigor (coverage matrix + PROVENANCE + DISCREPANCIES/XFAIL + golden discipline via insta+scrubber); D6.4 mutation-testing gate (cargo-mutants >=90% kill on guard+audit+decode) — THE proof the safety tests are not placebo; D6.6 optimization discipline (baseline->profile->isomorphism-proof->committed regression gate); D6.7 kani bounded-model-checking on the BMC-tractable safety helpers; D6.8 pre-tag security-domain audit of the new attack surface (gates the tag).

DoD addendum (folds into every feature bead): strongest oracle + mutation-validation for any metamorphic relation + fixture provenance + XFAIL-not-SKIP for any divergence.
close_reason: Workstream complete — all leaf beads closed; driver 0.8.2 + server 0.8.0 published.

title: D6.1: metamorphic property tests, mutation-validated
description:
D6.1 — CLASSIFIER metamorphic property tests, mutation-validated (per testing-metamorphic). repo: oraclemcp. SAFETY CORE — no dependency, START EARLY.
CHANGE: express the classifier's safety properties as metamorphic relations (proptest), each scored >=2.0 and MUTATION-VALIDATED (each MR must catch a planted bug or it is decorative). MRs: monotonicity (adding a marker never LOOSENS the verdict), reclass-idempotence, SideEffectOracle-never-loosens, flashback-with-any-write-token still refused, normalize-before-classify stability. This is what the D6.4 mutation gate kills guard mutants with, so it must land EARLY and does NOT wait on any differentiator (split from D6.1b).

TEST/DoD: MR suite green with property-based input generation + DETAILED per-case logging (input, transform, expected relation, actual verdict); cargo-mutants confirms each MR kills >=1 planted guard mutant (feeds D6.4).

AC2: each MR is MUTATION-VALIDATED — cargo-mutants confirms it kills >=1 planted guard mutant. AC3: no dependency on any differentiator (starts week 1). AC4: detailed per-case logging (input, transform, expected relation, actual verdict).

title: D6.3d: golden discipline (insta + shared Scrubber)
description:
D6.3d — golden-artifact discipline (per testing-golden-artifacts). repo: both. This is the FRAMEWORK that C6 (doctor golden) and b4-contract-tests (dashboard bundle/SBOM golden) adopt.
CHANGE: the snapshot surfaces (stdio serverInfo, capabilities JSON, C6 doctor output, dashboard bundle/SBOM) adopt the insta crate + a SHARED Scrubber (timestamps / UUIDs / durations / SCN / paths canonicalized -> so a golden can never itself become a secret-leak or a flake), the UPDATE_GOLDENS -> git diff -> human review -> commit workflow, gitignore *.actual, and CI FAILS on any un-approved golden diff (no auto-update in CI).
DEPS: none (framework — build it early; per-surface goldens plug in via their own beads).
TEST/DoD: the assert_golden/insta infra + shared Scrubber exist; CI fails on an un-approved diff; a demo golden round-trips through UPDATE_GOLDENS; detailed diff logging in failure messages.
close_reason: DONE. Framework: shared Scrubber (golden_support) with [TIMESTAMP/UUID/ADDR/PATH/DURATION/SCN] rules; redaction subset wired into every assert_golden surface (leak-proof). check_golden Result + .actual sidecar + unified-diff + UPDATE_GOLDENS workflow; CI runs goldens UNSET + explicit guard (fail if set) + insta refuses update under CI. Capabilities migrated to insta (Scrubber filters + version mask); transcripts kept JSON-golden (documented anti-over-scrub). Round-trip demo test. *.actual gitignored. ZERO semantic churn; cargo-deny green for insta. Framework for C6/b4-contract to adopt.

title: D6.2: fuzzing hardening + TSan cancel-safety campaign
description:
D6.2 — fuzzing HARDENING layer (per testing-fuzzing) — EXTENDS A1.4. repo: both.
SCOPE: builds on A1.4's baseline crash targets with (1) per-surface STRUCTURE-AWARE fuzz targets (Arbitrary-derived corpora for 0mk VECTOR / x3s stream / bbx LOB / 8pp cache — random bytes waste ~99% of cycles on structured formats); (2) a TSan CONCURRENCY campaign for cancel-safety (R6 / cn4 cross-lane cancel isolation + x3s cancel-mid-stream — a data-race hunt across lanes); (3) DIFFERENTIAL-FUZZ-AFTER-OPTIMIZATION (fuzz each optimized path from D6.6 against its pre-opt reference). Every crash -> regression test.
DEPS: A1.4 (baseline targets, related); a4-0mk, a4-x3s, a4-bbx, a4-8pp, a4-cn4.
TEST/DoD: structure-aware targets reach deep paths; TSan finds no data races on the lane/cancel paths; the differential-after-opt pass confirms optimized == reference; detailed crash logging + committed regressions.
close_reason: Completed driver decode fuzz hardening: added required typed_decode_boundary cargo-fuzz target, manifest/CI smoke coverage, bounded fuzz campaign, protocol tests, and focused TSan cancel pass.

title: D6.4: cargo-mutants >=90% kill gate (guard+audit+decode)

CHANGE: run cargo-mutants on oraclemcp-guard (classifier), oraclemcp-audit (hash-chain), and the driver's decode boundary; require KILL-RATE >=90% on guard/audit; surviving mutants triaged (new test, or documented equivalent). Slow -> runs NIGHTLY + in the local pre-tag gate (D3.2), not every PR.

Added targeted guard/audit tests, committed mutation-safety report marker, nightly workflow, and release_preflight check-report gate. Full memory-capped script run passed at default j=1 after j=4 was cgroup-killed before complete outcomes.

title: D6.6: optimization discipline (baseline+isomorphism+regression gate)
description:
D6.6 — optimization discipline (per extreme-software-optimization). repo: oracledb (mostly).
CHANGE: the perf differentiators (x3s, 0mk, 8eo, A8 pipelining, decode-tuning) do not ship on "feels faster." Each follows: BASELINE (criterion/hyperfine, p50/p95/p99 + allocs) -> PROFILE (cargo flamegraph, hotspot in top-5) -> ISOMORPHISM PROOF (byte-identical wire/rows vs the pre-opt path) -> ONE lever per commit -> COMMIT the baseline number as a CI regression gate (REVERT if it does not beat threshold). Opportunity score >=2.0 or it is not worth the risk. Pairs with D6.2 differential-fuzz-after-optimization (correctness) — this is the measured-win half.
DEPS: a4-x3s, a4-0mk, a4-8eo, A8.
TEST/DoD: each perf bead carries a committed criterion baseline + isomorphism proof + a regression gate that fails CI on a slowdown.
close_reason: DONE. D6.6 optimization discipline landed in the DRIVER (rust-oracledb 5763e40 + docs/quality/optimization-discipline.md + scripts/check_perf_regression.sh + _quality.yml perf gate); shipped in oracledb 0.8.2 (published). Perf gate green under the 16G cap (ratios 1.03-1.10x vs 2.00x threshold).

title: D6.7: kani BMC on the safety helpers (tier-C)
description:
D6.7 — formal assurance on the safety core (per lean-formal-feedback-loop, tier-C). repo: oraclemcp.
CHANGE: beyond D6.1 (metamorphic) + D6.4 (mutation), add bounded model checking with kani (assurance tier C) on the SELF-CONTAINED, BMC-TRACTABLE safety helpers: the operating-level lattice (READ_ONLY < READ_WRITE < DDL < ADMIN is total + monotone), the danger-marker -> required-level mapping (marker implies required_level >= the marker floor), and the audit-chain step (append-only + each record MAC verifies against its predecessor). SCOPE NOTE: BMC of the end-to-end classify() over arbitrary SQL is INTRACTABLE (it runs through sqlparser); that end-to-end property stays covered by D6.1 + D6.4 — kani adds a proof floor under the small critical helpers those tests exercise. kani is a DEV/CI verifier (its CBMC backend is external tooling, like cargo-fuzz's libFuzzer); it never ships in the crates, so the pure-Rust / forbid(unsafe) posture is unaffected. (K9's redesign means the flashback path needs NO new proof — the classifier is unchanged.)
DEPS: D6.1.
TEST/DoD: kani proves the three helper properties for bounded inputs; a CI job runs them; a mutation to any helper breaks a proof.
close_reason: D6.7 Kani tier-C proofs added and verified locally: guard lattice, danger marker floor, session gate allow invariant, and audit chain-step/MAC verifier all pass under memory-capped cargo kani. Added Kani CI workflow and proof report. Normal gates green: fmt, targeted guard/audit tests, clippy, secret scan, cargo deny, diff check.

title: D6.8: pre-tag security-domain audit (gates the tag)
description:

description:

title: K9: flashback/as-of read mode (structured as_of param; classifier untouched)
description:
K9 (K.2 medium) — flashback / AS-OF read mode. repo: oraclemcp. Fail-closed invariant preserved (additive/observational). Code-validated by 3 agents; grounded in real file:line.
DESIGN (revised for safety — see the K9 discussion): a flashback query (SELECT ... AS OF SCN/TIMESTAMP) is a pure read, currently OVER-refused only because sqlparser 0.62 cannot parse the syntax. Do NOT teach the classifier to prove raw flashback SQL (that would modify the safety-critical prover). Instead add a STRUCTURED as_of {scn|timestamp} parameter to oracle_query: the agent passes a NORMAL SELECT + an as_of value; the server proves the base SELECT read-only via the EXISTING, UNCHANGED classifier, then applies the flashback itself (append AS OF SCN :scn to the proven query's table refs, OR a bounded DBMS_FLASHBACK.ENABLE_AT_SYSTEM_CHANGE_NUMBER(:scn) ... DISABLE around it). AS OF cannot turn a read into a write, so the result stays provably read-only — the classifier prover is NEVER touched and no new proof obligation is created. Better ergonomics: agents pass an SCN, not hand-written flashback SQL. FLASHBACK privilege enforced by Oracle at execution (ORA-01031 = correct fail-closed).
DEPS: B1.
TEST/DoD: oracle_query(sql=SELECT..., as_of=SCN n) on 21c/23ai returns the historical snapshot classified READ_ONLY; the base SELECT classifies IDENTICALLY with/without as_of; a non-read base SELECT is still refused BEFORE any flashback is applied.
close_reason: DONE. as_of {scn|timestamp} on oracle_query; base SELECT proven read-only by the UNCHANGED classifier first, then flashback via bounded DBMS_FLASHBACK enable/disable around the byte-unchanged query (bind-only value). Guard/classifier/purity UNTOUCHED (git-clean); GuardDecision byte-identical w/wo as_of; non-read base refused before any flashback/DB-IO; both-set/empty rejected. Cancel-safe teardown; flashback mode's own DML-refusal preserves DB-level read-only. Live-green on 23ai. api-lock rebaselined; fmt/clippy/secret_scan clean.

PHASE 2 (post-x3s): pipe the driver Stream -> SSE chunks, add a streaming param, advertise streaming in oracle_capabilities (tool-surface section, distinct from K2 ServerFeatures). close_reason: DONE (bead CHANGE spec = Stream->SSE chunks, delivered). Phase-1 incremental fetch (resume byte-identical, proven) + phase-2 cursor-chunked SSE streaming (event:chunk frames, inline stdio, tool_features advertise, budget backpressure, 50k cap). Guard untouched (DELETE+streaming refused before I/O). db api unchanged; goldens=advertisement only; fmt/clippy/api-lock/secret_scan clean. True row-by-row-to-socket = dispatch re-architecture (not driver) -> follow-up filed.

title: K10 follow-up: true row-by-row SSE streaming via a dispatch streaming channel
description: K10 delivered cursor-chunked SSE streaming (page-by-page). True row-by-row-to-socket streaming is blocked NOT by the driver (oracledb::for_each_row_ref is public at lib.rs:5386, sufficient) but by the MCP dispatch architecture: dispatch is request->single-Value-response, marshaled to a lane thread over mpsc+oneshot returning one DispatchOutcome, so the socket-owning connection thread can't receive rows as produced. FIX: a lane->bounded-mpsc->socket chunk channel (new streaming LaneCommand) or transport-driven execution — a cross-crate dispatch/lane change (safety-sensitive concurrency, design carefully). Optional driver ergonomic that would help a row-by-row consumer: an owned-row paged Stream<Item=Result<Vec<Option<QueryValue>>>> over fetch_rows_with_columns that does NOT hold &mut Connection across the yield (for_each_row_ref's callback holds &mut Connection so can't materialize LOB/structured cell content, which needs another round trip). Discovered during K10.
close_reason: Implemented true row-by-row HTTP/SSE streaming through a bounded lane channel while preserving guard-first execution and chunk fallback for complex values.

title: W0 Train infrastructure: dev pins, sibling bootstrap, pin refresh, RC integration, hygiene
description:
## Goal
Let oraclemcp consume unreleased driver (`oraclemcp-driver-cx` 0.10.0 line) and engine (`plsql-*` 0.8.0 line) work from the first commit of the train, without publishing anything to crates.io early. crates.io versions are immutable and R24 forbids extra patch releases, so each sibling is published exactly once (REL R.3/R.4) after the whole train is proven on pinned git revisions.

## Current state (measured 2026-09-23)
- oraclemcp root `Cargo.toml` pins `oraclemcp-driver-cx = "=0.9.2"`, `oraclemcp-driver-cx-protocol = "=0.9.2"` and the 13 engine crates (plsql-core, plsql-engine, plsql-catalog, plsql-depgraph, plsql-lineage, plsql-project, plsql-ir, plsql-parser-antlr, plsql-symbols, plsql-cicd, plsql-doc, plsql-sast, plsql-output) at `=0.7.0`. `deny.toml` `[sources]` has `unknown-git = "deny"` and only the crates.io registry allowed.
- rust-oracledb (public, `MuhDur/rust-oracledb`): local checkout is on `master`, **ahead 2 / behind 12** of `origin/main` (`cdc3e82`, which renamed the crates to the `oraclemcp-driver-cx` family). On `origin/main` `oraclemcp-driver-cx` is 0.9.3 (docs-only "discontinued" README republish) and `-protocol` is 0.9.2. The `Required` workflow is red on `origin/main` head since 2026-08-06; the scheduled `Canary` workflow is red daily. Beads DB reports `SCHEMA_MISMATCH`. R27 lifts the off-limits rule for this repo.
- plsql-intelligence (public, `MuhDur/plsql-intelligence`): local `main` == `origin/main` `5834197` (2026-06-30, "Complete offline pivot epic"); every crate at 0.7.0. `bindgen-roundtrip` is red (last runs 2026-08-29 and 2026-09-05, failing step "Deploy synthetic test package") and is now `disabled_inactivity` together with `usr-loop`. Beads DB reports `SCHEMA_MISMATCH`.
- Host clean-up (R16) is complete (operator deleted the 465 GB `target/` and 15 upstream branches; worktrees pruned). Remaining: 17 stashes, unmerged branches/worktrees, untracked `npm/`, `refactor/`, `web/playwright-report/`, `.skill-loop-progress.md`.

## Design (plan §19.4 steps 1 and 5, §23.3 T0.1)
1. **Dev pins (T0.1):** `[patch.crates-io]` entries point the two driver crates and the 13 engine crates at **pushed git revisions** of the public sibling repos, never local paths; `deny.toml` gets `allow-git` for exactly those two URLs. A gate in `scripts/local_release_gate.sh` and in the release.yml gate job refuses a tag while any `[patch]` or `allow-git` entry exists. The Docker/GHCR build is proven to fetch the git dependencies.
2. **Bootstrap (T0.2a/T0.3a):** each sibling first pushes a revision oraclemcp can pin; repo health (T0.2b/T0.3b) repairs trackers and CI.
3. **Pin refresh (T0.6 engine, T0.7 driver):** whenever oraclemcp consumes a later producer change, the producer revision is pushed and one coordinated oraclemcp consumer commit refreshes the `rev`, the exact requirement and `Cargo.lock`. The refresh repeats as a child bead each time (every producer-repo fix found by T9.6a also needs a following T0.6/T0.7 refresh child that blocks T9.6b).
4. **RC integration (T0.5):** each producer version bump (engine 0.8.0, driver 0.10.0) lands as one atomic explicit-path commit in its own repo; the immediately following oraclemcp consumer commit refreshes revs, exact requirements and lockfile. Neither commit is eligible for a release tag on its own.
5. **Hygiene close-out (T0.4):** the §17 tracker/host items are closed with evidence; remaining stashes/branches reviewed; deletions only on exact operator commands.

## Invariants
- Rule 17: a version requirement moves in the same commit as the producer bump or rev refresh it matches (a `[patch]` whose version does not satisfy the requirement is silently unused by cargo).
- Never local `path` patches in a commit; only pushed revisions of the public repos.
- No tag while any dev pin exists (T0.1 gate); R.5 removes the pins.
- Binding rules: RULE 1 (no file/dir deletion without an exact in-session operator command); commit only explicit paths (`git commit -- <path>...`, then `git show --stat HEAD`, constitution #18); never `-a`/`git add -A`; pushes and tags need the operator's go-ahead; confidentiality (#9): no live-OCI, customer or field identifiers in any committed artifact, synthetic only; close only through `scripts/bead_tracker_guard.sh close` with committed evidence (implementers never self-close); workspace-wide cargo runs go through `scripts/build_lease.sh` with a dedicated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.

## Acceptance (epic)
All children closed with evidence; at R.5 the pins are gone and both sibling versions resolve from crates.io in a clean `cargo fetch`.

## Size
9 tasks (T0.1, T0.2a, T0.2b, T0.3a, T0.3b, T0.6, T0.7, T0.5, T0.4) plus repeated T0.6/T0.7 refresh children.

## Dependencies
T0.6 waits on T7.2/T7.3; T0.7 on T9.3, T9.4a, T9.5a, T8.1, T8.13; T0.5 on T7.1, T0.6, T0.7, T0.2b, T0.3b. Consumers: T7.4 and T7.7 need T0.1; T9.5b and T9.7 need T0.7; T9.6a and R.0 need T0.5.

## Children
T0.1, T0.2a, T0.2b, T0.3a, T0.3b, T0.6, T0.7, T0.5, T0.4

title: Dev pins: [patch.crates-io] to pushed sibling revs, allow-git, tag-refusal gate, Docker
description:
## Context
The train ships driver 0.10.0, engine 0.8.0 and oraclemcp 0.12.0 together (R25). oraclemcp must build against unreleased sibling work from the first commit, but crates.io versions are immutable and R24 forbids extra patch releases, so siblings are published exactly once at R.3/R.4. The mechanism is dev pins (plan §19.4 step 1, §23.3 T0.1). This is the **first oraclemcp consumer commit** of the train.

Measured state at `1fbe6eb0`/`8b788a0b`:
- Root `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.dependencies]`: `oraclemcp-driver-cx = { version = "=0.9.2", default-features = false }`, `oraclemcp-driver-cx-protocol = { version = "=0.9.2", default-features = false }`, and the 13 engine crates (plsql-core, plsql-engine, plsql-catalog, plsql-depgraph, plsql-lineage, plsql-project, plsql-ir, plsql-parser-antlr, plsql-symbols, plsql-cicd, plsql-doc, plsql-sast, plsql-output) at `=0.7.0`, `default-features = false`.
- Driver `origin/main` (`cdc3e82`): `oraclemcp-driver-cx` is **0.9.3** (docs-only republish), `-protocol` is 0.9.2. A `[patch]` whose version does not satisfy the requirement is silently not used by cargo, so the requirement moves in the same commit as the patch (rule 17).
- `deny.toml` `[sources]`: `unknown-git = "deny"`, `allow-registry = ["https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"]`; it would reject git patches.
- Release gate chain today: `release.yml` job `checks` ("release gates") step "Validate release metadata" runs `scripts/release_preflight.sh`, which calls `scripts/local_release_gate_check.sh` (proof required on tag refs). `scripts/local_release_gate.sh` writes the D3.2 proof.
- `Dockerfile` builder stage: `COPY . .` then `cargo build --locked --release -p oraclemcp --features dashboard-bundle,oracledb` (plus a `builder-plsql-intelligence` stage until T7.4 removes it) on `oraclelinux:9` with `ENV CI=true`.
Both sibling repos are public: `https://github.com/MuhDur/rust-oracledb`, `https://github.com/MuhDur/plsql-intelligence`.

## Outcome
oraclemcp `main` resolves `oraclemcp-driver-cx`, `oraclemcp-driver-cx-protocol` and the 13 engine crates from pushed git revisions of the public sibling repos (T0.2a and T0.3a SHAs), `cargo deny check` passes with exactly two `allow-git` URLs, any attempt to tag while a `[patch]`/`allow-git`/git lock source exists is refused locally and in release.yml, and the Docker/GHCR build is proven to fetch the git dependencies.

## Deliverable
- Repo: oraclemcp.
- `Cargo.toml` (root): new `[patch.crates-io]` table with 15 entries: `oraclemcp-driver-cx` and `oraclemcp-driver-cx-protocol` -> `{ git = "https://github.com/MuhDur/rust-oracledb", rev = "<T0.2a pushed sha>" }`; each of the 13 engine crates -> `{ git = "https://github.com/MuhDur/plsql-intelligence", rev = "<T0.3a pushed sha>" }`. In the same commit, `[workspace.dependencies]` `oraclemcp-driver-cx` requirement -> the exact version at the pinned rev (`=0.9.3` if T0.2a's rev keeps 0.9.3); `-protocol` stays `=0.9.2` unless the rev differs; engine stays `=0.7.0`. Update the explanatory comments above those entries (re-derive with `rg -n 'driver-cx|plsql-' Cargo.toml`).
- `Cargo.lock`: regenerated; the 15 crates (and their git-resolved transitive siblings, e.g. `oraclemcp-driver-cx-derive`, `plsql-parser`, `plsql-support`) show `source = "git+https://github.com/MuhDur/...?rev=<sha>#<sha>"`.
- `deny.toml` `[sources]`: `allow-git = ["https://github.com/MuhDur/rust-oracledb", "https://github.com/MuhDur/plsql-intelligence"]` with a comment "removed by R.5".
- `scripts/local_release_gate_check.sh`: new mode `--refuse-dev-pins` (function `refuse_dev_pins`), shared by both call sites: fails when (a) root `Cargo.toml` has any `[patch.*]` table, (b) `deny.toml` `sources.allow-git` is non-empty, or (c) `Cargo.lock` contains any `source = "git+` line. Parsing uses `python3 -c 'import tomllib'` (no new dependency).
- `scripts/local_release_gate.sh`: calls `local_release_gate_check.sh --refuse-dev-pins` before writing a `--commit-proof`.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` job `checks`: new step "Refuse dev pins" (runs `bash scripts/local_release_gate_check.sh --refuse-dev-pins`) gated on `startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')`, placed before "Validate release metadata".
- No new files.

## Implementation notes
1. Wait for T0.2a and T0.3a to report their pushed SHAs (both must be reachable on `origin/main` of the public repos; `git ls-remote` proves it).
2. Add the `[patch.crates-io]` table and move the driver-cx requirement in one edit; run `cargo metadata --format-version 1 --locked` after `cargo update -p <each patched crate>` (never a blanket `cargo update`, which would drift unrelated crates).
3. Check cargo emits no "Patch `...` was not used in the crate graph" warning; that warning means a version/requirement mismatch and is a failure.
4. Add `allow-git`; run `cargo deny check` and `cargo deny --features oraclemcp/dashboard-bundle,oraclemcp-core/dashboard-bundle check` (both invocations used by the `supply-chain` lane).
5. Implement `refuse_dev_pins`: only refuses in tag context (`RELEASE_TAG` set, `GITHUB_REF_TYPE=tag` or `refs/tags/*`), or unconditionally when invoked with `--refuse-dev-pins` explicitly; print each offending entry as `field -> found -> expected none`.
6. Build `cargo check -p oraclemcp` (default features) and `cargo check -p oraclemcp --features plsql-intelligence` against the pins (scoped `-p`, no lease needed), then `scripts/build_lease.sh -- cargo test --workspace` once.
7. Docker proof: `docker build --target runtime .` (and the PL/SQL target while it exists) from a clean clone with no `~/.cargo` mounted; capture the log lines `Updating git repository https://github.com/MuhDur/rust-oracledb` and `...plsql-intelligence` and the final binary `oraclemcp info` showing the driver and engine versions. If the container cannot fetch git (e.g. missing CA certs), fix it in the Dockerfile (`ca-certificates` is already installed; `CARGO_NET_GIT_FETCH_WITH_CLI` only if libgit2 fails).
8. Known effect: `release.yml` `workflow_dispatch` rehearsals run `cargo package --workspace --locked --no-verify`; with git patches this is expected to be unrepresentative until R.5. Tags are refused by the new gate anyway.
9. Commit Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, deny.toml, the two scripts and release.yml as explicit paths in one commit (rule 17: patch + requirement + lock are one logical change).

## Test plan
- `tests/release_contract_test.sh` new cases (offline, temp copies of the three manifests): `dev_pins_refuse_tag_patch_entry` (a `[patch.crates-io]` table -> refused), `dev_pins_refuse_tag_allow_git` (non-empty `allow-git` -> refused), `dev_pins_refuse_tag_git_lock_source` (a `git+` lock source without any `[patch]` -> refused), `dev_pins_clean_manifest_passes` (current post-R.5 shape -> exit 0), `dev_pins_non_tag_run_is_not_refused` (dev pins present, no tag context, no explicit flag -> exit 0). Each case logs a JSONL line `{case, expected, actual, exit}` to the e2e artifact dir.
- `cargo deny check` (both invocations) green in the `supply-chain` lane.
- Workspace build/test green through the build lease; `cargo metadata` excerpt proving the git sources is attached to the close evidence.
- Docker build log excerpt (sanitized) attached to the close evidence.

## Proof split
This bead proves the pins resolve, the supply-chain policy admits exactly them, the tag gate refuses them, and Docker fetches them. T0.6/T0.7 prove each later refresh; T0.5 proves the RC versions; R.5 proves their removal and crates.io resolution; R.7 proves the tag pipeline passes the gate after removal.

## Non-goals
- Bumping sibling versions (T0.5) or refreshing revisions (T0.6/T0.7).
- Making PL/SQL-intelligence a default feature or removing the Docker variant (T7.4).
- Any change to the sibling repos.

## No-claim boundary
Green here does not prove the siblings' own CI is green (T0.2b/T0.3b), that release.yml's cross-compiled targets fetch git deps (exercised at R.1 rehearsal), or anything about crates.io resolution (R.5).

## Considerations
- Rule 17: `[patch]`, requirement and `Cargo.lock` land in one commit; a split breaks every other agent's build.
- Hot file: `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`/`deny.toml` are the `file-lane:cargo-manifest` lane shared with T0.5, T0.6, T0.7, T7.4 and R.5; take a file reservation.
- Never commit a `path =` patch; a local path would make the build machine-specific and is refused in review.
- The refusal must be fail-closed: any parse error in the three files is a refusal in tag context, not a skip.
- Binding rules: RULE 1 (no file/dir deletion without an exact in-session operator command); commit only explicit paths (`git commit -- <path>...`, then `git show --stat HEAD`, constitution #18); never `-a`/`git add -A`; pushes and tags need the operator's go-ahead; confidentiality (#9): no live-OCI, customer or field identifiers in any committed artifact, synthetic only; close only through `scripts/bead_tracker_guard.sh close` with committed evidence (implementers never self-close); workspace-wide cargo runs go through `scripts/build_lease.sh` with a dedicated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.

## Absorbs
None.

A `crates/plsql-mcp` directory remains although `plsql-mcp` is retired and not a workspace member. oraclemcp requires 13 of them at `=0.7.0`: plsql-core, plsql-engine, plsql-catalog, plsql-depgraph, plsql-lineage, plsql-project, plsql-ir, plsql-parser-antlr, plsql-symbols, plsql-cicd, plsql-doc, plsql-sast, plsql-output.

## Outcome
A recorded, pushed engine SHA (expected `5834197` unless a fix is needed) from which cargo can resolve all 13 required crates at 0.7.0 over git, including every build-time input (notably the ANTLR-generated parser sources used by `plsql-parser-antlr`).

## Deliverable
- Repo: plsql-intelligence. No code change unless the git checkout cannot build (then: the minimal fix, committed with explicit paths and pushed).
- Bead comment: the SHA, `cargo metadata` excerpt for the 13 crates, and the build proof.

## Implementation notes
1. `git fetch`; confirm `main` == `origin/main`.

title: Engine pin refresh: push T7.2/T7.3 engine rev; refresh oraclemcp patch rev + Cargo.lock
description:
## Context
Plan §19.4 step 1: oraclemcp consumes later producer changes only through pushed git revisions; each refresh is one coordinated oraclemcp consumer commit that updates the git `rev`, the exact requirement (unchanged at `=0.7.0` until T0.5) and `Cargo.lock`. T7.2 (engine soundness gaps 1-5 + `RoutineEffectsV1` + `InvocationClosureV1`) and T7.3 (engine parser fuzz targets) land in plsql-intelligence; T7.7 (engine adapter in oraclemcp) consumes them. The refresh **repeats as a child bead** whenever a later engine change is consumed (T7.1 gap children, T9.6a findings in the engine): each such child blocks its consumer, and for T9.6a findings it also blocks T9.6b.

## Outcome
oraclemcp `main` resolves all 13 engine crates (plsql-core, plsql-engine, plsql-catalog, plsql-depgraph, plsql-lineage, plsql-project, plsql-ir, plsql-parser-antlr, plsql-symbols, plsql-cicd, plsql-doc, plsql-sast, plsql-output) from the pushed engine revision that contains the T7.2/T7.3 work, and oraclemcp's tier-A gates (including the PL/SQL feature build) are green on that consumer commit.

## Deliverable
- plsql-intelligence: the pushed SHA containing T7.2 and T7.3 (no new engine code in this bead).
- oraclemcp: root `Cargo.toml` `[patch.crates-io]` `rev` for the 13 engine entries; `Cargo.lock`. One explicit-path commit.
- Bead comment with old rev -> new rev and the consumer commit SHA.

## Implementation notes
1. Confirm T7.2 and T7.3 are merged on engine `origin/main`; record the SHA (`git ls-remote`).
2. Edit the 13 `rev =` values; `cargo update -p <crate>` for each patched engine crate only.
3. Build `cargo check -p oraclemcp --features plsql-intelligence` (or default features once T7.4 makes it default), then `scripts/build_lease.sh -- cargo test --workspace` and the PL/SQL lane command.
4. Commit `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` together (rule 17).
5. For every later consumption, create a child `T0.6.<n>` with the same steps and the consuming bead as the blocked task.

## Test plan
- `cargo metadata --locked` shows the new rev for all 13 crates.
- oraclemcp tier-A lanes (ci.yml) green on the consumer commit; read the verdict yourself.

## Proof split
Proves the consumer resolves and builds the refreshed engine. Engine behaviour is proved by T7.2/T7.3 and their oraclemcp consumers (T7.7, T7.9, T4.9).

## Non-goals
- Engine code changes; version bumps (T0.5).

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove the engine changes are correct.

## Considerations
- Rule 17: rev + lock in one commit. Hot lane `file-lane:cargo-manifest`.
- All 13 engine entries must point at the same rev (mixed revs would link two engine copies).
- Binding rules: RULE 1 (no file/dir deletion without an exact in-session operator command); commit only explicit paths (`git commit -- <path>...`, then `git show --stat HEAD`, constitution #18); never `-a`/`git add -A`; pushes and tags need the operator's go-ahead; confidentiality (#9): no live-OCI, customer or field identifiers in any committed artifact, synthetic only; close only through `scripts/bead_tracker_guard.sh close` with committed evidence (implementers never self-close); workspace-wide cargo runs go through `scripts/build_lease.sh` with a dedicated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.

## Absorbs
None.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: All 13 engine `[patch.crates-io]` entries in oraclemcp name the same pushed engine SHA that contains T7.2 and T7.3, and `Cargo.lock` agrees.
- [ ] Negative: A refresh that updates `Cargo.toml` but not `Cargo.lock` (or vice versa) fails `cargo metadata --locked`; a mixed-rev state (some crates on the old rev) is rejected by the check `rg -c 'rev = "<new sha>"' Cargo.toml` returning 13 for the engine URL.
- [ ] Tests: oraclemcp ci.yml tier-A lanes green on the consumer commit, including the PL/SQL feature build/tests.
- [ ] Proof class: CI run on the exact consumer SHA; forbidden substitutes: a local path patch, an unpushed engine commit.
- [ ] Consumers: T7.7, T0.5, T9.6b (refresh children).
- [ ] No-claim: Does not prove engine correctness.

title: RC sibling integration: engine 0.8.0 + driver 0.10.0 bumps, READMEs, consumer pin commit
description:
## Context
Plan §19.4 step 1: "Each producer version bump lands as one atomic explicit-path commit in its own repository. The immediately following coordinated consumer commit in oraclemcp refreshes the pushed git revision, the exact requirement and `Cargo.lock`. Neither commit is eligible for a release tag on its own." Target versions (TL;DR): engine **0.8.0** (from 0.7.0), driver **0.10.0** (from `oraclemcp-driver-cx` 0.9.3 / `-protocol` 0.9.2 / `-derive` 0.9.2). The driver is "maintained again" (R12): its crates.io README (`crates/oracledb/README.md` and any README the driver-cx package points at) loses the "discontinued" disclaimer added by `69ea00f` and republished in 0.9.3 (`cdc3e82`). Depends on: T7.1 (engine completeness controller closed), T0.6/T0.7 (latest refreshes), T0.2b/T0.3b (sibling repo health). Later fixes after this bead stay at 0.10.0/0.8.0 (unpublished) and are consumed through further T0.6/T0.7 refresh children.

## Outcome
Driver `origin/main` carries 0.10.0 for all three published driver crates with an honest README; engine `origin/main` carries 0.8.0 for every published `plsql-*` crate; oraclemcp `main` pins `=0.10.0`/`=0.8.0` against those pushed candidate SHAs in one consumer commit, with tier-A green.

## Deliverable
- rust-oracledb (one commit): workspace `version` -> 0.10.0; `crates/oracledb/Cargo.toml` explicit `version = "0.9.3"` -> 0.10.0 (remove the docs-only republish comment); inter-crate requirements (`oraclemcp-driver-cx-protocol`, `oraclemcp-driver-cx-derive`) -> 0.10.0; README(s) without the discontinued disclaimer, stating the driver is maintained and primary for oraclemcp; package metadata complete (`description`, `repository`, `documentation`, `readme`); release-surface files used by `scripts/check_release_surface_versions.sh` / `scripts/release_surface_manifest.py` updated. The CHANGELOG entry is R.0.
- plsql-intelligence (one commit): workspace `version` 0.7.0 -> 0.8.0 and every intra-workspace `plsql-*` requirement; metadata complete for every published crate.
- oraclemcp (one commit): `[workspace.dependencies]` `oraclemcp-driver-cx`/`-protocol` -> `=0.10.0`, 13 engine crates -> `=0.8.0`; `[patch.crates-io]` revs -> the two candidate SHAs; `Cargo.lock`. Comments in `Cargo.toml` that name 0.9.2 updated.

## Implementation notes
1. Driver bump: edit versions with the release-surface tooling the driver already has; run its fmt/clippy/test and the `Required` profile locally; commit explicit paths; push (operator go-ahead); read the `Required` verdict.
2. Engine bump: same; `CI` + `bindgen-roundtrip` verdicts.
3. Consumer commit: requirement + rev + lock in one commit (rule 17); tier-A green on it.
4. Record both candidate SHAs in the bead comment; R.1 freezes these (or later refreshed) SHAs.
5. Grep sibling repos for stale version strings: `rg -n '0\.9\.[23]' crates/*/Cargo.toml README.md` (driver), `rg -n '0\.7\.0' crates/*/Cargo.toml` (engine) must return nothing.

## Test plan
- Driver `Required` and engine `CI` green on the candidate SHAs.
- oraclemcp tier-A green on the consumer commit; `cargo metadata --locked` shows versions 0.10.0/0.8.0 from the git revs.

## Considerations
- Rule 17 per repo: a version bump and every requirement that names it are one commit.
- Nothing is tagged here; tags are R.3/R.4/R.7 only.
- Binding rules: RULE 1 (no file/dir deletion without an exact in-session operator command); commit only explicit paths (`git commit -- <path>...`, then `git show --stat HEAD`, constitution #18); never `-a`/`git add -A`; pushes and tags need the operator's go-ahead; confidentiality (#9): no live-OCI, customer or field identifiers in any committed artifact, synthetic only; close only through `scripts/bead_tracker_guard.sh close` with committed evidence (implementers never self-close); workspace-wide cargo runs go through `scripts/build_lease.sh` with a dedicated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.

title: W7: PL/SQL-intelligence stable, built into every artifact, custom PL/SQL tools
description:
## Goal
Operator rulings R13 (PL/SQL-intelligence is part of oraclemcp: stable, fully integrated, no gaps, no stubs, nothing untested; custom PL/SQL tools enabled) and R14 (custom PL/SQL tools ship in 0.12.0 and may run in parallel with the rest). R25: nothing deferred. R34: no process ceremony.

## Current state (measured 2026-09-23; oraclemcp 1fbe6eb0, plsql-intelligence 5834197)
- Classifier core works and is fail-closed (sqlparser AST; highest level wins; fail-closed default `75f956c1`).
- Served classifiers have no engine: `DEFAULT_CLASSIFIER` (`crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/mod.rs`, static `LazyLock`) uses `UnknownOracle` for execute/compile/patch/create, re-checked at apply. `READ_PRECHECK_CLASSIFIER` + `ensure_resolved_read_only`. `GENERATED_READ_CLASSIFIER` trusts only `DBMS_LOB.SUBSTR`, `DBMS_METADATA.GET_DDL`, `DBMS_XPLAN.DISPLAY`.
- User functions in SELECT are always refused (`classifier.rs`). BEGIN/DECLARE/CALL/EXEC are refused at every level (`unanalyzable_plsql_construct`); CALL's `ObjectRef` has only schema + name; BEGIN only admits `NULL;` and one `DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE` form; CREATE of PL/SQL needs >= DDL.
- The B12a pure-function allowlist (`OperatorPureFunctionRestriction`, `purity.rs`) has no effect: it can only narrow an independent proof and the served path has none.
- 9 PL/SQL tools (`crates/oraclemcp/src/plsql_tools.rs`: oracle_plsql_parse, _analyze, _what_breaks, _lineage, _sast, _doc offline; oracle_lineage, oracle_plsql_live_snapshot, oracle_plsql_blast_radius live-catalog) behind the off-by-default `plsql-intelligence` feature; 13 engine crates pinned `=0.7.0` in the root `Cargo.toml`.
- Engine purity oracle `PlsqlSideEffectOracle` is test-only (`ge6xe.2` open).
- Artifacts: `release.yml` builds `dashboard-bundle,oracledb` only; the PL/SQL image exists only as the manual `docker.yml` variant (`runtime-plsql-intelligence` stage); the CI `plsql-intelligence` lane is `continue-on-error` (hosted-runner OOM).
- Custom tools: `tools.d/*.toml`, HMAC v2, load-time ceiling check (B12b), re-check at apply; `call=` (Form B) rejected at load (`crates/oraclemcp-core/src/custom_tools.rs`); scalar output unsupported.
- Engine repo: last commit 2026-06-30; `bindgen-roundtrip` CI red since 2026-09-05; beads `SCHEMA_MISMATCH`.

Engine soundness gaps (plan §9.1, measured at plsql-intelligence 5834197 / oraclemcp 1fbe6eb0): (1) only three verdicts (`oraclemcp_guard::Purity` = ProvenReadOnly / ProvenSideEffecting / Unknown), so DML, DDL and COMMIT are indistinguishable; (2) no depgraph edges for COMMIT/ROLLBACK or `PRAGMA AUTONOMOUS_TRANSACTION`, although the IR models `Statement::TransactionControl` / `Statement::ExecuteImmediate` (`plsql-ir/src/stmt.rs`); `plsql_depgraph::EdgeKind` has no transaction/autonomous variant; (3) FAIL-OPEN: a routine without outgoing edges counts as `ProvenReadOnly` (`PlsqlSideEffectOracle::routine_node_purity` starts from ProvenReadOnly), so unloaded SYS calls (UTL_HTTP, DBMS_*) may pass; (4) case-insensitive fallback in `PlsqlSideEffectOracle::resolve_candidates` (`eq_ignore_ascii_case`); (5) `CompletenessPosture::Partial` still counts as trusted (`from_analysis_run`).

## Design
1. Engine repo (§9.2): audit the whole repo (stubs, `todo!`/`unimplemented!`/placeholders, dead crates, coverage per crate, parser fuzz); every stub implemented or removed; fix the five soundness gaps with a test each; repair CI/tracker (W0/W5 beads); release 0.8.0 of the crates oraclemcp consumes plus their deps. `plsql-mcp` stays retired.
2. Built in (§9.3): PL/SQL-intelligence is a default feature of the `oraclemcp` crate and ships in all 7 target archives and the single GHCR image (Docker variants removed). The engine is pure Rust; ANTLR/Java only behind the off-by-default `antlr-codegen` feature, and a release gate asserts `PLSQL_ANTLR_REGEN` unset and `antlr-codegen` off. Resource envelope measured; CI OOM fixed by runner sizing/build settings, never by shrinking the product; size budget (today warn 43 MB / hard 48 MB) set to measured + headroom. Artifact acceptance runs `--version`, `doctor`, `tools/list` on every archive target and the GHCR image on a native runner or declared emulator and asserts all 9 PL/SQL tools. The CI lane becomes required.
3. Custom PL/SQL tools (§9.4), fail-closed throughout. W7 invariants (plan §9.4, binding on every W7 bead): a routine that can't be proven stays refused; effects map to a required level; identity is exact and the whole call closure is pinned by hash; everything is re-checked at apply (SEC-1); DML rolls back by default; nothing ever auto-commits (AGENTS.md); caller text is never concatenated into PL/SQL.
   - Step 1 `RoutineEffectsV1` effect SET `{ReadDb, RowLock, SessionState, Dml, Ddl, Admin, SequenceAdvance, OperatorOnly(OperatorStatementClass), TxnControl, Autonomous, DynamicSql, ExternalIo, Unknown}`, one context-specific admission function, level derivation (ReadDb->READ_ONLY; RowLock/SessionState/Dml->READ_WRITE; Ddl->DDL; Admin->ADMIN); always refused in 0.12: TxnControl, Autonomous, unresolved DynamicSql, ExternalIo, Unknown, SequenceAdvance, OperatorOnly. `InvocationClosureV1` unions selected overload + transitive callees + spec/body declaration initializers + package-body initialization section + evaluated default-parameter expressions.
   - `Unknown` by construction (always refused; each case has a unit test asserting `Unknown`): wrapped bodies (`ALL_SOURCE` shows `wrapped`); any unresolved or data-dependent `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` (dynamic text built from a parameter, variable, table, function call, conditional concatenation or external input); any `DBMS_SQL`, `DBMS_SCHEDULER`, `DBMS_PIPE`, `DBMS_AQ` or `UTL_*` call; Java stored procedures and external procedures; `AUTHID CURRENT_USER` units in v1 (they resolve unqualified names in the caller's schema at run time, so the closure proven at load isn't the closure executed); any callee whose source the profile can't read; any SYS/SYSTEM routine absent from the committed, reviewed, tighten-only allowlist `sys_effects.toml`; ambiguous overloads; any closure member with `STATUS <> 'VALID'`. Exception (PL/SQL can only issue DDL through dynamic SQL): a single compile-time string literal used by `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` may be folded by the engine, parsed and classified recursively; on success its inner effects replace `DynamicSql`, otherwise it stays `DynamicSql`/`Unknown`; no caller value may contribute to the text; literal dynamic SQL propagates `OperatorOnly` (never reduced to `Admin`).
   - Step 2 exact identity `RoutineRef { schema, package?, member, overload }`; step 3 sound engine adapter (Clean + exact identity only); step 4 per-database fact store with whole-closure keys; step 5 served binding (proven read-only functions clear in `oracle_query`); shared collectors `MutationEffectClosureV1` and `DdlEffectClosureV1`; step 6 structured, signed package-call custom tools with live activation, named-notation wrapper, name-capture check, DDL one-shot execution model, masked-profile output refusal; step 7 SEC-1 re-check + quarantine; step 8 output shaping; step 9 gates; step 10 operator UX.
   - Also: ANTLR-parser over-refusal reduction (`ge6xe.4`, tighten-only) and OLS/RAS/Data Redaction detection -> refuse (`nn3ne`).

## Invariants
The fail-closed guard is sacred and tighten-only (AGENTS.md). Never bypass the classifier; never let elevation exceed `max_level`; never make a `protected` profile writable; never auto-commit DML; never admit a statement the classifier can't prove safe for the active level. `sec`-labelled children need a second-agent review before the batch verify.

## Acceptance (workstream)
- Engine 0.8.0: no production-reachable stub (T7.1 controller closes only after T7.1b), each soundness gap closed with a test, parser fuzz targets running.
- All 9 PL/SQL tools present in every archive and the single GHCR image; CI lane required and green; size budget = measured + headroom.
- Proven read-only functions clear in `oracle_query`; every Unknown-by-construction case refused with a unit test; every §9.4 step-9 W4 case green on FREE 23ai (tier A) and XE 18/21 + ADB (tier C via T9.6).

## Size and dependencies
Largest-risk workstream (20 tasks). Engine 0.8.0 is a prerequisite only for step 5 (T7.9) and whatever depends on it. T7.5 (step 1) is a standalone early seam consumed by W12, W13 and W14. Hot files: `classifier.rs` (`file-lane:classifier`) and `dispatch/mod.rs` (`file-lane:dispatch`) are shared with W1/W2/W3/W13/W14; land seams first, take file reservations. If W7 threatens the release date, the operator decides whether it ships in this train; the plan does not quietly shrink it (§24).

## Children
T7.1 (controller epic; children T7.1a, T7.1b and every T7.1a discovery), T7.2a, T7.2, T7.3, T7.4, T7.5, T7.6, T7.7, T7.8, T7.9, T7.9a, T7.9b, T7.10, T7.11, T7.12, T7.13, T7.14, T7.15, T7.16.

title: Engine completeness controller: close only when all discovered gaps and the rescan pass
description:
## Context
R13 requires PL/SQL-intelligence to be stable with "no gaps, no stubs, nothing untested". Plan §9.2 step 1: audit the whole engine repo (`/home/durakovic/projects/plsql-intelligence`, 0.7.0 at 5834197) for stubs, `todo!`/`unimplemented!`/placeholder code, dead crates, per-crate test coverage and parser fuzz targets; every stub is implemented or removed; nothing ships half-done. Definition used by this controller: "no stubs" = no production-reachable placeholder behaviour; test doubles are not defects. This epic is graph structure only (R34 anti-ceremony audit: kept because it makes discovered bugs required release work; it creates no artifacts).

## Outcome
T7.1 closes only when (a) every child bead created by T7.1a (`discovered-from:T7.1a`) is closed with evidence, and (b) T7.1b's rescan passes on a SHA that is at or after every child's landing commit. R.1 requires zero open descendants under this epic.

## Deliverable
- No code of its own. Children: T7.1a (inventory, spawns one bounded child per production gap), T7.1b (final rescan), plus every discovered child.
- Graph rule (plan §23.1): every child created by T7.1a blocks T7.1b and is parented under T7.1.

## Implementation notes
1. Wait for T7.1a to file its discovered children (each parented to T7.1, `discovered-from:T7.1a`, blocking T7.1b).
2. Children are worked like any leaf; each carries its own test.
3. T7.1b runs last; its evidence records the tested SHA and is invalid once any blocking child lands a later commit.
4. Close through `scripts/bead_tracker_guard.sh close` citing the T7.1b evidence.

## Test plan
No tests of its own. The rescan evidence of T7.1b (deterministic inventory output with zero unresolved production-reachable gaps, at a named SHA) is the closing proof.

## Proof split
Proves nothing by itself; T7.1a proves the inventory is complete and deterministic, each child proves its own fix, T7.1b proves nothing unresolved remains.

## Non-goals
No new process artifacts, dashboards or reports. Soundness gaps 1-5 are owned by T7.2/T7.2a/T7.7, fuzz by T7.3, not by this controller.

## No-claim boundary
A closed controller does not prove the engine's analysis is sound for effects (T7.2/T7.7/T7.13 prove that) nor that oraclemcp has no stubs (R.1 runs `/mock-code-finder` on oraclemcp).

## Considerations
- Closes only when every discovered child closes AND the T7.1b rescan passes (plan §23.2, §23.1 "discovered children block the final task").
- R.1 depends on this epic (zero open descendants).
- Governance: AGENTS.md constitution binds (commit explicit paths, rule 17 atomicity, never weaken the fail-closed guard, confidentiality: synthetic fixtures only, no customer/OCI/field identifiers). Line numbers are hints at 1fbe6eb0 (oraclemcp) / 5834197 (plsql-intelligence); re-derive with `rg -n`.

## Absorbs
None.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: Every bead with `discovered-from:T7.1a` is closed with committed evidence.
- [ ] Positive: T7.1b evidence names a tested SHA that is at or after the landing commit of every discovered child and reports zero unresolved production-reachable gaps.
- [ ] Negative: If any discovered child lands a commit after the T7.1b evidence SHA, the epic is not closable until T7.1b reruns.
- [ ] Tests: T7.1b rescan evidence file; `br dep tree` of T7.1 shows no open descendant.
- [ ] Proof class: offline (engine repo inventory + unit tests); forbidden substitutes: closing on a partial inventory, closing children without their own test.
- [ ] Consumers: T0.5, R.1, R.2.
- [ ] No-claim: Does not prove effect-analysis soundness or oraclemcp-side completeness.

title: Inventory the engine repo by crate/symbol/reachability; file one child per gap
description:
## Context
Plan §9.2 step 1 / R13 "no gaps, no stubs, nothing untested". The engine repo (`/home/durakovic/projects/plsql-intelligence`, workspace `Cargo.toml` members: plsql-core, -output, -render, -store, -engine, -catalog, -depgraph, -ir, -privileges, -symbols, -parser, -parser-antlr, -project, -doc, -bindgen, -lineage, -sast, -cicd, -support, -accretion plus tools/corpus-bench, corpus-grow, corpus-license-check, plan-lint, usr-loop) was last changed 2026-06-30 ("offline pivot"; `plsql-mcp` retired). Measured hints at 5834197: a `crates/plsql-mcp` directory still exists outside the workspace members; `fuzz/Cargo.toml` still references `plsql-mcp` and `oraclemcp-core = "=0.4.1"` / `oraclemcp-db = "=0.4.1"` under a `live-mcp` feature; `rg -c 'todo!|unimplemented!|placeholder|stub'` hits concentrate in `plsql-bindgen/src/emit.rs`, `plsql-accretion/src/proposer.rs`, `plsql-symbols/src/dynamic_sql.rs`, `plsql-bindgen/src/overload.rs`, `plsql-ir/src/table_stub.rs` (not yet classified; many are likely generated-code text or test names). Definition: "no stubs" = no production-reachable placeholder behaviour; test doubles are not defects.

## Outcome
A deterministic, re-runnable inventory classifies every candidate by crate, symbol and reachability from the crates oraclemcp consumes (the 13 pinned: plsql-core, -engine, -catalog, -depgraph, -lineage, -project, -ir, -parser-antlr, -symbols, -cicd, -doc, -sast, -output, plus their transitive workspace deps), and one bounded child bead exists for every concrete production-reachable gap, each with its own test.

## Deliverable
- Engine repo: a deterministic inventory command (extend an existing script under the engine repo's `scripts/` or `tools/` rather than adding a new tool; re-derive) whose output lists: crate, file, symbol, marker kind (`todo!`, `unimplemented!`, `panic!("not implemented")`, placeholder return, `#[ignore]`d test, dead crate/module), reachability (production-reachable from a consumed crate's public API / test-only / dead), and per-crate test counts.
- Child beads: one per concrete production-reachable gap, `discovered-from:T7.1a`, parent T7.1, blocking T7.1b, each naming the symbol and the test that proves the fix.
- A disposition for every dead crate/directory (e.g. `crates/plsql-mcp`, the stale `fuzz` `live-mcp` feature): implement, keep with reason, or propose removal.

## Implementation notes
1. Run `/codebase-archaeology` + `/mock-code-finder` on the engine repo (plan §18 skill mapping for W7).
2. Build the reachability view from the 13 consumed crates' public APIs (`cargo metadata` + `rg` over symbols); anything reachable only from `#[cfg(test)]`, `tests/`, `benches/` or `tools/` is test-only.
3. Classify every marker; sort output by crate/file/symbol so two runs on one SHA are byte-identical.
4. For every production-reachable gap, file a child bead (small, bounded, own test, owner repo plsql). Coverage gaps (a consumed public function with no test) also become children.
5. Record the inventory output and the SHA in the T7.1a evidence.

## Test plan
- Determinism: run the inventory twice on the same SHA; outputs byte-identical (recorded in evidence).
- Planted check: a temporary local `todo!()` in a consumed public function is reported as production-reachable (run in a scratch worktree, not committed).
- Each child bead carries its own test; T7.1a itself adds no product tests.

## Proof split
Proves the inventory and the child list; each child proves its fix; T7.1b proves nothing remains.

## Non-goals
Fixing gaps inside this bead (children do that), soundness gaps 1-5 (T7.2/T7.2a/T7.7), fuzz targets (T7.3), CI/tracker repair (T0.3b, T5.4).

## No-claim boundary
An empty gap list at T7.1a time does not prove later commits introduce none (T7.1b rescans).

## Considerations
- RULE 1: deleting a dead crate/directory (e.g. `crates/plsql-mcp`) or fuzz feature needs the operator's explicit in-session command; the child bead for such a removal must say so and wait for it. Structure-owner check: whether `crates/plsql-mcp` and the `fuzz` `live-mcp` feature (pinned to oraclemcp-core 0.4.1) are removed or kept as documented dead code.
- Starts after T0.3a pushes a pinnable engine revision (dependency).
- Governance: AGENTS.md constitution binds (commit explicit paths, rule 17 atomicity, never weaken the fail-closed guard, confidentiality: synthetic fixtures only, no customer/OCI/field identifiers). Line numbers are hints at 1fbe6eb0 (oraclemcp) / 5834197 (plsql-intelligence); re-derive with `rg -n`.

## Absorbs
None.

title: Rescan the engine and prove no production-reachable gap remains
description:
## Context
Final child of controller epic T7.1 (plan §9.2 step 1, R13). Every child created by T7.1a blocks this bead; its evidence records the tested SHA and is invalid once any blocking child lands a later commit (plan §23.1).

## Outcome
The T7.1a inventory command, rerun on a SHA at or after every discovered child's landing commit, reports zero unresolved production-reachable gaps, and every consumed crate has tests for its public entry points.

## Deliverable

- No product code.

1. Confirm all `discovered-from:T7.1a` children are closed (`br list` / `br dep tree`).
2. Check out the engine `origin/main` SHA that contains every child fix; run the inventory and `cargo test --workspace`.
3. Any remaining gap: file a new child (blocks this bead) instead of closing.
4. Record evidence; if a child lands later, rerun.

## Test plan
The inventory command from T7.1a (zero production-reachable gaps) + `cargo test --workspace` in the engine repo on the recorded SHA.

## Proof split
Proves absence of production-reachable placeholders at the recorded SHA; does not re-prove each child's behaviour (their own tests do).

## Non-goals
Fixing gaps (children do that), publishing (R.3).

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove analysis soundness (T7.2/T7.7/T7.13) or that later commits stay clean.

## Considerations
- Evidence is invalid once any blocking child lands a commit after the tested SHA.
- `/mock-code-finder` on the engine is DoD item 3 (plan §20) for the engine.

title: Served engine-backed classifier per profile generation; proven read-only UDFs clear
description:
## Context
Plan §9.4 step 5 (`ge6xe.2`): an engine-backed classifier per profile generation for `execute_sql`, `oracle_query` and custom tools. Level = max(classifier level, level derived from the effect set). B12a (`OperatorPureFunctionRestriction`, `purity.rs`) wraps it, so it can only narrow. Proven read-only functions then clear in `oracle_query`, removing the biggest remaining over-refusal. Today `DEFAULT_CLASSIFIER`, `READ_PRECHECK_CLASSIFIER` and `GENERATED_READ_CLASSIFIER` in `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/mod.rs` are process-wide statics with `UnknownOracle`; user functions in SELECT are always refused (`classifier.rs`). Every decision is re-classified at apply (`DEFAULT_CLASSIFIER.classify(&executed_sql) != decision` pattern). Absorbed `ge6xe.2` tests: a proven-read-only UDF clears at READ_ONLY; an unknown or side-effecting UDF stays refused; catalog-incomplete analysis yields Unknown and fails closed. The read path goes through `GuardedReadExecutor` (T1.2a/T1.2b) and the per-block proof (T1.1). W7 invariants (plan §9.4, binding on every W7 bead): a routine that can't be proven stays refused; effects map to a required level; identity is exact and the whole call closure is pinned by hash; everything is re-checked at apply (SEC-1); DML rolls back by default; nothing ever auto-commits (AGENTS.md); caller text is never concatenated into PL/SQL.

## Outcome
Each profile generation holds an engine-backed `Classifier` built from the adapter (T7.7) over fresh facts (T7.8); `oracle_query` (via `GuardedReadExecutor`), `oracle_execute` and custom tools use it; required level = max(classifier, `admit()`-derived); B12a only narrows; the same generation is used at preview and at apply, and a generation change between them refuses; proven read-only UDFs return rows in `oracle_query` at READ_ONLY.

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/mod.rs`: replace the static `DEFAULT_CLASSIFIER`/`READ_PRECHECK_CLASSIFIER` uses on execute/query/custom-tool paths with a per-profile-generation classifier handle (stored alongside the profile generation); `GENERATED_READ_CLASSIFIER` stays narrow (server-generated SQL).
- `crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/classifier.rs`: user-function-in-SELECT branch consults the oracle's effect set (`{ReadDb}` only -> admissible; anything else refused).
- Apply-time check: generation id + closure fact keys recorded in the preview/confirmation material; mismatch -> typed refusal.
- Registration in the T1.2b all-paths registry for every path that now consults the engine.

## Implementation notes
1. Build the classifier at profile activation/generation change; engine analysis failure -> classifier with `UnknownOracle` (fail closed) and a `doctor` finding.
2. Wrap with `OperatorPureFunctionRestriction` (narrow only).
3. For each admitted routine, revalidate its closure facts (T7.8) before execution; stale -> refuse.
4. Level: `max(classifier_level, admit(effects, context))`; never lower.
5. Keep the re-check at apply.

## Test plan
- Unit/in-process: `served_proven_readonly_udf_clears_at_read_only`, `served_side_effecting_udf_refused`, `served_unknown_udf_refused`, `served_catalog_incomplete_is_unknown`, `served_b12a_only_narrows`, `served_generation_change_between_preview_and_apply_refuses`, `served_engine_init_failure_falls_back_to_unknown_oracle`.
- Live external (FREE 23ai lane, external client via the T4.2 harness; case ids registered in the W4 matrix): `w4_query_proven_udf_returns_rows`, `w4_query_dml_udf_refused_no_execution` (audit shows zero executions and `V$SQL` has no SQL_ID for the run-id comment), `w4_query_nextval_udf_refused`.

## Proof split
Proves served wiring and the over-refusal fix for UDFs. Collectors (T7.9a/b), custom tools (T7.10+) and W12-W14 consume it; T9.6 proves on ADB.

## Non-goals
Custom package-call tools (T7.10), DDL/mutation trigger collectors (T7.9a/T7.9b), ANTLR fallback (T7.15).

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove custom tools, DDL paths or ADB behaviour.

## Considerations
- Hot files: `dispatch/mod.rs` and `classifier.rs` (shared with W1/W2/W3/W13/W14): reserve, land in small commits, rule 17 for type + callers.
- Fail-closed fallback when the engine can't build facts.
- `sec`: second-agent review.
- Governance: AGENTS.md constitution binds (commit explicit paths, rule 17 atomicity, never weaken the fail-closed guard, confidentiality: synthetic fixtures only, no customer/OCI/field identifiers). Line numbers are hints at 1fbe6eb0 (oraclemcp) / 5834197 (plsql-intelligence); re-derive with `rg -n`.

## Absorbs
- oraclemcp-ge6xe.2: wire the engine side-effect oracle into the served classifier per DB; proven-read-only UDF clears, unknown/side-effecting stays refused, incomplete analysis fails closed (kept whole; now per profile generation, level = max(classifier, effects)).

- [ ] Negative: A UDF performing DML in the same SELECT shape is refused before Oracle: audit shows zero executions and `V$SQL` holds no SQL_ID for the run-id comment.
