title: MutationEffectClosureV1 collector (seam): everything a DML statement can fire
description:
## Context
Shared collector used by W13 grant admission (`dml_effect_closure`, T13.2a/T13.5) and W14 row estimates (T14.2) (plan §15, §16). Every mechanism has an explicit catalog source, cap, identity, hash and `unavailable` behaviour. Non-transactional or user-autonomous effects refuse. Transactional internal effects, such as a materialized-view log, are included in the impact and in `scope_digest`; their absence or drift must be proven, never assumed. It covers: the target's enabled triggers for the exact statement kind, including compound and column-specific DML triggers; incoming enabled foreign keys and their delete actions; indexes and index callbacks (domain indexes); virtual/generated expressions (user functions behind virtual columns or function-based indexes); VPD statement-type-specific policy functions and check-option policies; FGA handlers (W1, T1.9); OLS / Real Application Security / Data Redaction behaviour (T7.16), including OLS write-control triggers; materialized-view logs (maintained by an internal DML trigger); a privilege-completeness proof: every catalog source above is readable, or the result is `Unknown`. User code is admitted only through the shared `RoutineEffectsV1` admission function (T7.5, context `DmlMutationClosure`).

## Outcome
`MutationEffectClosureV1::collect(target, statement_kind, columns)` returns a canonical, hashable closure: each mechanism with identity, source hash, W7 effect set, status and per-mechanism `computed | unavailable(reason)`; any unreadable source, cap exhaustion or unknown mechanism makes the closure `Unknown`. Seam only: consumers T13.2a, T13.5, T14.2 wait on it.

## Deliverable
- Type in `oraclemcp-guard` (engine-free, so W13/W14 can consume it): `MutationEffectClosureV1`, `MutationMechanism` enum (`DmlTrigger{timing, level, compound, columns}`, `ForeignKeyAction{on_delete}`, `IndexCallback{domain}`, `VirtualColumnExpr`, `FunctionBasedIndex`, `VpdPolicy{statement_types, check_option}`, `FgaHandler`, `OlsPolicy`, `RasRealm`, `RedactionPolicy`, `MvLog`), canonical encoding + SHA-256.
- Collection in `oraclemcp-db` next to the T7.8 `catalog_facts.rs` domain (re-derive; split into a sibling module only if it exceeds reviewable size). Catalog sources: `ALL_TRIGGERS` (`TRIGGERING_EVENT`, `TRIGGER_TYPE`, `BASE_OBJECT_TYPE`) + `ALL_TRIGGER_COLS`, `ALL_CONSTRAINTS` (R constraints referencing the target, `DELETE_RULE`), `ALL_INDEXES` (`ITYPE_OWNER/ITYPE_NAME`, `FUNCIDX_STATUS`), `ALL_TAB_COLS` (`VIRTUAL_COLUMN`, `DATA_DEFAULT`), `ALL_POLICIES` (`SEL/INS/UPD/DEL`, `CHK_OPTION`), the FGA catalog (T1.9), OLS/RAS/Redaction sources (T7.16), `ALL_MVIEW_LOGS`.
- Tests only for the collector; no grant/impact wiring.

## Implementation notes
1. Collect per statement kind (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE) and column set (column-specific `UPDATE OF` triggers).
2. User code (trigger bodies, policy functions, virtual-column/function-index functions, domain-index callbacks) -> engine effects via T7.9's binding, admitted through `admit(.., DmlMutationClosure)`; `Autonomous`/`TxnControl`/`ExternalIo`/`DynamicSql`/`Unknown`/`SequenceAdvance` refuse.
3. Every catalog query bounded; privilege failure or cap -> `unavailable` -> closure Unknown.
4. MV logs recorded as transactional internal effects (not user triggers).

## Test plan
- Unit (synthetic catalog rows): `mutation_closure_compound_trigger_collected`, `mutation_closure_column_specific_trigger_only_for_listed_columns`, `mutation_closure_on_delete_cascade_collected`, `mutation_closure_on_delete_set_null_collected`, `mutation_closure_domain_index_collected`, `mutation_closure_virtual_column_udf_collected`, `mutation_closure_vpd_update_policy_with_check_option`, `mutation_closure_mv_log_is_transactional_internal`, `mutation_closure_unreadable_source_is_unknown`, `mutation_closure_cap_exhaustion_is_unknown`, `mutation_closure_autonomous_trigger_refused`, `mutation_closure_hash_changes_on_trigger_source_change`.
- Live in-process on FREE 23ai with a synthetic fixture: `mutation_closure_live_fixture_matches_expected` (row trigger + compound trigger + FK cascade child + MV log + VPD update policy), JSONL log.

## Proof split
Proves collection and hashing. T13.2a/T13.5 prove grant admission/use; T14.2 proves estimates; T13.8/T14.9 prove them live.

## Non-goals
Grant admission rules (T13.2a), impact rows (T14.2), OLS/RAS/Redaction detection itself (T7.16), FGA discovery itself (T1.9).

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove a grant or estimate is correct; only that the closure is complete or Unknown.

## Considerations
- Seam: consumers T13.2a, T13.5, T14.2 wait on it.
- Structure-owner check: file placement (type in `oraclemcp-guard`, collection in `oraclemcp-db`); decided above.
- `sec`: second-agent review.
- Governance: AGENTS.md constitution binds (commit explicit paths, rule 17 atomicity, never weaken the fail-closed guard, confidentiality: synthetic fixtures only, no customer/OCI/field identifiers). Line numbers are hints at 1fbe6eb0 (oraclemcp) / 5834197 (plsql-intelligence); re-derive with `rg -n`.

## Absorbs
None.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: For the synthetic fixture table (row trigger, compound trigger, FK ON DELETE CASCADE child, MV log, VPD update policy) the live collector returns exactly those mechanisms with source hashes.
- [ ] Negative: Removing visibility of one catalog source makes the closure Unknown (not a smaller closure).
- [ ] Negative: A column-specific trigger `UPDATE OF c2` is absent for an UPDATE of `c1` and present for `c2`.
- [ ] Negative: An autonomous trigger body makes `admit` refuse.
- [ ] Tests: Unit tests named in the Test plan + `mutation_closure_live_fixture_matches_expected` on the FREE 23ai lane.
- [ ] Proof class: unit + live in-process; forbidden substitutes: mock DB for the live case.
- [ ] Consumers: T13.2a, T13.5, T14.2, T14.6a.
- [ ] No-claim: Does not prove grant or impact behaviour.

title: DdlEffectClosureV1 collector (seam): DDL event to enabled SCHEMA/DATABASE triggers
description:
## Context
Plan §9.4 step 6 (shared `DdlEffectClosureV1`) and §14 (W12). Literal DDL can fire enabled `SCHEMA`/`DATABASE` DDL triggers; they run in the user's transaction and may be autonomous. Custom-tool DDL preview and apply bind and revalidate the exact DDL event's trigger closure: identity, event predicates, source hash, status, W7 effects, catalog completeness and container. Trigger effects are admitted only through the shared `RoutineEffectsV1` admission function for the DDL-trigger context: anything beyond `ReadDb`/`SessionState` refuses. Missing visibility or unsupported event semantics count as `Unknown`. W12 uses the same collector (T12.4a), including for child creation (`open`) and retirement; `ALTER DATABASE DEFAULT EDITION` is excluded only because Oracle documents that `ALTER DATABASE` does not fire ALTER DDL triggers (its other operator-only checks stay mandatory). A missing catalog privilege counts as `Unknown` and refuses.

## Outcome
`DdlEffectClosureV1::collect(event, object, container)` returns every enabled trigger that can fire for that exact DDL event (BEFORE/AFTER, ON SCHEMA of the relevant schema, ON DATABASE) with identity, event predicates (`WHEN` clause and statically decidable `ora_dict_obj_*` guards), source hash, status and admitted effects; unsupported predicate semantics, invisible triggers or unreadable source -> `Unknown`. Seam only: consumers T7.10 and T12.4a.

## Deliverable
- Type in `oraclemcp-guard`: `DdlEffectClosureV1`, `DdlEvent` enum (CREATE, ALTER, DROP, TRUNCATE, RENAME, GRANT, REVOKE, COMMENT, ANALYZE, AUDIT, NOAUDIT, ASSOCIATE STATISTICS, DISASSOCIATE STATISTICS, and the catch-all DDL event), canonical encoding + SHA-256.
- Collection in `oraclemcp-db` (same domain as T7.8/T7.9a): `ALL_TRIGGERS` where `BASE_OBJECT_TYPE` is SCHEMA or DATABASE, `TRIGGERING_EVENT`, `WHEN_CLAUSE`, `STATUS`, source hash; DATABASE-level triggers are often invisible through `ALL_TRIGGERS` -> positive visibility proof or `Unknown`.
- Tests only; no custom-tool or W12 wiring.

## Implementation notes
1. Map the exact statement to its DDL event(s) (`CREATE OR REPLACE` fires CREATE; the catch-all DDL event fires for all DDL).
2. Container: collect in the current container; triggers that can fire in the PDB but are not visible -> `Unknown`.
3. Visibility proof: absence of DATABASE triggers is accepted only with positive evidence that the profile can see them (readable DBA-level trigger view or an equivalent documented check); otherwise `Unknown`.
4. Effects via T7.9's engine binding; `admit(.., DdlTrigger)`.

## Test plan
- Unit: `ddl_closure_catch_all_ddl_trigger_fires_for_create`, `ddl_closure_before_create_on_schema_collected`, `ddl_closure_disabled_trigger_excluded`, `ddl_closure_when_clause_unsupported_is_unknown`, `ddl_closure_database_trigger_invisible_is_unknown`, `ddl_closure_trigger_with_nextval_refused`, `ddl_closure_trigger_with_dynamic_sql_refused`, `ddl_closure_trigger_with_operator_only_refused`, `ddl_closure_trigger_with_dml_refused`, `ddl_closure_trigger_with_autonomous_refused`, `ddl_closure_readonly_trigger_admitted`, `ddl_closure_alter_database_default_edition_has_no_ddl_trigger_event`, `ddl_closure_hash_changes_on_trigger_recompile`.
- Live in-process FREE 23ai: `ddl_closure_live_schema_trigger_collected` (synthetic `AFTER CREATE ON SCHEMA` trigger inserting into a canary table is collected and refused), JSONL log.

## Proof split
Proves collection. T7.10 proves custom-tool DDL binds/revalidates it; T12.4a proves W12 binding; T4.9a/T12.9 prove it live.

## Non-goals
Custom-tool DDL execution (T7.10), W12 adapter (T12.4a), compile-parse callbacks (`CompileParseEffectClosureV1`, T12.4b).

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove DDL execution is safe end to end.

## Considerations
- Seam: T7.10 and T12.4a wait on it.
- Over-refusal on profiles without DBA-level trigger visibility is accepted (fail closed).
- `sec`: second-agent review.
- Governance: AGENTS.md constitution binds (commit explicit paths, rule 17 atomicity, never weaken the fail-closed guard, confidentiality: synthetic fixtures only, no customer/OCI/field identifiers). Line numbers are hints at 1fbe6eb0 (oraclemcp) / 5834197 (plsql-intelligence); re-derive with `rg -n`.

## Absorbs
None.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: On FREE 23ai, a synthetic enabled `AFTER CREATE ON SCHEMA` trigger is collected for `CREATE TABLE` with its source hash and effects.
- [ ] Negative: The same trigger with an autonomous INSERT makes `admit(DdlTrigger)` refuse.
- [ ] Negative: Without DATABASE-trigger visibility the closure is Unknown.
- [ ] Negative: A disabled trigger is not collected.
- [ ] Tests: Unit tests named in the Test plan + `ddl_closure_live_schema_trigger_collected` on the FREE 23ai lane.
- [ ] Proof class: unit + live in-process; forbidden substitutes: mock DB for the live case.
- [ ] Consumers: T7.10, T12.4a, T14.6a.
- [ ] No-claim: Does not prove custom-tool or W12 DDL safety end to end.

title: Package-call custom tools: signed structured definitions, live activation, safe wrapper
description:
## Context
Plan §9.4 step 6. Today `crates/oraclemcp-core/src/custom_tools.rs` supports only Form A (inline SQL) from `tools.d/*.toml`; `call =` (Form B) is rejected at load; the HMAC v2 signature (`oraclemcp-custom-tool:v2:hmac-sha256:`) is mandatory only on `protected` profiles (which can't hold write tools); `classify_at_load` checks the level against `max_level`; dispatch lives in `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/custom_tool.rs`. W7 invariants (plan §9.4, binding on every W7 bead): a routine that can't be proven stays refused; effects map to a required level; identity is exact and the whole call closure is pinned by hash; everything is re-checked at apply (SEC-1); DML rolls back by default; nothing ever auto-commits (AGENTS.md); caller text is never concatenated into PL/SQL.

Binding design:
- Declared structurally, never as a SQL string: `routine = { owner, package, member, subprogram_id, overload }`, `args = [{ oracle_name, oracle_type, direction, bind_name }]`, plus `closure_sha256`. Literals, expressions, comments and database links are not accepted in configuration.
- Definitions are parsed and signature-checked at startup. A tool is advertised only after profile-specific live activation succeeds: it resolves, its proof holds and its hash matches.
- Loads only if the effect-derived level is at or below the profile `max_level`, the closure hash matches, and the definition is HMAC-signed. The signature is required whenever `required_level > READ_ONLY`; the pin is inside the HMAC canonical bytes.
- The server generates a fixed wrapper in named notation from the pinned overload's `ALL_ARGUMENTS` rows, with explicit bind types: `BEGIN "SCHEMA"."PKG"."PROC"(p_a => :a, p_b => :b); END;`.
- Name-capture check at load and at every run: no object in the current schema or `PUBLIC` may be named like `SCHEMA` (Oracle resolves the first part as a local object first, so such an object would capture the call).
- The tool listing shows `required_level`. Writes and DDL go through preview -> token -> apply.
- DDL-trigger closure: custom-tool DDL preview and apply bind and revalidate the exact DDL event's `DdlEffectClosureV1` (T7.9b).
- DDL execution model (Oracle commits before and after DDL): a routine whose proven closure contains `Ddl` runs only on a fresh one-shot connection with an empty workspace, destroyed after the call; a closure with both `Dml` and `Ddl`, or DDL plus unresolved dynamic SQL, is refused (the implicit DDL commit could permanently commit the preceding DML); DDL calls are always `commit=true`, marked irreversible, previewed and confirmed; `ddl_outcome_unknown` is never retried automatically.
- Masked-profile output refusal (§9.4 step 8): on a profile with result masking, every package-call tool exposing a scalar return, OUT/IN OUT binds, a REF CURSOR, implicit results or captured `DBMS_OUTPUT` is refused in 0.12 whatever its `RoutineEffects` (package state, initialization code, session context and IN OUT aliasing can launder a masked value). Output-bearing package calls stay available on profiles without result masking.

## Outcome
Operators can declare signed, structured package-call tools; the server activates each per profile only after live resolution, proof and hash match; the tool executes only through the server-built named-notation wrapper with typed binds, at the effect-derived level, under preview -> token -> apply for writes/DDL, DML rolled back by default, DDL on a one-shot connection; output-bearing tools are refused on masked profiles.

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp-core/src/custom_tools.rs`: replace the Form B `call` string with the structured `routine`/`args`/`closure_sha256` schema (no compat shim; a `call` string keeps being rejected with guidance); canonical HMAC bytes include the pin; signature required when `required_level > READ_ONLY` or on `protected`; config refuses literals, expressions, comments and DB links.
- Activation (per profile generation): resolve via T7.6, prove via T7.9 + T7.8 facts, compare `closure_sha256`, check name capture, apply the masked-profile output rule; only then register in `ToolRegistry` with `required_level` shown.
- Wrapper builder (pure function, fuzzed in T7.13): pinned `ALL_ARGUMENTS` rows -> `BEGIN "S"."P"."M"(a => :b1, ...); END;` with quoted identifiers and typed binds; never interpolates caller values.
- `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/custom_tool.rs`: execution through preview/token/apply; DML rollback by default; DDL on a one-shot connection (`crates/oraclemcp-core/src/lane.rs`: a one-shot lane kind or the existing fresh-connection facility, re-derive); `StatementOutcome` (T2.2a) for `ddl_outcome_unknown` with no auto-retry.
- Typed load/activation errors consumed by `doctor` (T7.14).

## Implementation notes
1. Parse -> signature check at startup (fail load on a bad signature).
2. Live activation per profile: exact identity, overload pin (`subprogram_id`, `overload`), `ALL_ARGUMENTS` fetch, closure effects, `admit(.., CustomToolCall)`, level <= `max_level`, hash equality, name capture (objects in the current schema and PUBLIC synonyms named like the schema).
3. Refusals at activation: Dml+Ddl mix; Ddl + unresolved DynamicSql; masked profile + any output channel; unsigned when level > READ_ONLY.
4. Execution: re-run the name-capture check each run (SEC-1 fact re-check is T7.11); DDL path binds `DdlEffectClosureV1` into preview material and revalidates before apply; the one-shot connection is destroyed after the call.
5. Compile-class literal DDL (CREATE OR REPLACE of PL/SQL units, ALTER ... COMPILE) inside a custom routine requires `CompileParseEffectClosureV1` (T12.4b); until it is wired, such closures are refused as Unknown.

## Test plan

title: SEC-1 re-check of the closure fact key before every run; refuse and quarantine on drift
description:
## Context
Plan §9.4 step 7 (SEC-1: everything is re-checked at apply). Before each run of a package-call custom tool, re-read the closure fact key (T7.8) with bounded fact queries and require every member `VALID`. Any change, including a repointed synonym whose automatic recompile hasn't happened yet, -> refuse AND quarantine the tool, with a typed error and an audit entry. Audit entries carry the closure hash (§9.4 step 9).

## Outcome
Every custom package-call run revalidates the pinned closure (`revalidate` from T7.8) within bounded queries; Fresh -> run; Stale/Unknown -> typed refusal, the tool is quarantined (removed from `tools/list` with a list-changed notification, further calls refused with the same typed error), and an audit entry records tool name, closure hash, reason class and the drifted component (no data values).

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/custom_tool.rs`: pre-run revalidation + quarantine transition.
- Quarantine state in the `oraclemcp-core` custom-tools registry (per profile generation); cleared only by a new live activation (T7.10) after an operator reload/restart that re-proves and re-matches the signed hash.
- Error taxonomy: `CUSTOM_TOOL_QUARANTINED` (typed, with reason class), aligned with the W3 T3.4 taxonomy.
- Audit: `custom_tool_quarantine` event with the closure hash; every custom-tool execution audit entry carries the closure hash.

1. Bounded fact queries only (caps, timeouts from the request budget).
2. Check members `STATUS='VALID'`, LAST_DDL_TIME/OBJECT_ID/source hashes, dependency targets (synonym repoint), triggers on DML targets, edition/container, name capture.
3. Refuse first, then quarantine atomically (no race where a concurrent call runs the stale tool).

## Test plan

title: Custom-tool output: OUT/IN OUT binds, scalar, bounded DBMS_OUTPUT, capped REF CURSOR
description:
## Context
Plan §9.4 step 8. Output channels: OUT and IN OUT binds; scalar mode (today scalar output is unsupported in custom tools); bounded `DBMS_OUTPUT` capture; REF CURSOR results read through the same row/byte caps as `oracle_query`. Masking closes every output channel: masking today works on serialized query-result cells (`crates/oraclemcp-db/src/masking.rs`, `serialize.rs`), and a routine can copy a masked column into any PL/SQL output and lose the column identity masking needs. On a profile with result masking, every package-call tool that exposes a scalar return, OUT/IN OUT binds, a REF CURSOR, implicit results or captured `DBMS_OUTPUT` is refused in 0.12, whatever its `RoutineEffects` (enforced at activation by T7.10; this bead enforces it again at execution as defence in depth). An effect set proves what a routine does, not where an output value came from. Output-bearing package calls stay available on profiles without result masking. `DBMS_OUTPUT` capture is bounded and off by default.

## Outcome
On unmasked profiles, package-call tools return typed OUT/IN OUT values, a scalar return, REF CURSOR rows under the `oracle_query` row/byte caps (NUMBER as string, per the hard invariant) and, only when enabled in the signed definition, bounded `DBMS_OUTPUT` lines; on masked profiles, any output channel refuses at execution even if activation was bypassed.

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/custom_tool.rs` + `crates/oraclemcp-core/src/custom_tools.rs`: output schema per tool (derived from pinned `ALL_ARGUMENTS` directions/types); config fields `output = { scalar, dbms_output = { enabled = false, max_lines, max_bytes } }` inside the signed canonical bytes.
- REF CURSOR fetch via the same serializer and caps as `oracle_query` (`oraclemcp-db` `serialize.rs`).
- `DBMS_OUTPUT` capture: server-owned `DBMS_OUTPUT.ENABLE(<bounded>)` before and `DBMS_OUTPUT.GET_LINES` after, on the same session, with an explicit `truncated` flag.
- Execution-time masking guard.

## Implementation notes
1. Bind directions from `ALL_ARGUMENTS.IN_OUT`; types mapped via the driver's typed binds; unsupported type -> refuse at activation.
2. REF CURSOR: fetch with caps; close the cursor on every path (ties to T2.7 cursor lifecycle).
3. DBMS_OUTPUT: off by default; enabling it is part of the signed definition.
4. Masked profile: refuse before execution when the tool has any output channel.

## Test plan
- Unit: `output_out_and_inout_binds_typed`, `output_scalar_return`, `output_refcursor_respects_row_cap`, `output_refcursor_respects_byte_cap`, `output_refcursor_number_as_string`, `output_dbms_output_off_by_default`, `output_dbms_output_bounded_and_flagged_truncated`, `output_masked_profile_refused_at_execution_for_each_channel`, `output_refcursor_closed_on_error`.
- Live in-process FREE 23ai: `custom_tool_live_refcursor_caps`, `custom_tool_live_out_inout`. External cases (REF CURSOR, scalar/OUT, DBMS_OUTPUT, masking exfiltration) are owned by T4.9a.

## Proof split
Proves output channels and the execution-time masking guard. T4.9a proves them externally; T7.13 proves the laundering canary.

## Non-goals
Implicit-results support (implicit results require `DBMS_SQL.RETURN_RESULT`, which makes the routine Unknown anyway); masking of PL/SQL outputs on masked profiles (refused in 0.12 instead).

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove masking of routine outputs; it proves refusal on masked profiles.

## Considerations
- Must not weaken the masking invariant: refusal, never partial masking, on masked profiles in 0.12.
- Cursor lifecycle interacts with T2.7 (ORA-01000); close on every path.
- `sec`: second-agent review.
- Governance: AGENTS.md constitution binds (commit explicit paths, rule 17 atomicity, never weaken the fail-closed guard, confidentiality: synthetic fixtures only, no customer/OCI/field identifiers). Line numbers are hints at 1fbe6eb0 (oraclemcp) / 5834197 (plsql-intelligence); re-derive with `rg -n`.

## Absorbs
None.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: On an unmasked profile, a synthetic procedure with OUT and IN OUT parameters returns typed values; a REF CURSOR function returns rows capped exactly like `oracle_query`.
- [ ] Negative: With `DBMS_OUTPUT` not enabled in the signed definition, no output lines are returned.

For every resolved relation in a read proof (and in the mutation closure via T7.9a), the server determines whether an OLS table policy, a RAS data realm or a Data Redaction policy applies; if one applies, or if its absence can't be proven from readable catalog evidence, the statement is refused with a typed reason (`protected_by_ols`, `protected_by_ras`, `protected_by_redaction` or `security_feature_visibility_unknown`) before Oracle executes it.

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/catalog_resolver.rs` (proof path), with per-relation facts exposed for T7.9a: bounded, server-owned detection queries (via `CatalogQueryId` once T1.2a provides it):
  - OLS: installation evidence (`LBACSYS` in `ALL_USERS` and/or `V$OPTION` 'Oracle Label Security'), then the OLS table-policy view (`ALL_SA_TABLE_POLICIES` or the version-appropriate view) for the relation;
  - RAS: data-realm objects for the relation (`ALL_XDS_OBJECTS` or the version-appropriate equivalent);
  - Data Redaction: `REDACTION_POLICIES` for the relation.
- Typed refusal reasons in the guard/error taxonomy; registration in the T1.2b all-paths registry.

## Implementation notes
1. Absence is accepted only with positive evidence (feature not installed, or the policy view readable and empty for the relation); otherwise `Unknown` -> refuse.
2. Verify view names/columns per version in the version matrix (18c/21c/23ai); where a view doesn't exist on a version, rely on installation evidence.
3. Integrate into the per-block proof so every relation (subqueries, CTEs, recursively resolved views) is checked.
4. Same checks for server-generated reads (W13 pre-counts, W14 estimates) through the executor.

## Test plan
- Unit: `ols_policy_on_relation_refused`, `ras_realm_on_relation_refused`, `redaction_policy_on_relation_refused`, `security_view_unreadable_is_unknown_refused`, `feature_not_installed_evidence_allows`, `nested_subquery_relation_with_redaction_refused`.
- Live external FREE 23ai: `w4_query_redaction_policy_table_refused_no_execution` (audit shows zero executions, `V$SQL` has no SQL_ID for the run-id comment). OLS/RAS live where the image allows enabling them; otherwise unit + version-matrix catalog proof.

## Proof split
Proves detection and refusal on the read path; T7.9a folds it into the mutation closure; T9.6 proves on ADB.

## Non-goals
Enforcing or emulating OLS/RAS/Redaction semantics; licence handling of the operator-side native redaction tier (`native_redaction.rs`).

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove data visible through other channels is filtered; it proves the server refuses.

## Considerations
- Structure-owner check: catalog view names and their readability by non-DBA users differ by version; this can over-refuse on profiles without catalog visibility (accepted: fail closed). Verify per version before hard-coding.
- Structure-owner check: FREE 23ai live coverage for OLS/RAS depends on whether the image allows enabling them; if not, those two are unit + catalog proof only and T9.6 covers ADB.
- Supersedes the earlier nn3ne "future hardening only" scoping per the plan; fail-open fix -> priority 0.
- `sec`: second-agent review.
- Governance: AGENTS.md constitution binds (commit explicit paths, rule 17 atomicity, never weaken the fail-closed guard, confidentiality: synthetic fixtures only, no customer/OCI/field identifiers). Line numbers are hints at 1fbe6eb0 (oraclemcp) / 5834197 (plsql-intelligence); re-derive with `rg -n`.

## Absorbs
- oraclemcp-nn3ne: OLS/RAS/Data Redaction outside the VPD proof (kept, upgraded from future hardening to detect-and-refuse per plan §9).

title: Preserve package members, initializers and default-expression call edges in AST/IR
description:
## Context
Round-5 Critical (plan §24, integrated): package initialization and default-argument effects. `InvocationClosureV1` (plan §9.4 step 1) requires that a packaged-member invocation always unions: the selected overload and its transitive callees; the package-spec and package-body declaration initializers; the package-body initialization section (always included, because pooled-session initialization state is not an authorization fact); every default-parameter expression the call shape actually evaluates. If member/initializer/default identity isn't preserved, the result is `Unknown`. Today the engine loses that identity: `lower_create_package_body` in `plsql-parser-antlr/src/tree_lower.rs` concatenates the statements of every `procedure_body`/`function_body` and the package-level `seq_of_statements` into one `Vec<AstStatement>` attached to a single `AstDecl::PackageBody { name, span }`; `plsql-ir/src/lower.rs` drops routine parameters and their default expressions.

## Outcome
The engine AST/IR keeps, per package: each member (procedure/function) with its overload ordinal, parameters (name, mode, type, default expression) and body statements; the spec and body declaration initializers; and the body initialization section, each as a separately addressable unit with its own call/read/write edges in the depgraph. Anything the lowerer cannot attribute to one of those units is reported as an unattributed-construct diagnostic that downstream turns into `Unknown`.

## Deliverable
- Engine repo: `crates/plsql-parser-antlr/src/tree_lower.rs` (`lower_create_package`, `lower_create_package_body`): emit per-member declarations instead of the flattened statement list; keep the initialization section and declaration initializers as distinct units.
- `crates/plsql-parser-antlr/src/lower/mod.rs`, `crates/plsql-ir/src/lower.rs`, `crates/plsql-ir/src/decl.rs`: parameter list with default expressions; `crates/plsql-ir/src/calls.rs` + depgraph emission (`plsql-depgraph`): edges from member (`<pkg>.<member>#<overload>`), spec-initializer, body-initializer and per-parameter default-expression units.
- Public IR types changed in place (no v2 clones, AGENTS.md); callers migrated.

## Implementation notes
1. Introduce IR units: `PackageMember { name, overload_ordinal, params: Vec<Param{name, mode, ty, default: Option<Expr>}>, body }`, `PackageInit { spec_decl_initializers, body_decl_initializers, body_init_section }` (names are the engine's to choose; identity must be stable and exact, case preserved for quoted names).
2. Overload ordinal must match Oracle's `ALL_ARGUMENTS.OVERLOAD` / `ALL_PROCEDURES.SUBPROGRAM_ID` ordering so the catalog pin (T7.6/T7.8) can join on it; if the ordering can't be established from source alone, emit the identity without an ordinal and mark it ambiguous (-> `Unknown` downstream).
3. Default-expression edges are recorded per parameter so a consumer can include only the defaults the call shape evaluates (explicitly supplying the optional argument must not evaluate the default).
4. Unattributed statements/expressions produce a diagnostic that lowers completeness for that unit.
5. Keep existing snapshot tests green or update them deliberately with review.

## Test plan
Engine unit/snapshot tests (crate `plsql-parser-antlr` / `plsql-ir`), fixtures are synthetic PL/SQL:
- `package_body_members_are_separate_units` (two procedures, one function; each has its own statement list and edges).
- `package_overloads_keep_distinct_identity` (two overloads of `P`).
- `package_body_initialization_section_is_its_own_unit` (init section containing `INSERT`, `COMMIT`, `x := seq.NEXTVAL`, `UTL_HTTP.REQUEST` call).
- `package_declaration_initializer_call_edge_preserved` (`g NUMBER := f_side_effect();` in spec and in body).
- `default_parameter_expression_call_edge_preserved` (`p IN NUMBER DEFAULT f_side_effect()`).
- `quoted_member_identity_case_preserved`.
- `unattributed_package_construct_lowers_completeness`.
JSONL case log per fixture (case id, expected units/edges, actual).

## Proof split
Proves the AST/IR carries the identities `InvocationClosureV1` needs. T7.2 builds the closure and effects on top; T7.7 consumes them in oraclemcp; T7.13/T4.9a prove behaviour live.

## Non-goals
Effect classification and the `RoutineEffectsV1` contract (T7.2), fuzz targets (T7.3), oraclemcp-side adapter (T7.7).

## No-claim boundary
A green run does not prove effect sets are correct; it proves only that the units and edges exist and are addressable.

## Considerations
- Fail-closed: any loss of identity must surface as reduced completeness, never as a silently smaller closure.
- Engine API changes reach oraclemcp's `plsql_tools.rs` only through the pin refresh (T0.6); oraclemcp keeps compiling against the old pin until then.
- `sec`: second-agent review before batch verify.
- Governance: AGENTS.md constitution binds (commit explicit paths, rule 17 atomicity, never weaken the fail-closed guard, confidentiality: synthetic fixtures only, no customer/OCI/field identifiers). Line numbers are hints at 1fbe6eb0 (oraclemcp) / 5834197 (plsql-intelligence); re-derive with `rg -n`.

## Absorbs
None.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: For a synthetic package with two overloads, a spec initializer, a body initializer, an init section and a defaulted parameter, the IR exposes each as a distinct unit with its own edges (snapshot).
- [ ] Negative: A lowerer that keeps flattening member bodies fails `package_body_members_are_separate_units`.
- [ ] Negative: Dropping the default expression fails `default_parameter_expression_call_edge_preserved`.
- [ ] Tests: `package_body_members_are_separate_units`, `package_overloads_keep_distinct_identity`, `package_body_initialization_section_is_its_own_unit`, `package_declaration_initializer_call_edge_preserved`, `default_parameter_expression_call_edge_preserved`, `quoted_member_identity_case_preserved`, `unattributed_package_construct_lowers_completeness` green in engine `cargo test --workspace`.
- [ ] Proof class: unit (engine); forbidden substitutes: asserting on flattened statement lists, hand-built IR instead of parsed source.
- [ ] Consumers: T7.2, T7.3, T7.7, T7.8.
- [ ] No-claim: Does not prove effect correctness or live Oracle agreement.

title: Engine: close soundness gaps, emit RoutineEffectsV1 and InvocationClosureV1 exhaustively
description:
## Context
Engine soundness gaps (plan §9.1, measured at plsql-intelligence 5834197 / oraclemcp 1fbe6eb0): (1) only three verdicts (`oraclemcp_guard::Purity` = ProvenReadOnly / ProvenSideEffecting / Unknown), so DML, DDL and COMMIT are indistinguishable; (2) no depgraph edges for COMMIT/ROLLBACK or `PRAGMA AUTONOMOUS_TRANSACTION`, although the IR models `Statement::TransactionControl` / `Statement::ExecuteImmediate` (`plsql-ir/src/stmt.rs`); `plsql_depgraph::EdgeKind` has no transaction/autonomous variant; (3) FAIL-OPEN: a routine without outgoing edges counts as `ProvenReadOnly` (`PlsqlSideEffectOracle::routine_node_purity` starts from ProvenReadOnly), so unloaded SYS calls (UTL_HTTP, DBMS_*) may pass; (4) case-insensitive fallback in `PlsqlSideEffectOracle::resolve_candidates` (`eq_ignore_ascii_case`); (5) `CompletenessPosture::Partial` still counts as trusted (`from_analysis_run`).

Plan §9.2 step 2 / §9.4 step 3: engine 0.8.0 fixes the five soundness gaps, each with a test. §9.4 step 1: effects are a SET `{ReadDb, RowLock, SessionState, Dml, Ddl, Admin, SequenceAdvance, OperatorOnly(OperatorStatementClass), TxnControl, Autonomous, DynamicSql, ExternalIo, Unknown}` (contract `RoutineEffectsV1`, owned oraclemcp-side by T7.5); any parsed construct without an explicit effect mapping becomes `Unknown`; effects propagate through the call closure by set union; transaction control and autonomous transactions are separate effects (an earlier draft mapping transaction control to ">= DDL" is withdrawn). `InvocationClosureV1` for a packaged member unions overload + transitive callees + spec/body declaration initializers + body initialization section + evaluated default expressions; lost identity -> `Unknown` (T7.2a preserves the identities).

`Unknown` by construction (always refused; each case has a unit test asserting `Unknown`): wrapped bodies (`ALL_SOURCE` shows `wrapped`); any unresolved or data-dependent `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` (dynamic text built from a parameter, variable, table, function call, conditional concatenation or external input); any `DBMS_SQL`, `DBMS_SCHEDULER`, `DBMS_PIPE`, `DBMS_AQ` or `UTL_*` call; Java stored procedures and external procedures; `AUTHID CURRENT_USER` units in v1 (they resolve unqualified names in the caller's schema at run time, so the closure proven at load isn't the closure executed); any callee whose source the profile can't read; any SYS/SYSTEM routine absent from the committed, reviewed, tighten-only allowlist `sys_effects.toml`; ambiguous overloads; any closure member with `STATUS <> 'VALID'`. Exception (PL/SQL can only issue DDL through dynamic SQL): a single compile-time string literal used by `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` may be folded by the engine, parsed and classified recursively; on success its inner effects replace `DynamicSql`, otherwise it stays `DynamicSql`/`Unknown`; no caller value may contribute to the text; literal dynamic SQL propagates `OperatorOnly` (never reduced to `Admin`).

## Outcome
The engine computes, for every routine/member invocation shape, an `InvocationClosureV1` (member identities, overloads, initializer units, evaluated defaults) and its effect set in the engine's `RoutineEffectsV1` vocabulary, with a per-closure completeness flag. Every parsed construct has an explicit construct-to-effect mapping or maps to `Unknown`; an exhaustive coverage test fails when a new construct lacks a mapping.

## Deliverable
- Engine repo:
  - an effect vocabulary type mirroring T7.5's `RoutineEffectsV1` variants exactly (placed in `plsql-core` or `plsql-depgraph`, re-derive; contract version string `RoutineEffectsV1`), plus the `InvocationClosureV1` result type;
  - `plsql-depgraph` `EdgeKind`: add variants for transaction control (COMMIT/ROLLBACK/SAVEPOINT/SET TRANSACTION), autonomous transaction (`PRAGMA AUTONOMOUS_TRANSACTION`), sequence advance (`NEXTVAL`), row lock (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, `LOCK TABLE`), session state (`ALTER SESSION`, `DBMS_SESSION`, package-state writes), DDL, unresolved dynamic SQL and external I/O; an explicit unresolved-callee edge so "no outgoing edges" can never be read as proof (gap 3, engine side);
  - `plsql-ir/src/stmt.rs` / `plsql-engine/src/lib.rs`: map `Statement::TransactionControl`, `Statement::ExecuteImmediate` and every other statement/expression kind to effects; compile-time-literal `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` folding (parse + classify the literal recursively; `OperatorOnly` propagates);
  - exact-identity lookup API (no case folding for quoted identifiers) (gap 4, engine side);
  - per-closure completeness (Clean / not Clean) instead of a run-wide posture only (gap 5, engine side).
- Tests listed below.

## Implementation notes
1. Define the engine effect enum with the same 13 variants as T7.5 (`OperatorOnly` carries the operator statement class, e.g. `AlterDatabaseDefaultEdition`) and a `CONTRACT = "RoutineEffectsV1"` constant.
2. Construct-to-effect table: SELECT/cursor reads -> ReadDb; SELECT FOR UPDATE/LOCK TABLE -> RowLock; INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE -> Dml; `NEXTVAL` -> SequenceAdvance; COMMIT/ROLLBACK/SAVEPOINT/SET TRANSACTION -> TxnControl; `PRAGMA AUTONOMOUS_TRANSACTION` -> Autonomous; CREATE/ALTER/DROP/TRUNCATE/GRANT/REVOKE via folded literal -> Ddl (Admin for system-level statements; `ALTER DATABASE DEFAULT EDITION` -> OperatorOnly); unresolved/data-dependent `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE`, `DBMS_SQL` -> DynamicSql; `UTL_*`, `DBMS_PIPE`, `DBMS_AQ`, `DBMS_SCHEDULER` -> ExternalIo or Unknown; wrapped units, `LANGUAGE JAVA`/`EXTERNAL` call specs, `AUTHID CURRENT_USER` -> Unknown; any construct without a mapping -> Unknown.
3. Closure: walk calls with set union; include T7.2a initializer units and only the defaults the call shape evaluates (explicit argument supplied -> default not evaluated); any unresolved callee -> Unknown + not Clean.
4. SYS/SYSTEM callees are emitted as unresolved external calls with exact identity; the oraclemcp adapter (T7.7) resolves them against `sys_effects.toml`; the engine never assumes them pure.
5. Exhaustiveness: a test enumerates every AST/IR statement and expression variant (compile-time `match` without wildcard, or a variant-count assertion) and asserts a mapping exists.
6. Keep `plsql-sast`, lineage and doc consumers compiling.

## Test plan
Engine unit tests (synthetic PL/SQL fixtures), JSONL case log (case id, expected effect set, actual, completeness):
- Gap tests: `gap1_dml_ddl_commit_are_distinct_effects`; `gap2_commit_rollback_and_autonomous_emit_effects`; `gap3_routine_without_edges_is_not_proven` (a routine calling unloaded `UTL_HTTP.REQUEST` or `DBMS_SCHEDULER.CREATE_JOB` yields Unknown/ExternalIo, never ReadDb-only); `gap4_exact_identity_no_case_fold` (`"MixedCase"` vs `MIXEDCASE` are distinct); `gap5_partial_completeness_not_clean`.
- Effect tests: `select_calling_nextval_routine_has_sequence_advance`; `select_for_update_routine_has_row_lock`; `literal_alter_database_default_edition_is_operator_only`; `literal_execute_immediate_create_table_folds_to_ddl`; `concatenated_execute_immediate_is_dynamic_sql`; `variable_execute_immediate_is_dynamic_sql`.
- Closure tests (with T7.2a units): `package_init_with_dml_in_closure`, `package_init_with_commit_in_closure`, `package_init_with_autonomous_in_closure`, `package_init_with_nextval_in_closure`, `package_init_with_utl_call_in_closure`; `declaration_initializer_effectful_function_in_closure`; `omitted_default_expression_effectful_function_in_closure`; `explicit_argument_does_not_evaluate_default`.
- Unknown-by-construction: `wrapped_body_is_unknown`, `dbms_sql_is_unknown`, `dbms_scheduler_is_unknown`, `dbms_pipe_is_unknown`, `dbms_aq_is_unknown`, `utl_call_is_unknown`, `java_call_spec_is_unknown`, `external_procedure_is_unknown`, `authid_current_user_is_unknown`.
- `construct_to_effect_mapping_is_exhaustive`.

## Proof split
Proves the engine's effect sets and closures on source. T7.7 proves the adapter trusts only Clean + exact identity and maps effects exhaustively; T7.8 proves catalog facts (VALID, overload ambiguity, unreadable callees); T7.7 owns the SYS allowlist; T7.13 proves proof vs observed behaviour live (differential).

## Non-goals
oraclemcp-side types and admission (T7.5), adapter (T7.7), catalog facts (T7.8), parser fuzz (T7.3), publishing (R.3).

## No-claim boundary
Green engine tests do not prove Oracle executes what the source says (T7.13 differential), nor that catalog state matches the analysed source (T7.8/T7.11).

## Considerations
- Structure-owner check: gaps 3, 4 and 5 physically live in the oraclemcp adapter (`crates/oraclemcp/src/plsql_tools.rs` `PlsqlSideEffectOracle`) and gap 1's three-verdict type is `oraclemcp_guard::Purity`. Decision: this bead fixes the engine half (explicit edges/effects, exact lookup, per-closure completeness); T7.7 fixes the adapter half with its own tests. Both halves must land before T7.9.
- Structure-owner check: `RoutineEffectsV1` crosses the engine-free boundary (oraclemcp-* library crates must not import plsql-* crates, ci.yml `boundary` job; the engine must not depend on oraclemcp-guard). Decision: T7.5 owns the canonical type in `oraclemcp-guard`; this bead defines an engine mirror with identical variant names and the same contract string; T7.7 maps it with an exhaustive `match` (no wildcard) plus a parity test.
- Consumed by oraclemcp via the T0.6 pin refresh (which depends on this bead).
- `sec`: second-agent review before batch verify.
- Governance: AGENTS.md constitution binds (commit explicit paths, rule 17 atomicity, never weaken the fail-closed guard, confidentiality: synthetic fixtures only, no customer/OCI/field identifiers). Line numbers are hints at 1fbe6eb0 (oraclemcp) / 5834197 (plsql-intelligence); re-derive with `rg -n`.

## Absorbs
None.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: For each synthetic fixture the engine reports the exact effect set and closure listed in the test plan; the literal `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'CREATE TABLE t (x NUMBER)'` folds to Ddl.
- [ ] Positive: A routine whose only statement calls an unloaded SYS routine reports Unknown (or ExternalIo), never a ReadDb-only set.
- [ ] Negative: A walker that treats no-outgoing-edges as proven fails `gap3_routine_without_edges_is_not_proven`.

title: Engine parser fuzz targets: repair, extend to package units and effect extraction
description:
## Context
Plan §9.2 step 1 requires fuzz targets for the engine parser; §18 maps W7 to `/testing-fuzzing` (parser, wrapper). T0.6 (engine pin refresh) depends on this bead. Measured at 5834197: the engine already has a detached cargo-fuzz crate `fuzz/` (own `[workspace]`) with targets `parse_lower`, `lower_statement_body`, `lower_expression`, `lower_type_decl`, `ir_lower_statement_body`, `catalog_snapshot_json`, `catalog_async_loader`, `live_runtime_ops`, `mcp_async_dispatch`, plus `corpus/` and `artifacts/`. Its optional `live-mcp` feature pins `plsql-mcp` and `oraclemcp-core`/`oraclemcp-db = "=0.4.1"`, which are retired/stale (`plsql-mcp` retired 2026-06-30).

## Outcome
`cargo fuzz build` succeeds for every retained target on the pinned nightly; new targets cover package-body lowering with members/initializers/defaults (T7.2a) and effect/closure extraction including literal `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` folding (T7.2); every target runs for a bounded time in the engine's scheduled tier-B lane (T5.4 tier rules), and any crash input is committed to the corpus with a regression test.

## Deliverable
- Engine repo `fuzz/`: repair `Cargo.toml` so default targets build without retired crates; new targets `package_units_lower` (arbitrary text wrapped as a package spec/body) and `effects_extract` (parse -> lower -> closure -> effect set; asserts no panic and that an input with parse diagnostics never yields a Clean closure).
- Seed corpus from the engine's existing PL/SQL fixtures (synthetic only).
- Scheduled workflow entry in the engine repo's CI (tier B, bounded time per target), coordinated with T5.4.

## Implementation notes
1. Build every target on the pinned toolchain; list which fail and why.
2. Retired-crate targets (`mcp_async_dispatch`, `live_runtime_ops` under `live-mcp`): propose removal to the operator (RULE 1) or keep them excluded from default builds; do not delete without the explicit command.
3. Add the two new targets and their invariants (no panic; diagnostics => not Clean; a routine body containing a statement never yields an empty effect set).
4. Wire a bounded scheduled run (5 minutes per target) into the engine CI; failures report through the repo's tier-B reporting (T5.4).
5. Minimize and commit any crash; add a unit regression test named `fuzz_regression_<id>`.

## Test plan
- `cargo +<pinned nightly> fuzz build` for every retained target (evidence log).
- Bounded run of every target in the scheduled lane: zero crashes over the budget (evidence: run log with target, iterations, duration).
- Regression unit tests for every committed crash input.

## Proof split
Proves the parser/lowerer/effect extractor does not panic or mis-report completeness on fuzzed input within the budget. Wrapper/bind-builder fuzz is T7.13 (oraclemcp).

## Non-goals
Guard fuzz corpus in oraclemcp (W1 T1.3), wrapper fuzz (T7.13), fixing oraclemcp's `fuzz.yml` (T5.1).

## No-claim boundary
A clean fuzz run does not prove semantic correctness of effect sets.

## Considerations
- Structure-owner check: the plan calls this "engine parser fuzz targets" as if none exist; targets already exist, so this bead is repair + extension. RULE 1 applies to removing the stale `live-mcp` targets.
- Resource discipline (AGENTS.md rule 6): bounded runs, dedicated target dir.
- Governance: AGENTS.md constitution binds (commit explicit paths, rule 17 atomicity, never weaken the fail-closed guard, confidentiality: synthetic fixtures only, no customer/OCI/field identifiers). Line numbers are hints at 1fbe6eb0 (oraclemcp) / 5834197 (plsql-intelligence); re-derive with `rg -n`.

## Absorbs
None.

title: Build PL/SQL-intelligence into every artifact and one image; prove all 9 tools per target
description:
## Context
Plan §9.3 (R13): every release artifact (binaries for all 7 targets + the GHCR image) includes PL/SQL-intelligence; no separate flavour; the feature becomes a default of the `oraclemcp` crate. Today: `crates/oraclemcp/Cargo.toml` has `default = []` and an optional `plsql-intelligence` feature over 13 `plsql-*` crates pinned `=0.7.0` (root `Cargo.toml`); `release.yml` builds `--features dashboard-bundle,oracledb` only, with a per-target size check (`binary_warn_bytes: 43000000`, `binary_limit_bytes: 48000000`); `Dockerfile` has a `runtime-plsql-intelligence` stage next to `runtime`; `.github/workflows/docker.yml` has a `core|plsql-intelligence` variant matrix with `-plsql-intelligence` / `plsql-intelligence-latest` tags; `ci.yml` job `plsql-intelligence` is `continue-on-error: true` (hosted 2-core runner OOM/timeout) and runs `scripts/plsql_feature_lane_check.sh`, which asserts "exactly the eight oracle_plsql_* tools" (the ninth tool, `oracle_lineage`, is not `oracle_plsql_`-prefixed). README claims a `:plsql-intelligence-latest` image that doesn't exist. The engine is pure Rust; ANTLR runtime and Java sit only behind the off-by-default `antlr-codegen` feature (`plsql-parser-antlr/build.rs`: normal builds never require Java; regeneration only with `PLSQL_ANTLR_REGEN=1`). W6 "one image": remove the Docker variant matrix, the `runtime-plsql-intelligence` stage and the extra tags; one image remains. Absorbed `1efki`: lock the complete container OS and Python dependency closure (Oracle Linux dnf packages resolve from moving repos; python-oracledb 4.0.2 transitive `cryptography`/`typing_extensions` float).

## Outcome
`cargo build -p oraclemcp` (default features) includes the engine; every release archive (7 targets) and the single GHCR image list all 9 PL/SQL tools in `tools/list`; the CI PL/SQL lane is required and green within its budget; size budgets equal measured size + headroom; a release gate refuses `PLSQL_ANTLR_REGEN` set or `antlr-codegen` enabled; container OS packages and Python deps are hash-locked.

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp/Cargo.toml`: `plsql-intelligence` in `default`.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: build with the default feature set; per-target measured size budgets; gate step asserting `PLSQL_ANTLR_REGEN` is unset and `antlr-codegen` is not in the resolved feature set (`cargo tree -e features`); artifact-acceptance job running `--version`, `doctor` and `tools/list` against every archive target and the GHCR image on a compatible native runner or a declared emulator per target, asserting all 9 tools (`oracle_plsql_parse`, `oracle_plsql_analyze`, `oracle_plsql_what_breaks`, `oracle_plsql_lineage`, `oracle_lineage`, `oracle_plsql_sast`, `oracle_plsql_doc`, `oracle_plsql_live_snapshot`, `oracle_plsql_blast_radius`).
- `Dockerfile`: remove the `runtime-plsql-intelligence` stage and its builder; single `runtime`. `.github/workflows/docker.yml`: remove the variant matrix and `-plsql-intelligence`/`plsql-intelligence-latest` tags.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` job `plsql-intelligence`: required (drop `continue-on-error`), runner sizing / `codegen-units` / `debug=0` for deps; `scripts/plsql_feature_lane_check.sh`: assert all 9 tools by name from the registry list, not a hard-coded 8.
- Container closure (1efki): RPM snapshot or equivalent immutable OS-package closure per architecture; hash-locked Python constraints/wheelhouse for CI/runtime images; contract tests that mutate a transitive version/hash and prove the build refuses.
- Record the measured build memory/time and binary size per target in the bead evidence and in the plan's §9.3 numbers (plan asks to record them).

## Implementation notes
1. Measure: build each target with the engine on the release profile; record peak RSS, wall time, binary size.
2. Fix CI OOM only by runner sizing or build settings, never by shrinking the product.
3. Set `binary_limit_bytes` and `binary_warn_bytes` per target from the measurement (see Considerations).
4. Artifact acceptance: native runners for linux x86_64/aarch64, macOS, Windows; a declared emulator (qemu-user) for any target without one; unpacking a foreign archive without running it proves nothing.
5. Single image: builder with default features; GHCR acceptance runs `docker run --rm <image> --json info` + `tools/list` and asserts engine=true and the 9 tools; prints the digest.
6. 1efki closure locks with refusal contract tests; keep nonroot and complete-context invariants.

## Test plan
- CI lane `plsql-intelligence` required and green (`cargo test -p oraclemcp --all-targets` with default features + `scripts/plsql_feature_lane_check.sh`).
- Release-gate job `artifact-acceptance` (per target + image) green on a release-candidate run; log per target: target, runner/emulator, `--version` output, `doctor` exit, tool count, the 9 names.
- `antlr_codegen_gate` step: negative run with `PLSQL_ANTLR_REGEN=1` exported fails the gate (recorded once in evidence).
- 1efki contract tests: mutate one RPM/wheel hash -> build refuses before execution.

## Proof split
Proves packaging and presence of the 9 tools on every artifact. Tool behaviour is proven by T4.9 (offline + live external); the image-tag truth in docs by T6.2.

## Non-goals
Tool behaviour tests (T4.9), README/docs edits (T6.2/T6.3), the served engine-backed classifier (T7.9).

## No-claim boundary
Tools listed on every artifact does not prove they work against a database (T4.9, T9.6).

## Considerations
- Structure-owner check: headroom value (plan says "measured + headroom"). Decision: hard budget = measured + 15%, warn = measured + 5%, per target; the operator may change the percentage but not skip measurement.
- The Docker stage/matrix removal is authorised by the one-image decision (W6/§9.3); RULE 1 applies to any whole-file deletion.
- AGENTS.md "pure Rust, no C toolchain" must stay true: the gate proves `antlr-codegen` is off.
- Heavy builds through `scripts/build_lease.sh`.
- Governance: AGENTS.md constitution binds (commit explicit paths, rule 17 atomicity, never weaken the fail-closed guard, confidentiality: synthetic fixtures only, no customer/OCI/field identifiers). Line numbers are hints at 1fbe6eb0 (oraclemcp) / 5834197 (plsql-intelligence); re-derive with `rg -n`.

## Absorbs
- oraclemcp-xoflp.3.2: restore the required PL/SQL feature CI lane after runner sizing (kept whole).
- oraclemcp-2q4em.4.3: publish the PL/SQL image on every tag and verify engine=true + tools listed (kept as single-image acceptance; the separate `-plsql-intelligence` tags are dropped per the one-image decision).
- oraclemcp-1efki: lock the container OS and Python dependency closure with refusal contract tests (kept whole).

title: RoutineEffectsV1 set, one admission function and level derivation (seam)
description:
## Context
Plan §9.4 step 1, a standalone early seam: W12, W13 and W14 depend on it, not on all of W7 (plan §19 track F). It answers "how can a custom tool whose package performs DDL be supported": the routine's proven effects set `Admission.required_level` (`crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/policy_gate.rs`). Today `crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/purity.rs` has only `Purity` (ProvenReadOnly / ProvenSideEffecting / Unknown), `ObjectRef` and the `SideEffectOracle` trait (default `Unknown`). W7 invariants (plan §9.4, binding on every W7 bead): a routine that can't be proven stays refused; effects map to a required level; identity is exact and the whole call closure is pinned by hash; everything is re-checked at apply (SEC-1); DML rolls back by default; nothing ever auto-commits (AGENTS.md); caller text is never concatenated into PL/SQL.

Shape (binding): `RoutineEffects` (contract `RoutineEffectsV1`) is a SET, not an ordered lattice: `{ReadDb, RowLock, SessionState, Dml, Ddl, Admin, SequenceAdvance, OperatorOnly(OperatorStatementClass), TxnControl, Autonomous, DynamicSql, ExternalIo, Unknown}`. Any parsed construct without an explicit effect mapping becomes `Unknown`. Effects propagate through the call closure by set union. Transaction control and autonomous transactions are separate effects that break rollback-by-default, not "more privileged DDL" (an earlier "TxnControl >= DDL" mapping is withdrawn).
Always refused in 0.12: `TxnControl`, `Autonomous`, unresolved `DynamicSql`, `ExternalIo`, `Unknown`, `SequenceAdvance` (non-transactional; the guard already treats `NEXTVAL` as permanent) and `OperatorOnly` (refused on every agent path at every level; literal dynamic SQL propagates `OperatorOnly` instead of reducing it to `Admin`, so a routine containing a literal `ALTER DATABASE DEFAULT EDITION` can't become agent-reachable through a custom tool).
One admission function: `RoutineEffectsV1` owns one context-specific admission function; consumers (custom tools, DDL-trigger closures, W12, W13, W14) call it and never repeat hand-maintained effect lists. In every context, `DynamicSql` (unresolved), `SequenceAdvance`, `OperatorOnly`, `TxnControl`, `Autonomous`, `ExternalIo` and `Unknown` refuse. DDL-trigger context: anything beyond `ReadDb`/`SessionState` refuses.
Level derivation (after the refusal check): highest of `ReadDb -> READ_ONLY`, `RowLock/SessionState/Dml -> READ_WRITE` (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` holds row locks, as the guard already maps it), `Ddl -> DDL`, `Admin -> ADMIN`. `Purity` stays for SELECT expressions.

## Outcome
`oraclemcp-guard` exports `RoutineEffectsV1` (set), the `RoutineEffect` variants, `OperatorStatementClass`, `AdmissionContext`, and one `admit(effects, context) -> Result<OperatingLevel, EffectRefusal>` function; `Admission.required_level` in `policy_gate.rs` is raised to the effect-derived level when a routine effect set is present (never lowered). Consumers wait on this seam.

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/purity.rs`: `RoutineEffect` enum (13 variants; `OperatorOnly(OperatorStatementClass)`), `RoutineEffectsV1` (ordered set, stable serialization with contract tag `"RoutineEffectsV1"`, union), `OperatorStatementClass` (at least `AlterDatabaseDefaultEdition`), `AdmissionContext` (decision: `CustomToolCall`, `DdlTrigger`, `DmlMutationClosure`, `ChangeRequestTest`, `ImpactReport`), `EffectRefusal` typed reasons, `admit()` and `derived_level()`.
- `crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/policy_gate.rs`: `Admission.required_level` hook-up (max with the effect-derived level) in the SAME commit (rule 17).
- `crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/lib.rs`: exports.
- Seam only: no engine, catalog or dispatch wiring. Consumers waiting on it: T7.2, T7.6, T7.9, T7.9a, T7.9b, T7.10, T12.1, T12.4a, T13.2a, T14.4.

## Implementation notes
1. Types with exhaustive `match` everywhere (no wildcard arms) so adding a variant forces every consumer to decide.
2. `admit()`: first refuse the always-refused set; then the context-specific allowed set (DdlTrigger: only ReadDb/SessionState; ImpactReport: reports, never admits execution); then `derived_level()` = max over the mapping.
3. `policy_gate.rs`: when an effect set accompanies a decision, `required_level = max(base, derived)`; the existing test `a_policy_can_never_lower_a_required_level` stays green and gains an effect-set variant.
4. Serialization is canonical (sorted variants) so it can be hashed into closure pins and impact bindings.

## Test plan
Unit tests in `oraclemcp-guard` (synthetic effect sets; engine-derived versions live in T7.2):
- `effects_select_calling_nextval_routine_not_read_only` (SequenceAdvance refused).
- `effects_select_for_update_routine_not_read_only` (RowLock -> READ_WRITE).
- `effects_literal_alter_database_default_edition_is_operator_only_on_admin_lane` (refused even with ADMIN max_level).
- `effects_package_init_dml_requires_read_write`, `effects_package_init_commit_refused`, `effects_package_init_autonomous_refused`, `effects_package_init_nextval_refused`, `effects_package_init_utl_refused` on synthetic unions.
- `effects_ddl_trigger_context_refuses_nextval`, `..._refuses_dynamic_sql`, `..._refuses_operator_only`, `..._refuses_dml`; `effects_ddl_trigger_context_admits_read_and_session_state`.
- `effects_union_is_order_independent` (proptest).
- `effects_level_derivation_table` (every variant, every context).
- `admission_required_level_never_lowered_by_effects` (policy_gate).
- `effects_serialization_is_canonical`.

## Proof split
Proves the type, admission and level rules on synthetic sets. T7.2 proves engine-derived sets; T7.7/T7.9 prove the served path uses `admit()`; consumers prove their own contexts.

## Non-goals
Computing effects from source (T7.2/T7.7), identity (T7.6), dispatch wiring (T7.9/T7.10), the operator executor for `ALTER DATABASE DEFAULT EDITION` (T12.1).

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove any real routine's effects are computed correctly.

## Considerations
- Seam: consumers never start before it lands (plan §19.3).
- Rule 17: the type and its `policy_gate.rs` hook-up land in one commit.
- Structure-owner check: the `AdmissionContext` variant list and the owner of `OperatorStatementClass`. Decision: this bead defines both; T12.1 consumes `OperatorStatementClass` and never changes the refusal rule.

title: Exact routine identity RoutineRef; resolve CALL instead of always refusing it
description:
## Context
Plan §9.4 step 2: exact identity `RoutineRef { schema, package?, member, overload }`; quoting is preserved; synonyms resolve through the catalog; database links are refused. This removes the reason CALL is always refused (`crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/classifier.rs`, the `unanalyzable_plsql_construct` CALL branch): today `ObjectRef` (`purity.rs`) has only `schema` + `name`, so a packaged member or overload can't be named. Ambiguous overloads are `Unknown` by construction (§9.4). W7 invariants (plan §9.4, binding on every W7 bead): a routine that can't be proven stays refused; effects map to a required level; identity is exact and the whole call closure is pinned by hash; everything is re-checked at apply (SEC-1); DML rolls back by default; nothing ever auto-commits (AGENTS.md); caller text is never concatenated into PL/SQL.

## Outcome
The guard represents a routine by exact `RoutineRef`; the classifier parses CALL/`BEGIN pkg.proc(...); END;` call targets into a `RoutineRef` candidate; resolution (synonym -> target, overload selection) happens through a catalog port; a CALL is still refused unless an effect proof admits it (no proof = Unknown = refused). DB-link targets are refused.

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/purity.rs`: `RoutineRef { schema, package: Option<_>, member, overload: Option<u32> }` with an identifier type preserving quoted case; `SideEffectOracle` gains `routine_effects(&RoutineRef) -> RoutineEffectsV1` (default `{Unknown}`); keep `routine_purity` for SELECT expressions.
- `crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/classifier.rs`: CALL branch builds a `RoutineRef` and asks the oracle; with `UnknownOracle` (served default until T7.9) CALL stays refused.
- `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/catalog_resolver.rs`: synonym resolution (`ALL_SYNONYMS`), overload listing (`ALL_PROCEDURES.SUBPROGRAM_ID`, `ALL_ARGUMENTS.OVERLOAD`) returning exact identities; DB link (`@`) -> refusal.

## Implementation notes
1. Identifier normalization: unquoted -> uppercase; quoted -> exact bytes; never case-fold a quoted name.
2. Overload: named-notation arity/type matching against `ALL_ARGUMENTS`; more than one candidate -> ambiguous -> Unknown.
3. Synonyms: private then PUBLIC per Oracle resolution; chains followed with a cap; a remote synonym -> refused.
4. Name capture (Oracle resolves a first part as a local object first) is checked in T7.10; this bead records the resolved owner.

## Test plan
Unit (guard) + in-process catalog tests with synthetic catalogs:
- `routine_ref_quoted_identity_preserved`, `routine_ref_unquoted_uppercased`.
- `call_with_db_link_refused`.
- `call_unresolved_stays_refused` (UnknownOracle: CALL still refused at every level).
- `call_ambiguous_overload_is_unknown`.
- `call_synonym_resolves_to_exact_target`, `call_public_synonym_after_private`.
- `call_proven_by_oracle_admitted_at_derived_level` (test oracle returns `{Dml}` -> READ_WRITE).

## Proof split
Proves identity and resolution. T7.7 proves the adapter looks up by exact identity only; T7.8 pins identities in facts; T7.10 proves name-capture checks live.

## Non-goals
Engine adapter (T7.7), fact store (T7.8), served binding (T7.9), custom-tool wrapper (T7.10).

## No-claim boundary
Does not make any CALL executable on the served path (T7.9 wires the oracle).

## Considerations
- Fail-closed: removing the CALL-always-refused reason must not admit any CALL without an effect proof; `call_unresolved_stays_refused` guards it.
- Hot lane `file-lane:classifier`; coordinate with W1 edits of `classifier.rs`.
- `sec`: second-agent review.
- Governance: AGENTS.md constitution binds (commit explicit paths, rule 17 atomicity, never weaken the fail-closed guard, confidentiality: synthetic fixtures only, no customer/OCI/field identifiers). Line numbers are hints at 1fbe6eb0 (oraclemcp) / 5834197 (plsql-intelligence); re-derive with `rg -n`.

## Absorbs
None.

- [ ] Negative: With the served `UnknownOracle`, `CALL pkg.p()` is refused at every level.

title: Engine adapter trusts only Clean closures and exact identity; map effects exhaustively
description:
## Context
Plan §9.4 step 3: engine 0.8.0 fixes the five soundness gaps; the adapter trusts only `Clean` completeness and exact identity. The adapter is `PlsqlSideEffectOracle` in `crates/oraclemcp/src/plsql_tools.rs` (impl `SideEffectOracle`, used only in `#[cfg(test)]` today via `classifier_from_analysis_run`). Engine soundness gaps (plan §9.1, measured at plsql-intelligence 5834197 / oraclemcp 1fbe6eb0): (1) only three verdicts (`oraclemcp_guard::Purity` = ProvenReadOnly / ProvenSideEffecting / Unknown), so DML, DDL and COMMIT are indistinguishable; (2) no depgraph edges for COMMIT/ROLLBACK or `PRAGMA AUTONOMOUS_TRANSACTION`, although the IR models `Statement::TransactionControl` / `Statement::ExecuteImmediate` (`plsql-ir/src/stmt.rs`); `plsql_depgraph::EdgeKind` has no transaction/autonomous variant; (3) FAIL-OPEN: a routine without outgoing edges counts as `ProvenReadOnly` (`PlsqlSideEffectOracle::routine_node_purity` starts from ProvenReadOnly), so unloaded SYS calls (UTL_HTTP, DBMS_*) may pass; (4) case-insensitive fallback in `PlsqlSideEffectOracle::resolve_candidates` (`eq_ignore_ascii_case`); (5) `CompletenessPosture::Partial` still counts as trusted (`from_analysis_run`). Gaps 3-5 are in this adapter: `routine_node_purity` starts from `ProvenReadOnly` and only downgrades via outgoing edges; `resolve_candidates` falls back to `eq_ignore_ascii_case`; `from_analysis_run` sets `source_trustworthy` for `Clean | Partial`. Also `catalog_vpd_purity_for_node` returns `ProvenReadOnly` when no catalog is attached, and `statement_purity([])` returns `ProvenReadOnly`.
`Unknown` by construction (always refused; each case has a unit test asserting `Unknown`): wrapped bodies (`ALL_SOURCE` shows `wrapped`); any unresolved or data-dependent `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` (dynamic text built from a parameter, variable, table, function call, conditional concatenation or external input); any `DBMS_SQL`, `DBMS_SCHEDULER`, `DBMS_PIPE`, `DBMS_AQ` or `UTL_*` call; Java stored procedures and external procedures; `AUTHID CURRENT_USER` units in v1 (they resolve unqualified names in the caller's schema at run time, so the closure proven at load isn't the closure executed); any callee whose source the profile can't read; any SYS/SYSTEM routine absent from the committed, reviewed, tighten-only allowlist `sys_effects.toml`; ambiguous overloads; any closure member with `STATUS <> 'VALID'`. Exception (PL/SQL can only issue DDL through dynamic SQL): a single compile-time string literal used by `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` may be folded by the engine, parsed and classified recursively; on success its inner effects replace `DynamicSql`, otherwise it stays `DynamicSql`/`Unknown`; no caller value may contribute to the text; literal dynamic SQL propagates `OperatorOnly` (never reduced to `Admin`).

## Outcome
The adapter consumes the engine's `RoutineEffectsV1`/`InvocationClosureV1` (T7.2 via the T0.6 pin), maps it to `oraclemcp_guard::RoutineEffectsV1` with an exhaustive match, and returns `{{Unknown}}` for any non-Clean closure, any non-exact identity match, any routine without a resolved closure and any SYS/SYSTEM callee absent from `sys_effects.toml`; absence of edges or absence of a catalog is never proof.

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp/src/plsql_tools.rs` (`PlsqlSideEffectOracle`): implement `routine_effects(&RoutineRef)`; remove the case-insensitive fallback; accept only Clean (run posture and per-closure flag from T7.2); a routine without an engine-reported effect set -> Unknown; missing catalog -> Unknown (not ProvenReadOnly); exhaustive engine->guard effect mapping + `effects_contract_parity` test.
- `sys_effects.toml`: committed, reviewed, tighten-only allowlist of SYS/SYSTEM routines with their effect sets (location decision: `crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/sys_effects.toml`, embedded with `include_str!`, parsed at startup; a malformed file fails startup), starting minimal (`DBMS_LOB.SUBSTR`, `DBMS_METADATA.GET_DDL`, `DBMS_XPLAN.DISPLAY`, already trusted by `GENERATED_READ_CLASSIFIER`, each re-justified in a comment).
- Tighten-only check: a test that fails if an entry's effect set shrinks or a new entry appears relative to the committed baseline without the reviewed-marker update in the same commit.

## Implementation notes
1. Pin refresh T0.6 brings the engine with T7.2; adapt the API.
2. Rewrite lookup to exact `RoutineRef` (T7.6) -> engine node; no candidate lists with case-insensitive fallback.
3. Map effects; an unmatched engine variant is a compile error (exhaustive match).
4. SYS callees: look up exact identity in `sys_effects.toml`; absent -> Unknown.
5. Keep the `Purity` path for SELECT expressions derived from the effect set (`{{ReadDb}}` only -> ProvenReadOnly; anything else -> not proven).

## Test plan
Unit tests in `crates/oraclemcp` (feature now default), synthetic analysis runs:
- `adapter_gap3_no_edges_is_unknown`, `adapter_gap3_unloaded_sys_call_is_unknown` (UTL_HTTP, DBMS_SCHEDULER absent from sys_effects.toml).
- `adapter_gap4_no_case_insensitive_fallback`.
- `adapter_gap5_partial_is_untrusted`, `adapter_low_confidence_is_untrusted`.
- `adapter_missing_catalog_is_unknown`.
- `adapter_ambiguous_overload_is_unknown`.
- `effects_contract_parity` (engine variants == guard variants).
- `sys_effects_toml_parses_and_is_tighten_only`.
- Unknown-by-construction end to end (engine + adapter): `wrapped_body_refused`, `dynamic_execute_immediate_refused`, `dbms_sql_refused`, `authid_current_user_refused`, `java_and_external_procedure_refused`.

## Proof split
Proves the adapter never upgrades uncertainty to proof. T7.8 proves catalog facts (VALID, readable source); T7.9 proves served wiring; T7.13 proves proof vs behaviour live.

## Non-goals
Engine changes (T7.2), fact store (T7.8), served binding (T7.9).

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove the engine's effect sets are right (T7.2) or that the database matches the analysed source (T7.8/T7.11).

## Considerations
- Structure-owner check: split of gaps 1-5 between T7.2 (engine) and this bead (adapter); both must land before T7.9.
- Structure-owner check: `sys_effects.toml` location and owner (decision above: guard crate, owned by this bead).
- Fail-open fix: priority 0; `sec` second-agent review.
- Engine-free boundary: the adapter stays in `crates/oraclemcp` (the only crate allowed to import plsql-*).
- Governance: AGENTS.md constitution binds (commit explicit paths, rule 17 atomicity, never weaken the fail-closed guard, confidentiality: synthetic fixtures only, no customer/OCI/field identifiers). Line numbers are hints at 1fbe6eb0 (oraclemcp) / 5834197 (plsql-intelligence); re-derive with `rg -n`.

## Absorbs
None.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: A Clean synthetic closure with only reads maps to `{ReadDb}` and the guard admits it at READ_ONLY.
- [ ] Negative: A routine with no outgoing edges and no engine effect set is Unknown (today's code returns ProvenReadOnly).
- [ ] Negative: A `Partial` run is untrusted (today's code trusts it).
- [ ] Negative: A lowercase candidate does not resolve a quoted mixed-case node (today's fallback does).
- [ ] Negative: A SYS routine absent from `sys_effects.toml` is Unknown.
- [ ] Tests: Tests named in the Test plan green in `cargo test -p oraclemcp`.
- [ ] Proof class: unit; forbidden substitutes: a hand-written oracle stub in place of `PlsqlSideEffectOracle`.
- [ ] Consumers: T7.9, T7.13, T14.4.
- [ ] No-claim: Does not prove live Oracle behaviour or catalog freshness.

title: Catalog fact store with whole-closure keys (DB/PDB, edition, AUTHID, settings, triggers)
description:
## Context
Plan §9.4 step 4 (`ge6xe.8` -> `ge6xe.2`): per-database facts built per profile from live-snapshot extraction. A fact key covers the WHOLE closure: identity, the database/PDB and the edition; `AUTHID` and the compiler settings (e.g. `PLSQL_CCFLAGS`, which change conditionally compiled code); SHA-256 of the spec AND body source (including the package initialization section and default-parameter expressions); `ALL_OBJECTS.LAST_DDL_TIME` and `OBJECT_ID` of every closure member; the `ALL_DEPENDENCIES` targets (synonyms, types, sequences, tables) with their `LAST_DDL_TIME`; the triggers fired by the routine's own DML (from `ALL_TRIGGERS` on each DML target, with their source hashes and effects); the catalog revision. A missing or stale fact means `Unknown`. The store is file-backed (D14, no bundled DB). §23.3 notes (binding): extraction lives in `oraclemcp-db` (a new `catalog_facts.rs`); storage uses `oraclemcp-core::file_store`, per profile under the state directory; the in-memory resolver counter in `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/orient.rs` (`catalog_revision`, monotonic, resets on restart) must never key persisted facts: use DBID + container + edition + the closure's `LAST_DDL_TIME`s and hashes; only `ALL_*` views are used; a missing privilege yields `Unknown`. Absorbed `ge6xe.8` (Glean-pattern typed, file-backed schema+effect facts; adopt the design, not the software: pure Rust, no bundled DB).

## Outcome
For a profile, the server extracts and persists typed closure facts keyed by `(DBID, container, edition, RoutineRef, closure fingerprint)` where the fingerprint covers every item above; a lookup returns the facts only when every component re-reads identical, else `Unknown`; every missing `ALL_*` privilege, `STATUS <> 'VALID'` member, unreadable source (including `wrapped`) or truncated query yields `Unknown`.

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/catalog_facts.rs` (new domain file named by the plan): `ClosureFactKey`, `ClosureFacts` (members with OBJECT_ID, LAST_DDL_TIME, STATUS, AUTHID, compiler settings from `ALL_PLSQL_OBJECT_SETTINGS`, spec/body SHA-256 from `ALL_SOURCE`, dependency targets from `ALL_DEPENDENCIES`, DML-target triggers from `ALL_TRIGGERS` with source hashes), bounded extraction queries (server-owned; routed through the T1.2a `CatalogQueryId` catalog-read path once it exists).
- Storage: `oraclemcp-core::file_store` per profile under the state directory; schema-versioned records; corrupt/unknown version -> ignored (Unknown), never trusted.
- Revalidation API `revalidate(&ClosureFactKey) -> Fresh | Stale(reason) | Unknown(reason)` with bounded queries (used by T7.11 and W12/W13/W14).

## Implementation notes
1. Identity: DBID via a readable source (`SYS_CONTEXT('USERENV','DBID')`), container (`SYS_CONTEXT('USERENV','CON_NAME')`), edition (`SYS_CONTEXT('USERENV','CURRENT_EDITION_NAME')`).
2. Closure members come from the engine closure (T7.2 via T7.7) joined to catalog rows by exact identity (T7.6).
3. Hash canonical source bytes (ordered by LINE); `wrapped` -> Unknown.
4. Caps on members, dependencies and triggers; cap exhaustion -> Unknown.
5. The in-memory `catalog_revision` may be used only as a cache-invalidation hint, never in the persisted key.

## Test plan
- Unit (oraclemcp-db): `fact_key_changes_on_spec_source`, `fact_key_changes_on_body_source`, `fact_key_changes_on_authid`, `fact_key_changes_on_ccflags`, `fact_key_changes_on_last_ddl_time`, `fact_key_changes_on_object_id`, `fact_key_changes_on_dependency_target`, `fact_key_changes_on_trigger_source`, `fact_key_changes_on_edition`, `fact_key_changes_on_container`; `fact_store_ignores_in_memory_catalog_revision`; `fact_missing_privilege_is_unknown`; `fact_wrapped_source_is_unknown`; `fact_invalid_member_is_unknown`; `fact_cap_exhaustion_is_unknown`; `fact_store_corrupt_record_is_unknown`.
- Live in-process (FREE 23ai lane, synthetic package): `catalog_facts_live_roundtrip` (extract, persist, restart process, revalidate Fresh), `catalog_facts_live_recompile_is_stale` (`ALTER PACKAGE ... COMPILE` changes LAST_DDL_TIME -> Stale). JSONL case logs.

## Proof split
Proves fact extraction, keying and staleness. T7.11 proves per-run revalidation and quarantine; T7.9 consumes facts in the served binding; W12/W13/W14 reuse revalidation.

## Non-goals
The engine closure itself (T7.2), served binding (T7.9), quarantine policy (T7.11), DDL/mutation trigger collectors (T7.9a/T7.9b).

## No-claim boundary
Fresh facts do not prove the routine's effects (engine + adapter prove that).

## Considerations
- Structure-owner check: §9.4 step 4 lists "the catalog revision" in the key while §23.3 forbids keying persisted facts by the in-memory resolver counter. Decision: persisted key = DBID + container + edition + LAST_DDL_TIMEs + hashes; `catalog_revision` only invalidates the in-memory cache.
- Only `ALL_*` views on this path.
- Confidentiality: fact files contain object names of the operator's database; they stay in the state directory, never in committed artifacts or evidence (tests use synthetic schemas).
- Governance: AGENTS.md constitution binds (commit explicit paths, rule 17 atomicity, never weaken the fail-closed guard, confidentiality: synthetic fixtures only, no customer/OCI/field identifiers). Line numbers are hints at 1fbe6eb0 (oraclemcp) / 5834197 (plsql-intelligence); re-derive with `rg -n`.

## Absorbs
- oraclemcp-ge6xe.8: typed, file-backed catalog fact store (Glean design, pure Rust, no bundled DB) (kept; keys widened to the whole closure per §9.4 step 4).

- [ ] Proof class: unit + live in-process; forbidden substitutes: mock DB for the live cases, fixture JSON in place of extraction.
- [ ] Consumers: T7.9, T7.11, T7.9a, T7.9b, T12.6, T13.5, T14.6a.
