title: W8 Driver: all remaining driver-cx and backend fixes with full test coverage
description:
## Goal
Land every remaining driver-side and backend-side fix for the 0.12.0 train with full fix coverage (R15: "all fixes in, full fix coverage; no big driver features"), and release `oraclemcp-driver-cx` / `oraclemcp-driver-cx-protocol` **0.10.0** with a CHANGELOG, tests and green CI; oraclemcp then pins `=0.10.0`.

## Rulings that bind this workstream
- **R12** driver-cx stays the primary driver ("our driver is ahead and better"); the official `oracledb` crate is not made primary.
- **R15** all driver fixes in, full fix coverage; no big driver features.
- **R19** every claim is verified by a test; "already solved" is not accepted without proof.
- **R22** approved: the mcp-publisher installer `trap` cleans its own temp dir (RULE 1 permission for that deletion).
- **R24/R34** no process ceremony: nothing here produces an artifact that running code does not branch on.
- **R27** the rust-oracledb off-limits rule is lifted for this train.
- **R30** stable Rust on non-Windows (`k6q.14`) is kept as a cheap feature.

## Why driver-cx stays primary (R12)
- The official `oracledb` backend capabilities are `pem_wallet: false`, `iam_token: false`, `auto_login_wallet: false` (`crates/oraclemcp-db/src/connection.rs`, the official backend capability constant; re-derive with `rg -n "pem_wallet" crates/oraclemcp-db/src/connection.rs`). ADB wallets, IAM and PEM therefore work only on driver-cx.
- The official driver is a synchronous beta (`oracledb =26.0.0-beta.3`) with an uncancellable connect (`xoflp.1.6`). Making it primary would regress every OCI route.
- #54 (OCI ADB handshake) is a driver-cx defect we can fix ourselves; that is not possible upstream.

## Current state (evidence-backed)
- driver-cx 0.9.2 is primary on every route. The official `oracledb` fallback (in every build since `5aad87bb`) is tried only for basic-password connects without a wallet, after a raw driver-cx failure before any session exists, through a 2-slot / 250 ms guard (`OfficialConnectGuard` in `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/oracledb_actor.rs`, `OFFICIAL_CONNECT_GUARD_CAPACITY = 2`, `OFFICIAL_CONNECT_GUARD_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT = 250 ms`); driver-cx then gets one retry. PEM, cwallet.sso and IAM are driver-cx only; a live session never switches backend.
- Already fixed and closed with evidence (2026-09-23): VECTOR (`xoflp.1.3`), queued timeout (1.4), actor lifecycle (1.5, 1.10, 1.12), timezones (1.8, 1.9), fallback only before a session (1.13, 1.14), docs/tooling/ADR (1.2, 1.7, 1.15, 3.1, 3.3, 4.1, `qm4c9`, `ft0ti.3`).
- Retired by ruling (R12/R15, 2026-09-23): backend-qualification evidence (`2q4em.1.2`), capability lattice + Kani (`1.4/1.5`), frozen-driver lane (`1.8`), stable-Rust spike (`1.9`), the dual-backend epic `nhteq` (+ `.3/.4/.6`). Retired under R34: the metamorphic cross-backend suite `2q4em.1.6` (duplicates T8.6-T8.9).
- Driver repo: local `master` is pre-rename (`name = "oracledb"`), ahead 2 / behind 12 of `origin/main` (`cdc3e82`, `oraclemcp-driver-cx` 0.9.3 docs-only "discontinued" README). The rebase of `c467efd` + `4204676` across the rename is T0.2a (W0), not this workstream.

## Design (all remaining fixes)
| Task | Fix | Repo |
|---|---|---|
| T8.1 | Refuse non-regular wallet files (FIFO/device) and symlinks before any blocking read: driver `read_wallet_file` + oraclemcp doctor/wallet-validity readers | both |
| T8.2 | `trap` cleans the mcp-publisher installer's own temp dir (R22) | oraclemcp |
| T8.3 | Reproducible semver baseline (the yanked-dependency failure class); api-lock can be required again (T5.3 restores it) | oraclemcp |
| T8.4 | Prove the installer E2E passes (currently claimed only) | oraclemcp |
| T8.5 | Official `oracledb` connect cannot be cancelled (upstream `TcpStream::connect`): keep the bounded 2-slot/250 ms guard, **prove** its bound with a black-holed TCP endpoint test, document it as a mitigated upstream limit. No patches to Oracle's crate | oraclemcp |
| T8.6-T8.9 | Cross-backend parity: DATE/TIMESTAMP/INTERVAL, LOB/NULL, NUMBER boundaries, streaming, ORA error taxonomy, VECTOR variants, TCPS/PEM, reproducible in the FREE 23ai lane. Where the official backend lacks a type, a **typed refusal** is the tested behaviour | oraclemcp |
| T8.10 | Loom model for the official-driver actor (observed defects: actor lifecycle bugs `xoflp.1.5`/`1.10`/`1.12`) | oraclemcp |
| T8.12 | Finish the boundary/seam lints (no Tokio via the Oracle backend; one adapter file per backend; UPL allow-list already done) | oraclemcp |

title: Refuse non-regular and symlinked wallet files before any blocking read (driver + doctor)
description:
## Context
Wallet reads can hang forever. The driver protocol crate's `read_wallet_file` (`rust-oracledb/crates/oracledb-protocol/src/tls/wallet.rs`, published as `oraclemcp-driver-cx-protocol`; re-derive with `git grep -n "fn read_wallet_file"`) does `std::fs::File::open(path)` then `read_to_end` under only a byte cap (`MAX_WALLET_FILE_BYTES`, 16 MiB, via `read_wallet_reader`). A named pipe (FIFO) or character device placed at `ewallet.pem`, `ewallet.p12` or `cwallet.sso` passes `path.exists()` and `File::open` and then blocks forever in `open`/`read` before the cap applies. A symlink is followed.

Affected callers:
- driver: `read_ewallet_pem` / `read_ewallet_p12` (same file) and the SSO read in `crates/oracledb/src/tls.rs` (`read_wallet_file(&sso)`), i.e. every live driver-cx wallet connection setup;
- oraclemcp: `crates/oraclemcp-core/src/doctor.rs` delegates to the driver's `read_wallet_file` for SSO, PEM and P12 (around lines 1837-1870 at 1fbe6eb0), so `oraclemcp doctor` inherits the hang;
- oraclemcp: `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/connection.rs` `wallet_certificate_validity` reads `pem_wallet_path(dir)` with a plain `std::fs::read` (around line 317 at 1fbe6eb0), unbounded and blocking.

Rulings: R15 (all driver fixes, full coverage), R19 (proven by a test), R27 (driver repo in scope). Old bead `oraclemcp-xoflp.5.12`.

## Outcome
A FIFO, device, socket, directory or symlink at any accepted wallet filename is refused promptly with a typed wallet I/O error (no hang) by the driver reader, by `oraclemcp doctor`, and by `wallet_certificate_validity`; regular files still read exactly as before with the 16 MiB cap and the existing wallet precedence (SSO / PEM / P12) unchanged.

## Deliverable
- **Driver** (`rust-oracledb`, on the post-rename `main` from T0.2a): `crates/oracledb-protocol/src/tls/wallet.rs` `read_wallet_file` opens with no-follow + non-blocking semantics and verifies the opened handle is a regular file (`File::metadata()` on the opened handle, `file_type().is_file()`) before any read; new `WalletError` variant `NotRegularFile { path }` (or the existing `Io` with `ErrorKind::InvalidInput`, choose the typed variant; it is `#[non_exhaustive]`-compatible). The SSO read in `crates/oracledb/src/tls.rs` keeps calling this one reader.
- **oraclemcp**: `crates/oraclemcp-core/src/doctor.rs` wallet posture reads go through a local bounded, no-follow, non-blocking reader and then call the driver's pure parsers (`parse_ewallet_pem`, `parse_ewallet_p12`, SSO parse), so doctor is fixed without waiting for a pin refresh; `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/connection.rs` `wallet_certificate_validity` uses the same reader instead of `std::fs::read`. The reader is one function owned by `oraclemcp-db` (e.g. `read_wallet_file_bounded` next to `wallet_certificate_validity`), re-used by doctor; no second copy.
- CHANGELOG line in the driver repo (Unreleased section).

## Implementation notes
1. Unix: `OpenOptions::new().read(true).custom_flags(libc::O_NOFOLLOW | libc::O_NONBLOCK | libc::O_CLOEXEC)` via `std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt` (safe API). `O_NONBLOCK` makes `open` of a FIFO with no writer return immediately; `O_NOFOLLOW` fails with `ELOOP` on a final-component symlink. Then `file.metadata()?.file_type().is_file()` or refuse. After the check, reading a regular file is unaffected by `O_NONBLOCK`.
2. Windows: `custom_flags(FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT)` and refuse if the opened handle reports a reparse point or is not a regular file (same pattern as `crates/oraclemcp-core/src/file_store.rs`). Named pipes are not reachable through a wallet directory path on Windows; the regular-file check still covers devices.
3. Keep the 16 MiB cap and the `take(limit+1)` bounded read unchanged; keep `FileMissing` semantics for an absent file.
4. The check is on the opened handle (post-open verification), never a separate `symlink_metadata` pre-check alone (TOCTOU).
5. No `unsafe`; the `libc` constants are plain integers (use the `libc` crate or `rustix` already in the graph; do not add a new crate if one of these is present, check with `cargo tree -i libc`).
6. Error text names the path and "not a regular file"; never prints wallet bytes.

## Test plan
- Driver unit tests (`crates/oracledb-protocol/src/tls/wallet.rs` `#[cfg(test)]`, Unix-gated where they create FIFOs with `nix`-free `mkfifo` via `std::process::Command::new("mkfifo")` in a tempdir):
  - `read_wallet_file_refuses_fifo_without_blocking` for each of `ewallet.pem`, `ewallet.p12`, `cwallet.sso` (parametrised; each run under a 5 s watchdog thread that fails the test on timeout);
  - `read_wallet_file_refuses_symlink_to_regular_wallet`;
  - `read_wallet_file_refuses_directory_at_wallet_name`;
  - `read_wallet_file_refuses_char_device` (`/dev/null` symlinked is covered by the symlink case; use a direct path argument `/dev/zero` to prove the device refusal and that the cap is not what stops it);
  - `read_wallet_file_reads_regular_file_unchanged` and the existing oversize test stay green.
- oraclemcp tests: `crates/oraclemcp-core/tests/doctor_wallet_posture.rs` gains `doctor_wallet_posture_refuses_fifo_wallet_without_hanging` (all three filenames, watchdog) and `doctor_wallet_posture_refuses_symlinked_wallet`; `crates/oraclemcp-db` unit `wallet_certificate_validity_refuses_fifo_pem`.
- Connect path (driver-cx live connect with a FIFO wallet): `connect_refuses_fifo_wallet_before_blocking` in `crates/oraclemcp-db/tests/` runs against the fixed driver revision via a non-committed `cargo --config 'patch.crates-io...'` override pointing at the pushed driver SHA; the same test runs in CI once T0.7 refreshes the pin.
- Logging: each test prints one JSONL line `{case_id, wallet_file, file_kind, expected:"refused", actual, elapsed_ms}`.
- No release_0_12.json case (not a field issue).

## Proof split
This bead proves the refusal in the driver reader, doctor, `wallet_certificate_validity` and the driver-cx connect path (unit + offline). T0.7 proves the fixed driver revision is consumed by oraclemcp CI. T9.5a/T9.5b prove every legitimate wallet form still works live against ADB.

## Non-goals
- New wallet forms (T9.5a), connect_timeout for ADB descriptors (T9.5b).
- Changing wallet precedence, the 16 MiB cap, or wallet-password handling.
- Directory-level permission policy for wallet directories.

## No-claim boundary
A green result does not prove any wallet form connects to a real ADB, nor that wallet parsing is correct for malformed regular files beyond existing parser tests.

## Considerations
- Dependency note: the oraclemcp connect-path test needs the fixed driver, but T0.7 (pin refresh) depends on this bead, so this bead proves it with a non-committed `--config` patch override and records the exact command and driver SHA in the close evidence; T0.7 then runs it in CI. **structure-owner check**: confirm T0.7's acceptance lists `connect_refuses_fifo_wallet_before_blocking`.
- Hot files: `connection.rs` is shared with W2/W9 (file lane `wallet-io` covers only the wallet reader region; reserve the file before editing).
- `sec`: a hang during connect is a denial of service on a shared server lane; second-agent review before batch verify.
- Rule 17: the driver `WalletError` variant and every exhaustive match on it land in one driver commit.

## Absorbs
- `oraclemcp-xoflp.5.12`: full scope kept (non-blocking no-follow open with post-open type check, 16 MiB cap and precedence preserved, FIFO and symlink regressions for every accepted wallet filename).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: `read_wallet_file` on a regular `ewallet.pem`/`ewallet.p12`/`cwallet.sso` returns the same bytes as before; `oraclemcp doctor` wallet posture on the synthetic fixture wallet reports unchanged results.
- [ ] Negative: a FIFO with no writer at each of the three wallet filenames is refused with a typed not-regular-file error in under 5 s by the driver reader, by doctor, and by `wallet_certificate_validity` (a naive `File::open` implementation hangs and the watchdog fails the test).
- [ ] Negative: a symlink to a valid regular wallet file is refused (a follow-then-check implementation accepts it).
- [ ] Negative: `/dev/zero` passed as a wallet file path is refused as not-regular, not as oversized.
- [ ] Tests: `read_wallet_file_refuses_fifo_without_blocking`, `read_wallet_file_refuses_symlink_to_regular_wallet`, `read_wallet_file_refuses_directory_at_wallet_name`, `read_wallet_file_refuses_char_device`, `read_wallet_file_reads_regular_file_unchanged` (driver); `doctor_wallet_posture_refuses_fifo_wallet_without_hanging`, `doctor_wallet_posture_refuses_symlinked_wallet`, `wallet_certificate_validity_refuses_fifo_pem`, `connect_refuses_fifo_wallet_before_blocking` (oraclemcp); all green in `cargo test -p oraclemcp-driver-cx-protocol` and `cargo test -p oraclemcp-core -p oraclemcp-db`.
- [ ] Proof class: unit / offline; forbidden substitutes: a `symlink_metadata` pre-check without post-open verification, a test that skips on timeout instead of failing.
- [ ] Consumers: T0.7, T9.5a, T9.5b.
- [ ] No-claim: does not prove any wallet form works against a real ADB.

title: Loom model of the official-driver actor lifecycle and connect guard
description:
## Context
The official `oracledb` backend runs each physical connection on a dedicated OS thread (`BlockingConnectionActor` in `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/oracledb_actor.rs`): bounded asupersync `mpsc` mailbox (capacity `ACTOR_MAILBOX_CAPACITY = 1`), `oneshot` replies, an atomic state `ACTOR_ACTIVE / ACTOR_QUARANTINED / ACTOR_CLOSED`, a quarantine reason mutex, a completion ack with `ACTOR_COMPLETION_ACK_GRACE = 250 ms`, a join handle, and the global `OfficialConnectGuard` semaphore (2 slots, 250 ms acquire). ADR-0014 (`docs/adr/0014-blocking-driver-backend-execution-model.md`) is the decided execution model. Observed defects in this code were the actor lifecycle bugs `xoflp.1.5`, `1.10`, `1.12` (all fixed); the lost-wakeup class also hung the shipping spool in 0.9.x.

Plan W8 + R34 anti-ceremony audit: the loom model is **kept** because of those observed defects. Only the loom part of the old bead `2q4em.1.3` survives; its design-spike/ADR part is done (ADR-0014 exists) and its `nhteq.4` design section is obsolete (nhteq retired).

Existing loom pattern: `crates/oraclemcp-core/tests/loom_admission.rs` and `loom_lane_lock_order.rs`, `crates/oraclemcp-audit/tests/loom_shipping_spool.rs`; loom is a `[target.'cfg(loom)'.dev-dependencies]` entry; `.github/workflows/loom.yml` runs each with `RUSTFLAGS="--cfg loom" cargo test -p <crate> --test <name> --release -- --test-threads=1`. Because the actor uses asupersync channels and `std::sync::Mutex`, which loom cannot instrument, the models are **mirror models**: they replicate the exact synchronization skeleton with loom primitives and include a deliberately injected ordering bug that must fail.

## Outcome
A loom model of the actor lifecycle and connect guard runs exhaustively in `loom.yml` (tier C, release-only), proving: no lost wakeup between caller cancel and actor completion; a session is never reused after cancel/quarantine; the join is bounded; connect-guard slots are always returned (success, failure, spawn failure, stuck-then-released); and an injected ordering bug makes the model fail.

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp-db/Cargo.toml`: `[target.'cfg(loom)'.dev-dependencies] loom = "0.7"` (same version as the other crates).
- `crates/oraclemcp-db/tests/loom_official_actor.rs`: header doc naming each mirrored function (`BlockingConnectionActor::request`, `ActorState` transitions, completion ack, `OfficialConnectGuard::acquire`/slot drop) and the source line anchors to re-derive with `rg -n`.
- `.github/workflows/loom.yml`: one more step for `-p oraclemcp-db --test loom_official_actor`.
- A doc comment in `oracledb_actor.rs` pointing to the model, so changes to the skeleton update the mirror.

## Implementation notes
Actors in the model: caller (lane thread) issuing a request and possibly cancelling; the actor thread executing and replying; the quarantine decision; the guard. Properties:
1. Caller cancel racing actor completion: exactly one of {reply delivered, actor quarantined}; never both lost.
2. After quarantine, any further request is refused (no reuse); the resource is dropped exactly once.
3. Join completes within the modelled grace (no unbounded wait on a live sender).
4. Guard: for every path (connect ok, connect err, spawn failure, stuck connect released later), available permits return to capacity.
5. `injected_reuse_after_cancel_bug` (quarantine check split from the state transition) must be detected: the test asserts the buggy model panics under loom (`#[should_panic]`).
Keep models small enough for exhaustive exploration (`LOOM_MAX_PREEMPTIONS=3` documented).

## Test plan
- `loom_actor_cancel_vs_completion_no_lost_wakeup`, `loom_actor_no_reuse_after_quarantine`, `loom_actor_join_bounded`, `loom_connect_guard_slots_always_returned`, `loom_injected_reuse_after_cancel_bug_is_detected` (`#[should_panic]`).
- Log: loom's own output to `$LOOM_RESULTS_DIR/db-official-actor.log` as the other steps do.

## Proof split
This bead model-checks the synchronization skeleton. T8.5 proves the containment bound on the real upstream connect; existing unit tests prove the concrete implementation paths.

## Non-goals
Rewriting the actor on loom-instrumentable primitives; Kani/capability lattice (retired); a new ADR.

## No-claim boundary
A mirror model proves the modelled skeleton, not that the production code still matches it; the doc-comment link and review keep them aligned.

## Considerations
- Tier C (release-only) per plan W5; R.1 runs it on the candidate SHA.
- File lane `official-backend` shared with T8.5.

## Absorbs
- `oraclemcp-2q4em.1.3`: only the loom model (actors: lane thread, driver island, Cx cancel edge, quarantine decision; properties: no lost wakeup, no reuse after cancel, bounded join) is kept; the ADR/design-spike output is already delivered by ADR-0014 and the `nhteq.4` citation is obsolete.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: `RUSTFLAGS="--cfg loom" cargo test -p oraclemcp-db --test loom_official_actor --release -- --test-threads=1` passes all non-injected models exhaustively.
- [ ] Negative: `loom_injected_reuse_after_cancel_bug_is_detected` panics under loom (the model detects the planted ordering bug).

title: Finish boundary and seam lints: no Tokio via Oracle backend, one adapter per backend
description:
## Context
Two lints guard the driver boundary:
- `scripts/oraclemcp_boundary_lint.sh`: forbidden-package gate over `cargo tree -e normal --workspace --target all -i <package>` (`tokio`, `tokio-stream`, `tokio-util`, `asupersync-tokio-compat`, plus reqwest/hyper/axum class and the OpenTelemetry `rt-tokio` feature check).
- `scripts/oraclemcp_driver_seam_lint.sh`: fails if an `oraclemcp_driver_cx::` path appears outside `ADAPTER_ALLOWLIST=("crates/oraclemcp-db/src/connection.rs")`; mirrored by the `driver_seam` test in `connection.rs`.

The official `oracledb` backend is now in every build (`oraclemcp-db` feature `oracledb` is default; `crates/oraclemcp/Cargo.toml` feature `oracledb`), but the seam lint does not know it: `oracledb::` paths appear in `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/oracledb_backend.rs` (the adapter) and `oracledb_actor.rs` (a doc comment only at 1fbe6eb0). Plan W8: "Finish the boundary/seam lints (no Tokio via the Oracle backend; UPL allow-list done)". `deny.toml` already allows `UPL-1.0` (done). Old bead `2q4em.1.7` asked for: boundary lint green with the Oracle backend feature on and part of the feature powerset; seam lint enforcing exactly one adapter file per backend; the arch-fitness path ratchet for the new adapter; negative fixtures in each lint's `--selftest`; lints print the offending path and the resolved feature set.

## Outcome
The boundary lint proves no Tokio (or other forbidden package) enters the graph with the official backend on and off; the seam lint enforces exactly one adapter file per backend (`connection.rs` for driver-cx, `oracledb_backend.rs` for official); each lint has a `--selftest` whose negative fixtures fail it; CI runs the selftests.

## Deliverable
- `scripts/oraclemcp_boundary_lint.sh`: run the forbidden-package gate twice, default features (official on) and `-p oraclemcp-db --no-default-features` (official off); print the resolved feature set on failure; `--selftest` using a temp crate that depends on `tokio` behind a feature named like the Oracle backend feature and must fail the gate.
- `scripts/oraclemcp_driver_seam_lint.sh`: a second pattern for the official crate path (`(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])oracledb[[:space:]]*::`, ignoring comment lines starting with `//`) with its own one-file allowlist `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/oracledb_backend.rs`; `--selftest` with a temp tree where a second file names each driver crate path and must fail.
- The `driver_seam` Rust test in `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/connection.rs` mirrors the second allowlist.
- `scripts/oraclemcp_arch_fitness_lint.sh`: path ratchet entry for `oracledb_backend.rs` / `oracledb_actor.rs`.
- `scripts/oraclemcp_feature_powerset.sh`: includes the `oracledb` on/off combination for `oraclemcp-db` (verify; add if missing).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `boundary` job runs both `--selftest`s.

## Implementation notes
1. The official crate identifier `oracledb` also appears in docs/comments; match only code paths (strip `//` comment lines before matching, as the lint's docstring promises for the driver-cx pattern).
2. `oracledb_actor.rs` must not reference `oracledb::` in code (it is backend-generic); if a code path does, move it into `oracledb_backend.rs`.
3. Output on violation: the offending path, line and the allowlisted adapter per backend.

## Test plan
- `oraclemcp_boundary_lint.sh --selftest`: cases `boundary_tokio_under_oracle_feature_fails`, `boundary_clean_graph_passes`.
- `oraclemcp_driver_seam_lint.sh --selftest`: cases `seam_second_file_driver_cx_path_fails`, `seam_second_file_official_path_fails`, `seam_comment_mention_passes`.
- `cargo test -p oraclemcp-db driver_seam`.
- Each selftest case prints `{case_id, expected, actual}`.

## Proof split
Static lints only. T8.13 owns the feature-level proof that `nightly-outcome-try` is absent.

## Non-goals
Changing `deny.toml` licences (UPL done); moving code between crates.

## No-claim boundary
A green lint does not prove runtime behaviour of either backend.

## Considerations
- Tier A (`boundary` job) per plan W5.
- File lane `lints`; `connection.rs` edit is limited to the `driver_seam` test (reserve the file).

## Absorbs
- `oraclemcp-2q4em.1.7`: kept except the UPL allow-list (already done): boundary lint with the Oracle backend on, seam lint one adapter per backend, arch-fitness ratchet, feature-powerset combo, negative selftest fixtures, offending path + feature set in output.

title: Stable Rust on Linux/macOS: drop nightly-outcome-try from driver-cx, add stable jobs
description:
## Context
Nothing in the oraclemcp or driver-cx source needs nightly on Linux/macOS. The nightly requirement arrives transitively: asupersync 0.3.9's `default = ["proc-macros", "nightly-outcome-try"]`, and `nightly-outcome-try` enables `feature(try_trait_v2)` + `try_trait_v2_residual` inside asupersync (`asupersync-0.3.9/src/lib.rs:52-53`). oraclemcp already asks for `asupersync = { version = "0.3.9", default-features = false, features = ["metrics"] }` (root `Cargo.toml`), but driver-cx declares `asupersync = "=0.3.9"` in `rust-oracledb/Cargo.toml` `[workspace.dependencies]` with default features, used by `crates/oracledb/Cargo.toml` (`features = ["tls"]`) and `crates/oracledb-pyshim` (workspace default), so Cargo feature unification turns the nightly feature back on for the whole graph. The driver bead `rust-oracledb-q20z` (closed) confirmed a direct stable build fails with E0554 for exactly this reason. Windows additionally needs nightly because `windows_by_handle` (`MetadataExt::number_of_links`, `volume_serial_number`) is enabled in **both** `crates/oraclemcp-core/src/lib.rs` and `crates/oraclemcp-audit/src/lib.rs`.

Ruling **R30**: stable Rust on non-Windows (`k6q.14`) is kept as a cheap feature. Plan W8 acceptance: `cargo tree -e features` proves `nightly-outcome-try` absent, and stable check/test/package jobs pass for the driver and oraclemcp. **If that cannot be met, it is a release blocker requiring operator disposition, never silently counted as done.**

## Outcome
On Linux and macOS, both the driver workspace and the oraclemcp workspace check, test and package on the current stable toolchain; `cargo tree -e features` shows no `nightly-outcome-try` anywhere in either graph; CI has a stable job (tier A) per repo on Linux and macOS; the pinned nightly stays the default toolchain and stays required on Windows; docs name both Windows reasons.

## Deliverable
- **Driver** (`rust-oracledb`, post-rename `main`, one atomic commit, rule 17): root `Cargo.toml` `asupersync = { version = "=0.3.9", default-features = false }`; `crates/oracledb/Cargo.toml` asupersync features `["tls"]` plus `"proc-macros"` only if the driver uses asupersync proc-macros (check `asupersync::join!` in `crates/oracledb/src/pool.rs` and every `#[asupersync::...]` attribute); `crates/oracledb-pyshim` likewise opts out (it is `publish = false` but is a workspace member, so its defaults would re-unify inside the driver workspace). Stable CI job in the driver's `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (Linux + macOS): `cargo +stable check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo +stable test --workspace --exclude oracledb-pyshim` (the pyshim is excluded from tests only because it needs Python; it must still `check`), `cargo +stable package -p oraclemcp-driver-cx-protocol -p oraclemcp-driver-cx --no-verify` followed by a verify build on stable. Driver `AGENTS.md`/`rust-toolchain.toml` comments and `docs/TOOLCHAIN.md` updated; README nightly badge wording corrected.
- **oraclemcp**: stable job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (Linux + macOS; tier A per plan W5 "stable-toolchain check (Linux/macOS, T8.13)"): `cargo +stable check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo +stable test --workspace` (via `scripts/build_lease.sh` locally; CI is single-tenant), `cargo +stable package --workspace --no-verify` (package verification is deferred to R.5 because `cargo package` ignores `[patch]`). `docs/toolchain.md`, `rust-toolchain.toml` comment and the root `Cargo.toml` comment block state: Linux/macOS build on stable; Windows needs nightly for `windows_by_handle` in `oraclemcp-core` and `oraclemcp-audit`; the pinned nightly remains the default. AGENTS.md "Rust toolchain" reason 1 updated to match.
- A script `scripts/check_no_nightly_features.sh` (or a step inside the existing boundary lint, prefer the boundary lint) that runs `cargo tree -e features --workspace --target all -i asupersync` and fails if `nightly-outcome-try` appears; the same check in the driver repo.

## Implementation notes
1. Driver first: make the dependency change, then `cargo +stable check --workspace --all-targets`; fix any stable-only compile error in driver code (e.g. use of `?` on `Outcome`, which needs `try_trait_v2`: replace with explicit matches). No `unsafe`.
2. Push the driver revision (T0.2a's branch discipline). The oraclemcp half is proven before T0.7 with a non-committed override: `cargo +stable --config 'patch.crates-io.oraclemcp-driver-cx.git="https://github.com/MuhDur/rust-oracledb"' --config 'patch.crates-io.oraclemcp-driver-cx.rev="<sha>"'` (and the same for `-protocol`), recording the command and SHA in the close evidence; T0.7 then refreshes the committed pin and the stable job runs in CI on it.
3. `cargo tree` check must use `--target all` so Windows-only edges are included.
4. Edition 2024 and every language feature used must be stable at the chosen stable version; record `rustc +stable -V` in evidence.
5. Windows keeps nightly: the Windows jobs (`windows-rust`, `windows-installer`, release Windows targets) stay on the pinned nightly.

## Test plan
- Driver: stable CI job green on Linux and macOS; `cargo tree -e features --workspace --target all -i asupersync | grep -c nightly-outcome-try` = 0.
- oraclemcp: stable CI job green on Linux and macOS (after T0.7); the override-based local proof before T0.7; the no-nightly-features check green in the tier-A `boundary` job.
- Negative: re-adding default features to the driver's asupersync dependency (scratch branch) makes the no-nightly-features check fail and the stable job fail with E0554.
- Evidence log per job: `{repo, toolchain, os, step, result}`.

## Proof split
This bead proves stable builds and the absence of the nightly feature. R.5 reruns package verification against crates.io-resolved versions; T5.x places the stable job in tier A.

## Non-goals
Stable Windows (needs `windows_by_handle` stabilization or a vetted safe replacement); moving release builds off the pinned nightly; bumping asupersync.

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove Windows builds on stable, nor that release artifacts are built with stable.

## Considerations
- **Release blocker rule**: if any acceptance line cannot be met, stop and escalate to the operator for disposition; never close as done and never mark the stable job advisory.
- Dependency note: the oraclemcp stable job in CI needs the driver revision consumed through T0.7, and T0.7 depends on this bead, so the pre-T0.7 proof uses the non-committed `--config` patch override. **structure-owner check**: confirm T0.7's acceptance includes "oraclemcp stable job green on the refreshed pin".
- Rule 17: the dependency-feature change and any code change it forces land in one commit per repo.
- File lane `toolchain` (rust-toolchain.toml, docs/toolchain.md, Cargo.toml comment block; AGENTS.md toolchain paragraph coordinated with T6.2).

## Absorbs
- `oraclemcp-040-epic-deferred-k6q.14`: kept per R30 (stable Rust on non-Windows via driver-cx asupersync `default-features = false`); its original "wait for asupersync to stabilise" resume trigger is replaced by the opt-out.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: `cargo tree -e features --workspace --target all -i asupersync` in both repos contains no `nightly-outcome-try`.
- [ ] Positive: stable `check`, `test` and `package` jobs are green on Linux and macOS in the driver repo and in oraclemcp (oraclemcp on the pin refreshed by T0.7; before that, via the recorded `--config` patch override).
- [ ] Negative: a scratch change restoring asupersync default features in the driver makes the no-nightly-features check fail and the stable job fail with E0554.
- [ ] Tests: driver CI job `stable (linux, macos)`; oraclemcp CI job `stable-toolchain (linux, macos)`; the no-nightly-features check in the `boundary` job; all green in tier A.
- [ ] Proof class: offline build/test on the real stable toolchain; forbidden substitutes: marking the stable job `continue-on-error`, excluding crates from `check` to get green.
- [ ] Consumers: T0.7, T0.5, R.1, R.5.
- [ ] No-claim: does not prove Windows builds on stable or that release artifacts use stable.
- [ ] Release-blocker rule honoured: any unmet line is escalated to the operator, not closed.

title: Clean the mcp-publisher installer's own temp dir with an EXIT trap
description:
## Context
`scripts/install_mcp_publisher.sh` function `install_mcp_publisher` creates `work_dir="$(mktemp -d "${RUNNER_TEMP:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}/mcp-publisher.XXXXXX")"` (around line 113 at 1fbe6eb0), downloads the release archive into it, verifies SHA-256 (`verify_sha256`), extracts the executable and `install`s it to the destination. No EXIT cleanup removes `work_dir` after success or failure, so reused self-hosted runners and manual invocations accumulate archives and extracted binaries. The script is called by `.github/workflows/release.yml` and `.github/workflows/publish-mcp.yml` (`bash scripts/install_mcp_publisher.sh`) and is sourced by `scripts/workflow_supply_chain_check.sh`, which asserts line ordering (`verify_sha256 "$archive"` before `tar -xzf "$archive"`).

Ruling **R22**: the operator approved the trap deleting the installer's own temp dir (this is the RULE 1 permission for exactly this deletion and nothing else).

## Outcome
After any invocation (success, SHA mismatch, download failure, extraction failure) the `mcp-publisher.XXXXXX` work directory created by that invocation no longer exists; nothing else is deleted.

## Deliverable
- `scripts/install_mcp_publisher.sh`: after `mktemp -d` succeeds, install a quoted cleanup trap scoped to that exact directory, e.g. `trap 'rm -rf -- "$work_dir"' EXIT` inside the function (the script is also `source`d, so the trap must not clobber a caller's EXIT trap: run the body in a subshell function `install_mcp_publisher() ( ... )` so the trap is local to that subshell).
- A regression test script or a test in the existing check: extend `scripts/workflow_supply_chain_check.sh` (it already sources the installer) or add cases to `crates/oraclemcp/tests/installer_e2e.rs`; choose `scripts/workflow_supply_chain_check.sh` because it already owns this installer's contract.

## Implementation notes
1. Guard: set the trap only after `work_dir` is non-empty and a directory (`[[ -n "$work_dir" && -d "$work_dir" ]]`), never with an unset variable (`set -u` is on).
2. Keep `verify_sha256` before `tar -xzf` (the supply-chain check asserts the line order; keep those line patterns intact).
3. Subshell-function form keeps `source` callers' traps and shell state untouched; `install` still writes the destination outside the work dir.
4. Test harness: stub `curl` via PATH (a script that copies a local fixture archive or exits 22) and set `TMPDIR` to a private temp root; assert the root has no `mcp-publisher.*` entry after (a) success with a matching SHA fixture, (b) SHA mismatch, (c) curl failure.

## Test plan
- `scripts/workflow_supply_chain_check.sh` cases `mcp_publisher_workdir_removed_on_success`, `mcp_publisher_workdir_removed_on_sha_mismatch`, `mcp_publisher_workdir_removed_on_download_failure`; each prints `{case_id, expected:"absent", actual}`.
- `shellcheck scripts/install_mcp_publisher.sh` clean.
- The existing ordering assertions in the check stay green.

## Proof split
This bead proves cleanup on all three exit paths offline. The real release run (R.7) exercises the installer on GitHub runners; no separate proof is needed.

## Non-goals
Changing the pinned publisher version, checksum source or download URL; cleaning any other temp directory.

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove the MCP registry publish step succeeds.

## Considerations
- RULE 1: the only deletion is the directory this invocation created (R22). The trap must never expand to an empty or caller-supplied path.
- File lane `release-scripts` (also touched by T6.1 for `release.yml`; this bead edits only the installer and the check script).

## Absorbs
- `oraclemcp-xoflp.5.8`: full scope kept (quoted EXIT trap after `mktemp` succeeds; cleanup proven on success and failed SHA verification).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: a successful stubbed install leaves the destination executable installed and no `mcp-publisher.*` directory under the test `TMPDIR`.
- [ ] Negative: with a mismatching SHA fixture the script exits non-zero, the destination is not written, and the work directory is gone (the pre-fix script leaves it behind).
- [ ] Negative: sourcing the script in a shell that has its own EXIT trap leaves that caller trap intact after calling `install_mcp_publisher`.
- [ ] Tests: `mcp_publisher_workdir_removed_on_success`, `mcp_publisher_workdir_removed_on_sha_mismatch`, `mcp_publisher_workdir_removed_on_download_failure` in `scripts/workflow_supply_chain_check.sh`; `shellcheck` clean; green in the tier-A supply-chain job.
- [ ] Proof class: offline; forbidden substitutes: a real network download in the test.
- [ ] Consumers: R.7 (release pipeline uses the installer).
- [ ] No-claim: does not prove registry publication works.

title: Make the public-API semver baseline reproducible independent of registry yanks
description:
## Context
The `api-lock` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `bash scripts/oraclemcp_api_lock.sh` (exact `cargo public-api` snapshots) and then `cargo semver-checks check-release -p oraclemcp-error -p oraclemcp-guard -p oraclemcp-db`, whose baseline defaults to the **latest crates.io release**. During 0.11.0 that baseline was 0.10.0, whose `oraclemcp-db` pinned `oracledb = "=0.9.1"`, since yanked upstream, so cargo-semver-checks could not construct the baseline and the lane went permanently red. The job was demoted to advisory (`continue-on-error: true`, runs only on `pull_request`). Measured 2026-09-23: on PR run 35556613151 (2026-09-21) the job was green, because the registry baseline is now 0.11.0; the failure class is latent and returns whenever a baseline's exact dependency is yanked (0.11.0 itself pins `oracledb = "=26.0.0-beta.3"`, a beta).

Plan W5: api-lock returns as a **required tier-A lane**; T5.3 does the promotion and depends on this bead. R.5 regenerates the api-lock baseline after the sibling crates are published. Operator decision recorded on the old bead: do not weaken API snapshots, alter guard behaviour or hide the failure; restore a reproducible historical baseline.

## Outcome
The semver check builds its baseline from the previous release **tag in this repository with that tag's committed `Cargo.lock`**, so a later yank on crates.io cannot break it; a planted breaking change still fails the check.

## Deliverable
- `scripts/oraclemcp_api_lock.sh`: gains the semver step (so CI and the local gate run one command): `cargo semver-checks check-release --baseline-rev "$BASELINE_TAG" -p oraclemcp-error -p oraclemcp-guard -p oraclemcp-db`, where `BASELINE_TAG` is the most recent `v*` release tag that is an ancestor of HEAD and differs from HEAD's own version (derived with `git describe --tags --abbrev=0 --match 'v[0-9]*'`, skipping a tag equal to the workspace version), overridable by `ORACLEMCP_SEMVER_BASELINE_TAG`.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `api-lock` job: `actions/checkout` with `fetch-depth: 0` (tags needed); the separate `cargo semver-checks` line is replaced by the script. Promotion to required (removing `continue-on-error`, `if: pull_request`) is **T5.3**, not this bead.
- `docs/toolchain.md` or the script header documents the baseline rule in two lines.

## Implementation notes
1. `--baseline-rev` checks the tag out into a temporary worktree and builds rustdoc JSON there; the tag's `Cargo.lock` lets Cargo resolve even yanked versions it already locks. Verify this empirically: run it once with `--offline` after a fetch to prove no registry resolution is needed beyond the lockfile.
2. Crates added after the baseline tag (e.g. `oraclemcp-verifier`, W11) are skipped by semver-checks when absent in the baseline; keep the explicit `-p` list.
3. The exact public-API snapshots (`cargo public-api` baselines) stay as they are; R.5 refreshes them after pins become exact versions.
4. Runs under the pinned nightly (cargo-semver-checks works under the pin; verified in the driver repo).

## Test plan
- `scripts/oraclemcp_api_lock.sh --selftest` (new flag, CI-run): (a) HEAD vs derived baseline passes; (b) a planted breaking change in a scratch worktree (remove one `pub fn` from `oraclemcp-error`) makes the script exit non-zero; (c) `ORACLEMCP_SEMVER_BASELINE_TAG=v0.10.0` (the yanked-dependency baseline) builds successfully from its lockfile, which is the reproduction of the original failure now passing.
- Each case logs `{case_id, baseline_tag, expected, actual}`.

## Proof split
This bead proves the baseline is reproducible and still detects breaks. T5.3 proves the lane runs required and green on main. R.5 refreshes the snapshots and reruns it against crates.io-resolved dependencies.

## Non-goals
Promoting the lane (T5.3); refreshing public-API snapshots (R.5); adding semver-checks to crates not already listed.

## No-claim boundary
A green check does not prove the 0.12.0 API is free of intended breaking changes; it proves unintended ones are detected against the previous release.

## Considerations
- If `--baseline-rev v0.10.0` still fails because cargo-semver-checks resolves outside the lockfile, the fallback is `--baseline-root` on a `git worktree` of the tag built with `--locked`; the acceptance stays the same. **structure-owner check**: the plan says "against the yanked 0.10 `oracledb`" while the registry baseline is now 0.11.0; this bead implements the tag-baseline rule that covers both.
- File lane `ci-workflows` (ci.yml is also edited by T5.x and T10.3); reserve before editing.

## Absorbs
- `oraclemcp-ft0ti.1`: full scope kept (reproducible historical baseline; no snapshot weakening; no hidden failure).

title: Prove the installer E2E suite passes on the final installer and docs
description:
## Context
`crates/oraclemcp/tests/installer_e2e.rs` is the installer contract suite: `installer_lint_and_offline_smoke_passes` (runs `scripts/installer_lint_and_offline_smoke.sh`), `install_manual_preserves_detailed_contract_and_readme_stays_install_first`, `windows_installer_verifies_before_mutating_and_requires_service_consent`, `unix_installer_reinstall_is_idempotent_for_identical_files`, `installer_ci_runs_built_artifact_and_windows_pssa_gates`, the SBOM tests, `npm_release_channel_is_retired`, `cargo_binstall_metadata_matches_release_assets`, `binstall_brew_winget_metadata_valid`, `installers_offer_consent_gated_tns_discovery_via_the_binary` (names at 1fbe6eb0; re-derive with `rg -n "^fn " crates/oraclemcp/tests/installer_e2e.rs`). The old bead `ft0ti.2` recorded README-string assertions failing after the README decoupling in `0d421462`; the test names have since changed, but no evidence shows the whole suite green. Plan W8: "Prove the installer E2E passes (currently claimed only)". R19: nothing is fixed until a test proves it.

T6.1 (retire Homebrew/winget/npm, R17/R32) edits this same file (lines around 178, 680, 728-729, 794-816 at 1fbe6eb0) and deletes `.github/workflows/publish-npm.yml`, which `npm_release_channel_is_retired` reads today. A proof taken before T6.1 would be invalidated by it.

## Outcome
`cargo test -p oraclemcp --test installer_e2e` and `scripts/installer_lint_and_offline_smoke.sh --log` pass on HEAD after T6.1, locally and in the tier-A `installer` job, with every test asserting a current, true contract (no assertion on a retired channel's presence, no weakened coverage).

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp/tests/installer_e2e.rs`: repair any failing or stale assertion so it checks the retained behaviour/docs source (README install-first, `docs/install.md` detailed contract, retired channels absent); every test keeps asserting something load-bearing.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `installer` job runs `cargo test -p oraclemcp --test installer_e2e` in addition to the offline smoke (if the `test` job's workspace run already covers it, record the job/step name instead of adding a duplicate step).

## Implementation notes
1. Run the suite first and record the exact failures (`--no-fail-fast`), then fix each failure at its cause.
2. `npm_release_channel_is_retired` must survive the deletion of `publish-npm.yml`: assert the file is absent and that no workflow contains `npm publish` / `NPM_TOKEN`, instead of reading the deleted file.
3. `binstall_brew_winget_metadata_valid` becomes binstall-only after T6.1 (brew/winget retired); keep the binstall checks intact.
4. Scoped build: `cargo test -p oraclemcp --test installer_e2e` (no workspace build).

## Test plan

title: Prove the official-driver connect bound against a black-holed TCP endpoint and document it
description:
## Context
The official `oracledb =26.0.0-beta.3` connect is synchronous and cannot be cancelled: `OfficialCommand::Connect` in `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/oracledb_backend.rs` calls `oracledb::connect(config)` on the actor thread; the initial/redirected `TcpStream::connect` plus TLS handshake inside the upstream crate runs before any `Connection`/call timeout exists, and `validate_supported_connect_options` rejects `OracleConnectOptions.connect_timeout`. A stalled TCP/handshake can outlive the `Cx`/request deadline and keep its actor OS thread blocked.

Accepted mitigation (operator decision 2026-09-16, ADR-0014 `docs/adr/0014-blocking-driver-backend-execution-model.md`): the global `OfficialConnectGuard` (`crates/oraclemcp-db/src/oracledb_actor.rs`, capacity `OFFICIAL_CONNECT_GUARD_CAPACITY = 2`, acquire timeout `OFFICIAL_CONNECT_GUARD_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT = 250 ms`) caps the number of stalled official connect actors; an exhausted guard falls back to driver-cx exactly once; the lane never hangs. Existing proofs are unit tests with in-process stub factories: `bounded_connect_guard_caps_stalled_actors_and_recovers_every_slot`, `successful_official_setup_releases_its_connect_guard_slot`, `actor_spawn_failure_returns_the_reserved_connect_guard_slot`, `exhausted_official_connect_guard_falls_back_to_driver_cx_once`, `failed_official_connect_discards_actor_and_refuses_reuse`, `expired_absolute_deadline_quarantines_before_the_blocking_operation`. None drives the **real** upstream connect against a stalled network endpoint.

Plan W8 (R12, R15, R19): keep the bounded guard; **prove** its bound with a test using a black-holed TCP endpoint; document it as a mitigated upstream limit. We do not ship patches to Oracle's crate.

## Outcome
A test drives the real official adapter connect against a local endpoint that accepts TCP and never answers, and proves: the caller returns within its deadline plus bounded slack; no more than two official connect actors are ever stalled; a third concurrent acquisition gets the driver-cx fallback once after at most 250 ms; no stalled actor's session is ever reused; every slot is recovered once the endpoint closes the sockets. The limit is documented for operators.

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/oracledb_backend.rs` `#[cfg(test)]` (or `crates/oraclemcp-db/tests/official_connect_blackhole.rs`, feature `oracledb`): the black-hole tests below, using a `std::net::TcpListener` on `127.0.0.1:0` whose accept loop holds accepted sockets open without writing (a TNS CONNECT then never receives ACCEPT/REFUSE).
- `docs/adr/0014-blocking-driver-backend-execution-model.md`: a "Residual upstream limit (mitigated)" section naming the bound (2 stuck threads max, 250 ms acquire, one driver-cx fallback, reclaimed by OS TCP timeout or peer close) and the test names.
- Operator-facing line in `docs/` troubleshooting (the page that documents the official fallback; find with `rg -n "official" docs/*.md`).
- If the test exposes a defect in the guard, fix it in `oracledb_actor.rs`/`oracledb_backend.rs` in the same bead.

## Implementation notes
1. Black-hole endpoint: accept connections and park them (keep the `TcpStream`s in a `Vec` owned by the fixture); dropping the fixture closes them, which simulates the OS TCP timeout reclaiming the stuck actors.
2. Drive the official adapter directly (`OfficialOracleConnection::connect`) and through the acquisition router for the fallback case, with a password profile without a wallet (the only route that may try official).
3. Use a test-local `OfficialConnectGuard::for_test(2, Duration::from_millis(250))` where the API allows; one test must use the shared production constants to prove the shipped values.
4. Measure with `Instant`; allow slack of 1 s over the configured deadline for scheduler noise; the failure condition is "did not return" (watchdog at 10 s).
5. After closing the endpoint, poll (bounded, 10 s) until both slots are reacquirable.

## Test plan
- `official_connect_blackhole_returns_within_deadline`: one connect with a 2 s request deadline returns a typed timeout/unavailable error within 3 s.
- `official_connect_blackhole_caps_stuck_actors_at_two`: four concurrent connects; at most two official actor threads are alive (count via the guard's available permits), the other two fall back.
- `official_connect_blackhole_third_acquire_falls_back_to_driver_cx_once`: with both slots stuck, the next acquisition waits at most 250 ms (plus slack) and then attempts driver-cx exactly once (count via the test factory hook).
- `official_connect_blackhole_slots_recover_after_peer_close`.
- `official_connect_blackhole_never_reuses_stuck_session`: a late-completing stuck connect is discarded, never handed to a lane.
- JSONL per case: `{case_id, deadline_ms, elapsed_ms, stuck_actors, fallback_attempts, expected, actual}`.
- Runs in tier A (`cargo test -p oraclemcp-db --features oracledb`); no database needed.

## Proof split
This bead proves the containment bound on the real upstream connect path. T8.10 model-checks the actor state machine with loom. The upstream inability to cancel an individual connect stays a documented limit (not fixed).

## Non-goals
Patching or forking `oracledb`; making the official backend primary (R12); changing guard constants without evidence.

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove an individual stalled official connect can be cancelled; it proves the number of stuck threads is bounded and callers never hang.

## Considerations
- Ports: bind `127.0.0.1:0` only; no external network.
- File lane `official-backend` (shared with T8.10); `connection.rs` is not touched.

## Absorbs
- `oraclemcp-xoflp.1.6`: kept (deterministic stalled-connect regression proving prompt caller completion, actor retirement, no reusable session); the "fully closes when upstream adds cancellable connect" clause becomes the documented residual limit.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: against a black-holed local endpoint, an official connect with a 2 s deadline returns a typed error within 3 s, and slots recover after the endpoint closes its sockets.
- [ ] Negative: with four concurrent black-holed connects, never more than two official actor threads are stuck and the third acquisition falls back to driver-cx exactly once after at most 250 ms plus slack (a guard without the cap or with an unbounded acquire wait fails).
- [ ] Negative: a stuck connect that completes late is discarded and never reused.
- [ ] Tests: `official_connect_blackhole_returns_within_deadline`, `official_connect_blackhole_caps_stuck_actors_at_two`, `official_connect_blackhole_third_acquire_falls_back_to_driver_cx_once`, `official_connect_blackhole_slots_recover_after_peer_close`, `official_connect_blackhole_never_reuses_stuck_session`; green in tier A `cargo test -p oraclemcp-db --features oracledb`.
- [ ] Proof class: unit with the real upstream connect over loopback TCP; forbidden substitutes: a stub connect factory standing in for the upstream `oracledb::connect`.
- [ ] Consumers: T8.10, R.1.
- [ ] No-claim: does not prove an individual stalled upstream connect can be cancelled.

title: Parity: DATE/TIMESTAMP/INTERVAL and LOB/NULL across driver-cx and official backends
description:
## Context
Cross-backend parity compares the primary driver-cx backend (`RustOracleConnection`) with the official `oracledb` backend (`OfficialOracleConnection`) through the shared `OracleConnection` seam. Today the suite is `crates/oraclemcp-db/tests/cross_backend_parity.rs` (`#![cfg(all(feature = "oracledb", feature = "live-xe"))]`), two `#[ignore]` lab tests (`live_cross_backend_parity_for_supported_basic_auth`, `live_cross_backend_tcps_pem_connection_parity`) gated on `ORACLEMCP_DUAL_BACKEND_LAB=1` + `ORACLEMCP_TEST_DSN/USER/PASSWORD`; it covers TSTZ, one positive 38-digit NUMBER, dense/sparse FLOAT32 VECTOR, a missing-object error envelope and a transaction scenario, and never runs in CI.

Plan W8 (R12, R15, R19): parity for DATE/TIMESTAMP/INTERVAL, LOB/NULL, NUMBER boundaries, streaming, ORA error taxonomy, VECTOR variants and TCPS/PEM, made reproducible in the FREE 23ai lane. **Where the official backend lacks a type, a typed refusal is the tested behaviour**: the official adapter must return the same explicit `UnsupportedFeature` envelope (error class + stable reason) every time, never a silently different value. driver-cx stays primary (R12); these tests do not change routing. The metamorphic cross-backend suite (`2q4em.1.6`) was retired under R34 because these parity tests cover it.

Fixture rule: parity tables are created per run with the run-id stamping from T4.3 (the existing `ORACLEMCP_PARITY_*_{suffix}` naming becomes the T4.3 run-id stamp) and dropped at the end; the T4.3 janitor removes stale owned runs.

Gaps this bead closes (old beads `xoflp.4.2`, `xoflp.4.3`): only TSTZ is compared today. DATE and plain TIMESTAMP wire values must match with **no invented UTC suffix**; INTERVAL YEAR TO MONTH and INTERVAL DAY TO SECOND must match or be a typed refusal. No CLOB, BLOB or NULL cell is compared; each must match as a safe value or return an identical explicit `UnsupportedFeature` envelope with a documented reason, including typed NULL results. The timezone adapter defects (`xoflp.1.8`, `1.9`) are already fixed and closed; this is the independent live proof.

## Outcome
The parity suite compares, row by row and as serialized JSON, DATE, TIMESTAMP (incl. fractional seconds 0-9), TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE, INTERVAL YM/DS, CLOB (empty, ASCII, multibyte, above the inline threshold), BLOB (empty, small, above threshold), and typed NULLs of every covered type, and every cell either matches exactly or is an identical typed refusal from the official backend.

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp-db/tests/cross_backend_parity.rs`: new scenario functions `run_datetime_interval_scenario`, `run_lob_null_scenario`, called from the lab test entry (T8.9 makes the entry CI-reproducible).
- Adapter fixes in `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/oracledb_backend.rs` (value mapping) for any mismatch the cases expose, or an explicit typed `UnsupportedFeature` refusal with a stable reason string for a type the official beta cannot represent.

## Implementation notes
1. Fixture table per run: `ORACLEMCP_PARITY_DT_<run>` with one column per type and rows: min/max representable DATE, a leap-day timestamp, `TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00.123456789'`, negative and positive intervals, and a row of NULLs.
2. Set session `NLS_*` explicitly on both connections so format differences come only from the backends; assert the serialized strings, not driver-native structs.
3. Assert DATE/TIMESTAMP strings carry no `Z`/`+00:00` suffix; TSTZ keeps its offset; TSLTZ is rendered in the session time zone on both.
4. LOBs: read through the same `read_clob`-style path both backends expose; compare length and SHA-256 of content plus the serialized preview.
5. For a type the official backend refuses: assert `ErrorClass`, the reason string and that the same query on driver-cx returns a value (the refusal is the tested behaviour, the value is the driver-cx proof).

## Test plan
- Cases (each a named sub-case with JSONL `{case_id, column_type, backend, expected, actual}`): `parity_date_min_max`, `parity_timestamp_fractional_0_to_9`, `parity_timestamp_no_utc_suffix`, `parity_tsltz_session_zone`, `parity_interval_ym_signed`, `parity_interval_ds_signed`, `parity_clob_empty_ascii_multibyte_large`, `parity_blob_empty_small_large`, `parity_typed_null_every_type`.
- Run against FREE 23ai (the container from T4.1) with the run-id stamped fixture.

## Proof split
This bead proves value/refusal parity for these types. T8.9 makes the whole suite run reproducibly in the FREE 23ai lane; T8.7 and T8.8 cover the other type families.

## Non-goals
Changing routing (official stays a bounded alternate); XE 18/21 parity (the official beta targets 23ai in the tier-A lane; tier C may add it later only by a separate ruling).

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove parity for NUMBER, streaming, errors, VECTOR or TCPS (T8.7-T8.9), nor any guard behaviour.

## Considerations
- Hot file: every parity bead edits `crates/oraclemcp-db/tests/cross_backend_parity.rs`; file lane `parity` serialises T8.6, T8.7, T8.8, T8.9 (one owner at a time).
- A value mismatch found here is a driver or adapter bug: fix it in this bead if it is in oraclemcp's adapter (`oracledb_backend.rs` or `connection.rs` serialization); if it is in driver-cx, file a `discovered-from` bug in the driver repo that blocks this bead and is consumed through a T0.7 pin refresh.
- Serialization contract to preserve: NUMBER defaults to an exact JSON string, never a rounded JSON number (hard invariant).

## Absorbs
- `oraclemcp-xoflp.4.2`: kept in full (DATE, TIMESTAMP without invented UTC suffix, INTERVAL YM/DS, or explicit typed refusal).
- `oraclemcp-xoflp.4.3`: kept in full (CLOB, BLOB, NULL cells; matching safe values or identical explicit `UnsupportedFeature` envelope with documented reason, typed NULLs).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: every DATE/TIMESTAMP/TSLTZ/INTERVAL/CLOB/BLOB/NULL cell in the fixture serializes identically on driver-cx and the official backend, or the official backend returns the documented typed refusal while driver-cx returns the value.
- [ ] Negative: a planted UTC suffix on plain TIMESTAMP (or a NULL rendered as empty string) in either adapter's serialization fails `parity_timestamp_no_utc_suffix` / `parity_typed_null_every_type`.
- [ ] Tests: `parity_date_min_max`, `parity_timestamp_fractional_0_to_9`, `parity_timestamp_no_utc_suffix`, `parity_tsltz_session_zone`, `parity_interval_ym_signed`, `parity_interval_ds_signed`, `parity_clob_empty_ascii_multibyte_large`, `parity_blob_empty_small_large`, `parity_typed_null_every_type`; green on FREE 23ai.
- [ ] Proof class: live in-process (real FREE 23ai, both real drivers); forbidden substitutes: mock DB, recorded fixture values in place of a live query.
- [ ] Consumers: T8.9.
- [ ] No-claim: does not prove parity for other type families or any guard decision.

title: Parity: NUMBER boundaries and empty/multi-row streaming across backends
description:
## Context
Cross-backend parity compares the primary driver-cx backend (`RustOracleConnection`) with the official `oracledb` backend (`OfficialOracleConnection`) through the shared `OracleConnection` seam. Today the suite is `crates/oraclemcp-db/tests/cross_backend_parity.rs` (`#![cfg(all(feature = "oracledb", feature = "live-xe"))]`), two `#[ignore]` lab tests (`live_cross_backend_parity_for_supported_basic_auth`, `live_cross_backend_tcps_pem_connection_parity`) gated on `ORACLEMCP_DUAL_BACKEND_LAB=1` + `ORACLEMCP_TEST_DSN/USER/PASSWORD`; it covers TSTZ, one positive 38-digit NUMBER, dense/sparse FLOAT32 VECTOR, a missing-object error envelope and a transaction scenario, and never runs in CI.

Plan W8 (R12, R15, R19): parity for DATE/TIMESTAMP/INTERVAL, LOB/NULL, NUMBER boundaries, streaming, ORA error taxonomy, VECTOR variants and TCPS/PEM, made reproducible in the FREE 23ai lane. **Where the official backend lacks a type, a typed refusal is the tested behaviour**: the official adapter must return the same explicit `UnsupportedFeature` envelope (error class + stable reason) every time, never a silently different value. driver-cx stays primary (R12); these tests do not change routing. The metamorphic cross-backend suite (`2q4em.1.6`) was retired under R34 because these parity tests cover it.

Fixture rule: parity tables are created per run with the run-id stamping from T4.3 (the existing `ORACLEMCP_PARITY_*_{suffix}` naming becomes the T4.3 run-id stamp) and dropped at the end; the T4.3 janitor removes stale owned runs.

Gaps this bead closes (old beads `xoflp.4.4`, `xoflp.4.5`):
- NUMBER: the live proof has one positive 38-digit integer only. Needed: negative 38-digit boundary, fractional/scale values, zero (incl. `-0`), precision/rounding boundaries, and the assertion that default NUMBER stays an **exact JSON string**, never a rounded JSON number.
- Streaming: parity materializes one row and never calls `query_row_stream`. Needed: live empty-result and ordered multi-row streaming, and early drop/cancellation followed by a query proving no stale session reuse (actor quarantine semantics from the closed `xoflp.1.5`).

## Outcome
NUMBER values at every boundary serialize to identical exact strings on both backends; streaming yields identical ordered rows, identical empty results, and after an early drop or cancel the next query on the same logical connection returns fresh, correct results (or the connection is quarantined and replaced) on both backends.

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp-db/tests/cross_backend_parity.rs`: `run_number_boundary_scenario`, `run_streaming_scenario`.
- Adapter fixes in `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/oracledb_backend.rs` / stream path for any mismatch exposed.

## Implementation notes
1. NUMBER literals (selected from DUAL and stored in a `NUMBER`, `NUMBER(38,0)`, `NUMBER(10,4)`, `BINARY_DOUBLE` column set): `99999999999999999999999999999999999999`, `-99999999999999999999999999999999999999`, `0`, `-0`, `0.0001`, `123.4567`, `1E-130`, `9.999999999999999999999999999999999999E125`, and a value that rounds at scale 4 (`1.23455` into `NUMBER(10,4)`).
2. Assert the JSON value type is string for NUMBER and that the text equals Oracle's canonical `TO_CHAR` for the same value.

title: Parity: ORA error taxonomy and VECTOR variants across backends
description:
## Context
Cross-backend parity compares the primary driver-cx backend (`RustOracleConnection`) with the official `oracledb` backend (`OfficialOracleConnection`) through the shared `OracleConnection` seam. Today the suite is `crates/oraclemcp-db/tests/cross_backend_parity.rs` (`#![cfg(all(feature = "oracledb", feature = "live-xe"))]`), two `#[ignore]` lab tests (`live_cross_backend_parity_for_supported_basic_auth`, `live_cross_backend_tcps_pem_connection_parity`) gated on `ORACLEMCP_DUAL_BACKEND_LAB=1` + `ORACLEMCP_TEST_DSN/USER/PASSWORD`; it covers TSTZ, one positive 38-digit NUMBER, dense/sparse FLOAT32 VECTOR, a missing-object error envelope and a transaction scenario, and never runs in CI.

Plan W8 (R12, R15, R19): parity for DATE/TIMESTAMP/INTERVAL, LOB/NULL, NUMBER boundaries, streaming, ORA error taxonomy, VECTOR variants and TCPS/PEM, made reproducible in the FREE 23ai lane. **Where the official backend lacks a type, a typed refusal is the tested behaviour**: the official adapter must return the same explicit `UnsupportedFeature` envelope (error class + stable reason) every time, never a silently different value. driver-cx stays primary (R12); these tests do not change routing. The metamorphic cross-backend suite (`2q4em.1.6`) was retired under R34 because these parity tests cover it.

Fixture rule: parity tables are created per run with the run-id stamping from T4.3 (the existing `ORACLEMCP_PARITY_*_{suffix}` naming becomes the T4.3 run-id stamp) and dropped at the end; the T4.3 janitor removes stale owned runs.

Gaps this bead closes (old beads `xoflp.4.6`, `xoflp.4.7`):
- Errors: only a missing-object envelope is compared. Needed: syntax/parse, constraint/duplicate value, privilege, and cancellation/timeout, comparing `ErrorClass`, ORA code, retry metadata (`retry_after_ms`) and operation context across both backends.
- VECTOR: only dense and sparse FLOAT32 are covered. Needed: FLOAT64, INT8, BINARY (FREE 23ai supports them), NULL vectors, and non-finite component serialization; projection must preserve the stable structured vector shape.

## Outcome
Each error kind yields the same `ErrorEnvelope` class, ORA code, retry metadata and operation context on both backends; every VECTOR variant serializes to the same structured shape on both backends or is an identical typed refusal on the official backend.

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp-db/tests/cross_backend_parity.rs`: `run_error_taxonomy_scenario`, `run_vector_variants_scenario`.
- Adapter fixes in `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/oracledb_backend.rs` error mapping / vector projection for mismatches.
- Fixture: a second, low-privilege user created by the T4.1/T4.3 rig (run-id stamped) for the privilege case.

## Implementation notes
1. Errors: `SELEC 1 FROM dual` (ORA-00900 class syntax), `INSERT` duplicate into a PK table (ORA-00001), SELECT from a table the low-privilege user cannot see (ORA-00942/ORA-01031 per Oracle semantics; assert the same code on both), and a call timeout on `DBMS_SESSION.SLEEP(5)` with a 1 s call timeout (ORA-03156 / ORA-01013 class, classified as cancelled/timeout with the same retry metadata).
2. Compare envelope fields, not message text (message text may differ by driver); never compare raw driver strings.
3. VECTOR: columns `VECTOR(3, FLOAT64)`, `VECTOR(3, INT8)`, `VECTOR(16, BINARY)`, sparse FLOAT64, a NULL vector row; non-finite: attempt inserting `NaN`/`Inf` components and assert both backends produce the same outcome (Oracle refusal code or identical serialization).
4. Assert the projected JSON shape (`format`, `dimensions`, `values` / sparse `indices`) is identical.

## Test plan
- JSONL `{case_id, backend, expected, actual}` for: `parity_error_syntax`, `parity_error_unique_constraint`, `parity_error_privilege`, `parity_error_call_timeout`, `parity_vector_float64_dense`, `parity_vector_float64_sparse`, `parity_vector_int8`, `parity_vector_binary`, `parity_vector_null`, `parity_vector_non_finite_components`.

## Proof split
Envelope and vector parity at the `OracleConnection` seam. T3.4 owns the end-to-end error taxonomy at the MCP tool surface (#38, #42, #45).

## Non-goals
Changing the public error taxonomy (T3.4); new VECTOR features.

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove tool-level error responses or any guard decision.

## Considerations
- Hot file: every parity bead edits `crates/oraclemcp-db/tests/cross_backend_parity.rs`; file lane `parity` serialises T8.6, T8.7, T8.8, T8.9 (one owner at a time).
- A value mismatch found here is a driver or adapter bug: fix it in this bead if it is in oraclemcp's adapter (`oracledb_backend.rs` or `connection.rs` serialization); if it is in driver-cx, file a `discovered-from` bug in the driver repo that blocks this bead and is consumed through a T0.7 pin refresh.
- Serialization contract to preserve: NUMBER defaults to an exact JSON string, never a rounded JSON number (hard invariant).
- The privilege case needs the second user from the rig; it must be created per run and dropped by the janitor (no persistent grants).

## Absorbs
- `oraclemcp-xoflp.4.6`: kept in full (syntax, constraint, privilege, cancellation/timeout; ErrorClass, ORA code, retry metadata, operation context).
- `oraclemcp-xoflp.4.7`: kept in full (FLOAT64, INT8/BINARY, NULL vectors, non-finite components, stable structured shape).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: the four error kinds produce identical `ErrorClass`, ORA code, `retry_after_ms` and operation context on both backends; all VECTOR variants produce identical structured JSON or an identical typed official-backend refusal.
- [ ] Negative: a planted mapping of ORA-00001 to a generic `Internal` class in the official adapter fails `parity_error_unique_constraint`; a planted FLOAT64-as-FLOAT32 projection fails `parity_vector_float64_dense`.
- [ ] Tests: `parity_error_syntax`, `parity_error_unique_constraint`, `parity_error_privilege`, `parity_error_call_timeout`, `parity_vector_float64_dense`, `parity_vector_float64_sparse`, `parity_vector_int8`, `parity_vector_binary`, `parity_vector_null`, `parity_vector_non_finite_components`; green on FREE 23ai.
- [ ] Proof class: live in-process; forbidden substitutes: mock DB, synthetic error objects.
- [ ] Consumers: T8.9, T3.4.
- [ ] No-claim: does not prove tool-level error responses.

AC 1 Positive / live FREE 23ai: `live_cross_backend_error_and_vector_parity` passed in-process against both real adapters (fixture W40951D45BFE; teardown PASS, zero leftovers). title: Parity: TCPS/PEM connection and whole parity suite reproducible in the FREE 23ai lane
description:
## Context
Cross-backend parity compares the primary driver-cx backend (`RustOracleConnection`) with the official `oracledb` backend (`OfficialOracleConnection`) through the shared `OracleConnection` seam. Today the suite is `crates/oraclemcp-db/tests/cross_backend_parity.rs` (`#![cfg(all(feature = "oracledb", feature = "live-xe"))]`), two `#[ignore]` lab tests (`live_cross_backend_parity_for_supported_basic_auth`, `live_cross_backend_tcps_pem_connection_parity`) gated on `ORACLEMCP_DUAL_BACKEND_LAB=1` + `ORACLEMCP_TEST_DSN/USER/PASSWORD`; it covers TSTZ, one positive 38-digit NUMBER, dense/sparse FLOAT32 VECTOR, a missing-object error envelope and a transaction scenario, and never runs in CI.

Plan W8 (R12, R15, R19): parity for DATE/TIMESTAMP/INTERVAL, LOB/NULL, NUMBER boundaries, streaming, ORA error taxonomy, VECTOR variants and TCPS/PEM, made reproducible in the FREE 23ai lane. **Where the official backend lacks a type, a typed refusal is the tested behaviour**: the official adapter must return the same explicit `UnsupportedFeature` envelope (error class + stable reason) every time, never a silently different value. driver-cx stays primary (R12); these tests do not change routing. The metamorphic cross-backend suite (`2q4em.1.6`) was retired under R34 because these parity tests cover it.

Fixture rule: parity tables are created per run with the run-id stamping from T4.3 (the existing `ORACLEMCP_PARITY_*_{suffix}` naming becomes the T4.3 run-id stamp) and dropped at the end; the T4.3 janitor removes stale owned runs.

Gaps this bead closes (old beads `xoflp.4.8`, `p85od`):
- TCPS + `ewallet.pem` username/password connect and ping parity exists only as a manual `#[ignore]` test (`live_cross_backend_tcps_pem_connection_parity`, env `ORACLEMCP_DUAL_BACKEND_TCPS_PEM_LAB`, `ORACLEMCP_TCPS_PEM_DSN/USER/PASSWORD/WALLET_LOCATION`). It asserts routing stays driver-cx (`select_connection_backend` returns `OracleBackend::RustOracle` for a PEM wallet) and then connects both adapters directly. cwallet.sso and IAM must never route to official.
- The whole parity suite is `#[ignore]` and lab-gated and never runs in CI; the parity claim rests on a single manual lab run. It must become reproducible, CI-gated against a FREE 23ai container with both backends compiled, with a PL/SQL parity case.

The tier-A FREE 23ai lane (plan W5; infrastructure from T4.11, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` job `oracle-free23`) has a hard 25-minute budget; if it runs over, it is split by family, never `continue-on-error`.

## Outcome
The complete parity suite (T8.6-T8.8 scenarios, the existing TSTZ/NUMBER/VECTOR/transaction scenarios, a PL/SQL case and the TCPS/PEM connection case) runs on every push/PR in the tier-A FREE 23ai lane against a freshly provisioned container, with a runtime-generated synthetic PEM wallet and TCPS listener, and fails the lane on any mismatch.

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp-db/tests/cross_backend_parity.rs`: remove `#[ignore]` from the parity entry points; replace the manual `ORACLEMCP_DUAL_BACKEND_*` acknowledgement with the lane's standard env (T4.1 rig variables) so the test runs when the rig env is present and **fails** (not skips) when the lane sets `ORACLEMCP_REQUIRE_LIVE=1` and the env is incomplete; add `run_plsql_parity_scenario`.
- Lane wiring in the FREE 23ai job (T4.11's script, e.g. `scripts/e2e/oracle_version_matrix.sh --lane free23` or its T4.11 successor): run `cargo test -p oraclemcp-db --features oracledb,live-xe --test cross_backend_parity` inside the budget.
- TCPS fixture step: inside the FREE 23ai container, generate a throwaway server wallet and self-signed certificate with `orapki` at run time, add a TCPS listener endpoint (e.g. port 2484) via `listener.ora`/`sqlnet.ora`, export the client trust as `ewallet.pem` into a temp dir; nothing is committed.

## Implementation notes
1. PL/SQL case: create a run-stamped function `ORACLEMCP_PARITY_FN_<run>(n NUMBER) RETURN NUMBER` and a procedure with an OUT parameter; compare `SELECT fn(41) FROM dual` and an anonymous-block OUT bind across both backends.
2. TCPS case: keep the routing assertion (PEM wallet stays driver-cx), then direct-adapter connect + ping + `describe` identity parity (server version, session user, current schema) as the existing test does; add the negative that an SSO wallet and an IAM token are refused by the official adapter with its typed refusal (`reject_auto_login_wallet_at_consumption` and the IAM rejection in `oracledb_backend.rs`).
3. Time budget: measure the suite; record duration in the lane log; if the lane would exceed 25 minutes, split parity into its own family job in the same tier (never `continue-on-error`).
4. Redact: the lane logs never print the generated wallet or passwords.

## Test plan
- `live_cross_backend_parity_for_supported_basic_auth` (un-ignored, now including T8.6-T8.8 scenarios), `live_cross_backend_tcps_pem_connection_parity` (un-ignored), `parity_plsql_function_and_out_bind`, `official_adapter_refuses_sso_wallet_typed`, `official_adapter_refuses_iam_token_typed`, `parity_suite_fails_when_required_env_missing` (runs with `ORACLEMCP_REQUIRE_LIVE=1` and no DSN, expects failure).
- JSONL per case `{case_id, backend, expected, actual, lane:"free23"}`, uploaded as the lane artifact.

## Proof split
This bead proves reproducibility in CI and TCPS/PEM parity on FREE 23ai with a synthetic wallet. W9 (T9.5b, T9.6a) proves wallet forms and TCPS against a real ADB.

## Non-goals
Real ADB wallets (W9); routing changes; making the official backend handle SSO/IAM.

## No-claim boundary
A green lane does not prove ADB TCPS, SNI or wallet-form behaviour against OCI.

## Considerations
- Hot file: every parity bead edits `crates/oraclemcp-db/tests/cross_backend_parity.rs`; file lane `parity` serialises T8.6, T8.7, T8.8, T8.9 (one owner at a time).
- A value mismatch found here is a driver or adapter bug: fix it in this bead if it is in oraclemcp's adapter (`oracledb_backend.rs` or `connection.rs` serialization); if it is in driver-cx, file a `discovered-from` bug in the driver repo that blocks this bead and is consumed through a T0.7 pin refresh.
- Serialization contract to preserve: NUMBER defaults to an exact JSON string, never a rounded JSON number (hard invariant).
- **structure-owner check**: the TCPS listener is configured inside the tier-A FREE 23ai container with a runtime `orapki` wallet; confirm with the T4.11 owner that the container image exposes `orapki` and that the extra listener fits the 25-minute budget; otherwise the parity family becomes its own tier-A job (still required).
- File lanes `parity` and `ci-workflows` (the lane script/ci.yml is shared with T4.11 and T5.x).
- Confidentiality: generated wallet material lives only in the job's temp dir.

## Absorbs
- `oraclemcp-xoflp.4.8`: kept (live-gated TCPS + `ewallet.pem` connect and ping parity; SSO and IAM never routed to official).
- `oraclemcp-p85od`: kept, and the conditional "assess effort / keep as follow-up" clause is dropped by R25 (nothing deferred): reproducible CI-gated parity against FREE 23ai incl. a PL/SQL case.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: on a push to main, the tier-A FREE 23ai lane runs the full cross-backend parity suite (incl. PL/SQL and TCPS/PEM cases) green, with the parity JSONL uploaded as an artifact.
- [ ] Negative: with `ORACLEMCP_REQUIRE_LIVE=1` and the DSN unset, the suite fails instead of skipping.
- [ ] Negative: the official adapter refuses an SSO wallet and an IAM token with its typed refusal; routing for a PEM wallet stays driver-cx.
- [ ] Tests: `live_cross_backend_parity_for_supported_basic_auth`, `live_cross_backend_tcps_pem_connection_parity`, `parity_plsql_function_and_out_bind`, `official_adapter_refuses_sso_wallet_typed`, `official_adapter_refuses_iam_token_typed`, `parity_suite_fails_when_required_env_missing`; green in the tier-A FREE 23ai lane within the 25-minute budget.
- [ ] Proof class: live in-process against a CI-provisioned FREE 23ai container; forbidden substitutes: `#[ignore]`, `continue-on-error`, a committed real wallet, a mock TLS terminator in place of the Oracle TCPS listener.
