title: W10 Windows audit security: verify the ACL-takeover fix natively and restore windows-rust
description:
## Goal
Close the Windows audit security gap (ruling **R21**: "fix the Windows audit security gap in this release") with native-Windows proof, and return the native Windows runtime lane `windows-rust` to a **required** tier-A lane. Windows is a supported platform: every release ships `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` and `install.ps1`.

## Current state (measured 2026-09-23)
- Commit `f0f2b54f` normalised ownership of every authenticated audit object with WRITE_OWNER + WRITE_DAC. On a pre-existing (pre-planted) audit file or directory that could adopt an attacker-held object whose handles stay open.
- Commit **`ee2c04a7` ("refuse Windows ACL takeover")** is in the baseline: `harden_windows_private_acl` in `crates/oraclemcp-audit/src/sink.rs` checks the owner SID before changing the DACL (`before.owner() != Some(&*current_sid)` -> refuse) and does not set the owner; it verifies with `verify_windows_private_acl`, refuses reparse points, hard links (`number_of_links`), type changes and identity swaps (`open_file_identity`). Startup preparation `create_private_audit_dir` (`crates/oraclemcp/src/main.rs`) hardens directories through `harden_windows_private_directory`; the WORM mirror parent on Windows goes through `create_private_audit_dir`.
- **The native lane is still red.** PR run 35556613151 (2026-09-21), job `Rust workspace (Windows)`: 139 passed, 3 failed: `build_auditor_installs_when_writable_profile_has_a_key`, `build_auditor_hardens_a_new_worm_parent_before_opening_the_mirror`, `startup_performs_authenticated_mixed_key_rotation_end_to_end`, each with `audit path ... is not owned by the current Windows process user` on a freshly created temp directory. Root cause (TokenOwner vs TokenUser, recorded on `xuaea`): on the elevated `windows-latest` runner new objects are owned by the token's default owner (BUILTIN\Administrators), not the user SID, so the strict owner check refuses the process's own fresh directories.
- `windows-rust` is advisory (`continue-on-error: true`, `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'`, operator steering 2026-09-16 on `2q4em.2.1`); a README Limitations note says native-Windows audit-DACL hardening is under repair. The Windows installer/service lane (`windows-installer`) is required and green.
- Constraint: every crate is `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`; an atomic `CreateDirectoryW` + `SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES` create-time descriptor has no vetted safe wrapper. `windows-permissions 0.2.4` (in the graph) exposes `SetSecurityInfo`/`GetSecurityInfo` and `current_process_sid` (TokenUser) safely, but not TokenOwner.

## Design
W10 is **verification of a landed fix on native Windows, not a re-implementation. Patch only what the tests expose.** The first exposed defect is known (fresh objects owned by TokenOwner). Allowed fix shape, safe Rust only: strict TokenUser ownership stays mandatory for every **pre-existing** object; owner normalisation to TokenUser is permitted only for an object this process has just created (non-recursive create returned success) beneath an already verified private parent (or, for the top-level directory, immediately after creation with handle identity re-verified), followed by the exact owner/DACL readback.

Required native tests (all on the GitHub `windows-latest` runner, which is native Windows):
- an attacker-owned pre-planted file and directory;
- an attacker-held open handle;
- a reparse point;
- a hard link;
- an identity swap;
- a current-owner broad DACL that is tightened successfully;
- fresh private parent and file creation, with exact readback.

Siblings folded in as far as needed to prove these: `8n02c` (WORM shipping audit parent), `windows-audit-owner-proof-sd39s` (temp-dir ownership proof), `2q4em.10.1/10.2` (minimal Windows proof tier + durable-state release-acceptance step). Stale CI comments are removed only after the native lane passes.

## Invariants
- Fail closed: an audit path that cannot be proven private is refused (`ORACLEMCP_AUDIT_PATH_INVALID` / `ORACLEMCP_AUDIT_SHIPPING_INVALID`), never silently accepted.
- Never adopt (take ownership of) a pre-existing object.
- No `unsafe`; no new unvetted crate without operator approval.
- The audit hash chain and its verifier are unchanged.

## Acceptance
`windows-rust` returns as a **required** tier-A lane (promotion done by T5.3, which depends on T10.3); `2q4em.2.1` (three consecutive green heartbeats) closes after it.

## Size and dependencies
3 leaves, sequential: T10.1 -> T10.2 -> T10.3. Consumer: T5.3 (restore windows-rust + api-lock as tier A).

## Children
T10.1, T10.2, T10.3.

title: Verify the Windows ACL-takeover fix natively; fix fresh-object ownership
description:
## Context
Windows audit security (ruling **R21**, plan W10). `harden_windows_private_acl` in `crates/oraclemcp-audit/src/sink.rs` (landed fix `ee2c04a7`, "refuse Windows ACL takeover") opens a security handle with `FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT` (+ `FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS` for directories) and share mode read/write/delete, refuses reparse points, type changes, `number_of_links() != 1` for files and identity changes (`open_file_identity` vs `metadata_identity`), refuses unless the owner equals `windows_permissions::utilities::current_process_sid()` (TokenUser), sets the protected owner-only DACL `D:P(A;;FA;;;<sid>)` (directories `D:P(A;OICI;FA;;;<sid>)`, `windows_private_dacl_sddl`), then `verify_windows_private_acl` and a final identity recheck. Entry points: `harden_windows_private_directory`, `harden_windows_private_directory_handle`, `harden_windows_private_file_handle`, `open_private_append_file`; startup: `create_private_audit_dir` in `crates/oraclemcp/src/main.rs`; WORM mirror parent in the shipping setup of `main.rs` (Windows branch calls `create_private_audit_dir(parent)`).

Measured red (PR run 35556613151, 2026-09-21, job `Rust workspace (Windows)`, 3 of 142 failed): `build_auditor_installs_when_writable_profile_has_a_key`, `build_auditor_hardens_a_new_worm_parent_before_opening_the_mirror`, `startup_performs_authenticated_mixed_key_rotation_end_to_end` (`crates/oraclemcp/src/main_tests_audit_startup.rs`, `main_tests.rs`), all "audit path ... is not owned by the current Windows process user" on a fresh temp directory: on the elevated runner new objects are owned by the token's default owner (BUILTIN\Administrators = TokenOwner), not TokenUser.

Constraints: `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`; `windows-permissions 0.2.4` offers safe `SetSecurityInfo`/`GetSecurityInfo`/`current_process_sid` but no TokenOwner query and no create-time `SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES`. W10 rule: verify the landed fix natively and **patch only what the tests expose**.

Old bead `xuaea` (P0, in progress): restore strict TokenUser ownership for existing objects and allow owner normalisation only after an atomic fresh-create proof beneath an already verified private parent; preserve exact post-set owner/DACL verification; add focused Windows regression coverage for existing-object refusal and fresh create.

## Outcome
On native Windows (`windows-latest`), every hostile fixture in the required list is refused fail-closed, a current-owner broad DACL is tightened and read back exactly, and fresh private parent/file creation succeeds with exact owner (TokenUser) and DACL readback, including on the elevated runner where the default owner is BUILTIN\Administrators. The three measured failures pass.

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp-audit/src/sink.rs`: a fresh-create path that knows it created the object (non-recursive `create_dir` / `create_new` returned success), reopens it no-follow, re-verifies identity, and only then normalises the owner to TokenUser with `SetSecurityInfo(Owner | Dacl | ProtectedDacl)` followed by `verify_windows_private_acl` (owner + exact DACL). Pre-existing objects keep the strict owner check (no normalisation). Exposed as the one function the startup path and the sink both use (e.g. `create_private_windows_directory_fresh` / the file analogue inside `open_or_create_private_windows_file`).
- `crates/oraclemcp/src/main.rs` `create_private_audit_dir`: on Windows, directories it creates go through the fresh-create path (component by component for `recursive(true)`, so each newly created component is normalised and verified; pre-existing components are held to the strict check).
- Pre-existing object with a non-private DACL and another open handle: hardening must not tighten while a foreign handle survives; open the object with exclusive share mode (share mode 0) before tightening and refuse on a sharing violation.
- Tests below (Windows-gated, in `sink.rs` `#[cfg(all(test, windows))]` and `crates/oraclemcp/src/main_tests_audit_startup.rs`).
- Only what the tests expose is patched; no other audit behaviour changes.

## Implementation notes
1. Fixture tooling (test-only, via `std::process::Command`): `icacls <path> /setowner *S-1-5-18` (SYSTEM) to plant a foreign-owned file/dir (the runner is elevated, icacls enables SeRestorePrivilege itself); a child process (`powershell -Command` opening `[System.IO.File]::Open(path,'Open','ReadWrite','ReadWrite')` and sleeping) to hold a foreign handle; a directory junction (`cmd /c mklink /J`) for the reparse case; `fsutil hardlink create` or `std::fs::hard_link` for the hard-link case; rename-swap during the hook points (`set_file_audit_parent_handle_hook`, `set_file_audit_open_hook`) for the identity swap.
2. A fixture that cannot be created on the runner is a **test failure**, never a SKIP (the existing `load_anchor_refuses_an_intermediate_reparse_parent` prints SKIP when junction creation fails; the new tests must not).
3. Fresh top-level directory in a non-private parent (e.g. `%TEMP%`): after create, open no-follow, verify it is a directory with no entries and the identity matches, then normalise; a race that replaces it is detected by the identity check.
4. Exclusive-share open applies only while tightening a pre-existing object whose DACL is not already the exact private DACL, so normal restarts (object already private) are not blocked by the sink's own lock handles.
5. Every refusal keeps the existing error codes (`ORACLEMCP_AUDIT_PATH_INVALID`, `ORACLEMCP_AUDIT_SHIPPING_INVALID`) with a precise reason string.

## Test plan
Windows-only tests (run in `windows-rust` via `cargo test --lib --bins`):
- `windows_audit_refuses_preplanted_foreign_owned_file`, `windows_audit_refuses_preplanted_foreign_owned_directory`;
- `windows_audit_refuses_broad_dacl_object_with_foreign_open_handle`;
- `windows_audit_refuses_junction_audit_directory`, `windows_audit_refuses_reparse_intermediate_component`;
- `windows_audit_refuses_hard_linked_audit_file`;
- `windows_audit_refuses_identity_swap_before_hardening`;
- `broad_windows_file_and_directory_dacls_are_tightened_and_read_back` (existing, must stay green);
- `windows_audit_fresh_parent_and_file_owner_is_token_user_with_exact_dacl` (reads back owner SID and the exact SDDL);
- the three measured failures: `build_auditor_installs_when_writable_profile_has_a_key`, `build_auditor_hardens_a_new_worm_parent_before_opening_the_mirror`, `startup_performs_authenticated_mixed_key_rotation_end_to_end`.
- Each hostile test prints JSONL `{case_id, fixture, expected:"refused"|"private", actual, owner_sid_kind, dacl_sddl}` (SIDs of the runner are not secrets but print only the SID kind: user / administrators / system).

## Proof split
This bead proves the sink/startup hardening on native Windows. T10.2 proves the WORM parent and temp-dir ownership sibling paths end to end; T10.3 wires the proof tier and makes `windows-rust` green on consecutive runs.

## Non-goals
`unsafe` FFI; a new security crate (needs operator approval); non-Windows behaviour changes; the audit chain format.

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove non-elevated interactive Windows accounts behave identically (the runner is elevated); does not prove the release-acceptance Windows step (T10.3).

## Considerations
- **structure-owner check**: the fresh-create owner normalisation design and the exclusive-share rule for pre-existing broad-DACL objects are implied by the required tests (TokenOwner failure, attacker-held handle) but not spelled out in the plan; if safe Rust cannot express either, stop and escalate to the operator (options on record: a vetted crate or an `unsafe` exception) instead of weakening a refusal.
- `sec`: second-agent review before batch verify.
- Never adopt a pre-existing object; never widen a DACL; never downgrade a refusal to a warning.
- File lane `windows-audit` (sink.rs Windows section, main.rs audit startup); reserve before editing.

## Absorbs
- `oraclemcp-xuaea`: kept in full (strict TokenUser for existing objects; owner normalisation only after a proven fresh create under a verified private parent; exact post-set owner/DACL verification; Windows regression coverage for existing-object refusal and fresh create). Its 2026-09-16 "demote rather than fix" steering is superseded by R21.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: on `windows-latest`, fresh audit parent directory and file creation succeed and read back owner = TokenUser and DACL exactly `D:P(A;OICI;FA;;;<user-sid>)` / `D:P(A;;FA;;;<user-sid>)`; a current-owner broad DACL is tightened and read back exactly.
- [ ] Positive: `build_auditor_installs_when_writable_profile_has_a_key`, `build_auditor_hardens_a_new_worm_parent_before_opening_the_mirror`, `startup_performs_authenticated_mixed_key_rotation_end_to_end` pass on the native runner.
- [ ] Negative: a pre-planted SYSTEM-owned file and directory, a broad-DACL object with a foreign open handle, a junction, a hard-linked file and an identity swap are each refused with the existing error code (an implementation that normalises every owner, as `f0f2b54f` did, accepts the foreign-owned fixtures).
- [ ] Tests: `windows_audit_refuses_preplanted_foreign_owned_file`, `windows_audit_refuses_preplanted_foreign_owned_directory`, `windows_audit_refuses_broad_dacl_object_with_foreign_open_handle`, `windows_audit_refuses_junction_audit_directory`, `windows_audit_refuses_reparse_intermediate_component`, `windows_audit_refuses_hard_linked_audit_file`, `windows_audit_refuses_identity_swap_before_hardening`, `broad_windows_file_and_directory_dacls_are_tightened_and_read_back`, `windows_audit_fresh_parent_and_file_owner_is_token_user_with_exact_dacl`; green in the native `windows-rust` job; no SKIP output.
- [ ] Proof class: live on native Windows (GitHub `windows-latest`); forbidden substitutes: Wine, cross-compilation-only checks, a SKIP when a fixture cannot be created.
- [ ] Consumers: T10.2, T10.3.
- [ ] No-claim: does not prove non-elevated interactive accounts or the release-acceptance step.

Two sibling Windows paths were filed separately and are now partly landed in code but never proven green on a native runner:

1. Use the T10.1 fixture helpers (icacls owner planting, broad DACL installer) rather than new copies.

title: Minimal Windows proof tier, Windows release-acceptance step, windows-rust green
description:
## Context
Windows audit security (ruling **R21**, plan W10). `harden_windows_private_acl` in `crates/oraclemcp-audit/src/sink.rs` (landed fix `ee2c04a7`, "refuse Windows ACL takeover") opens a security handle with `FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT` (+ `FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS` for directories) and share mode read/write/delete, refuses reparse points, type changes, `number_of_links() != 1` for files and identity changes (`open_file_identity` vs `metadata_identity`), refuses unless the owner equals `windows_permissions::utilities::current_process_sid()` (TokenUser), sets the protected owner-only DACL `D:P(A;;FA;;;<sid>)` (directories `D:P(A;OICI;FA;;;<sid>)`, `windows_private_dacl_sddl`), then `verify_windows_private_acl` and a final identity recheck. Entry points: `harden_windows_private_directory`, `harden_windows_private_directory_handle`, `harden_windows_private_file_handle`, `open_private_append_file`; startup: `create_private_audit_dir` in `crates/oraclemcp/src/main.rs`; WORM mirror parent in the shipping setup of `main.rs` (Windows branch calls `create_private_audit_dir(parent)`).

Measured red (PR run 35556613151, 2026-09-21, job `Rust workspace (Windows)`, 3 of 142 failed): `build_auditor_installs_when_writable_profile_has_a_key`, `build_auditor_hardens_a_new_worm_parent_before_opening_the_mirror`, `startup_performs_authenticated_mixed_key_rotation_end_to_end` (`crates/oraclemcp/src/main_tests_audit_startup.rs`, `main_tests.rs`), all "audit path ... is not owned by the current Windows process user" on a fresh temp directory: on the elevated runner new objects are owned by the token's default owner (BUILTIN\Administrators = TokenOwner), not TokenUser.

Constraints: `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`; `windows-permissions 0.2.4` offers safe `SetSecurityInfo`/`GetSecurityInfo`/`current_process_sid` but no TokenOwner query and no create-time `SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES`. W10 rule: verify the landed fix natively and **patch only what the tests expose**.

CI state: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` job `windows-rust` ("Rust workspace (Windows)") runs `--lib --bins` with reduced debuginfo (the 2026-07-19 speedup, ~6 min instead of ~2 h), `timeout-minutes: 75`, `RUSTC_WRAPPER: ""`, and is advisory: `continue-on-error: true` and `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` (commit `f93d2a66`, operator steering 2026-09-16 on `2q4em.2.1`), classified advisory in `docs/ci_taxonomy.json` / `crates/oraclemcp-core/ci_taxonomy.json` (`scripts/ci_taxonomy.py`), noted in `docs/test-tiers.md` ("advisory (pending oraclemcp-xuaea, see README Limitations)") and in the README Limitations section. The heartbeat `.github/workflows/ci-heartbeat.yml` watches required lanes.

Plan W10: the Windows proof tier is kept **minimal** (`2q4em.10.1/10.2` "as far as needed to prove these"), and stale CI comments are removed only after the native lane passes. Plan W5: windows-rust returns as a required tier-A lane (the promotion itself is T5.3, which depends on this bead). Plan acceptance: `2q4em.2.1` (three consecutive green heartbeats) closes after it. R24/R34: no ceremony; no new manifest format.

## Outcome
The Windows audit/durable-state suites run first in `windows-rust` as a named step (fast, clear failure names), then the workspace `--lib --bins` tests; the release pipeline has a Windows durable-state acceptance step that blocks the tag on a Windows regression; `windows-rust` is green on three consecutive runs on main-equivalent SHAs; stale advisory comments are removed once green.

## Deliverable
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `windows-rust`: a first step "Windows proof tier" running `cargo test -p oraclemcp-audit -p oraclemcp-core -p oraclemcp --lib --bins -- windows_audit_ worm_parent_ startup_audit_parent_ build_auditor_ file_store::windows` (the exact filter list for the T10.1/T10.2 tests plus the existing `cfg(windows)` suites in `oraclemcp-core` `file_store` and `service_lifecycle`), then the existing workspace step. The filter list lives in the workflow step (no separate manifest file). The job gains `workflow_dispatch`/`push` triggering needed for the consecutive-run proof; `continue-on-error` removal and the `if:` change are **T5.3**.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: a Windows job in the gate path: build the Windows zip, `install.ps1 -DryRun` then a real install into a temp prefix, `oraclemcp service install --dry-run` (no host mutation on shared runners), `oraclemcp serve --listen 127.0.0.1:<port>` with a temp state dir, trigger an audited action that needs no database (startup and session-level audit records), stop the server, run `oraclemcp audit verify` on the produced JSONL + anchor, and check the audit and durable-state directory ACLs with the hardener's own verifier (exposed as `oraclemcp doctor` output or a hidden test hook, whichever already exists; do not add a new CLI surface for this). The same job runs on `workflow_dispatch` for a rehearsal.
- `docs/test-tiers.md`: the Windows row names the proof-tier step and the release step; the "advisory (pending oraclemcp-xuaea)" wording is removed after the lane is green.
- README Limitations note about native-Windows audit-DACL hardening removed once green; stale `ci.yml` comments about the demotion removed at the same time.

## Implementation notes
1. Keep the `--lib --bins` + reduced-debuginfo speedup; do not add integration-test binaries to the Windows job.
2. Consecutive-run proof: three consecutive green `windows-rust` runs on successive main SHAs (push or dispatch), and three consecutive green scheduled heartbeat runs after T5.3 makes the lane required; record run ids. Waits are bounded (rule 16): check once per session, report, move on.
3. Negative rehearsal for the release step: a dispatch run on a scratch branch that plants an ACL regression (e.g. an env-gated test hook that installs a broad DACL on the audit directory after startup) must fail the step; record the run id.
4. If the heartbeat stays red for a non-Windows reason, file it as a `discovered-from:T10.3` bug and surface it; do not close.

## Test plan
- CI: `windows-rust` proof-tier step + workspace step, three consecutive green runs; release Windows acceptance job green on a rehearsal dispatch; negative rehearsal red.
- Step summary lines `{check, result}` for install, service dry-run, serve, audit append, audit verify, ACL verify.

## Proof split
This bead proves the lane is reliably green and the release step exists and fails on a regression. T5.3 promotes windows-rust to required; R.1/R.7 run the release step on the candidate and the tag.

## Non-goals
A separate Windows tier manifest file or PowerShell runner script (anti-ceremony: the workflow step is the tier); Windows stable toolchain; Windows integration-test binaries.

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove non-elevated interactive Windows accounts or Windows Server editions other than the hosted image.

## Considerations
- **structure-owner check**: `2q4em.2.1` ("three consecutive green heartbeats") is absorbed here, but the heartbeat watches required lanes and windows-rust becomes required only in T5.3, which depends on this bead. This spec proves three consecutive green `windows-rust` runs here and records the three heartbeat run ids after T5.3 lands, as a closing condition of this bead; confirm the structure owner accepts that T10.3 closes after T5.3 lands (a close-order note, not a graph dependency), or moves the heartbeat line to T5.3.
- **structure-owner check**: the database-free audited action for the release step (startup/session-level records) is assumed sufficient; if `audit verify` needs a privileged DB action to be meaningful, the release job uses a FREE 23ai service container, which is not available on Windows runners, so the step would stay database-free.
- File lanes `ci-workflows` (ci.yml, release.yml shared with T5.x/T6.1/T7.4) and `windows-audit`.
- Old bead `2q4em.10.2` referenced "the 0.10.1 tag"; the tag here is v0.12.0.

## Absorbs
- `oraclemcp-2q4em.10`: kept minimal (Windows proof tier + release-acceptance step so a Windows regression blocks a tag).
- `oraclemcp-2q4em.10.1`: kept minus the separate `windows_tier.toml` manifest and `.ps1` runner (anti-ceremony, R34); named suites run first in windows-rust; test-tiers doc updated.
- `oraclemcp-2q4em.10.2`: kept (install -> service dry-run -> serve -> audit append -> audit verify -> ACL check on the Windows runner; negative rehearsal).
- `oraclemcp-2q4em.2.1`: kept (three consecutive green scheduled heartbeats with windows-rust included, run ids in evidence); its demotion steering is superseded by R21.


## Structure-owner note
The "three consecutive green heartbeats" condition (old `oraclemcp-2q4em.2.1`) moved to T5.3, which runs after this bead because windows-rust becomes a required lane there.

title: W9: OCI Autonomous Database: fix the driver, then test-and-triage until clean
description:
## Goal
Make oraclemcp connect to **OCI Autonomous Database (ADB)** and then test-and-triage through all of OCI until an ADB run is clean (operator rulings R19, R20, R27, R30). Field issues: **#54** (ADB post-ACCEPT auth/TTC handshake fails in `oraclemcp-driver-cx`; python-oracledb thin works with the same wallet, credentials and descriptor; on-prem 19c works with the same driver), **#55** (stock ADB wallet forms: `cwallet.sso`, `ewallet.pem`/`.p12` with legacy 3DES PKCS#12 OID `1.2.840.113549.1.12.1.3`), **#56** (diagnosability: "driver detail suppressed", connect trace appears to stop at `read ACCEPT`, the first hint wrongly says "verify the connect string").

## Current state (measured 2026-09-23)
- OCI ADB does **not** work (#54). #55 and #56 are open. driver-cx 0.9.2 *contains* `cwallet.sso` and legacy 3DES PKCS#12 support (`rust-oracledb/crates/oracledb-protocol/src/tls/{sso,pfx}.rs`), but that is **claimed**, not proven: the 0.11 install still failed against ADB.
- Infrastructure exists (so nothing here is blocked-born): `infra/oci-adb/main.tf` (`is_free_tier = true`, provider pinned), `scripts/e2e/oci_adb_terraform.sh` (plan / apply-and-signoff with a teardown trap, redacted command runner, IAM bootstrap, committed-tree `scripts/secret_scan.sh`), `scripts/e2e/real_adb_tcps_signoff.sh`, `.github/workflows/oci-adb.yml` (dispatch-only, `environment: oci-adb-acceptance`, `OCI_*` secrets). The workflow has never had a real dispatch.
- oraclemcp's stash list holds 8 stashes labelled "temporary ... OCI ... local-driver override" (IAM subject mapping, classic IAM, Legacy16 trace, StaticClientCert, diagnostics + RUST_LOG pass-through, validation retries). The local rust-oracledb `master` holds unpushed commit `4204676` (TTC unknown-message-type 129 classified as a transient desync).
- The driver already prints `ORACLEDB_TRACE_CONNECT` steps after ACCEPT (ACCEPT capability line, fast-auth / classic negotiation, AUTH phase one/two) in 0.9.2, so the #56 observation that the trace "stops at read ACCEPT" means the failure happens at or immediately after reading/parsing ACCEPT, or on a path that emits no step (claimed; T9.2 proves it).
- `connect_string_with_transport_timeout` in `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/connection.rs` refuses `connect_timeout_seconds` for any full `(DESCRIPTION=...)` descriptor, i.e. for every ADB wallet `tnsnames` entry (deferred bug `yb7m`).

## Design
**Phase A: make the connection work (driver).**
1. Reproduce against an Always-Free ADB (zero cost, constitution #10) with the provisioning + teardown-as-incident harness. Versions: query OCI's version list, filter on `is_free_tier_enabled`, use only free-enabled versions, record the exact returned version and capabilities (Oracle's docs currently list 19c and 26ai; never hard-code). Ownership: snapshot pre-existing resources by OCID; create only Always-Free resources tagged with the run id; assertions and cleanup touch only OCIDs this run created.
2. Trace the post-ACCEPT auth/TTC exchange with driver-cx vs python-oracledb thin, same wallet and credentials; review the 8 OCI stashes and driver commit `4204676`.
3. Fix the negotiation in driver-cx (#54); ship in driver 0.10.0.
4. #56: (a) opt-in `doctor --online --verbose` / env switch revealing the driver error class + ORA/TNS code with secrets redacted (redaction canaries); (b) driver tracing that covers auth/TTC after ACCEPT; (c) phase-aware hints from the furthest phase reached (DNS -> TCP -> TLS -> wallet -> ACCEPT -> auth/TTC -> session); (d) request-span correlation (`m6e6l`, R30): one request span carrying request, session, lane, subject and tool ids, propagated to local logs and OTLP, never raw secrets.
5. #55: prove every wallet form live: `cwallet.sso` auto-login, `ewallet.p12`/`ewallet.pem` with legacy 3DES PKCS#12 **without** `cwallet.sso`, AES/PBES2, encrypted PEM and standalone `.p12` (`k6q.7`, R30), plus synthetic unit fixtures (no real wallet material committed). Truly passwordless external auth is retired (R30). Fix bug `yb7m` (`connect_timeout_seconds` refused for ADB descriptors).

**Phase B: test and triage through all of OCI (R20).** Loop run -> triage -> fix -> rerun until clean; every failure gets a fix and a regression case.
- Full W4 matrix once per free-enabled ADB version on the canonical mTLS-wallet connection.
- Connection-contract subset (connect, governed SELECT, rollback DML/refusal, cancel, reconnect) for every variant: mTLS wallet (`cwallet.sso`), PEM-only wallet, walletless TLS, IAM database token, service levels `_low/_medium/_high/_tp/_tpurgent`, SNI/TLS 1.3.
- ADB behaviours tested deliberately (correct result or honest typed refusal): ADMIN is not SYSDBA; restricted `DBA_*`/`V$` views and restricted SYS packages (`UTL_*`, `DBMS_*`); no AWR/Diagnostics-Pack assumptions (`top_queries` licence path); idle-session disconnects (#47); Always-Free session/connection limits; Resource Manager cancels (`ORA-56735` class); database links refused; CQN availability; editions, VPD, masking, VECTOR on 23ai; `ALTER SESSION` restrictions; NLS/time zone of the service; wallet rotation.
- Lanes: the OCI lane joins tier C (release-only; capability sweep open -> exercise -> close); `091-f4` (B6 trust union + SNI on real ADB) runs inside it; `oci-adb.yml` gets its first real dispatch.
- Confidentiality: redact at capture time; only phase/state summaries and synthetic fixtures are persisted; raw auth/TTC bytes, wallet identifiers and tokens stay in gitignored quarantine and are covered by redaction-canary tests.

## Invariants
- Confidentiality (constitution #9): no live OCI, tenancy, compartment, region-host, database-name, IP, OCID, wallet or token value enters any committed file, test fixture, log excerpt, bead comment or evidence file. Field issues are cited by GitHub number only. Raw captures live only in gitignored quarantine (`todelete/`, `target/e2e/`).
- Zero cost (constitution #10): Always-Free resources only. The authoritative zero-cost check (no billable ADB in state AVAILABLE besides the run's own Always-Free one, using a known-non-empty control query in the same OCI CLI invocation because the CLI omits the `data` key on empty lists) runs before and after every run.
- A connection subset result is never presented as a full W4 run.
- driver-cx stays the primary driver (R12); no silent fallback to password, thick mode or the official `oracledb` driver for a wallet/TCPS/IAM route.

## Acceptance (workstream)
- #54/#55/#56 closed by passing live ADB runs.
- For every free-enabled ADB version: the full W4 matrix is green once on the canonical mTLS-wallet connection, and the connection-contract subset is green for every supported authentication, wallet, TLS and service-level variant.
- Unsupported combinations return the capability matrix's exact typed refusal.
- The evidence manifest names the canonical connection and lists every subset variant separately.
- Every triage finding has a fix + a regression case.
- The OCI local-gate results JSON is committed for the release tag (bound by T5.5/R.6).

## Size and dependencies
The plan gives no size for W9; it is Track D (section 19): W8 fixes + W9 Phase A -> driver 0.10.0 (via pin refresh T0.7 and RC integration T0.5) -> W9 Phase B triage loop. Phase B also exercises the W7/W12/W13/W14 live cases, so T9.6a waits on T4.9, T12.9, T13.8, T14.9.

## Children
T9.1, T9.2, T9.3, T9.4a, T9.4b, T9.5a, T9.5b, T9.6 (controller epic; children T9.6a, T9.6b and every discovered finding), T9.7.

title: Always-Free ADB harness: free-version discovery, run-tag ownership, redaction, tier-C lane
description:
## Context
Every W9 claim needs a real Always-Free ADB (R19, R20). The infrastructure exists, so this bead is **not blocked-born**: `infra/oci-adb/main.tf` (`is_free_tier = true`, `db_workload = "OLTP"`, OCI provider pinned `= 8.19.0`), `scripts/e2e/oci_adb_terraform.sh` (plan / `--apply-and-signoff`, `cleanup` EXIT trap that always destroys, `run_redacted`, IAM bootstrap, final `scripts/secret_scan.sh`), `scripts/e2e/real_adb_tcps_signoff.sh`, `.github/workflows/oci-adb.yml` (dispatch-only, `confirmation=provision-and-destroy`, `OCI_*` secrets). Gaps: no ADB version is chosen (Terraform uses the service default), no free-enabled version discovery, no run-id tagging/ownership snapshot, no before/after zero-cost check, the workflow has never had a real dispatch, and the OCI lane is not part of tier C.

Rulings: R19: verify every claim with a test; oraclemcp 0.11 did **not** connect to OCI on the field machine, so nothing is "already solved" without a passing test. R20: fix OCI fully in the driver, then test and triage through all of OCI and fix everything found. R24/R34: no process ceremony; deliverables are working capability and the tests that prove it.
- Tier C = release-only lanes run on the exact release-candidate SHA; their results feed the release proof (T5.5) committed before the tag.
- Confidentiality (constitution #9): no live OCI, tenancy, compartment, region-host, database-name, IP, OCID, wallet or token value enters any committed file, test fixture, log excerpt, bead comment or evidence file. Field issues are cited by GitHub number only. Raw captures live only in gitignored quarantine (`todelete/`, `target/e2e/`).
- Zero cost (constitution #10): Always-Free resources only. The authoritative zero-cost check (no billable ADB in state AVAILABLE besides the run's own Always-Free one, using a known-non-empty control query in the same OCI CLI invocation because the CLI omits the `data` key on empty lists) runs before and after every run.

## Outcome
One command (and the dispatched `oci-adb.yml`) provisions one Always-Free ADB **per free-enabled version** returned by OCI, tags it with the run id, exposes it as a tier-C target (connection material in a runner-private, gitignored run directory), lets a caller run the W4 matrix or a subset against it, and always destroys only what it created, with zero-cost checks before and after and a confidentiality scan that fails the lane on any live identifier.

## Deliverable
Repo: oraclemcp.
- `infra/oci-adb/main.tf`: new variable `db_version` (required, no default) passed to `oci_database_autonomous_database.signoff`; a freeform tag `oraclemcp-run-id = var.run_id`; keep `is_free_tier = true` and its precondition.
- `scripts/e2e/oci_adb_terraform.sh`:
  - `discover_free_versions`: `oci db autonomous-db-versions list --compartment-id ... --db-workload OLTP --all`, keep entries whose `is-free-tier-enabled` is true, write the exact version strings + details into the run dir; zero free versions -> typed `SKIP_NO_FREE_VERSION` failure (never a silent pass).
  - `snapshot_owned_state`: record pre-existing ADB OCIDs in the compartment before apply; after apply, the run owns exactly the new OCID carrying its run-id tag. Every assertion and teardown operates on that owned set only.
  - `zero_cost_check pre|post`: the authoritative check described in Considerations; a failure is a lane failure.
  - per-version loop (one ADB at a time, Always-Free limits) with a hook `--run <cmd>` that receives the target env file (connect string path, wallet dir, credentials file) for the W4 runner (T4.1/T4.11) or a subset driver.
  - capability-sweep scaffolding (open -> exercise -> close): isolated per-run schemas/users named from the run id, created at open, dropped at close (from `bp8ia.10.2`).
- Confidentiality guard (from `bp8ia.10.3`): extend `scripts/secret_scan.sh` with an `--deny-values-from <file>` mode; the lane writes this run's live values (tenancy/compartment/user OCIDs, region host, ADB name/OCID, service hosts, IPs, wallet file names) to a runner-private file and scans every artifact it is about to persist (results JSON, JSONL logs, evidence) against both the generic patterns (existing `ocid1.` rule) and those exact values. Raw captures go only to `target/e2e/<run>/quarantine/` (gitignored).
- `.github/workflows/oci-adb.yml`: new operation `tier-c` (provision per free version -> run the supplied W4/subset command -> destroy), same confirmation input; results JSON uploaded as an artifact only after the scan passes.
- Results JSON per version (`oci_adb_results.json`: version string, run id, canonical-connection name, per-case verdicts, teardown verdict, zero-cost pre/post verdicts) in the shape the tier-C runner (T4.1) and release proof (T5.5) consume.

## Implementation notes
1. Add `db_version`/`run_id` variables; thread `TF_VAR_db_version` from discovery.
2. Implement discovery and the filter; log each candidate version with its free-tier flag (no identifiers).
3. Ownership: `oci db autonomous-database list` before apply -> pre-existing set; after apply -> owned set = new minus pre-existing, cross-checked against the run-id tag. Refuse to continue unless the owned set is exactly one ADB.
4. Teardown-as-incident already exists (`cleanup` trap); extend it to the per-version loop and prove a forced mid-run failure (test switch `--fail-after-apply`) still destroys.
5. Zero-cost check pre and post (method in Considerations).
6. Confidentiality scan before any artifact leaves the run dir.
7. Tier-C wiring: the OCI lane appears in the tier-C list the release gate consults (`scripts/local_release_gate.sh` already delegates to the real-ADB signoff harness on explicit request).
8. First real dispatch of `oci-adb.yml` with `operation=apply-and-signoff`: provision, python-oracledb thin control connect (the workflow already installs `oracledb==4.0.2`), oraclemcp `doctor --online` attempt (expected to fail until T9.3; the verdict is recorded, not hidden), destroy.

## Test plan
- `bash scripts/e2e/oci_adb_terraform.sh --selftest` (offline, synthetic OCI JSON under `scripts/e2e/fixtures/oci/`):
  - `oci_harness_version_filter`: a synthetic list with free and non-free versions yields exactly the free ones; an all-non-free list fails with `SKIP_NO_FREE_VERSION`;
  - `oci_harness_ownership`: synthetic pre-existing OCIDs are never selected for assertion or teardown;
  - `oci_harness_zero_cost_empty_list`: an empty `data` list with the control query present passes; a missing control result fails closed.
- `bash scripts/secret_scan.sh --self-test` extended with `oci_confidentiality_deny_values`: a fixture containing a planted synthetic deny-value fails; the clean synthetic fixture passes.
- Live (dispatched workflow and local run): provision per free-enabled version, python-oracledb control connect succeeds, forced failure after apply still destroys (`--fail-after-apply`), zero-cost pre/post pass, scan passes. JSONL log per step: `{case_id, phase, expected, actual, verdict, duration_ms}` with no identifiers.

## Proof split
Proves provisioning, per-version discovery, ownership isolation, teardown, zero-cost checks, the confidentiality scan and tier-C wiring. Does not prove oraclemcp connects (T9.3 + T9.5b), wallet forms (T9.5a/T9.5b), the W4 matrix on ADB (T9.6a/T9.6b) or B6/SNI (T9.7).

## Non-goals
- Fixing the handshake (T9.3) or any driver code.
- Running the W4 matrix (T9.6a); authoring W4 cases (W4).
- Paid shapes, paid storage or any non-Always-Free resource.
- A new evidence-manifest format (the release proof is the existing D3.2 file extended by T5.5).

## No-claim boundary
A green harness run does not prove oraclemcp works on ADB; the python-oracledb control connect proves only that the provisioned ADB, wallet and credentials are good.

## Considerations
- Zero-cost method (from `091-f4` and the OCI verify method in use): per-run OCI config, compartment taken from Terraform state, list ADBs with a known-non-empty control query in the same invocation (the CLI omits `data` on empty lists), trust the ADB list, assert no ADB other than the run's own Always-Free one is AVAILABLE.
- Always-Free allows only a small number of free ADBs per tenancy; run versions sequentially and destroy before the next.
- The deny-value file is runner-private (`umask 077`) and never uploaded.
- `bp8ia.10.1` cross-references the deferred provision guard `i-oci-free-tier-provision-guard-ilr4`; the existing `assert_free_tier_module` covers that refusal; do not duplicate it.
- File lane `oci-harness`: T9.5b, T9.6a and T9.7 extend the same scripts; claim the lane before editing.

## Absorbs
- `oraclemcp-eng-program-bp8ia.10` (Cluster I: OCI Always-Free ADB e2e): the container; its scope is this harness plus T9.6a.
- `oraclemcp-eng-program-bp8ia.10.1` (provisioning + teardown-as-incident): kept in full, plus per-version discovery and run-tag ownership.
- `oraclemcp-eng-program-bp8ia.10.2` (capability sweep open -> exercise -> close): the open/close scaffolding and isolated schemas live here; the exercise is T9.6a.
- `oraclemcp-eng-program-bp8ia.10.3` (confidentiality guard): kept in full as the deny-value scan.

title: Reproduce and trace #54 against python-oracledb; review the OCI stashes and driver 4204676
description:
## Context
Issue #54: against OCI ADB (mTLS wallet, TCPS descriptor) `oraclemcp-driver-cx 0.9.2` completes TLS, wallet load (`cwallet.sso`) and TNS ACCEPT, then fails the post-ACCEPT auth/TTC handshake. python-oracledb thin succeeds with the same wallet, credentials and descriptor; on-prem 19c works with the same driver. ADB tends to run a newer RDBMS/TTC protocol than on-prem 19c.

What exists (claimed, section 2.2): driver 0.9.2 already emits `ORACLEDB_TRACE_CONNECT` steps after ACCEPT (the `ACCEPT sdu=... fast_auth=... end_of_response=... oob=...` line, fast-auth vs classic negotiation, `send/read AUTH phase one/two`, token paths) in `crates/oracledb/src/lib.rs` (connect path around `trace_connect_step("read ACCEPT")`, `parse_accept_payload`, RESEND/REDIRECT/REFUSE handling; re-derive with `rg -n trace_connect_step`). #56 says the field trace stopped at `read ACCEPT`, so the failure is at or immediately after reading/parsing ACCEPT, or on a path that prints no step.

Leads to review:
- oraclemcp stashes labelled "temporary ... OCI ... local-driver override" (8 entries: IAM local-driver overlay after subject-mapping revalidation; final OCI classic-IAM local driver override; v6z2 local driver OCI override; r2t0 OCI Legacy16 trace; r2t0 StaticClientCert revalidation; r2t0 diagnostics + RUST_LOG pass-through; r2t0 validation full retry; r2t0 validation). Identify them by label with `git stash list`, never by index.
- Unpushed rust-oracledb commit `4204676` (docs-only): TTC unknown-message-type 129 is not a real TTC type (valid 1..34) and is classified as a transient desync; residual classic-path hole: `response_complete` stops mid-response and strands packets; fixing it safely needs a live capture.

Rulings: R19: verify every claim with a test; oraclemcp 0.11 did **not** connect to OCI on the field machine, so nothing is "already solved" without a passing test. R20: fix OCI fully in the driver, then test and triage through all of OCI and fix everything found. R27: the rust-oracledb off-limits rule is lifted for this train (driver fixes are in scope).
- Confidentiality (constitution #9): no live OCI, tenancy, compartment, region-host, database-name, IP, OCID, wallet or token value enters any committed file, test fixture, log excerpt, bead comment or evidence file. Field issues are cited by GitHub number only. Raw captures live only in gitignored quarantine (`todelete/`, `target/e2e/`).

## Outcome
The exact diverging post-ACCEPT message (or pre-auth step) between driver-cx and python-oracledb thin against a real ADB is identified per free-enabled version, captured as a sanitized phase/state summary, and encoded as a **red** driver regression test that T9.3 turns green. Every OCI stash and `4204676` has a recorded verdict (points at the fix / irrelevant / superseded).

## Deliverable
Repos: rust-oracledb (test), oraclemcp (read-only stash review).
- A driver regression test reproducing the divergence offline: `crates/oracledb-protocol/tests/adb_post_accept_divergence.rs` (follow the crate's test layout), built from a **synthetic reconstruction** of the diverging server message(s) with every identifier-bearing field replaced, failing on current code for the reason observed live.
- A sanitized finding appended to the bead (not a new document): versions tested, furthest phase reached by driver-cx, first diverging message type/field vs python-oracledb, per-lead verdicts.
- Raw captures (driver trace with T9.4a tracing, python-oracledb thin packet output) stay in `target/e2e/<run>/quarantine/` only.

## Implementation notes
1. On a T9.1-provisioned ADB (each free-enabled version): run python-oracledb thin with packet tracing (`PYO_DEBUG_PACKETS=1`) and driver-cx with `ORACLEDB_TRACE_CONNECT=1` (T9.4a structured phases), same wallet/credentials/descriptor.
2. Align both traces by message: CONNECT, RESEND/REDIRECT, ACCEPT fields (version, SDU, flags, fast-auth, end-of-response), protocol negotiation, data types, AUTH phase one, AUTH phase two, session.
3. Name the first divergence: a field the driver rejects, a message it does not expect, a framing (end-of-response vs classic) mismatch, a redirect it does not follow, or a desync of the `4204676` class.
4. Review each OCI stash with `git stash show -p` (read-only; never `drop`/`pop`: RULE 1). Record what it changed in the driver override and whether it addresses the divergence. Stash clean-up belongs to T0.4.
5. Encode the divergence as the red regression test; cite the python-oracledb reference behaviour (file/function under python-oracledb `src/oracledb/impl/thin/`) it must match.
6. Run the same trace on XE 18/21 and FREE 23ai to record which branch they take (explains why on-prem passes).

## Test plan
- `adb_post_accept_divergence` (driver, offline): red on current `origin/main`, with an assertion message naming the diverging message/field.
- Live repro log per ADB version (JSONL `{case_id: "w9_54_repro_<version>", phase_reached, expected: "session established", actual, verdict}`), persisted only after the T9.1 confidentiality scan.
- Case manifest: the #54 case in `scripts/e2e/cases/release_0_12.json` (T4.0) gets its `pre_fix_outcome` from this run.

## Proof split
Proves where and why the handshake fails. The fix and its green proof are T9.3; oraclemcp-level proof is T9.5b/T9.6a after the pin refresh (T0.7).

## Non-goals
- Writing the fix (T9.3).
- Dropping, applying or rewriting stashes or branches (T0.4, operator-run).
- Persisting any raw auth/TTC bytes.

## No-claim boundary
A reproduced divergence does not prove it is the only ADB defect; Phase B (T9.6a) triages the rest.

## Considerations
- Wire bytes can include user names, service names, session keys and verifier material: never commit them; the synthetic reconstruction replaces every such field.
- Differential-first: python-oracledb thin is the reference behaviour; no fix is guessed without a captured divergence.
- If the divergence is version-specific (for example only on the newest free version), the finding lists each version separately.
- Confidentiality (constitution #9): no live OCI, tenancy, compartment, region-host, database-name, IP, OCID, wallet or token value enters any committed file, test fixture, log excerpt, bead comment or evidence file. Field issues are cited by GitHub number only. Raw captures live only in gitignored quarantine (`todelete/`, `target/e2e/`).

## Absorbs
None.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: the bead records, per free-enabled ADB version, the furthest phase driver-cx reaches and the first message/field where it diverges from python-oracledb thin
- [ ] Positive: `adb_post_accept_divergence` exists and fails on current driver `origin/main` for the recorded reason
- [ ] Positive: each of the 8 OCI stashes and commit `4204676` has a one-line verdict in the bead
- [ ] Negative: the regression test contains no live identifier (the T9.1 confidentiality scan passes on it)
- [ ] Tests: `adb_post_accept_divergence` (red, driver repo); live repro JSONL `w9_54_repro_<version>`
- [ ] Proof class: live (real Always-Free ADB) for the repro; offline for the regression test; forbidden substitutes: a hypothesised message layout without a live capture
- [ ] Consumers: T9.3
- [ ] No-claim: does not prove the fix or that no other ADB defect exists

title: Fix the driver-cx post-ACCEPT handshake against OCI ADB (#54)
description:
## Context
Issue #54: OCI ADB profiles cannot be used through oraclemcp at all; driver-cx fails the post-ACCEPT auth/TTC negotiation while python-oracledb thin works with the same wallet, credentials and descriptor. T9.2 identifies the exact divergence and leaves a red regression test (`adb_post_accept_divergence`). The fix ships in driver **0.10.0**. Rulings: R12 (driver-cx stays primary), R15 (all fixes, no big features), R20 (fix OCI fully in the driver), R27 (driver repo in scope).

Code: `rust-oracledb/crates/oracledb/src/lib.rs` connect path (ACCEPT parsing, fast-auth vs classic negotiation, AUTH phase one/two, framing mode via `set_classic_framing`), `crates/oracledb-protocol/src/thin/{connect.rs,mod.rs,constants.rs}`, `crates/oracledb-protocol/src/capabilities.rs`. Line numbers are hints as of `1fbe6eb0` (oraclemcp) / `cdc3e82` (rust-oracledb `origin/main`); re-derive every one with `rg -n` before editing. Symbol names are the stable reference.

## Outcome
driver-cx establishes a session against every free-enabled OCI ADB version over the canonical mTLS wallet connection, matching python-oracledb thin's behaviour at the diverging step, with no regression on XE 18/21, FREE 23ai or on-prem 19c-class servers.

## Deliverable
Repo: rust-oracledb (packages `oraclemcp-driver-cx` / `oraclemcp-driver-cx-protocol`).
- The minimal protocol change at the step T9.2 names, matching the python-oracledb reference.
- `adb_post_accept_divergence` turns green.
- A gated live test `crates/oracledb/tests/adb_live_connect.rs` (runs only when the T9.1 target env file is supplied): connect, `SELECT 1 FROM DUAL`, one round trip with a bind, clean close.
- CHANGELOG entry under the 0.10.0 section.

## Implementation notes
1. Implement the fix exactly at the divergence, in the reference-faithful shape (cite the python-oracledb file/function in a code comment).
2. If the divergence is the `4204676` desync class, implement the reference-faithful classic-path completion fix described in that commit and add a framed/classic test pair, so the deliberate framed-path behaviour (`exercise_borrowed_stream_fetch_decode_failure`) is preserved.
3. Keep every existing refusal (for example `AccessTokenRequiresTcps`, unsupported NNE) intact.
4. Run the driver's live version matrix (XE 18/21, FREE 23ai) to prove no on-prem regression.
5. Push the driver revision; T0.7 refreshes the oraclemcp pin.

## Test plan
- `adb_post_accept_divergence` green (driver unit, tier A).
- `adb_live_connect` green on each free-enabled ADB version from a T9.1 run (JSONL `{case_id: "w9_54_driver_<version>", expected: "session", actual, verdict}`).
- Driver live matrix green on XE 18, XE 21, FREE 23ai (existing lanes).
- Existing golden handshake tests (`pre23ai_handshake_golden`) unchanged and green.

## Proof split
Proves the driver connects to ADB. oraclemcp-level proof (external MCP client, `doctor --online`, governed SELECT) is T9.5b and T9.6a after T0.7 refreshes the pin; wallet forms are T9.5a/T9.5b.

## Non-goals
- New driver features (R15), for example NNE or DRCP.
- Wallet-form work (T9.5a).
- Server-side diagnostics (T9.4b).

## No-claim boundary
A driver-level ADB connect does not prove every ADB variant (IAM, walletless TLS, service levels) or the full tool matrix; T9.6a covers those.

## Considerations
- Confidentiality: the live test reads connection material only from the runner-private env file; nothing live is committed.
- The fix must not loosen TLS verification, DN matching or token-over-TLS rules.
- File lane `driver-connect` is shared with T9.4a; claim it before editing `lib.rs`.

None.

title: Driver: structured, redaction-safe connect tracing through auth/TTC with phase on errors
description:
## Context
Issue #56 (driver half): the suggested `ORACLEDB_TRACE_CONNECT=1` trace appeared to stop at `read ACCEPT`, before the failing phase, so a protocol gap looked like a config mistake.

Current code (driver `origin/main cdc3e82`, same step set in 0.9.2): `trace_connect_step` / `trace_connect_value` / `trace_connect_bytes` in `crates/oracledb/src/lib.rs` `eprintln!` when `ORACLEDB_TRACE_CONNECT` is set. Steps exist for tcp/tls, CONNECT, `read ACCEPT`, RESEND/REDIRECT/REFUSE, the ACCEPT capability line, fast-auth/classic negotiation and AUTH phase one/two. Gaps:
- no phase is attached to the returned `Error`, so the server cannot say how far the handshake got;
- steps are unstructured stderr lines, not `tracing` events;
- `trace_connect_bytes` hex-dumps AUTH phase one/two **payloads and responses** (user name, session-key and verifier material) to stderr: a confidentiality hazard;
- some post-ACCEPT branches (ACCEPT parse failure, framing selection, the password fast-auth bundle) may fail before emitting any step (claimed; prove with tests).
The existing test `crates/oracledb/tests/connect_trace_secret.rs` checks that secrets stay out of the trace.

Rulings: R27 (driver in scope), R15 (fixes, no big features). Confidentiality (constitution #9): no live OCI, tenancy, compartment, region-host, database-name, IP, OCID, wallet or token value enters any committed file, test fixture, log excerpt, bead comment or evidence file. Field issues are cited by GitHub number only. Raw captures live only in gitignored quarantine (`todelete/`, `target/e2e/`).

## Outcome
With tracing enabled, every connect emits one structured event per phase (DNS, TCP, TLS, wallet, CONNECT, ACCEPT, negotiation, data types, AUTH phase one, AUTH phase two, session) through `tracing` (target `oracledb::connect`), still honouring `ORACLEDB_TRACE_CONNECT` for stderr, and every connect error exposes the furthest phase reached. Default trace output contains message types, lengths and capability flags only, never payload bytes.

## Deliverable
Repo: rust-oracledb.
- `ConnectPhase` enum (public, `#[non_exhaustive]`) in the `oraclemcp-driver-cx` crate: `Dns, Tcp, Tls, Wallet, Connect, Accept, Negotiation, DataTypes, AuthPhaseOne, AuthPhaseTwo, Session` (seam owned here; consumer: oraclemcp T9.4b through the T0.7 pin refresh).
- `Error::connect_phase(&self) -> Option<ConnectPhase>` populated on every connect-path error.
- `trace_connect_*` helpers emit `tracing` events with fields `{phase, step, message_type, len, flags}`; stderr printing kept for `ORACLEDB_TRACE_CONNECT=1`.
- `trace_connect_bytes` no longer prints AUTH payload/response hex by default; raw hex only with `ORACLEDB_TRACE_CONNECT=raw`, which first prints a one-line warning that the output contains credential-derived material and must stay in quarantine.
- Missing steps added on every post-ACCEPT branch, including ACCEPT parse failure and the password fast-auth bundle.

## Implementation notes
1. Introduce `ConnectPhase`; track `furthest_phase` in the connect state and attach it when mapping errors.
2. Convert the helpers to `tracing::event!` (target `oracledb::connect`), keeping the env-var stderr mirror.
3. Classify every `trace_connect_bytes` call: AUTH payload/response -> length + message type only unless `raw`; ACCEPT/negotiation/data-types responses -> length + parsed flags.
4. Audit every `?` between `read ACCEPT` and session establishment for a preceding step event; add the missing ones.
5. Document the switch values in the driver README (0.10.0).

## Test plan
- `connect_phase_reported_on_accept_parse_failure`, `connect_phase_reported_on_auth_phase_two_failure`, `connect_phase_reported_on_tls_failure` (fault-injection style of `crates/oracledb-protocol/tests/fault_injection.rs`).
- `connect_trace_secret` extended: with `ORACLEDB_TRACE_CONNECT=1` a planted password/user/token canary never appears; with `raw` the warning line comes first.
- `trace_events_cover_every_post_accept_step`: a loopback handshake records the ordered phase list for both fast-auth and classic branches.
- Live: driver live matrix (FREE 23ai) with a wrong password -> `connect_phase()` reports the AUTH phase the server rejects in.

## Proof split
Proves driver-side tracing and phase reporting. The server consumes the phase in T9.4b; T9.2 uses the tracing for the ADB capture.

## Non-goals
- Server-side hints, verbose doctor or request spans (T9.4b).
- Fixing the ADB handshake (T9.3).

## No-claim boundary
Better tracing does not make any failing connect succeed.

## Considerations
- Adding `ConnectPhase` is a public API addition; record it in the driver's API baseline in the same commit (rule 17).
- File lane `driver-connect` is shared with T9.3 and T9.2's test; coordinate via reservations.
- Structure-owner check: the `raw` switch value is this bead's decision to satisfy "raw auth/TTC bytes stay in quarantine".

## Absorbs
None.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: every connect-path error returned by the driver carries `connect_phase()`; a wrong-password connect against FREE 23ai reports an AUTH phase
- [ ] Positive: with `ORACLEDB_TRACE_CONNECT=1` a successful connect emits one ordered event per phase through session establishment
- [ ] Negative: a planted password/user/token canary never appears in default trace output
- [ ] Negative: AUTH payload hex appears only under `ORACLEDB_TRACE_CONNECT=raw`, after the warning line
- [ ] Tests: `connect_phase_reported_on_accept_parse_failure`, `connect_phase_reported_on_auth_phase_two_failure`, `connect_phase_reported_on_tls_failure`, `connect_trace_secret`, `trace_events_cover_every_post_accept_step` (driver tier A); the FREE 23ai wrong-password live case
- [ ] Proof class: unit + live in-process (driver); forbidden substitutes: asserting on log strings from a mocked connect
- [ ] Consumers: T9.2, T9.4b (via T0.7), T0.7
- [ ] No-claim: does not prove server-side hint quality or any ADB connect

title: Server diagnosability: verbose opt-in, phase-aware hints, request spans, stderr redaction
description:
## Context
Issue #56 (server half):
1. The client gets `Oracle connection failed; driver detail suppressed` (`DbError::Connect` -> `into_envelope` in `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/error.rs`) with no documented switch to reveal the driver error.
2. The first remediation hint is always "verify the connect string (host, port, service name), credentials, and listener reachability", which points the wrong way once TLS + TNS ACCEPT succeeded; `CONNECT_TRACE_NEXT_STEP` follows it.
3. Operators cannot follow one failing call end to end.

Existing pieces: `ConnectFailureKind` (`UnexpectedTnsPacket`, `ConnectResendLoop`, `FastAuthNotAdvertised`, `UnsupportedWireFeature`, `ListenerRefused`, `ListenerRedirectUnsupported`, the protocol-floor kind, `HandshakeProtocol`) in `error.rs`; `doctor` (`crates/oraclemcp/src/cli.rs` `Command::Doctor { profile, online, fix }`, `crates/oraclemcp-core/src/doctor.rs` `run_doctor`); `otlp::Redactor` (`crates/oraclemcp-telemetry/src/otlp/redact.rs`) applied to OTLP only; local structured logging in `crates/oraclemcp-telemetry/src/logging.rs`; OTLP traces in `otlp/traces.rs`. The invariant "driver transport detail is never rendered on a tool surface" stays.

Rulings: R30 keeps request-span correlation (`m6e6l`) in this train; R19 (verify by test). Confidentiality (constitution #9): no live OCI, tenancy, compartment, region-host, database-name, IP, OCID, wallet or token value enters any committed file, test fixture, log excerpt, bead comment or evidence file. Field issues are cited by GitHub number only. Raw captures live only in gitignored quarantine (`todelete/`, `target/e2e/`).

## Outcome
An operator can run `oraclemcp doctor --online --verbose` (or set `ORACLEMCP_CONNECT_DETAIL=1` for the server) and see the driver error class, ORA/TNS code and the furthest connect phase reached, with every secret redacted; the first hint matches that phase; one request span with request/session/lane/subject/tool ids appears identically in local logs and OTLP; local stderr passes through the same redactor as OTLP. MCP tool envelopes stay detail-suppressed.

## Deliverable
Repo: oraclemcp.
- `crates/oraclemcp/src/cli.rs`: `Doctor { verbose: bool }` (`--verbose`, valid only with `--online`); `ORACLEMCP_CONNECT_DETAIL=1` env switch read once at startup (the name is this bead's decision).
- `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/error.rs`: `ConnectPhaseReached { Dns, Tcp, Tls, Wallet, Accept, AuthTtc, Session, Unknown }` derived from the driver error (`ConnectFailureKind`, TLS/IO error classes today; the driver's `connect_phase()` once T0.7 pins T9.4a); `connect_hint_for(phase)` replaces the static first hint; verbose rendering `DbError::connect_detail_redacted()` used only by doctor and stderr, never by `into_envelope`.
- `crates/oraclemcp-core/src/doctor.rs`: phase + hint in the online report (JSON and human).
- `crates/oraclemcp-telemetry`: a request span created at tool dispatch carrying `request_id, session_id, lane_id, subject_id, tool` (subject as the server-derived key, never a raw token), propagated to `logging.rs` records and OTLP trace/span ids; `Redactor` applied to local structured stderr as well as OTLP.

## Implementation notes
1. Phase derivation: TLS handshake failure -> Tls; wallet load error -> Wallet; `ListenerRefused` / `ConnectResendLoop` / `ListenerRedirectUnsupported` -> Accept (not reached); `HandshakeProtocol` / `FastAuthNotAdvertised` / ORA-01017 -> AuthTtc; DNS/IO connect errors -> Dns/Tcp; when the pinned driver exposes `connect_phase()`, prefer it.
2. Hints: Dns/Tcp -> connect string and reachability; Tls/Wallet -> wallet location, `ssl_server_cert_dn`, SNI; Accept -> listener/service; AuthTtc -> "TLS and TNS ACCEPT succeeded; failure is in authentication/protocol negotiation" + credentials/IAM + `CONNECT_TRACE_NEXT_STEP`; Session -> session setup hooks.
3. Verbose detail: redact passwords, wallet passwords, tokens, OCIDs, DSN credentials and bind values with the shared `Redactor`; show the driver error class and ORA/TNS code.
4. Request span: create at the dispatch entry (stdio and HTTP), record the ids as span fields; assert the local log line carries the same trace/span ids as the OTLP export.
5. Apply `Redactor` in the local stderr layer; add negative canaries so non-secret context (tool name, error class, ORA code) survives.

## Test plan
- Unit: `connect_hint_after_accept_never_suggests_connect_string`, `connect_phase_from_error_kind_table` (one row per kind), `verbose_detail_redacts_password_token_ocid_dsn_canaries`, `tool_envelope_stays_detail_suppressed_with_verbose_env`, `stderr_redactor_scrubs_dsn_bind_ocid_reference`, `stderr_redactor_keeps_tool_error_class_and_ora_code`, `request_span_ids_match_local_log_and_otlp`, `concurrent_requests_separable_by_request_id`.
- Live external (FREE 23ai lab lane, installed binary): `doctor --online --verbose` with a wrong password -> phase `AuthTtc`, ORA-01017 shown, password canary absent; closed port -> phase `Tcp`; bad wallet dir -> phase `Wallet`. JSONL per case `{case_id, expected_phase, actual_phase, canary_leak}`.
- Case manifest: the #56 cases in `scripts/e2e/cases/release_0_12.json` (T4.0) green.

## Proof split
Proves server-side diagnosability on lab databases. ADB-specific phases are exercised in T9.6a; driver tracing is T9.4a.

## Non-goals
- Driver tracing (T9.4a).
- Showing driver detail on MCP tool envelopes.
- A new logging backend.

## No-claim boundary
A correct hint does not fix the underlying connect failure.

## Considerations
- Structure-owner check: the exact post-ACCEPT sub-phase needs the driver `ConnectPhase` from T9.4a. This bead does not depend on it: it maps today's error kinds, and the T0.7 pin-refresh consumer commit adapts the mapping to `connect_phase()` in the same commit as the pin move (rule 17). Confirm T0.7's consumer commit carries that adaptation.
- `selftest` (T4.15) reuses the phase report; keep the report type stable.
- File lanes `db-connection` (error.rs/connection.rs, shared with T9.5b) and `telemetry`.

## Absorbs
- `oraclemcp-h-server-request-span-correlation-m6e6l`: kept in full (one request span; local and OTLP ids match; no raw secrets).
- `oraclemcp-h-server-local-log-redaction-r622e`: kept in full (Redactor over local stderr; DSN/bind/OCID/reference canaries; negative canaries against destructive over-redaction).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: `oraclemcp doctor --online --verbose` against FREE 23ai with a wrong password prints phase `AuthTtc`, the ORA-01017 code and an authentication-phase hint, not the connect-string hint
- [ ] Positive: a single tool call's request id appears on the local log line and on the OTLP span with identical trace/span ids
- [ ] Negative: planted password, token, OCID and DSN canaries never appear in verbose doctor output or stderr
- [ ] Negative: an MCP tool call that fails to connect still returns `driver detail suppressed` with `ORACLEMCP_CONNECT_DETAIL=1` set
- [ ] Tests: unit tests listed in the Test plan (tier A); live external doctor cases on FREE 23ai; the #56 manifest cases
- [ ] Proof class: live external client (installed binary + FREE 23ai) + unit; forbidden substitutes: in-process `Dispatcher::new` for the live claim
- [ ] Consumers: T4.15, T9.6a
- [ ] No-claim: does not prove any ADB connect succeeds

title: Driver wallet forms: SSO, 3DES and AES .p12, encrypted PEM, with synthetic fixtures (#55)
description:
## Context
Issue #55: the default musl build once rejected a stock OCI ADB wallet (`cwallet.sso` unsupported; `ewallet.pem`/`.p12` keys under legacy 3DES PKCS#12, PBE OID `1.2.840.113549.1.12.1.3`, rejected; only PBES2/AES accepted). driver-cx 0.9.2 **contains** SSO and legacy 3DES support in `crates/oracledb-protocol/src/tls/{sso.rs,pfx.rs,wallet.rs}` (claimed, section 2.2). Open question from the issue: does the `ewallet.pem`/`.p12` path still fail when `cwallet.sso` is absent?

R30 keeps encrypted PEM and standalone `.p12` (`k6q.7`) in this train; truly passwordless external auth is retired. From `k6q.7`: never silently fall back to password or thick mode. No real wallet material is ever committed.

## Outcome
The driver loads every supported wallet form on its own (`cwallet.sso` auto-login; `ewallet.p12` with legacy 3DES PBE and with AES/PBES2, without `cwallet.sso`; unencrypted `ewallet.pem`; encrypted PKCS#8 PEM; a standalone `.p12`), each proven by a synthetic-fixture test, with a typed error naming the form and OID for anything unsupported.

## Deliverable
Repo: rust-oracledb.
- `crates/oracledb-protocol/src/tls/pfx.rs`: legacy PBE (3DES-SHA1 `1.2.840.113549.1.12.1.3`; RC2 variants refused with a typed error naming the OID) and PBES2 (PBKDF2 + AES-128/256-CBC) paths verified; standalone `.p12` (explicit file path) supported.
- `crates/oracledb-protocol/src/tls/wallet.rs`: encrypted PEM (`-----BEGIN ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY-----`, PBES2 and legacy PBE) with `wallet_password`; the existing form precedence re-derived, documented in the module doc and README, and unchanged unless a test proves it wrong.
- `crates/oracledb-protocol/src/tls/sso.rs`: `cwallet.sso` auto-login verified against a synthetic SSO fixture.
- Synthetic fixtures generated at test time (throwaway CA/leaf from the test's own generator) or committed synthetic files carrying throwaway keys only, documented as synthetic.

## Implementation notes
1. Verify-before-implement: inventory what 0.9.2 already supports with tests first; implement only the gaps the tests expose.
2. Add missing PBE/PBES2 branches and encrypted-PEM decode with crates already in the dependency set (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`).
3. Errors: `WalletError::{UnsupportedPbe{oid}, WrongPassword{form}, MissingKey{form}, AmbiguousForms}`; keep the existing OID message.
4. No fallback: a failing wallet never retries as password auth or with another driver.
5. Coordinate with T8.1 (refuse non-regular wallet files) in the same lane.

## Test plan
- `wallet_sso_autologin_synthetic`, `wallet_p12_legacy_3des_without_sso`, `wallet_p12_pbes2_aes256_without_sso`, `wallet_pem_unencrypted`, `wallet_pem_encrypted_pkcs8_pbes2`, `wallet_pem_encrypted_legacy_pbe`, `wallet_standalone_p12_explicit_path`.
- Negatives: `wallet_wrong_password_names_form`, `wallet_rc2_pbe_refused_names_oid`, `wallet_no_fallback_to_password_auth`.
- Loopback TLS: each fixture completes a TLS handshake against a local test server using the fixture's CA (driver test harness).

## Proof split
Proves wallet parsing and TLS use offline with synthetic material. Live proof of every form against a real ADB is T9.5b.

## Non-goals
- Truly passwordless external auth (retired, R30).
- Server-side config or docs (T9.5b, W6).

## No-claim boundary
Synthetic fixtures do not prove a real OCI-downloaded wallet loads; T9.5b proves that live.

## Considerations
- Confidentiality (constitution #9): no live OCI, tenancy, compartment, region-host, database-name, IP, OCID, wallet or token value enters any committed file, test fixture, log excerpt, bead comment or evidence file. Field issues are cited by GitHub number only. Raw captures live only in gitignored quarantine (`todelete/`, `target/e2e/`).
- File lane `driver-tls` shared with T8.1; rule 17 for any public error-type change.
- The dependency on T9.3 serializes driver commits in Track D before the T0.7 pin refresh.

## Absorbs
- `oraclemcp-040-epic-deferred-k6q.7`: kept: encrypted PEM and standalone `.p12`; retired: truly passwordless external auth (R30).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: each synthetic form (SSO, 3DES `.p12` without SSO, AES `.p12` without SSO, unencrypted PEM, encrypted PEM PBES2 and legacy PBE, standalone `.p12`) loads and completes a loopback TLS handshake

- [ ] Tests: `wallet_sso_autologin_synthetic`, `wallet_p12_legacy_3des_without_sso`, `wallet_p12_pbes2_aes256_without_sso`, `wallet_pem_unencrypted`, `wallet_pem_encrypted_pkcs8_pbes2`, `wallet_pem_encrypted_legacy_pbe`, `wallet_standalone_p12_explicit_path`, `wallet_wrong_password_names_form`, `wallet_rc2_pbe_refused_names_oid`, `wallet_no_fallback_to_password_auth` (driver tier A)

title: Server: connect_timeout for ADB wallet descriptors (yb7m); prove every wallet form live
description:
## Context
Bug `yb7m`: `connect_string_with_transport_timeout` in `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/connection.rs` (near line 2229 at `1fbe6eb0`) returns `DbError::UnsupportedAuth("connect_timeout_seconds cannot be injected into a full Oracle Net descriptor; ...")` whenever the connect string starts with `(`. Every ADB wallet `tnsnames` entry is a full `(DESCRIPTION=...)` descriptor, so `connect_timeout_seconds` + ADB can never connect. The driver takes its connect timeout only from the descriptor (`transport_connect_timeout_duration(primary_description.tcp_connect_timeout)`); it has no `ConnectOptions` timeout. The existing conflict refusal (a timeout already present in the connect string) stays.

Issue #55 closes only when every wallet form is proven live against a real ADB (R19). Driver support lands in T9.5a and reaches oraclemcp through the T0.7 pin refresh. Confidentiality (constitution #9): no live OCI, tenancy, compartment, region-host, database-name, IP, OCID, wallet or token value enters any committed file, test fixture, log excerpt, bead comment or evidence file. Field issues are cited by GitHub number only. Raw captures live only in gitignored quarantine (`todelete/`, `target/e2e/`).

## Outcome
An ADB profile with a wallet `tnsnames` descriptor and `connect_timeout_seconds` connects, and times out within the configured bound against an unreachable address; oraclemcp connects to a real ADB with each wallet form (SSO auto-login, `ewallet.pem` without SSO, `ewallet.p12` legacy 3DES without SSO, AES/PBES2 `.p12`, encrypted PEM, standalone `.p12`) through an external MCP client.

## Deliverable
Repo: oraclemcp.
- `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/connection.rs` `connect_string_with_transport_timeout`: for a full descriptor, insert `(TRANSPORT_CONNECT_TIMEOUT=<n>)` into every `DESCRIPTION` (including each entry of a `DESCRIPTION_LIST`) through a structured, balanced-parenthesis descriptor edit (reuse the driver's descriptor parser if the pinned crate exposes it, else a small server-side editor with its own tests); keep the typed conflict refusal when any `DESCRIPTION` already carries `TRANSPORT_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` or `CONNECT_TIMEOUT` with a different value.
- Harness (T9.1 scripts): a `wallet-forms` subset that derives each form from the downloaded wallet inside the run's quarantine dir (remove `cwallet.sso`; re-encrypt the `.p12` with AES/PBES2 via `openssl pkcs12`; export an encrypted PKCS#8 PEM; standalone `.p12`), then runs connect + governed SELECT through the external client per form.

## Implementation notes
1. Descriptor edit: parse into nodes, insert into each `DESCRIPTION` node, re-serialize; never touch `SECURITY`/`ADDRESS` contents; reject malformed descriptors with a typed error instead of a string splice.
2. Keep the EZConnect path unchanged.
3. Wallet-form subset: one profile per form (synthetic profile names), `oraclemcp` binary over stdio via the external client; case: connect, `oracle_query SELECT 1 FROM DUAL`, `oracle_connection_info`.
4. Timeout case: a synthetic descriptor pointing at a TEST-NET address (192.0.2.1) with `connect_timeout_seconds = 3` must fail with a typed timeout within 3 s plus a fixed slack.

## Test plan
- Unit: `transport_timeout_injected_into_full_descriptor`, `transport_timeout_injected_into_each_description_in_list`, `transport_timeout_conflict_in_descriptor_refused`, `malformed_descriptor_refused_typed`, `ezconnect_timeout_path_unchanged`.
- Live external (ADB via T9.1, each free-enabled version): `w9_wallet_sso_connect`, `w9_wallet_pem_without_sso_connect`, `w9_wallet_p12_3des_without_sso_connect`, `w9_wallet_p12_aes_connect`, `w9_wallet_encrypted_pem_connect`, `w9_wallet_standalone_p12_connect`, `w9_adb_descriptor_connect_timeout_connects`; JSONL `{case_id, version, expected, actual, verdict}`.
- Live external (lab): `w9_descriptor_connect_timeout_blackhole_bounded`.
- Case manifest: the #55 cases (T4.0) green.

## Proof split
Proves the server timeout path and live wallet forms. The broader connection-contract subset per variant (cancel, reconnect, DML refusal, IAM, walletless TLS, service levels) is T9.6a.

## Non-goals
- Driver wallet parsing (T9.5a).
- Passwordless external auth (retired, R30).

## No-claim boundary
Connect + SELECT per wallet form does not prove the full W4 matrix on ADB.

## Considerations
- Derived wallet forms and passwords live only in the run's quarantine dir and are destroyed with it. Confidentiality (constitution #9): no live OCI, tenancy, compartment, region-host, database-name, IP, OCID, wallet or token value enters any committed file, test fixture, log excerpt, bead comment or evidence file. Field issues are cited by GitHub number only. Raw captures live only in gitignored quarantine (`todelete/`, `target/e2e/`).
- File lanes `db-connection` (shared with T9.4b) and `oci-harness` (shared with T9.1/T9.6a/T9.7).
- Descriptor editing is security-relevant parsing: fuzz the editor with the existing connect-string fuzz seeds where present.

## Absorbs
- `oraclemcp-yb7m`: kept in full (inject `TRANSPORT_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` into the descriptor automatically); the `ConnectOptions` alternative it mentions does not exist in the driver.
