title: OCI clean-run controller: every Phase-B finding fixed, then a clean rerun
description:
## Context
R20: once connections work, loop run -> triage -> fix -> rerun until the ADB run is clean; every failure found gets a fix. This controller epic is graph structure only (it creates no artifacts): it makes every Phase-B finding required release work. R.1 requires zero open descendants under it.

## Outcome
All Phase-B findings are fixed with regression cases and the final ADB rerun (T9.6b) is clean.

## Deliverable
No code. Children: T9.6a (first full run; files findings), T9.6b (final clean rerun), and every finding bug filed by T9.6a (`discovered-from:T9.6a`, parent T9.6, each blocking T9.6b). Every finding fixed in a producer repo (driver or engine) also gets a following T0.7 (driver) or T0.6 (engine) pin-refresh child that blocks T9.6b.

## Implementation notes
**Closure rule:** this controller epic closes only when every discovered child is closed and the rerun child T9.6b passes. T9.6b's evidence records the tested SHA and is invalid once any blocking child lands a later commit.

## Test plan
None of its own; T9.6a, T9.6b and each finding carry the tests.

## Proof split
Structure only; the proof lives in the children.

## Non-goals
- Any fix work directly on this epic.

## No-claim boundary
Closing it does not replace the final release-candidate tier-C run in R.1.

## Considerations
- Findings are filed as bugs with a regression case each; none is closed as "won't fix" without an operator ruling (R25).

## Absorbs
None.

title: OCI Phase B first run: full W4 matrix per ADB version + connection subset; file findings
description:
## Context
R20 Phase B. Runs on the T0.5 release-candidate sibling integration (driver/engine candidate SHAs pinned), after the tier-C runner (T4.11), the PL/SQL tool cases (T4.9) and the W12/W13/W14 live suites (T12.9, T13.8, T14.9) exist. Harness: T9.1 (per free-enabled version, run-tagged, zero-cost checks, confidentiality scan).

Scope:
- **Full W4 matrix once per free-enabled ADB version** on the canonical mTLS-wallet connection (`cwallet.sso`), including the W7/W12/W13/W14 cases (ADB EBR support is itself claimed until this run proves it).
- **Connection-contract subset** (connect, governed SELECT, rollback DML/refusal, cancel, reconnect) for every variant: mTLS wallet (`cwallet.sso`), PEM-only wallet, walletless TLS, IAM database token, service levels `_low/_medium/_high/_tp/_tpurgent`, SNI/TLS 1.3.
- **ADB behaviours, each with a correct result or an honest typed refusal:** ADMIN is not SYSDBA; restricted `DBA_*`/`V$` views and restricted SYS packages (`UTL_*`, `DBMS_*`); no AWR/Diagnostics-Pack assumption (`top_queries` licence path); idle-session disconnects (#47); Always-Free session/connection limits; Resource Manager cancels (`ORA-56735` class); database links refused; CQN availability; editions, VPD, masking, VECTOR on 23ai-class versions; `ALTER SESSION` restrictions; NLS/time zone of the service; wallet rotation.
- The capability sweep (open -> exercise every capability -> close) from `bp8ia.10.2` runs on the T9.1 scaffolding. `oci-adb.yml` gets its first real tier-C dispatch.

Confidentiality (constitution #9): no live OCI, tenancy, compartment, region-host, database-name, IP, OCID, wallet or token value enters any committed file, test fixture, log excerpt, bead comment or evidence file. Field issues are cited by GitHub number only. Raw captures live only in gitignored quarantine (`todelete/`, `target/e2e/`). Zero cost (constitution #10): Always-Free resources only. The authoritative zero-cost check (no billable ADB in state AVAILABLE besides the run's own Always-Free one, using a known-non-empty control query in the same OCI CLI invocation because the CLI omits the `data` key on empty lists) runs before and after every run.

## Outcome
A recorded first Phase-B run per free-enabled ADB version with a verdict for every W4 case, every subset variant and every listed ADB behaviour; every non-green result is filed as a child bug with a regression case, parented to T9.6 and blocking T9.6b.

## Deliverable
Repos: oraclemcp (runner inputs, results); driver only through filed findings.
- Tier-C run results per version: the W4 results JSON (canonical connection named) and a separate subset results section listing each variant separately; ADB-behaviour cases added to the W4 case set as `w9_adb_<behaviour>` with the capability-matrix expectation.
- Walletless-TLS and IAM variants provisioned through the T9.1 harness (TLS without mTLS needs the ADB network ACL for the runner; set per run and removed at teardown).
- One child bug per finding: `discovered-from:T9.6a`, parent T9.6, blocks T9.6b; producer-repo fixes also get a T0.6/T0.7 pin-refresh child blocking T9.6b.

## Implementation notes
1. Dispatch the tier-C OCI lane per free-enabled version; canonical connection first.
2. Run the W4 matrix via T4.11's tier-C runner against the ADB target env file.
3. Run the subset per variant; never label a subset as a full run.
4. Run the ADB-behaviour cases; an unsupported combination must return the capability matrix's exact typed refusal (a wrong refusal class is a finding).
5. Triage each failure to a repo/symbol; file the finding bug with the sanitized repro and the expected result.

## Test plan
- W4 case ids across all tools (registry-generated), per version.
- Subset: `w9_subset_<variant>_{connect,select,dml_rollback,refusal,cancel,reconnect}` for variants `mtls_sso`, `pem_only`, `walletless_tls`, `iam_token`, `svc_low`, `svc_medium`, `svc_high`, `svc_tp`, `svc_tpurgent`, `sni_tls13`.
- ADB behaviours: `w9_adb_admin_not_sysdba`, `w9_adb_restricted_views`, `w9_adb_restricted_sys_packages`, `w9_adb_top_queries_no_awr`, `w9_adb_idle_disconnect_47`, `w9_adb_session_limits`, `w9_adb_resource_manager_cancel`, `w9_adb_dblink_refused`, `w9_adb_cqn_availability`, `w9_adb_editions`, `w9_adb_vpd`, `w9_adb_masking`, `w9_adb_vector`, `w9_adb_alter_session_restrictions`, `w9_adb_nls_timezone`, `w9_adb_wallet_rotation`.
- JSONL per case `{case_id, version, variant, expected, actual, verdict, timings}`; results pass the T9.1 confidentiality scan before persistence.

## Proof split
Proves the first-run state and produces the finding list. Clean status is proven only by T9.6b; the final release run is R.1.

## Non-goals
- Fixing findings inside this bead (each finding is its own child).
- Paid ADB features or shapes.

## No-claim boundary
A first run with findings filed proves nothing is clean; it proves only what was observed.

## Considerations
- Structure-owner check: walletless TLS on Always-Free requires an ACL. If the runner's egress address cannot be allow-listed within free-tier rules, that variant becomes a finding escalated to the operator (rule 12); it is never silently dropped (R25).
- The IAM variant reuses the existing IAM bootstrap in `oci_adb_terraform.sh`.
- Always-Free limits may cap concurrency; run sequentially.

## Absorbs
None (the capability-sweep scope of `bp8ia.10.2` is absorbed by T9.1 and exercised here).

- [ ] Positive: for every free-enabled ADB version the results record a verdict for every registry-generated W4 case on the canonical mTLS-wallet connection

- [ ] Positive: every listed ADB behaviour has a case with a verdict

title: Validate driver B6 trust union and SNI default on a real ADB endpoint
description:
## Context
From `091-f4`: validate driver B6 (system roots UNION wallet trust) against a real ADB endpoint, the field's failure shape. ADB endpoints present either Oracle's self-signed ADB-CA chain (anchored by the downloaded wallet; the free-tier lane always passed this) or a publicly-signed chain whose root the wallet does not carry (a wallet-only trust store can never verify it). Also verify P2-4 on the same endpoint (SNI default flip; driver `crates/oracledb-protocol/src/tls/sni.rs` `build_sni`). Runs inside the OCI tier-C lane (T9.1). Zero cost (constitution #10): Always-Free resources only. The authoritative zero-cost check (no billable ADB in state AVAILABLE besides the run's own Always-Free one, using a known-non-empty control query in the same OCI CLI invocation because the CLI omits the `data` key on empty lists) runs before and after every run. Confidentiality (constitution #9): no live OCI, tenancy, compartment, region-host, database-name, IP, OCID, wallet or token value enters any committed file, test fixture, log excerpt, bead comment or evidence file. Field issues are cited by GitHub number only. Raw captures live only in gitignored quarantine (`todelete/`, `target/e2e/`).

## Outcome
A stock-config profile with the downloaded wallet connects to a real ADB endpoint, the observed chain kind (wallet-anchored ADB-CA or publicly signed) is recorded, and SNI is sent by default and accepted.

## Deliverable
Repo: oraclemcp (harness cases); evidence from the OCI lane.
- Cases `w9_b6_trust_union_real_adb` and `w9_sni_default_real_adb` in the OCI lane: connect with stock config (wallet + default trust), record the chain kind (issuer class only: `adb_ca` / `public_ca`), SNI on the wire (from driver tracing), verdict.

## Implementation notes
1. Extend the OCI lane subset with the two cases (after T0.7 pins the driver with B6/SNI).
2. Record the chain kind via the driver's TLS trace (issuer class only, never a live DN string).
3. If the endpoint presents only the ADB-CA chain, the publicly-signed path is not exercised live: record that as a finding and escalate to the operator (rule 12); the offline driver test for the public-chain union remains the only proof of that half.

`w9_b6_trust_union_real_adb`, `w9_sni_default_real_adb` (tier C, OCI lane); JSONL `{case_id, version, chain_kind, sni_sent, verdict}`.

## Proof split

- Changing driver trust logic (a failure becomes a finding under T9.6).

title: W12: Agent change requests on Oracle editions (EBR) with operator-only promotion
description:
## Goal
An agent can propose a PL/SQL change on a production database without touching live code (R31, idea 1). The change is built in a new **child edition** (Oracle Edition-Based Redefinition, EBR), verified there **without running unproven code**, and reviewed by a human with its full impact (W14). The **operator** then promotes it with one action. The agent can never promote its own change, and that is a code-enforced rule, not a convention.

**Honest scope.** Promotion is an online cutover **for new sessions** under supported EBR conditions. It does not isolate table data, switch existing sessions, override service-pinned editions, or undo sequence, trigger or autonomous effects. Rollback switches the default back for new sessions only.

## What exists today (measured at `1fbe6eb0`; re-derive line numbers with `rg -n`)
- Per-profile session edition `profiles.session_identity.edition` (`crates/oraclemcp-config/src/profile.rs`), sent at authentication (`crates/oraclemcp-db/src/connection.rs`, `connect_options.with_edition`). The current edition is read from `SYS_CONTEXT('USERENV','CURRENT_EDITION_NAME')` and shown by `doctor`.
- `ALTER SESSION SET EDITION = x` is the only EDITION form the ALTER SESSION allowlist admits (`crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/enforcement.rs`); it invalidates the catalog cache (`CatalogInvalidation::Edition`).
- Lifecycle grammar is exactly `CREATE EDITION c AS CHILD OF p` and `DROP EDITION e [CASCADE]` (`crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/edition_lifecycle.rs`, `parse_edition_lifecycle_sql`); both run through `oracle_execute` at DDL.
- One-child rule: an in-process reservation (`dispatch/mod.rs`) plus an `all_editions` check; a second child is refused (`ReasonCategory::OneChildEdition` / ORA-38807).
- Operator board: `EditionProposal{profile, child_edition, base_edition, objects (1..=64), status: Requested|Reviewing|Withdrawn}` in `crates/oraclemcp-core/src/change_proposal.rs` (file-backed `ChangeProposalStore`), with branch-conflict detection (`active_edition_branch_conflict`); `from_request` rejects zero objects. Merge and rollback (`handle_operator_edition_default_flip` in `crates/oraclemcp-core/src/http/operator.rs`) build `ALTER DATABASE DEFAULT EDITION = X` and send it through **plain `oracle_execute`**, with an ADMIN `oracle_preview_sql` confirmation and an exact `lane_generation`.
- Dashboard edition timeline (`web/src/app/presentation-model.ts`). Live proof `crates/oraclemcp/tests/edition_lifecycle_live_xe.rs` (create child -> second child refused -> drop). `crates/oraclemcp-guard/tests/default_edition_flip_guard.rs` asserts the flip is ADMIN-reachable.

**Gaps found in review (all must be closed):** an agent lane on an ADMIN-capable profile can `preview_sql` + `execute` `ALTER DATABASE DEFAULT EDITION` and **promote its own change**; the editionable check trusts the declared `object_type` string only; there is no editions-enabled check; there is no crossedition or database-trigger handling; a switch into the child would leave the agent's pinned session in the child; `open` can't precede `stage` (zero objects are rejected); proposals are keyed per profile and base-edition name, while ORA-38807 applies per **parent edition** within the DB/PDB edition namespace; there is no journal for database effects (a lost connection after a DDL leaves Oracle and the proposal store disagreeing); already-enabled schema/database DDL triggers can fire during staging and are not inspected.

## Design (each task bead carries its full slice)
1. **Promotion is operator-only, enforced in the guard** (T12.1). `ALTER DATABASE ... DEFAULT EDITION` in any spelling is refused on every agent-reachable path (`oracle_query`, `oracle_execute`, `preview_*`, custom tools, scoped grants) with typed `OPERATOR_ONLY_STATEMENT` at every level. Only a dedicated **operator executor** runs it: operator-authenticated, never registered as an MCP tool, accepts no SQL, renders the fixed template `ALTER DATABASE DEFAULT EDITION = "<ident>"` from a validated identifier taken from a proposal record, classifies with an exact-match `OperatorStatementClass`, and re-enforces `max_level == ADMIN`, protected-profile refusal, exact lane generation, operator authentication, the decisive W14 binding and one-use confirmation. This is tighter, not a classifier bypass: the statement leaves every agent path and the only remaining path takes no free text. `default_edition_flip_guard.rs` is rewritten to assert `OPERATOR_ONLY_STATEMENT` at every level, including ADMIN.
2. **Agent tool `oracle_change_request`** with actions `open | stage | verify | status | submit | withdraw`; no promote, rollback or retire action.
3. **`open`** (T12.2, T12.3, T12.5). Preconditions: profile opt-in `edition_change_requests = true`; `max_level >= DDL`; not `protected`; no other open request on the same parent edition in the same DB/PDB (Oracle's per-parent restriction) and, as an intentional, labelled oraclemcp product policy, at most one open request per PDB (scoped to the service state store by R5B5). `EditionProposal` gains a server-derived stable identity (`DB_UNIQUE_NAME`/DBID plus the PDB GUID or `CON_UID`; a container name alone is not an identity). Probe with two proofs, missing privilege or evidence refusing before any DDL: (1) the owner is editions-enabled (`USER_USERS.EDITIONS_ENABLED` for the connected schema, `DBA_USERS.EDITIONS_ENABLED` for other owners when privileged; unknown or disabled -> typed refusal naming `ALTER USER ... ENABLE EDITIONS`, irreversible operator DDL never run by the server); (2) the exact `(owner, object_type)` pair is editions-enabled per `USER_`/`DBA_EDITIONED_TYPES` (`V$EDITIONABLE_TYPES` only for database capability); columns claimed until verified on 18c, 21c, 23ai and ADB. Two-phase: without `confirm`, a non-effecting preview returns the W14 impact, the exact child/base/database binding and a one-use confirmation; with `confirm`, it revalidates the binding, persists the operation intent, then executes `CREATE EDITION`; no confirmation means zero DDL; retirement (`DROP EDITION`) is two-phase the same way. Effect: records separately the database default, service initial, session and current editions; creates the child only after proving the database default still equals the requested base, through the existing grammar and one-child rule; status `Open`, zero objects allowed. **Durable operation intent** (a journal, not ceremony): `{operation_id, kind, proposal_revision, precondition_digest, expected_postcondition, started_at}` recorded before Oracle is called; states `Prepared | Executing | OutcomeUnknown | Reconciling | Applied | Refused`; `OutcomeUnknown` is never replayed; recovery re-probes identity, parent/default edition, edition existence/usability and object hashes (exact postcondition -> `Applied`; exact precondition -> explicit retry; anything else -> operator reconciliation); crash-injection tests at four points. **State machine**: `Open -> Staged -> Verified -> Reviewing -> Promoted` (settled), rollback path `Promoted -> RolledBack -> ChildRetired`, `Withdrawn`/`Expired`/`Failed` -> `ChildRetired` after reconciliation; each successful stage increments `stage_revision` and invalidates earlier verification/review; a stage from `Reviewing` is CAS-protected and visibly withdraws the old review; every transition uses a `proposal_revision` CAS plus an idempotency key. **TTL** default 7 days -> `Expired`, with a dashboard prompt to retire. Returns `change_request_id`.
4. **`stage`** (T12.4, T12.4a, T12.4b, T12.5). Dedicated staging lane authenticated **directly into the child edition**; the server never runs `ALTER SESSION SET EDITION` on the agent's pinned lane; the lane is destroyed after completion and destroyed or quarantined after cancellation or protocol error; if no separate connection can be opened, staging is refused, no fallback. `CREATE OR REPLACE` through the existing `create_or_replace`/`patch_source` paths with their preview -> token ladder at DDL. Refused in staged source: `NONEDITIONABLE`; `CROSSEDITION` triggers; `ON DATABASE`/`ON SCHEMA` triggers; tables, indexes and any data change. Copy-on-change-aware dictionary checks before and after stage (`*_OBJECTS_AE`; identical content -> `NoChange`; an object that became non-editioned fails the stage; `not_editionable_error` still covers TABLE). Pre-existing DDL triggers via the shared `DdlEffectClosureV1` (T7.9b) before every W12 CREATE, ALTER/COMPILE or DROP incl. `open` and retirement (readable source, exact identity, VALID, W7-Clean closure admitted only through the shared `RoutineEffectsV1` function with nothing beyond `ReadDb`/`SessionState`; bound into the W14 decisive binding and rechecked before execution; missing privilege = Unknown = refuse; `ALTER DATABASE DEFAULT EDITION` excluded only because Oracle documents that `ALTER DATABASE` does not fire ALTER DDL triggers). `CompileParseEffectClosureV1` for embedded static SQL (VPD/OLS/RAS/Redaction policy functions, extensible-optimizer and domain-index callbacks, types and operators) before any `CREATE OR REPLACE` or `ALTER ... COMPILE`, also applied to custom-tool DDL and the source tools. Anti-bypass on opted-in profiles: no agent `ALTER SESSION SET EDITION` or editionable DDL outside a staging context.
5. **`verify`** (T12.6). Fresh verification lane into the child; compile every child-actual object; `oracle_plsql_sast`; W14 impact base vs child (transitive dependents, predicted invalidations, W7 effect set incl. effect changes). Production verification is static plus READ_ONLY check queries through the W1 proof; it never executes a staged routine. Executable tests only on a designated verification profile or under an operator-approved manifest whose closure W7 proves rollback-safe; utPLSQL presence grants nothing. Manifests: the complete actual-object manifest from `DBA_OBJECTS_AE` in the exact container (`OWNER`, `NAMESPACE`, `OBJECT_TYPE`, `OBJECT_NAME`, `EDITION_NAME`, `STATUS`, `ORACLE_MAINTAINED`) + `DBA_ERRORS_AE` (`ALL_OBJECTS_AE` not accepted; otherwise `MANIFEST_INCOMPLETE`), and the requested changed-object manifest, both hashed per `EditionObjectKindV1` (closed allowlist: PL/SQL units and triggers = ordered `ALL_SOURCE` + compiler settings; views = canonical text, columns, editioning/read-only/check-option; private synonyms = resolved target tuple; types = spec + body + no non-editioned table dependents; `LIBRARY` and `SQL TRANSLATION PROFILE` refused).
6. **`submit` / `withdraw`** (T12.7).
7. **Operator promote** (T12.7, dashboard / operator API only). SEC-1 CAS preconditions (DB/PDB identity; actual default == base; direct parentage; `USE`/`PUBLIC` exposure; service-pinned editions; both manifests equal the verified ones; every object `VALID`; `verification_revision == stage_revision`), extended by R5B2's effective-edition closure; explicit acknowledgement that promotion makes the edition usable by `PUBLIC` and affects new sessions only; runs through the operator executor with ADMIN confirmation and exact `lane_generation`; reports new-sessions-only, re-leases the server's own sessions, `V$SESSION` edition usage and service edition attributes where privileged (else `unavailable`); rollback through the executor; retire `DROP EDITION ... CASCADE` after the operator's retention decision (ORA-38805 typed refusal).
8. **Audit** (T12.8): every step a hash-chained audit entry with the manifest and verification-bundle digest; the W3 session report renders a change request as one story.

**W14 decisive-field row for W12 promotion** (matrix owned by T14.6b; every field must be `computed`, or the confirmation refuses): the complete `DBA_OBJECTS_AE` manifest + changed manifest; DB/PDB identity; default == base; parentage; USE/PUBLIC exposure; service editions; `DdlEffectClosureV1` (for create/drop). For W12 promotion an `unavailable` or `truncated` decisive field always refuses, regardless of configuration.

## Invariants
- The agent can never promote (guard-enforced).
- Promotion needs ADMIN confirmation through the operator executor.
- Every staged statement is still classified at the current level.
- `protected` profiles are refused.
- Non-editionable, crossedition and database-trigger objects are refused.
- Oracle's one-child rule holds per parent edition; the separate oraclemcp policy allows at most one open request per PDB.
- Promote is refused on any drift after verify.
- Verify never executes non-ReadOnly code.

## Tests (workstream)
W4 fixture; live on XE 18/21, FREE 23ai and ADB (ADB EBR support is claimed until W9 proves it): the lifecycle open -> stage -> verify -> submit -> promote -> rollback -> retire with a revision-CAS conflict test and an idempotent-retry test; metamorphic (promote + rollback leaves the base edition's source manifest byte-identical; the only claim); differential (objects flagged "will be invalid" are exactly those observed invalid immediately after stage/compile in the child); the full negative list carried by T12.9; audit-chain verification; dashboard e2e review -> promote -> rollback.

## Acceptance (workstream, definition of done item 8)
A change request completes the full lifecycle on XE, FREE 23ai and ADB (where ADB EBR is proven); promote + rollback is identity-preserving on the base source manifest; tokens are refused after impact drift.

## Size and dependencies
Size L. Depends on W7 step 1 (effect set, T7.5), W7 step 5 (engine-backed effects, T7.9) and the DDL-trigger collector (T7.9b); W14 binding + collectors (T14.3, T14.4, T14.6a, T14.6b); W1 task 1 (read proof, T1.1/T1.2b); W2 T2.2 (statement outcome / lane recovery for the dedicated lanes). Every W12 bead carries `sec` (second-agent review before the batch verify).

## Children
T12.1, T12.2, T12.3, T12.4, T12.4a, T12.4b, T12.5, T12.6, T12.7, T12.8, T12.9, T12.10; round-5 bug beads R5B2 (`EffectiveEditionClosureV1`, blocks T12.7), R5B4 (operator-only browser route, blocks T12.10), R5B5 (per-PDB policy scoped to the service state store, blocks T12.2).

title: Make ALTER DATABASE DEFAULT EDITION operator-only; add the operator edition executor
description:
## Context
Fail-open gap: `ALTER DATABASE DEFAULT EDITION` is an ordinary ADMIN statement today, so an agent lane on an ADMIN-capable profile can `oracle_preview_sql` + `oracle_execute` it and **promote its own change**. `crates/oraclemcp-guard/tests/default_edition_flip_guard.rs` asserts it is ADMIN-reachable (step-up to ADMIN). The operator merge/rollback route `handle_operator_edition_default_flip` (`crates/oraclemcp-core/src/http/operator.rs`, around lines 1848-2050 at `1fbe6eb0`) builds `format!("ALTER DATABASE DEFAULT EDITION = {target_edition}")` (unquoted) and dispatches it through plain `oracle_execute` with an ADMIN `oracle_preview_sql` confirmation and an exact `lane_generation`; its refusal text tells the caller to "obtain an oracle_preview_sql confirmation".

Design (plan section 14, design item 1; R31):
- `ALTER DATABASE ... DEFAULT EDITION`, in any spelling, is refused on **every agent-reachable path** (`oracle_query`, `oracle_execute`, `oracle_preview_sql`, `oracle_preview_dml`, custom tools, scoped grants) with typed `OPERATOR_ONLY_STATEMENT`, whatever the level, including ADMIN.
- Only a dedicated **operator executor** can run it: operator-authenticated, never registered as an MCP tool, used by the merge/rollback routes, which stop calling `oracle_execute`.
- The executor **re-enforces** the controls it used to inherit from `oracle_execute`: `max_level == ADMIN`, protected-profile refusal, exact lane generation, operator authentication, the decisive W14 binding (wired by T12.7) and one-use confirmation. Exact SQL rendering alone replaces none of them.
- The executor **accepts no SQL**: it renders one fixed template `ALTER DATABASE DEFAULT EDITION = "<ident>"` from a validated edition identifier taken from a proposal record, classifies the result with a dedicated exact-match `OperatorStatementClass`, and refuses anything else.
- Why this is tighter, not a classifier bypass (AGENTS.md): the statement leaves every agent path, and the only remaining path takes no free text.

This bead touches the fail-closed guard (`sec` label): it needs a second-agent review before the batch verify. Invariants that must hold (AGENTS.md "safety invariant"): never bypass the classifier, never let elevation exceed a profile's `max_level`, never make a `protected` profile writable, never auto-commit DML, never admit a statement the classifier cannot prove safe for the active level. Line numbers are hints as of `1fbe6eb0` (oraclemcp) / `cdc3e82` (rust-oracledb `origin/main`); re-derive every one with `rg -n` before editing. Symbol names are the stable reference.

## Outcome
No agent-reachable path can run, or mint a confirmation for, a default-edition flip at any level; the operator merge and rollback routes flip the default edition only through the operator executor, which renders a fixed template from a proposal record and itself enforces the ADMIN ceiling, protected refusal, lane generation, operator authentication and one-use confirmation.

## Deliverable
Repo: oraclemcp.
- `crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/classifier.rs`: recognize the default-edition flip in any spelling (case, whitespace/newlines, comments between tokens, optional database name `ALTER DATABASE <name> DEFAULT EDITION`, quoted identifiers, trailing `;`, and `ALTER PLUGGABLE DATABASE ... DEFAULT EDITION`) -> a decision carrying `OPERATOR_ONLY_STATEMENT` that no `OperatingLevel` satisfies.
- `crates/oraclemcp-error/src/lib.rs`: `ReasonCategory::OperatorOnlyStatement` (wire `OPERATOR_ONLY_STATEMENT`).
- New `crates/oraclemcp-core/src/edition_executor.rs` (new domain): `OperatorEditionExecutor` with `preview(&OperatorAuth, &EditionProposal, EditionFlipTarget) -> OperatorConfirmation` and `apply(&OperatorAuth, OperatorConfirmation, lane_generation) -> Result<EditionFlipOutcome, _>`; `ValidatedEditionIdent` (reuses `normalize_edition_identifier` from `change_proposal.rs`; rejects `"` and NUL; at most 128 bytes); `OperatorStatementClass::DefaultEditionFlip` exact-match check of the rendered text.
- `crates/oraclemcp-core/src/http/operator.rs`: `handle_operator_edition_default_flip` routes merge/rollback through the executor (its preview step mints the executor's one-use confirmation, bound to proposal id, target edition, lane generation and operator subject); no `oracle_execute` call remains on this route; refusal text updated.
- `web/src/app/operator-client.ts`: the dashboard's merge/rollback flow uses the operator preview step instead of `oracle_preview_sql`, so the existing flow keeps working (the dedicated browser-route hardening is R5B4/T12.10).
- `crates/oraclemcp-guard/tests/default_edition_flip_guard.rs` rewritten to assert `OPERATOR_ONLY_STATEMENT` at every level including ADMIN, and for protected and read-only-standby profiles.

## Implementation notes
1. Guard: add the recognizer ahead of level gating so no level (ADMIN included) admits it; preview paths return the same typed refusal and mint no token.
2. Dynamic form: an anonymous block with `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'ALTER DATABASE DEFAULT EDITION = x'` must stay refused (dynamic SQL is already unprovable); add it to the corpus.
3. Custom tools (`crates/oraclemcp-core/src/custom_tools.rs`, `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/custom_tool.rs`) inherit the classifier decision; add a test. Scoped grants (W13, not yet built) consume the same decision: T13.0/T13.5 are listed as consumers and must not admit it.
4. Executor: load the proposal by id; require profile `max_level == ADMIN` and not protected; require operator authentication (existing operator auth, `dashboard_auth.rs` / `admin_auth.rs`); render the template; assert the `OperatorStatementClass` exact match; check the lane generation; consume the one-use confirmation; execute on the operator's bound lane; audit. The W14 decisive binding is added by T12.7 (it depends on T14.6b).
5. Registry test: no MCP tool name resolves to the executor.

## Test plan
- Guard (unit): `default_edition_flip_is_operator_only_at_every_level` (rewritten file), `default_edition_flip_spelling_corpus_refused` (lower case, newlines, `/*c*/` between tokens, `-- c` line comment, quoted identifier, database name, `ALTER PLUGGABLE DATABASE DEFAULT EDITION = x`, trailing `;`), `default_edition_flip_in_execute_immediate_refused`, `alter_database_open_classification_unchanged` (regression).
- Dispatcher (unit, in-process): `preview_sql_default_edition_flip_operator_only_no_token`, `execute_default_edition_flip_operator_only_at_admin_zero_db_io`, `custom_tool_default_edition_flip_refused`.
- Executor (unit): `executor_refuses_max_level_below_admin`, `executor_refuses_protected_profile`, `executor_refuses_lane_generation_mismatch`, `executor_refuses_unauthenticated`, `executor_confirmation_is_one_use`, `executor_rejects_identifier_with_quote_or_nul`, `executor_rendered_sql_is_exact_template`, `operator_statement_class_rejects_any_other_text`, `operator_executor_not_registered_as_mcp_tool`.
- Operator route (`crates/oraclemcp-core/src/http/tests_operator.rs`): `edition_merge_and_rollback_use_executor_not_oracle_execute`.
- Live in-process (XE 21, `crates/oraclemcp/tests/edition_lifecycle_live_xe.rs`): `operator_executor_flips_default_edition_and_back_live_xe`. The external-client ADMIN-agent negative is `w4_oracle_change_request_agent_default_edition_flip_refused` in T12.9.

## Proof split
Proves the guard refusal on every agent path (unit / in-process) and the executor's own controls. The external-client live negative with an ADMIN agent lane is T12.9; the W14 decisive binding at promote is T12.7.

## Non-goals
- Change-request state, proposal identity or the new tool (T12.2, T12.5).
- The dedicated browser-route hardening (R5B4) and dashboard e2e (T12.10).
- The W14 decisive binding on the executor (T12.7).

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove promotion preconditions (manifests, parentage, drift) are checked; that is T12.7.

## Considerations
- Hot file lane `classifier` (shared with W1 and W7 steps 1-5): take the reservation; keep the change to the recognizer and its tests.
- Rule 17: the new `ReasonCategory` variant and every exhaustive match land in one commit.
- Structure-owner check: refusing `ALTER PLUGGABLE DATABASE ... DEFAULT EDITION` as well is a tightening this bead adds under "any spelling".
- The operator preview/confirmation replaces the `oracle_preview_sql` confirmation this route used; this is not a weakening, because the executor re-enforces every control and takes no free text.

## Absorbs
None.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: the operator merge/rollback routes flip the database default edition through the operator executor and never invoke `oracle_execute`
- [ ] Positive: the executor renders exactly `ALTER DATABASE DEFAULT EDITION = "<ident>"` from the proposal record
- [ ] Negative: an agent lane at ADMIN on an ADMIN-capable profile gets `OPERATOR_ONLY_STATEMENT` from `oracle_preview_sql` and `oracle_execute` for every spelling in the corpus, no confirmation token is minted, and zero statements reach the database
- [ ] Negative: the executor refuses a protected profile, a `max_level` below ADMIN, a lane-generation mismatch, an unauthenticated caller and a reused confirmation
- [ ] Tests: tests listed in the Test plan (tier A) + `operator_executor_flips_default_edition_and_back_live_xe`
- [ ] Proof class: unit + live in-process (XE 21); forbidden substitutes: asserting on the old ADMIN step-up behaviour
- [ ] Consumers: T12.4, T12.7, T12.9, T12.10, T13.0, T13.5
- [ ] No-claim: does not prove promotion preconditions or the dashboard flow

title: Change-request audit entries and session-report story
description:
## Context
Plan section 14, design item 8: every change-request step is a hash-chained audit entry (`oraclemcp-audit`) carrying the manifest and verification-bundle digests. The W3 session report (`oraclemcp audit report`, T3.7) renders a change request as one story. Raw bind values and credentials never enter audit or report output.

This bead touches the fail-closed guard (`sec` label): it needs a second-agent review before the batch verify. Invariants that must hold (AGENTS.md "safety invariant"): never bypass the classifier, never let elevation exceed a profile's `max_level`, never make a `protected` profile writable, never auto-commit DML, never admit a statement the classifier cannot prove safe for the active level.

## Outcome
Each change-request step (open preview/apply, every stage, verify, submit, withdraw, promote, rollback, retire, expiry, reconciliation) produces a hash-chained audit entry with the relevant manifest/bundle digests and journal state, and `oraclemcp audit report` renders the whole request as one ordered story.

## Deliverable
Repo: oraclemcp.
- Audit event kinds for change-request steps in `crates/oraclemcp-audit` with fields `{change_request_id, state_from, state_to, proposal_revision, stage_revision, operation_id, journal_state, actual_manifest_digest, changed_manifest_digest, bundle_digest, decisive_digest, actor: agent|operator}`.
- A session-report section (in T3.7's report) grouping entries by `change_request_id`.

## Implementation notes
1. Emit audit entries from each transition and executor action (one emit point per transition).
2. Report: order by audit sequence; show the journal `OutcomeUnknown`/reconciliation path explicitly.
3. Digests only: no source text, bind values or credentials.

## Test plan
- `w12_audit_chain_verifies_across_full_lifecycle` (live in-process, FREE 23ai; chain checked with `oraclemcp-verifier`), `w12_audit_entry_carries_manifest_and_bundle_digests`, `w12_session_report_renders_change_request_story` (golden with volatile fields scrubbed), `w12_audit_records_outcome_unknown_and_reconciliation`, `w12_report_contains_no_bind_or_credential_canary`.

## Proof split
Proves audit and report content. The external lifecycle is T12.9.

## Non-goals
- The report framework itself (T3.7).

## No-claim boundary
Audit completeness does not prove the underlying actions were safe.

## Considerations
- File lane `audit`.

## Absorbs
None.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: a full lifecycle on FREE 23ai produces one audit entry per step, the chain verifies, and `oraclemcp audit report` renders the request as one ordered story
- [ ] Negative: a planted bind/credential canary never appears in audit entries or the report
- [ ] Tests: `w12_audit_chain_verifies_across_full_lifecycle`, `w12_audit_entry_carries_manifest_and_bundle_digests`, `w12_session_report_renders_change_request_story`, `w12_audit_records_outcome_unknown_and_reconciliation`, `w12_report_contains_no_bind_or_credential_canary` (tier A)
- [ ] Proof class: live in-process + golden; forbidden substitutes: hand-written audit fixtures for the chain claim
- [ ] Consumers: T12.9, R.1
- [ ] No-claim: does not prove action safety

title: W12 live suite via external MCP client: lifecycle, metamorphic, differential, negatives
description:
## Context
W4 requires every canonical tool (36, including `oracle_change_request`) to be proven through an **external** MCP client: the real release-profile binary over stdio and Streamable HTTP, with no in-process dispatcher. This bead adds the W12 cases to the T4.2 tool-matrix driver on the T4.3 run-id-stamped fixture schema, live on XE 18, XE 21 and FREE 23ai; ADB runs them inside T9.6a (ADB EBR support is claimed until then). Operator steps (promote/rollback/retire) are driven through the operator HTTP API as an authenticated operator.

Plan section 14 tests carried here:
- **Lifecycle:** open -> stage -> verify -> submit -> promote -> rollback -> retire, with a revision-CAS conflict test and an idempotent-retry test.
- **Metamorphic:** promote + rollback leaves the base edition's **source manifest** byte-identical (the only claim; sessions, audit state, timestamps and database data are not asserted identical).
- **Differential:** objects flagged "will be invalid" are exactly the invalid objects observed immediately after stage/compile in the child (where copy-on-change invalidates them). Promotion tests cover only the default-edition switch, new-session routing, service-pinned exceptions and session re-leasing.
- **Negatives:** an ADMIN agent lane `preview_sql` + `execute` of `ALTER DATABASE DEFAULT EDITION` -> `OPERATOR_ONLY_STATEMENT`, no database I/O; source tampered after verify -> promote refused; an extra object created in the child after verify -> promote refused; owner not editions-enabled -> typed refusal; an object actualized under an owner not visible through `ALL_OBJECTS_AE` -> verify/promote refuse (`MANIFEST_INCOMPLETE`); a pre-existing autonomous `AFTER CREATE OR ALTER ON SCHEMA` trigger -> stage/compile refuses before any DDL and its audit table is unchanged; DDL-trigger drift after preview -> apply refused; `open` without confirmation creates no edition; `CREATE EDITION` with an autonomous database DDL trigger is refused before any DDL; one stage/drift case per admitted object kind; identical inherited source -> `NoChange`; an unsupported editioned kind (`LIBRARY`, `SQL TRANSLATION PROFILE`) -> typed refusal; schema enabled but the requested object type omitted -> refusal before DDL; an inherited base object passes the precheck and actualizes only after a change; crash injection at each of the four journal points -> correct `Applied`/retry/reconciliation outcome, with no replayed DDL; staging into a second schema whose owner is not editions-enabled -> refused; `NONEDITIONABLE` / `CROSSEDITION` / `ON DATABASE` trigger staged -> refused, and the base edition's source hashes and trigger firing are unchanged; a staged `PRAGMA AUTONOMOUS_TRANSACTION` routine that inserts and commits, then `verify` -> not executed, base table row count unchanged; a second concurrent change request on the same parent edition (Oracle's rule) or the same PDB (oraclemcp policy) from another profile -> refused with the reason naming which rule applied; staging a table -> refused; `ALTER SESSION SET EDITION` from the agent on an opted-in profile -> refused; `protected` profile -> refused; the agent's pinned session edition unchanged after stage and verify; the VPD autonomous-canary source -> stage and verify refuse, canary unchanged.

This bead touches the fail-closed guard (`sec` label): it needs a second-agent review before the batch verify. Invariants that must hold (AGENTS.md "safety invariant"): never bypass the classifier, never let elevation exceed a profile's `max_level`, never make a `protected` profile writable, never auto-commit DML, never admit a statement the classifier cannot prove safe for the active level.

## Outcome
The W12 case set runs green through the external client on XE 18, XE 21 and FREE 23ai (FREE 23ai in tier A), every case deterministic (exact rows/errors/ORA codes, a verified audit chain, an independent re-read after every mutation) and logged as JSONL.

## Deliverable
Repo: oraclemcp.
- W12 case definitions in the T4.2 generator input (ids `w4_oracle_change_request_<case>`) and fixture additions in T4.3's schema builder: an editions-enabled owner, a second owner not enabled, an owner enabled only `FOR PROCEDURE`, a VPD autonomous-canary table, an autonomous schema DDL trigger fixture (created and dropped per run), inherited base objects of every admitted kind.
- Crash-injection cases run against a test binary built with the `test-failpoints` feature (T12.2), launched by the external client exactly like the release binary; a release-artifact check asserts the feature is off in shipped builds.

## Implementation notes
1. Extend the fixture per run id; teardown drops every created edition (leaf first) and object.
2. Drive agent steps over stdio and Streamable HTTP; drive operator steps via the operator HTTP API.
3. After every mutation, independently re-read `ALL_EDITIONS`, `DATABASE_PROPERTIES`, `DBA_OBJECTS_AE`, source hashes and canary row counts.
4. Metamorphic: capture the base source manifest before `open` and after rollback; compare bytes.
5. Differential: compare T12.6's predicted-invalid set with `DBA_OBJECTS_AE` STATUS immediately after stage/compile.

## Test plan
Case ids (each `w4_oracle_change_request_*`): `lifecycle_full`, `revision_cas_conflict`, `idempotent_retry`, `metamorphic_base_manifest_identity`, `differential_predicted_invalid`, `agent_default_edition_flip_refused`, `promote_source_tampered_refused`, `promote_extra_object_refused`, `owner_not_enabled_refused`, `manifest_incomplete_invisible_owner`, `autonomous_schema_ddl_trigger_refused`, `ddl_trigger_drift_refused`, `open_without_confirm_no_edition`, `create_edition_autonomous_db_trigger_refused`, `stage_kind_{function,package,procedure,private_synonym,trigger,type,view}`, `identical_inherited_nochange`, `unsupported_kind_library_refused`, `unsupported_kind_sql_translation_profile_refused`, `type_omitted_refused`, `inherited_actualizes_after_change`, `crash_{after_intent,after_oracle_success,after_response,before_final_state}`, `second_schema_owner_not_enabled_refused`, `noneditionable_refused`, `crossedition_refused`, `on_database_trigger_refused`, `verify_autonomous_not_executed`, `concurrent_same_parent_refused`, `concurrent_same_pdb_refused`, `stage_table_refused`, `agent_alter_session_edition_refused`, `protected_profile_refused`, `pinned_edition_unchanged`, `vpd_autonomous_canary_refused`. JSONL per case `{case_id, target, transport, expected, actual, verdict, timings}`.

## Proof split
Proves W12 through the public surface on lab databases. ADB proof is T9.6a; dashboard proof is T12.10.

## Non-goals
- New W12 behaviour (a red case becomes a bug on the owning bead).

## No-claim boundary
Green on XE/FREE does not prove ADB EBR behaviour.

## Considerations
- `ON DATABASE` trigger fixtures need a privileged lab account; lab-only.
- Structure-owner check: live crash injection uses the `test-failpoints` build rather than the release binary.
- File lane `w4-cases`.

## Absorbs
None.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: every `w4_oracle_change_request_*` case listed in the Test plan is green through the external client over stdio and Streamable HTTP on XE 18, XE 21 and FREE 23ai
- [ ] Positive: promote + rollback leaves the base edition's source manifest byte-identical
- [ ] Negative: an ADMIN agent lane gets `OPERATOR_ONLY_STATEMENT` for `ALTER DATABASE DEFAULT EDITION` via `preview_sql` and `execute`, and `V$SQL` has no matching statement
- [ ] Negative: the predicted-invalid set equals the observed invalid set after stage on the fixture
- [ ] Tests: all `w4_oracle_change_request_*` ids (FREE 23ai tier A; XE 18/21 tier C)
- [ ] Proof class: live external client; forbidden substitutes: in-process `Dispatcher::new`, mock DB
- [ ] Consumers: T4.14, T9.6a
- [ ] No-claim: does not prove ADB behaviour or the dashboard flow

title: Dashboard e2e: change-request review, promote and rollback
description:
## Context
The operator reviews and promotes change requests in the dashboard (Change Review; edition timeline in `web/src/app/presentation-model.ts`; operator client `web/src/app/operator-client.ts`; existing Playwright specs in `web/e2e/`). Round-5 Medium **R5B4** (a dedicated operator-only browser route for promote/rollback, instead of turning on broad SQL-workbench DDL) blocks this bead. Use `/e2e-testing-for-webapps`.

This bead touches the fail-closed guard (`sec` label): it needs a second-agent review before the batch verify. Invariants that must hold (AGENTS.md "safety invariant"): never bypass the classifier, never let elevation exceed a profile's `max_level`, never make a `protected` profile writable, never auto-commit DML, never admit a statement the classifier cannot prove safe for the active level.

## Outcome
An operator can open a submitted change request in the dashboard, see the W14 impact, manifests and verification bundle, acknowledge the PUBLIC / new-sessions-only notice, promote and roll back, proven end to end in a browser against a served binary and a live database.

## Deliverable
Repo: oraclemcp (web).
- Change Review view for change requests: the T12.2 states, impact fields with their statuses, manifests, the verification bundle, a PUBLIC acknowledgement control (promote disabled until checked), promote/rollback actions on the R5B4 route, the re-verify refusal display, and the TTL-expired prompt to retire.
- `presentation-model.ts` edition timeline mapped to the new states.
- Playwright spec `web/e2e/change-request-review.spec.ts` against a live served binary + FREE 23ai (pattern of `live-serve-browser.spec.ts`).

## Implementation notes
1. Seed a submitted change request via the external client (T12.9 fixture helpers).
2. Drive the browser: review -> acknowledge -> promote -> check the default edition with an independent query -> rollback -> check again.
3. Negative flows: promote disabled without acknowledgement; drift after verify shows `REVERIFY_REQUIRED`; an agent-lane credential cannot call the route.

## Test plan
`change_request_review_promote_rollback_e2e`, `change_request_promote_disabled_without_ack_e2e`, `change_request_drift_shows_reverify_e2e`, `change_request_expired_prompts_retire_e2e`, `change_request_route_refuses_agent_credential_e2e`; component tests in `web/src/app/*.test.tsx` for the timeline states.

## Proof split
Proves the operator UI flow. Server-side promote safety is T12.7; the external agent surface is T12.9.

## Non-goals
- The route itself (R5B4).

## No-claim boundary
UI green does not prove server-side precondition checks beyond what the flows exercise.

## Considerations
- File lane `web`.

## Absorbs
None.

title: EffectiveEditionClosureV1: bind inherited objects + non-editioned deps at promotion
description:
## Context
Plan review round 5 finding (High — W12 promotion does not bind the complete effective child-edition state). Owning tasks: T12.7. The text below is the reviewer's analysis, evidence and required change. The change is binding for this bead.

**Problem.** Promotion binds the child’s actual objects from `DBA_OBJECTS_AE` and the requested-change manifest. That does not constitute the effective namespace seen from the child edition.

   **Analysis.** EBR distinguishes actual objects from inherited objects. `*_OBJECTS_AE` enumerates actual objects across editions; `*_OBJECTS` in a child-edition session describes what is effectively visible, including inherited objects. `NoChange` deliberately leaves an object inherited. Noneditioned dependencies—tables, policies, privileges, sequences and similar shared objects—can also drift without appearing as child actual objects.

   W14 has generic dependency language, but the action-specific W12 decisive matrix lists only the actual and changed manifests. Promotion therefore needs an explicit effective-resolution/dependency manifest, not an inference from generic prose.

   **Evidence.** The plan recognizes inherited objects at [PLAN_0_12_0.md:709](/home/durakovic/projects/oraclemcp/docs/plan/PLAN_0_12_0.md:709), but defines only actual/changed manifests at [PLAN_0_12_0.md:727](/home/durakovic/projects/oraclemcp/docs/plan/PLAN_0_12_0.md:727) and rechecks those at [PLAN_0_12_0.md:749](/home/durakovic/projects/oraclemcp/docs/plan/PLAN_0_12_0.md:749). Oracle’s [EBR documentation](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/21/adfns/editions.html) distinguishes inherited, actual, and effectively visible objects.

   ```diff
   @@ W12 verify manifests
   - There are two manifests:
   + There are three decisive manifests:
     - the complete child actual-object inventory from DBA_OBJECTS_AE, used to
       detect unexpected actualizations;
     - the requested changed-object manifest;
   + - EffectiveEditionClosureV1, built through a connection authenticated into
   +   the child edition. For every requested object and transitive dependency it
   +   records the effective visible identity, actual-provider edition, canonical
   +   content hash, synonym target, status, compiler/AUTHID facts, and all
   +   relevant noneditioned dependency/policy/privilege fingerprints.
   + NoChange objects remain present in the effective closure even though they
   + have no child actual row.
   @@ W12 promotion
   + Re-resolve and compare all three manifests. Drift in an inherited object,
   + its actual-provider edition, or any noneditioned dependency requires re-verify.
   @@ Tests
   + - alter an inherited/NoChange object or noneditioned dependency after verify;
   +   promotion refuses;
   + - repoint an inherited private synonym after verify; promotion refuses.
   ```

## Outcome
The design change described above is implemented, with the tests listed in it, before the owning task(s) can close.

## Non-goals
No scope beyond the finding. Other hardening goes through its own bead.

## No-claim boundary
A green result proves only the finding's stated property.

## Governance
Filed from plan review round 5 under the R34 freeze rule: a release-blocking design bug, fixed during implementation in the owning workstream. Real code + real tests in the same bead; closure only through `scripts/bead_tracker_guard.sh close` with committed evidence; never weaken the fail-closed guard.

title: Scope the one-request-per-PDB policy to the service state store
description:
## Context
Plan review round 5 finding (Medium — “One open request per PDB” is stated as global but only local state is designed). Owning tasks: T12.2. The text below is the reviewer's analysis, evidence and required change. The change is binding for this bead.

**Problem.** Stable DB/PDB identity allows local comparison, but neither the current file-backed proposal store nor the planned journal coordinates independent oraclemcp deployments with different state directories.

   **Analysis.** Oracle globally enforces one child per parent, but the additional one-open-request-per-PDB policy is an oraclemcp rule. Without database-backed or shared transactional coordination, it can only be promised per service state store.

   **Evidence.** The current store is local `FileStore`: [change_proposal.rs:41](/home/durakovic/projects/oraclemcp/crates/oraclemcp-core/src/change_proposal.rs:41). Current edition reservation is process-local and keyed by profile and parent: [dispatch/mod.rs:6987](/home/durakovic/projects/oraclemcp/crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/mod.rs:6987). The unqualified PDB-wide claim is at [PLAN_0_12_0.md:667](/home/durakovic/projects/oraclemcp/docs/plan/PLAN_0_12_0.md:667).

   ```diff
   @@ W12 open preconditions
   - oraclemcp additionally allows at most one open change request per PDB.
   + One oraclemcp service state store allows at most one open change request for
   + a stable DBID/CON_UID. This is a local control-plane policy, not a
   + cross-deployment database invariant. Oracle's per-parent one-child rule
   + remains the global authority.
   + A deployment claiming PDB-global exclusivity must configure a shared,
   + transactional coordination backend; absent that capability, diagnostics
   + report `coordination_scope = service_state_store`.
   @@ Tests
   + - two profiles in one service serialize on DBID/CON_UID;
   + - two independent services do not claim shared-state exclusivity, while a
   +   same-parent CREATE race is reconciled against Oracle's authoritative state.
   ```

## Outcome
The design change described above is implemented, with the tests listed in it, before the owning task(s) can close.

title: Change-request state machine, operation journal, DB/PDB identity, TTL, opt-in config
description:
## Context
Today `EditionProposal` (`crates/oraclemcp-core/src/change_proposal.rs`, file-backed `ChangeProposalStore` on `FileStore`) has `status: Requested|Reviewing|Withdrawn`, objects 1..=64 (`from_request` rejects zero), and is keyed per profile + base-edition name. Oracle's one-child restriction (ORA-38807) applies per **parent edition** within the database/PDB edition namespace. There is no journal: a lost connection after a DDL leaves Oracle and the store disagreeing. `crates/oraclemcp-core/src/write_intent.rs` already implements a durable append + fsync intent log on `FileStore` for permanent effects (the pattern to reuse). `StatementOutcome` (T2.2a seam) classifies confirmed vs unknown statement outcomes.

Design (plan section 14, design item 3):
- **State machine** replacing `Requested|Reviewing|Withdrawn`: main path `Open -> Staged -> Verified -> Reviewing -> Promoted` (`Promoted` is a valid settled state); optional rollback path `Promoted -> RolledBack -> ChildRetired`; `Withdrawn`, `Expired` and `Failed` may move to `ChildRetired` after reconciliation. `stage` may run repeatedly: every successful stage increments `stage_revision`, moves the request to `Staged` and invalidates any earlier verification or review bundle; a stage from `Reviewing` is CAS-protected and visibly withdraws the old review. Every transition uses a `proposal_revision` compare-and-swap plus an idempotency key. `Open` allows zero objects.
- **Durable operation intent** (a journal, not ceremony: it is the only way to recover from unknown DDL outcomes): every effectful transition durably records `{operation_id, kind, proposal_revision, precondition_digest, expected_postcondition, started_at}` **before** Oracle is called. States `Prepared | Executing | OutcomeUnknown | Reconciling | Applied | Refused`. A protocol loss or cancellation after dispatch records `OutcomeUnknown` and is **never replayed**. Recovery re-probes the exact DB/PDB identity, the parent/default edition, whether the edition exists and is usable, and the object hashes: exact expected postcondition -> `Applied`; exact precondition -> explicit retry allowed; anything else -> operator reconciliation required. Crash-injection tests cover a failure after the intent is persisted, after Oracle succeeds, after the response is received, and before the final state is persisted.
- **Identity**: server-derived stable `DB_UNIQUE_NAME`/DBID plus the PDB GUID or `CON_UID`; a container name alone is not an identity.
- **Concurrency rules**: no other open request on the same parent edition in the same DB/PDB (Oracle's rule); at most one open request per PDB (intentional oraclemcp product policy, labelled as such; R5B5 scopes it to the service state store).
- **TTL**: default 7 days; an expired request moves to `Expired`, and the dashboard prompts the operator to retire its edition, so an abandoned request can't block the DBA's own EBR work.
- **Config**: `edition_change_requests` (default `false`) in `crates/oraclemcp-config/src/profile.rs` + `config_docs.rs`.

This bead touches the fail-closed guard (`sec` label): it needs a second-agent review before the batch verify. Invariants that must hold (AGENTS.md "safety invariant"): never bypass the classifier, never let elevation exceed a profile's `max_level`, never make a `protected` profile writable, never auto-commit DML, never admit a statement the classifier cannot prove safe for the active level.

## Outcome
Change requests are persisted with the full state machine, revision CAS and idempotency; every effectful transition is journaled before Oracle is called and recovers deterministically after a crash without replaying unknown DDL; requests carry a proven DB/PDB identity and a TTL; profiles opt in explicitly.

## Deliverable
Repo: oraclemcp.
- `crates/oraclemcp-core/src/change_proposal.rs`: `ChangeRequestState { Open, Staged, Verified, Reviewing, Promoted, RolledBack, Withdrawn, Expired, Failed, ChildRetired }` with a single transition-table function; `stage_revision`, `verification_revision`, `proposal_revision`; `DatabaseIdentity { db_unique_name, dbid, container_uid }`; `parent_edition`; `expires_at`; zero objects allowed in `Open`; schema-version bump with a one-time load migration (`Requested -> Open`, `Reviewing -> Open` because no verification bundle exists, `Withdrawn -> Withdrawn`), no compat shim kept.
- New `crates/oraclemcp-core/src/edition_journal.rs` (new domain): `EditionOperationJournal` on `FileStore` (append + fsync before the call, as in `write_intent.rs`), `OperationState`, `reconcile(operation_id, &dyn EditionStateProbe) -> ReconcileVerdict { Applied, RetryAllowed, OperatorReconciliationRequired }`; `EditionStateProbe` trait (seam; implemented by T12.5/T12.7 with catalog queries).
- `crates/oraclemcp-config/src/profile.rs` + `config_docs.rs`: `edition_change_requests: bool` (default false; config load refuses it on a `protected` profile); `edition_change_request_ttl_days` (default 7, range 1-90).
- Concurrency check `open_conflict(identity, parent_edition)` returning which rule applied (`OracleOneChildPerParent` vs `OraclemcpOnePerPdbPolicy`).

## Implementation notes
1. Write the transition table first as data; derive every check from it.
2. CAS: every mutation takes `expected_revision`; a mismatch -> typed `REVISION_CONFLICT`. Idempotency: same key + same request -> same stored result; same key + different request -> refusal.
3. Journal: `Prepared` (persisted, fsync) -> `Executing` (persisted before dispatch) -> terminal `Applied`/`Refused`; map `StatementOutcome` unknown outcomes (T2.2a) to `OutcomeUnknown`; on startup list non-terminal operations and require `reconcile`.
4. Failpoints at the four crash points behind `#[cfg(test)]` and a test-only cargo feature `test-failpoints` (never enabled in release artifacts).
5. Identity is supplied by the probe; `open` refuses when any identity component is unproven.
6. TTL sweep on store open and before every transition.

## Test plan
- Unit: `change_request_transition_table_exhaustive`, `stage_increments_revision_and_invalidates_verification`, `stage_from_reviewing_withdraws_review_under_cas`, `revision_cas_conflict_refused`, `idempotent_retry_same_key_same_result`, `idempotency_key_reuse_with_different_request_refused`, `open_allows_zero_objects`, `ttl_expiry_moves_to_expired`, `container_name_alone_is_not_identity`, `open_conflict_same_parent_edition_names_oracle_rule`, `open_conflict_same_pdb_names_oraclemcp_policy`, `legacy_status_records_migrate_once`.
- Journal crash injection (unit, `test-failpoints`): `journal_crash_after_intent_persisted`, `journal_crash_after_oracle_success`, `journal_crash_after_response_received`, `journal_crash_before_final_state_persisted` (each asserts the `reconcile` verdict and that no DDL is replayed); `outcome_unknown_never_replayed`.
- Config: `edition_change_requests_defaults_false`, `edition_change_requests_on_protected_profile_refused_at_load`, `ttl_days_out_of_range_refused`.

## Proof split
Proves state, journal and identity logic offline. Live crash injection and the lifecycle against XE/FREE are T12.9; the catalog probes implementing `EditionStateProbe` are T12.5/T12.7.

## Non-goals
- The tool surface (T12.5), verification (T12.6), promotion (T12.7).
- Cross-deployment PDB exclusivity (R5B5 defines the scope).

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove the probes query the right catalog facts on each Oracle version.

## Considerations
- R5B5 (one-request-per-PDB policy scoped to the service state store) blocks this bead; implement the policy check against the local store and label it.
- Structure-owner check: the TTL override field name/range and the legacy-status migration mapping are decisions this bead makes.
- Rule 17: `EditionProposal` field changes and all initializers (operator routes, tests, web types in `presentation-model.ts`) land in one commit.
- File lanes `change-proposal` and `config`.

## Absorbs
None.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: a change request moves through `Open -> Staged -> Verified -> Reviewing -> Promoted -> RolledBack -> ChildRetired` only along the transition table, with `Open` holding zero objects
- [ ] Positive: after a simulated crash at each of the four journal points, `reconcile` returns the correct `Applied` / `RetryAllowed` / `OperatorReconciliationRequired` verdict
- [ ] Negative: an `OutcomeUnknown` operation is never replayed by recovery

title: Editions-enabled probe: owner and per (owner, object_type), verified per Oracle version
description:
## Context
Gap: there is no editions-enabled check; the editionable check trusts the declared `object_type` string. Oracle allows enabling editions per object type (`ALTER USER ... ENABLE EDITIONS [FOR type, ...]`), and an object whose owner or type is not editions-enabled is not editioned: staging it would change live code.

Design (plan section 14, `open` probe): **two proofs are required, and missing privilege or evidence refuses before any DDL**:
1. the owner of every object the request names is editions-enabled: `USER_USERS.EDITIONS_ENABLED` for the connected schema, `DBA_USERS.EDITIONS_ENABLED` when the profile has that privilege for other owners; an unknown or disabled owner gets a typed refusal naming the remediation `ALTER USER ... ENABLE EDITIONS`, which is irreversible operator DDL and is **never run by the server**;
2. the exact `(owner, object_type)` pair is editions-enabled per the version-appropriate `USER_`/`DBA_EDITIONED_TYPES` evidence. `V$EDITIONABLE_TYPES` is used only to establish database capability.
*Claimed (section 2.2): verify these columns on 18c, 21c, 23ai and ADB.* T4.1 provides the XE 18 / XE 21 / FREE 23ai containers (needed for acceptance only).

This bead touches the fail-closed guard (`sec` label): it needs a second-agent review before the batch verify. Invariants that must hold (AGENTS.md "safety invariant"): never bypass the classifier, never let elevation exceed a profile's `max_level`, never make a `protected` profile writable, never auto-commit DML, never admit a statement the classifier cannot prove safe for the active level.

## Outcome
A typed `EditionsEnabledProof` for each `(owner, object_type)` in a request, derived from catalog facts on the exact version, with `Unknown` (missing privilege or column) and `Disabled` both refusing before any DDL.

## Deliverable
Repo: oraclemcp.
- Catalog queries as `CatalogQueryId` variants (the T1.2a closed enum: fixed SQL, bind schema, purpose, output policy, audit class): `EditionsEnabledOwnerSelf`, `EditionsEnabledOwnerDba`, `EditionedTypesSelf`, `EditionedTypesDba`, `EditionableTypesCapability`.
- `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/catalog_resolver.rs` (or a sibling module in `oraclemcp-db`): `probe_editions_enabled(owner, object_type) -> EditionsEnabledProof { owner_enabled: Proven|Disabled|Unknown, type_enabled: Proven|Disabled|Unknown, evidence_view }`.
- `crates/oraclemcp-error/src/lib.rs`: `ReasonCategory::EditionsNotEnabled` (wire `EDITIONS_NOT_ENABLED`), whose message names the remediation and states that the server never runs it.

## Implementation notes
1. Detect version and view availability once per connection; pick the view per version; record which view produced the evidence.
2. Owner check: self via `USER_USERS`; other owners via `DBA_USERS` only if readable; otherwise `Unknown`.
3. Type check: `*_EDITIONED_TYPES` rows for the owner; an absent object type -> `Disabled`; an unreadable view -> `Unknown`.
4. Capability: `V$EDITIONABLE_TYPES` only answers "can this database edition this type"; it never proves an owner/type is enabled.
5. Never issue `ALTER USER`.

## Test plan
- Unit: `editions_probe_unknown_refuses`, `editions_probe_capability_view_never_proves_enablement`, `editions_not_enabled_message_names_remediation`.
- Live in-process on XE 18, XE 21, FREE 23ai (T4.1 containers): `editions_probe_owner_enabled_live`, `editions_probe_owner_disabled_refuses_live`, `editions_probe_type_omitted_refuses_live` (owner enabled `FOR PROCEDURE` only; a VIEW request is refused), `editions_probe_other_owner_without_dba_privilege_unknown_live`, `editions_probe_columns_present_per_version_live` (JSONL `{case_id, version, view, column, present}`).
- ADB: exercised in T9.6a (`w9_adb_editions`).

## Proof split
Proves the probe on XE 18/21 and FREE 23ai. ADB is proven in T9.6a; its use in `open`/`stage` is T12.5.

## Non-goals
- Enabling editions for anyone.
- Staging or the tool surface (T12.5).

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove ADB column availability.

## Considerations
- Added dependency **T1.2a**: this probe adds catalog reads, and the T1.2a seam (closed `CatalogQueryId` enum, no raw `query_rows` outside the executor) must exist first so this code is not written against the raw path and migrated later.
- File lane `catalog` (catalog_resolver.rs is shared with W1/W7).

## Absorbs
None.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: on XE 18, XE 21 and FREE 23ai the probe returns `Proven` for an editions-enabled owner and type, and the JSONL records which view and columns were present per version
- [ ] Negative: an owner enabled only `FOR PROCEDURE` is refused with `EDITIONS_NOT_ENABLED` for a VIEW before any DDL
- [ ] Negative: without DBA-view privilege another owner's status is `Unknown` and refuses
- [ ] Negative: no `ALTER USER` statement is ever sent (the audit shows none)
- [ ] Tests: unit tests + `editions_probe_*_live` on XE 18, XE 21, FREE 23ai (FREE 23ai tier A; XE tier C)
- [ ] Proof class: live in-process + unit; forbidden substitutes: a mocked catalog answering the per-version column question
- [ ] Consumers: T12.5
- [ ] No-claim: does not prove ADB behaviour
