title: WriteAuthorization seam: explicit scoped_grant argument, no fallback, policy floor
description:
## Context
W13 (plan section 15; operator ruling R31 "ship next-version ideas 1-3 in this train": W12 editions, W13 scoped grants, W14 impact) replaces session-wide level jumps with least privilege at statement-shape granularity. Instead of raising the whole session to READ_WRITE, an agent asks for exactly what it needs, e.g. "UPDATE APP.ORDERS column STATUS where ID IN (101, 102, 103), at most 5 rows per statement, 20 statements, 10 minutes"; that shape is approved and the guard enforces it on every statement. The 0.12 contract covers single-target UPDATE and DELETE only. The value holds with or without a human approver: a confused or compromised agent can do far less with a narrow grant than with a session-wide level.

Honesty rule: the existing single-use `ExecGrantStore` (`crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/exec_grant.rs`) documents grants as "friction + an audit artifact, not a security boundary". Without step-up delivery configured, the agent confirms its own grants. Nothing in W13 may claim a human approved unless step-up delivery is configured.

W13 invariants (never weaken; AGENTS.md safety invariant): a grant never exceeds the profile `max_level` or the OAuth scope ceiling; `protected` profiles cannot hold grants; the classifier runs on every statement; a grant dies on reconnect, lane/profile generation change, drop or TTL; every grant and every use is an audit entry (scope digest, statement digest, pre-count, rows affected); DML stays rollback-by-default and nothing auto-commits.

Problem (plan section 15 design item 3): today `oracle_execute` is hidden from `tools/list` below READ_WRITE (`required_current_level_for_tool` maps `oracle_execute | execute_approved | oracle_explain_plan` to ReadWrite in `crates/oraclemcp-core/src/server.rs`; `descriptor_visible_for_surface` requires `current_level >= required`), and `execute_sql_inner` (`crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/mod.rs`) runs classify -> `apply_sql_policy` -> `decision.gate(session)` -> composed gate before any confirmation is consumed. So without this change a READ_ONLY agent could neither discover nor use a grant.

Design (binding):
- A shared `WriteAuthorization` seam with exactly two variants: `SessionLevel` and `ScopedGrant`.
- `oracle_execute` and its compatibility aliases stay discoverable at READ_ONLY when the effective profile/OAuth ceiling is at least READ_WRITE. Visibility grants no authority: a call without a sufficient session level or an explicit scoped-grant reference is refused before any database I/O.
- `ExecuteArgs` gains `scoped_grant: Option<SignedGrantRef>`, distinct from `confirm`; the two tokens are never interchangeable, and a grant is never inferred from "the only active grant".
- A scoped grant never mutates `SessionLevelState` and never authorizes any other statement.
- Selection is explicit: supplying `scoped_grant` selects ScopedGrant authorization. Unknown, expired, revoked, drifting or mismatched grant material is a terminal typed refusal, never a fallback to the session level. SessionLevel authorization is used only when the field is absent.
- Policy composition: `sql_policy::Deny` stays terminal; `RequirePredicate` is conjoined structurally with the grant predicate (caller WHERE AND policy predicate AND grant predicate; built by T13.2/T13.4).
- Authorization order: 1 classify; 2 sql_policy Deny/RequireLevel; 3 profile max_level and the OAuth ceiling; 4 compute `classifier_level` and `policy_level_floor` separately: the session must satisfy `policy_level_floor` (a `sql_policy RequireLevel` rule can never be satisfied by a grant), and a scoped grant may satisfy only the classifier's exact READ_WRITE requirement; 5 reclassify the server rewrite and re-check policy; 6 reserve counters and re-check drift; 7 clear the READ_ONLY transaction backstop; 8 execute.
- Backstop transition (plan design item 4 c2): a grant-admitted UPDATE runs while the session level is below READ_WRITE, so inside the backstop's `SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY` it would fail with ORA-01456. A grant-admitted statement calls `ReadOnlyBackstop::clear_before_write` (a bounded ROLLBACK; the workspace is already empty by rule) before execution; if that rollback fails the session is quarantined; the backstop re-arms after finalize.
- Depends on T2.2a `StatementOutcome` so every authorization path reports a typed outcome (not_started / rolled_back / committed / commit_unknown ...).

## Outcome
`execute_sql_inner` authorizes through `WriteAuthorization`; READ_ONLY agents on a profile whose ceiling admits READ_WRITE see `oracle_execute`/`execute_approved` in `tools/list`; calls without level or grant are refused with zero database I/O; an explicit `scoped_grant` selects the grant path and any invalid grant is a terminal typed refusal even when the session is already READ_WRITE; the policy floor is enforced against the session only. Until T13.5 lands, a well-formed scoped grant that passes steps 1-4 is refused with `GRANT_ENFORCEMENT_UNAVAILABLE` (fail-closed seam).

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/scoped_grant/authorization.rs`: `enum WriteAuthorization { SessionLevel, ScopedGrant(ScopedGrantId) }` and `fn authorize_level(classifier_level, policy_level_floor, session, ceiling, grant: Option<&ScopedGrant>) -> Result<WriteAuthorization, WriteAuthRefusal>` (pure, unit-testable). Typed refusals: `GRANT_UNKNOWN`, `GRANT_EXPIRED`, `GRANT_REVOKED`, `GRANT_SUSPENDED_DRIFT`, `GRANT_MISMATCH`, `GRANT_POLICY_FLOOR_UNMET`, `GRANT_LEVEL_NOT_GRANTABLE` (classifier level above READ_WRITE), `GRANT_TOKEN_KIND_MISMATCH`, `GRANT_ENFORCEMENT_UNAVAILABLE`.
- `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/args.rs`: `ExecuteArgs.scoped_grant: Option<String>` (no serde aliases); `ExecuteApprovedArgs` forwards the same field.
- `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/mod.rs` `execute_sql_inner`: restructured into the 8-step order; steps 6 (reserve/drift) and the grant execute body are hook points that T13.5 fills; clear-backstop via `clear_read_only_transaction_before_write` / `ReadOnlyBackstop::clear_before_write` with quarantine on error.
- `crates/oraclemcp-core/src/server.rs`: `required_current_level_for_tool` / `min_visible_level_for_tool` / `descriptor_visible_for_surface`: `oracle_execute` and `execute_approved` visible when `effective_ceiling >= ReadWrite` regardless of current level; `oracle_explain_plan` unchanged (READ_WRITE).
- `crates/oraclemcp/src/registry.rs` tool description for `oracle_execute` documents `scoped_grant` and that visibility grants no authority.

## Implementation notes
1. Keep the existing `apply_sql_policy` call first (Deny refuses before anything). Compute `statement_level` from the classifier and `policy.required_level` separately (today they are max'ed into `required_level`).
2. If `scoped_grant` is absent: unchanged SessionLevel path (existing gates, confirmation, hold/commit rules).
3. If present: verify the `SignedGrantRef` under scope `grant:scoped` with the lane binding; a string that verifies as `grant:execute` instead yields `GRANT_TOKEN_KIND_MISMATCH`; a `confirm` value that verifies as `grant:scoped` likewise. Look up the grant in `ScopedGrantStore`; any failure is terminal. Require `statement_level == ReadWrite` exactly and `session.current >= policy_level_floor`; otherwise refuse. Never call `session.evaluate` to elevate, never touch `SessionLevelState`.
4. Refusals in steps 1-5 happen before `clear_read_only_transaction_before_write`, `collect_effect_audit_db_evidence`, write-intent append or any connection call; assert with a counting connection.
5. Emit a typed `StatementOutcome::NotStarted` on every pre-I/O refusal (T2.2a).
6. Visibility: extend `descriptor_visible_for_surface` with an explicit arm for `oracle_execute | execute_approved` => `surface.effective_ceiling >= ReadWrite`; protected profiles and READ_ONLY OAuth ceilings keep it hidden.

## Test plan
In-process dispatch tests (new module `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/tests/write_authorization.rs`, counting `OracleConnection` so `caller_queries`/execute counts are valid) and pure unit tests in the guard:
- `write_auth_execute_visible_at_read_only_when_ceiling_allows`
- `write_auth_execute_hidden_when_ceiling_read_only_or_protected`
- `write_auth_read_only_without_grant_refused_before_io` (0 connection calls)
- `write_auth_confirm_token_as_scoped_grant_refused`
- `write_auth_scoped_grant_as_confirm_refused`
- `write_auth_invalid_grant_never_falls_back_to_elevated_session` (session READ_WRITE, bogus/expired/revoked grant => terminal refusal, 0 executions)
- `write_auth_policy_require_level_not_satisfied_by_grant`
- `write_auth_grant_never_satisfies_ddl_or_admin`
- `write_auth_grant_does_not_mutate_session_level`
- `write_auth_policy_deny_precedes_grant_lookup`
- `write_auth_backstop_clear_failure_quarantines`
- `write_auth_well_formed_grant_refused_until_enforcement_wired` (GRANT_ENFORCEMENT_UNAVAILABLE; removed/replaced by T13.5's positive tests in the same commit that wires enforcement)
Guard unit: `authorize_level_table` (exhaustive table over levels x floor x grant presence).
Live external cases (owned and run by T13.8): `w4_execute_read_only_visible_without_grant_refused`, `w4_request_grant_token_swap_refused`, `w4_request_grant_policy_require_level_holds`, `w4_request_grant_invalid_never_falls_back`. Each JSONL case line logs case id, expected, actual, verdict.

## Proof split
Proves the authorization boundary, ordering, visibility and no-fallback selection in-process and at unit level. T13.5 proves the grant execute body (match, rewrite, pre-count, cap, reservation); T13.8 proves the same properties through the external client with audit + V$SQL evidence.

## Non-goals
No grant matching, predicate rewrite, pre-count, counters or commit semantics (T13.5). No `oracle_request_grant` tool (T13.6). No change to `oracle_explain_plan` visibility.

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove any grant-admitted statement executes correctly or within scope; only that authorization selection and ordering are fail-closed.

## Considerations
Fail-closed guard (AGENTS.md "The safety invariant", doctrine rule 1): tighten-only; never admit a statement not proven safe for the active level; never exceed profile max_level or the OAuth ceiling; protected profiles stay READ_ONLY; never auto-commit DML. This bead is labelled `sec`: it needs a second-agent adversarial review before the batch verify (plan 23.1), and any later non-critical finding becomes a `discovered-from` bug bead, not a planning round (plan section 24, R34).
Rule 17: a struct field and all its initializers, a trait method and its impls, an enum variant and its exhaustive matches land in one commit by one agent. Commit explicit paths only.
Confidentiality (constitution 9): fixtures and canaries are synthetic (e.g. schema OMCP_FX_<runid>, tenant ids 7/8); no customer, field or OCI identifiers anywhere.
Anti-ceremony (R24/R34): deliver code plus tests; no new process artifacts, manifests or report files beyond what running code branches on.
Hot file `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/mod.rs` (`file-lane:dispatch`): reserve via Agent Mail before editing; `execute_sql_inner` is also touched by W1/W2/W14 beads. `server.rs` visibility changes must keep `min_visible_level_for_tool` a documentation projection consistent with `descriptor_visible_for_surface` (existing comment) and update the generated tool docs input for T6.3.
Structure-owner check: the plan names "oracle_execute and its compatibility aliases"; this bead decides that `execute_approved` accepts and forwards `scoped_grant` identically rather than refusing it, so the alias stays semantically equivalent (W4 T4.8 alias equivalence).
Seam rule: T13.5 and T13.6 wait on this bead; the fail-closed `GRANT_ENFORCEMENT_UNAVAILABLE` placeholder is a refusal, not a stub, and is removed only by T13.5.

## Absorbs
None. No earlier bead covers this scope (plan section 23.2 absorbs column is empty for this task).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: On a profile with max_level READ_WRITE and session at READ_ONLY, `tools/list` (stdio and HTTP) contains `oracle_execute` and `execute_approved`.
- [ ] Positive: A call without `scoped_grant` at READ_WRITE behaves exactly as before (existing dispatch tests stay green).
- [ ] Negative: A READ_ONLY call to `oracle_execute` with an UPDATE and no grant is refused with zero connection calls (no backstop rollback, no audit-evidence query).
- [ ] Negative: A confirm token passed as `scoped_grant`, and a scoped-grant ref passed as `confirm`, are each refused with `GRANT_TOKEN_KIND_MISMATCH`.
- [ ] Negative: With the session at READ_WRITE, an expired/revoked/unknown `scoped_grant` is refused and the UPDATE is not executed (a fallback implementation fails this).
- [ ] Negative: A READ_ONLY session with a valid grant still fails a matching `sql_policy RequireLevel(READ_WRITE)` rule with `GRANT_POLICY_FLOOR_UNMET`.
- [ ] Negative: A grant never authorizes a statement the classifier rates DDL or ADMIN.
- [ ] Negative: `SessionLevelState` is byte-identical before and after any scoped-grant call.
- [ ] Tests: `write_auth_*` tests listed in the description and `authorize_level_table`; green in `cargo test -p oraclemcp -p oraclemcp-guard` (through `scripts/build_lease.sh` for workspace runs).
- [ ] Proof class: live in-process (dispatch with counting connection) + unit; forbidden substitutes: none for these claims; the external-client proof is T13.8, and an in-process test must not be cited as external reachability.
- [ ] Consumers: T13.5, T13.6, T13.8.
- [ ] No-claim: Does not prove grant enforcement of rows/columns/predicates, nor external reachability.

title: Grant admission: MutationEffectClosureV1 closure rule and ordinary-heap-table rule
description:
## Context
W13 (plan section 15; operator ruling R31 "ship next-version ideas 1-3 in this train": W12 editions, W13 scoped grants, W14 impact) replaces session-wide level jumps with least privilege at statement-shape granularity. Instead of raising the whole session to READ_WRITE, an agent asks for exactly what it needs, e.g. "UPDATE APP.ORDERS column STATUS where ID IN (101, 102, 103), at most 5 rows per statement, 20 statements, 10 minutes"; that shape is approved and the guard enforces it on every statement. The 0.12 contract covers single-target UPDATE and DELETE only. The value holds with or without a human approver: a confused or compromised agent can do far less with a narrow grant than with a session-wide level.

Honesty rule: the existing single-use `ExecGrantStore` (`crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/exec_grant.rs`) documents grants as "friction + an audit artifact, not a security boundary". Without step-up delivery configured, the agent confirms its own grants. Nothing in W13 may claim a human approved unless step-up delivery is configured.

W13 invariants (never weaken; AGENTS.md safety invariant): a grant never exceeds the profile `max_level` or the OAuth scope ceiling; `protected` profiles cannot hold grants; the classifier runs on every statement; a grant dies on reconnect, lane/profile generation change, drop or TTL; every grant and every use is an audit entry (scope digest, statement digest, pre-count, rows affected); DML stays rollback-by-default and nothing auto-commits.

Plan section 15 design items 1 (`dml_effect_closure`) and 2 (closure rule). The shared `MutationEffectClosureV1` collector (T7.9a, seam) gives, per mechanism, an explicit catalog source, cap, identity, hash and `unavailable` behaviour for: the target's enabled triggers for the exact statement kind including compound and column-specific DML triggers; incoming enabled foreign keys and their delete actions; indexes and index callbacks; virtual/generated expressions; VPD statement-type-specific policy functions and check-option policies; FGA handlers (W1 T1.9: an enabled policy with a non-null `handler_module` is `Autonomous`); OLS / Real Application Security / Data Redaction (T7.16), including OLS write-control triggers; materialized-view logs (maintained by an internal DML trigger); and a privilege-completeness proof (every source readable, else `Unknown`).

Admission rule (binding): a grant is admitted in 0.12 only for an ordinary local heap table with no enabled user-defined DML trigger for the granted statement kind, even for purely transactional triggers (a 5-row UPDATE can fire a statement trigger that updates a million rows elsewhere; a BEFORE EACH ROW trigger can assign :NEW columns outside the approved SET list). Oracle-internal transactional maintenance, such as a proven MV log, is modelled separately and does not make an arbitrary user trigger admissible. Also refused: enabled ON DELETE CASCADE or ON DELETE SET NULL (deleting 5 parent rows could delete millions of child rows the pre-count never sees); domain indexes; user functions behind virtual columns or function-based indexes unless their closure is W7-Clean and rollback-safe; unproven mutation-time policy/callback code; partitioned, IOT, external and clustered targets. Closure rule at preview: refuse any enabled user DML trigger for the statement kind whatever its effects; any callback that could change :NEW, another table, another row set or session state; any `Autonomous`, `TxnControl`, `ExternalIo`, `DynamicSql`, `SequenceAdvance` or `Unknown` effect. Effects are judged only through the shared `RoutineEffectsV1` admission function (T7.5/T7.2), never a hand-maintained list. Transactional internal effects (MV log) are included in the impact and in `scope_digest`; their absence or drift must be proven, never assumed.

## Outcome
A single admission function turns a resolved target plus its `MutationEffectClosureV1` into either an `AdmittedGrantTarget` (with closure fingerprints written into the grant's `ClosureFingerprints` slot and folded into `scope_digest`) or a typed refusal naming the mechanism. A recheck helper recomputes the closure and reports drift for T13.5.

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/scoped_grant/admission.rs`: `admit_grant_target(target: &GrantTargetFacts, closure: &MutationEffectClosureV1, verbs: &GrantVerbs, effects_admission: &dyn RoutineEffectsAdmission) -> Result<AdmittedGrantTarget, GrantAdmissionRefusal>`; `GrantAdmissionRefusal` variants `NotOrdinaryHeapTable{kind}`, `UserDmlTrigger{trigger}`, `FkDeleteAction{constraint, rule}`, `DomainIndex{index}`, `UnprovenCallback{mechanism, identity}`, `EffectRefused{effect}`, `ClosureUnknown{source, reason}`.
- `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/` catalog facts for the target: extend the T7.9a collector's target-facts query set (ALL_TABLES/ALL_OBJECTS: PARTITIONED, IOT_TYPE, CLUSTER_NAME, TEMPORARY, external via ALL_EXTERNAL_TABLES, remote/DB-link refusal) as `CatalogQueryId` variants (T1.2a rule: no raw query strings in served code).
- `fn recheck_grant_closure(grant, fresh_closure) -> Result<(), GrantDrift>` used by T13.5 before every use.

## Implementation notes
1. Target kind: admit only a permanent, non-partitioned, heap-organized (IOT_TYPE null), non-clustered, non-external, local table owned by the resolved owner in the current container. Global temporary tables are treated as not ordinary and refused.
2. Triggers: any enabled trigger (simple, compound, column-specific `UPDATE OF`) whose triggering event includes a granted verb refuses, regardless of timing or effects. Disabled triggers are recorded in the fingerprint (enabling one is drift).
3. FKs: any enabled incoming FK with DELETE_RULE CASCADE or SET NULL refuses the grant (for any verb set).
4. Indexes: domain index refuses; function-based index or virtual column whose expression calls a user function is admitted only if `RoutineEffectsV1` admission in the grant context returns Clean with rollback-safe effects (ReadDb only); otherwise refuse.
5. Policies: VPD policies applying to UPDATE/DELETE (and check-option policies) with a policy function whose closure is not W7-Clean refuse; FGA handler => Autonomous => refuse; OLS/RAS/Redaction detected by T7.16 => refuse.
6. MV logs: include the MV log identity in the fingerprint; if MV-log presence cannot be read, `ClosureUnknown`.
7. Any `unavailable`, truncated or privilege-incomplete mechanism => `ClosureUnknown` refusal (unknown != absent).
8. Fingerprints: SHA-256 over each mechanism's canonical identity/source-hash list plus the target LAST_DDL_TIME; write into `ClosureFingerprints`; `ScopedGrant` digest recomputed.

## Test plan
Unit/offline with synthetic closure values (constructed `MutationEffectClosureV1` instances, not a mock database) in `crates/oraclemcp-guard/tests/scoped_grant_admission.rs`:
- `grant_admission_ordinary_heap_table_admitted`
- `grant_admission_refuses_partitioned_iot_external_clustered_temporary`
- `grant_admission_refuses_any_enabled_user_dml_trigger` (row, statement, compound, column-specific; transactional-only effects too)
- `grant_admission_disabled_trigger_in_fingerprint`
- `grant_admission_refuses_on_delete_cascade_and_set_null`
- `grant_admission_refuses_domain_index`
- `grant_admission_fbi_user_function_requires_clean`
- `grant_admission_refuses_fga_handler_autonomous`
- `grant_admission_refuses_vpd_unproven_policy_function`
- `grant_admission_mv_log_included_in_digest`
- `grant_admission_unknown_source_refuses`
- `grant_admission_each_forbidden_effect_refuses` (Autonomous, TxnControl, ExternalIo, DynamicSql, SequenceAdvance, Unknown)
- `grant_closure_recheck_detects_trigger_added_after_apply`
Live in-process on FREE 23ai fixture (`crates/oraclemcp/tests/grant_admission_live.rs`, gated like the existing live tests): `grant_admission_live_autonomous_trigger_refused`, `grant_admission_live_before_update_trigger_refused`, `grant_admission_live_cascade_fk_refused`, `grant_admission_live_heap_table_admitted`. External-client cases (run by T13.8): `w4_request_grant_autonomous_trigger_preview_refused`, `w4_request_grant_before_update_trigger_refused`, `w4_request_grant_after_update_statement_trigger_refused`, `w4_request_grant_on_delete_cascade_refused`.

## Proof split
Proves the admission decision over closure facts (unit) and that the facts are collected from a real catalog (live in-process). T7.9a proves the collector's completeness; T13.5 proves per-use recheck; T13.8 proves the external behaviour.

## Non-goals
No new closure mechanisms (collector scope is T7.9a). No INSERT/MERGE support. No admission of triggers with "harmless" effects.

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove the collector finds every mechanism on every Oracle version (T7.9a + tier C), nor that admitted grants are enforced (T13.5).

## Considerations
Fail-closed guard (AGENTS.md "The safety invariant", doctrine rule 1): tighten-only; never admit a statement not proven safe for the active level; never exceed profile max_level or the OAuth ceiling; protected profiles stay READ_ONLY; never auto-commit DML. This bead is labelled `sec`: it needs a second-agent adversarial review before the batch verify (plan 23.1), and any later non-critical finding becomes a `discovered-from` bug bead, not a planning round (plan section 24, R34).
Rule 17: a struct field and all its initializers, a trait method and its impls, an enum variant and its exhaustive matches land in one commit by one agent. Commit explicit paths only.
Confidentiality (constitution 9): fixtures and canaries are synthetic (e.g. schema OMCP_FX_<runid>, tenant ids 7/8); no customer, field or OCI identifiers anywhere.
Anti-ceremony (R24/R34): deliver code plus tests; no new process artifacts, manifests or report files beyond what running code branches on.
Structure-owner check: the plan lists ON DELETE CASCADE / SET NULL refusal without restricting it to DELETE grants; this bead refuses it for every grant (tighten-only). It also classifies global temporary tables as not "ordinary" and refuses them. Either may be narrowed only by the structure owner.
Engine dependency: admission of function-based-index/virtual-column functions relies on the served W7 engine binding (via T7.9a -> T7.9).

## Absorbs
None. No earlier bead covers this scope (plan section 23.2 absorbs column is empty for this task).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: A permanent heap table with no enabled DML trigger, no cascading FK and no policy code is admitted, and its closure fingerprint is folded into `scope_digest`.
- [ ] Negative: An enabled BEFORE EACH ROW trigger that only assigns `:NEW.updated_at` (purely transactional) still refuses the grant (a trigger-effects-based implementation fails this).
- [ ] Negative: An enabled AFTER UPDATE statement trigger that updates a second large table refuses the grant.
- [ ] Negative: An incoming enabled FK with ON DELETE CASCADE refuses the grant.
- [ ] Negative: A collector result with any mechanism `unavailable` or privilege-incomplete refuses with `ClosureUnknown` (unknown != absent).
- [ ] Negative: Partitioned, IOT, external, clustered and temporary targets are each refused with `NotOrdinaryHeapTable`.
- [ ] Negative: Enabling a previously disabled trigger after apply is reported as drift by `recheck_grant_closure`.
- [ ] Tests: `grant_admission_*` and `grant_closure_recheck_detects_trigger_added_after_apply` (guard, `cargo test -p oraclemcp-guard`); `grant_admission_live_*` green on FREE 23ai.
- [ ] Proof class: unit + live in-process; forbidden substitutes: a mocked connection or hand-written catalog rows standing in for the live admission tests.
- [ ] Consumers: T13.5, T13.6, T13.8.
- [ ] No-claim: Does not prove enforcement at execute time or completeness of the underlying collector.

title: AND-only typed grant predicate DSL with immutable bound values and policy conjunction
description:
## Context
W13 (plan section 15; operator ruling R31 "ship next-version ideas 1-3 in this train": W12 editions, W13 scoped grants, W14 impact) replaces session-wide level jumps with least privilege at statement-shape granularity. Instead of raising the whole session to READ_WRITE, an agent asks for exactly what it needs, e.g. "UPDATE APP.ORDERS column STATUS where ID IN (101, 102, 103), at most 5 rows per statement, 20 statements, 10 minutes"; that shape is approved and the guard enforces it on every statement. The 0.12 contract covers single-target UPDATE and DELETE only. The value holds with or without a human approver: a confused or compromised agent can do far less with a narrow grant than with a session-wide level.

Honesty rule: the existing single-use `ExecGrantStore` (`crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/exec_grant.rs`) documents grants as "friction + an audit artifact, not a security boundary". Without step-up delivery configured, the agent confirms its own grants. Nothing in W13 may claim a human approved unless step-up delivery is configured.

W13 invariants (never weaken; AGENTS.md safety invariant): a grant never exceeds the profile `max_level` or the OAuth scope ceiling; `protected` profiles cannot hold grants; the classifier runs on every statement; a grant dies on reconnect, lane/profile generation change, drop or TTL; every grant and every use is an audit entry (scope digest, statement digest, pre-count, rows affected); DML stays rollback-by-default and nothing auto-commits.

Plan section 15 design item 1 (`row_predicate`) and item 3 (policy composition). The existing `sql_policy` RequirePredicate grammar (`crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/policy.rs`) is a literal-only regex with no binds and no IN, re-rendered through `statement.to_string()`; it must not be reused for grants. The grant predicate is built by a new predicate module:
- A separate typed DSL: AND-only conjunctions of comparisons over resolved target columns. Allowed forms: `=`, `<>`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, IN lists (<= 1000 values), BETWEEN, IS [NOT] NULL. No OR/NOT in 0.12.
- Values are immutable, typed, stored in the approved grant and bound, never concatenated. Caller-supplied values never define or widen the predicate.
- Subqueries, functions, column-to-column comparisons, OR and NOT are not part of the 0.12 DSL and are rejected.
- Policy composition: `RequirePredicate` is conjoined structurally with the grant predicate: caller WHERE AND policy predicate Q AND grant predicate P. `sql_policy::Deny` stays terminal.
Column resolution uses the W1 per-block resolved identities (T1.1) so a predicate column is a resolved column of the bound target, never a free identifier.

## Outcome
`GrantPredicateV1` values are built only through a validating builder from a structured request, checked against the target's resolved column types, rendered to a sqlparser `Expr` whose values are server-named binds (`:omcp_g1`..), and conjoined with the caller WHERE and the policy predicate as three parenthesised AST conjuncts. Everything outside the grammar is refused with a typed reason.

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/scoped_grant/predicate.rs`: `GrantPredicateBuilder::from_request(conjuncts: &[PredicateConjunctRequest], columns: &ResolvedColumns) -> Result<GrantPredicateV1, PredicateRefusal>`; `render_ast(&GrantPredicateV1) -> (Expr, Vec<GrantBind>)`; `compose_where(caller: Option<Expr>, policy_q: Option<Expr>, grant_p: Expr) -> Expr`.
- Request shape (consumed by T13.6): a JSON array of `{column, op, value | values | low+high}` objects; `op` in `eq, ne, lt, le, gt, ge, in, between, is_null, is_not_null`.
- `PredicateRefusal` variants: `OrNotUnsupported`, `SubqueryRefused`, `FunctionRefused`, `ColumnToColumnRefused`, `InListTooLarge{len}`, `InListEmpty`, `UnknownColumn`, `TypeMismatch{column, expected}`, `NullComparison` (use is_null), `ReservedBindName`.
- Fuzz target `crates/oraclemcp-guard/fuzz/fuzz_targets/grant_predicate.rs`.
- Reserved bind prefix `omcp_g` documented; T13.3 refuses caller binds using it.

## Implementation notes
1. Parse structured JSON only; there is no SQL-text predicate input, so OR/NOT/subqueries/functions are unrepresentable; SQL-text-looking values are plain typed values.
2. Types: NUMBER (canonical decimal, precision/scale checked), VARCHAR2/NVARCHAR2/CHAR (length checked), DATE and TIMESTAMP (ISO-8601 input, bound as typed Oracle values, never TO_DATE text with session NLS). No implicit conversion: a value whose type differs from the column type is refused.
3. IN: 1..=1000 values (Oracle ORA-01795 limit), duplicates removed canonically; BETWEEN requires low <= high.
4. Rendering: each value becomes a server-named bind; the rendered Expr contains no literal value text; render -> parse -> structural equality round-trip asserted.
5. `compose_where` produces `(caller) AND (Q) AND (P)` as AST nodes (Nested), omitting absent parts, never string concatenation. Q comes from `policy.rs` `combined_policy_predicate` as an AST.

## Test plan
Unit (`crates/oraclemcp-guard/tests/scoped_grant_predicate.rs`): `grant_predicate_accepts_each_allowed_operator`, `grant_predicate_rejects_or_and_not`, `grant_predicate_rejects_subquery_value`, `grant_predicate_rejects_function_value`, `grant_predicate_rejects_column_to_column`, `grant_predicate_rejects_in_list_over_1000_and_empty`, `grant_predicate_rejects_type_mismatch_no_implicit_conversion`, `grant_predicate_rejects_unknown_column`, `grant_predicate_values_bound_never_inlined` (canary value absent from rendered SQL), `grant_predicate_render_parse_round_trip`, `compose_where_is_three_parenthesised_conjuncts`, `compose_where_caller_injection_cannot_escape` (caller WHERE containing `1=1) OR (1=1` as parsed AST stays inside its conjunct).
Property: `prop_composed_where_implies_p_and_q` (an in-memory evaluator over random rows: every row satisfying the composed predicate satisfies P and Q).
Fuzz: `grant_predicate` target (no panic; every accepted input round-trips; nothing outside the grammar accepted); seeds committed under `crates/oraclemcp-guard/fuzz/corpus/grant_predicate/`.
Live (run by T13.8): `w4_request_grant_policy_and_grant_predicates_conjoined`, `w4_request_grant_caller_predicate_bind_refused`.

## Proof split
Proves the DSL, typing, binding and structural conjunction offline. T13.4 proves the full rewrite; T13.8 proves on Oracle that touched rows satisfy P AND Q.

## Non-goals
No OR/NOT, no functions, no subqueries, no column-to-column comparisons in 0.12. No changes to the `sql_policy` RequirePredicate grammar itself.

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove Oracle evaluates the rendered predicate identically for every NLS setting beyond the typed binds used; live behaviour is T13.8.

## Considerations
Fail-closed guard (AGENTS.md "The safety invariant", doctrine rule 1): tighten-only; never admit a statement not proven safe for the active level; never exceed profile max_level or the OAuth ceiling; protected profiles stay READ_ONLY; never auto-commit DML. This bead is labelled `sec`: it needs a second-agent adversarial review before the batch verify (plan 23.1), and any later non-critical finding becomes a `discovered-from` bug bead, not a planning round (plan section 24, R34).
Rule 17: a struct field and all its initializers, a trait method and its impls, an enum variant and its exhaustive matches land in one commit by one agent. Commit explicit paths only.
Confidentiality (constitution 9): fixtures and canaries are synthetic (e.g. schema OMCP_FX_<runid>, tenant ids 7/8); no customer, field or OCI identifiers anywhere.
Anti-ceremony (R24/R34): deliver code plus tests; no new process artifacts, manifests or report files beyond what running code branches on.
Structure-owner check: the plan does not fix the request encoding; this bead decides a structured JSON conjunct list (no SQL-text predicates) and forbids implicit type conversion. The round-5 High bug bead (owners T13.4/T14.6a) adds a restricted caller-WHERE grammar `DmlCallerPredicateV1`; it should reuse this module's comparison grammar, so keep the comparison AST reusable (no grant-specific coupling in the operator/value types).

## Absorbs
None. No earlier bead covers this scope (plan section 23.2 absorbs column is empty for this task).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: A request `[{column: ID, op: in, values: [101,102,103]}, {column: TENANT_ID, op: eq, value: 7}]` over NUMBER columns builds a predicate that renders to `("ID" IN (:omcp_g1, :omcp_g2, :omcp_g3)) AND ("TENANT_ID" = :omcp_g4)` (modulo exact quoting) with four typed binds.
- [ ] Positive: `compose_where` of caller WHERE, policy Q and grant P yields three parenthesised AND conjuncts.
- [ ] Negative: OR, NOT, a subquery, a function call, a column-to-column comparison, an IN list of 1001 values, an empty IN list, a string value for a NUMBER column and an unknown column are each refused with their typed reason.
- [ ] Negative: The canary value 913377 never appears in any rendered SQL text (an implementation that inlines literals fails).
- [ ] Negative: A caller WHERE AST crafted to close a parenthesis cannot change the conjunction structure (property holds over 10k proptest cases).
- [ ] Tests: `grant_predicate_*`, `compose_where_*`, `prop_composed_where_implies_p_and_q` green in `cargo test -p oraclemcp-guard`; fuzz target `grant_predicate` builds and runs 60 s without findings in the tier-B fuzz lane.
- [ ] Proof class: unit / offline + fuzz; forbidden substitutes: none (no database claim).
- [ ] Consumers: T13.4, T13.5, T13.6.
- [ ] No-claim: Does not prove the executed statement is restricted to P on Oracle (T13.4/T13.8).

W13 invariants (never weaken; AGENTS.md safety invariant): a grant never exceeds the profile `max_level` or the OAuth scope ceiling; `protected` profiles cannot hold grants; the classifier runs on every statement; a grant dies on reconnect, lane/profile generation change, drop or TTL; every grant and every use is an audit entry (scope digest, statement digest, pre-count, rows affected); DML stays rollback-by-default and nothing auto-commits.

Plan section 15 design item 4(b) "Match": if the session level is below `required_level`, the statement may pass only by matching its explicitly supplied grant exactly: the verb is in `verbs`; the single target resolves to the bound OBJECT_ID; the touched columns are within `columns`; SET is exactly one typed bind or literal per assignment (all functions, subqueries, sequences and RETURNING clauses refused in 0.12); no column referenced by `row_predicate` appears in the SET list. A statement that does not match its explicitly supplied grant is refused; a grant never widens anything implicitly. Target rules (item 1): exactly one table; synonym or object-identity drift forces re-approval; views, synonyms-to-views, remote objects (DB links), `TABLE()` collection expressions and partition-extended names are refused. INSERT and MERGE get typed refusals (injecting into MERGE ON turns out-of-scope rows into WHEN NOT MATCHED inserts); multi-table INSERT ALL/FIRST refused. Plan unit tests: scope matching with quoting, case, synonyms, schema-qualified vs unqualified names; a private synonym ORDERS -> APP2.ORDERS (refused); multi-table and MERGE statements (refused); CTE-DML (refused unless the single target resolves); SET with a subquery, RETURNING, NEXTVAL or an unproven function (refused); SET of a predicate column (refused). Plan fuzz: the scope matcher.

## Outcome
`match_statement` accepts a parsed UPDATE/DELETE plus its resolved target identity and returns `GrantMatch` only when every scope dimension matches exactly; every other statement shape yields a typed `GrantMismatch`. Caller binds using the reserved `omcp_g` prefix are refused.

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/scoped_grant/matcher.rs`: `match_statement(grant: &ScopedGrant, stmt: &sqlparser::ast::Statement, resolved: &ResolvedDmlTarget) -> Result<GrantMatch, GrantMismatch>`; `GrantMatch { verb, target, set_assignments: Vec<(ColumnIdent, AssignedValue)>, caller_where: Option<Expr> }`.
- `GrantMismatch` variants: `VerbNotGranted`, `InsertRefused`, `MergeRefused`, `MultiTableInsertRefused`, `MultiTarget`, `TargetIdentityMismatch`, `SynonymPathMismatch`, `ViewTarget`, `RemoteObject`, `CollectionExpression`, `PartitionExtended`, `ColumnNotGranted{column}`, `SetExpressionRefused{kind}` (function, subquery, sequence, arithmetic, multi-column tuple), `ReturningRefused`, `SetPredicateColumn{column}`, `CteDmlUnresolved`, `ReservedBindName`.
- `ResolvedDmlTarget` produced in dispatch by the W1 resolver (T1.1) with CURRENT_SCHEMA and synonym chain recorded.
- Fuzz target `crates/oraclemcp-guard/fuzz/fuzz_targets/grant_scope_match.rs`.

## Implementation notes
1. Identifiers: unquoted names uppercase; quoted names exact; compare on resolved identity (owner, OBJECT_ID, container, edition), never on spelling.
2. Synonyms: the grant records the resolution path at approval (`resolved_via`). A statement whose name resolves through a different synonym, or through a synonym when the grant was approved on the base name (or the reverse), is `SynonymPathMismatch`; a private synonym pointing to another owner's same-named table is `TargetIdentityMismatch`.
3. Target shape: reject `@dblink`, `TABLE(...)`, `PARTITION (...)`, `PARTITION FOR (...)`, `SUBPARTITION ...`, inline views, joins/USING in UPDATE/DELETE, and any target whose resolved object type is VIEW.
4. SET: each assignment `col = <single typed bind | literal>`; reject CASE, arithmetic, concatenation, function calls, `seq.NEXTVAL/CURRVAL`, subqueries, `(a, b) = (...)` tuples, `DEFAULT` keyword.
5. RETURNING / RETURN ... INTO refused. DELETE never has SET.
6. CTE-DML: admitted only when the parsed DML target (not a CTE name) resolves to the bound OBJECT_ID and no CTE is referenced by the target; otherwise `CteDmlUnresolved`.
7. The caller WHERE is passed through as an AST for T13.4 (restriction of its grammar is the round-5 bug bead).

## Test plan
Unit (`crates/oraclemcp-guard/tests/scoped_grant_matcher.rs`): `scope_match_exact_update_admitted`, `scope_match_quoted_case_distinct`, `scope_match_unqualified_resolves_current_schema`, `scope_match_private_synonym_to_other_owner_refused`, `scope_match_synonym_path_change_refused`, `scope_match_view_and_synonym_to_view_refused`, `scope_match_dblink_refused`, `scope_match_partition_extended_refused`, `scope_match_table_collection_refused`, `scope_match_multi_table_refused`, `scope_match_insert_refused_typed`, `scope_match_merge_refused_typed`, `scope_match_insert_all_first_refused`, `scope_match_cte_dml_refused_unless_single_target`, `scope_match_set_subquery_refused`, `scope_match_set_returning_refused`, `scope_match_set_nextval_refused`, `scope_match_set_function_refused`, `scope_match_set_arithmetic_refused`, `scope_match_set_predicate_column_refused`, `scope_match_ungranted_column_refused`, `scope_match_reserved_bind_prefix_refused`.
Property: `prop_out_of_scope_mutation_never_admitted` (take an admitted statement, mutate exactly one scope dimension: column, table, verb, SET expression kind, target decoration; always refused).
Fuzz: `grant_scope_match` with an independent structural oracle; seeds from the unit cases; the guard corpus gets every refused shape.
Live (T13.8): `w4_request_grant_out_of_scope_column_refused`, `w4_request_grant_insert_refused_typed`, `w4_request_grant_merge_refused_typed`, `w4_request_grant_set_predicate_column_refused`.

## Proof split
Proves the matcher offline (unit, property, fuzz). Identity resolution correctness is T1.1; live refusal through the external client is T13.8.

## Non-goals
No rewrite, no pre-count, no caller-WHERE grammar restriction (round-5 bug bead), no INSERT/MERGE support.

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove the dispatch resolver produces the correct `ResolvedDmlTarget` on every Oracle version.

## Considerations
Fail-closed guard (AGENTS.md "The safety invariant", doctrine rule 1): tighten-only; never admit a statement not proven safe for the active level; never exceed profile max_level or the OAuth ceiling; protected profiles stay READ_ONLY; never auto-commit DML. This bead is labelled `sec`: it needs a second-agent adversarial review before the batch verify (plan 23.1), and any later non-critical finding becomes a `discovered-from` bug bead, not a planning round (plan section 24, R34).
Rule 17: a struct field and all its initializers, a trait method and its impls, an enum variant and its exhaustive matches land in one commit by one agent. Commit explicit paths only.
Confidentiality (constitution 9): fixtures and canaries are synthetic (e.g. schema OMCP_FX_<runid>, tenant ids 7/8); no customer, field or OCI identifiers anywhere.
Anti-ceremony (R24/R34): deliver code plus tests; no new process artifacts, manifests or report files beyond what running code branches on.
Structure-owner check: the plan says synonym drift forces re-approval but does not define admission of a synonym path that resolves to the bound OBJECT_ID; this bead decides the resolution path is part of the approved identity (same path required).
Hot file: the classifier is not modified here; matcher consumes parsed ASTs only (`file-lane:guard-grant`).

## Absorbs
None. No earlier bead covers this scope (plan section 23.2 absorbs column is empty for this task).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: `UPDATE APP.ORDERS SET STATUS = :s WHERE ID = :id` matches a grant on APP.ORDERS/{UPDATE}/{STATUS} and returns the assignment and caller WHERE AST.
- [ ] Negative: `UPDATE ORDERS ...` where ORDERS is a private synonym for APP2.ORDERS is refused with `TargetIdentityMismatch`.
- [ ] Negative: `SET STATUS = (SELECT ...)`, `SET STATUS = UPPER(:s)`, `SET ID = s.NEXTVAL`, `SET STATUS = :s + 1`, `RETURNING ID INTO :x` are each refused with their typed reason.
- [ ] Negative: `SET TENANT_ID = 8` under predicate `TENANT_ID = 7` is refused with `SetPredicateColumn`.
- [ ] Negative: INSERT, MERGE and INSERT ALL are refused with distinct typed reasons (a matcher that only checks the target fails).
- [ ] Negative: Every single-dimension mutation of an admitted statement is refused across 10k proptest cases.
- [ ] Tests: `scope_match_*` and `prop_out_of_scope_mutation_never_admitted` green in `cargo test -p oraclemcp-guard`; fuzz target `grant_scope_match` runs 60 s clean in the tier-B fuzz lane.
- [ ] Proof class: unit / offline + fuzz; forbidden substitutes: none (no database claim).
- [ ] Consumers: T13.4, T13.5.
- [ ] No-claim: Does not prove live refusal through MCP (T13.8) or resolver correctness (T1.1).

title: Grant rewrite: server-owned CHECK OPTION UPDATE template and DELETE conjunct (spike first)
description:
## Context W13 (plan section 15; operator ruling R31 "ship next-version ideas 1-3 in this train": W12 editions, W13 scoped grants, W14 impact) replaces session-wide level jumps with least privilege at statement-shape granularity. Instead of raising the whole session to READ_WRITE, an agent asks for exactly what it needs, e.g. "UPDATE APP.ORDERS column STATUS where ID IN (101, 102, 103), at most 5 rows per statement, 20 statements, 10 minutes"; that shape is approved and the guard enforces it on every statement. The 0.12 contract covers single-target UPDATE and DELETE only. The value holds with or without a human approver: a confused or compromised agent can do far less with a narrow grant than with a session-wide level. Honesty rule: the existing single-use `ExecGrantStore` (`crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/exec_grant.rs`) documents grants as "friction + an audit artifact, not a security boundary". Without step-up delivery configured, the agent confirms its own grants. Nothing in W13 may claim a human approved unless step-up delivery is configured. W13 invariants (never weaken; AGENTS.md safety invariant): a grant never exceeds the profile `max_level` or the OAuth scope ceiling; `protected` profiles cannot hold grants; the classifier runs on every statement; a grant dies on reconnect, lane/profile generation change, drop or TTL; every grant and every use is an audit entry (scope digest, statement digest, pre-count, rows affected); DML stays rollback-by-default and nothing auto-commits. Plan section 15 design item 4(c) and plan 23.3 note for T13.4. Rewrite is AST, never text: - UPDATE targets an inline view `(SELECT * FROM owner.t WHERE

) WITH CHECK OPTION`.

selects the old rows, and the check option refuses any post-update row that would leave the scope (ORA-01402). Updating a column that

references is refused outright. - DELETE gets

as a parenthesised conjunct of its WHERE. - Every rewrite is reclassified. - Parser limit (verified in planning): sqlparser 0.62 (`crates/oraclemcp-guard/Cargo.toml`) parses WITH CHECK OPTION only in CREATE VIEW, so Oracle's `UPDATE (SELECT ... WHERE P WITH CHECK OPTION) SET ...` does not parse. The rewrite is therefore a server-owned template: `UPDATE (SELECT * FROM "O"."T" WHERE WITH CHECK OPTION) SET WHERE `. Only the AST parts are rendered and round-tripped (render -> parse -> structurally equal per part). This bead starts with a spike confirming this. - The existing `sql_policy` rewrite (`policy.rs`, `rewrite_statement_ast` then `statement.to_string()`) is not reused for grants. - Policy composition from T13.2: = caller WHERE AND policy predicate Q (the grant predicate P lives in the inline view for UPDATE and as the third conjunct for DELETE). - Row cap slot: the executed form carries `AND ROWNUM <= ` where cap = reserved_rows + 1, a validated server integer supplied by T13.5. ## Outcome A committed spike test pins the sqlparser limit and proves on FREE 23ai that the template executes and raises ORA-01402 on a scope-leaving update; `render_grant_update` / `render_grant_delete` produce the executable text from validated AST parts, each part round-trips, and each rewrite is reclassified through an equivalent parseable form with a verdict equal to the caller statement's. ## Deliverable - `crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/scoped_grant/rewrite.rs`: `GrantRewriteV1 { executable_sql: String, parts: RewriteParts { target: QuotedIdent, p: Expr, set: Vec, where_: Expr, cap: u32 }, binds: Vec, reclass_form: String }`; `render_grant_update(match: &GrantMatch, p, q, cap)`; `render_grant_delete(match, p, q, cap)`. - Spike tests: `sqlparser_rejects_update_inline_view_check_option` (unit; fails loudly if a sqlparser upgrade changes the limit, prompting reuse of a real parse) and `grant_template_check_option_live_free23` (live in-process: template executes; a scope-leaving UPDATE raises ORA-01402). - Fuzz target `crates/oraclemcp-guard/fuzz/fuzz_targets/grant_rewrite_round_trip.rs`. ## Implementation notes 1. Spike first; record the result in the test itself (no report file). 2. Target rendered only from catalog identity, always double-quoted exact case. 3. Each AST part rendered with sqlparser Display, then parsed back as the same syntactic category (expression / assignment list) and compared structurally; mismatch => refuse `GRANT_REWRITE_ROUND_TRIP`. 4. Reclassification: because the full template does not parse, classify (a) the inner `SELECT * FROM "O"."T" WHERE

` (must be READ_ONLY with W1 proof) and (b) the equivalent parseable statement `UPDATE "O"."T" SET WHERE () AND (

)` (must classify READ_WRITE with the same verdict as the caller statement). DELETE's rewrite parses directly and is classified as-is. Any divergence refuses. 5. Refuse again (defence in depth) if any SET column is referenced by P. 6. No caller text is ever concatenated; binds keep caller binds and grant binds in separate namespaces (`omcp_g*` reserved). ## Test plan Unit: `grant_rewrite_update_template_parts_round_trip`, `grant_rewrite_delete_conjunct_parenthesised`, `grant_rewrite_reclassification_matches_caller_verdict`, `grant_rewrite_refuses_set_predicate_column`, `grant_rewrite_no_caller_text_concatenation` (caller WHERE with `--`, `/*`, quotes and `) OR (` survives only as AST), `grant_rewrite_cap_is_validated_integer`. Property: `prop_rewrite_never_widens_row_set` (in-memory relational evaluator over random tables/predicates: rows touched by the rewritten statement are a subset of rows satisfying P, and of rows satisfying caller WHERE AND Q). Fuzz: `grant_rewrite_round_trip`. Live in-process (FREE 23ai): `grant_template_check_option_live_free23`, `grant_rewrite_live_delete_touches_only_p_rows` (independent re-read of the table afterwards). Live external (T13.8): `w4_request_grant_mr_rewrite_subset_of_p`. ## Proof split Proves template correctness, round-trip, reclassification and non-widening (offline + live in-process). T13.5 proves execution with cap and savepoint; T13.8 proves through the external client. ## Non-goals No execution, pre-count, counters or commit (T13.5). No MERGE/INSERT templates. ## No-claim boundary Does not prove the executed statement stays within the cap under concurrency (T13.5). ## Considerations Fail-closed guard (AGENTS.md "The safety invariant", doctrine rule 1): tighten-only; never admit a statement not proven safe for the active level; never exceed profile max_level or the OAuth ceiling; protected profiles stay READ_ONLY; never auto-commit DML. This bead is labelled `sec`: it needs a second-agent adversarial review before the batch verify (plan 23.1), and any later non-critical finding becomes a `discovered-from` bug bead, not a planning round (plan section 24, R34). Rule 17: a struct field and all its initializers, a trait method and its impls, an enum variant and its exhaustive matches land in one commit by one agent. Commit explicit paths only. Confidentiality (constitution 9): fixtures and canaries are synthetic (e.g. schema OMCP_FX_, tenant ids 7/8); no customer, field or OCI identifiers anywhere. Anti-ceremony (R24/R34): deliver code plus tests; no new process artifacts, manifests or report files beyond what running code branches on. Round-5 High bug bead (plan section 24, owners T13.4/T14.6a): `EffectiveDmlPlanV1` + restricted caller-WHERE grammar (`DmlCallerPredicateV1`). It is filed as a release-blocking bug bead that blocks this bead; `GrantRewriteV1` must be the single object that later becomes `EffectiveDmlPlanV1` (resolved target, assignments, caller predicate, matched policy rules and Q, P, bind HMACs, row cap) so impact, pre-count, classification and execution consume the same plan. Structure-owner check: reclassification of the non-parseable template through an equivalent parseable form per part is this bead's decision implied by the plan's "every rewrite is reclassified". ## Absorbs None. No earlier bead covers this scope (plan section 23.2 absorbs column is empty for this task).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: On FREE 23ai, the rendered UPDATE template updates exactly the rows satisfying caller WHERE AND Q AND P, and an UPDATE that would move a row out of P raises ORA-01402 (spike test).
- [ ] Positive: Every rendered AST part round-trips structurally, and the reclassification verdict equals the caller statement's.
- [ ] Negative: A sqlparser upgrade that starts parsing `UPDATE (SELECT ... WITH CHECK OPTION)` makes `sqlparser_rejects_update_inline_view_check_option` fail (the spike is pinned, not assumed).
- [ ] Negative: A caller WHERE containing `) OR (1=1` does not widen the DELETE (row set subset property holds; a text-concatenating rewrite fails).
- [ ] Negative: A rewrite whose SET touches a P column is refused before rendering.
- [ ] Tests: `sqlparser_rejects_update_inline_view_check_option`, `grant_rewrite_*`, `prop_rewrite_never_widens_row_set` (guard); `grant_template_check_option_live_free23`, `grant_rewrite_live_delete_touches_only_p_rows` (FREE 23ai); fuzz `grant_rewrite_round_trip` 60 s clean.
- [ ] Proof class: unit + live in-process; forbidden substitutes: a mocked connection for the ORA-01402 and subset claims.
- [ ] Consumers: T13.5, T13.8.
- [ ] No-claim: Does not prove row caps, reservation or commit isolation.

title: Grant execute path: empty workspace, pre-count, ROWNUM cap, atomic credits, drift, commit
description:
## Context
W13 (plan section 15; operator ruling R31 "ship next-version ideas 1-3 in this train": W12 editions, W13 scoped grants, W14 impact) replaces session-wide level jumps with least privilege at statement-shape granularity. Instead of raising the whole session to READ_WRITE, an agent asks for exactly what it needs, e.g. "UPDATE APP.ORDERS column STATUS where ID IN (101, 102, 103), at most 5 rows per statement, 20 statements, 10 minutes"; that shape is approved and the guard enforces it on every statement. The 0.12 contract covers single-target UPDATE and DELETE only. The value holds with or without a human approver: a confused or compromised agent can do far less with a narrow grant than with a session-wide level.

Honesty rule: the existing single-use `ExecGrantStore` (`crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/exec_grant.rs`) documents grants as "friction + an audit artifact, not a security boundary". Without step-up delivery configured, the agent confirms its own grants. Nothing in W13 may claim a human approved unless step-up delivery is configured.

W13 invariants (never weaken; AGENTS.md safety invariant): a grant never exceeds the profile `max_level` or the OAuth scope ceiling; `protected` profiles cannot hold grants; the classifier runs on every statement; a grant dies on reconnect, lane/profile generation change, drop or TTL; every grant and every use is an audit entry (scope digest, statement digest, pre-count, rows affected); DML stays rollback-by-default and nothing auto-commits.

Plan section 15 design item 4 (steps 4-8 of the authorization order in detail), wired into the `WriteAuthorization::ScopedGrant` hook that T13.0 left fail-closed:
- (a) Classify: classifier + `sql_policy` Deny/RequireLevel still apply; a grant never overrides a Deny.
- (b) Match (T13.3) against the explicitly supplied grant; mismatch is terminal.
- (c) Rewrite (T13.4), reclassified.
- (c2) Read-only backstop: `ReadOnlyBackstop::clear_before_write` (bounded ROLLBACK; the workspace is already empty by rule) before execution; if that rollback fails the session is quarantined; the backstop re-arms after finalize.
- Workspace rule: a grant use requires an empty reversible workspace (no uncommitted work held on the pinned session, `ctx.checkpoints` closed and no held statements), so an allowed commit can only ever commit the isolated granted statement.
- (d) Pre-count: `SELECT COUNT(*)` over the rewritten predicate and the statement's WHERE, classified READ_ONLY through the W1 proof (GuardedReadExecutor, T1.2b, including the FGA closure). If it exceeds `max_rows_per_statement` or the remaining `max_total_rows`, refuse `GRANT_ROW_LIMIT` before any row is touched.
- (e) Execute with a cap: inject `AND ROWNUM <= cap` and run inside a savepoint. If `rows_affected` exceeds the limit (a race with concurrent inserts), roll back to the savepoint and refuse `GRANT_ROW_LIMIT`.
- (f) Re-check drift: the entire `MutationEffectClosureV1` and every `scope_digest` component are revalidated before every statement (T13.2a `recheck_grant_closure`); any drift refuses the statement and suspends the grant.
- (g) Row credits: pre-count n; re-check drift; then atomically reserve one statement credit and min(n, max_rows_per_statement, remaining_total_rows) row credits. No database write happens until the reservation succeeds. The executed cap is reserved_rows + 1. If actual rows exceed the reservation, roll back to the savepoint, suspend the grant and record the attempted breach. On success consume the actual attempted rows and release unused credits. Revocation and TTL serialize against the reservation state, so a concurrent use and revoke cannot both succeed.
- (h) Commit only if `commit_allowed` and the call asks to commit; otherwise rollback-by-default.
- W14 decisive-field matrix row "W13 grant creation/use" (T14.6b): envelope; `scope_digest` (incl. `MutationEffectClosureV1`); rows (pre-count); policy floor; generation. An unavailable or truncated decisive field always refuses.
- Audit: every use is an audit entry with scope digest, statement digest, pre-count, rows affected (and any attempted breach). Raw predicate/bind values never enter audit.

## Outcome
A statement carrying a valid `scoped_grant` at READ_ONLY either executes exactly once within scope, cap and credits (rolled back unless commit is allowed and requested) or is refused with a typed reason before any write; concurrent uses and revocations have exactly one outcome; drift suspends the grant; the backstop is cleared only after reservation and re-armed afterwards.

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/mod.rs`: the ScopedGrant branch of `execute_sql_inner` (or a helper `execute_scoped_grant` in the same module): workspace check, pre-count via `GuardedReadExecutor` server read (`CatalogQueryId`/`AdmittedRead` rules from T1.2a), drift recheck, reservation, backstop clear, savepoint (`OMCP_GRANT_EXEC`), capped execution, finalize, commit/rollback, backstop re-arm, audit.
- `crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/scoped_grant/mod.rs`: `ScopedGrantStore::reserve(id, n) -> Reservation`, `finalize(reservation, actual_rows) -> FinalizeOutcome`, `release(reservation)`, with revoke/TTL/reserve under one lock; `GrantState::Suspended{AttemptedBreach|Drift}`.
- Audit fields in the existing audit record path (`crates/oraclemcp-audit/src/record.rs` detail): `scope_digest`, `statement_digest`, `pre_count`, `reserved_rows`, `rows_affected`, `outcome` (StatementOutcome from T2.2a), `breach: bool`.
- Remove T13.0's `GRANT_ENFORCEMENT_UNAVAILABLE` placeholder in the same commit (rule 17).

## Implementation notes
Order inside the grant branch (after T13.0 steps 1-4): match -> rewrite + reclassify -> workspace empty check -> decisive-field revalidation (T14.6a/b) -> pre-count (READ_ONLY, backstop still armed) -> drift recheck -> reserve credits (fails => refuse, no write) -> clear backstop (failure => quarantine, StatementOutcome per T2.2a) -> SAVEPOINT -> execute capped rewrite -> if rows > reserved_rows: ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT, suspend, audit breach, refuse -> finalize credits -> commit if allowed+asked else ROLLBACK -> re-arm backstop -> audit.
Edge cases: n = 0 reserves 0 rows, cap 1 (any row touched is a breach); TTL expiry between reserve and execute refuses and releases; revoke during execution waits on the reservation lock and then takes effect for the next use; connection loss mid-statement returns the typed StatementOutcome and never replays; `hold=true` with a grant is refused (grant uses need an empty workspace and leave none); DDL-level statements never reach here (T13.0).
Oracle semantics: ROWNUM in UPDATE/DELETE WHERE is legal; ORA-01402 from the CHECK OPTION surfaces as a typed `GRANT_SCOPE_VIOLATION` refusal after savepoint rollback.

## Test plan
In-process dispatch with counting connection (`crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/tests/scoped_grant_exec.rs`): `grant_exec_nonempty_workspace_refused`, `grant_exec_precount_over_limit_refused_before_write`, `grant_exec_rownum_cap_breach_rolls_back_and_suspends`, `grant_exec_credits_released_on_refusal`, `grant_exec_drift_suspends_grant`, `grant_exec_commit_only_when_allowed_and_requested`, `grant_exec_backstop_cleared_after_reservation_and_rearmed`, `grant_exec_backstop_clear_failure_quarantines`, `grant_exec_audit_records_digests_and_counts_without_values`, `grant_exec_ttl_expiry_between_reserve_and_execute_refused`, `grant_exec_hold_with_grant_refused`.
Store unit: `grant_store_concurrent_reserve_total_rows_one_wins`, `grant_store_reserve_vs_revoke_single_outcome` (deterministic barrier threads).
Live in-process on FREE 23ai (`crates/oraclemcp/tests/scoped_grant_exec_live.rs`): `grant_exec_live_concurrent_uses_one_reaches_oracle` (two sessions, each pre-counting 5 under max_total_rows = 5; ordering by DBMS_PIPE barrier; V$SQL shows one execution of the run-id-tagged statement), `grant_exec_live_million_rows_precount_refused_zero_touched`, `grant_exec_live_race_insert_breach_rolled_back`.
External-client cases (T13.8): `w4_request_grant_in_scope_update_passes`, `w4_request_grant_uncommitted_prior_work_refused`, `w4_request_grant_concurrent_use_revoke_single_outcome`, `w4_request_grant_concurrent_uses_total_rows_one_reaches_oracle`, `w4_request_grant_million_rows_precount_refused`, `w4_request_grant_trigger_drift_suspends`, `w4_request_grant_commit_only_when_allowed`.

## Proof split
Proves the enforcement pipeline in-process and on a live database in-process. External reachability and the full negative matrix through MCP are T13.8; ADB is T9.6a.

## Non-goals
No new tool (T13.6), no dashboard (T13.7), no INSERT/MERGE, no net-row accounting (attempted rows only).

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove that concurrent DDL between the drift recheck and execution is impossible (residual race stated in W14; the audit records both digests).

## Considerations
Fail-closed guard (AGENTS.md "The safety invariant", doctrine rule 1): tighten-only; never admit a statement not proven safe for the active level; never exceed profile max_level or the OAuth ceiling; protected profiles stay READ_ONLY; never auto-commit DML. This bead is labelled `sec`: it needs a second-agent adversarial review before the batch verify (plan 23.1), and any later non-critical finding becomes a `discovered-from` bug bead, not a planning round (plan section 24, R34).
Rule 17: a struct field and all its initializers, a trait method and its impls, an enum variant and its exhaustive matches land in one commit by one agent. Commit explicit paths only.
Confidentiality (constitution 9): fixtures and canaries are synthetic (e.g. schema OMCP_FX_<runid>, tenant ids 7/8); no customer, field or OCI identifiers anywhere.
Anti-ceremony (R24/R34): deliver code plus tests; no new process artifacts, manifests or report files beyond what running code branches on.
Never weaken: no write before the reservation succeeds; no commit unless both `commit_allowed` and the call ask; no fallback to session level on any grant failure; the backstop is never disarmed for a statement that has not passed every check.
Round-5 High bug bead (`EffectiveDmlPlanV1`, owners T13.4/T14.6a): this bead must consume the single plan object from T13.4 for pre-count and execution, so the counted and executed predicates are the same AST.
Hot file `dispatch/mod.rs` (`file-lane:dispatch`); coordinate with W2 T2.2b/T2.4 (re-lease and cancel) since quarantine paths are shared.

## Absorbs
None. No earlier bead covers this scope (plan section 23.2 absorbs column is empty for this task).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: At READ_ONLY with a valid grant (UPDATE STATUS, P: ID IN (101,102,103), max 5/stmt), `UPDATE APP.ORDERS SET STATUS = :s WHERE ID IN (101,102)` executes, reports rows_affected 2, rolls back by default, and the audit entry carries scope_digest, statement_digest, pre_count 2 and rows_affected 2.
- [ ] Positive: With `commit_allowed=true` and `commit=true`, only the granted statement is committed (workspace was empty) and an independent re-read shows exactly those rows changed.
- [ ] Negative: A grant use with uncommitted prior work on the session is refused before any write.
- [ ] Negative: An UPDATE matching 1,000,000 rows under max 5 is refused by the pre-count with the audit showing 0 rows touched and V$SQL holding no execution of the tagged candidate statement.
- [ ] Negative: Two concurrent uses each pre-counting 5 rows under max_total_rows = 5: exactly one reaches Oracle.
- [ ] Negative: Concurrent use + revoke: exactly one of (use succeeded, revoke took effect first) holds, never both.
- [ ] Negative: A concurrent insert that makes rows_affected exceed the reservation rolls back to the savepoint and suspends the grant.
- [ ] Negative: Adding an enabled trigger after apply makes the next use refuse and suspends the grant.

title: oracle_request_grant tool: preview/apply/status/drop with impact bundle, honest approval
description:
## Context
W13 (plan section 15; operator ruling R31 "ship next-version ideas 1-3 in this train": W12 editions, W13 scoped grants, W14 impact) replaces session-wide level jumps with least privilege at statement-shape granularity. Instead of raising the whole session to READ_WRITE, an agent asks for exactly what it needs, e.g. "UPDATE APP.ORDERS column STATUS where ID IN (101, 102, 103), at most 5 rows per statement, 20 statements, 10 minutes"; that shape is approved and the guard enforces it on every statement. The 0.12 contract covers single-target UPDATE and DELETE only. The value holds with or without a human approver: a confused or compromised agent can do far less with a narrow grant than with a session-wide level.

Honesty rule: the existing single-use `ExecGrantStore` (`crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/exec_grant.rs`) documents grants as "friction + an audit artifact, not a security boundary". Without step-up delivery configured, the agent confirms its own grants. Nothing in W13 may claim a human approved unless step-up delivery is configured.

W13 invariants (never weaken; AGENTS.md safety invariant): a grant never exceeds the profile `max_level` or the OAuth scope ceiling; `protected` profiles cannot hold grants; the classifier runs on every statement; a grant dies on reconnect, lane/profile generation change, drop or TTL; every grant and every use is an audit entry (scope digest, statement digest, pre-count, rows affected); DML stays rollback-by-default and nothing auto-commits.

Plan section 15 design item 2 (request and approval):
- `oracle_request_grant`, with actions `preview | apply | status | drop`, mirrors `oracle_set_session_level` (preview/apply with confirm; `SetSessionLevelArgs` pattern in `dispatch/args.rs`, handler `set_session_level` in `dispatch/mod.rs`).
- `preview` validates the shape, runs the trigger/closure check (T13.2a), returns the W14 impact bundle and mints a confirmation token bound to `scope_digest`. `apply` installs the grant.
- The approval path is never weaker than the equivalent level elevation needs on that profile: step-up delivery (a human) if configured (`crates/oraclemcp-auth/src/stepup_delivery.rs`, `crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/stepup.rs`), otherwise the preview -> confirm round trip.
- Grants are listed by `status`, revocable by `drop`, and visible and revocable in the dashboard (T13.7).
- Closure rule, refused at preview: any enabled user DML trigger for the statement kind, whatever its effects; any callback that could change :NEW, another table, another row set or session state; any Autonomous, TxnControl, ExternalIo, DynamicSql, SequenceAdvance or Unknown effect.
- W14 decisive-field matrix row "W13 grant creation/use": envelope; `scope_digest` (incl. MutationEffectClosureV1); rows (pre-count); policy floor; generation. Unavailable/truncated decisive fields always refuse (T14.6b).
- Honesty: without step-up delivery the agent confirms its own grant; the tool result and description say so.
- W4 acceptance counts `oracle_request_grant` among the 36 canonical tools.

## Outcome
`oracle_request_grant` is registered, discoverable at READ_ONLY when the ceiling admits READ_WRITE (hidden on protected profiles and READ_ONLY OAuth ceilings), and returns a typed impact bundle on preview, a `SignedGrantRef` on apply, a redacted list on status and a revocation on drop; every state-changing action is audited; approval requires step-up when configured.

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/args.rs`: `RequestGrantArgs { action, target {owner, table}, verbs, columns, predicate: Vec<PredicateConjunctRequest>, max_rows_per_statement, max_statements, max_total_rows, ttl_seconds, commit_allowed, confirm, grant }` with strict decoding (the T3.1 strict decoder pattern; no aliases).
- `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/mod.rs`: `request_grant` handler (preview/apply/status/drop) using T13.1 construction, T13.2 builder, T13.3 static shape checks on the requested scope, T13.2a admission, T14 impact bundle, T14.6a confirmation material, step-up path.
- `crates/oraclemcp/src/registry.rs` + `crates/oraclemcp-core/src/tools.rs`: descriptor, input/output schema, description text (states the approval honesty rule); `crates/oraclemcp-core/src/server.rs` visibility arm (same rule as `enable_writes`: visible when effective ceiling >= READ_WRITE).
- Audit entries for preview (digest only), apply, drop, suspend; status is read-only and not audited as a privileged action.

## Implementation notes
1. preview: build grant candidate (no install), resolve target via W1 resolver, admission, compute impact (rows = pre-count estimate via T14.2 path over P AND Q; effects = closure summary; locks = target; reversibility = rolled_back_by_default unless commit_allowed), check decisive fields, mint confirmation (scope `grant:request-apply`, bound to scope_digest + decisive digest + binding + generation).
2. apply: verify confirm; if step-up delivery is configured, require the step-up challenge exactly as `set_session_level` to READ_WRITE does on that profile; revalidate decisive facts (REPREVIEW_REQUIRED on drift); install via `ScopedGrantStore::issue`; return `SignedGrantRef`, expiry, limits, `approved_by: step_up | agent_self_confirmation`.
3. status: list grants for the caller's binding: id, state, verbs, target identity, columns, predicate structure with values redacted, counters, remaining TTL.
4. drop: revoke (serialized with reservations), audit.
5. Refusals typed: every T13.1/T13.2/T13.3/T13.2a refusal plus `GRANT_PROTECTED_PROFILE`, `GRANT_ABOVE_CEILING`, `REPREVIEW_REQUIRED`, `STEP_UP_REQUIRED`.

## Test plan
In-process (`crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/tests/request_grant.rs`): `request_grant_registered_and_visible_at_read_only_with_ceiling`, `request_grant_hidden_on_protected_profile_and_read_only_oauth`, `request_grant_apply_without_preview_refused`, `request_grant_apply_after_drift_repreview_required`, `request_grant_step_up_required_when_configured`, `request_grant_approval_label_honest_without_step_up`, `request_grant_status_redacts_values` (canary), `request_grant_drop_then_use_refused`, `request_grant_insert_merge_typed_refusal`, `request_grant_preview_returns_every_impact_field_with_status`, `request_grant_decisive_rows_unavailable_refuses`.
Registry: the tool appears in the registry-driven schema/runtime differential test (T3.1) and the completeness gate (T4.14).
External-client (T13.8): every `w4_request_grant_*` case.

## Proof split
Proves the tool surface and approval path in-process. End-to-end behaviour through stdio and HTTP is T13.8; dashboard is T13.7; docs regeneration is T6.3.

## Non-goals
No dashboard UI (T13.7); no persistence across restart; no grant for INSERT/MERGE; no multi-target grants.

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove a human approved a grant unless step-up delivery is configured and exercised.

## Considerations
Fail-closed guard (AGENTS.md "The safety invariant", doctrine rule 1): tighten-only; never admit a statement not proven safe for the active level; never exceed profile max_level or the OAuth ceiling; protected profiles stay READ_ONLY; never auto-commit DML. This bead is labelled `sec`: it needs a second-agent adversarial review before the batch verify (plan 23.1), and any later non-critical finding becomes a `discovered-from` bug bead, not a planning round (plan section 24, R34).
Rule 17: a struct field and all its initializers, a trait method and its impls, an enum variant and its exhaustive matches land in one commit by one agent. Commit explicit paths only.
Confidentiality (constitution 9): fixtures and canaries are synthetic (e.g. schema OMCP_FX_<runid>, tenant ids 7/8); no customer, field or OCI identifiers anywhere.
Anti-ceremony (R24/R34): deliver code plus tests; no new process artifacts, manifests or report files beyond what running code branches on.
Never weaker than elevation: if the equivalent `set_session_level` to READ_WRITE on the profile would require step-up, apply must too; OAuth scopes can only lower the ceiling.
Hot files: `dispatch/mod.rs`, `registry.rs`, `server.rs` (`file-lane:dispatch`).

## Absorbs
None. No earlier bead covers this scope (plan section 23.2 absorbs column is empty for this task).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: Preview of a valid UPDATE grant returns `impact` with every field present and a status, a confirmation token, and the scope digest; apply with that token returns a `SignedGrantRef` usable by `oracle_execute`.
- [ ] Positive: `status` lists the grant with predicate values redacted; `drop` revokes it and a subsequent use is refused.
- [ ] Positive: With step-up delivery configured, apply without the step-up challenge is refused with `STEP_UP_REQUIRED`.
- [ ] Negative: Apply with a token from a preview whose target trigger set changed since preview is refused with `REPREVIEW_REQUIRED`.
- [ ] Negative: A protected profile never lists the tool and a direct call is refused.
- [ ] Negative: A preview request with verbs [INSERT] or [MERGE] is refused with the typed verb refusal.
