title: W14: Impact shown at every approval (ActionEnvelopeV1, ImpactBindingV1)
description:
## Goal and current state
W14 (plan section 16; operator ruling R31) makes every approval show what the change will actually do before anyone confirms it: rows, dependents, predicted invalidations, effect changes, security findings, cost, locks and reversibility. Computing that picture must itself never execute anything the current level does not already admit ("a preview never executes a statement the current level refuses").

State at 1fbe6eb0 (re-derive line numbers with rg -n): `oracle_preview_sql` executes nothing and returns danger, required level, gate decision, objects affected, reason, safe alternative and a confirmation token, but no cost and no dependents; its args (`PreviewSqlArgs` in `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/args.rs`) accept only `sql`, while `ExecuteArgs` also takes `binds`, `commit`, `hold`, `capture_dbms_output`, `dbms_output_max_lines/chars` and `timeout_seconds`. `oracle_preview_dml` really executes inside savepoint `OMCP_PREVIEW_DML` (`dispatch/workspace.rs` `PREVIEW_SANDBOX`) and rolls back; it requires READ_WRITE (`ensure_workspace_level`) and its caveat admits autonomous work survives the rollback. Dependents appear only in `create_or_replace`/`patch_source` previews, one hop (`probe_dependents` in `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/intelligence.rs`); `compile_object` has none. Cost gates only `oracle_query` (EXPLAIN PLAN, `max_query_cost`); EXPLAIN PLAN is classified READ_WRITE because it writes `PLAN_TABLE`. PL/SQL `what_breaks`, `blast_radius` and `sast` exist as separate tools (`crates/oraclemcp/src/plsql_tools.rs`). Confirmation tokens bind the SQL text only: `ExecGrantStore::issue(material: &str)` stores a SQL digest, and `execute_grant_token_fields` / `sign_execute_grant_reference` (`dispatch/mod.rs`) sign only profile/session/lane/subject/generation/level.

## Design (binding for every child)
1. One `impact` object on every preview that mints a confirmation: `preview_sql`, `preview_dml`, the `compile_object`/`create_or_replace`/`patch_source` previews, the `set_session_level` preview, custom-tool previews (W7), change-request verify (W12) and grant preview (W13). Every field carries `status: computed | estimated | unavailable(reason) | not_applicable(reason)` and is never silently omitted.
   - `rows`: for UPDATE/DELETE a non-executing estimate only when `DmlImpactShapeV1` proves an equivalent server-owned COUNT query (AST-derived, through `GuardedReadExecutor` and `MutationEffectClosureV1`); unsupported targets (views with INSTEAD OF triggers, inline or multi-table views, partition-extended names, remote objects, CURRENT OF, TABLE(), ambiguous rewrites) return `unavailable(unsupported_dml_shape)`; returned as `{kind: snapshot_estimate, value, scn bounds, profile_generation}`; apply returns `observed_rows` separately (equality claimed only on isolated fixtures). The sandbox `rows_affected` (preview_dml machinery) is computed only when the session's effective level admits the statement, the target's closure is free of Autonomous/TxnControl/ExternalIo/DynamicSql/Unknown/SequenceAdvance, and no sequence is advanced; otherwise `not_applicable(level_below_required | untrusted_triggers)`. A preview never executes a statement the current level refuses.
   - `dependents`: transitive ALL_DEPENDENCIES closure with depth/count caps and a `truncated` flag; predicted invalid set from `blast_radius`/`what_breaks` (catalog-aware or live-snapshot mode).
   - `effects`: the W7 effect set for changed or called routines, including before -> after; `unavailable(engine_not_wired)` until W7 step 5.
   - `sast`: PL/SQL-intelligence findings on new or changed source.
   - `cost`: EXPLAIN PLAN cost/cardinality vs profile `max_query_cost`; server-built only, savepoint always rolled back, only for statements classified with a known level at preview; server-generated random STATEMENT_ID literal from a strict ASCII alphabet; PLAN_TABLE resolution verified before running (PUBLIC synonym to SYS.PLAN_TABLE$ with session-private temporary semantics and no local/private shadow, or an explicitly configured server-owned GTT with pinned identity) else `unavailable` and a decisive confirmation refuses; server-fixed INTO only; reads/cleanup by statement id, never MAX(plan_id); at READ_ONLY advisory cost reports `unavailable(read_only_txn)` instead of clearing the backstop; EXPLAIN runs only when `HardParseEffectClosureV1` (W1 task 7, T1.8) proves no user callback can fire, else `unavailable(hard_parse_callbacks)`; VPD targets `unavailable(vpd)`. Claimed: EXPLAIN inside the backstop's READ ONLY transaction may raise ORA-01456 - verify on 18c/21c/23ai/ADB; if so report `unavailable(read_only_txn)`, never disarm the backstop.
   - `locks`: DML target tables; DDL on objects in use probed where privileged (DBA_DDL_LOCKS / V$ACCESS), else `unavailable(no_privilege)`.
   - `reversibility`: `rolled_back_by_default | needs_checkpoint | irreversible`.
2. `ActionEnvelopeV1` (seam, T14.0): one shared codec canonically encoding SQL/source digest, typed bind arity + Oracle bind types + a value HMAC, commit/hold/output-capture modes and caps, action kind, scoped-grant reference. Every minting preview accepts the same envelope minus the token; apply recomputes it and refuses mismatch with `REPREVIEW_REQUIRED`. Every allowlisted ALTER SESSION increments the lane generation, invalidating every outstanding confirmation.
3. The token binds `ImpactBindingV1` with two sections. `decisive` (compared at apply, action-specific per the T14.6b matrix): statement/source digest; a domain-separated keyed HMAC of canonical bind types and values; exact object identities and source/dependency/trigger hashes; object status and edition/compiler facts; effect-analysis engine version and ruleset digest; DB/PDB, CURRENT_SCHEMA, profile/lane generation and the W13 `scope_digest` (opaque `Option<[u8; 32]>`). `observations` (display/audit only, never compared): row estimates, cost, timings, field statuses, SCN bounds (a single `observed_at_scn` only when the query ran AS OF that SCN, else `{scn_before, scn_after}`; an advancing SCN with unchanged facts never invalidates). Raw bind values are never stored in ExecGrant, audit or logs; transient buffers are cleared. Storage: T14.6a changes `ExecGrantStore::issue` material to `(sql_digest, decisive_digest)` and signs `decisive_digest`. Revalidation runs the bounded fact queries the action requires, never re-runs analysis, immediately before token consumption and before execution; drift refuses with `REPREVIEW_REQUIRED`. Residual race (concurrent DDL between recheck and execution) is stated; the audit records both digests.
4. Decisive-field matrix (T14.6b; every listed field must be `computed` or the confirmation refuses):
   | Action | Required decisive fields |
   |---|---|
   | Generic DML (preview_sql/execute) | envelope; object identities; MutationEffectClosureV1; rows (when DmlImpactShapeV1 supports the shape, else advisory); edition/schema/generation |
   | DDL / ADMIN statement | envelope; object identities; dependents + predicted invalid set; DdlEffectClosureV1; effects of changed source; reversibility |
   | Session elevation (set_session_level) | envelope (level, TTL); profile/OAuth ceiling; generation |
   | Custom package call | envelope; closure fact key; RoutineEffectsV1; DdlEffectClosureV1 (for DDL); masking-profile output check |
   | W12 promotion | the complete DBA_OBJECTS_AE manifest + changed manifest; DB/PDB identity; default == base; parentage; USE/PUBLIC exposure; service editions; DdlEffectClosureV1 (for create/drop) |
   | W13 grant creation/use | envelope; scope_digest (incl. MutationEffectClosureV1); rows (pre-count); policy floor; generation |
5. Bounded and honest: per-field time budget and depth/count caps; timeout => `unavailable(timeout)`; decisive fields always refuse when unavailable/truncated for W12 promotion, W13 grant creation/use, custom-tool DDL and every ADMIN action regardless of configuration; `require_impact` (default false, per profile) governs only advisory fields; previews rate-limited per lane.
6. Surfaces: agent tool result, dashboard Change Review, W3 session report, audit entry (drift digest + field statuses).

## Acceptance (epic level)
Tokens are refused after impact drift; predicted invalid sets equal observed on the fixture and are a superset in general runs; golden and differential suites (T14.9) green; no preview executes a statement the current level refuses.

## Size and dependencies
Size M. Depends on W7 step 1 (effect set, T7.5) and the existing SAST/blast-radius tools; the `effects` field is fully wired after W7 step 5 (T7.9); W1 task 1 (read proof for the COUNT estimate, T1.1/T1.2b); T1.8 (hardened EXPLAIN, HardParseEffectClosureV1); T3.1 (strict decoding) for the envelope; T3.7 for the session report. Hot file `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/mod.rs` preview paths.

## Round-5 release-blocking bug bead owned in this epic (plan section 24)
High, owners T13.4/T14.6a: `EffectiveDmlPlanV1` - bind effective_plan_digest, sql_policy ruleset digest, matched rule identities and rewrite-algorithm version as decisive fields; impact rows computed from exactly the executed effective plan.

## Children
T14.0, T14.1, T14.2, T14.3, T14.4, T14.5, T14.6a, T14.6b, T14.7, T14.8, T14.9.

Session semantics: every allowlisted ALTER SESSION (NLS, optimizer, edition, current schema, ...; allowlist in `crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/enforcement.rs`) increments the lane generation (`crates/oraclemcp-core/src/lane.rs` `bump_generation`), which invalidates every outstanding confirmation, so session settings that change parsing, resolution or execution cannot drift between preview and apply. Bind HMAC (design item 3): a domain-separated, keyed HMAC, because low-entropy identifiers could be brute-forced from a plain SHA-256; raw bind values are never stored in ExecGrant, audit records or logs, and transient canonical bind buffers are cleared after the HMAC is computed. Depends on T3.1 so the new preview arguments go through the strict decoder (unknown and duplicate members refused).

## Outcome
`ActionEnvelopeV1` and its canonical codec exist in the guard crate; every confirmation-minting preview (`oracle_preview_sql`, `oracle_preview_dml`, compile/create_or_replace/patch_source previews, `set_session_level` preview, custom-tool previews) accepts the execution envelope fields; the envelope digest is bound into the minted confirmation, and apply with any differing envelope (commit flip, hold flip, bind value/type change, output caps, action kind, grant ref) is refused with `REPREVIEW_REQUIRED`; allowlisted ALTER SESSION bumps the lane generation.

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/action_envelope.rs` (new): `ActionEnvelopeV1 { version, action_kind: ActionKind, statement_digest: [u8;32], binds: BindEnvelope { arity, types: Vec<OracleBindType>, value_hmac: [u8;32] }, commit: bool, hold: bool, output: OutputCapture { capture_dbms_output, max_lines, max_chars }, limits: ExecLimits { timeout_seconds }, scoped_grant_ref: Option<[u8;32]> }`; `ActionKind { ExecuteDml, ExecuteDdlAdmin, PreviewDmlSandbox, CompileObject, CreateOrReplace, PatchSource, SetSessionLevel{level, ttl}, CustomToolCall, ChangeRequestPromote, GrantCreate, GrantUse }`; `canonical_bytes()`, `digest()`.
- Canonical bind codec: `canonical_binds(&[OracleBind]) -> Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>` and `bind_value_hmac(key, bytes)` with domain `omcp/bind-hmac/v1`; key = per-process random 32 bytes held by the dispatcher (pattern of `oraclemcp-core/src/tamper_token.rs`).
- `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/args.rs`: `PreviewSqlArgs`, `PreviewDmlArgs`, `SetSessionLevelArgs` preview path, compile/create_or_replace/patch_source preview args, custom-tool preview args gain the envelope fields matching their apply counterparts.
- `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/mod.rs`: `preview_sql`, `preview_dml_inner`, `set_session_level`, `compile_object`, `create_or_replace`, `patch_source`, `issue_confirmation_grant` / `consume_execute_confirmation`: material = statement text + envelope digest (T14.6a later restructures the material into `(sql_digest, decisive_digest)` with the envelope inside decisive).
- ALTER SESSION apply path in `dispatch/mod.rs` (where `catalog_invalidation_for_sql` runs): call the lane's `bump_generation()` after every successful allowlisted ALTER SESSION.
- `zeroize` as a direct dependency of `oraclemcp-guard` (already in `Cargo.lock`; `cargo deny check` must stay green).

## Implementation notes
1. Canonical encoding: version tag, length-prefixed fields, fixed order, binds encoded as (Oracle type tag, canonical value bytes: NUMBER canonical decimal, strings exact UTF-8 bytes, dates ISO, NULL tag), never serde_json text.
2. Defaults: a preview called without envelope fields encodes the defaults (no binds, commit false, hold false, no output capture); an agent that previews without `commit` and applies with `commit=true` gets `REPREVIEW_REQUIRED` with next step "re-preview with commit=true".
3. `json_to_bind` (`dispatch/mod.rs`) is the single conversion; the codec runs on its output so preview and apply see identical typed binds.
4. Buffers holding canonical bind bytes are `Zeroizing`; no Debug impl prints them; the HMAC is the only persisted form.
5. Refusal code `REPREVIEW_REQUIRED` added to the error taxonomy (`oraclemcp-error`) with a refusal hint (T3.6 catalogue picks it up).

## Test plan
Unit (`crates/oraclemcp-guard/tests/action_envelope.rs`): `envelope_canonical_encoding_deterministic`, `envelope_digest_changes_on_each_field`, `bind_hmac_domain_separated`, `bind_hmac_dictionary_attack_fails` (enumerate 0..100_000 low-entropy ids with SHA-256 and with a wrong key; never matches), `bind_canonical_buffer_zeroized`.
Property: `prop_envelope_injective`.
In-process dispatch (`crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/tests/action_envelope.rs`): `envelope_commit_flip_repreview_required`, `envelope_hold_flip_repreview_required`, `envelope_bind_value_change_repreview_required`, `envelope_bind_type_change_repreview_required`, `envelope_output_caps_change_repreview_required`, `envelope_action_kind_mismatch_refused`, `alter_session_nls_bumps_generation_and_invalidates_confirmations`, `alter_session_current_schema_bumps_generation`, `bind_redaction_canary_absent_from_audit_and_logs`, `preview_strict_decoding_rejects_unknown_envelope_member`.
Live external (run in T14.9): `w4_impact_token_changed_bind_refused`, `w4_impact_bind_redaction_canary`.

## Proof split
Proves the envelope contract, keyed bind codec and generation bump (unit + in-process). T14.6a proves persistence into ExecGrant and signed fields plus fact revalidation; T14.9 proves through the external client.

## Non-goals
No impact fields (T14.1-T14.5), no decisive-field matrix (T14.6b), no change to what is admitted at any level.

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove object/fact drift detection (T14.6a) or that previews are side-effect free (T14.2/T14.5).

## Considerations
Fail-closed guard (AGENTS.md "The safety invariant", doctrine rule 1): tighten-only; never admit a statement not proven safe for the active level; never exceed profile max_level or the OAuth ceiling; protected profiles stay READ_ONLY; never auto-commit DML. This bead is labelled `sec`: it needs a second-agent adversarial review before the batch verify (plan 23.1), and any later non-critical finding becomes a `discovered-from` bug bead, not a planning round (plan section 24, R34).
Rule 17: a struct field and all its initializers, a trait method and its impls, an enum variant and its exhaustive matches land in one commit by one agent. Commit explicit paths only.
Confidentiality (constitution 9): fixtures and canaries are synthetic (e.g. schema OMCP_FX_<runid>, tenant ids 7/8); no customer, field or OCI identifiers anywhere.
Anti-ceremony (R24/R34): deliver code plus tests; no new process artifacts, manifests or report files beyond what running code branches on.
Seam: consumers T14.1, T14.6a, T13.5, T13.6 (and W7/W12 previews) wait on this bead.
Structure-owner check: the plan leaves the bind-HMAC key lifecycle open; this bead uses a per-process random key, so restart invalidates outstanding confirmations (already true of the tamper tokens) and audited bind HMACs are not comparable across restarts. Binding the envelope digest into the confirmation material here (before T14.6a) is this bead's decision, so the commit-flip hole closes as soon as the seam lands.
Behaviour change: agents that preview without `commit` and apply with `commit=true` must re-preview; document in the tool descriptions (T6.3 regenerates docs).

## Absorbs
None. No earlier bead covers this scope (plan section 23.2 absorbs column is empty for this task).

title: Impact surfaces: agent result hints, dashboard Change Review, session report, audit
description:
## Context
W14 (plan section 16; operator ruling R31) makes every approval show what the change will actually do before anyone confirms it: rows, dependents, predicted invalidations, effect changes, security findings, cost, locks and reversibility. Computing that picture must itself never execute anything the current level does not already admit ("a preview never executes a statement the current level refuses").

State at 1fbe6eb0 (re-derive line numbers with rg -n): `oracle_preview_sql` executes nothing and returns danger, required level, gate decision, objects affected, reason, safe alternative and a confirmation token, but no cost and no dependents; its args (`PreviewSqlArgs` in `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/args.rs`) accept only `sql`, while `ExecuteArgs` also takes `binds`, `commit`, `hold`, `capture_dbms_output`, `dbms_output_max_lines/chars` and `timeout_seconds`. `oracle_preview_dml` really executes inside savepoint `OMCP_PREVIEW_DML` (`dispatch/workspace.rs` `PREVIEW_SANDBOX`) and rolls back; it requires READ_WRITE (`ensure_workspace_level`) and its caveat admits autonomous work survives the rollback. Dependents appear only in `create_or_replace`/`patch_source` previews, one hop (`probe_dependents` in `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/intelligence.rs`); `compile_object` has none. Cost gates only `oracle_query` (EXPLAIN PLAN, `max_query_cost`); EXPLAIN PLAN is classified READ_WRITE because it writes `PLAN_TABLE`. PL/SQL `what_breaks`, `blast_radius` and `sast` exist as separate tools (`crates/oraclemcp/src/plsql_tools.rs`). Confirmation tokens bind the SQL text only: `ExecGrantStore::issue(material: &str)` stores a SQL digest, and `execute_grant_token_fields` / `sign_execute_grant_reference` (`dispatch/mod.rs`) sign only profile/session/lane/subject/generation/level.

Plan section 16 design item 5 (surfaces): the agent receives `impact` in the tool result, so it can self-correct; the dashboard Change Review renders it; the W3 session report (`oraclemcp audit report`, T3.7, an export of "what the agent did" from the existing hash chain) includes it; the audit entry stores the drift digest and the field statuses. Raw bind values and grant predicate values never appear on any surface. Dashboard code: `web/src/app/reviews-page.tsx`, `presentation-model.ts`, `operator-client.ts`; operator routes `crates/oraclemcp-core/src/http/operator.rs`. Audit records: `crates/oraclemcp-audit/src/record.rs`.

## Outcome
Every approval is visible with its impact on all four surfaces: tool results carry `impact` plus next-step hints per unavailable reason; the Change Review page renders each field with status; the session report shows impact per approval; audit entries store `decisive_digest` and field statuses (no values).

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/impact.rs`: reason -> next-step hint mapping (e.g. `level_below_required` -> `oracle_set_session_level` or `oracle_request_grant`; `needs_checkpoint` -> `oracle_checkpoint`).
- `crates/oraclemcp-audit/src/record.rs`: `impact_statuses` and `decisive_digest` in the audit detail for preview/apply entries (hash-chain compatible; `crates/oraclemcp-audit/src/verify.rs` and `crates/oraclemcp-verifier` accept the fields).
- Session report (T3.7 module): impact section per approval, golden-tested.
- Web: Change Review impact panel in `web/src/app/reviews-page.tsx` + presentation model; operator route returns impact for pending reviews.

## Implementation notes
1. Audit stores statuses and digests only; values of observations (rows, cost) may be stored as numbers; bind/predicate values never.
2. Report and dashboard render `unavailable(reason)` explicitly, never hide the field.
3. Redaction canaries (bind and predicate) are threaded through a live flow and asserted absent from every surface.

## Test plan
Rust: `audit_entry_contains_decisive_digest_and_statuses`, `audit_chain_verifies_with_impact_fields` (verifier), `session_report_golden_includes_impact` (golden file under the T3.7 goldens), `tool_result_hints_per_unavailable_reason`.
Web: `web/src/app/change-review-impact.test.tsx` (every field and status rendered).
E2E: `dashboard_change_review_impact_e2e` in `crates/oraclemcp/tests/dashboard_e2e.rs` (real binary, real preview, Change Review shows impact).
Canary: `impact_redaction_canary_absent_from_all_surfaces` (tool output, logs, audit, session report, dashboard payload).

## Proof split
Proves presentation and persistence. Impact correctness is T14.2-T14.5; refusal T14.6b; external goldens T14.9.

## Non-goals
No new impact fields; no dashboard approval of DDL (browser policy unchanged).

## No-claim boundary
Rendering an impact does not prove it is correct.

## Considerations
Fail-closed guard (AGENTS.md "The safety invariant", doctrine rule 1): tighten-only; never admit a statement not proven safe for the active level; never exceed profile max_level or the OAuth ceiling; protected profiles stay READ_ONLY; never auto-commit DML. This bead is labelled `sec`: it needs a second-agent adversarial review before the batch verify (plan 23.1), and any later non-critical finding becomes a `discovered-from` bug bead, not a planning round (plan section 24, R34).
Rule 17: a struct field and all its initializers, a trait method and its impls, an enum variant and its exhaustive matches land in one commit by one agent. Commit explicit paths only.
Confidentiality (constitution 9): fixtures and canaries are synthetic (e.g. schema OMCP_FX_<runid>, tenant ids 7/8); no customer, field or OCI identifiers anywhere.
Anti-ceremony (R24/R34): deliver code plus tests; no new process artifacts, manifests or report files beyond what running code branches on.
Audit format change must keep existing chains verifiable (additive fields only) and the published `oraclemcp-verifier` (W11) in sync.
File lanes `file-lane:dashboard` (shared with T12.10, T13.7) and `file-lane:dispatch`.

## Absorbs
None. No earlier bead covers this scope (plan section 23.2 absorbs column is empty for this task).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: A preview -> apply of a fixture UPDATE produces: a tool result with `impact` and hints, a Change Review page showing all seven fields with statuses, a session report section for that approval, and audit entries holding `decisive_digest` and field statuses; the audit chain still verifies.
- [ ] Negative: The bind and predicate canaries appear on none of the five outputs (tool, logs, audit, report, dashboard).
- [ ] Negative: An `unavailable` field is rendered as unavailable with its reason on the dashboard and in the report (hiding it fails the golden).
- [ ] Tests: `audit_entry_contains_decisive_digest_and_statuses`, `audit_chain_verifies_with_impact_fields`, `session_report_golden_includes_impact`, `tool_result_hints_per_unavailable_reason`, `change-review-impact.test.tsx`, `dashboard_change_review_impact_e2e`, `impact_redaction_canary_absent_from_all_surfaces` green.
- [ ] Proof class: live external client (dashboard e2e with the real binary) + unit/golden; forbidden substitutes: a stubbed server for the dashboard e2e.
- [ ] Consumers: R.1; T12.8 (change-request story in the same report).
- [ ] No-claim: Does not prove impact correctness.

title: W14 golden and differential live tests through the external client
description:
## Context
W14 (plan section 16; operator ruling R31) makes every approval show what the change will actually do before anyone confirms it: rows, dependents, predicted invalidations, effect changes, security findings, cost, locks and reversibility. Computing that picture must itself never execute anything the current level does not already admit ("a preview never executes a statement the current level refuses").

State at 1fbe6eb0 (re-derive line numbers with rg -n): `oracle_preview_sql` executes nothing and returns danger, required level, gate decision, objects affected, reason, safe alternative and a confirmation token, but no cost and no dependents; its args (`PreviewSqlArgs` in `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/args.rs`) accept only `sql`, while `ExecuteArgs` also takes `binds`, `commit`, `hold`, `capture_dbms_output`, `dbms_output_max_lines/chars` and `timeout_seconds`. `oracle_preview_dml` really executes inside savepoint `OMCP_PREVIEW_DML` (`dispatch/workspace.rs` `PREVIEW_SANDBOX`) and rolls back; it requires READ_WRITE (`ensure_workspace_level`) and its caveat admits autonomous work survives the rollback. Plan section 16 Tests and plan section 6 W4 rules (external client only: real release-profile binary over stdio and Streamable HTTP; fixture schema per run with run-id stamping (T4.3); deterministic verification; golden files with volatile fields scrubbed; JSONL per case). Definition of done item 8: predicted invalid sets equal the observed ones on the fixture and are a superset of them in general runs; tokens are refused after impact drift. Plan test list:
- Golden impact bundles on the W4 fixture schema.
- Differential (live): on the controlled fixture, after `create_or_replace` of a package with 3 dependents, predicted invalid set equals observed ALL_OBJECTS.STATUS = 'INVALID'; in general runs observed is a subset of the bounded prediction (false positives and truncation reported; a false negative fails); estimated rows equal observed rows on the isolated fixture.
- Token binding: a dependent altered between preview and apply -> apply refused; a changed bind value -> refused; an advancing SCN with unchanged facts does not invalidate; changed source with unchanged or coarse LAST_DDL_TIME still invalidates; a dictionary attack over low-entropy bind values cannot reproduce the logged keyed digest; bind redaction canaries never reach audit or session-report output; a local PLAN_TABLE with an autonomous INSERT trigger: no trigger fires and cost is unavailable or refused; a private-synonym shadow of PLAN_TABLE is refused; two interleaved plan requests each return only their own statement id.
- No side effects: preview_sql at READ_ONLY for an UPDATE returns a snapshot estimate with zero candidate-DML executions in audit (server-owned probes recorded separately); one negative per unsupported DML target shape returns `unavailable(unsupported_dml_shape)`; a preview of an UPDATE on a table with an autonomous trigger executes nothing.
- Honesty paths: `unavailable` paths without privilege (and on ADB via W9); a statement padded to time out at DDL is refused.

## Outcome
The W14 case set runs through the external client on FREE 23ai (tier A) and XE 18/21 (tier C), with scrubbed golden impact bundles and live differential checks, registered in the W4 matrix so T4.14 and T9.6a (ADB) include them.

## Deliverable
- Case definitions in the T4.2 tool-matrix driver; golden files under `tests/golden/impact/` (scrubbed: SCNs, timings, run ids, statement ids).
- Fixture additions (T4.3 schema): package with exactly 3 dependents (view, procedure, function) for equality; deeper chain for truncation; local `PLAN_TABLE` with autonomous INSERT trigger + canary table; private synonym `PLAN_TABLE`; table with autonomous trigger canary; INSTEAD OF view, inline-view target, partitioned table, a DB-link-qualified name (refused before any network use), CURRENT OF cursor procedure; an unprivileged profile for no_privilege paths.
- Case ids: `w4_impact_golden_{preview_sql_update,preview_sql_ddl,preview_dml,create_or_replace,patch_source,compile_object,set_session_level,request_grant}`, `w4_impact_dependents_fixture_equality`, `w4_impact_dependents_general_subset`, `w4_impact_rows_estimate_equals_observed`, `w4_impact_rows_read_only_estimate`, `w4_impact_rows_unsupported_shape_{instead_of_view,inline_view,partition_extended,remote,current_of,table_collection}`, `w4_impact_rows_autonomous_trigger_no_execution`, `w4_impact_token_dependent_altered_refused`, `w4_impact_token_changed_bind_refused`, `w4_impact_token_scn_advance_accepted`, `w4_impact_token_source_change_coarse_ddl_time_refused`, `w4_impact_bind_dictionary_attack_fails`, `w4_impact_bind_redaction_canary`, `w4_impact_cost_local_plan_table_trigger`, `w4_impact_cost_private_synonym_shadow_refused`, `w4_impact_cost_interleaved_ids`, `w4_impact_unavailable_no_privilege`, `w4_impact_decisive_timeout_ddl_refused`.

1. Refusal and no-side-effect cases assert audit zero candidate executions plus no V$SQL SQL_ID for the run-id tag; canary tables re-read by an independent session.

3. Interleaving uses two clients with DBMS_PIPE barriers.
4. Goldens scrub volatile fields with the existing golden scrubber framework (`crates/oraclemcp/tests/golden_scrubber_framework.rs` conventions).

## Test plan
The case ids above in the tier-A FREE 23ai lane (T4.11) and tier C XE 18/21; ADB coverage via T9.6a.

## Proof split
External-client proof for W14. Unit/in-process proofs are in T14.0-T14.8; ADB is T9.6a.

## Non-goals
No new product code; defects found become `discovered-from:T14.9` bugs against the owning W14 bead.

## No-claim boundary

## Considerations
Fail-closed guard (AGENTS.md "The safety invariant", doctrine rule 1): tighten-only; never admit a statement not proven safe for the active level; never exceed profile max_level or the OAuth ceiling; protected profiles stay READ_ONLY; never auto-commit DML. Rule 17: a struct field and all its initializers, a trait method and its impls, an enum variant and its exhaustive matches land in one commit by one agent. Commit explicit paths only.
Confidentiality (constitution 9): fixtures and canaries are synthetic (e.g. schema OMCP_FX_<runid>, tenant ids 7/8); no customer, field or OCI identifiers anywhere.
Anti-ceremony (R24/R34): deliver code plus tests; no new process artifacts, manifests or report files beyond what running code branches on.
Added dependency T4.2 (not in plan 23.2 for T14.9): the golden and differential cases must run through the external-client tool-matrix driver (W4 rule "external client only"); without T4.2 they could only run in-process, which is a forbidden substitute for these live claims.
Rate-limit and time-budget honesty cases are owned by T14.7 (its own acceptance), so this bead does not depend on T14.7.
File lane `file-lane:e2e`; fixture DDL only inside run-owned schemas (RULE 1, T4.3 janitor).

None. No earlier bead covers this scope (plan section 23.2 absorbs column is empty for this task).

title: ImpactBindingV1 decisive digest unchanged for decisive field 8 (proptest counterexample)
description:
## Context
Orchestrator batch gate at d46d8c03 (clean worktree): `prop_decisive_digest_changes_on_each_decisive_field` (crates/oraclemcp-guard/tests/impact_binding.rs:226, assertion at :261) FAILED with proptest minimal failing input `field = 8, change = 1`: the ImpactBindingV1 decisive digest is identical before and after the change (seed recorded as `cc 3fcf7d31...`). No code touched impact_binding since .16.2 closed at 5b5b93f7; the earlier passing runs simply did not hit this input.

Two possibilities: (a) the test's mutator for decisive field 8 is a no-op for change=1 (test defect, like .15.12), or (b) decisive field 8 is not actually bound into the digest / its encoding collides (product defect: an approval could carry a changed decisive fact). Treat as (b) until proven (a).

## Outcome
Root cause stated; if (b), every decisive field is bound into the canonical digest and a deterministic regression test pins field 8; if (a), the mutator always changes the field and a deterministic test proves each decisive field changes the digest. Commit the proptest regression seed.

## Considerations

title: ImpactBindingV1 type, canonical encoding, field statuses on every minting preview (seam)
description:
## Context
W14 (plan section 16; operator ruling R31) makes every approval show what the change will actually do before anyone confirms it: rows, dependents, predicted invalidations, effect changes, security findings, cost, locks and reversibility. Computing that picture must itself never execute anything the current level does not already admit ("a preview never executes a statement the current level refuses").

State at 1fbe6eb0 (re-derive line numbers with rg -n): `oracle_preview_sql` executes nothing and returns danger, required level, gate decision, objects affected, reason, safe alternative and a confirmation token, but no cost and no dependents; its args (`PreviewSqlArgs` in `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/args.rs`) accept only `sql`, while `ExecuteArgs` also takes `binds`, `commit`, `hold`, `capture_dbms_output`, `dbms_output_max_lines/chars` and `timeout_seconds`. `oracle_preview_dml` really executes inside savepoint `OMCP_PREVIEW_DML` (`dispatch/workspace.rs` `PREVIEW_SANDBOX`) and rolls back; it requires READ_WRITE (`ensure_workspace_level`) and its caveat admits autonomous work survives the rollback. Dependents appear only in `create_or_replace`/`patch_source` previews, one hop (`probe_dependents` in `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/intelligence.rs`); `compile_object` has none. Cost gates only `oracle_query` (EXPLAIN PLAN, `max_query_cost`); EXPLAIN PLAN is classified READ_WRITE because it writes `PLAN_TABLE`. PL/SQL `what_breaks`, `blast_radius` and `sast` exist as separate tools (`crates/oraclemcp/src/plsql_tools.rs`). Confirmation tokens bind the SQL text only: `ExecGrantStore::issue(material: &str)` stores a SQL digest, and `execute_grant_token_fields` / `sign_execute_grant_reference` (`dispatch/mod.rs`) sign only profile/session/lane/subject/generation/level.

Plan section 16 design items 1 and 3. `ImpactBindingV1` is a versioned, canonically encoded structure with two explicit sections: `decisive` (facts compared at apply: statement/source digest; keyed bind HMAC from the envelope; exact object identities and source/dependency/trigger hashes; object status and edition/compiler facts; effect-analysis engine version and ruleset digest; DB/PDB, CURRENT_SCHEMA, profile/lane generation; the W13 `scope_digest` typed as opaque `Option<[u8; 32]>` so the seam does not depend on W13) and `observations` (display and audit only, never compared: row estimates, cost, timings, field statuses, SCN bounds; a single `observed_at_scn` only when the query actually ran AS OF that SCN, otherwise `{scn_before, scn_after}`; an SCN that advances while every fact is unchanged must not invalidate a token). Every impact field carries `status: computed | estimated | unavailable(reason) | not_applicable(reason)` and is never silently omitted. Bounded and honest: a per-field time budget and depth/count caps; a timeout reports `unavailable(timeout)`.

## Outcome
`oraclemcp_guard::impact_binding` exports `ImpactBindingV1`, `ImpactV1` (rows, dependents, effects, sast, cost, locks, reversibility), `FieldStatus`, a closed `UnavailableReason`/`NotApplicableReason` set, `decisive_digest()` and a `FieldBudget` wrapper; every confirmation-minting preview returns an `impact` object with all seven fields present (initially `unavailable(not_wired)` until T14.2-T14.5 fill them).

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/impact_binding.rs` (new): `ImpactBindingV1 { version, decisive: DecisiveFacts, observations: Observations }`; `DecisiveFacts { envelope_digest, statement_digest, bind_hmac, objects: Vec<ObjectFact{identity, status, source_hash, dependency_hash, trigger_hash}>, edition, compiler_facts, engine_version, ruleset_digest, db_identity{dbid, con_uid}, current_schema, profile_generation, lane_generation, scope_digest: Option<[u8;32]> }` (each fact itself a `FieldStatus` so a missing fact is visible); `Observations { rows: Option<RowEstimate{kind, value, scn: ScnBounds, profile_generation}>, cost, timings, statuses }`; `ScnBounds::{AsOf(scn), Window{before, after}}`.
- `ImpactV1 { rows, dependents, effects, sast, cost, locks, reversibility }`, each `FieldStatus<T>` serialized always (no `skip_serializing_if`).
- Reasons: `level_below_required`, `untrusted_triggers`, `unsupported_dml_shape`, `engine_not_wired`, `read_only_txn`, `hard_parse_callbacks`, `vpd`, `no_privilege`, `plan_table_unverified`, `timeout`, `truncated`, `not_wired`.
- `FieldBudget::run(deadline, caps, fut) -> FieldStatus<T>` mapping timeout to `unavailable(timeout)` and cap hits to `truncated`.
- `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/mod.rs`: attach `impact` (all `unavailable(not_wired)`) to every confirmation-minting preview result.

## Implementation notes
1. Canonical encoding shared with T14.0 codec conventions; `decisive_digest` = SHA-256 over canonical `decisive` only (secret-bearing parts are already HMACs).
2. Observations never enter the digest; a test mutates every observation field and asserts the digest is unchanged.
3. Registry-driven discovery of minting previews: the test enumerates tools whose result schema carries a confirmation token (from `registry.rs`), not a hard-coded list.
4. JSON output schema for `impact` added to the tool output schemas so the T3.1 schema/runtime differential test covers it.

## Test plan
Unit (`crates/oraclemcp-guard/tests/impact_binding.rs`): `impact_every_field_serialized_with_status`, `impact_decisive_digest_ignores_observations`, `impact_scn_advance_does_not_change_decisive_digest`, `impact_observed_at_scn_only_with_as_of`, `impact_binding_version_mismatch_refused`, `field_budget_timeout_maps_to_unavailable_timeout`, `field_budget_cap_maps_to_truncated`.
Property: `prop_decisive_digest_changes_on_each_decisive_field`.
In-process: `impact_attached_to_every_minting_preview` (registry-driven).

## Proof split
Proves the binding type, encoding, status discipline and presence on every minting preview. Field computation is T14.2-T14.5; persistence/revalidation T14.6a; refusal matrix T14.6b.

## Non-goals
No field computation, no token persistence change, no refusal logic.

## No-claim boundary
An `impact` object being present does not mean any field is computed correctly.

## Considerations
Fail-closed guard (AGENTS.md "The safety invariant", doctrine rule 1): tighten-only; never admit a statement not proven safe for the active level; never exceed profile max_level or the OAuth ceiling; protected profiles stay READ_ONLY; never auto-commit DML. This bead is labelled `sec`: it needs a second-agent adversarial review before the batch verify (plan 23.1), and any later non-critical finding becomes a `discovered-from` bug bead, not a planning round (plan section 24, R34).
Rule 17: a struct field and all its initializers, a trait method and its impls, an enum variant and its exhaustive matches land in one commit by one agent. Commit explicit paths only.
Confidentiality (constitution 9): fixtures and canaries are synthetic (e.g. schema OMCP_FX_<runid>, tenant ids 7/8); no customer, field or OCI identifiers anywhere.
Anti-ceremony (R24/R34): deliver code plus tests; no new process artifacts, manifests or report files beyond what running code branches on.
Seam: T14.2, T14.3, T14.4, T14.5 and T14.6a wait on this bead.
Structure-owner check: attaching the `impact` object with `unavailable(not_wired)` fields at the seam is this bead's decision, so field beads fill their field without waiting on T14.8 (surfaces). The `not_wired` reason must be absent from every preview by the time T14.6b closes (asserted there).

## Absorbs
None. No earlier bead covers this scope (plan section 23.2 absorbs column is empty for this task).

- [ ] Positive: Every confirmation-minting preview (enumerated from the registry) returns an `impact` object containing rows, dependents, effects, sast, cost, locks and reversibility, each with a status.
- [ ] Negative: Changing only `observations` (cost, timings, SCN window) leaves `decisive_digest` unchanged; changing any single decisive fact changes it (property over all fields).
- [ ] Negative: A serializer that skips `unavailable` fields fails `impact_every_field_serialized_with_status`.
- [ ] Negative: `observed_at_scn` is emitted only for an AS OF query; otherwise the window form is used.
- [ ] Tests: `impact_*`, `field_budget_*`, `prop_decisive_digest_changes_on_each_decisive_field`, `impact_attached_to_every_minting_preview` green.
- [ ] Proof class: unit + live in-process (dispatch); forbidden substitutes: a hard-coded tool list in place of the registry enumeration.
- [ ] Consumers: T14.2, T14.3, T14.4, T14.5, T14.6a.
- [ ] No-claim: Does not prove any impact value is correct.

Plan section 16 design item 1 `rows`:
- For UPDATE/DELETE, a non-executing estimate is computed only when `DmlImpactShapeV1` proves an equivalent server-owned COUNT query for the fully resolved DML target and condition. That query is AST-derived and goes through `GuardedReadExecutor` (T1.2b) and `MutationEffectClosureV1` (T7.9a).
- Unsupported targets return `unavailable(unsupported_dml_shape)`: views with INSTEAD OF triggers, inline or multi-table views, partition-extended names, remote objects, CURRENT OF, TABLE() and ambiguous rewrites.
- A decisive action refuses when its required row field is unavailable (enforced by T14.6b).
- The estimate is returned as `{kind: snapshot_estimate, value, scn bounds, profile_generation}`.
- Apply returns `observed_rows` separately. Equality with the estimate is guaranteed only on isolated test fixtures, never claimed for concurrent production data. Row caps are W13's job.
- The sandbox `rows_affected` (the `preview_dml` machinery, savepoint `OMCP_PREVIEW_DML`) is computed only when: the session's effective level already admits the statement; the target's `MutationEffectClosureV1` is proven free of Autonomous/TxnControl/ExternalIo/DynamicSql/Unknown/SequenceAdvance effects; no sequence is advanced. Otherwise `not_applicable(level_below_required | untrusted_triggers)`.
- A preview never executes a statement the current level refuses.
Plan tests: `preview_sql` at READ_ONLY for an UPDATE returns a snapshot estimate and the audit shows zero candidate-DML executions, with server-owned impact probes recorded separately; one negative per unsupported target shape; a preview of an UPDATE on a table with an autonomous trigger executes nothing; estimated rows equal observed rows on the isolated fixture.

## Outcome
`oracle_preview_sql` (and the other DML-minting previews) fill `impact.rows` with a snapshot estimate or a typed unavailable/not_applicable reason; `oracle_preview_dml` executes its sandbox only under the three conditions (tightening today's behaviour); `oracle_execute` returns `observed_rows`; server-owned count probes are audited separately from candidate executions.

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/impact_binding.rs` (or sibling `dml_impact_shape.rs`): `DmlImpactShapeV1::prove(stmt, resolved) -> Result<CountQueryPlan, UnsupportedDmlShape>` producing the AST of `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "O"."T" WHERE (<where>) [AND (<policy Q>)]`.
- `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/impact.rs` (new, the dispatch-side home for W14 field computation): `compute_rows_impact(ctx, stmt) -> FieldStatus<RowsImpact>` running the count through `GuardedReadExecutor` with SCN window capture (`scn_before`/`scn_after`).
- `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/mod.rs` `preview_dml_inner`: gate the sandbox on level + closure + no sequence; otherwise return `not_applicable(...)` without executing. `execute_sql_inner`: add `observed_rows` to the result.
- Audit: server-owned impact probes recorded with a distinct audit class (`impact_probe`), never counted as candidate executions.

## Implementation notes
1. Shape proof: resolved single target of kind TABLE (not view, not remote, not partition-extended), no CURRENT OF, no TABLE(), WHERE expressible over the target alone (subqueries allowed only if the W1 proof admits the count read); otherwise unsupported.
2. The count read is a server read under the W1 proof (FGA closure, VPD proof); a VPD-protected target returns the count Oracle computes for this session (documented), never bypasses policy.
3. Sandbox gating uses `MutationEffectClosureV1` for the target plus the classifier's `non_transactional_effect` (sequence) flag.
4. At READ_ONLY, `preview_dml` never clears the backstop to run its sandbox: it reports `not_applicable(level_below_required)`.
5. Candidate statements in live tests carry a run-id comment; the probe carries a different server tag so V$SQL assertions can tell them apart.

Unit: `dml_shape_update_single_table_supported`, `dml_shape_delete_supported`, `dml_shape_unsupported_{instead_of_view,inline_view,multi_table_view,partition_extended,remote,current_of,table_collection,ambiguous}`.

External (T14.9): `w4_impact_rows_read_only_estimate`, `w4_impact_rows_unsupported_shape_*`, `w4_impact_rows_autonomous_trigger_no_execution`, `w4_impact_rows_estimate_equals_observed`.

## Proof split
Proves the rows field and sandbox gating (unit, in-process, live in-process). External-client proof and goldens are T14.9; decisive refusal on unavailable rows is T14.6b.

## Non-goals
No row caps (W13), no estimate equality claims for concurrent data, no INSERT/MERGE estimates (they report `unavailable(unsupported_dml_shape)`).

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove the estimate matches production row counts under concurrency.

## Considerations
Fail-closed guard (AGENTS.md "The safety invariant", doctrine rule 1): tighten-only; never admit a statement not proven safe for the active level; never exceed profile max_level or the OAuth ceiling; protected profiles stay READ_ONLY; never auto-commit DML. This bead is labelled `sec`: it needs a second-agent adversarial review before the batch verify (plan 23.1), and any later non-critical finding becomes a `discovered-from` bug bead, not a planning round (plan section 24, R34).
Rule 17: a struct field and all its initializers, a trait method and its impls, an enum variant and its exhaustive matches land in one commit by one agent. Commit explicit paths only.
Confidentiality (constitution 9): fixtures and canaries are synthetic (e.g. schema OMCP_FX_<runid>, tenant ids 7/8); no customer, field or OCI identifiers anywhere.
Anti-ceremony (R24/R34): deliver code plus tests; no new process artifacts, manifests or report files beyond what running code branches on.

Plan section 16 design item 1 `cost`, `locks`, `reversibility`, and W1 task 7 (T1.8). Today `explain_plan` (`crates/oraclemcp-db/src/intelligence.rs`) runs `EXPLAIN PLAN FOR <sql>` into an unqualified `PLAN_TABLE` with no statement id and reads `WHERE plan_id = (SELECT MAX(plan_id) FROM plan_table)`, so interleaved requests can read the wrong plan and a user's local PLAN_TABLE with triggers would receive the write. T1.8 hardens that path; this bead reuses it for impact:
- EXPLAIN is server-built only, in a savepoint that is always rolled back, and only for statements the classifier already admitted at preview ("admitted at preview" = classified with a known level, not admitted at the current level).
- STATEMENT_ID is string grammar, not a bind: a server-generated random id from a strict ASCII alphabet, rendered as a validated literal.
- PLAN_TABLE resolution before running. Accept only the expected PUBLIC synonym resolving to SYS.PLAN_TABLE$ with verified session-private temporary semantics and no local or private shadow, or an explicitly configured, server-owned GTT with pinned identity. Otherwise cost is `unavailable` and a decisive confirmation refuses.
- A server-fixed INTO is allowed; a caller-selected INTO is not. Reads and cleanup select only the generated statement id, never MAX(plan_id).
- At READ_ONLY, advisory cost reports `unavailable(read_only_txn)` instead of clearing the database-side backstop.
- `HardParseEffectClosureV1` (W1 task 7): a hard parse can run user code. EXPLAIN runs only when the closure proves no user callback can fire (extensible-optimizer ODCI callbacks ODCIStatsSelectivity/ODCIStatsFunctionCost/ODCIStatsIndexCost via associated statistics types from ALL_ASSOCIATIONS; domain-index optimizer callbacks; VPD/OLS/RAS/Redaction policy code; any callback whose identity or absence cannot be proven); otherwise `unavailable(hard_parse_callbacks)`. Missing privilege or truncated discovery means unavailable, and decisive confirmations refuse.
- Targets under a VPD policy report `unavailable(vpd)`.
- Claimed: EXPLAIN inside the backstop's READ ONLY transaction may raise ORA-01456; verify on 18c, 21c, 23ai and ADB; if it fails, cost reports `unavailable(read_only_txn)`; the backstop is never disarmed for it.
- `locks`: DML -> target tables; DDL on objects in use -> probed where privileged (DBA_DDL_LOCKS / V$ACCESS), else `unavailable(no_privilege)`.
- `reversibility`: `rolled_back_by_default`, `needs_checkpoint` (suggest `oracle_checkpoint`) or `irreversible`.
- Compare cost/cardinality against profile `max_query_cost` (`crates/oraclemcp-config/src/profile.rs`).

## Outcome
Previews fill `impact.cost` from the T1.8 hardened EXPLAIN (or a precise unavailable reason), `impact.locks` and `impact.reversibility`; no preview ever writes a non-verified PLAN_TABLE, fires an ODCI/policy callback, or disarms the READ_ONLY backstop; ORA-01456 behaviour is recorded per version.

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/impact.rs`: `compute_cost_impact` (calls the T1.8 API for statement-id EXPLAIN with a verified PLAN_TABLE and a proven `HardParseEffectClosureV1`), `compute_locks_impact`, `compute_reversibility`.
- `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/intelligence.rs`: lock probe queries as `CatalogQueryId` variants.
- Version-matrix recording of the ORA-01456 claim in the tier-C runner results (T4.1 runner).

## Implementation notes
1. Order: classify (known level) -> resolve PLAN_TABLE (T1.8) -> HardParseEffectClosureV1 -> if session READ_ONLY: `unavailable(read_only_txn)` -> SAVEPOINT -> EXPLAIN with literal statement id -> read by id -> ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT (always, including error paths) -> assert the id's rows are gone.
2. VPD detection comes from the W1 proof facts for the statement's relations.
3. Reversibility: DML without commit => rolled_back_by_default; DML with hold => needs_checkpoint; DDL/ADMIN, commit=true, sequence NEXTVAL => irreversible.
4. Locks: for DDL, DBA_DDL_LOCKS/V$ACCESS rows for the target when privileged; unprivileged => unavailable(no_privilege), never "no locks".

## Non-goals
No change to the `oracle_explain_plan` tool contract beyond what T1.8 does; no new EXPLAIN mechanism.

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove ADB ORA-01456 behaviour (T9.6a) or that every callback class on every version is discovered beyond T1.8's catalog sources.

Plan section 16 design item 3 (storage, revalidation) and plan 23.3 note for T14.6 ("compared vs recorded-only fields" and the `ExecGrantStore::issue` / `execute_grant_token_fields` change):
- The decisive digest goes into the immutable ExecGrant material and the signed token fields. Today `ExecGrantStore::issue` takes `material: &str` (the SQL) and stores `sql_digest(sql)`, and `execute_grant_token_fields` / `sign_execute_grant_reference` sign only profile/session/lane/subject/generation/level. This bead changes the material to `(sql_digest, decisive_digest)` and signs `decisive_digest`.
- Revalidation runs the bounded fact queries the action requires. It is not "one dictionary query", and it never re-runs the analysis. It happens immediately before token consumption and before execution. Any changed decisive fingerprint refuses with `REPREVIEW_REQUIRED`. This extends SEC-1 from "the statement text is unchanged" to "what it is bound to is unchanged".
- Residual race, stated honestly: concurrent DDL between the recheck and execution remains possible; the audit records both digests.
- Raw bind values are never stored in ExecGrant, audit records or logs; transient canonical bind buffers are cleared after the HMAC is computed.
- Decisive facts: statement/source digest; keyed bind HMAC; exact object identities and source/dependency/trigger hashes; object status, edition/compiler facts; engine version and ruleset digest; DB/PDB, CURRENT_SCHEMA, profile/lane generation; W13 scope_digest. Observations never compared; an advancing SCN with unchanged facts must not invalidate; changed source with unchanged or coarse LAST_DDL_TIME still invalidates.

## Outcome
Every confirmation minted by a preview stores and signs `(sql_digest, decisive_digest)`; before consuming a confirmation and again before executing, the server re-runs a bounded, action-specific set of fact queries, recomputes the decisive digest and refuses with `REPREVIEW_REQUIRED` on any difference; audit records both digests; no raw bind value reaches ExecGrant, audit or logs.

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/exec_grant.rs`: `issue(material: GrantMaterial { sql_digest, decisive_digest }, ...)`, `Entry` stores both, `consume` verifies both (rule 17: all callers migrated in the same commit; no compat shim).
- `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/mod.rs`: `execute_grant_token_fields` adds hex `decisive_digest`; `sign_execute_grant_reference` / `verify_execute_grant_reference` / `issue_confirmation_grant` / `consume_execute_confirmation` migrated.
- `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/impact.rs`: `DecisiveFactProbe` per fact kind (object identity/status/hash, dependency hash, trigger hash, edition/compiler facts, CURRENT_SCHEMA/DB identity, scope_digest provider) with a declared per-action query bound; `revalidate_decisive(action, stored_digest) -> Result<(), RepreviewRequired>`.
- Audit record fields (`crates/oraclemcp-audit/src/record.rs` detail): `statement_digest`, `decisive_digest`, `revalidated_at` stage.

## Implementation notes
1. Material digest domain-separated (`omcp/exec-grant/material/v1`).
2. Revalidation recomputes only facts (hashes, identities, statuses), never effect analysis, SAST or blast radius; source hashes are content hashes, so a same-second recompile with new source is caught.
3. Two checkpoints: before `ExecGrantStore::consume` (a stale token is not burned) and immediately before the database call.
4. Each action declares its maximum revalidation query count; a test asserts the bound.
5. Canonical bind buffers `Zeroizing`; audit stores only HMACs.

Unit: `exec_grant_material_binds_decisive_digest`, `exec_grant_consume_rejects_decisive_mismatch`, `token_fields_sign_decisive_digest_tamper_refused`.

## Non-goals
No action-specific matrix (T14.6b); no closing of the residual DDL race (stated, audited).

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove absence of concurrent DDL between the final recheck and execution.

title: Decisive-field matrix per action; fail-closed REPREVIEW_REQUIRED and unavailable refusal
description:
## Context
W14 (plan section 16; operator ruling R31) makes every approval show what the change will actually do before anyone confirms it: rows, dependents, predicted invalidations, effect changes, security findings, cost, locks and reversibility. Computing that picture must itself never execute anything the current level does not already admit ("a preview never executes a statement the current level refuses").

State at 1fbe6eb0 (re-derive line numbers with rg -n): `oracle_preview_sql` executes nothing and returns danger, required level, gate decision, objects affected, reason, safe alternative and a confirmation token, but no cost and no dependents; its args (`PreviewSqlArgs` in `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/args.rs`) accept only `sql`, while `ExecuteArgs` also takes `binds`, `commit`, `hold`, `capture_dbms_output`, `dbms_output_max_lines/chars` and `timeout_seconds`. `oracle_preview_dml` really executes inside savepoint `OMCP_PREVIEW_DML` (`dispatch/workspace.rs` `PREVIEW_SANDBOX`) and rolls back; it requires READ_WRITE (`ensure_workspace_level`) and its caveat admits autonomous work survives the rollback. Dependents appear only in `create_or_replace`/`patch_source` previews, one hop (`probe_dependents` in `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/intelligence.rs`); `compile_object` has none. Cost gates only `oracle_query` (EXPLAIN PLAN, `max_query_cost`); EXPLAIN PLAN is classified READ_WRITE because it writes `PLAN_TABLE`. PL/SQL `what_breaks`, `blast_radius` and `sast` exist as separate tools (`crates/oraclemcp/src/plsql_tools.rs`). Confirmation tokens bind the SQL text only: `ExecGrantStore::issue(material: &str)` stores a SQL digest, and `execute_grant_token_fields` / `sign_execute_grant_reference` (`dispatch/mod.rs`) sign only profile/session/lane/subject/generation/level.

Plan section 16 design items 3 (decisive-field matrix, owned by this bead) and 4 (bounded and honest). Every listed field must be `computed`, or the confirmation refuses:

| Action | Required decisive fields |
|---|---|
| Generic DML (preview_sql/execute) | envelope; object identities; MutationEffectClosureV1; rows (when DmlImpactShapeV1 supports the shape, else advisory); edition/schema/generation |
| DDL / ADMIN statement | envelope; object identities; dependents + predicted invalid set; DdlEffectClosureV1; effects of changed source; reversibility |
| Session elevation (set_session_level) | envelope (level, TTL); profile/OAuth ceiling; generation |
| Custom package call | envelope; closure fact key; RoutineEffectsV1; DdlEffectClosureV1 (for DDL); masking-profile output check |
| W12 promotion | the complete DBA_OBJECTS_AE manifest + changed manifest; DB/PDB identity; default == base; parentage; USE/PUBLIC exposure; service editions; DdlEffectClosureV1 (for create/drop) |
| W13 grant creation/use | envelope; scope_digest (incl. MutationEffectClosureV1); rows (pre-count); policy floor; generation |

Decisive fields always refuse: for W12 promotion, W13 grant creation and use, custom-tool DDL and every ADMIN action, an unavailable or truncated decisive field always refuses the confirmation, regardless of configuration; an agent cannot hide impact by forcing a timeout. `require_impact` (T14.7) governs only advisory fields. Plan test: a statement padded to time out at DDL is refused (decisive field unavailable).

## Outcome
A single `DecisiveFieldMatrixV1` maps every `ActionKind` to its required decisive fields; preview does not mint and apply does not execute when any required field is not `computed` (typed `IMPACT_DECISIVE_UNAVAILABLE{field, reason}`) or when revalidation differs (`REPREVIEW_REQUIRED`). Rows for generic DML are decisive only when the shape is supported. No preview reports `not_wired`.

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/impact_binding.rs`: `DecisiveFieldMatrixV1::required(action: &ActionKind, ctx) -> &[DecisiveField]` (exhaustive match; adding an `ActionKind` variant without a row does not compile) and `check_decisive(binding, required) -> Result<(), DecisiveRefusal>`.
- `crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/mod.rs`: enforcement at every minting preview and every apply path (execute, compile_object, create_or_replace, patch_source, set_session_level, custom-tool calls; W12/W13 consume the same function).
- Error taxonomy: `IMPACT_DECISIVE_UNAVAILABLE` and `IMPACT_DECISIVE_TRUNCATED` with refusal hints.
- Fields that belong to other workstreams (DdlEffectClosureV1 from T7.9b, W12 manifests, masking-profile check from W7) are referenced by field id here; their producers fill them.

## Implementation notes
1. Matrix is data plus an exhaustive match; the registry test maps every minting tool to an ActionKind.
2. Generic DML rows: decisive iff `DmlImpactShapeV1` supported the shape; else advisory (status still shown).
3. Timeouts: a decisive field hitting its `FieldBudget` yields `unavailable(timeout)` -> refusal; there is no configuration to waive it.
4. Apply path calls T14.6a revalidation then `check_decisive` against the stored binding.
5. Assert `not_wired` never appears once this bead lands.

## Test plan
Unit: `decisive_matrix_every_action_kind_has_row`, `decisive_unavailable_refuses_for_each_row_field` (table test: each required field set to unavailable in turn), `decisive_truncated_dependents_refuses_ddl`, `generic_dml_unsupported_shape_rows_advisory_only`, `admin_action_unavailable_always_refuses`, `require_impact_false_cannot_waive_decisive`.
In-process: `every_minting_tool_maps_to_action_kind` (registry-driven), `no_preview_reports_not_wired`.
Live in-process (FREE 23ai): `ddl_padded_to_timeout_refused` (dependents probe forced over budget via a fixture with a deep dependency chain and a lowered test budget).
External (T14.9): `w4_impact_decisive_timeout_ddl_refused`.

## Proof split
Proves the matrix and fail-closed refusal. Field computations are T14.2-T14.5 and the W7/W12/W13 producers; external proof T14.9.

## Non-goals
No advisory `require_impact` handling or rate limit (T14.7); no new fact producers.

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove the correctness of any producer's field value.

## Considerations
Fail-closed guard (AGENTS.md "The safety invariant", doctrine rule 1): tighten-only; never admit a statement not proven safe for the active level; never exceed profile max_level or the OAuth ceiling; protected profiles stay READ_ONLY; never auto-commit DML. This bead is labelled `sec`: it needs a second-agent adversarial review before the batch verify (plan 23.1), and any later non-critical finding becomes a `discovered-from` bug bead, not a planning round (plan section 24, R34).
Rule 17: a struct field and all its initializers, a trait method and its impls, an enum variant and its exhaustive matches land in one commit by one agent. Commit explicit paths only.
Confidentiality (constitution 9): fixtures and canaries are synthetic (e.g. schema OMCP_FX_<runid>, tenant ids 7/8); no customer, field or OCI identifiers anywhere.
Anti-ceremony (R24/R34): deliver code plus tests; no new process artifacts, manifests or report files beyond what running code branches on.
Consumers W12 (T12.5, T12.7) and W13 (T13.5, T13.6) must call this function, not reimplement lists (same one-admission-function discipline as RoutineEffectsV1).

## Absorbs
None. No earlier bead covers this scope (plan section 23.2 absorbs column is empty for this task).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: For each ActionKind, a binding with every required field `computed` passes `check_decisive` and the action proceeds.
- [ ] Negative: For each row of the matrix and each required field, setting that field to `unavailable(timeout)` refuses the confirmation (table test; an implementation checking only some fields fails).
- [ ] Negative: A DDL statement whose dependents probe exceeds its time budget is refused (padding cannot hide impact).
- [ ] Negative: Truncated dependents refuse a DDL confirmation.
- [ ] Negative: An ADMIN action with any unavailable decisive field is refused even with `require_impact=false`.
- [ ] Negative: Adding an ActionKind without a matrix row fails to compile (exhaustive match).
- [ ] Tests: `decisive_*`, `generic_dml_unsupported_shape_rows_advisory_only`, `admin_action_unavailable_always_refuses`, `require_impact_false_cannot_waive_decisive`, `every_minting_tool_maps_to_action_kind`, `no_preview_reports_not_wired`, `ddl_padded_to_timeout_refused` green.
- [ ] Proof class: unit + live in-process; forbidden substitutes: a hard-coded tool list in place of the registry mapping.
- [ ] Consumers: T14.7, T14.8, T14.9, T13.5, T13.6, T12.5, T12.7.
- [ ] No-claim: Does not prove the correctness of any producer's field value.

title: W5 CI tiers: honest, lightweight three-tier CI + local gate (R10, R24)
description:
## Goal
CI that is honest but lightweight (R10, R24): three explicit tiers, no permanently red lane anywhere, scheduled failures noticed, and release evidence committed before the tag.

## Current state (dishonest today, measured 2026-09-23)
- `Fuzz Campaign` (`.github/workflows/fuzz.yml`) fails at "Set up job" on every scheduled run since 2026-09-18 and fuzzes nothing. GitHub's annotation names the cause: the pinned `actions/cache` SHA `0c45773b623bea8c8e75f6c82b208c3cf94ea4f9` (added by `774f0550` "ci: persist guard fuzz corpora") is refused as a deprecated version. `scripts/ci_heartbeat.sh` watches scheduled lanes but only required lanes drive its exit code, so the heartbeat stayed green for 6 days.
- Permanently red advisory lanes in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `windows-rust` (audit DACL, fixed by W10), `api-lock` (yanked `oracledb =0.9.1` in the published 0.10.0 baseline, fixed by T8.3/`ft0ti.1`), `coverage-ratchet` and `release-metadata` (stale mutation seal; `release_preflight.sh` runs `mutation_safety_gate.sh check-report`).
- The `plsql-intelligence` lane is advisory for OOM on the hosted runner while `scripts/e2e/COVERAGE.md` row "PL/SQL-intelligence feature lane" says "PASS (verified locally ...)".
- `thin-db` only builds. Only FREE 23ai runs live in CI (`oracle-free23`).
- Siblings: driver `Required` red since 2026-08-06, driver `Canary` red daily; engine `bindgen-roundtrip` red and disabled by inactivity.

## Target shape (plan §7)
| Tier | What | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| A: required PR/push | fmt, clippy, `cargo test --workspace`, deny/supply-chain, docs drift, boundary + seam lints, installer smoke, FREE 23ai lane running the W4 suite, PL/SQL-intelligence build + tests, windows-rust (restored after W10), api-lock (restored by `ft0ti.1`), stable-toolchain check (Linux/macOS, T8.13) | Bounded runtime: the W4 lane has a hard 25-minute budget; if it runs over it is split by tool family, never `continue-on-error`. The matrix is generated from the registry, so an unregistered tool fails the lane. Verdicts are derived fail-closed (`r0pd`). |
| B: scheduled | fuzz (`fuzz.yml`, repaired), version matrix | The heartbeat reports scheduled-lane failures. A red tier-B lane blocks the release tag. |
| C: release-only | W4 on XE 18/21, FREE 23ai and ADB; loom; kani; multi-nightly; feature-powerset; the OCI lane | Run on the exact release-candidate SHA. Results feed the release proof, committed before tagging. |

Removed rather than left red: `coverage-ratchet` and `release-metadata`, permanently (the mutation seal gates no user-facing capability; the re-seal `2q4em.5.3` was retired under R34). `thin-db` goes too, or it gets a real connect. Experimental lanes are explicitly non-release and never contribute green status.

Honesty fixes: repair `fuzz.yml`; correct `COVERAGE.md`; apply the same tier rules in the driver and engine repos (fix `bindgen-roundtrip`).

Release proof (T5.5): the existing D3.2 file (`scripts/local_release_gate.sh`, `scripts/local_release_gate_check.sh`, `tests/artifacts/local_gate/results-<sha>.json`) grows three fields (`tested_candidate_sha`, sibling SHAs + crate checksums, tier-C pass/fail); the tag workflow verifies it. No new manifest format (R34 cut the richer one).

## Invariants
- No `continue-on-error` on a tier-A lane; no lane left permanently red; advisory/experimental lanes never count as green.
- Anti-ceremony (R24/R34): no freshness SLO, no mutation/fuzz threshold formalism, no new manifest format, no additional lanes beyond this table.
- Binding rules: RULE 1 (no file/dir deletion without an exact in-session operator command); commit only explicit paths (`git commit -- <path>...`, then `git show --stat HEAD`, constitution #18); never `-a`/`git add -A`; pushes and tags need the operator's go-ahead; confidentiality (#9): no live-OCI, customer or field identifiers in any committed artifact, synthetic only; close only through `scripts/bead_tracker_guard.sh close` with committed evidence (implementers never self-close); workspace-wide cargo runs go through `scripts/build_lease.sh` with a dedicated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.

## Acceptance (epic)
DoD #4: tier-A lanes green in all three repos; tier-B lanes green on their last run; tier-C results recorded in the release proof; no permanently red lane anywhere.

## Size
5 tasks.

## Dependencies
T5.3 waits on T10.3 (Windows) and T8.3 (semver baseline). T5.4 waits on T0.2a/T0.3a. T5.5 waits on T4.11, T9.1, T4.1. Related owners outside W5: T4.11 (tier-A W4 lane with 25-minute budget + tier-C runner infra), T7.4 (PL/SQL lane CI memory, making the PL/SQL build required), T8.13 (stable-toolchain jobs), T8.12 (boundary/seam lints).

T5.1, T5.2, T5.3, T5.4, T5.5

title: Repair fuzz.yml (deprecated actions/cache pin); heartbeat fails on red scheduled lanes
description:
## Context
Plan §2.1 "Hidden red": the `Fuzz Campaign` fails at "Set up job" every night since 2026-09-18; it fuzzes nothing, and the heartbeat doesn't act on scheduled lanes. Plan §7 tier B: "The heartbeat reports scheduled-lane failures (the observed defect: fuzz was red for 6 days, unnoticed). A red tier-B lane blocks the release tag."

Measured root cause (GitHub annotation on run 35839299781, 2026-09-23, all 8 matrix jobs failing in ~7 s at "Set up job"): "This request has been automatically failed because it uses a deprecated version of `actions/cache: 0c45773b623bea8c8e75f6c82b208c3cf94ea4f9`." That SHA (commented `# v4`) is used by the `actions/cache/restore` and `actions/cache/save` steps added in `774f0550` "ci: persist guard fuzz corpora" (2026-09-17). `fuzz.yml` also uses unpinned `actions/checkout@v7` and `actions/upload-artifact@v7`, unlike the SHA-pinned actions elsewhere (e.g. `release.yml` pins checkout `3d3c42e5...` `# v7`).

Heartbeat today (`scripts/ci_heartbeat.sh`, driven by `.github/workflows/ci-heartbeat.yml` every 30 min): watches required lanes and the scheduled lanes named in `docs/ci_taxonomy.json` (tier `scheduled`, per job), but **only required lanes drive the exit code**; scheduled reds "ride GitHub's scheduled-workflow-failure notification", which is exactly what failed. The driver lane is advisory by R1 and must stay so.

Absorbed `ge6xe.5` (in_progress): promote the two guard libfuzzers (classify, differential alter-session) to a scheduled lane with a persistent corpus; the lane and corpus persistence exist in `fuzz.yml` but never ran.

## Outcome
The scheduled Fuzz Campaign runs all 8 matrix jobs to completion on schedule with the guard corpora persisted, and any red or unknown tier-B (scheduled) lane of oraclemcp makes the heartbeat fail and blocks a release tag.

## Deliverable
- `.github/workflows/fuzz.yml`: replace the deprecated `actions/cache/restore` and `actions/cache/save` pin with the SHA of the current `actions/cache` v4 release (v4.3.0 was the newest v4 tag on 2026-09-23; re-verify with `gh api repos/actions/cache/git/refs/tags`), and pin `actions/checkout` / `actions/upload-artifact` to the same SHAs the other workflows use.
- `scripts/ci_heartbeat.sh`: scheduled server lanes (tier `scheduled`, excluding the heartbeat itself) that are red or unknown on their latest completed scheduled run now count toward the exit code; snapshot JSON gains `scheduled_not_green: [check names]`; the stderr banner names them. Driver rows stay `driver_advisory` (notify=0, R1).
- `scripts/release_preflight.sh` (runs in `release.yml` `checks` on tags): refuses a tag when `scripts/ci_heartbeat.sh` reports any `scheduled_not_green` entry.
- `scripts/test_ci_heartbeat.sh`: new cases (below).
- `docs/ci-taxonomy.md` / heartbeat header comment: describe the new exit semantics in one paragraph.

## Implementation notes
1. Release the stale claim on `ge6xe.5` (`scripts/bead_tracker_guard.sh release-claim oraclemcp-ge6xe.5`).
2. Pin fix; run `bash scripts/workflow_supply_chain_check.sh` (the release gate's workflow dependency policy) and `python3 scripts/ci_taxonomy.py --check-workflows`.
3. `gh workflow run fuzz.yml` on the fix SHA; confirm all 8 jobs pass "Set up job", run the 300 s campaign, and upload artifacts; the corpus save step runs only on `schedule`, so also confirm the next scheduled run.
4. Heartbeat change: reuse `watch_server_scheduled_jobs`; flip `notify` to 1 for server scheduled rows; keep `record_unknown_server_scheduled_jobs` counting as not green (fail-closed: unknown is not green). No freshness SLO (cut by R34).
5. Tag refusal: in `release_preflight.sh`, run the heartbeat with `CI_HEARTBEAT_OUTPUT` set and fail if `scheduled_not_green` is non-empty; print `lane -> found conclusion -> expected success`.
6. Note: `mutation-safety.yml` scheduled shards are currently tier `scheduled` and green; T5.2 removes their schedule. Whichever lands second regenerates `docs/ci_taxonomy.json`.

## Test plan
- `scripts/test_ci_heartbeat.sh` new cases with recorded `gh api` fixtures: `scheduled_red_exits_nonzero`, `scheduled_setup_failure_exits_nonzero` (the observed failure shape: job conclusion failure with only "Set up job"), `scheduled_unknown_exits_nonzero`, `scheduled_green_required_green_exits_zero`, `driver_advisory_red_still_exits_zero` (R1 preserved). Each logs `{case, expected_exit, actual_exit, scheduled_not_green}` as JSONL.
- Live: fuzz.yml dispatch run URL green; the next scheduled run green; heartbeat run after it green.

## Proof split
Proves the fuzz lane runs and that scheduled reds are no longer silent and block tags. Fuzz-target quality (what the targets assert) belongs to the guard work (T1.3 seeds); tier re-classification is T5.2.

## Non-goals
- New fuzz targets or seeds (T1.3, T7.3, T13.2/T13.3 own theirs).
- Freshness SLOs, fuzz acceptance thresholds (cut by R34).
- Changing the driver advisory status (R1).

## No-claim boundary
A green fuzz lane does not prove the guard is bypass-free; it proves the campaign ran without a crash for its time budget.

## Considerations
- Honest badge semantics: after this change a red fuzz lane turns the heartbeat red - that is the intended notification path.
- Supply chain: pin by full SHA with a version comment, consistent with `scripts/workflow_supply_chain_check.sh`.
- Hot lane `file-lane:ci-workflows` shared with T5.2, T5.3, T5.4, T4.11, T7.4, T8.13, T10.3.
- Binding rules: RULE 1 (no file/dir deletion without an exact in-session operator command); commit only explicit paths (`git commit -- <path>...`, then `git show --stat HEAD`, constitution #18); never `-a`/`git add -A`; pushes and tags need the operator's go-ahead; confidentiality (#9): no live-OCI, customer or field identifiers in any committed artifact, synthetic only; close only through `scripts/bead_tracker_guard.sh close` with committed evidence (implementers never self-close); workspace-wide cargo runs go through `scripts/build_lease.sh` with a dedicated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.

## Absorbs
- `oraclemcp-ge6xe.5` (promote the two libfuzzers to a scheduled lane with persistent corpus): kept fully - the scheduled lane, persistent per-shard corpus, crash artifacts failing the lane; this bead makes it actually run and makes its failure visible.
