title: Remove permanently red lanes, re-tier per plan 7, fix COVERAGE.md, fail-closed verdicts
description:
## Context
Plan §7 (R10 honest but lightweight, R24 no ceremony). "Removed rather than left red: coverage-ratchet and release-metadata, permanently. The mutation seal gates no user-facing capability, and re-sealing it is a heavy campaign (R24). `thin-db` goes too, or it gets a real connect. Experimental lanes are explicitly non-release and never contribute green status." Honesty fix: correct `COVERAGE.md`. Tier A verdicts are derived fail-closed (`r0pd`). §17/§24: the mutation re-seal `2q4em.5.3` is retired under R34; "its lanes are removed permanently".

Measured in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (re-derive with `rg -n` at HEAD):
- `coverage-ratchet` ("changed-line coverage + mutation floor"): `continue-on-error: true`, blocked by the stale mutation seal.
- `release-metadata` ("release metadata sync"): `continue-on-error: true`; runs `scripts/release_preflight.sh`, whose `mutation_safety_gate.sh check-report` (line ~131) hard-fails `E_STALE_SEAL`. `release.yml` `checks` sets `ALLOW_STALE_MUTATION_SEAL: "1"` to pass the same preflight on tags.
- `thin-db` ("build thin driver"): `cargo build -p oraclemcp --features dashboard-bundle` only; live connect is already proven by `oracle-free23`.
- `.github/workflows/mutation-safety.yml`: nightly `schedule` (5 surfaces x 2 shard offsets, tier `scheduled`, green) that only accrues seal evidence.
- Tier mismatches vs §7: `kani-safety.yml` (push/PR, tier `required`), `loom.yml` (weekly schedule), `multi-nightly` (PR, advisory), `feature-powerset` (push, required) all belong to **tier C** (release-only, run on the exact RC SHA, results in the release proof).
- `plsql-intelligence` job: advisory for OOM; `scripts/e2e/COVERAGE.md` row "PL/SQL-intelligence feature lane" says "PASS (feature build + tool-registration assertion verified locally in an isolated target dir)".
- Verdict derivation: `scripts/ci_taxonomy.py` `status_report()` / `job_is_success()` (fixtures in `tests/ci_taxonomy/`, run by `--check-fixtures` in the `boundary` job); taxonomy tiers are derived from `continue-on-error`/triggers and committed in `docs/ci_taxonomy.json` + `crates/oraclemcp-core/ci_taxonomy.json`.

## Outcome
ci.yml has no permanently red or `continue-on-error` lane other than the explicitly experimental `fuzz-build` and the three awaiting restoration by other beads (`windows-rust`, `api-lock` -> T5.3; `plsql-intelligence` -> T7.4); tier-C lanes run only on release candidates; `COVERAGE.md` states what CI actually proves; and the CI verdict distinguishes crash, red, unknown, advisory and unexpanded check names while never calling any of them green.

## Deliverable
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: delete jobs `coverage-ratchet`, `release-metadata`, `thin-db`; move `multi-nightly` and `feature-powerset` to tier C (trigger: `workflow_dispatch` with the candidate SHA / called by the tier-C runner from T4.11; no `push`/`pull_request`).
- `.github/workflows/kani-safety.yml`, `.github/workflows/loom.yml`: triggers -> `workflow_dispatch` (tier C, run on the RC SHA by R.1/R.5).
- `.github/workflows/mutation-safety.yml`: remove the `schedule:` trigger (manual-only, never contributes to status).
- `scripts/release_preflight.sh`: remove the `mutation_safety_gate.sh check-report` call; `.github/workflows/release.yml` `checks`: remove `ALLOW_STALE_MUTATION_SEAL` and its comment.
- `scripts/ci_taxonomy.py`: tier `release` for tier-C lanes; `status_report()` gains `infrastructure_failed` (conclusions `startup_failure`, `cancelled`, `timed_out`, or a failed job whose only failed step is "Set up job"), rejects check names containing unexpanded `${{ ... }}` as `unknown_jobs`, treats `skipped`/`neutral` on a non-path-filtered required job as not green, and keeps `advisory_not_green` visible but never green-contributing.
- `tests/ci_taxonomy/`: new fixtures `crash-startup-failure-run.json`, `cancelled-required-run.json`, `unexpanded-expression-run.json`, `skipped-required-run.json`, `advisory-green-required-red-run.json`.
- `scripts/e2e/COVERAGE.md`: PL/SQL row -> "ADVISORY in CI (OOM on hosted 2-core runner); local-only pass; required after T7.4"; every other row whose status cites only a local run gets the same treatment.
- Regenerated: `docs/ci_taxonomy.json`, `crates/oraclemcp-core/ci_taxonomy.json`, `docs/test-tiers.md` and `docs/ci-taxonomy.md` tier tables (A = required, B = scheduled, C = release).

## Implementation notes
1. Edit ci.yml job by job; update the long advisory comments that promise re-requirement "when the re-seal lands" (they become false).
2. `release_preflight.sh`: remove the seal check only; every other preflight check stays and must pass without the env override.
3. Re-tier: kani/loom/multi-nightly/feature-powerset keep their job definitions; only triggers change. They run at R.1 (RC SHA) and R.5 (post-publish consumer SHA) via the tier-C runner (T4.11); their pass/fail enters the release proof (T5.5). No path filters or new lanes are added.
4. `ci_taxonomy.py`: extend `status_report` without changing the `ci-taxonomy/v1` fields consumers already read (`ci_green`, `required_not_green`, ...); add fields, never remove.
5. `python3 scripts/ci_taxonomy.py --write` then `--check`; the heartbeat fixture tests (T5.1 cases) stay green.
6. COVERAGE.md sweep: `rg -n 'verified locally|locally' scripts/e2e/COVERAGE.md` and fix each row honestly.
7. File deletions (the now-unused `scripts/coverage_ratchet.{py,sh}`, `scripts/coverage_baseline.{py,sh}`, `scripts/mutation_safety_gate.sh`, `.github/workflows/mutation-safety.yml` and their tests) are **not** executed without an exact operator command (RULE 1; not covered by R17/R32). Propose them in the bead comment; if not approved, leave them unreferenced by any lane.

## Test plan
- `python3 scripts/ci_taxonomy.py --check-fixtures` with the new fixtures; each fixture logs `{fixture, expected_verdict, actual_verdict}`.
- `python3 scripts/ci_taxonomy.py --check` (committed taxonomy == derived).
- `bash scripts/release_preflight.sh` passes locally with no `ALLOW_STALE_MUTATION_SEAL` set.
- ci.yml run on the change SHA: every remaining non-advisory job green; the removed jobs absent from check-runs; `ci_taxonomy.py --status <sha>` reports `ci_green: true`.

## Proof split
Proves lane removal/re-tiering, honest COVERAGE.md, and fail-closed verdict derivation. T5.1 proves tier-B reporting; T5.3 restores windows-rust/api-lock; T7.4 makes the PL/SQL lane required; T4.11 runs tier C; T5.5 binds tier-C results.

## Non-goals
- Mutation re-seal and any mutation/coverage threshold (retired, R34).
- Adopting nextest, fast pre-gate targets, or optional CI optimizations (bb42/3osj/8odq scope beyond the tier split is dropped, R24).
- Fixing the PL/SQL lane's memory (T7.4).

## No-claim boundary
A green tier A no longer includes kani/loom/feature-powerset/multi-nightly; their proof is the tier-C result in the release proof, not the PR check.

## Considerations
- `sec`: kani (guard + audit BMC proofs) moves from every push to every release candidate per the plan's §7 tier C. It still blocks the tag through the release proof. Second-agent review required before the batch verify.
- Structure-owner check: `thin-db` is removed rather than given a real connect (the FREE 23ai lane already connects live).
- Structure-owner check: the plan names a tier-B "version matrix"; oraclemcp has no scheduled version-matrix workflow (XE 18/21 runs are tier C), so the tier-B version matrix is the driver's scheduled `version-matrix.yml` handled in T5.4.
- Structure-owner check: deleting the unused mutation/coverage scripts and `mutation-safety.yml` needs an operator command; default is schedule removal only.
- Structure-owner check: moving kani/loom/multi-nightly/feature-powerset triggers to release-only is assigned here because no other W5 task owns the §7 re-tiering.
- Hot lane `file-lane:ci-workflows`.
- Binding rules: RULE 1 (no file/dir deletion without an exact in-session operator command); commit only explicit paths (`git commit -- <path>...`, then `git show --stat HEAD`, constitution #18); never `-a`/`git add -A`; pushes and tags need the operator's go-ahead; confidentiality (#9): no live-OCI, customer or field identifiers in any committed artifact, synthetic only; close only through `scripts/bead_tracker_guard.sh close` with committed evidence (implementers never self-close); workspace-wide cargo runs go through `scripts/build_lease.sh` with a dedicated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.

## Absorbs
- `oraclemcp-d-server-gate-honesty-r0pd`: kept fully - crash vs red vs unknown vs advisory vs unexpanded-expression fixtures with distinct correct outcomes, none counted green. (Anchoring drift guards on version tokens is already done by `release_surface_sync_check.sh`; not extended.)
- `oraclemcp-d-server-nextest-bb42`: kept only - no doctest or live-serialization loss while lanes move; nextest adoption dropped (R24).
- `oraclemcp-d-server-fast-pregate-3osj`: kept - fast tier A on push vs heavy tier C on release candidates; the 5-minute target and merge-group fan-out dropped (R24).
- `oraclemcp-d-server-optional-ci-efficiency-8odq`: nothing kept beyond removing dead lanes; optional optimizations dropped (R24).

- [ ] Positive: ci.yml on the change SHA has no `coverage-ratchet`, `release-metadata` or `thin-db` check-runs, and `python3 scripts/ci_taxonomy.py --status <sha>` reports `ci_green: true`.
- [ ] Positive: `kani-safety.yml`, `loom.yml`, `multi-nightly`, `feature-powerset` are tier `release` in `docs/ci_taxonomy.json` and do not run on push.
- [ ] Positive: `scripts/e2e/COVERAGE.md` PL/SQL row says ADVISORY/local-only until T7.4.
- [ ] Negative: Fixtures crash-startup-failure-run, cancelled-required-run, unexpanded-expression-run, skipped-required-run each yield `ci_green: false` with the cause in its own field.

- [ ] Consumers: T5.1, T5.3, T5.5, T4.11, R.1, R.5.
- [ ] No-claim: Does not prove tier-C lanes pass; only that they are release-only and cannot fake green.

title: Restore windows-rust and api-lock as required tier-A lanes
description:
## Context
Plan §7 tier A lists **windows-rust** ("restored after W10") and **api-lock** ("restored by `ft0ti.1`"). Both were demoted by R2 (2026-09-17): in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` both jobs carry `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` and `continue-on-error: true`, which `scripts/ci_taxonomy.py` classifies as `advisory`.
- `windows-rust` ("Rust workspace (Windows)", `windows-latest`): red on the native-Windows audit-DACL gap (`xuaea`, R21). W10 fixes it; T10.3 delivers "windows-rust green" plus the minimal Windows proof tier.
- `api-lock` ("public-API lock (cargo public-api + semver-checks)"): red because the published v0.10.0 baseline transitively pins the yanked `oracledb =0.9.1`, which `cargo-semver-checks` can't resolve. T8.3 (`ft0ti.1`) delivers a reproducible semver baseline. The job runs `bash scripts/oraclemcp_api_lock.sh` and `cargo semver-checks check-release -p oraclemcp-error -p oraclemcp-guard -p oraclemcp-db` (T11.1 adds `oraclemcp-verifier`).
The `windows-latest` runner is native, so this is not blocked-born (§23.1).

## Outcome
Both lanes run on every push and PR as required checks, are green on main, and a red in either blocks the badge and the release like any other tier-A lane.

## Deliverable
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` jobs `windows-rust` and `api-lock`: remove `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` and `continue-on-error: true`; replace the demotion comments with one line naming the owning proof (T10.3 / T8.3).
- Regenerated `docs/ci_taxonomy.json` and `crates/oraclemcp-core/ci_taxonomy.json` (both jobs -> `required`); `docs/test-tiers.md` rows.

## Implementation notes
1. Confirm T10.3 and T8.3 are closed and both lanes were green on their last PR runs.
2. Edit the two jobs; `python3 scripts/ci_taxonomy.py --write` and `--check`.
3. Push; both lanes must be green on two consecutive main pushes (one is not enough to distinguish a flake from a fix); read the verdicts yourself.
4. The heartbeat picks them up automatically from the taxonomy (required tier).

## Test plan
- CI: two consecutive green main runs of `Rust workspace (Windows)` and `public-API lock` on push events.
- `python3 scripts/ci_taxonomy.py --check` green; `--status <sha>` lists both under required with success.

## Proof split
Proves the lanes are required and green. The Windows security property is proved by T10.1-T10.3; the baseline's reproducibility by T8.3.

## Non-goals
- Fixing Windows audit security (W10) or the semver baseline (T8.3).
- Adding the verifier to the API lock (T11.1).

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove Windows ACL correctness beyond what the windows-rust test suite asserts.

## Considerations
- Hot lane `file-lane:ci-workflows`.
- If either lane goes red again after promotion, it is fixed, not re-demoted (constitution #2).
- Binding rules: RULE 1 (no file/dir deletion without an exact in-session operator command); commit only explicit paths (`git commit -- <path>...`, then `git show --stat HEAD`, constitution #18); never `-a`/`git add -A`; pushes and tags need the operator's go-ahead; confidentiality (#9): no live-OCI, customer or field identifiers in any committed artifact, synthetic only; close only through `scripts/bead_tracker_guard.sh close` with committed evidence (implementers never self-close); workspace-wide cargo runs go through `scripts/build_lease.sh` with a dedicated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.

title: Apply the tier rules in the driver and engine repos (no permanently red lanes)
description:
## Context
Plan §7: "apply the same tier rules in the driver and engine repos (fix `bindgen-roundtrip`, red since 09-05)". DoD #4: tier-A lanes green in all three repos; tier-B green on their last run; no permanently red lane anywhere. Tier rules: A = required on push/PR, no `continue-on-error`; B = scheduled, a red run is reported and blocks the release tag; C = release-only on the exact RC SHA.

Measured 2026-09-23:
- rust-oracledb workflows: `required.yml` (calls reusable `_quality.yml` with `profile: required`; red on `origin/main` head since 2026-08-06 - T0.2b fixes it), `ci.yml`, `canary.yml` (scheduled, **red daily**; failing steps "Validate release metadata", "Supply-chain checks", "Verify checked entry traces and release/evidence contracts", "Aggregate quality results"), `live.yml` (scheduled, green), `version-matrix.yml` (scheduled, green - this is the plan's tier-B "version matrix"), `tsan.yml` (scheduled, green), `soak.yml`, `release-qualification.yml`, `release.yml` (tag `v*`).
- plsql-intelligence workflows: `ci.yml` (push; last run green 2026-07-01), `plsql-gate.yml`, `plsql-change-impact-selftest.yml`, `bindgen-roundtrip.yml` (scheduled, red, `disabled_inactivity` - T0.3b fixes and re-enables it), `usr.yml` (`usr-loop`, scheduled, green until disabled by inactivity), `release.yml` (tag; GitHub release binaries, no crates publish).
- oraclemcp's heartbeat (`scripts/ci_heartbeat.sh`) already watches the driver's `required.yml` as `driver_advisory` (R1: never fails oraclemcp's heartbeat).

## Outcome
Each sibling workflow is classified A/B/C; no sibling lane is permanently red (each red lane is fixed or removed); sibling tier-B scheduled lanes are active (not disabled by inactivity) and their red state is reported in oraclemcp's heartbeat snapshot as advisory rows; and R.1 can check sibling tier-A/B green mechanically.

## Deliverable
- rust-oracledb: `canary.yml` fixed (root causes of the four failing steps) or, if it duplicates `required.yml` content, its schedule removed (workflow file deletion only on operator command); tier noted in a header comment of each workflow (one line: `# tier: A|B|C`).
- plsql-intelligence: `usr.yml` re-enabled (`gh workflow enable`) or its schedule removed; tier header comment per workflow.
- oraclemcp `scripts/ci_heartbeat.sh`: `DRIVER_REQUIRED_WORKFLOWS` stays; add the siblings' tier-B workflows (`version-matrix.yml`, `live.yml`, `tsan.yml` for the driver; `bindgen-roundtrip.yml`, `usr.yml` for the engine) as advisory rows (notify=0, consistent with R1) in the snapshot under `sibling_scheduled`; `scripts/test_ci_heartbeat.sh` fixture case for a red sibling scheduled lane (reported, exit 0).

## Implementation notes
1. List every workflow in both repos with its triggers and last 5 conclusions (`gh run list -R ... --workflow <f>`); assign A/B/C by the rule above.
2. Canary: pull logs, fix root causes (likely stale release metadata/version surfaces after the 0.9.3 republish and supply-chain policy drift); coordinate with T0.2b, which fixes overlapping checks in the required profile - land each fix once, in whichever bead reaches it first, and reference it in the other.
3. Scheduled workflows in a repo with no commits for 60 days are disabled by GitHub; re-enable with the operator's go-ahead (outward-facing); train commits keep them active.
4. Heartbeat: extend the snapshot only; the exit code stays driven by oraclemcp's own lanes (R1). R.1 reads `sibling_scheduled` and treats any red as blocking the tag (DoD #4).

## Test plan
- CI: last run of every sibling tier-A and tier-B workflow green (URLs in the bead comment).
- `scripts/test_ci_heartbeat.sh` case `sibling_scheduled_red_reported_advisory` (row present, exit 0).

## Proof split
Proves sibling tier classification and no permanently red sibling lane. Driver `Required` green is T0.2b; `bindgen-roundtrip` is T0.3b; oraclemcp tiers are T5.1/T5.2.

## Non-goals
- New sibling lanes or a sibling-local heartbeat (R24).
- Changing R1 (driver lanes stay advisory in oraclemcp's heartbeat exit code).

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove sibling code correctness; only lane honesty and visibility.

## Considerations
- Structure-owner check: T0.2b ("tiered CI" in the driver) and this bead overlap; the split used here is T0.2b = driver `Required` green, T5.4 = tier classification + scheduled/canary lanes in both siblings + heartbeat visibility.

## Absorbs
None.

title: Extend D3.2 release proof: tested_candidate_sha, sibling SHAs + checksums, tier-C results
description:
## Context
Plan §23.3 T5.5: "Extend `scripts/local_release_gate.sh` / `local_release_gate_check.sh` and `tests/artifacts/local_gate/results-<sha>.json` with `tested_candidate_sha`, the sibling SHAs, crate checksums and tier-C pass/fail. The release.yml verify step checks it. No new manifest format: the existing D3.2 file grows three fields." §24: kept minimal; the tag workflow branches on it; the defect it prevents was observed in the 0.11.0 re-tag anchoring; a richer manifest (capability matrix, image digests, freshness) was cut, and "more digests" was rejected as ceremony.

Plan §19.4 steps 5-7 (binding): R.5 reruns tier A and **all** tier-C lanes against crates.io-resolved versions; every R.5 tier-C result names the post-publish consumer SHA and the lockfile digest. The proof is committed as an **evidence-only commit** whose first parent is the tested candidate; it may change only canonical evidence paths; it can't contain its own SHA, so it records `tested_candidate_sha`, which must equal the evidence commit's first parent. It binds `tested_candidate_sha`, driver and engine SHAs, crate checksums (published crates == tested ones) and tier-C pass/fail. The tag workflow **verifies** and never generates evidence after publication has started: parent == `tested_candidate_sha`; parent-to-tag diff evidence-only; sibling SHAs, checksums and result digests match; cheap static and tag-time gates pass.

Current D3.2 (measured):
- `scripts/local_release_gate.sh` runs the synthetic OCI/TCPS proof (`cargo test -p oraclemcp-core --test oci_tcps_e2e profile_wallet_and_iam_token_reach_local_tcps_terminator`), writes `results-<short12 sha>.json` (`schema_version: 1`, `gate`, `source_sha`, `created_at`, `confidentiality{committed_identifiers, server_certificate_subject: "CN=oracle-test.invalid", real_adb_evidence: "out-of-band; never committed"}`, `checks[]`), with `--commit-proof` writing under `tests/artifacts/local_gate/`; `proof_scan` rejects `ocid1.`, `the Oracle Cloud wildcard certificate-CN pattern`, private keys, `todelete` markers.
- `scripts/local_release_gate_check.sh` validates schema 1, `source_sha`, confidentiality fields, all checks pass, forbidden markers; accepts HEAD^'s proof when `git diff --name-only HEAD^..HEAD` touches only `tests/artifacts/local_gate/`. Required on tag refs; called by `scripts/release_preflight.sh` (release.yml `checks` step "Validate release metadata") and `scripts/release_acceptance_ci_suite.sh`.
- Inputs from other beads: the tier-C runner (T4.1 rig for XE 18/21/FREE 23ai; T4.11 tier-C runner infra) and the ADB harness (T9.1, OCI lane in tier C, redaction at capture) write per-lane results JSON.

## Outcome
A release proof in the existing D3.2 file that, once committed as an evidence-only child of the tested candidate, lets the tag workflow mechanically verify - offline, before any publish step - that the tag's parent is exactly the tested candidate, that the sibling crates on crates.io are byte-identical to the tested ones, and that every required tier-C lane passed on that candidate with the recorded lockfile.

## Deliverable
- `scripts/local_release_gate.sh`: new inputs `--tested-candidate <40-hex sha>`, `--siblings <json>` (driver/engine repo, SHA, version, and per-crate `{name, version, sha256}` from R.2's `.crate` files), `--tier-c-dir <dir>` (per-lane result files from the T4.11/T9.1 runners); writes `schema_version: 2` with three new top-level fields `tested_candidate_sha`, `siblings`, `tier_c` (array of `{lane, target, status, consumer_sha, lockfile_sha256, results_path, results_sha256}`), and copies the per-lane results files under `tests/artifacts/local_gate/tier-c-<short sha>/`.
- `scripts/local_release_gate_check.sh`: for schema 2 (required on tags from v0.12.0): `tested_candidate_sha` == `git rev-parse HEAD^` when HEAD is the evidence commit (and == HEAD for a pre-commit dry check); parent-to-HEAD diff only under `tests/artifacts/local_gate/`; every required lane present with `status: pass` (lanes: W4 on `xe18`, `xe21`, `free23`, `adb`; `loom`; `kani`; `multi-nightly`; `feature-powerset`; `oci`) and each `consumer_sha` == `tested_candidate_sha` and `lockfile_sha256` == sha256 of `Cargo.lock` at that SHA; each `results_sha256` matches the committed file; every sibling crate `sha256` equals the `checksum` of that crate in `Cargo.lock` at `tested_candidate_sha` (crates.io checksums after R.5); sibling SHAs equal the sibling repos' `v0.10.0` / `v0.8.0` tag commits (`git ls-remote`; unreachable = failure, never a pass). Failure messages use `field -> found -> expected`.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: no new job; the existing `checks` job path (`release_preflight.sh` -> `local_release_gate_check.sh --require`) runs these verifications before any publish job (re-derive the `needs:` chain and keep every publish job downstream of `checks`).
- `docs/release-checklist.md`: the proof step described in one paragraph.

## Implementation notes
1. Keep schema-1 acceptance for historical proofs in `tests/artifacts/local_gate/` (existing files stay valid for non-tag checks); require schema 2 in tag context when the tag version is >= 0.12.0.
2. Lockfile digest: `git show <sha>:Cargo.lock | sha256sum`.
3. Crate checksum identity: R.2 records the `sha256` of each sibling `.crate` from `cargo package` at the frozen SHA; after R.3/R.4 publication, `Cargo.lock` (R.5) carries crates.io's checksum for each; equality proves the published bytes are the tested bytes.
4. Confidentiality: `proof_scan` runs over the proof and every copied tier-C results file; ADB results arrive already redacted (T9.1) and must still pass the scan.
5. The check never calls the network except `git ls-remote` for sibling tags; it never writes evidence.

## Test plan
- `tests/release_contract_test.sh` new cases on temp git repos (synthetic SHAs, synthetic crate names): `local_gate_v2_accepts_evidence_only_child`, `local_gate_v2_rejects_parent_mismatch`, `local_gate_v2_rejects_non_evidence_path_in_diff`, `local_gate_v2_rejects_missing_tier_c_lane` (drop `adb`), `local_gate_v2_rejects_failed_tier_c_lane`, `local_gate_v2_rejects_consumer_sha_mismatch`, `local_gate_v2_rejects_lockfile_digest_mismatch`, `local_gate_v2_rejects_results_digest_mismatch`, `local_gate_v2_rejects_sibling_checksum_mismatch`, `local_gate_v2_rejects_forbidden_marker_in_tier_c_results`, `local_gate_v1_rejected_for_0_12_tag`, `local_gate_v1_still_accepted_for_non_tag`. Each case logs `{case, expected, actual, exit}` JSONL.
- `bash scripts/release_acceptance_ci_suite.sh` still green.

## Proof split
Proves the proof format and its verification. The contents are produced by R.1/R.5 (runs), R.2 (checksums) and written/committed by R.6; R.7 exercises verification on the real tag.

## Non-goals
- A new manifest format, capability matrices, image digests, freshness fields (cut by R34).
- Running tier-C lanes (T4.11, T9.1, R.1, R.5).
- Release-acceptance de-duplication flag plumbing (gkcz beyond binding each result once is dropped).

## No-claim boundary
A valid proof shows the recorded lanes passed on the recorded SHA with the recorded lockfile; it does not re-prove behaviour, and it does not prove channels after publication (R.7).

## Considerations
- Structure-owner check: "crate checksums prove the published crates equal the tested ones" assumes `cargo package` output is byte-reproducible; if R.2's reproducibility re-run shows otherwise, R.3/R.4 must publish from the recorded frozen checkout and verify the index checksum against R.2's record immediately, and this check compares against that record.
- Structure-owner check: tier-C results files are committed under `tests/artifacts/local_gate/tier-c-<sha>/` so digests are verifiable offline at tag time; they are canonical evidence paths.
- Confidentiality (#9): only synthetic identifiers; ADB results are redacted at capture and scanned again here.
- Hot lane `file-lane:release-gate` shared with T0.1, R.6, R.7.
- Binding rules: RULE 1 (no file/dir deletion without an exact in-session operator command); commit only explicit paths (`git commit -- <path>...`, then `git show --stat HEAD`, constitution #18); never `-a`/`git add -A`; pushes and tags need the operator's go-ahead; confidentiality (#9): no live-OCI, customer or field identifiers in any committed artifact, synthetic only; close only through `scripts/bead_tracker_guard.sh close` with committed evidence (implementers never self-close); workspace-wide cargo runs go through `scripts/build_lease.sh` with a dedicated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.

## Absorbs
- `oraclemcp-b-server-release-surface-runbook-t8rs`: kept - specific `field -> found -> expected` diagnostics in the check; the pre-publish same-tag retry message and binary headroom ratchet dropped (R24).
- `oraclemcp-b-server-acceptance-dedupe-gkcz`: kept - each tier-C lane (incl. feature-powerset) is run once per candidate and bound once in the proof; release-acceptance flag plumbing dropped.
- `oraclemcp-d-server-exact-sha-tag-gate-reuse-egzz`: kept fully - only complete same-SHA evidence is accepted; missing, stale, incomplete or mismatched evidence fails closed.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: `scripts/local_release_gate.sh --commit-proof --tested-candidate <sha> --siblings <file> --tier-c-dir <dir>` writes a schema-2 `results-<sha>.json` with `tested_candidate_sha`, `siblings` and `tier_c`, and `scripts/local_release_gate_check.sh --require` accepts it at an evidence-only child commit.
- [ ] Negative: Each planted defect is refused with a field-specific message: parent != tested_candidate_sha; a non-evidence path in the parent-to-HEAD diff; missing `adb` lane; a failed lane; consumer_sha or lockfile digest mismatch; results file digest mismatch; a sibling crate checksum differing from Cargo.lock; an `ocid1.` string inside a tier-C results file; a schema-1 proof for a 0.12.0 tag.
- [ ] Tests: `tests/release_contract_test.sh` cases local_gate_v2_accepts_evidence_only_child, local_gate_v2_rejects_parent_mismatch, local_gate_v2_rejects_non_evidence_path_in_diff, local_gate_v2_rejects_missing_tier_c_lane, local_gate_v2_rejects_failed_tier_c_lane, local_gate_v2_rejects_consumer_sha_mismatch, local_gate_v2_rejects_lockfile_digest_mismatch, local_gate_v2_rejects_results_digest_mismatch, local_gate_v2_rejects_sibling_checksum_mismatch, local_gate_v2_rejects_forbidden_marker_in_tier_c_results, local_gate_v1_rejected_for_0_12_tag, local_gate_v1_still_accepted_for_non_tag.
- [ ] Proof class: offline (temp git repos, synthetic data); forbidden substitutes: generating evidence inside the tag workflow, accepting a proof from a non-parent commit, network-fetched results.
- [ ] Consumers: R.6, R.7.
- [ ] No-claim: Does not prove any lane's behaviour or any post-publication channel.

description:
## Context

The driver's own crates.io README loses the "discontinued" disclaimer in 0.10.0 (done in T0.5, published in R.4).
- SECURITY.md supported line -> 0.12.x (`2q4em.3.4`).
- The README image claim becomes true: one image with PL/SQL-intelligence built in (T7.4 removes the Docker variant matrix and makes the engine part of every artifact).

- `README.md` ~266: "An optional `--features plsql-intelligence` build embeds the offline PL/SQL engine (also published as the `:plsql-intelligence-latest` GHCR image)" - false today.
- `docs/comparison.md` ~27 and ~57: "the frozen, async `oraclemcp-driver-cx` 0.9.2".
- `docs/toolchain.md` ~39-82: asupersync/driver-cx nightly attribution naming 0.9.2.

## Outcome
README, AGENTS.md, `docs/toolchain.md` and `docs/comparison.md` state that driver-cx is oraclemcp's maintained, primary driver and that PL/SQL-intelligence is built into the single image and every archive; SECURITY.md names 0.12.x as the current line; lint checks refuse the stale phrases.

- `scripts/release_surface_sync_check.sh`: assert SECURITY.md's current-line row equals the workspace `major.minor.x`.

## Implementation notes
1. Wait for T7.4 (single image + default feature) so the image claim is true when written.
2. Edit prose by hand (no bulk sed); run `/de-slopify` on changed paragraphs.
3. README front page (tqxj, bounded): keep positioning, install, quickstart, safety invariant and support links on the front page; move only paragraphs this bead rewrites if they are detail; every anchor still resolves (`scripts/docs_generate.sh --check` + a link check over README anchors).

title: Regenerate tool/config docs for the v2 contract; worked tools.d custom PL/SQL tool example
description:
## Context
Plan §8: tool/config docs regenerated; a worked `tools.d` example for custom PL/SQL tools. §19.4 step 0: final docs (T6.3) land before the candidate freeze so the proven SHA contains them.

Inputs that change the surface: T3.1 strict decoding; T3.2 enums, `get_source` VIEW, `search_objects.object_types`, array payloads; T3.3 unified argument names + deprecated aliases (R9: old names kept as deprecated aliases, removal in 0.14.0, conflict rule); T7.10 package-call custom tools (structured signed definitions, live activation, named-notation wrapper, name-capture check, masked-profile output refusal) loaded from `tools.d`; T12.7 `oracle_change_request` submit/withdraw/promote; T13.6 `oracle_request_grant` (preview/apply/status/drop). Config fields added by the train (e.g. `edition_change_requests` from T12.2, keepalive default 10 from T2.2b) appear through the typed config renderer.

Measured: `scripts/docs_generate.sh` (`--write`/`--check`/`--selftest`) fills fenced `<!-- generated:<id> -->` blocks in `README.md` and `docs/configuration.md` (`tools`, `tools-aliases` from `crates/oraclemcp/src/registry.rs` via `oraclemcp robot-docs tools --markdown`; `config` via `oraclemcp robot-docs config --markdown`). It **refuses a renderer built with `plsql-intelligence`** because "the README tables document the default distribution"; after T7.4 the engine is part of the default distribution, so that refusal must be inverted. The drift check runs in the `boundary` job. No `tools.d` documentation exists yet.

## Outcome
README and `docs/configuration.md` generated blocks match the default 0.12.0 build (including the 9 PL/SQL tools, `oracle_change_request`, `oracle_request_grant`, and every deprecated alias with its 0.14.0 removal note), and a worked `tools.d` example for a custom PL/SQL package-call tool exists and is proven to load.

## Deliverable

- Regenerated blocks in `README.md` and `docs/configuration.md`.
- `docs/configuration.md` new section "Custom PL/SQL tools (`tools.d`)": where the directory lives, the signed definition format from T7.10, activation, refusal behaviour (mixed-effect routines refused, masked profiles refuse output), with one worked example.
- Example definition file `docs/examples/tools.d/<synthetic_package_call>.toml` (synthetic schema/package names only) - a new file justified as user-facing example content.

## Implementation notes
1. After all six deps close, build the default binary through the lease and run `scripts/docs_generate.sh --write`.
2. Review the diff by hand: every tool, alias (with deprecation text from T3.3) and config field present; no feature-gated tool missing.

## Test plan
- `scripts/docs_generate.sh --check` and `--selftest` green in the `boundary` lane.
- `tools_d_docs_example_loads` unit test green; a copy with a flipped signature byte is refused (`tools_d_docs_example_tampered_is_refused`).

## Proof split
Proves docs match the served surface and the example is loadable. Behaviour of the tools is proved by W3/W4/W7/W12/W13 tests.

## Non-goals
- Hand-written tool tables; CHANGELOG/release notes (R.0).

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove the documented tools behave as described beyond registry/schema equality.

## Considerations
- Confidentiality: the example uses synthetic names only.
- Hot lane `file-lane:docs` (README.md shared with T6.1, T6.2, R.0).
- Binding rules: RULE 1 (no file/dir deletion without an exact in-session operator command); commit only explicit paths (`git commit -- <path>...`, then `git show --stat HEAD`, constitution #18); never `-a`/`git add -A`; pushes and tags need the operator's go-ahead; confidentiality (#9): no live-OCI, customer or field identifiers in any committed artifact, synthetic only; close only through `scripts/bead_tracker_guard.sh close` with committed evidence (implementers never self-close); workspace-wide cargo runs go through `scripts/build_lease.sh` with a dedicated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.

description:
## Goal

## Current state (measured 2026-09-23)
- `crates/oraclemcp-verifier` is a workspace member at 0.11.0 with no README and no `readme` key.
- `scripts/publish_crates.sh --print-order` derives the order from cargo metadata (`scripts/release_surface_manifest.py --publish-order`) and already prints `...audit, guard, verifier, config...`; `tests/release_contract_test.sh` already pins that full order in `expected_current_order`.
- **Measured deviation from the plan text:** crates.io already lists `oraclemcp-verifier` 0.11.0 (created 2026-09-17T19:01Z, published by the v0.11.0 tag pipeline). The plan's "new on crates.io" is stale; 0.12.0 is its second release. The remaining W11 work is unchanged.
- `scripts/oraclemcp_api_lock.sh` locks only `oraclemcp-error`, `oraclemcp-guard`, `oraclemcp-db`.

## Design (plan §13)
- Test asserting the verifier's position in `--print-order` (nothing consumes it, so the test pins the position rather than "before consumers").
- Crate README + complete package metadata; `cargo package --list` check; public-API lock entry; `cargo publish --dry-run`; exact crates.io post-publication verification in release acceptance (`2q4em.4.4`).

## Invariants
- No new publish script; `publish_crates.sh` stays the single derivation of publish order.
- Governance: RULE 1, explicit-path commits, crates.io publishes only through the tag pipeline with operator go-ahead.

## Acceptance (epic)
The v0.12.0 pipeline publishes `oraclemcp-verifier` 0.12.0 and release acceptance verifies it on crates.io exactly.

## Size
1 task.

## Dependencies
None to start. R.5 (package dry runs, api-lock regen) and R.7 (publish + verify) consume it.

T11.1

Plan §13: `scripts/publish_crates.sh` already derives every publishable workspace crate and its order from cargo metadata, and its print order includes the verifier (`...audit, guard, verifier, config...`). Work: a test pinning that position (nothing consumes the verifier, so it pins the position rather than "before consumers"); the missing crate README and complete package metadata; a `cargo package --list` check; the public-API lock entry; `cargo publish --dry-run`; exact crates.io post-publication verification in release acceptance (`2q4em.4.4`).

Measured 2026-09-23:
- `crates/oraclemcp-verifier/Cargo.toml`: version 0.11.0, `description = "Standalone external verifier for redacted oraclemcp verdict certificates"`, workspace-inherited edition/license/repository/homepage/keywords/categories; **no `readme`, no `documentation`**; deps `oraclemcp-audit`, `oraclemcp-guard` (path + `0.11.0`), serde, serde_json, thiserror. Lib `src/lib.rs`, `src/attestation.rs`, bin under `src/bin/` (`oraclemcp-test-attest`), tests `served_verdict_certificate.rs`, `verdict_verifier.rs`, `test_attestation.rs`, `test_attest_cli.rs` with `tests/fixtures/`.
- **Deviation from plan text:** crates.io already has `oraclemcp-verifier` 0.11.0 (created 2026-09-17T19:01Z by the v0.11.0 pipeline). 0.12.0 will be its second release.
- `tests/release_contract_test.sh` already asserts the full `publish_crates.sh --print-order` list (`expected_current_order`: error, telemetry, audit, guard, verifier, config, db, auth, core, oraclemcp).
- `publish_crates.sh` runs `cargo publish -p <crate> --locked --dry-run` then publish per crate, and polls crates.io until the exact version appears (bounded retry; validates the registry response incl. `yanked=false`).
- API lock: `scripts/oraclemcp_api_lock.sh` `LOCKED_CRATES=(oraclemcp-error oraclemcp-guard oraclemcp-db)`, baselines `crates/<crate>/api/<crate>.txt`; ci.yml `api-lock` runs it plus `cargo semver-checks check-release -p oraclemcp-error -p oraclemcp-guard -p oraclemcp-db`.
- Crate-count statements: README ("9 pure-Rust crates + binary") and AGENTS.md ("9 `oraclemcp-*` library crates plus the `oraclemcp` binary") match the workspace (9 libraries incl. the verifier + binary).

## Outcome
The verifier ships in v0.12.0 as a first-class crate: README on crates.io, complete metadata, a pinned package file list, a locked public API with semver checks, a green dry run, and release acceptance that fails if `oraclemcp-verifier` 0.12.0 is not installable from crates.io after publication.

## Deliverable
- `crates/oraclemcp-verifier/README.md` (new): what it verifies (ADR-0010 verdict certificates; the `oraclemcp-test-attest` binary), install (`cargo install oraclemcp-verifier`), offline usage, trust-policy pointer to `docs/operations.md`.
- `crates/oraclemcp-verifier/Cargo.toml`: `readme = "README.md"`, `documentation = "https://docs.rs/oraclemcp-verifier"`, `include` (or `exclude`) so the package has `src/**`, `README.md`, license files, and no test fixtures unless needed.
- `tests/release_contract_test.sh`: keep the existing order assertion (it is the print-order test); add case `verifier_package_list` asserting `cargo package --list -p oraclemcp-verifier --allow-dirty` equals a committed expected list.
- `scripts/oraclemcp_api_lock.sh`: add `oraclemcp-verifier` to `LOCKED_CRATES`; baseline `crates/oraclemcp-verifier/api/oraclemcp-verifier.txt` (`cargo public-api -p oraclemcp-verifier`); `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `api-lock`: add `-p oraclemcp-verifier` to `cargo semver-checks check-release` (baseline 0.11.0 exists on crates.io).
- `scripts/publish_crates.sh`: new mode `--verify-published` that, for every crate in print order at the workspace version, validates the crates.io response (exists, exact version, `yanked=false`), then runs `cargo install --locked oraclemcp-verifier --version =<v> --root <tmp>` and prints the installed version; `.github/workflows/release.yml` `publish-crates` job: final step "Verify published crates" running it.

## Implementation notes
1. Write README; `cargo package -p oraclemcp-verifier --list` and review; commit the expected list as a fixture next to the contract test.
2. API lock baseline via `cargo public-api`; semver-checks against 0.11.0 locally (`cargo semver-checks check-release -p oraclemcp-verifier`).
3. `cargo publish -p oraclemcp-verifier --dry-run --locked` now (0.11.0 deps resolve from crates.io). At 0.12.0 the dry run depends on unpublished 0.12.0 siblings (`oraclemcp-audit`, `oraclemcp-guard`) - R.5 runs the dry run for all crates.
4. `--verify-published` reuses the existing registry-response validator in `publish_crates.sh`; bounded retries; no unbounded wait (rule 16).
5. The `oraclemcp-test-attest` binary (ADR-0012 test attestations) ships as-is; its retirement is not in this bead.

## Test plan
- `tests/release_contract_test.sh` (existing order assertion + new `verifier_package_list`, + `publish_crates_verify_published_rejects_missing_version` and `publish_crates_verify_published_rejects_yanked` using the existing fake-curl harness `run_with_fake_curl`).
- `bash scripts/oraclemcp_api_lock.sh` green; `cargo semver-checks check-release -p oraclemcp-verifier` green.
- `cargo publish -p oraclemcp-verifier --dry-run --locked` green (log tail in evidence).

## Proof split
Proves the crate is publishable and verifiable. R.5 runs the 0.12.0 dry run; R.7 publishes and runs `--verify-published` for real.

## Non-goals
- Removing or reworking the test-attestation binary; changing verifier behaviour.
- A new publish script (the existing one stays the single derivation).

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove the verifier's verification logic (its own tests do) or that 0.12.0 is published (R.7).

## Considerations
- Structure-owner check: the plan says "new on crates.io", but 0.11.0 is already published; scope unchanged otherwise.
- Structure-owner check: `oraclemcp-test-attest` belongs to the test-attestation cluster K retired under R29; it ships unchanged unless the operator rules otherwise.
- api-lock is advisory until T5.3; the baseline is regenerated again at R.5 (`ft0ti.1`).
- Hot lane `file-lane:release-pipeline` (release.yml, publish_crates.sh).
- Binding rules: RULE 1 (no file/dir deletion without an exact in-session operator command); commit only explicit paths (`git commit -- <path>...`, then `git show --stat HEAD`, constitution #18); never `-a`/`git add -A`; pushes and tags need the operator's go-ahead; confidentiality (#9): no live-OCI, customer or field identifiers in any committed artifact, synthetic only; close only through `scripts/bead_tracker_guard.sh close` with committed evidence (implementers never self-close); workspace-wide cargo runs go through `scripts/build_lease.sh` with a dedicated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.

## Absorbs
- `oraclemcp-2q4em.4.4` (publish the verifier or mark it publish=false): ruling resolved by R23 (publish); kept - API lock, release-acceptance verification with the installed version printed, consistent crate-count statements; the `publish = false` alternative dropped.

title: REL Release: final docs, RC freeze, sibling publish, consumer rerun, proof, tag v0.12.0
description:
## Goal
Ship engine 0.8.0, driver 0.10.0 and oraclemcp 0.12.0 exactly once each, with every claim proven on the exact release candidate before publication starts (plan §19.4, §20). The train root closes only when REL closes.

## Release order (plan §19.4, binding)
0. **Final docs first (R.0):** final docs (T6.3), CHANGELOGs in all three repos and release notes land before the candidate freeze, so the proven SHA contains them.
1. Dev pins exist from the first train commit (T0.1).
2. **RC freeze (R.1):** when W1-W14 are done, W9 Phase B is clean and the W7 engine fixes pass on the pinned revisions, freeze release-candidate revisions of the driver and engine; run the full tier-A/B/C gates on them.
3. **Sibling package dry runs (R.2):** `cargo package` + `cargo publish --dry-run` for the driver and engine crates only (oraclemcp's crates can't be packaged yet: `cargo package` verification ignores `[patch]`, and the exact versions aren't on crates.io).
4. **Publish siblings exactly once:** engine 0.8.0 (R.3), then driver 0.10.0 (R.4). Each has green CI and a CHANGELOG; the driver README drops the "discontinued" disclaimer. crates.io versions are immutable; R24 forbids extra patch releases.
5. **Consumer rerun (R.5):** remove the patch and `allow-git` entries, pin `=0.10.0` / `=0.8.0`, regenerate `Cargo.lock` and the api-lock baseline (`ft0ti.1`), run `cargo package` + `publish --dry-run` for oraclemcp's crates, rerun tier A **and tier C** against the crates.io-resolved versions. No tier-C lane is skipped after the git patches are replaced: checksum equality satisfies only the producer package-identity subcheck, never consumer resolution, feature unification, artifact construction or the live runs. Every R.5 tier-C result names the post-publish consumer SHA and the lockfile digest. oraclemcp is published only if this rerun is green.
6. **Evidence-only commit (R.6):** the release proof (T5.5, extended D3.2) is committed as an evidence-only commit whose first parent is the post-R.5 candidate; it may change only canonical evidence paths; it records `tested_candidate_sha` (= first parent), driver and engine SHAs, crate checksums, tier-C pass/fail.
7. **Tag and publish (R.7):** tag v0.12.0 on that evidence commit. The tag workflow verifies (parent == `tested_candidate_sha`; parent-to-tag diff evidence-only; sibling SHAs, checksums and result digests match; cheap static and tag-time gates pass) and never generates evidence after publication has started. Then `release.yml` runs (gates, B.12, 7 targets, crates incl. verifier, GitHub release, one GHCR image, MCP registry) and every channel is verified.

## Definition of done (plan §20)
1. Issues #28-#56 closed, each with a fix commit and a named passing test (live where reproducible).
2. W4 suite green: FREE 23ai in tier A; XE 18/21, FREE 23ai and ADB in tier C; results bound in the proof committed before the tag.
3. PL/SQL-intelligence 0.8.0 built into every artifact: artifact acceptance lists all 9 PL/SQL tools on every archive and on the single GHCR image. No stubs (`/mock-code-finder`: engine in T7.1, driver in T0.2b, oraclemcp in R.1). All 9 PL/SQL tools and the custom PL/SQL tool kinds tested end to end.
4. Tier-A lanes green in all three repos; tier-B green on their last run; tier-C results in the release proof; no permanently red lane anywhere.
5. Docs regenerated and truthful; no documented channel that doesn't resolve; CHANGELOGs in all three repos.
6. Standard gates (fmt, clippy x3, default and `--no-default-features`, `cargo test --workspace`, deny, drift) and the full release pipeline; size budgets set to measured values; no `[patch.crates-io]` at the tag; both sibling versions resolve from crates.io in a clean `cargo fetch`.
7. Trackers truthful in all three repos: every train bead closed with evidence; nothing deferred without an operator ruling.
8. W12-W14 acceptance met (change-request lifecycle on XE, FREE 23ai and ADB where ADB EBR is proven; promote + rollback identity-preserving; grant metamorphic suite passes; predicted invalid sets equal observed on the fixture and a superset in general runs; tokens refused after impact drift).

## Invariants
- Publishing is permanent and operator-gated (AGENTS.md "Irreversible / outward-facing actions"); each crate version is published exactly once.
- Read every gate verdict yourself; a successful push is not a pass (constitution #15).
- Binding rules: RULE 1 (no file/dir deletion without an exact in-session operator command); commit only explicit paths (`git commit -- <path>...`, then `git show --stat HEAD`, constitution #18); never `-a`/`git add -A`; pushes and tags need the operator's go-ahead; confidentiality (#9): no live-OCI, customer or field identifiers in any committed artifact, synthetic only; close only through `scripts/bead_tracker_guard.sh close` with committed evidence (implementers never self-close); workspace-wide cargo runs go through `scripts/build_lease.sh` with a dedicated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.

## Size
8 tasks (R.0-R.7), strictly sequential.

## Dependencies
R.1 depends on every W0-W14 task, T4.14, T4.10 and the controller epics T7.1 and T9.6 (zero open descendants).

## Children
R.0, R.1, R.2, R.3, R.4, R.5, R.6, R.7

## Context
Plan §19.4 step 2: when W1-W14 are done, W9 Phase B is clean (T9.6 closed, T9.6b passed) and the W7 engine fixes pass on the pinned revisions, freeze release-candidate revisions of the driver and engine and run the full tier-A/B/C gates against them. §23.2: "`/mock-code-finder` on oraclemcp; **zero open descendants** under the controller epics (T7.1, T9.6) and the T4.10 environment gate." DoD #2-#4, #6, #7. Deps: R.0, T4.14, T4.10, T7.1, T9.6 and every W0-W14 task.

Tiers (§7): A = ci.yml required lanes (fmt, clippy x3 incl. `dashboard-bundle`, default and `--no-default-features`, `cargo test --workspace`, deny/supply-chain, docs drift, boundary + seam lints, installer smoke, FREE 23ai W4 lane, PL/SQL build + tests, windows-rust, api-lock, stable-toolchain check); B = scheduled `fuzz.yml` (+ sibling scheduled lanes incl. the driver's `version-matrix.yml`); C = W4 on XE 18, XE 21, FREE 23ai and ADB (the final tier-C run incl. ADB belongs here; infra from T4.11), loom, kani, multi-nightly, feature-powerset, the OCI lane. T4.10: a hard environment gate with one blocked child per unavailable MCP client binary, **no substitute**. Controller epics close only when every discovered child closes and their rescan/rerun child (T7.1b, T9.6b) passes; final-rescan evidence is invalid once any blocking child lands a later commit.

## Outcome
A recorded triple of frozen SHAs (driver, engine, oraclemcp candidate) on which every tier-A lane in all three repos, the last tier-B runs, and every tier-C lane passed; `/mock-code-finder` on oraclemcp found no unresolved production-reachable stub; `br` shows zero open descendants under T7.1, T9.6 and T4.10; every W0-W14 bead is closed with evidence.

## Deliverable
- Bead comment: the three frozen SHAs; tier-A run URLs (three repos); tier-B last-run URLs; tier-C per-lane result files (from the T4.11 runner and the T9.1 OCI lane) with pass/fail, candidate SHA and `Cargo.lock` sha256, stored where T5.5 expects them for R.6.
- `/mock-code-finder` report on oraclemcp (file/symbol, reachability, verdict); each production-reachable finding becomes a child bug (`discovered-from:R.1`) that blocks this bead.
- No code changes in this bead; any fix is a child bead, and after it lands the freeze is redone.

## Implementation notes
1. Check preconditions mechanically: `br list --json` - no open bead with label `train-0.12` other than REL children; T7.1/T9.6/T4.10 descendants all closed; T4.14 registry completeness gate green.
2. Freeze: record the pinned driver and engine SHAs from oraclemcp `Cargo.toml` `[patch]` and the oraclemcp HEAD.
3. Run tier A (push CI on the candidate), confirm tier-B last runs green (oraclemcp heartbeat snapshot `scheduled_not_green` empty; `sibling_scheduled` all green), dispatch tier C through the T4.11 runner and `oci-adb.yml` (zero-cost check before and after every ADB run, T9.1).
4. Artifact acceptance (T7.4): `tools/list` on every archive and the single image lists all 9 PL/SQL tools.
5. `/mock-code-finder` over `crates/*/src` (test doubles in `tests/`/`#[cfg(test)]` are not defects).
6. Any failure: file a child, fix, re-freeze, rerun everything affected - final evidence must name the final SHAs.

## Test plan
- Tier-A/B/C result set as above; each tier-C lane's JSONL case logs (case id, expected, actual) retained by the runner.
- `python3 scripts/ci_taxonomy.py --status <candidate sha>` reports `ci_green: true`.

## Proof split
Proves the whole train on git-pinned siblings. R.2 proves sibling packaging; R.5 re-proves tier A + C on crates.io-resolved versions; R.6 binds the results.

## Non-goals
- Any fix work (children); publication (R.3/R.4/R.7).

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove the published crates behave identically - R.5 reruns tier A and C after publication.

## Considerations
- Rule 16: every dispatched lane has a deadline; a timeout is a reported failure, not a reason to wait again.
- Zero-cost (constitution #10): ADB runs stay Always-Free; the zero-cost check runs before and after.
- Confidentiality: ADB results redacted at capture (T9.1) before they reach any committed path.
- Binding rules: RULE 1 (no file/dir deletion without an exact in-session operator command); commit only explicit paths (`git commit -- <path>...`, then `git show --stat HEAD`, constitution #18); never `-a`/`git add -A`; pushes and tags need the operator's go-ahead; confidentiality (#9): no live-OCI, customer or field identifiers in any committed artifact, synthetic only; close only through `scripts/bead_tracker_guard.sh close` with committed evidence (implementers never self-close); workspace-wide cargo runs go through `scripts/build_lease.sh` with a dedicated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.

## Absorbs
None.

- [ ] Positive: The bead records frozen driver, engine and oraclemcp SHAs, and for those SHAs: every tier-A lane green in all three repos, the latest tier-B runs green, and every tier-C lane (W4 on xe18, xe21, free23, adb; loom; kani; multi-nightly; feature-powerset; oci) passing with results files naming the candidate SHA and lockfile digest.
- [ ] Positive: `br` shows zero open descendants under T7.1, T9.6 and T4.10, and no open `train-0.12` bead outside REL.

- [ ] Negative: Production-reachable `/mock-code-finder` findings are child bugs blocking this bead until closed.
- [ ] Tests: ci.yml tier A on the candidate; heartbeat snapshot; tier-C runner results for all ten lanes; artifact acceptance `tools/list` on every archive + image.

description:

## Non-goals
- Publishing (R.3/R.4); oraclemcp packaging (R.5).

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove the crates are published or byte-identical after upload (R.3/R.4/R.5 compare).

## Considerations
- If `.crate` bytes differ between runs, R.3/R.4 must publish from the recorded frozen checkout and verify the index checksum immediately (see T5.5 structure-owner check).

None.

title: Consumer rerun: drop patches, pin =0.10.0/=0.8.0, regen lock + api-lock, rerun tier A + C
description:
## Context
Plan §19.4 step 5: oraclemcp removes the patch and `allow-git` entries and pins `=0.10.0` / `=0.8.0`. It regenerates `Cargo.lock` and the api-lock baseline (`ft0ti.1`), and runs `cargo package` + `publish --dry-run` for its own crates. It then reruns **tier A and tier C** against the crates.io-resolved versions. **No tier-C lane is skipped** after the git patches are replaced by crates.io versions: checksum equality satisfies only the producer package-identity subcheck, never consumer resolution, feature unification, artifact construction or the live runs. Every R.5 tier-C result names the post-publish consumer SHA and the lockfile digest. oraclemcp is published only if this rerun is green. DoD #6: no `[patch.crates-io]` at the tag, and both sibling versions resolve from crates.io in a clean `cargo fetch`.

State entering R.5: root `Cargo.toml` has `[patch.crates-io]` for `oraclemcp-driver-cx`, `oraclemcp-driver-cx-protocol` and the 13 engine crates (plsql-core, plsql-engine, plsql-catalog, plsql-depgraph, plsql-lineage, plsql-project, plsql-ir, plsql-parser-antlr, plsql-symbols, plsql-cicd, plsql-doc, plsql-sast, plsql-output); `deny.toml` has `allow-git` for the two sibling URLs (T0.1); the T0.1 gate refuses tags while either exists.

## Outcome
oraclemcp at a new consumer SHA resolves the driver and engine exclusively from crates.io (lockfile checksums equal R.2's records), all 10 oraclemcp crates pass `cargo package` + `publish --dry-run`, the api-lock baselines are regenerated, and tier A plus every tier-C lane pass again on that SHA with results naming it and the lockfile digest.

## Deliverable
- `Cargo.toml`: remove `[patch.crates-io]`; requirements `=0.10.0` / `=0.8.0` (already set by T0.5); `deny.toml`: remove `allow-git`; `Cargo.lock` regenerated (`cargo update -p` for the sibling crates only). One explicit-path commit (rule 17).
- api-lock: regenerate `crates/<crate>/api/<crate>.txt` for every `LOCKED_CRATES` entry (incl. `oraclemcp-verifier` from T11.1) using the reproducible baseline procedure from T8.3; semver-checks against 0.11.0.
- Tier-C results files for T5.5 (candidate SHA = this consumer SHA).

## Implementation notes
1. Edit, regenerate, `cargo metadata --locked`: every sibling crate `source = "registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"`; compare each lock `checksum` with R.2's sha256.
2. `bash scripts/local_release_gate_check.sh --refuse-dev-pins` now exits 0.
3. Clean fetch: `CARGO_HOME=$(mktemp -d) cargo fetch --locked` in a fresh clone succeeds.
4. `cargo publish --workspace --dry-run --locked` for the 10 oraclemcp crates (order per `scripts/publish_crates.sh --print-order`); the workspace dry run packages the unpublished 0.12.0 crates together.
5. Push (operator); tier A on this SHA; dispatch every tier-C lane (W4 on xe18, xe21, free23, adb; loom; kani; multi-nightly; feature-powerset; oci) via the T4.11 runner and `oci-adb.yml`; ADB zero-cost check before/after.
6. Any failure: fix in a child bead; if a sibling defect, the train cannot republish (R24) - escalate to the operator immediately (constitution #12).

## Test plan
- `cargo metadata` / lockfile checksum comparison table.
- Tier-A run URLs; tier-C per-lane result files with `consumer_sha` = this SHA and `lockfile_sha256` = sha256 of its `Cargo.lock`; JSONL case logs retained.
- `scripts/oraclemcp_api_lock.sh` and the `api-lock` lane green.

## Proof split
Proves consumer resolution, feature unification, artifact construction and live behaviour on crates.io versions. R.6 binds the results; R.7 publishes.

## Non-goals
- Changing sibling code (published, immutable).

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove the tag pipeline or channels (R.7).

## Considerations
- Rule 17: patch removal, requirement, deny.toml and lock in one commit.
- Escalation path if a published sibling is defective: operator ruling required (R24 forbids an extra patch release; the plan provides no silent workaround).
- Confidentiality and zero-cost as in R.1.
- Binding rules: RULE 1 (no file/dir deletion without an exact in-session operator command); commit only explicit paths (`git commit -- <path>...`, then `git show --stat HEAD`, constitution #18); never `-a`/`git add -A`; pushes and tags need the operator's go-ahead; confidentiality (#9): no live-OCI, customer or field identifiers in any committed artifact, synthetic only; close only through `scripts/bead_tracker_guard.sh close` with committed evidence (implementers never self-close); workspace-wide cargo runs go through `scripts/build_lease.sh` with a dedicated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.

## Absorbs
None.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: At the R.5 consumer SHA, `Cargo.toml` has no `[patch]`, `deny.toml` has no `allow-git`, `Cargo.lock` sources both siblings from crates.io with checksums equal to R.2's records, and a clean-`CARGO_HOME` `cargo fetch --locked` succeeds.
- [ ] Positive: Tier A is green and every tier-C lane (xe18, xe21, free23, adb, loom, kani, multi-nightly, feature-powerset, oci) passes with results naming this SHA and its lockfile sha256.
- [ ] Positive: `cargo publish --dry-run` succeeds for all 10 oraclemcp crates; api-lock baselines are regenerated and the lane is green.
- [ ] Negative: Omitting any single tier-C lane (e.g. reusing R.1's ADB result) makes the T5.5 check refuse the proof; a leftover `git+` lock source is refused by `--refuse-dev-pins`.
- [ ] Tests: ci.yml tier A; tier-C runner results for all ten lanes; `scripts/local_release_gate_check.sh --refuse-dev-pins`; `scripts/oraclemcp_api_lock.sh`.
- [ ] Proof class: live external client (W4 tier C incl. ADB) + CI on exact SHA; forbidden substitutes: checksum equality in place of a rerun, a fixture in place of ADB, the in-process harness for live claims.
- [ ] Consumers: R.6, R.7.
- [ ] No-claim: Does not prove the tag pipeline or channel availability.

title: Write the release proof from R.1/R.5 results; commit it as an evidence-only commit
description:
## Context
Plan §19.4 step 6: the release proof (T5.5, the extended D3.2 proof) is committed as an **evidence-only commit** whose first parent is the post-R.5 candidate. This is the existing D3.2 rule in `scripts/local_release_gate_check.sh`: a proof is accepted at HEAD, or at HEAD's parent when HEAD is evidence-only. The evidence commit may change **only** canonical evidence paths (`tests/artifacts/local_gate/`). The manifest can't contain its own commit SHA; it records `tested_candidate_sha`, which must equal the evidence commit's first parent. It binds `tested_candidate_sha` and the driver and engine SHAs, the crate checksums (published crates == tested ones), and the tier-C pass/fail results.

## Outcome
A single commit on `main`, child of the R.5 consumer SHA, adding only `tests/artifacts/local_gate/results-<sha>.json` (schema 2) and the tier-C results files it references, which `scripts/local_release_gate_check.sh --require` accepts.

## Deliverable
- `tests/artifacts/local_gate/results-<R.5 short sha>.json` + `tests/artifacts/local_gate/tier-c-<R.5 short sha>/*` written by `scripts/local_release_gate.sh --commit-proof --tested-candidate <R.5 sha> --siblings <R.2 checksum file> --tier-c-dir <R.5 results>`.
- One commit with exactly those paths.

## Implementation notes
1. Ensure HEAD == R.5 consumer SHA and the worktree is clean except the evidence paths (rule 14: generate from a clean worktree at HEAD).
2. Run the writer; `proof_scan` must pass (no `ocid1.`, no `*.oraclecloud.com` CN, no private keys, no `todelete` markers).
3. Stage only the evidence paths; `git commit -- tests/artifacts/local_gate/...`; `git show --stat HEAD` must list nothing else.
4. `bash scripts/local_release_gate_check.sh --require` at the new HEAD (accepts the parent proof).
5. Push with the operator's go-ahead; confirm nothing else landed on `main` between R.5 and this commit (else redo R.5 on the new HEAD).

## Test plan
- `scripts/local_release_gate_check.sh --require` output `OK ... (accepted parent source proof from evidence-only commit)`.
- `git diff --name-only HEAD^..HEAD` lists only `tests/artifacts/local_gate/` paths.

## Proof split
Proves the evidence commit shape. Verification on the tag is R.7; the check logic is T5.5.

## Non-goals
- Changing any non-evidence path; regenerating results.

## No-claim boundary
Does not re-prove any lane; it binds recorded results.

## Considerations
- Confidentiality (#9): ADB results must already be redacted; any scan hit aborts the commit.
- Hot lane `file-lane:release-gate`.
- Binding rules: RULE 1 (no file/dir deletion without an exact in-session operator command); commit only explicit paths (`git commit -- <path>...`, then `git show --stat HEAD`, constitution #18); never `-a`/`git add -A`; pushes and tags need the operator's go-ahead; confidentiality (#9): no live-OCI, customer or field identifiers in any committed artifact, synthetic only; close only through `scripts/bead_tracker_guard.sh close` with committed evidence (implementers never self-close); workspace-wide cargo runs go through `scripts/build_lease.sh` with a dedicated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.

## Absorbs
None.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: HEAD of `main` is an evidence-only commit whose first parent is the R.5 consumer SHA, adding the schema-2 proof and its tier-C results files, and `scripts/local_release_gate_check.sh --require` accepts it.
- [ ] Negative: `git diff --name-only HEAD^..HEAD` contains no path outside `tests/artifacts/local_gate/`; a proof whose `tested_candidate_sha` differs from HEAD^ is refused by the check.
- [ ] Tests: `scripts/local_release_gate_check.sh --require`; `git show --stat HEAD`.
- [ ] Proof class: offline (git + check script); forbidden substitutes: a proof committed together with code, evidence generated by the tag workflow.
- [ ] Consumers: R.7.
- [ ] No-claim: Does not re-prove lane results.

title: Tag v0.12.0 on the evidence commit; run release.yml; verify every channel
description:
## Context
Plan §19.4 step 7: tag **v0.12.0** on the evidence-only commit. The tag workflow **verifies** and never generates evidence after publication has started: parent == `tested_candidate_sha`; the parent-to-tag diff is evidence-only; all sibling SHAs, checksums and result digests match; the cheap static and tag-time gates pass on the tag commit (including the T0.1 dev-pin refusal and the T5.1 tier-B check). Then `release.yml` runs: gates (`checks`), `pinned-nightly`, B.12 (`release-acceptance`), `build` (7 targets), `release` (GitHub release with checksums, CycloneDX SBOM, cosign signatures and attestations; no Homebrew/winget assets after T6.1), `publish-crates` (10 crates incl. `oraclemcp-verifier`, followed by T11.1's `--verify-published`), `docker` (one GHCR image, `ghcr.io/muhdur/oraclemcp`, signed, smoked, promoted), `publish-mcp-registry` and `verify-mcp-registry`. Every channel is verified. Constitution #15: read each gate verdict yourself; a successful push is not a pass. R24: no extra releases; crates.io versions are immutable, so once `publish-crates` has run, 0.12.0 cannot be republished.

## Outcome
v0.12.0 is live on crates.io (10 crates), the GitHub release (signed archives for 7 targets + SBOM + attestations), GHCR (one image whose `tools/list` includes all 9 PL/SQL tools), and the MCP registry, each verified, and `install.sh`/`install.ps1`/`cargo binstall` resolve 0.12.0.

## Deliverable
- Tag `v0.12.0` (operator go-ahead) on the R.6 commit.
- Bead comment with every job verdict and channel verification output: `scripts/verify_release_artifacts.sh`, `scripts/verify_mcp_release.sh`, `scripts/promote_release_image.sh` smoke, `scripts/publish_crates.sh --verify-published`, `docker run ghcr.io/muhdur/oraclemcp:0.12.0 info` tools list, `install.sh` resolution of 0.12.0, `cargo binstall --dry-run oraclemcp@0.12.0`.

## Implementation notes
1. Pre-tag local: `bash scripts/local_release_gate_check.sh --require`, `--refuse-dev-pins`, `bash scripts/release_preflight.sh` with `RELEASE_TAG=v0.12.0`.
2. Tag + push; watch each job to completion with deadlines (rule 16); read conclusions.
3. If a job fails **before** `publish-crates` starts, fix forward on `main`, redo R.5/R.6 as needed, and move the tag only with the operator's explicit approval; if it fails **after** crates are published, escalate (no republish of 0.12.0 is possible).
4. Verify channels as listed; confirm the GitHub release has no `distribution-manifests` assets and GHCR has no `-plsql-intelligence` tag.
5. Close out: the train root closes when REL closes.

## Test plan
- release.yml run URL with all jobs green; each verification script's output.
- `gh release view v0.12.0 --json assets` lists 7 target archives with `.sha256`, `.sigstore.json`, attestation bundles, SBOM; no Homebrew/winget files.

## Proof split
Proves publication and channel availability. Everything behavioural was proven at R.1/R.5 and bound at R.6.

## Non-goals
- Launch activities (§22).

## No-claim boundary
Does not re-prove behaviour; it proves the tested bytes were shipped through every channel.

## Considerations
- Irreversible outward-facing action: operator go-ahead required for the tag push and any tag move.
- Binding rules: RULE 1 (no file/dir deletion without an exact in-session operator command); commit only explicit paths (`git commit -- <path>...`, then `git show --stat HEAD`, constitution #18); never `-a`/`git add -A`; pushes and tags need the operator's go-ahead; confidentiality (#9): no live-OCI, customer or field identifiers in any committed artifact, synthetic only; close only through `scripts/bead_tracker_guard.sh close` with committed evidence (implementers never self-close); workspace-wide cargo runs go through `scripts/build_lease.sh` with a dedicated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.

## Absorbs
None.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: Every job of the v0.12.0 release.yml run concludes success, and the tag's `checks` job log shows the proof accepted with parent == `tested_candidate_sha`.
- [ ] Positive: crates.io shows all 10 oraclemcp crates at 0.12.0 (verified by `scripts/publish_crates.sh --verify-published`), the GitHub release has signed archives for 7 targets, GHCR `ghcr.io/muhdur/oraclemcp:0.12.0` lists all 9 PL/SQL tools, and the MCP registry lists 0.12.0.
- [ ] Negative: The GitHub release contains no Homebrew/winget assets and GHCR has no `-plsql-intelligence` tag; a tag placed on a commit whose parent differs from `tested_candidate_sha` is refused by the `checks` job.
- [ ] Tests: release.yml jobs checks, pinned-nightly, release-acceptance, build (7), release, publish-crates (+ verify step), docker, publish-mcp-registry, verify-mcp-registry all green; channel verification scripts green.
- [ ] Proof class: live channel verification; forbidden substitutes: inferring success from `git push`, verifying a candidate digest instead of the promoted image.
- [ ] Consumers: ROOT (train closes).
- [ ] No-claim: Does not re-prove behaviour beyond the bound evidence.
