title: Test the nine PL/SQL tools with offline fixtures and live external cases
description:
## Context
R8 (every tool gets a deliberate in-house live test: create objects, run all statement kinds, verify deterministically), R25 (nothing deferred; all tools tested end to end). Plan §6 (binding): external client only - the real release-profile binary over MCP stdio **and** Streamable HTTP, no in-process dispatcher, no server helper crates in the client; deterministic verification (exact ordered rows, exact error class + ORA code, audit entries with a verified hash chain, an independent re-read of database state after every mutation, ordering by barriers never elapsed time, goldens with volatile fields scrubbed); one JSONL line per case (tool, level, input hash, expected, actual, verdict, timings) plus a summary table in the results JSON; counts come from the registry, never hard-coded.
The 9 PL/SQL-intelligence tools (`crates/oraclemcp/src/plsql_tools.rs` `TOOL_NAMES`): offline `oracle_plsql_parse`, `oracle_plsql_analyze`, `oracle_plsql_what_breaks`, `oracle_plsql_lineage`, `oracle_plsql_sast`, `oracle_plsql_doc`; live-catalog `oracle_lineage`, `oracle_plsql_live_snapshot`, `oracle_plsql_blast_radius`. Today: lineage/live_snapshot/blast_radius are tested in-process only; the six offline tools have no tests at the tool surface. R13: PL/SQL-intelligence is part of oraclemcp, "no gaps, no stubs, nothing untested". T7.4 makes the feature a default of the `oraclemcp` crate and builds it into every artifact, so the release binary serves these tools.
Plan §6/§9.3 (binding): offline tools run against committed PL/SQL fixtures; live ones run through the external client; all 9 covered by W4 and the CI lane becomes required (`xoflp.3.2`, delivered by T7.4/T4.11).

## Outcome
Committed PL/SQL fixtures and deliberate cases prove all nine tools through the release binary over stdio and HTTP: offline tools with exact golden outputs on fixture sources (no database), live tools against the T4.3 fixture package and dependency graph on FREE 23ai and XE 18/21.

## Deliverable
- `tests/fixtures/plsql/`: synthetic PL/SQL sources (package spec/body with dependencies, a procedure with a SAST finding such as dynamic SQL concatenation, a routine with table lineage, a documented package for `plsql_doc`, a syntax-error source).
- `scripts/e2e/w4/cases/plsql.json` with cases:
  - offline: `w4_plsql_parse_ok_ast_summary_golden`, `w4_plsql_parse_syntax_error_typed`, `w4_plsql_analyze_findings_golden`, `w4_plsql_what_breaks_change_impact_golden`, `w4_plsql_lineage_table_columns_golden`, `w4_plsql_sast_concat_dynamic_sql_finding`, `w4_plsql_sast_clean_source_no_findings`, `w4_plsql_doc_markdown_golden`;
  - live: `w4_lineage_fixture_package_edges`, `w4_plsql_live_snapshot_fixture_objects`, `w4_plsql_blast_radius_dependents_exact` (dependents re-read from `ALL_DEPENDENCIES` by the harness), `w4_plsql_live_tool_readonly_level_ok`, `w4_plsql_live_missing_object_not_found`.
- Goldens under `tests/golden/w4/plsql/` (scrubbed).

## Implementation notes
1. Offline cases still go through the release binary (MCP call), with no database profile required; they run in the tier-A lint lane as well as the live lanes.
2. Live results are checked against the harness's own dictionary reads, not against the tool's own previous output.
3. Fixture sources are synthetic and small; the engine version is whatever T0.1/T0.6 pin (the golden refresh is part of T0.6 when outputs change).

## Test plan
Every case runs over stdio and Streamable HTTP through the T4.2 driver against the T4.3 fixture; tier A lane FREE 23ai; tier C XE 18/21, FREE 23ai (and ADB through T9.6a). Case ids follow `w4_<tool>_<case>`. Each case logs one JSONL line (`case_id`, tool, level, transport, input hash, expected, actual, verdict, timings). Mutating cases re-read DB state through an independent python-oracledb connection owned by the harness (never through the server) and verify the audit chain with `oraclemcp audit verify` after the run.
Offline cases additionally run with no database lane (`--lane offline`).

## Proof split
This bead proves the nine tools at the MCP surface; engine soundness is proven in the engine repo (T7.2, T7.3); custom PL/SQL tool kinds by T4.9a/T7.13; artifact presence of the tools by T7.4.

## Non-goals
- Engine fixes (W7); custom package-call tools (T4.9a).

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove engine analysis is sound for arbitrary PL/SQL; only the fixture outputs.

## Considerations
- Engine output changes on pin refresh (T0.6) may change goldens; refreshing goldens requires a reviewed diff, never a blind re-record.
- Confidentiality (constitution #9): fixtures, goldens, case inputs and logs use synthetic identifiers only; no field/customer/OCI identifier ever enters a committed artifact.
- Consumers: T4.14, T9.6a, T4.11.

## Absorbs
None.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: all six offline PL/SQL tools produce outputs equal to their goldens through the release binary with no database profile.
- [ ] Positive: `oracle_plsql_blast_radius` dependents equal the harness's `ALL_DEPENDENCIES` re-read for the fixture package on FREE 23ai and XE 18/21.
- [ ] Negative: a syntax-error source yields a typed parse error (not success); a clean source yields zero SAST findings while the concat-dynamic-SQL fixture yields the expected finding.
- [ ] Tests: all ids in `scripts/e2e/w4/cases/plsql.json`.
- [ ] Proof class: offline (goldens via the binary) + live external client; forbidden substitutes: in-process calls of `plsql_tools::dispatch_static`, mock catalog.
- [ ] Consumers: T4.11, T4.14, T9.6a.
- [ ] No-claim: does not prove engine soundness beyond the fixtures.

title: Test custom package-call tool kinds through the external client incl. masking exfiltration
description:
## Context
R8 (every tool gets a deliberate in-house live test: create objects, run all statement kinds, verify deterministically), R25 (nothing deferred; all tools tested end to end). Plan §6 (binding): external client only - the real release-profile binary over MCP stdio **and** Streamable HTTP, no in-process dispatcher, no server helper crates in the client; deterministic verification (exact ordered rows, exact error class + ORA code, audit entries with a verified hash chain, an independent re-read of database state after every mutation, ordering by barriers never elapsed time, goldens with volatile fields scrubbed); one JSONL line per case (tool, level, input hash, expected, actual, verdict, timings) plus a summary table in the results JSON; counts come from the registry, never hard-coded.
W7 (§9.4) wires custom PL/SQL package-call tools under the fail-closed guard: a routine that cannot be proven stays refused; effects map to a required level; exact identity and the whole call closure pinned by hash; everything re-checked at apply (SEC-1); DML rolls back by default; nothing auto-commits; caller text is never concatenated into PL/SQL. Output: OUT/IN OUT binds, scalar mode, bounded `DBMS_OUTPUT` capture (off by default), REF CURSOR results through the same row/byte caps as `oracle_query`. **Masking closes every output channel**: on a profile with result masking, every package-call tool that exposes a scalar return, OUT/IN OUT binds, a REF CURSOR, implicit results or captured `DBMS_OUTPUT` is refused in 0.12 whatever its `RoutineEffects` (package state, initialization code, session context and IN OUT aliasing can launder a masked value). T7.13 lands the gates (Free23 invocation lane, differential, wrapper fuzz); this bead proves the tool kinds through the release binary.
§23.2 scope: pure, DML, literal-DDL, mixed (refused), scalar/OUT, DBMS_OUTPUT, REF CURSOR, masking exfiltration.

## Outcome
Signed `tools.d` definitions for each custom package-call kind are loaded by the release binary on a lab lane, and each kind's behaviour is proven over stdio and HTTP: admitted kinds at their exact required level with correct outputs and rollback-by-default, refused kinds refused with zero committed effects, and every masking exfiltration channel refused with masking canaries absent from tool output, logs, audit detail and the session report.

## Deliverable
- `scripts/e2e/w4/custom_tools/*.toml` (signed at run time with a test HMAC key via `oraclemcp sign-tool --write`) targeting routines added to the T4.3 fixture package (request the routines on T4.3's thread if missing: pure function, DML procedure, literal-DDL procedure, mixed DML+DDL procedure, scalar-return function, OUT/IN OUT procedure, DBMS_OUTPUT procedure, REF CURSOR function).
- `scripts/e2e/w4/cases/custom_tools.json` with cases:
  - `w4_custom_pure_fn_admitted_readonly`, `w4_custom_dml_proc_read_write_rollback_default` (re-read unchanged), `w4_custom_dml_proc_confirmed_commit`, `w4_custom_literal_ddl_proc_ddl_level_fresh_lane`, `w4_custom_mixed_dml_ddl_refused_zero_committed_dml`;
  - `w4_custom_scalar_return_value`, `w4_custom_out_in_out_binds`, `w4_custom_dbms_output_off_by_default`, `w4_custom_dbms_output_bounded_when_enabled`, `w4_custom_ref_cursor_row_byte_caps`;
  - masking (profile with result masking): `w4_custom_masked_profile_scalar_refused`, `w4_custom_masked_profile_out_refused`, `w4_custom_masked_profile_in_out_refused`, `w4_custom_masked_profile_ref_cursor_refused`, `w4_custom_masked_profile_dbms_output_refused`, `w4_custom_masked_profile_laundering_canary_refused` (routine A reads the masked value into package state; routine B has no direct ReadDb and returns it - B refused, value absent everywhere).
- Canary scan: after the masking cases, grep tool outputs, server stderr/log, the audit file and `oraclemcp audit report` output for the canary value (must be absent).

## Implementation notes
1. The remaining §9.4 W4 cases (autonomous procedure refused, COMMIT inside a routine refused, unloaded-SYS caller refused, repointed synonym between load and run refused and quarantined, local object named like the schema refused, unsigned write tool refused at load, variable/concatenated dynamic DDL refused) are owned by T7.13's gates; where they need the external client they are added to this same case file by T7.13's owner - this bead does not duplicate them.
2. Canary: a unique synthetic value stored in the masked column by the fixture; the scan fails on any occurrence.
3. Level assertions include the refusal at one level below the required level.

## Test plan
Every case runs over stdio and Streamable HTTP through the T4.2 driver against the T4.3 fixture; tier A lane FREE 23ai; tier C XE 18/21, FREE 23ai (and ADB through T9.6a). Case ids follow `w4_<tool>_<case>`. Each case logs one JSONL line (`case_id`, tool, level, transport, input hash, expected, actual, verdict, timings). Mutating cases re-read DB state through an independent python-oracledb connection owned by the harness (never through the server) and verify the audit chain with `oraclemcp audit verify` after the run.
Negative cases a naive implementation fails: the mixed DML+DDL routine is refused and the re-read shows zero committed DML; the laundering canary never appears in any output channel, log, audit record or session report.

## Proof split
This bead proves the custom-tool kinds through the release binary on lab lanes; T7.10-T7.13 prove the mechanism (signing, activation, re-check, output shaping, differential, fuzz); ADB via T9.6a.

## Non-goals
- Implementing custom-tool mechanics (W7); SQL-only custom tools (already covered).

## No-claim boundary
Does not prove the effect proof is sound for arbitrary routines; only the fixture kinds.

## Considerations
- `sec`: proves masking-channel closure and refusal of unprovable routines; second-agent review. Fail-closed invariant: nothing here may admit a statement the classifier cannot prove safe for the active level, let elevation exceed a profile's `max_level`, make a `protected` profile writable, or auto-commit DML.
- Confidentiality (constitution #9): fixtures, goldens, case inputs and logs use synthetic identifiers only; no field/customer/OCI identifier ever enters a committed artifact.
- Consumers: T4.14, T9.6a.

## Absorbs
None.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: the pure function is admitted at READ_ONLY; the DML procedure runs at READ_WRITE and the re-read shows rollback by default; the literal-DDL procedure runs only at DDL on a fresh lane.
- [ ] Positive: scalar, OUT/IN OUT, bounded DBMS_OUTPUT and REF CURSOR outputs are correct on an unmasked profile.
- [ ] Negative: the mixed DML+DDL routine is refused with zero committed DML.
- [ ] Negative: on a masked profile, scalar/OUT/IN OUT/REF CURSOR/DBMS_OUTPUT package calls and the laundering canary routine are refused, and the canary is absent from outputs, logs, audit detail and the session report.
- [ ] Tests: all ids in `scripts/e2e/w4/cases/custom_tools.json`.
- [ ] Proof class: live external client; forbidden substitutes: in-process invocation, unsigned definitions, mock DB.
- [ ] Consumers: T4.14, T9.6a.
- [ ] No-claim: does not prove soundness for arbitrary routines.

title: Prove MCP client config snippets against recorded client versions
description:
## Context
Plan §6 (binding): tested config snippets for **Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Codex and Gemini CLI**. Each snippet is proven against a **named, recorded client version** to launch the server and list tools, which prevents a recurrence of the #11 class (a documented snippet that did not work). Each artifact records the launch command, client version, transport, `tools/list` digest and exit status. A client whose binary isn't available is **blocked-born**: it names the missing binary and forbids a schema/parser/mock substitute. §23.1: T4.10 is the only blocked-born case in the train; §23.2: a hard R.1 environment gate with one blocked child per unavailable client binary, with no substitute.
Existing pieces: `oraclemcp setup` prints client snippets (`crates/oraclemcp/src/cli.rs` `Command::Setup`); `scripts/rig/onboarding_snippet_truth.py` (C9) extracts snippets from real `setup` output and drives raw JSON-RPC against the emitted command - it never runs the actual client.

## Outcome
For each of the five clients, a runner launches the **real client binary** (headless/non-interactive mode where the client offers one) with the snippet printed by `oraclemcp setup`, makes it start the oraclemcp server and list tools, and writes an artifact `{client, client_version, launch_command, transport, tools_list_sha256, exit_status}`. Every available client passes; every unavailable client has one blocked child bead naming the missing binary; R.1 cannot pass while any such child is open.

## Deliverable
- `scripts/rig/client_snippets.py` (extends/replaces the C9 runner's snippet extraction): per client an adapter that writes the client's config file in a temp HOME from `oraclemcp setup` output and invokes the client's non-interactive tool listing (e.g. Claude Code `claude mcp list`/headless print mode, Codex and Gemini CLI non-interactive modes, Cursor's CLI agent, VS Code's CLI/extension host where it can list MCP tools). The adapter records the exact client version (`<client> --version`).
- Artifacts `target/e2e/clients/<client>.json`; the tier-C summary (T4.1's `summary.json`) gains a `clients` section.
- `docs/` snippets (generated by `setup`) state the proven client versions (regenerated by T6.3).
- For each client whose binary is unavailable on the proving host at the time of the run: a child bead of this bead, status `blocked`, title "Prove <client> snippet: <binary> not available", body naming the binary and forbidding a schema/parser/mock substitute; each child blocks R.1.

## Implementation notes
1. The proof must come from the client itself listing oraclemcp's tools (the `tools/list` digest is computed from what the client reports or from the server-side log of the `tools/list` served to that client session - recorded as such).
2. No network credentials: use a lab profile against a FREE 23ai lane or an offline profile; the snippet under test is the one `setup` prints, unmodified except for temp paths.
3. Clients requiring a GUI without a headless mode cannot be proven this way; that is a blocked child, not a substitute.
4. Record versions exactly; a later client version is a new proof, not an inherited one.

## Test plan
- `scripts/rig/client_snippets.py --selftest` (offline): adapter config rendering for all five clients from a golden `setup` output; artifact schema validation; a planted "mock client" adapter is rejected by the runner (substitution guard).
- Live: one run per available client on the proving host, artifacts committed into the tier-C summary at R.1.
Logging: one JSONL line per client (`client`, `client_version`, `transport`, `tools_list_sha256`, `exit_status`, `verdict`).

## Proof split
This bead proves the snippets launch the server and list tools in the named client versions; tool behaviour is proven by W4 case beads; docs regeneration by T6.3.

## Non-goals
- Testing tool calls inside the clients beyond listing; supporting additional clients.

## No-claim boundary
A proof holds for the recorded client version only; it does not prove other versions.

## Considerations
- Blocked-born rule: the children are the only blocked-born items in the train; they must name the missing binary and must never be closed by a substitute (schema check, parser, mock). Whether a client is available is decided at run time on the proving host, not at conversion.
- Structure-owner check: Cursor and VS Code are primarily GUI clients; if no headless listing mode exists on the proving host, their children stay blocked and hold R.1 by design (operator decision to accept or supply the binary).
- Confidentiality: temp HOME per client; no real credentials in artifacts.
- Consumers: R.1, T6.3.

## Absorbs
None.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: for each available client, the artifact records client version, launch command, transport, a non-empty `tools_list_sha256` equal to the server's served `tools/list` digest, and exit status 0.
- [ ] Positive: each unavailable client has exactly one blocked child bead naming the missing binary and blocking R.1.
- [ ] Negative: the runner rejects a planted mock-client adapter and refuses to mark a client proven from a schema/parser check.
- [ ] Tests: `client_snippets.py --selftest`, live artifacts `target/e2e/clients/<client>.json` per available client.
- [ ] Proof class: live external client (the real MCP client binary); forbidden substitutes: schema/parser validation, mock client, raw JSON-RPC in place of the client.
- [ ] Consumers: R.1, T6.3.
- [ ] No-claim: proves only the recorded client versions.

title: Wire the tier-A FREE 23ai W4 lane (25-minute budget) and the tier-C runner
description:
## Context
Plan §7 tiers (R10 honest but lightweight CI; R24 no ceremony): **tier A** (required on PR/push) includes the **FREE 23ai lane running the W4 suite**, with a hard **25-minute budget**; if it runs over, it is split by tool family, **never `continue-on-error`**; the matrix is generated from the registry, so an unregistered tool fails the lane; verdicts are derived fail-closed. **Tier C** (release-only): W4 on XE 18/21, FREE 23ai and ADB on the exact release-candidate SHA; results feed the release proof committed before tagging (T5.5); the final tier-C run belongs to R.1.
Today `.github/workflows/ci.yml` job `oracle-free23` (timeout 45 minutes, `gvenzl/oracle-free:23-slim@sha256:...` service container, grants DBMS_FLASHBACK to the app user) runs `scripts/e2e/oracle_version_matrix.sh --log --lane free23` and then a test-attestation step (`scripts/check_test_attestations.py`) - the test-attestation cluster K was retired by R29.
§23.2 scope: the base-family lane infrastructure (families from T4.4-T4.8); PL/SQL/custom/W12-W14 families join the same lane as their beads land; the completeness gate is T4.14.

## Outcome
A required tier-A CI job runs the W4 driver (T4.2) with the T4.3 fixture on the FREE 23ai service container for the base families (write-tools, source-tools, dictionary-tools, ops-tools, aliases) over stdio and HTTP within 25 minutes, splitting into per-family jobs when the measured runtime exceeds the budget, with a fail-closed verdict (any error, timeout, missing result or missing manifest case = red). A tier-C runner entry (`scripts/rig/tier_c.sh` from T4.1 + a `workflow_dispatch`/release-gate invocation) runs the same suite on XE 18, XE 21, FREE 23ai and hands ADB to T9.1's lane, producing the summary T5.5 binds.

## Deliverable
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: the `oracle-free23` job (or new per-family jobs) runs `scripts/e2e/w4.sh --lane free23 --families <list>` after the existing build; `timeout-minutes: 25` per job; no `continue-on-error`; the verdict step derives pass only from `results.json` + `validate_manifest.py --check-results`. The test-attestation steps for this lane are removed (R29) unless still needed by another required gate - check with `rg -n check_test_attestations .github`.
- Branch-protection/required-check list updated so the W4 job(s) are required (documented in `docs/ci-taxonomy` or the file the repo uses; re-derive).
- `scripts/rig/tier_c.sh` integration: invoked by `scripts/local_release_gate.sh` (tier-C step) and by a manual `workflow_dispatch` in the existing release-candidate workflow; output path consumed by T5.5.
- Runtime measurement recorded in the job summary (per family duration) so a split is data-driven.

## Implementation notes
1. Keep the existing version-matrix and VECTOR smoke steps only if they are not subsumed by W4 families; remove duplicated coverage rather than run both.
2. The fixture run id includes the CI run id; teardown verdict is part of the job result (a leftover is red).
3. Split rule: if the 25-minute budget is exceeded on main for the combined job, split by family into parallel jobs sharing the build artifact; never raise the budget and never mark allowed-to-fail.
4. Tier C runs sequentially per lane (memory discipline) on the operator's lab host or a self-hosted runner; results are written, not uploaded as attestation.

## Test plan
- A PR with a planted failing case (in a throwaway branch) turns the W4 job red; a PR adding a tool to the registry without cases turns it red (via T4.2's coverage report, fully enforced by T4.14).
- The verdict step's selftest: missing `results.json`, a truncated JSONL, and a timeout each yield red.
- Measured durations for the base families recorded in the job summary on main.
- `scripts/rig/tier_c.sh --sha <candidate>` on the lab host produces a summary with all three local lanes.
Logging: job summary table (family x transport x pass/fail x duration); per-case JSONL uploaded as a plain artifact.

## Proof split
This bead proves the lanes run the suite and fail closed; case correctness is proven by the case beads; completeness by T4.14; the release binding by T5.5; the final tier-C run by R.1; ADB by T9.1/T9.6a.

## Non-goals
- Test attestation/signing (retired, R29); nightly schedules; tier-B changes (W5 T5.1/T5.2).

## No-claim boundary
A green tier-A lane proves FREE 23ai only; XE 18/21 and ADB are proven only by tier-C results.

## Considerations
- Workflow edits conflict with W5 (T5.1-T5.5) on `.github/workflows/*`: reserve `ci.yml` and coordinate on the W5 epic thread.
- AGENTS.md rule 15: read the gate verdict yourself; a push is not a pass.
- Confidentiality: CI logs carry synthetic identifiers only.
- Consumers: T5.5, T7.13, T8.9, T9.6a, T4.14.

## Absorbs
None.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: on main, the required W4 job(s) run the base families over stdio and HTTP on FREE 23ai and each finishes within 25 minutes (durations in the job summary).
- [ ] Positive: `scripts/rig/tier_c.sh --sha <sha>` produces a tier-C summary for XE 18, XE 21 and FREE 23ai consumed by `scripts/local_release_gate.sh`.
- [ ] Negative: a planted failing case, a missing `results.json`, a missing manifest case and a job timeout each make the W4 job red; no W4 job uses `continue-on-error`.
- [ ] Tests: verdict-step selftest, planted-failure PR run log, main-branch run log.
- [ ] Proof class: live external client in CI; forbidden substitutes: `continue-on-error`, advisory status, in-process tests counted as the lane.
- [ ] Consumers: T5.5, T7.13, T8.9, T9.6a, T4.14.
- [ ] No-claim: tier A proves FREE 23ai only.

title: Gate W4 completeness on the registry and capability matrix with no hard-coded counts
description:
## Context
Plan §6 acceptance (binding): all canonical tools (34 today + `oracle_change_request` (W12) + `oracle_request_grant` (W13) = 36), the 25 aliases, the 9 PL/SQL tools and the custom-tool kinds are covered per the capability-driven matrix rule (a positive case on at least one capable target; negative/level cases on every applicable target; exact typed refusal for unsupported combinations); every manifest case id present and green; counts come from the registry and are **never hard-coded**. R34 anti-ceremony audit: the registry completeness gate is **kept** because CI branches on it and "17 of 34 tools untested" was observed; the separate wiring task T4.16 was merged into it.
Today `scripts/rig/tool_surface_sweep.py` hard-codes `EXPECTED_REGISTRY_CANONICAL = 34` and `EXPECTED_REGISTRY_ALIASES = 25`; `crates/oraclemcp/src/registry.rs` `TOOL_NAMES: [&str; 59]` is the dispatch set (the array length is a type, not a test oracle).

## Outcome
A gate in the W4 lane (and in `cargo test` for the offline part) derives the required coverage from the served `tools/list` of the release binary (canonical tools, aliases, PL/SQL tools) plus the custom-tool kind list and the capability matrix, and fails when any tool/alias/kind lacks its required positive, level or negative cases, when a required case is missing or red on a lane, or when any script or test hard-codes a tool count. The gate is wired into tier A and tier C.

## Deliverable
- `scripts/e2e/w4/completeness.py`: inputs `tools/list` JSON, `scripts/e2e/w4/capabilities.json`, the custom-kind list (from `scripts/e2e/w4/cases/custom_tools.json` kinds + the W7 kind enum exposed by `oraclemcp robot-docs tools`), all case files, `results.json`; output a coverage table and a non-zero exit on any gap.
- Rules: every canonical tool -> >= 1 positive case on >= 1 capable lane; every tool with level-dependent behaviour -> level cases at each applicable level; every tool -> the W3 contract family; every alias -> an equivalence or wrapper case (T4.8); every PL/SQL tool (T4.9); every custom kind (T4.9a); W12/W13/W14 tools and bindings (T12.9, T13.8, T14.9); selftest's read-only case subset (T4.15) is a subset of W4 definitions.
- Removal of hard-coded counts: `scripts/rig/tool_surface_sweep.py` retired or rewritten to read counts from `tools/list`; a lint (`completeness.py --lint-hardcoded`) greps `scripts/e2e`, `scripts/rig`, `crates/*/tests` for literal tool-count constants and fails.
- Wired into the tier-A W4 job(s) (T4.11) and `scripts/rig/tier_c.sh`.

## Implementation notes
1. The canonical/alias split comes from the binary: canonical tools are the `oracle_*` names (`CANONICAL_TOOL_PREFIX`) and aliases are listed by `oraclemcp robot-docs tools` with their targets; the gate cross-checks both sources and fails on disagreement.
2. Level applicability is declared per tool in `capabilities.json` (`levels_behaviour_changes: [...]`), reviewed against the registry's `ToolTier`/required level.
3. The expected total today is 36 canonical once W12/W13 land; the gate never states the number - it asserts coverage for whatever `tools/list` returns.

## Test plan
- `completeness.py --selftest`: planted registry with an extra tool lacking cases -> red naming the tool; an alias without an equivalence case -> red; a custom kind without a case -> red; a hard-coded `34` in a script -> red; the real repo state -> green once all dependencies are done.
- `cargo test -p oraclemcp` test `registry_tools_have_w4_case_files` (offline: every registered tool name appears in at least one case file).
- Live: tier-A and tier-C runs include the coverage table in `results.json`.
Logging: coverage table JSON (`tool`, `kind`, `required`, `present`, `green`, `verdict`).

## Proof split
This bead proves coverage completeness; each case bead proves behaviour; T4.11 proves the lanes run; R.1 runs the final tier-C with this gate.

## Non-goals
- Writing cases; tracker/close tooling (cut by R34).

## No-claim boundary
Complete coverage does not prove the cases are strong; case quality is reviewed in each case bead.

## Considerations
- Closes after W12/W13/W14 live suites (T12.9, T13.8, T14.9) - the gate must include the two new canonical tools.
- Confidentiality: none (no data).
- Consumers: R.0, R.1.

## Absorbs
None.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: `completeness.py` on the release binary's `tools/list` reports every canonical tool (incl. `oracle_change_request` and `oracle_request_grant`), every alias, every PL/SQL tool and every custom kind as covered and green on FREE 23ai, and on XE 18/21 in tier C.
- [ ] Negative: a planted tool without cases, an alias without an equivalence case, a custom kind without a case, and a hard-coded tool count in a script each make the gate fail naming the gap.
- [ ] Tests: `completeness.py --selftest`, `registry_tools_have_w4_case_files`, tier-A and tier-C coverage tables.
- [ ] Proof class: live external client (coverage from executed results) + offline selftest; forbidden substitutes: a hand-maintained tool list or count.
- [ ] Consumers: R.0, R.1.
- [ ] No-claim: does not grade case strength.

title: Add `oraclemcp selftest`: forced READ_ONLY, typed outcomes, sanitized issue drafts
description:
## Context Operator ruling R33: **keep `oraclemcp selftest`, improved, with no ceremony** - no signing/attestation, no corpus feed. Field rounds against 0.9.0-0.11.0 discovered the P0s and the 29 issues #28-#56; the goal is that a field round **confirms** a release instead of discovering bugs. W4 creates and drops fixtures, so it runs only on lab databases; `selftest` is what a field agent or operator runs from the **installed binary** against a real, even customer, database after every install. Plan §6 (binding): - **Read-only by construction**: forces the session to READ_ONLY for its whole run, whatever the profile's `max_level`; creates no objects, uses no fixtures, executes no write; the audit chain proves no privileged action happened. - **Runs**: the read-only subset of the W4 case definitions, shared with the W4 generator so the two never drift; every advertised tool at READ_ONLY with synthetic inputs, where write tools must produce their exact typed refusal; `doctor --online` including the #56 phase-aware connection report (T9.4b); transport probes (stdio, plus HTTP when a listener is configured); refusal and bypass probes from the T4.0 case manifest. - **Outcomes** classified against the capability matrix: `pass`; `expected refusal` (unsupported version/privilege/licence); `environment` (e.g. a missing grant, reported with the exact privilege to add); `defect`. **Exit codes: 0 clean, 2 defect found, 3 environment only.** - **Outputs**: a human summary; `--json`; `--issue-draft` writing **sanitized, ready-to-file GitHub issue bodies** per defect (repro input, observed vs expected, versions) that never include host, schema, table, bind or credential identifiers; redaction canaries prove that. - **Bounds**: per-probe timeouts, an overall time budget and a row cap. - **No ceremony**: no report signing or attestation, and no refusal-corpus feed (those parts of old `2q4em.5.4` are dropped). §23.2 e2e on lab lanes: redaction canaries, forced READ_ONLY with the audit showing no privileged action, an injected defect gives exit 2, a missing grant gives exit 3. Existing CLI: `crates/oraclemcp/src/cli.rs` `Command` (no `selftest` today; `Doctor { profile, online, fix }` exits 2 on a blocker). ## Outcome `oraclemcp selftest --profile

[--json] [--issue-draft

] [--http ] [--budget ]` runs from the installed binary against the named profile with the session pinned to READ_ONLY, executes the shared read-only case definitions, the per-tool READ_ONLY sweep, `doctor --online`, transport probes and manifest refusal/bypass probes, classifies each outcome, prints a summary, and exits 0/2/3. `--issue-draft` writes one sanitized Markdown issue body per defect. The audit file of the run contains no privileged action. ## Deliverable - `crates/oraclemcp/src/cli.rs`: `Command::Selftest(SelftestCliArgs)`. - `crates/oraclemcp/src/selftest.rs` (new domain module): probe runner that starts an in-binary MCP server child over stdio (and connects to an HTTP listener when configured) and drives it as an external client would - the probes go through the served transport, not through `Dispatcher::new`; forced READ_ONLY by starting the child with a derived profile whose `max_level` is READ_ONLY (an immutable ceiling for the run, same mechanism as `protected`). - Shared case definitions: `crates/oraclemcp/selftest/readonly_cases.json` (inside the crate so `cargo package` includes it, embedded with `include_str!`), generated from the W4 case files (T4.2 schema, entries with `level: READ_ONLY` and no fixture dependency, rewritten to use only dictionary objects every database has, e.g. `DUAL`, `ALL_USERS`) plus the read-only refusal/bypass probes from `scripts/e2e/cases/release_0_12.json`; a generator `scripts/e2e/w4/export_selftest_cases.py` and a drift check (`--check`) in tier A, so W4 and selftest never drift. - Outcome classifier using error classes from T3.4 (`INSUFFICIENT_PRIVILEGE` -> environment with the privilege named; unsupported capability -> expected refusal; anything contradicting the case expectation -> defect). - Redactor for `--issue-draft` and `--json`: removes host, service, schema, table, column, bind and credential identifiers (replaces with placeholders), keeps ORA codes, classes, tool names, oraclemcp version and Oracle version banner. - `docs/operations.md`: a short "run a field round" section (regenerated by T6.3). ## Implementation notes 1. Read-only by construction, three layers: the derived READ_ONLY-ceiling profile; the selftest never calls `oracle_set_session_level` with a confirmation; the case set contains no write expectation other than "typed refusal". The run ends by verifying its own audit file and asserting no record has a decision above READ_ONLY or a privileged action. 2. Write tools at READ_ONLY: call with a synthetic statement carrying a unique marker; expected `OPERATING_LEVEL_TOO_LOW` (or the tool's documented class). 3. Exit code precedence: any defect -> 2 (even if environment findings exist); otherwise any environment finding -> 3; otherwise 0. Expected refusals do not affect the exit code. 4. Bounds: per-probe timeout (default 15 s), overall budget (default 300 s, remaining probes reported `skipped: budget`), row cap 5 on any read. 5. `--issue-draft` is written only locally; nothing is sent anywhere. 6. Phase-aware connection report comes from `doctor --online` as delivered by T9.4b. ## Test plan Unit (`cargo test -p oraclemcp`): `selftest::tests::exit_code_precedence` (defect+environment -> 2; environment only -> 3; clean -> 0), `redactor_removes_identifiers` (table-driven), `selftest_cases_are_readonly_subset_of_w4` (every embedded case is `READ_ONLY` and exists in W4 definitions), `cli_parses_selftest_args`. E2E on lab lanes (`scripts/e2e/selftest.sh`, registered in `run_all.sh`, lab lane from T4.1): - `selftest_e2e_clean_lane_exit_0`; - `selftest_e2e_forced_readonly_on_admin_profile` (profile with `max_level = ADMIN`; audit shows no privileged action; write tools counted as expected refusals, never executed; `V$SQL` has no marker); - `selftest_e2e_injected_defect_exit_2` (inject a defect by running against a build with a planted wrong expectation or a profile that makes a tool return a contradicting result - documented in the script); - `selftest_e2e_missing_grant_exit_3` (lab user without SELECT on a V$ view the tools need; output names the exact privilege); - `selftest_e2e_redaction_canaries` (planted synthetic host, schema, table, bind value and password markers absent from human output, `--json` and every `--issue-draft` file). Logging: one JSONL line per probe (`probe`, `outcome`, `class`, `duration_ms`), never inputs. ## Proof split This bead proves selftest behaviour on lab lanes; W4 proves tool behaviour; T9.4b proves the phase-aware connection report; field use on real databases is the operator's confirmation round after release. ## Non-goals - Report signing/attestation, refusal-corpus export, `--compare` deltas (dropped as ceremony per R33/R34). - Any write, fixture creation or elevation. ## No-claim boundary A clean selftest proves the read-only surface works on that database for the probes run; it does not prove write paths or tools beyond the read-only subset. ## Considerations - `sec`: touches level forcing and redaction; second-agent review. Fail-closed invariant: nothing here may admit a statement the classifier cannot prove safe for the active level, let elevation exceed a profile's `max_level`, make a `protected` profile writable, or auto-commit DML. The forced READ_ONLY ceiling must not be lowerable-then-raisable during the run. - Structure-owner check: the shared case definitions must live inside `crates/oraclemcp` (a path outside the crate breaks `cargo package`); this bead places the generated subset at `crates/oraclemcp/selftest/readonly_cases.json` with a tier-A drift check against the W4 case files. - Confidentiality (constitution #9): fixtures, goldens, case inputs and logs use synthetic identifiers only; no field/customer/OCI identifier ever enters a committed artifact. Customer databases: the selftest never writes identifiers to disk except in the human summary the operator reads locally; drafts are redacted. - Shares `cli.rs`/`main.rs` with T3.6, T3.7, T4.12 (file-lane:cli). - Consumers: T4.14. ## Absorbs - `oraclemcp-2q4em.5.4` (open, B5.5 selftest): kept - installed-binary field run with read-only tool sweep, `doctor --online`, transport probes, refusal probes, redaction, JSON output, exit codes, operations doc recipe; dropped - signing/attestation (ADR-0012 path), refusal-corpus flywheel, `selftest-report/v1` ADR ceremony, `--compare`, `--offline` mode. - `oraclemcp-2q4em.5.5` (open, B5.5t selftest e2e): kept - redaction canaries, exit codes (0 clean, 2 defect), READ_ONLY profile with write tools refused and never executed and the audit chain showing no privileged action, registration in `run_all.sh`; added - exit 3 for a missing grant; dropped - signed/unsigned labelling and corpus-delta cases.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: `oraclemcp selftest --profile <lab>` on a clean FREE 23ai lane exits 0 and prints a summary with every advertised tool classified.
- [ ] Positive: on a profile with `max_level = ADMIN`, the run's audit file shows no privileged action and every write tool is reported as an expected refusal; `V$SQL` has no probe marker for a write.
- [ ] Negative: an injected defect yields exit 2 and one sanitized issue draft; a missing grant alone yields exit 3 naming the exact privilege.
- [ ] Negative: planted synthetic host, schema, table, bind and password canaries are absent from human output, `--json` and every issue draft.
- [ ] Tests: `exit_code_precedence`, `redactor_removes_identifiers`, `selftest_cases_are_readonly_subset_of_w4`, `selftest_e2e_clean_lane_exit_0`, `selftest_e2e_forced_readonly_on_admin_profile`, `selftest_e2e_injected_defect_exit_2`, `selftest_e2e_missing_grant_exit_3`, `selftest_e2e_redaction_canaries`, `export_selftest_cases.py --check`.
- [ ] Proof class: live external client on lab lanes (installed release binary) + unit; forbidden substitutes: in-process `Dispatcher::new` probes, a mock DB, report signing as evidence.
- [ ] Consumers: T4.14.
- [ ] No-claim: does not prove write paths or tools beyond the read-only subset.

title: Add `oraclemcp demo`: --yes, --dry-run, pinned image, bounds, teardown report
description:
## Context Operator ruling R30 keeps `oraclemcp demo` as a cheap extra (in W4). Plan §6 (binding): reuses the W4 fixture (T4.3). One command starts FREE 23ai (Docker), seeds the schema and plays a scripted agent session: **refuse -> preview -> confirm -> rollback -> audit verify**. It is onboarding, a CI smoke case and launch-video material in one (§22 launch: the 90-second video shows exactly this flow). Requirements: an explicit `--yes` before changing anything in Docker; `--dry-run`; the image **pinned by digest**; **CPU/memory/time bounds** enforced; **port-conflict detection**; reports whether **teardown completed**. An older synthetic golden exists at `tests/golden/demo/roundtrip.json` (scrubbed placeholders); the CI FREE 23ai image pin is in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` job `oracle-free23` (`gvenzl/oracle-free:23-slim@sha256:...`). No `demo` subcommand exists in `crates/oraclemcp/src/cli.rs` today. ## Outcome `oraclemcp demo [--yes] [--dry-run] [--port

] [--keep]` checks Docker availability and the port, prints the exact plan (image digest, container name, port, CPU/memory limits, time budget, seed steps), and only with `--yes` starts a labelled FREE 23ai container with those limits, waits for readiness within the budget, seeds the demo subset of the W4 fixture, then drives its own server over stdio through: a refused write at READ_ONLY, a preview, a confirmed elevation, a DML that is rolled back by default (re-read proves it), and `audit verify` of the session's audit file. It prints a narrated transcript and a final teardown report (container stopped/removed, or kept with `--keep`). ## Deliverable - `crates/oraclemcp/src/cli.rs`: `Command::Demo(DemoCliArgs { yes, dry_run, port, keep, timeout_secs })`. - `crates/oraclemcp/src/demo.rs` (new domain module): Docker CLI orchestration via `std::process::Command` (no Docker SDK dependency): `docker run -d --label oraclemcp.demo=1 --cpus 2 --memory 3g -p 127.0.0.1::1521 gvenzl/oracle-free:23-slim@sha256:` with a generated one-time password passed via env, readiness wait, seed, scripted session, teardown. - Demo seed: `crates/oraclemcp/demo/seed.sql` (inside the crate for `cargo package`), a generated subset of the T4.3 fixture SQL with a drift check (`scripts/e2e/w4/export_demo_seed.py --check` in tier A). - Goldens: `tests/golden/demo/transcript.md` (scrubbed) replaces/extends `roundtrip.json`. - CI smoke: a tier-A job step running `oraclemcp demo --dry-run` (no Docker) and a tier-C/manual job running the full demo. ## Implementation notes 1. Without `--yes`, the command performs only read-only checks (docker version, port probe, image presence) and exits 0 with the plan; `--dry-run` never touches Docker beyond read-only queries even with `--yes`. 2. Port conflict: probe the chosen port (default 1525 to avoid the lab lanes 1518-1523) before `docker run`; on conflict exit with a clear error and a suggested `--port`. 3. Bounds: `--cpus`, `--memory`, and an overall wall-clock budget (default 600 s incl. image start); exceeding the budget triggers teardown and a non-zero exit. 4. Teardown: stop + remove only the container this invocation created (label + id match); report `teardown: completed | kept | failed()`. RULE 1: never touch other containers or images. 5. The scripted session uses the same external-client pattern as selftest (child server over stdio) and never bypasses the guard; the refusal and rollback are real. ## Test plan Unit: `demo::tests::dry_run_prints_plan_without_docker_calls` (command runner mock that fails on any mutating docker call), `demo::tests::no_yes_performs_no_mutation`, `demo::tests::port_conflict_detected`, `demo::tests::teardown_only_removes_own_container`, `seed_matches_fixture_subset` (drift). Live (tier C/manual, Docker host): `demo_e2e_full_flow` - asserts the transcript steps in order (refused, preview, confirm, rollback re-read unchanged, audit verify OK) against the scrubbed golden, and `teardown: completed`; `demo_e2e_budget_exceeded_tears_down` (tiny budget). Logging: one JSONL line per demo step (`step`, `ok`, `duration_ms`). ## Proof split This bead proves the demo flow and its safety bounds; the guard behaviours it shows are proven in depth by W1/W4 cases. ## Non-goals - A demo for XE 18/21 or ADB; video production (launch cluster `bp8ia.11`, after the train). ## No-claim boundary A successful demo proves the scripted path on FREE 23ai only. ## Considerations - Structure-owner check: embedding the seed inside `crates/oraclemcp` (for `cargo package`) with a drift check against the T4.3 fixture SQL; default demo port 1525. - RULE 1 / resource discipline: only the demo's own labelled container is ever stopped or removed; bounded CPU/memory. - Shares `cli.rs`/`main.rs` with T3.6, T3.7, T4.15 (file-lane:cli). Confidentiality (constitution #9): fixtures, goldens, case inputs and logs use synthetic identifiers only; no field/customer/OCI identifier ever enters a committed artifact. - Consumers: none inside the train (launch material, §22); docs via T6.3. ## Absorbs None.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: `oraclemcp demo --yes` on a Docker host starts the digest-pinned FREE 23ai container with CPU/memory limits, plays refuse -> preview -> confirm -> rollback -> audit verify matching the scrubbed golden transcript, and reports `teardown: completed`.
- [ ] Positive: `oraclemcp demo --dry-run` prints the plan and makes no mutating Docker call.
- [ ] Negative: without `--yes` no container is created; an occupied port is detected before `docker run`; exceeding the time budget tears down and exits non-zero; other containers are untouched.
- [ ] Tests: `dry_run_prints_plan_without_docker_calls`, `no_yes_performs_no_mutation`, `port_conflict_detected`, `teardown_only_removes_own_container`, `seed_matches_fixture_subset`, `demo_e2e_full_flow`, `demo_e2e_budget_exceeded_tears_down`.
- [ ] Proof class: live (real Docker + FREE 23ai) + unit; forbidden substitutes: a mocked Docker for the full-flow claim.
- [ ] Consumers: T6.3 (docs); launch cluster after the train.
- [ ] No-claim: proves the scripted FREE 23ai path only.

title: Fix TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE projection: served wall clock shifted by the offset
description:
## Context
Found live by the W4 external-client fidelity case (T4.3, .9.3, commit 2148ffc5) on FREE 23ai over stdio AND Streamable HTTP: a row inserted as `TIMESTAMP '2020-02-29 23:30:00 +05:45'` is served by `oracle_query` as `2020-02-29T17:45:00+05:45` — the numeric offset is kept but the wall clock is shifted by -05:45, i.e. the value names a different instant. An independent database re-read returns the correct `23:30:00 +05:45`.

Root cause (per the reporting agent; re-derive with `rg -n format_timestamp_tz crates/oraclemcp-db`): driver-cx documents `QueryValue::TimestampTz` fields as UTC with a separate display offset (`../rust-oracledb/docs/PARITY_LEDGER.md`, `sql_convert.rs`). `crates/oraclemcp-db/src/connection.rs` (~4272-4306 at 55a1e1ff) passes the raw UTC fields to `format_timestamp_tz` (~5978), which only appends the offset instead of converting UTC -> local wall clock first.

## Outcome
Every served TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE (and WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE, if routed through the same projection) renders the correct local wall clock for its offset/region, preserving the instant, on both backends (driver-cx primary and the official oracledb fallback).

## Deliverable
- Fix the projection in crates/oraclemcp-db (connection.rs / the TSTZ formatter); do not change driver-cx semantics.
- Check the official-backend projection (oracledb_backend.rs) for the same bug and fix it there if present.

## Test plan
- Unit: table-driven projection tests for offsets +05:45, -09:30, +00:00, +14:00, a DST-straddling region name, and a date crossing midnight/leap day (2020-02-29) — expected strings computed independently, not from the formatter under test.
- Live: the W4 TSTZ fidelity case in scripts/e2e/w4/cases (already pinned to 23:30 + independent DB reread) must go green on free23 over stdio and HTTP; also run xe21/xe18 lanes.
- Negative: a formatter that appends the offset to UTC fields (the current bug) fails the unit table.

## Non-goals
No change to TSTZ bind (input) handling unless the same defect is found there — if so, file it discovered-from this bead.

## Considerations
Hot file crates/oraclemcp-db/src/connection.rs: reserve narrowly. Confidentiality: synthetic values only.

title: Make the rig own XE 18, XE 21 and FREE 23ai containers and write tier-C results
description:
## Context
`scripts/rig/oracle_l1.sh` (lanes `xe18 xe21 free23`) today expects containers `oracle-xe18-1518`/`oracle-xe21-1520`, maps `free23` to :1522, and delegates bootstrap to the driver repo (`$ORACLEMCP_DRIVER_ROOT/scripts/container.sh`, `bootstrap_live_schema.sh`). The host actually has: running `rust-oracledb-free` (FREE 23ai :1522, owned by the driver repo) and `plsql-intelligence-xe` (FREE 23ai :1521, owned by the engine repo); stopped `oraclemcp-xe18-rel` (:1518) and `oraclemcp-xe21-rel` (:1520). Old beads `2q4em.5.1` (repo-owned lab lanes: pinned digests, synthetic principals, `up`/`down`, `rig.sh doctor`) and `2q4em.5.2` (a tier-2 nightly version matrix producing exact-SHA evidence) are absorbed.
Plan §6 (binding): fix `scripts/rig/oracle_l1.sh`; **the oraclemcp rig owns container lifecycle and the fixture; the driver repo's scripts are never called from oraclemcp tests.** Tier C (release-only) runs the W4 suite on XE 18, XE 21, FREE 23ai and Always-Free ADB on the release-candidate SHA; results feed the release proof (T5.5: `tests/artifacts/local_gate/results-<sha>.json` gains tier-C pass/fail), committed before tagging. R24/R34: no nightly ceremony lane; tier C is release-only (the nightly `live-matrix.yml` of `2q4em.5.2` is not built).

## Outcome
`scripts/rig/oracle_l1.sh up|status|down [--lane xe18|xe21|free23]` creates (when absent), starts and health-checks oraclemcp-owned containers from pinned image digests with synthetic principals and the idempotent bootstrap SQL living in this repo; `down` stops only containers it owns; nothing calls into the driver repo. A tier-C runner `scripts/rig/tier_c.sh --sha <sha>` runs the W4 suite (T4.2) on each lane and writes a per-lane pass/fail summary in the format T5.5 binds into the release proof.

## Deliverable
- `scripts/rig/oracle_l1.sh`: drop `DRIVER_ROOT`/`DRIVER_CONTAINER`/`DRIVER_BOOTSTRAP`; container names `oraclemcp-xe18-rel` (:1518, XEPDB1), `oraclemcp-xe21-rel` (:1520, XEPDB1), `oraclemcp-free23-rel` (FREE 23ai, FREEPDB1; port decided below); images pinned by digest in `scripts/rig/lanes.toml` (`gvenzl/oracle-xe:18-slim`, `gvenzl/oracle-xe:21-slim`, `gvenzl/oracle-free:23-slim` - the FREE digest equal to the one pinned in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` job `oracle-free23`).
- `scripts/rig/bootstrap/*.sql`: the lane bootstrap (application user, grants the W4 fixture needs: CREATE SESSION/TABLE/VIEW/PROCEDURE/TRIGGER/SEQUENCE/TYPE, EXECUTE on DBMS_RLS and DBMS_FLASHBACK, SELECT on the V$ views the tools read) with synthetic principals only; moves in the existing `oracle_l1_capabilities.sql`/`oracle_l1_privilege_matrix.sql`/`oracle_l1_vpd_fixture.sql` where they belong.
- `scripts/rig/rig.sh doctor`: one JSON line per lane (lane, container, image digest, present, healthy, version, port).
- `scripts/rig/tier_c.sh`: runs T4.2's driver per lane (`--lane xe18|xe21|free23`, plus `adb` delegated to the W9 harness T9.1) and writes `target/e2e/tier_c/<sha>/summary.json` (`{sha, lanes:[{lane, version, cases_total, cases_failed, verdict}]}`).

## Implementation notes
1. Port for `oraclemcp-free23-rel`: :1522 is held by the driver repo's `rust-oracledb-free`; use **:1523** by default with `ORACLEMCP_RIG_FREE23_PORT` override, and update every e2e script that hard-codes 1522 for the free23 lane (re-derive with `rg -n 1522 scripts`). Adopting another repo's container is forbidden (ownership rule).
2. `up` is idempotent: create if absent, start if stopped, wait for the gvenzl readiness sentinel with a bounded timeout, run bootstrap, smoke-query.
3. `down` stops only containers carrying the label `oraclemcp.rig=1`; removal requires an explicit `--remove` flag passed by the operator (RULE 1).
4. Admin passwords stay runtime-only (`ORACLEMCP_RIG_L1_*_ADMIN_PASSWORD`), never logged (canary assertion in the selftest).
5. Memory: three XE/FREE containers need several GB; `up --lane` starts one lane at a time for local runs; tier C runs lanes sequentially.

## Test plan
- `scripts/rig/oracle_l1.sh --selftest`/`up --dry-run`: prints the three lanes with names, pinned digests and ports; asserts no reference to `rust-oracledb` paths (`rg` check inside the selftest); registered in `scripts/e2e/run_all.sh` and asserted by a harness test in `crates/oraclemcp/tests/e2e_harness.rs` (`rig_l1_dry_run_lists_owned_lanes_with_digests`).
- Live: on a host with no oraclemcp lanes, `up` brings all three to smoke-green; `rig.sh doctor` reports them; `tier_c.sh --sha HEAD` on FREE 23ai produces a valid summary.
- Password canary: no log line contains the admin password (planted value).
Logging: one JSON line per lane action (`lane`, `action`, `image_digest`, `ready_ms`, `smoke_ok`).

## Proof split
This bead proves lane lifecycle, bootstrap ownership and the tier-C summary format. T4.3 owns the per-run fixture; T4.11 wires tier A and the tier-C runner into CI/release; T5.5 binds the summary into the release proof; T9.1 owns the ADB lane; R.1 performs the final tier-C run.

## Non-goals
- A nightly/scheduled live-matrix workflow (from `2q4em.5.2`; not built per R24/R34).
- Managing the driver or engine repos' containers.
- ADB provisioning (T9.1).

## No-claim boundary
Lanes coming up does not prove any tool works on them; the W4 cases do.

## Considerations
- Structure-owner check: the FREE 23ai lane port. The plan lists the host's :1522 container as the driver's `rust-oracledb-free`; owning the lane requires a separate oraclemcp container, so this bead chooses :1523 (overridable). CI (`ci.yml` service container) is unaffected.
- RULE 1: never remove containers or volumes without the operator's explicit flag. Resource discipline (constitution #6): sequential lanes.
- Confidentiality (constitution #9): fixtures, goldens, case inputs and logs use synthetic identifiers only; no field/customer/OCI identifier ever enters a committed artifact.
- Consumers: T2.7, T4.11, T5.5, T12.3, T4.12 (reuses lane conventions).

## Absorbs
- `oraclemcp-2q4em.5.1` (open, B5.1 repo-owned lab lanes): kept - `up` creates XE 18/XE 21/FREE 23ai from pinned digests recorded in `scripts/rig/lanes.toml`, bootstrap SQL moved into this repo, `down` stops only owned lanes, `rig.sh doctor` per-lane JSON line, dry-run registered in `run_all.sh` with a harness test, password canary.
- `oraclemcp-2q4em.5.2` (open, B5.2 nightly version matrix): kept - the multi-version run producing per-SHA results that the release consumer binds (now as tier-C `summary.json` for T5.5); dropped as ceremony - the nightly schedule, the 7-consecutive-green-nights requirement and heartbeat taxonomy work.

- [ ] Positive: on a host without oraclemcp lanes, `scripts/rig/oracle_l1.sh up` brings `oraclemcp-xe18-rel`, `oraclemcp-xe21-rel` and `oraclemcp-free23-rel` to smoke-green and `rig.sh doctor` reports each with version and image digest.
- [ ] Positive: `scripts/rig/tier_c.sh --sha <sha>` writes `target/e2e/tier_c/<sha>/summary.json` with one verdict per lane.
- [ ] Negative: `oracle_l1.sh` and every script it calls contain no reference to the rust-oracledb checkout (selftest `rg` check fails on a planted reference).
- [ ] Negative: `down` leaves a non-owned container (e.g. `rust-oracledb-free`) untouched; no admin password appears in any log line.
- [ ] Tests: `oracle_l1.sh --selftest`, `rig_l1_dry_run_lists_owned_lanes_with_digests`, live `up`/`doctor`/`tier_c.sh` run log.
- [ ] Proof class: live (real containers) + offline selftest; forbidden substitutes: the driver repo's containers or scripts.
- [ ] Consumers: T2.7, T4.11, T5.5, T12.3.
- [ ] No-claim: does not prove tool behaviour on the lanes.

title: Build the external-client tool-matrix driver for stdio and Streamable HTTP
description:
## Context
R8 (every tool gets a deliberate in-house live test: create objects, run all statement kinds, verify deterministically), R25 (nothing deferred; all tools tested end to end). Plan §6 (binding): external client only - the real release-profile binary over MCP stdio **and** Streamable HTTP, no in-process dispatcher, no server helper crates in the client; deterministic verification (exact ordered rows, exact error class + ORA code, audit entries with a verified hash chain, an independent re-read of database state after every mutation, ordering by barriers never elapsed time, goldens with volatile fields scrubbed); one JSONL line per case (tool, level, input hash, expected, actual, verdict, timings) plus a summary table in the results JSON; counts come from the registry, never hard-coded.
Today: `scripts/rig/tool_surface_sweep.py` is a raw-wire stdio sweep that checks envelopes only and hard-codes `EXPECTED_REGISTRY_CANONICAL = 34`/`EXPECTED_REGISTRY_ALIASES = 25`; per-scenario drivers exist in `scripts/e2e/*_session.py` (`oracle_ladder_session.py` already drives stdio and stateful Streamable HTTP, JSON-line events, evidence files; `reversible_session.py`, `sql_policy_session.py`, `editions_session.py`, `time_diff_session.py`), orchestrated by `scripts/e2e/lib.sh` and `run_all.sh`. The registry lives in `crates/oraclemcp/src/registry.rs` (`TOOL_NAMES` 34 canonical + 25 aliases, `alias_target`, `tool_registry()`), PL/SQL tools in `crates/oraclemcp/src/plsql_tools.rs` (`TOOL_NAMES`, 9).
Plan §6 (binding): **capability-driven matrix** generated from the **runtime registry** (read from the binary's `tools/list`, never hard-coded) plus an explicit database capability matrix (version, privileges, licence, feature); every canonical tool has a positive case on at least one capable target and negative/level cases on every applicable target; an unsupported version/privilege/licence combination must return the exact expected typed refusal. Extend the existing external harness into **one tool-matrix driver**. The W4 lane fails when a manifest case (T4.0) is missing or red.

## Outcome
`scripts/e2e/w4/driver.py` (stdlib-only Python, no oraclemcp crates or MCP libraries) installs/uses the release-profile binary, speaks MCP over stdio and Streamable HTTP, reads the tool set from `tools/list`, loads per-family case files and the capability matrix, runs each applicable case on each transport, verifies deterministically (ordered rows, error class + ORA code, independent DB re-read, audit chain verify, scrubbed goldens), and writes JSONL + a results JSON. It fails when any registered tool lacks required cases, any manifest case is missing or red, or any case is red. Case beads (T4.4-T4.9a, T12.9, T13.8, T14.9) only add case files.

## Deliverable
- `scripts/e2e/w4/driver.py`: transports (stdio newline-delimited JSON-RPC; Streamable HTTP with session id, bearer auth as the lab profile requires), `initialize` + `tools/list` discovery, case runner, barrier primitives (explicit sync points between concurrent clients; no sleeps as ordering), results writer.
- `scripts/e2e/w4/capabilities.json`: capability vocabulary and per-lane facts (`version`, `edition`, `priv:*`, `feature:*` such as VECTOR/JSON type/AWR licence, `adb`) plus a probe that fills observed capabilities at run start (e.g. `V$VERSION`, privilege checks) and fails on a declared/observed mismatch.
- `scripts/e2e/w4/cases/<family>.json` schema: `case_id`, `tool`, `level`, `transports`, `requires` (capabilities), `setup`/`call`/`expect` (`rows` exact ordered | `error_class` + `ora_code` | `json_subset` | `golden`), `db_reread` (SQL run by the harness's own python-oracledb connection), `audit_expect`, `on_unsupported` (the exact typed refusal).
- Generic W3 contract case families generated from each tool's `inputSchema`: `w4_contract_<tool>_unknown_argument`, `w4_contract_<tool>_duplicate_member`, `w4_contract_<tool>_wrong_enum` (for enum properties); asserted green by T4.8.
- `scripts/e2e/w4/scrub.py`: volatile-field scrubber (timestamps, request ids, SCNs, durations, run ids, session ids) shared with goldens under `tests/golden/w4/`.
- Completeness check hook: every tool name from `tools/list` must match at least one positive case per the capability rule (the full gate is T4.14; the driver exposes `--coverage-report`).
- Manifest enforcement: calls `scripts/e2e/cases/validate_manifest.py --required-ids`/`--check-results` (T4.0).
- `scripts/e2e/w4.sh` wrapper in the `lib.sh` conventions, registered in `run_all.sh`; `tool_surface_sweep.py` retired into the driver (its envelope checks become the generic family) - remove hard-coded counts.

## Implementation notes
1. Build the binary with the release profile (`cargo build --release -p oraclemcp --bin oraclemcp` under `scripts/build_lease.sh` when workspace-wide) or take `--binary <path>`; never import server helper crates.
2. Independent re-read uses python-oracledb thin (already pinned in CI as `PYTHON_ORACLEDB_VERSION`) with the harness's own fixture-owner credentials; the server under test never sees these reads.
3. Audit: each run configures a fresh audit file + test key; after the run `oraclemcp audit verify` must pass and `audit_expect` assertions (tool, decision, outcome, failure class) are checked record by record.
4. V$SQL assertions for refusal cases: the case embeds a unique marker comment; the harness queries `V$SQL` by marker with its own privileged read (the bootstrap grants SELECT on V$SQL to the harness user).
5. Unsupported combos: when `requires` is not met by the lane, the case runs `on_unsupported` and asserts the exact typed refusal instead of skipping; a silent skip is a failure.
6. Absorbed scope: `q289u` -> the column-type family asserts exact JSON for TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE (offset preserved) and VECTOR (element type, dimension, values) on real rows (cases authored in T4.6 via `oracle_query`/`sample_rows`); `11000` -> an error-path family (malformed frames, mid-call cancellation, server kill + restart, token expiry) with retry-no-duplicate-effect postconditions checked by DB re-read; `kjksu` -> an HTTP auth family (the OAuth rejection classes + one accept case) run through the HTTP transport.
7. Performance: cases grouped by family so T4.11 can split lanes if the 25-minute tier-A budget is exceeded.

## Test plan
- `python3 scripts/e2e/w4/driver.py --selftest` (offline): parses every case file against the schema; runs a stub transport that returns planted responses to prove the verifier fails on wrong row order, wrong error class, missing audit record, a broken chain, a silently skipped unsupported case, and a tool with no positive case.
- `manifest_enforcement_integration`: a results file missing one manifest case makes the driver exit non-zero.
- Harness registration test in `crates/oraclemcp/tests/e2e_harness.rs`: `w4_driver_is_registered_and_dry_runs`.
- Live smoke on FREE 23ai: the generic W3 contract family for every tool on both transports (these cases go green once T3.1-T3.3 land; T4.8 owns that verdict), plus the `q289u` TSTZ/VECTOR cases and the `kjksu` HTTP auth family.
Logging: one JSONL line per case per transport (`case_id`, tool, level, transport, input_sha256, expected, actual, verdict, duration_ms) to `target/e2e/w4/<lane>/cases.jsonl`; `results.json` with a summary table (tool x transport x verdict).

## Proof split
This bead proves the driver, verifier and generic families work and fail correctly; per-tool behaviour is proven by the case beads T4.4-T4.9a, T12.9, T13.8, T14.9; the completeness gate is T4.14; CI wiring is T4.11.

## Non-goals
- Writing the per-tool case content (T4.4-T4.9a).
- In-process tests, mocks, or MCP client libraries.
- Test attestation/signing (cluster K retired, R29).

## No-claim boundary
A green driver selftest proves the harness catches planted failures; it proves nothing about any tool until the case files run live.

## Considerations
- Structure-owner check: absorbed beads `q289u` (type fidelity), `11000` (error-path matrix) and `kjksu` (OAuth rejection/verifier tamper matrices) are only partly harness work; their scope is kept as case families run by this driver (verdict-verifier tamper cases stay unit tests in `oraclemcp-verifier`).
- The driver is the shared hot file of Track B: case beads must not edit it; they add case files only. Confidentiality (constitution #9): fixtures, goldens, case inputs and logs use synthetic identifiers only; no field/customer/OCI identifier ever enters a committed artifact.
- Consumers: T4.4, T4.5, T4.6, T4.7, T4.8, T4.9, T4.9a, T4.10, T4.14, T4.15 (shares case definitions), T7.13, T12.9, T13.8.

## Absorbs
- `oraclemcp-h-server-db-type-fidelity-tstz-vector-q289u` (deferred): kept - exact-JSON fidelity of real-row TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE and VECTOR values (offset, element type, shape, values) as a W4 case family.
- `oraclemcp-h-server-error-path-matrix-11000` (deferred): kept - fault/error-path family (malformed responses, cancellation boundaries, token expiry, restart recovery, retry-no-duplicate-effect) through the external client; dropped - disk/partial-write and clock-regression injection (not reachable externally; remain existing unit fault-injection tests).
- `oraclemcp-h-server-oauth-verifier-matrices-kjksu` (deferred): kept - the OAuth rejection classes plus one accept case as an HTTP-transport family; verdict-verifier tamper cases kept as unit tests, not live.

title: Create the run-id-stamped W4 fixture schema and a janitor for stale owned runs
description:
## Context
R8 (every tool gets a deliberate in-house live test: create objects, run all statement kinds, verify deterministically), R25 (nothing deferred; all tools tested end to end). Plan §6 (binding): external client only - the real release-profile binary over MCP stdio **and** Streamable HTTP, no in-process dispatcher, no server helper crates in the client; deterministic verification (exact ordered rows, exact error class + ORA code, audit entries with a verified hash chain, an independent re-read of database state after every mutation, ordering by barriers never elapsed time, goldens with volatile fields scrubbed); one JSONL line per case (tool, level, input hash, expected, actual, verdict, timings) plus a summary table in the results JSON; counts come from the registry, never hard-coded.
Plan §6 fixture design (binding): both fixture schemas and every created object are stamped with an exact **run id**, and teardown records its verdict. A janitor removes only stale objects owned by earlier run ids; **broad schema-prefix drops are forbidden**. Contents: tables covering every served column type - NUMBER edge values, VARCHAR2/NVARCHAR2, DATE, TIMESTAMP/TZ/LTZ, INTERVAL, CLOB/BLOB/NCLOB, RAW, JSON, VECTOR on 23ai, virtual and invisible columns; a view, index, trigger, sequence and type; a package with a pure function, a DML procedure, a DDL procedure and an autonomous-transaction procedure; a VPD policy and a masked column; a second schema for cross-owner cases. The same fixture is reused by `oraclemcp demo` (T4.12), the driver parity beads (T8.6-T8.8), W7 invocation gates (T7.13) and W12-W14 live suites.

## Outcome
`scripts/e2e/w4/fixture.py setup --run-id <id>` creates two schemas (`W4O_<id>` owner, `W4X_<id>` cross-owner) with the full object set and a VPD policy + masked column on a lab lane; every object carries the run id (name suffix and a `COMMENT`/registry row); `teardown --run-id <id>` drops exactly what that run created and writes a verdict JSON; `janitor --older-than <h>` removes only schemas/objects whose recorded run id is from an earlier, finished or expired run.

## Deliverable
- `scripts/e2e/w4/fixture/*.sql`: ordered DDL per object class with a `&run_id` substitution; version guards (VECTOR and JSON type only on 23ai; JSON stored as `CLOB CHECK (IS JSON)` on 18/21).
- `scripts/e2e/w4/fixture.py`: `setup`, `teardown`, `janitor`, `describe` (prints the object inventory the cases reference); uses python-oracledb with the lane admin credentials from the rig (T4.1 conventions); records each run in a lane-level registry table `W4_RUNS(run_id, started_at, finished_at, verdict, objects_json)` in a dedicated rig-owned schema.
- Object set (names are synthetic): `T_TYPES` (one column per served type incl. NUMBER edge rows: 0, -0, 1e-130, 9.99...e125, max precision 38 digits, NULL; NVARCHAR2 non-ASCII; DATE/TIMESTAMP boundary values; TZ with a non-UTC offset; INTERVAL YM/DS; CLOB/NCLOB > 32 KB; BLOB; RAW; virtual column; invisible column), `T_PARENT`/`T_CHILD` (FK), `V_TYPES` view, `IX_TYPES` index, `TRG_CHILD_AUDIT` trigger, `SEQ_W4` sequence, `TY_POINT` object type + body, package `PKG_W4` (`pure_fn`, `dml_proc`, `ddl_proc` with a compile-time-literal DDL, `auto_proc` with `PRAGMA AUTONOMOUS_TRANSACTION`), VPD policy on `T_SECURE` via `DBMS_RLS.ADD_POLICY`, a masked column on `T_SECURE` configured in the lab profile's masking config, cross-owner table + grant in `W4X_<id>`.
- The same SQL files are the single source for T4.12's demo seed (T4.12 embeds a subset).

## Implementation notes
1. Run id: `w4` + UTC timestamp + 6 random hex, uppercase-safe, length-bounded so names stay within Oracle's identifier limit on 18c (30 bytes): schema `W4O_<12-char id>`.
2. Teardown drops the two schemas of this run with `DROP USER ... CASCADE` **only after** checking the `W4_RUNS` row matches this run id; the VPD policy is dropped first. Verdict JSON: dropped objects, leftovers, errors.
3. Janitor: selects run ids from `W4_RUNS` with `finished_at IS NOT NULL` or `started_at` older than the threshold, and drops only those users; it never matches by prefix alone (a `W4O_` user without a registry row is reported, not dropped).
4. Required privileges come from T4.1's bootstrap; on CI's gvenzl service container the fixture runs as SYSTEM-granted app user (see the existing grant step in `ci.yml`).
5. Masking config for the masked column lives in the generated lab profile (the harness writes the profile TOML), not in the DB.

## Test plan
- Live on each lane (FREE 23ai in tier A, XE 18/21 in tier C): `fixture.py setup` then `describe` lists every required object; `teardown` verdict shows zero leftovers; a second run concurrently with the first proves isolation (distinct run ids, janitor does not touch the live run).
- `fixture.py --selftest` (offline): renders the SQL for 18/21/23 and asserts version guards, identifier length limits, and that no statement drops by prefix (`rg`-style check for `LIKE 'W4%'` in DROP paths).
- Janitor negative: a planted `W4O_` user with no registry row survives the janitor and is reported.
Logging: JSONL per object created/dropped (`run_id`, object, action, ok, ms) and the teardown verdict JSON.

## Proof split
This bead proves the fixture builds and tears down cleanly per run on each version; tool behaviour against it is proven by T4.4-T4.9a; type-value fidelity by T4.2's families and T8.6-T8.8.

## Non-goals
- Test cases themselves; ADB-specific fixture differences (handled when T9.6a runs the matrix; fixture SQL must not require SYS on ADB - noted for T9.x).

## No-claim boundary
A clean setup/teardown does not prove any tool returns correct values for these objects.

## Considerations
- RULE 1 / safety: the janitor deletes database objects only for recorded, finished run ids; never broad prefix drops; never on non-lab lanes (the script refuses a profile not marked `lab = true` in the rig config).
- Confidentiality (constitution #9): fixtures, goldens, case inputs and logs use synthetic identifiers only; no field/customer/OCI identifier ever enters a committed artifact.
- Consumers: T4.4, T4.5, T4.6, T4.7, T4.9, T4.9a, T4.12, T7.13, T8.6, T8.7, T8.8, T12.9, T13.8, T14.9.

## Absorbs
None.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: on FREE 23ai, XE 21 and XE 18, `fixture.py setup` creates every listed object (VECTOR/JSON type only on 23ai) and `teardown` reports zero leftovers.
- [ ] Positive: two concurrent runs use distinct run ids and neither's teardown or the janitor touches the other.
- [ ] Negative: a planted `W4O_` user without a `W4_RUNS` row survives the janitor and is reported.
- [ ] Negative: the selftest fails if any DROP path matches by name prefix.
- [ ] Tests: `fixture.py --selftest`, live setup/teardown/janitor logs per lane.
- [ ] Proof class: live (real databases) + offline selftest; forbidden substitutes: a mock DB or an in-memory SQL engine.
- [ ] Consumers: T4.4, T4.5, T4.6, T4.7, T4.9, T4.9a, T4.12, T7.13, T8.6, T8.7, T8.8, T12.9, T13.8, T14.9.
- [ ] No-claim: does not prove tool correctness.

title: Write W4 cases for query, execute, previews, session level, checkpoint and undo_to
description:
## Context
R8 (every tool gets a deliberate in-house live test: create objects, run all statement kinds, verify deterministically), R25 (nothing deferred; all tools tested end to end). Plan §6 (binding): external client only - the real release-profile binary over MCP stdio **and** Streamable HTTP, no in-process dispatcher, no server helper crates in the client; deterministic verification (exact ordered rows, exact error class + ORA code, audit entries with a verified hash chain, an independent re-read of database state after every mutation, ordering by barriers never elapsed time, goldens with volatile fields scrubbed); one JSONL line per case (tool, level, input hash, expected, actual, verdict, timings) plus a summary table in the results JSON; counts come from the registry, never hard-coded.
Tools in scope: `oracle_query`, `oracle_execute`, `oracle_preview_sql`, `oracle_preview_dml`, `oracle_set_session_level`, `oracle_checkpoint`, `oracle_undo_to`. Coverage gaps today (measured): No MERGE/CTE-DML/multi-row/LOB DML matrix.
Plan §6 statement matrix (binding), per tool and at each level: allowed vs refused; DML rollback-by-default vs confirmed commit; DDL via preview -> token -> apply; the W1 bypass shapes; the W2 runtime cases (idle, cancel, concurrency, timeout-0, second instance); the W3 negatives. Every canonical tool has a positive case on at least one capable target and negative/level cases on every applicable target; an unsupported version/privilege/licence combination returns the exact typed refusal.
The guarded write ladder: READ_ONLY < READ_WRITE < DDL < ADMIN; elevation via preview -> confirmation token -> TTL-bounded window; DML rolls back by default and commits only with explicit confirmation; `protected` profiles pinned at READ_ONLY. Existing external coverage (ladder, reversible, sql_policy, editions, time_diff, failure_recovery) is reused where it already asserts values; the missing part is the DML matrix.

## Outcome
`scripts/e2e/w4/cases/write-tools.json` holds deliberate cases for every tool in scope, and they are green over stdio and Streamable HTTP on FREE 23ai (tier A) and XE 18/XE 21 (tier C), each verified by exact values, typed errors, an independent DB re-read after mutations and a verified audit chain.

## Deliverable
- `scripts/e2e/w4/cases/write-tools.json` (case data only; no driver edits - request driver changes on T4.2's thread).
- Goldens (scrubbed) under `tests/golden/w4/write-tools/` for stable structured outputs.
- Case list (ids are `w4_<tool>_<case>`):
  - `w4_query_types_exact_rows` (every T_TYPES column, exact JSON incl. NUMBER as string), `w4_query_cte_read`, `w4_query_cross_owner_read`, `w4_query_vpd_filtered_rows`, `w4_query_masked_column_masked`, `w4_query_dml_refused_readonly`.
  - `w4_execute_insert_rollback_default`, `w4_execute_update_confirmed_commit`, `w4_execute_delete_multi_row_rollback`, `w4_execute_merge_rollback`, `w4_execute_cte_dml_refused_or_admitted_per_classifier` (records the classifier's decision as the expectation), `w4_execute_lob_insert_clob_blob`, `w4_execute_ddl_preview_token_apply`, `w4_execute_ddl_refused_at_read_write`, `w4_execute_token_replay_refused`, `w4_execute_protected_profile_refused`.
  - `w4_preview_sql_verdict_levels` (one statement per level), `w4_preview_dml_row_estimate_matches_reread`.
  - `w4_set_session_level_elevate_confirm`, `w4_set_session_level_exceeds_max_level_refused`, `w4_set_session_level_ttl_expiry_returns_readonly` (barrier on expiry event, not sleep), `w4_enable_disable_writes_alias_route` (wrapper check deferred to T4.8).
  - `w4_checkpoint_then_undo_to_restores_rows`, `w4_undo_to_unknown_checkpoint_typed_error`.
  - `w4_audit_report_after_ladder` (renders the run's audit via `oraclemcp audit report`; T3.7).

## Implementation notes
1. Use only T4.3 fixture objects (resolved via `fixture.py describe` for the run id); no pre-existing schema objects.
2. Every mutation case re-reads state with the harness's own connection; every refusal case asserts the audit and `V$SQL` marker per T4.2 conventions.
3. Level cases: run each tool at READ_ONLY and at every level where its behaviour changes (via `oracle_set_session_level` preview -> confirm on a writable lab profile; a `protected` lab profile proves the pinned ceiling).
4. W1 bypass-shape and W2 runtime cases that exercise these tools are authored by their owning beads (T1.x, T2.x) in this family's file when they land; this bead leaves a documented section for them and does not wait on them.
5. The generic W3 contract negatives (unknown argument, duplicate member, wrong enum, argument aliases) are generated by T4.2 and owned by T4.8; do not duplicate them here.
6. Unsupported combos on a lane (licence/privilege/version) assert the exact typed refusal, never skip.

## Test plan
Every case runs over stdio and Streamable HTTP through the T4.2 driver against the T4.3 fixture; tier A lane FREE 23ai; tier C XE 18/21, FREE 23ai (and ADB through T9.6a). Case ids follow `w4_<tool>_<case>`. Each case logs one JSONL line (`case_id`, tool, level, transport, input hash, expected, actual, verdict, timings). Mutating cases re-read DB state through an independent python-oracledb connection owned by the harness (never through the server) and verify the audit chain with `oraclemcp audit verify` after the run.
Negative cases that a naive implementation fails: an UPDATE without confirmation leaves the re-read row unchanged (rollback-by-default); a replayed confirmation token is refused; elevation above `max_level` is refused; DML at READ_ONLY is refused with zero audit executions and no `V$SQL` marker.

## Proof split
