title: Write W4 cases for search, semantic_search, diff, orient, health, plans and profiles
description:
## Context
R8 (every tool gets a deliberate in-house live test: create objects, run all statement kinds, verify deterministically), R25 (nothing deferred; all tools tested end to end). Plan §6 (binding): external client only - the real release-profile binary over MCP stdio **and** Streamable HTTP, no in-process dispatcher, no server helper crates in the client; deterministic verification (exact ordered rows, exact error class + ORA code, audit entries with a verified hash chain, an independent re-read of database state after every mutation, ordering by barriers never elapsed time, goldens with volatile fields scrubbed); one JSONL line per case (tool, level, input hash, expected, actual, verdict, timings) plus a summary table in the results JSON; counts come from the registry, never hard-coded.
Tools in scope: `oracle_search_objects`, `oracle_search_source`, `oracle_semantic_search`, `oracle_diff`, `oracle_orient`, `oracle_top_queries`, `oracle_plan_timeline`, `oracle_db_health`, `oracle_explain_plan`, `oracle_connection_info`, `oracle_switch_profile`, `oracle_list_profiles`. Coverage gaps today (measured): diff not in CI; orient in-process only; top_queries, plan_timeline, db_health and search_source have no live test; semantic_search 23ai only.
Plan §6 statement matrix (binding), per tool and at each level: allowed vs refused; DML rollback-by-default vs confirmed commit; DDL via preview -> token -> apply; the W1 bypass shapes; the W2 runtime cases (idle, cancel, concurrency, timeout-0, second instance); the W3 negatives. Every canonical tool has a positive case on at least one capable target and negative/level cases on every applicable target; an unsupported version/privilege/licence combination returns the exact typed refusal.
`oracle_semantic_search` needs VECTOR (23ai only): on 18/21 it must return its exact typed refusal. `oracle_top_queries` historical mode and `oracle_plan_timeline` read AWR (Diagnostics Pack licence) - the lab lanes declare the licence capability explicitly; without it the typed refusal is asserted. `oracle_diff` uses flashback/SCN (T2.1 capability cache). `oracle_connection_info`/`oracle_switch_profile` carry #44's effective-access block (T3.5). `oracle_explain_plan` is hardened by T1.8.

## Outcome
`scripts/e2e/w4/cases/ops-tools.json` holds deliberate cases for every tool in scope, and they are green over stdio and Streamable HTTP on FREE 23ai (tier A) and XE 18/XE 21 (tier C), each verified by exact values, typed errors, an independent DB re-read after mutations and a verified audit chain.

## Deliverable
- `scripts/e2e/w4/cases/ops-tools.json` (case data only; no driver edits - request driver changes on T4.2's thread).
- Goldens (scrubbed) under `tests/golden/w4/ops-tools/` for stable structured outputs.
- Case list (ids are `w4_<tool>_<case>`):
  - `w4_search_objects_name_like`, `w4_search_objects_object_types_filter` (#41), `w4_search_objects_fleet_names_only`, `w4_search_source_needle_exact_lines`, `w4_search_source_object_type_filter`.
  - `w4_semantic_search_ranked_results_23ai`, `w4_semantic_search_unsupported_version_typed_refusal` (18/21).
  - `w4_diff_as_of_scn_detects_change` (mutation between two SCNs, re-read), `w4_diff_flashback_capability_unavailable_typed` (lane without the grant), `w4_diff_retention_exceeded_typed`.
  - `w4_orient_sections_exact`, `w4_orient_include_filter`, `w4_orient_external_client` (replaces in-process-only coverage).
  - `w4_top_queries_live_cursor_cache_contains_marker`, `w4_top_queries_historical_without_licence_typed_refusal`, `w4_plan_timeline_awr_or_typed_refusal`, `w4_db_health_invalid_objects_includes_fixture_invalid_proc`, `w4_db_health_subcheck_filter`.
  - `w4_explain_plan_select_plan_rows`, `w4_explain_plan_dml_inner_sql_refused_readonly`, `w4_explain_plan_plan_table_write_flag`.
  - `w4_connection_info_effective_access_readonly_pinned` (#44), `w4_connection_info_effective_access_after_elevation`, `w4_switch_profile_to_protected_resets_level`, `w4_list_profiles_exact_names_no_secrets`.

## Implementation notes
1. Use only T4.3 fixture objects (resolved via `fixture.py describe` for the run id); no pre-existing schema objects.
2. Every mutation case re-reads state with the harness's own connection; every refusal case asserts the audit and `V$SQL` marker per T4.2 conventions.
3. Level cases: run each tool at READ_ONLY and at every level where its behaviour changes (via `oracle_set_session_level` preview -> confirm on a writable lab profile; a `protected` lab profile proves the pinned ceiling).
4. W1 bypass-shape and W2 runtime cases that exercise these tools are authored by their owning beads (T1.x, T2.x) in this family's file when they land; this bead leaves a documented section for them and does not wait on them.
5. The generic W3 contract negatives (unknown argument, duplicate member, wrong enum, argument aliases) are generated by T4.2 and owned by T4.8; do not duplicate them here.
6. Unsupported combos on a lane (licence/privilege/version) assert the exact typed refusal, never skip.

## Test plan
Every case runs over stdio and Streamable HTTP through the T4.2 driver against the T4.3 fixture; tier A lane FREE 23ai; tier C XE 18/21, FREE 23ai (and ADB through T9.6a). Case ids follow `w4_<tool>_<case>`. Each case logs one JSONL line (`case_id`, tool, level, transport, input hash, expected, actual, verdict, timings). Mutating cases re-read DB state through an independent python-oracledb connection owned by the harness (never through the server) and verify the audit chain with `oraclemcp audit verify` after the run.
Negative cases that a naive implementation fails: `oracle_semantic_search` on XE 18/21 returns its typed refusal (not an empty success); `oracle_diff` without flashback capability returns `FLASHBACK_CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE` and never a current read; `oracle_list_profiles` output contains no credential or connect-string material (canary).

## Proof split
This bead proves the in-scope tools' live behaviour on XE 18/21 and FREE 23ai; ADB is proven by T9.6a running the same cases; the generic contract negatives by T4.8; completeness by T4.14.

## Non-goals
- Driver/harness changes (T4.2), fixture changes (T4.3) beyond requesting them, fixing product defects found (each becomes a bug bead `discovered-from:` this bead, blocking it).

## No-claim boundary
Green cases prove the listed behaviours on the lab lanes run; they do not prove ADB behaviour (T9.6a) or behaviours not listed.

## Considerations
- A failing case caused by a product defect is filed as a bug bead (`discovered-from:T4.7`) that blocks this bead; the case is never weakened to pass. Fail-closed invariant: nothing here may admit a statement the classifier cannot prove safe for the active level, let elevation exceed a profile's `max_level`, make a `protected` profile writable, or auto-commit DML.
- Confidentiality (constitution #9): fixtures, goldens, case inputs and logs use synthetic identifiers only; no field/customer/OCI identifier ever enters a committed artifact. Licence honesty: AWR-backed cases run only where the lane declares the Diagnostics Pack licence capability; the lab never enables a licensed feature by default.
- Consumers: T4.11, T4.14, T9.6a, T3.5 (#44 cases), T1.8 (explain cases).

## Absorbs
None.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: every tool in scope (`oracle_search_objects`, `oracle_search_source`, `oracle_semantic_search`, `oracle_diff`, `oracle_orient`, `oracle_top_queries`, `oracle_plan_timeline`, `oracle_db_health`, `oracle_explain_plan`, `oracle_connection_info`, `oracle_switch_profile`, `oracle_list_profiles`) has at least one positive case green over stdio and HTTP on FREE 23ai, with exact ordered values checked.
- [ ] Positive: the same cases are green on XE 18 and XE 21 in the tier-C run, or return the exact typed refusal recorded for that lane's capabilities.
- [ ] Negative: `oracle_semantic_search` on XE 18/21 returns its typed refusal (not an empty success); `oracle_diff` without flashback capability returns `FLASHBACK_CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE` and never a current read; `oracle_list_profiles` output contains no credential or connect-string material (canary).
- [ ] Tests: all `w4_*` case ids in `scripts/e2e/w4/cases/ops-tools.json`; results in `target/e2e/w4/<lane>/cases.jsonl`.
- [ ] Proof class: live external client (release binary, stdio + HTTP); forbidden substitutes: in-process dispatcher, mock DB, envelope-only assertions.
- [ ] Consumers: T4.11, T4.14, T9.6a, T3.5 (#44 cases), T1.8 (explain cases).
- [ ] No-claim: does not prove ADB behaviour or unlisted behaviours.

title: Prove alias equivalence, wrapper behaviour and W3 contract negatives over the wire
description:
## Context
R8 (every tool gets a deliberate in-house live test: create objects, run all statement kinds, verify deterministically), R25 (nothing deferred; all tools tested end to end). Plan §6 (binding): external client only - the real release-profile binary over MCP stdio **and** Streamable HTTP, no in-process dispatcher, no server helper crates in the client; deterministic verification (exact ordered rows, exact error class + ORA code, audit entries with a verified hash chain, an independent re-read of database state after every mutation, ordering by barriers never elapsed time, goldens with volatile fields scrubbed); one JSONL line per case (tool, level, input hash, expected, actual, verdict, timings) plus a summary table in the results JSON; counts come from the registry, never hard-coded.
The registry (`crates/oraclemcp/src/registry.rs`) serves 25 tool-name aliases routed by `alias_target` / `dispatch/tool_routing.rs::canonical_tool_name`: plain renames (`current_database`, `switch_database`, `enable_writes`, `disable_writes`, `query`, `preview_sql`, `compile_object`, `compile_with_warnings`, `create_or_replace`, `patch_package`, `patch_view`, `list_objects`, `list_schemas`, `get_schema`, `describe_table`, `describe_index`, `describe_trigger`, `describe_view`, `get_ddl`, `get_object_source`, `get_errors`, `get_clob`) and three compatibility wrappers that extend a guarded path (`execute_approved` -> `oracle_execute`, `deploy_ddl` -> `oracle_create_or_replace`, `read_patch_preview` -> `oracle_patch_source`). Today aliases are covered by an envelope sweep only; "alias = canonical" was never proven.
Plan §6 (binding): plain rename aliases must be semantically equivalent to their canonical tool after volatile-field normalisation; compatibility-wrapper aliases are tested against their documented guarded target plus their extra wrapper behaviour. The W4 statement matrix includes the W3 negatives (unknown argument, wrong enum, deprecated-alias equivalence) - W3 (T3.1-T3.3) delivers strict decoding, enums and the argument alias map with the conflict rule and 0.14.0 removal note.

## Outcome
For every tool-name alias read from `tools/list` (never a hard-coded list), a paired case calls the alias and its canonical target with identical arguments on the same fixture state and asserts equal results after scrubbing; the three wrappers are proven against their guarded target plus their extra behaviour. For every tool, the generic W3 contract family from T4.2 (unknown argument, duplicate member, wrong enum) and the argument-alias family (lone deprecated alias equivalent + one deprecation note; canonical+alias conflict refused) are green over stdio and HTTP.

## Deliverable
- `scripts/e2e/w4/cases/aliases.json`: generated pairing rules (alias -> canonical from `alias_target`'s documented table as exposed by `oraclemcp robot-docs tools` output, verified against `tools/list`), with per-wrapper explicit cases:
  - `w4_alias_execute_approved_requires_token_then_executes_like_execute`, `w4_alias_execute_approved_without_token_refused`;
  - `w4_alias_deploy_ddl_preview_token_apply_equivalent`, `w4_alias_deploy_ddl_wait_timeout_behaviour`;
  - `w4_alias_read_patch_preview_returns_preview_without_apply` (re-read source unchanged).
- `w4_alias_<alias>_equivalent` for every plain rename (both transports), and `w4_alias_enable_writes_disable_writes_level_transitions`.
- Argument-alias family (from T3.3's alias map, read from the generated docs table): `w4_alias_arg_<tool>_<alias>_equivalent`, `w4_alias_arg_<tool>_<alias>_conflict`.
- Assertion of the T4.2-generated `w4_contract_<tool>_unknown_argument`, `w4_contract_<tool>_duplicate_member`, `w4_contract_<tool>_wrong_enum` families, and `w4_contract_refusal_has_next_steps` (T3.6).

## Implementation notes
1. Equivalence: same fixture state (fresh checkpoint or re-seeded rows), same arguments, compare scrubbed result JSON; for mutating tools compare DB re-reads and audit records (the audit `tool` field differs by name - assert the canonical tool is recorded as the executed path and the alias as the invoked name, per current audit semantics).
2. Wrapper differences are asserted explicitly (e.g. `execute_approved` consumes an approval token); anything else must be equal.
3. The contract families are generated by T4.2; this bead owns their green verdict and any expectation data (e.g. which properties are enums).

## Test plan
Every case runs over stdio and Streamable HTTP through the T4.2 driver against the T4.3 fixture; tier A lane FREE 23ai; tier C XE 18/21, FREE 23ai (and ADB through T9.6a). Case ids follow `w4_<tool>_<case>`. Each case logs one JSONL line (`case_id`, tool, level, transport, input hash, expected, actual, verdict, timings). Mutating cases re-read DB state through an independent python-oracledb connection owned by the harness (never through the server) and verify the audit chain with `oraclemcp audit verify` after the run.
Manifest cases: #36, #37 (wire counterpart of the unit proof), #40 (`w4_alias_arg_sample_rows_table_equivalent`), #41 wrong-enum/array negatives.

## Proof split
This bead proves alias and contract behaviour through the release binary; the mechanisms are proven at unit level by T3.1-T3.3; completeness by T4.14.

## Non-goals
- Changing alias routing or adding/removing aliases.

## No-claim boundary
Equivalence holds for the fixture states tested; it does not prove equivalence for every possible input.

## Considerations
- Added dependencies T3.1, T3.2, T3.3 (beyond §23.2's T4.2): the argument-alias and contract-negative cases this bead owns cannot be green before strict decoding, enums and the alias map exist; the tool-name alias pairs can be written earlier. Structure-owner check: alternatively split the W3-negative verdict into a separate bead.
- Confidentiality (constitution #9): fixtures, goldens, case inputs and logs use synthetic identifiers only; no field/customer/OCI identifier ever enters a committed artifact.
- Consumers: T4.11, T4.14, T9.6a.

## Absorbs
None.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: every plain-rename alias listed by `tools/list` returns a scrubbed result equal to its canonical tool's, over stdio and HTTP.
- [ ] Positive: `execute_approved`, `deploy_ddl` and `read_patch_preview` pass their target-equivalence and wrapper-specific cases.
- [ ] Positive: a lone deprecated argument alias returns the canonical result plus exactly one deprecation note naming 0.14.0.
- [ ] Negative: canonical+alias in one call, an unknown argument, a duplicate member and a wrong enum value are each refused with the expected class for every tool, and `read_patch_preview` never changes the re-read source.
- [ ] Tests: all ids in `scripts/e2e/w4/cases/aliases.json` plus the `w4_contract_*` families; manifest cases #36, #37, #40, #41 green.
- [ ] Proof class: live external client; forbidden substitutes: envelope-only sweep, in-process dispatch.
- [ ] Consumers: T4.11, T4.14, T9.6a.
- [ ] No-claim: does not prove equivalence beyond the tested fixture states.

title: MCP protocol-revision hygiene: capability surface not degraded to negotiated revision; version not stored per-session (no security impact)
description:
MCP protocol-revision hygiene (spec-fidelity, NOT a security bypass). From the 2026-07 multipass bug hunt protocol-negotiation audit (self-verified + peer-audited).

SECURITY CONCLUSION (verified, no action needed): version negotiation is spec-compliant (crates/oraclemcp-core/src/server.rs:525-542 echoes a supported requested version, else the server's latest; tests initialize_echoes_a_supported_client_protocol_version + initialize_frame_negotiates_older_client_version). There is NO fail-closed bypass via downgrade: the negotiated version is read in exactly one place (the echoed field), refusals always ride content[0].text + isError:true which are valid in every revision including 2024-11-05, and NO guard/classifier/consent code branches on the protocol version (guard enforcement is entirely server-side and version-independent). Pinning an old version cannot bypass any check.

RESIDUAL SPEC-FIDELITY GAPS (all benign today, additive-only):
(i) The served capability surface does not degrade to the negotiated revision: served_capabilities_json (server.rs:533) ignores the negotiated version, so a 2024-11-05 client is advertised structuredContent / completions / title / newer fields that post-date its revision. Additive; old clients ignore unknown fields.
(ii) The negotiated version is not stored per session: a repeated initialize is accepted and notifications/initialized is a no-op; a client could re-initialize mid-session to a different version. Nothing enforces off the stored version, so benign but non-conformant to the strict lifecycle.
(iii) The HTTP MCP-Protocol-Version header is only enforced when present (http/mod.rs:2050-2067); 2025-06-18 requires it on all post-init requests.
(iv) Tests do not assert per-revision capability degradation.

Audit file refs: server.rs:525-542, 875-895, 1654-1682, 1924-1941; http/mod.rs:2050-2067; capabilities.rs:16-23.

SUGGESTED (if pursued, low priority): thread the negotiated version into served_capabilities_json and gate version-specific fields; store the negotiated version per session and reject/annotate a re-initialize; add per-revision capability tests. Do NOT change the refusal encoding (content[0].text + isError) - that cross-revision compatibility is exactly what keeps downgrade safe.
close_reason: MCP revision hygiene landed: negotiated protocolVersion stored per session; second initialize on an initialized session rejected with a structured error; versioned advertisements gated on the negotiated revision WHILE refusal-carrying fields (isError+text) stay always-present (audited no-downgrade-bypass property preserved); HTTP MCP-Protocol-Version header required when the session negotiated >= 2025-06-18, lenient for older. Per-revision conformance tests added; full workspace tests + all lints green.

title: connect UX: wrong password on 18c surfaces as misleading 'not an Oracle listener / unexpected TNS packet type 12 (MARKER)' CONNECTION_FAILED
description:
CONFIRMED live on lab lane xe18 (Oracle 18c XE, plain TCP throwaway container) during the 2026-07 multipass bug hunt. Leave-as-bead: the mapping improvement is real but the fix may be partly upstream (driver) and needs a design decision, so filing with evidence rather than a hasty guess.

REPRO (deterministic, 2/2 runs): same profile (connect_string localhost:1518/XEPDB1, user testuser), only the password varies.
- CORRECT password: doctor --online Connectivity = pass ("connected + authenticated").
- WRONG password: Connectivity = fail, failure_class = CONNECTION_FAILED, detail =
  "connect failed: connect handshake failed [unexpected-tns-packet]: the server replied with unexpected low-level TNS packet type 12 during the connect handshake (network layer, before authentication) - the endpoint is not an Oracle listener, or speaks a protocol generation this driver does not recognise: unexpected TNS packet type 12 (MARKER)"
  fix = "verify the host:port points at an Oracle listener (not another service)...".

WHY IT MATTERS: a wrong password is the single most common connect error. Here it is mislabeled as a network/listener/protocol problem, and the actionable `fix` text misdirects the operator to check host/port/listener rather than credentials. The endpoint IS a valid Oracle listener; only the password is wrong.

LIKELY ROOT CAUSE: with the oracledb 0.6.0 fast-auth connect flow, credentials are sent early in the combined handshake; an 18c server rejecting them replies with a MARKER (TNS packet type 12) that the driver surfaces as a low-level "unexpected TNS packet" rather than a clean ORA-01017. oraclemcp's ConnectFailureKind mapping (crates/oraclemcp-db/src/connection.rs) then classes it CONNECTION_FAILED [unexpected-tns-packet]. So the wrong-password signal is lost before oraclemcp sees it.

SUGGESTED DIRECTIONS (needs review; do not weaken anything):
1. Confirm with the oracledb maintainers whether an auth rejection can be distinguished from a genuine non-listener endpoint at the driver layer (ideally the driver maps the credential-reject MARKER to an auth error). If yes, adopt and map to an AUTH_FAILED class with a "check username/password/credential_ref" fix.
2. If the driver cannot distinguish, soften oraclemcp's `fix` text for the [unexpected-tns-packet] case to ALSO mention credentials ("...or the username/password is wrong") so the message is not actively misleading, and keep the ORACLEDB_TRACE_CONNECT hint.
3. Add a matrix/negative e2e case that asserts the wrong-password envelope is actionable once the mapping is chosen.

EVIDENCE: /tmp scratch only (env + throwaway profile), binary /tmp/cargo-target/debug/oraclemcp --json doctor --online. No customer identifiers. Related but distinct from bhw6.2 (which covered connect-error envelopes generally); this is the specific wrong-credential-on-pre-23ai mislabel.
close_reason: Fixed by adopting oracledb 0.7.1 (classic connect-phase reads run the marker/reset dance upstream). Live-verified on XE 18: doctor --online with a wrong password now surfaces ORA-01017 in the connectivity failure; the misleading 'unexpected TNS packet type 12 (MARKER)' label is gone.

title: [P0][review] CQN registration skips live relation-purity proof
description: Review finding from pane-5 CQN/SEC-1 audit. Trigger: profile permits CQN, caller has confirmed READ_WRITE elevation plus audit sink, and registers a classifier-safe query such as SELECT id FROM APP.UNPROVEN_VIEW (or a table with a SELECT VPD policy / virtual column). CqnRegistrationGate::register_query re-classifies and calls semantic_read_plan, but it never resolves relations against the live Oracle catalog or calls resolved_relations_read_purity. The normal oracle_query path requires that proof and refuses views, VPD policy functions, virtual columns, remote objects, and unknown dependencies before execution. CQN registration reaches connection.register_cqn_query, which asks Oracle to register/evaluate the query, without that same side-effect proof. This widens the privileged CQN API beyond the guarded read path. Fix must add a live catalog/purity proof immediately before driver registration (and fail closed on resolver/purity errors); a stored permit/verdict must remain non-authoritative. Add negative coverage proving view/VPD/virtual dependency rejection before register_cqn_query is invoked.
close_reason: CQN registration now requires a fresh live catalog relation-purity proof before audit or driver registration; views, SELECT VPD, virtual columns, and absent proof are refused with regression coverage.

title: Arc M: ensure non-licensed row-scoping via the server-seam predicate (M4 deferral must not make row-scoping licensed-only)
description: GAP found in the alien-plan completeness audit. PLAN_0_8_x_ALIEN.md:288-289 promises row scoping via EITHER Oracle-native VPD/RLS OR a seam-applied predicate on the proven read so a principal never receives rows outside its policy. The M arc beaded only M1 column masking (.4.2, closed) and M4 the LICENSED native VPD/RLS tier (.4.5, deferred). With M4 deferred there is no dedicated bead ensuring the NON-licensed seam-applied row predicate is wired end-to-end; today it exists only implicitly via Arc N RequirePredicate (.5.4, closed). WHY IT MATTERS: deferring the licensed tier must not silently make row-scoping licensed-only — the server seam must still enforce row policy on an unlicensed DB, exactly as the server egress masker substitutes for licensed DBMS_REDACT. CHANGE: verify RequirePredicate actually applies the policy predicate to the proven read on the egress path and is enforced fail-closed; if the wiring or a test is missing, add it. ACCEPTANCE: on an unlicensed gvenzl DB, a RequirePredicate policy causes a principal to never receive out-of-policy rows; unit + live proof; guard re-checks at apply (SEC-1); documented as the non-licensed row-scoping path. NON-GOAL: the licensed native VPD/RLS tier (stays deferred in .4.5).
close_reason: Verified + documented (commit 3da0da8). VERDICT: the non-licensed seam-applied row predicate IS already wired end-to-end and enforced fail-closed; no code change was needed, so this bead's suspicion of a wiring/test hole did NOT reproduce. EVIDENCE (all re-run, not read): (1) WIRING - oracle_query executes PolicyGateAdmission::effective_sql when a RequirePredicate rewrite produced a candidate (dispatch/mod.rs:13962) and re-classifies the rendered candidate via ensure_resolved_read_only before it runs (SEC-1 re-check at apply). The rewrite is AST-based (Parser::parse_sql + AST insert), never text splicing; every shape it cannot prove it can scope (alias/join/CTE/derived) denies as UnsupportedStatementShape rather than running unscoped. (2) UNIT PROOF - a_predicate_rule_rewrites_the_read_that_reaches_the_database (dispatch/tests.rs) + policy_predicate_rewrite_refuses_aliases_instead_of_guessing_target_placement (policy.rs); cargo test -p oraclemcp-guard green (306 passed + all suites). (3) LIVE PROOF on the UNLICENSED gvenzl 23ai lab (scripts/e2e/sql_policy.sh, lane free23) re-run green this session: step narrow_reclassifies_and_proves_on_wire => candidate_digest_differs=true, returned_tenant_count=1 (tenant-8 rows never reach the principal), matched_rule_count=2; step policy_evaluation_failure_refuses => POLICY_DENIED/unresolved_policy_target for the alias case, i.e. a typed refusal, never a fall-open read of both tenants; deny/base-refusal/invalid-policy-startup all pass. So row scoping demonstrably works with NO Oracle licence. THE REAL GAP WAS DOCUMENTARY: ADR-0008 already states the licensed DBMS_REDACT tier does not replace the masking seam, but ADR-0009 (which owns RequirePredicate) never said the same for row scoping and never mentioned licensing at all -- a reader could reasonably conclude deferring M4 left row-scoping licensed-only. ADR-0009 now records that RequirePredicate IS the row-scoping path, is licence-free, that native VPD/RLS is an optional accelerator that does not replace the server seam, and that an unprovable rewrite is a denial not a fall-open read. NON-GOAL respected: licensed native VPD/RLS tier stays deferred in .4.5. Gates: guard tests green, dispatch wiring test green, oraclemcp_honesty_grep.sh OK.

title: Flaky test: shutdown wait_does_not_lose_wakeup_under_signal_race times out under CI load
description: Observed once on CI (feature powerset job, dashboard-bundle+default combo on oraclemcp-core): the test panicked with 'asupersync test future did not complete within 5s' at crates/oraclemcp-core/src/shutdown.rs:135, then passed on rerun of the same commit (28691901965) - a load-induced flake, not a regression (the failing commit only bumped the oracledb driver pins; shutdown.rs untouched). Options: raise the 5s harness budget for this test, make the signal-race deterministic (injected waker instead of wall-clock), or mark it serial if it contends with parallel tests for signal delivery. Do NOT weaken the lost-wakeup assertion itself - it pins a real invariant.
close_reason: Fixed deterministically: root cause is that a genuine lost wakeup parks asupersync block_on forever (no runtime deadlock detection), so the 5s recv_timeout was the only detector and the 1000-iteration probabilistic loop raced that wall clock under CI load. Rewrote wait_does_not_lose_wakeup_under_signal_race to drive wait_for_shutdown() by hand with a controlled wake-counting Waker (no runtime, no spawn, no timeout): interleaving 1 parks the waiter then fires begin_shutdown and asserts the wake edge was delivered (count>=1) and the future completes; interleaving 2 signals before first poll and asserts immediate completion. Stronger than the old loop (observes the wake edge directly) and has no wall clock to lose. title: Fail closed on symlinked or hard-linked FileStore service locks
description: Fresh cross-review finding. crates/oraclemcp-core/src/file_store.rs: open_private_lock_file opens root/.service.lock with OpenOptions create(true) and follows existing links; acquire_service_owner then set_len(0) rewrites it after locking. FileStore::open validates the root directory but does not authenticate the lock sidecar itself. A same-UID actor that can alter the state directory can replace .service.lock with a symlink or hard link to another writable file, producing an arbitrary truncate/write instead of a safe Locked/UnsafePath refusal. Implement an atomic no-follow lock open (preserving #![forbid(unsafe_code)]), reject non-regular and Unix multi-link existing sidecars, avoid TOCTOU between inspection and open, and add adversarial symlink/hard-link plus race tests. Do not weaken crash-recovery or replacement-lock semantics.
close_reason:
FIXED in 8c26968. Confirmed the attack was REAL, then proved the fix load-bearing by mutation.

ATTACK: open_private_lock_file used create(true) and followed links; acquire_service_owner then set_len(0)s that descriptor. FileStore::open validates the root dir but never authenticated the sidecar. A same-UID actor able to write the state dir could plant .service.lock as a symlink or hard link and convert lock acquisition into an arbitrary truncate+write of any file this UID can write.

FIX — two defences, because they stop DIFFERENT attacks:
1. O_NOFOLLOW on the open refuses a symlinked sidecar IN THE OPEN ITSELF. Atomicity is the point: inspect-then-open leaves a swap window (the TOCTOU the bead called out).
2. authenticate_lock_file rejects a sidecar that is not a lone regular file, by fstat-ing THE DESCRIPTOR WE HOLD (file.metadata()), never the path — so there is no inspection/use window. Catches what O_NOFOLLOW cannot: a hard link (shares the victim inode, so truncating ours truncates theirs) and a FIFO/device (diverts the write). Post-open link races give the attacker nothing: the inode is then our own lock content.
Both run BEFORE try_lock and before set_len(0), i.e. while refusal is still harmless.

ERROR SURFACE: a refused open is UnsafePath, not Io. ELOOP here is an attack signal; burying it in transient-io noise would hide it. Reused the existing UnsafePath variant rather than widening the enum.

UNSAFE POSTURE: OpenOptionsExt::custom_flags is a SAFE API — #![forbid(unsafe_code)] holds, zero unsafe blocks added. libc is unix-gated ([target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies]) because O_NOFOLLOW/ELOOP values are platform-specific and hardcoding them is exactly the fragility to avoid; libc 0.2.186 was ALREADY in the graph transitively, so Cargo.lock grew by ONE line and no package was added. cargo deny: advisories/bans/licenses/sources ok.

TESTS (4 new, unix-gated): symlink, hard link, FIFO, and a concurrent symlink-swap race. Each asserts the VICTIM'S BYTES SURVIVE — not merely that an error was returned. Refusing with the right error while still truncating would otherwise be a passing test and a live bug. The race test tolerates either outcome (genuine lock or refusal) but never a victim write.

MUTATION-VERIFIED (tests are not vacuous): reverting either defence makes all 3 refusal tests FAIL, and they fail at the Ok(...) branch — i.e. the lock was acquired THROUGH the link and set_len(0) truncated the victim. That is the vulnerability reproduced on demand, and the tests catch it. Fix restored and re-verified afterwards.

NOT WEAKENED: crash-recovery, replacement-lock identity, and partial-init release semantics untouched — service_lock_recovers_after_holder_process_is_killed, old_lock_drop_does_not_unlink_replacement_lock, and service_lock_initialization_failure_releases_os_lock all still pass (15/15 file_store tests green).

WINDOWS: O_NOFOLLOW has no equivalent; the unix-gated flag is skipped there, but the not-a-regular-file check still applies and Windows symlink creation requires privilege by default.

GATE (scoped): cargo fmt -p oraclemcp-core clean; clippy -p oraclemcp-core --all-targets -D warnings = 0 warnings; cargo test -p oraclemcp-core --lib file_store = 15 passed; cargo deny check ok.

title: shipping_spool shutdown lost-wakeup: worker join hangs forever
description: Production bug found via a 75-minute Windows CI timeout (run 29713554457, commit 835080b, test a_spool_refuses_a_second_concurrent_worker). DurableShippingForwarder::shutdown() stored the stopping flag (atomic, outside the queue mutex) and called wake.notify_all() without acquiring the queue mutex, while run_worker evaluates the stopping flag under that mutex immediately before parking in wake.wait. Both the store and the notify could land inside the worker's check-to-park window: the notify finds no parked waiter, the worker parks with an empty queue and no future notifies, and worker.join() in shutdown blocks forever — hanging any real service shutdown, not just the test. Windows runners widen the window (slow thread scheduling) but the race is platform-independent. Fix: bridge the store and the notify with the queue mutex (drop(queue.lock()) between them) so the notify always lands after the worker has either parked or re-checked the flag. wait_retry has the same window but is bounded by wait_for's delay. Verified: 237 oraclemcp-audit tests green, 30x shipping_spool hammer green, clippy/fmt/concurrency-lint clean.
close_reason: Fixed in the same commit that files this bead: shutdown() now takes and releases the queue mutex between setting the stopping flag and notify_all, closing the lost-wakeup window. Evidence: 237 audit tests + 30x spool hammer green locally; Windows CI lane green on the fix commit.

title: Workbench Classifier-Verdict badge shows green PASS for a blocked or step-up preview (client-derived over-trust)
description:
HONESTY VIOLATION (over-trust), found in the dashboard security/honesty review pass.

WHERE
- web/src/app/App.tsx:8434-8439 workbenchVerdictFromResponse computes `refused` by a fuzzy string match over result[decision] and result[danger] ONLY: decisionText.includes(refus|block|deny) OR dangerText === refused|blocked. It never inspects gate_decision.
- web/src/app/App.tsx:8428 reads decision = result[decision] ?? result[outcome]. Preview and denied bodies carry NO top-level decision or outcome key.
- web/src/app/App.tsx:8472 and 8487 WorkbenchVerdictBlock renders Badge PASS with the green (ok) tone whenever refused is false, and never renders gate_decision.

BACKEND REALITY
- DangerLevel serializes SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/levels.rs:87): SAFE, GUARDED, DESTRUCTIVE, FORBIDDEN. None of these equal refused or blocked, and DESTRUCTIVE/FORBIDDEN do not contain the substrings refus, block, or deny.
- The real block signal rides on gate_decision with value blocked or require_step_up, alongside danger and blocked_reason (crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/mod.rs:10438, 10757-10763, 10434-10441). Preview bodies have no top-level decision/outcome.

TRIGGER
Open the Workbench, enter a DESTRUCTIVE or FORBIDDEN or policy-denied statement (for example a table-drop DDL against hr.employees, or a CREATE OR REPLACE on an existing object, or a statement a protected profile or policy floor blocks), and preview it. The operator action succeeds as a preview (state success); its body has danger DESTRUCTIVE or FORBIDDEN and gate_decision blocked (or require_step_up) but no top-level decision. So `refused` computes to false, and the Classifier Verdict badge renders a green PASS for a statement the backend actually blocked or has not admitted. The prominent GO/NO-GO-style trust signal is wrong; the true gate_decision is present on the wire but simply not rendered by this component.

SCOPE / SEVERITY
Display-honesty bug, not a privilege bypass: the backend still refuses execution (SEC-1 re-classify at apply is intact; the execute-time hard refusal returns an ErrorEnvelope and yields state refused, which does NOT render this block). Severity HIGH because it is a client-side-derived trust signal that renders more-trusted than the backend proved, on the primary action surface, directly against the Arc L console contract (privileged actions gated by the GO/NO-GO signal). Partially mitigated: the adjacent line shows danger DESTRUCTIVE and needs DDL plus the reason text.

FIX DIRECTION (do not fix in this pass)
Derive the verdict from the backend gate_decision (blocked and require_step_up are non-PASS) and/or an explicit backend-set refusal boolean, not a string heuristic over decision/danger; render gate_decision; treat an unknown or absent gate decision as unproven, never PASS.
close_reason: Fixed in 1429edd (web only, TDD). The Workbench Classifier-Verdict badge now reflects the guard's ACTUAL admission from the wire instead of a client-side string heuristic. workbenchVerdictFromAction (web/src/app/App.tsx) reads gate_decision as the admission authority and yields an explicit status: gate_decision blocked / danger FORBIDDEN / decision refus|block|deny -> refused; gate_decision require_step_up -> step_up; gate_decision allow|allow_lowering, a classifier-proven SAFE read, or observed execution (committed|rolled_back|rows_affected) -> pass; anything else (present-but-unproven verdict) -> unknown. WorkbenchVerdictBlock renders PASS(green/ok) ONLY for status pass; refused->warn, step_up->info, unknown->off, and only pass gets the green affirmed border. Absent verdict -> unknown, never a defaulted PASS, matching the 15.7 no-fake-proof bar. Regression test web/src/app/workbench-verdict.test.ts (8 cases, TDD red-then-green) pins: blocked->refused, FORBIDDEN->refused, require_step_up->never pass, allow->pass, SAFE->pass, executed-rolled-back->pass, DESTRUCTIVE-with-no-gate->unknown-never-pass, no-verdict->null. Gate: web vitest 144 passed / 7 skipped (operator-gated e2e), tsc --noEmit clean. Blast radius: App.tsx + new test only; no dist rebuild (CI regenerates it).

title: audit resume: head anchor MAC not verified -> forged-anchor tail-truncation bypass
description:
MULTI-PASS BUG HUNT 2026-07-04, Part A audit fresh-eyes (resume/anchor).

FINDING P1 (tamper-detection bypass): Auditor::resume_from (sink.rs) cross-checked a loaded head anchor by comparing ONLY its plaintext seq + entry_hash, never verifying its keyed MAC (anchor.mac_is_valid). The keyed MAC is the sole binding of the anchor plaintext to the real durable head. A tamperer with file-write access but NO signing key could: delete durable records, truncate the log, and rewrite the .anchor sidecar plaintext DOWN to the truncated tail (matching entry_hash) with a garbage MAC -> resume passed (no truncation trip since anchor.seq==tail.seq; plaintext hash matched). The first durable append after resume re-anchors under the live key, making the truncation PERMANENTLY undetectable locally. verify path (anchor::check_anchor) does verify the MAC (and UnknownKeyId), so a pre-append audit verify would catch it -> held at P1 (agent originally leaned P0).

FIX (sink.rs): new Auditor::verify_anchor_authenticity, called at the top of the anchor cross-check block in resume_from BEFORE trusting plaintext. title: Streaming operator status has no aria-live region; async lane/action/SSE updates unannounced to assistive tech
description:

The two that matter most (safety-critical status a screen-reader operator must not miss):
- skin.tsx:1502 GroundControl2DRenderer — the GO/NO-GO fail-closed verdict banner at the top of every page. When it flips GO to NO-GO it is silent.

title: Parity 2462/2578 is REAL but STALE: measured 2026-06-14 at driver version 0.0.0, asserted CONFIRMED for the 0.8.4 release
description:
[MEDIUM — claim vs reality] PHASE-4 reality check of the headline conformance claim.

VERDICT: the number is REAL, not fabricated — but it is STALE, and it is asserted as CONFIRMED for a release it was never measured against.

WHAT IS GENUINELY GOOD (checked, credit where due): docs/PARITY_SKIPS.md in rust-oracledb documents a sound methodology. The skip decisions are made by the reference suite's own conftest.py fixtures and in-test pytest.skip calls BEFORE any driver code runs, so the driver under test cannot influence which tests skip — that is a real argument that the 116 skips do not hide engine defects, not spin. It further records skip sets identical at exact node-ID level between the reference thin driver and the Rust engine (116 vs 116), 303/303 baseline-passing tests still passing in those modules, and 0 regressions. A reproducer exists (scripts/parity_rigor.sh, harness/run.sh). The repo even ships scripts/fake_parity_scan.py + docs/FAKE_PARITY_AUDIT.md — it self-audits for fake parity. So question 1's 'any proven-skip that is actually a hidden defect?' = NO EVIDENCE OF ONE, and the methodology is the right one.

THE GAP — CURRENCY, NOT HONESTY:
- The measurement commit is 62c0c58, dated 2026-06-14. At that commit the driver's Cargo.toml said version = "0.0.0".
- The driver is now 0.8.4. Between then and now the line took 0.8.0's BREAKING shape_cache/lob_stream consolidation (7627a1e), decode-mutation work, K10 OwnedRowStream, and the asupersync 0.3.5 migration.
- docs/PARITY_SKIPS.md has not been re-derived since: its only later commit (23aa1b4) is a de-slopify docs pass, not a re-run.
- No newer full-parity artifact exists. docs/PARITY_LEDGER.md is a DIFFERENT artifact (upstream-issue triage, last audit 2026-06-29), and today's docs/baseline touch (f52dfae) is a K10 API baseline, not the conformance suite.
- The full suite is NOT a CI gate. _quality.yml:213 'Reference version-gate parity coverage' runs extract_reference_gates.sh --check, which is a version-gate DRIFT check, not a re-derivation of 2462/2578. live.yml only comments that the full suite additionally needs a Python venv + a maturin build, which it does not stand up.
- Meanwhile oraclemcp/docs/plan/PLAN_0_8_x_ALIEN.md:790 lists 'driver 0.8.2 / asupersync 0.3.5 / 2462-of-2578 parity | CONFIRMED'. It even names 0.8.2 — not the 0.8.4 shipping — so the row is self-evidently about an older driver while reading as a release confirmation.

FIX: re-run scripts/parity_rigor.sh against driver 0.8.4 and either (a) confirm 2462/2578 still holds and stamp the artifact with the driver version + commit SHA + date, or (b) record the true new numbers. Then make the claim self-dating: every place that cites 2462/2578 (driver README.md:49, docs/PARITY_SKIPS.md:18, oraclemcp PLAN_0_7_3.md:100, PLAN_0_8_x_ALIEN.md:790) should carry the driver version and run date it was measured at, so a stale number cannot masquerade as a current one. Best: make it a release gate so the number cannot drift from the artifact again.

DO NOT: re-close on the existing document. The whole point is that reading PARITY_SKIPS.md proves 0.0.0-era behaviour, not 0.8.4 behaviour.
close_reason:
FIXED in 453d6b6 (claim now dated). The number is REAL; presenting it as CONFIRMED for the shipping driver was not.

AUTHORITATIVE CURRENT VALUE — pulled from the driver's qualification bundle, not restated from a plan doc: 2578 collected / 2462 passed / 116 skipped / 0 regressions / 0 missing, measured 2026-06-22T18:28:26Z at driver candidate SHA b4a0cd3e77e3d7ed9cd875ba8002968860c9954a (rust-oracledb/docs/qualification/1.0.0-rc.1/SUMMARY.md). It has NOT been re-derived since.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN BEAD: I originally wrote 'measured 2026-06-14 at driver version 0.0.0', inferred from the PARITY_SKIPS commit date. That was imprecise. The authoritative qualification is 2026-06-22 @ b4a0cd3e. (GROUND_TRUTH.md separately records the count first observed 2026-06-11 @ 978491a; PARITY_SKIPS.md's taxonomy commit is 2026-06-14.) The conclusion — real but stale, never re-derived for the shipping driver — is unchanged; the date/SHA are now exact.

description: SYMPTOM: the Arc N policy evaluator is fully built and completely unreachable. crates/oraclemcp-guard/src/policy.rs implements the monotone evaluator SqlPolicyConfig::evaluate(base, context) -> PolicyTightening::Deny{reason, matched_rule_ids} | Narrow{base_required_level, required_level, predicates, matched_rule_ids} (ADR 0009, no Allow outcome), and a profile can carry one (ConnectionProfile::sql_policy, crates/oraclemcp-config/src/profile.rs:805). But NOTHING calls evaluate() outside the guard's own tests: grep for PolicyTightening / PolicyNarrowing / sql_policy across crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/ and crates/oraclemcp-core/src/http/ returns no hits. So a configured policy is (a) not enforced on the dispatch path and (b) not reported to any client. THE DASHBOARD IS SHOWING LESS PROOF THAN THE BACKEND HAS — and here it is worse than cosmetic: an operator can write a deny/require_level/require_predicate rule, load it, and the server will neither apply it nor say that it did not. WHY IT MATTERS: this is a silent policy-not-enforced condition, i.e. a safety gap, not just a UI gap. The dashboard policy badge (bead …15.11, commit 17062a1) already parses the ADR-0009 shape from result.policy / structured_reason.policy_tightening and renders data-policy-effect + data-narrowed-from; it currently and truthfully reports 'not reported' on every response, which is explicitly NOT the claim that no policy applied. A FIX MUST PROVE: (1) the active profile's sql_policy is evaluated against the classifier decision on the guarded dispatch path, before execution; (2) the narrowing is ENFORCED — the level floor composed with max() (never a replacement, never a lowering) and predicates applied via the N3 rewrite with mandatory re-classification of the rewritten SQL; (3) a require_level match returns base_required_level, required_level and the matched rule ids on the tool response, and a deny match returns POLICY_DENIED carrying its reason and rule ids; (4) a test proves a policy can never turn a classifier-refused statement into a dispatchable one, and can never lower a required level; (5) the dashboard badge lights up with NO client change.
close_reason:
Arc N policy is now enforced. Guard seam aba296f (enforce_sql_policy + the ADR-0009 response proof), dispatch wiring 2903998.

ALL FIVE OF THE BEAD'S 'A FIX MUST PROVE' ITEMS:
(1) EVALUATED ON THE GUARDED PATH, BEFORE EXECUTION - three call sites, because a statement becomes authority in three places: oracle_execute (refuses before the level gate, before a grant is consumed, before the DB is touched); oracle_query on BOTH the buffered AND the streaming path (a read that escaped the policy just by asking for SSE delivery would be a hole the size of the whole feature); and oracle_preview_sql - REQUIRED and easy to miss, because preview mints the single-use grant AT the required level: if a policy floor raised that level and preview did not know, the grant would be minted below the bar and refused at execute, and the agent could never obtain a usable one. Preview now mints at the COMPOSED level; a denied statement mints nothing.
(2) NARROWING IS ENFORCED - the level floor composes with max() (never a replacement, never a lowering) and the gate enforces the composed level; predicates are applied via the existing N3 rewrite_predicates_and_reclassify (bead 5.4, not reimplemented), the rewritten candidate re-enters the classifier (SEC-1) and is then re-marked and put through the SAME semantic read gate, so a rewrite can never widen what the read path admits. The predicate reaches Oracle - a test asserts the WHERE clause is in the SQL the database sees, because reporting a row filter is not enforcing it.
(3) THE RESPONSE CARRIES THE PROOF - base_required_level, required_level, matched_rule_ids, and predicates on the tool result; a Deny returns POLICY_DENIED with reason + rule ids on the envelope's structured_reason.
(4) TESTS - a configured Deny refuses at dispatch and never reaches the DB; a Narrow raises the required level and the RAISED level is what is gated (a READ_WRITE session is refused by a DDL floor on an UPDATE); a predicate rewrite actually reaches Oracle; a policy can never admit what the classifier refuses; an unevaluatable policy REFUSES (never falls open); an unpoliced profile is byte-for-byte unchanged and makes no claim. Plus the 9 guard-side tests incl. an exhaustive monotonicity check over the level lattice. 326 lib tests green.
(5) THE DASHBOARD BADGE LIGHTS UP WITH NO CLIENT CHANGE - the guard's PolicyTightening serializes into exactly the shape parsePolicyTightening already reads; a guard test pins that JSON against the client's parser contract.

TWO BUGS THE TESTS CAUGHT, both of which would have shipped: (a) a classifier-FORBIDDEN statement was coming back POLICY_DENIED - the policy taking credit for the guard's refusal, and claiming a policy refused it even on a profile that has none; the classifier's refusal now stands unchanged. (b) The policy floor was leaking into ORACLE-SEMANTICS checks. They are two different levels: statement_level is what the statement IS (DDL commits implicitly and cannot be rollback-previewed); required_level is what the session must HAVE. A DDL floor on an UPDATE means 'only a DDL-cleared caller may run this UPDATE' - it does not make the UPDATE un-rollbackable.

BEYOND THE BEAD, fail-closed: if a rule selects a schema/object and the statement's target cannot be PROVEN (a join, an alias, a CTE), the statement is refused rather than evaluated against a guess - a deny rule that quietly fails to match is a policy that silently did not apply. The schema a rule matches on is resolved from the CONNECTION once per session, never from a tool argument (a caller that could assert its own schema could dodge the rule naming it). The policy installs inside the same generation-locked commit as the profile's level and masking, so a lane can never run one profile's statements under another profile's policy.

TIGHTEN-ONLY, and no Allow outcome is representable anywhere in the chain: the grammar cannot express one, the evaluator returns only Deny/Narrow, and the gate's Admitted is explicitly not an authorization (the base gate still runs). The composed level is a max() and the gate re-checks it against the base, so a future edit that broke monotonicity would fail closed rather than silently grant.

title: audit resume seeds from tail without structural chain verification (interior fork accepted)
description: Auditor::resume_from (crates/oraclemcp-audit/src/sink.rs) parsed the on-disk JSONL and seeded chain state directly from records.last() without walking the chain. parse_jsonl only proves each line is valid JSON. Consequence: a forked interior (deleted, reordered, inserted, or in-place-edited middle record) that leaves the last line parseable was accepted at startup and the new run chained onto the forked prefix. The head anchor does NOT cover this: it attests only the head seq/entry_hash, so an interior deletion whose surviving tail still matches the anchored head passes the anchor cross-check. Only later ad-hoc 'audit verify' would catch it. FIX (landed): added a keyless structural pre-check (hash-link continuity + monotonic seq + hash_is_valid; no MAC so rotated chains are not false-refused) that fails closed with ResumeRefused before seeding. Tests: resume_refuses_a_deleted_interior_even_with_a_matching_anchor, resume_refuses_a_reordered_interior_without_an_anchor, resume_accepts_a_structurally_intact_multi_record_log.

title: classifier: derived/JOIN/UNION/Expr-subquery-smuggled DML cleared to Safe (fail-closed-net hole)
description:
MULTI-PASS BUG HUNT 2026-07-04, Part A adversarial classifier probe.

FINDING (fail-closed-net hole, smuggled-DML class flagged to re-probe): a DML SetExpr (UPDATE/DELETE/INSERT/MERGE) wrapped in a FROM/JOIN derived subquery, a UNION-branch FROM(...), or a WHERE/scalar/EXISTS Expr subquery parsed by sqlparser 0.62 as Statement::Query and cleared to danger=Safe, required_level=READ_ONLY. set_expr_carries_dml inspected only the TOP-LEVEL query body (prior oracle-cte-dml-body fix), missing derived and Expr subqueries.

Reproducers cleared to Safe BEFORE fix: SELECT * FROM (UPDATE t SET x=1); (DELETE FROM t); (INSERT INTO t VALUES(1)); (MERGE...); nested SELECT * FROM (SELECT * FROM (UPDATE...)); UNION branch; JOIN (UPDATE...); WHERE id IN (UPDATE...); nested-CTE WITH a AS(...) SELECT * FROM (WITH b AS(...) UPDATE t SET v=1).

SEVERITY P0 per operator rubric (write classifying Safe). Honest executability caveat: standard Oracle rejects DML inside FROM/WHERE subqueries so these exact strings are non-executable today; blast radius nil. But the fail-closed contract is violated and relying on Oracle-rejects is the implicit trust fail-closed design forbids.

FIX classifier.rs: (1) set_expr_carries_dml descends into SetExpr::Select FROM/JOIN derived subqueries, nested joins, CTE bodies via new helpers query_carries_dml / table_with_joins_carries_dml / table_factor_carries_dml (all 4 verbs, structural). (2) query_embeds_reserved_dml_verb: canonical-scan net for reserved INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE tokens covering Expr-embedded subqueries; reserved words = zero false positives (FOR UPDATE already Guarded via query.locks). MERGE excluded from token scan (non-reserved) but caught structurally. Query Safe arm gated on both.

RESIDUAL documented: MERGE embedded ONLY in an Expr subquery is not token-scanned; Oracle-invalid + non-executable.

TESTS adversarial_corpus.rs: 10 new CORPUS entries (min Guarded) + derived_subquery_smuggled_dml_is_never_read_only asserting writes>=Guarded and legit nested reads / DML-substring columns / DML-word literals stay Safe. Guard suite green.
close_reason: FIXED + tested (adversarial_corpus.rs: 10 corpus entries + derived_subquery_smuggled_dml_is_never_read_only). set_expr_carries_dml now descends into derived/JOIN/nested/CTE subqueries + query_embeds_reserved_dml_verb net for Expr-embedded reserved DML. Guard suite + full workspace test + clippy + 6 lints + api-lock green. Live-server regression step added to ladder (read_only_smuggled_dml_not_served_as_read), PENDING-LIVE.

title: A1d follow-up: live e2e ladder asserted the removed empty-describe shape
description:
CI-RED on main (run 29831595915, 7dce026, job 'Oracle FREE 23ai matrix + VECTOR smoke'): LADDER FAIL (free23) -- 'assertion failed: table is absent through the bounded describe tool' with context error_class=OBJECT_NOT_FOUND isError=True.

CAUSE: A1d (oraclemcp-091-a1d-describe-notfound-q9e4v) correctly replaced oracle_describe's empty-success-on-missing-object with a structured ObjectNotFound ErrorEnvelope (dispatch/mod.rs, the columns.is_empty() branch). scripts/e2e/oracle_ladder_session.py ddl_drop_table() still asserted the OLD shape: description.get('columns') == []. git log a8f31b0..7dce026 -- scripts/e2e is empty, so the contract moved and the live lane was never updated with it. The unit tests A1d shipped are all offline, so nothing caught it until the live matrix ran.

RULING (deliberate, not test-greening): the E2E LADDER is the wrong side. A1d's own analysis is the argument -- describe is catalog-based, so an empty ALL_TAB_COLUMNS can never mean VPD filtering; it meant 'not visible for the computed (owner, table)'. Using columns == [] as the absence signal forced one value to carry two incompatible meanings, and the field read it as the wrong one. This is the same conflation C7/A1c remove on the query side: an empty collection must never be the signal for 'does not exist'.

FIX LANDED: ddl_drop_table() now asserts isError is True, error_class == OBJECT_NOT_FOUND, and non-empty next_steps. Strictly stronger than the old assertion -- it proves the object is absent AND that the refusal is actionable, which columns == [] could not distinguish from a mis-computed owner.

CLASS FINDING worth acting on separately: an offline-only acceptance set for a contract that a live lane asserts will keep producing this. A1d's acceptance was 'unit tests for not-found, unresolved synonym, quoted lower-case identifier' -- all offline. When a tool's response SHAPE changes, scripts/e2e must be grepped for assertions on the old shape in the same commit.

title: W10: enforce HTTP OAuth scopes at dispatch
description: Fix the current captured-only ScopeGrant limitation. The HTTP path currently validates OAuth scopes but dispatch does not read them, so narrow tokens may authenticate without lowering authority. Carry a typed ScopeGrant through the native HTTP request/session context and apply monotone-down scope logic before tool dispatch. The effective operating level is the minimum of OAuth scope ceiling, profile max_level, and current session/step-up window. Scopes must never raise profile/session authority; protected profiles remain READ_ONLY even with broader tokens.
design: Implementation shape: fix the known HTTP security bug where ScopeGrant is validated but not enforced by dispatch. Carry ScopeGrant or equivalent through native HTTP request/session context and apply monotone-down logic before tool dispatch. Effective operating level is min(OAuth scope ceiling, profile max_level, current session/step-up window). Scopes can only lower authority; they never raise profile/session authority.
acceptance_criteria: A narrow read token cannot call higher-level tools; a broad token cannot exceed profile max_level; broad token plus protected profile remains READ_ONLY; missing token fails when OAuth is enabled; metadata route remains discoverable; no bearer token content is logged; the old captured-only regression is replaced by enforced least privilege.
notes: Tests: narrow oracle:read token can call read tools but cannot reach write/DDL/admin/challenge-confirmed paths if exposed; broad token cannot exceed profile max_level; broad token plus protected profile remains READ_ONLY; missing token fails when OAuth is enabled; metadata route remains discoverable; diagnostics may show resolved effective level but never token content.
close_reason: Implemented HTTP ScopeGrant dispatch context and monotone-down session-level enforcement. Verified with focused OAuth scope tests, golden HTTP tests, fmt, clippy, workspace tests, cargo deny, sensitive-data lint, boundary lint, release preflight, and cargo package.

title: audit verify: tail-truncation of the JSONL chain is undetected (no head anchor / expected-length)
description:
OBSERVATION (leave-as-bead; documented residual, NOT a regression) from the 2026-07 multipass bug hunt audit-chain e2e on xe18.

WHAT WAS TESTED: ran the operating-level ladder against xe18 with ORACLEMCP_AUDIT_KEY set, produced a 15-record signed hash-chain, then ran oraclemcp audit verify against tampered copies:
- in-place edit of a record  -> DETECTED (exit 2, HashMismatch, broken_at_index correct)
- delete a middle record (splice/reorder) -> DETECTED (PrevHashMismatch)
- wrong signing key -> DETECTED (SignatureMismatch)
- DROP THE LAST RECORD (tail truncation) -> NOT DETECTED: verify reported ok:true, records:14.

ROOT CAUSE: verify_records (crates/oraclemcp-audit/src/verify.rs) re-walks from genesis checking hash-link + monotonic-seq + keyed-MAC. A prefix of a valid chain is itself a valid chain, so dropping trailing records yields a still-valid shorter chain. There is no persisted head anchor (last seq / last entry_hash) or expected-count for verify to compare against.

STATUS: this is a KNOWN, DOCUMENTED design boundary, not a new bug. docs/threat-model.md T5 honestly claims only the three checks verify actually performs (in-place edit, reorder, recompute-from-genesis) and points at optional WORM/SIEM shipping (crates/oraclemcp-audit/src/shipping.rs, ADR 0003) as the mitigation for an independent tamper-evident copy — which is exactly what catches tail-truncation. The oracle_version_matrix.sh harness also asserts .records >= 10 as a coarse floor. So the property is covered at the architecture level; verify simply cannot detect it locally by design.

SUGGESTED HARDENING (optional, non-blocking): let audit verify optionally take an expected head (--expect-seq N / --expect-head <entry_hash>) or persist a separate head-pointer file that verify cross-checks, so a local-only deployment (no shipping) can detect tail-truncation too. Alternatively, have verify emit an advisory note that trailing truncation is not locally detectable without an anchor. Do NOT change the default success semantics without an explicit anchor input (would break the honest 'a valid prefix is valid' contract).

EVIDENCE: /tmp scratch repro (env-only + file copies, no repo mutation); binary /tmp/cargo-target/debug/oraclemcp audit verify.
close_reason: Fixed: audit verify now detects tail-truncation via a signed sidecar head anchor (crates/oraclemcp-audit/src/anchor.rs, with_head_anchor on the sink). Crash-consistency: the record fsync ALWAYS precedes the anchor update, so a crash window can leave the anchor BEHIND the durable chain (explainable, self-heals on next append) but NEVER ahead; verify reports TRUNCATED when the chain ends before the anchored head. Anchor update failure fails the call closed. Record format unchanged (anchor is additive sidecar). 11 anchor unit tests (intact/truncated/anchor-behind crash-window) + ladder e2e audit step, all green; documented in docs/hardening.md.

title: Bound post-reply actor completion acknowledgement waits
description: Commit 562ac340 fixes the reply-to-next-admission race by making the actor await a caller completion acknowledgement after every reply. That acknowledgement is received with the actor Cx and no timeout, so a caller future that remains alive but is never polled after its reply can retain the session and actor thread forever. The original request absolute deadline is not applied to the acknowledgement wait. Bound this wait by the copied request deadline and a finite completion-ack grace when the request has no deadline; expiry must quarantine and retire the actor. Add deterministic coverage that deliberately holds a live acknowledgement sender, then proves bounded actor retirement and refusal of queued work. Preserve the cancellation no-reuse guarantee.

title: Restrict backend fallback to pre-session acquisition
description: Finding from read-only review of 8a70a338: connect_with_backend_registry in crates/oraclemcp-db/src/connection.rs falls back to the official adapter after every driver-cx connect error. But RustOracleConnection::connect delegates to driver::connect, which first establishes a live Cx session and then applies session identity, canonical NLS statements, and configured session_statements. A failure in any of those post-connect steps is therefore an opened-session/setup failure, not a raw acquisition failure; the router can then open a second session through the official adapter. This violates the documented connect-only/no-open-session-migration boundary and can duplicate session-side setup effects. Fix by reporting or preserving the precise phase so the alternate path is allowed only when raw socket/auth acquisition failed before a Cx connection exists; propagate all identity/NLS/session-setup failures without alternate or fresh retry. Add feature-on selector tests for each post-connect error class asserting only driver-cx is attempted, alongside retained raw-connect failure alternate coverage.

title: Official adapter fabricates UTC for DATE and plain TIMESTAMP

title: Stream and capability-bind legacy audit migration
description: Finding: doctor legacy-state migration handles permanent audit JSONL using whole-file allocations and an unsafe equality reopen. The audit_files_match helper in crates/oraclemcp-core/src/doctor.rs calls fs::read on both paths after regular_file_status has inspected them, so arbitrarily large audit logs can exhaust memory and a path can be replaced or followed during the gap. The read_regular_file_nofollow helper later uses capability-relative open but still read_to_end into Vec, and migration writes the same Vec twice for backup and target. Impact: ordinary long-lived audit history can make doctor and doctor --fix unavailable; a concurrent path swap defeats the read-side no-follow check before the protected destination install. Fix: compare and copy through held no-follow parent capabilities in fixed-size chunks; enforce opened regular-file identity, preserve byte-identical backup/current writes and current atomic-install/rollback semantics, bounded memory, fsync and error behavior. Tests: multi-megabyte migration demonstrates bounded chunk path and byte equality; post-inspection source symlink or path swap refuses before reads; equal large legacy/current stays no-op; partial I/O failure does not publish a current target.

title: Bind audit parent fsync to actual file creation
description: Finding from round-three audit review: FileAuditSink::open in crates/oraclemcp-audit/src/sink.rs determines whether parent-directory fsync is required using path.exists and lock_path.exists before AuditLogLock::acquire and open_private_append_file. An audit log or lock sidecar can be removed after those prechecks and securely recreated by the later opens, but the stale true verdict skips fsync_parent_dir. A crash immediately after an audited fsync can then lose the newly created directory entry and its tamper-evidence. Fix: return actual created/not-created outcomes from secure audit and lock opens and fsync the held parent whenever either open actually creates an entry. Test a controlled precheck-to-open removal of existing regular audit and lock files; assert the open succeeds, the exact current files are owner-private, and parent-fsync observability increments. Preserve symlink/FIFO refusal and concurrent-writer fail-closed behavior.

description: OperatorIdempotencyLedger::begin calls prune_expired_operator_idempotency_entries before lookup. A guarded action exceeding the cache TTL can receive the same idempotency key again, get a Fresh lease, and execute twice. Retain in-progress entries until their lease completes or drops; expire only completed replay entries. title: Nightly requirement is misattributed: it comes from oracledb pulling asupersync's DEFAULT nightly-outcome-try, not from asupersync 'requiring' nightly
description:
[HIGH — claim vs reality] PHASE-4 reality check. README.md, AGENTS.md, Cargo.toml:22 and rust-toolchain.toml all state the thin-native line 'has no stable MSRV because asupersync 0.3.5 requires nightly-only language features (try_trait_v2 + try_trait_v2_residual)'. That attribution is WRONG, and it is load-bearing: it is why we tell users to install a pinned nightly and why we advertise no stable MSRV.

TRACED ROOT CAUSE (each step verified, not inferred):
1. asupersync 0.3.5 does NOT require nightly. Its only nightly use is CONDITIONAL: src/lib.rs:52 = #![cfg_attr(feature = "nightly-outcome-try", feature(try_trait_v2))]. (A plain grep for '#![feature(' finds nothing — the cfg_attr is why this went unnoticed.)
2. asupersync's default feature set = ["proc-macros", "nightly-outcome-try"] — so the nightly feature is ON BY DEFAULT but OPT-OUTABLE.
3. oraclemcp does it RIGHT: Cargo.toml:35 = asupersync { default-features = false, features = ["metrics"] }. We never ask for nightly.
4. oracledb 0.8.3 does NOT: its [dependencies.asupersync] declares version = "=0.3.5", features = ["tls"] with NO default-features = false. It therefore pulls asupersync's defaults, and cargo feature unification turns nightly-outcome-try ON for the whole graph — overriding our opt-out.
5. NEITHER repo ever requests nightly-outcome-try (grep: only comments mention it). The nightly feature appears to be entirely accidental.
6. Driver 0.8.4's own Cargo.toml:13-14 already states this accurately ('asupersync's DEFAULT nightly-outcome-try feature enables #![feature(try_trait_v2)]') — but documents the consequence instead of turning it off. oraclemcp's docs are the ones that misattribute it to asupersync 'requiring' nightly.

EVIDENCE THAT STABLE IS OTHERWISE FINE: cargo +stable check -p oraclemcp-error -p oraclemcp-guard = EXIT 0 on stable rustc 1.96.0. cargo +stable check -p asupersync fails ONLY with E0554 pointing at that cfg_attr line.

HYPOTHESIS TO TEST (explicitly NOT yet proven — do not close on reading alone): setting default-features = false on oracledb's asupersync dep retires the nightly requirement for BOTH repos. It must keep proc-macros, which is asupersync's other default and is probably genuinely used: i.e. asupersync = { version = "=0.3.5", default-features = false, features = ["tls", "proc-macros"] }. Test by patching the driver locally and running cargo +stable check on the driver, then on the server. If something DOES need Outcome's  (try_trait_v2), the requirement is real — and then the docs should say 'we opt into asupersync's nightly-outcome-try because X', not 'asupersync requires nightly'.

WHY IT MATTERS: 'no stable MSRV' is a significant adoption barrier stated as an inherent property of a dependency. If it is really an unrequested default feature, we are imposing nightly on every downstream user for nothing. Note tzju ('0.3.9 may retire nightly requirement') assumes the fix rides on the 0.3.9 bump — this analysis suggests the fix may be independent of 0.3.9 and available today.

SCOPE: the one-line dep change lives in the DRIVER repo (rust-oracledb), so this is cross-repo and gates on driver publish. oraclemcp's own docs (README toolchain section, AGENTS.md 'Rust toolchain & gates', Cargo.toml:22, rust-toolchain.toml) must be corrected either way — even if nightly stays, the stated reason is wrong.

DO NOT: silently drop the nightly pin without proving stable builds AND the full gate passes on stable.
close_reason:
FIXED in df41540 (docs + the gate that pinned the wrong claim). Scope was attribution, not the pin: the nightly requirement is REAL and stays.

TRUE SOURCE — verified, two INDEPENDENT reasons, neither is 'asupersync requires nightly':
1. ALL PLATFORMS: asupersync 0.3.5 gates its nightly use behind a cargo feature — asupersync-0.3.5/src/lib.rs:52-53 = #![cfg_attr(feature = "nightly-outcome-try", feature(try_trait_v2))] + the same for try_trait_v2_residual. The feature is OPT-IN, merely present in asupersync's default set (default = [proc-macros, nightly-outcome-try]). We already opt out (default-features = false). It lands anyway because oracledb declares its asupersync dep WITHOUT default-features = false, so cargo unifies it back on. PROOF: cargo tree -i asupersync -e features shows 'asupersync feature "default" <- oracledb v0.8.3'.
2. WINDOWS ONLY: our OWN oraclemcp-core/src/lib.rs:9 = #![cfg_attr(windows, feature(windows_by_handle))], needed for MetadataExt::number_of_links — file_store's hard-linked-lock refusal (bead 7oaa, the Windows counterpart of the unix nlink check from siry/em39) and the audit sink's file identity. No stable std equivalent, so Windows needs nightly even if (1) is resolved.

ANSWER TO THE BEAD'S QUESTION ('is try_trait_v2 used by OUR code or only by asupersync?'): only by asupersync, and only when its nightly-outcome-try feature is on. Our code's ONLY nightly feature is the Windows windows_by_handle above. Neither the driver's nor the server's source uses the try_trait_v2 syntax — it arrives transitively and unrequested. NOTE the docs' FEATURE NAMES were right (try_trait_v2 + try_trait_v2_residual both exist, lines 52-53); only the WHY was wrong.

CORRECTED: AGENTS.md, README.md (x2), Cargo.toml, rust-toolchain.toml, docs/TOOLCHAIN.md §1 (rewritten with the exact mechanism + a cargo tree reproducer), docs/operations.md. ADR-0001 keeps its original decision text (an ADR records what was decided) and gains a dated Correction section + a status banner, because its review trigger was materially wrong: it says 'wait for asupersync to stop needing nightly', when oracledb setting default-features = false may drop the requirement TODAY with no upstream release. That is recorded as a HYPOTHESIS TO PROVE (must keep proc-macros; must build AND gate green on stable first), not a claim — I did not prove it, and the pin stays until someone does.

ROOT CAUSE OF THE PERSISTENCE (the real find): scripts/release_surface_sync_check.sh REQUIRED the docs to contain the literal string '<driver> driver is stable-clean' — the drift-guard was actively pinning the inaccurate sentence in place, which is why it survived multiple doc passes. Anchors now require the accurate 'driver's own source is stable-clean' wording. The provenance INTENT is preserved, not weakened: the anchors still interpolate the pinned versions, and I verified the gate is still load-bearing by simulating both bumps — oracledb 0.8.3->0.8.4 and asupersync 0.3.5->0.3.9 each make it fail.

NOT CHANGED: the nightly pin itself, rust-toolchain.toml's channel, or any code. Docs + one gate script only.

GATE: release_surface_sync_check EXIT 0 (version=0.9.0, surfaces=26); oraclemcp_honesty_grep EXIT 0; oraclemcp_api_lock EXIT 0; cargo metadata EXIT 0.

title: Make profiles.pool runtime behavior honest and session-safe
description:
## Current gap

`[profiles.pool]` is documented and parsed by `oraclemcp-config`, and `oraclemcp-db` contains `OraclePool` plus `PoolSettings`. The shipping binary still opens a single `RustOracleConnection` in `try_open_connection`, so profile pool settings are currently misleading: operators can configure them, `oracle_list_profiles` can report the timeout metadata, but the server does not use a profile-backed pool.

## Required change

Make `[profiles.pool]` honest and functional, or deliberately remove/hide it from the user-facing profile contract until it can be used safely.

The preferred implementation is to wire the existing pool into the server connection strategy without breaking session-affinity-sensitive workflows.

## Design constraints

- Do not break session features that require affinity: transactions, savepoints, temp tables, package globals, DBMS_OUTPUT, login setup, and profile session identity.
- If only read-only stateless tools can safely use the pool, make that split explicit in code and docs.
- If the current `OracleConnection` trait is the wrong abstraction for `OraclePool`, add a narrow adapter rather than pretending pooled and leased sessions have identical semantics.
- Admission control should align with pool `max_size` instead of allowing unbounded agent concurrency to starve the pool.

## Acceptance criteria

- Either `[profiles.pool]` is wired into runtime behavior and verified, or profile docs/metadata stop claiming it is usable.
- Tests prove configured pool settings are converted to `PoolSettings` and used by the connection factory.
- Tests cover max/min/acquire-timeout validation and the default values.

title: SEC-6 regression: OAuth WWW-Authenticate leaks why a token was rejected (auth oracle)
description:
381c4703 'fix(auth): make OAuth token failures actionable' added token_error_description() at crates/oraclemcp-core/src/http/mod.rs:529, rendered into the WWW-Authenticate header at oauth_rs.rs:238-239. An UNAUTHENTICATED caller now receives a distinct reason per failure mode:

  Missing              -> 'Bearer access token is required'
  Malformed            -> 'Token is malformed'
  BadSignature         -> 'Token signature did not verify'
  Expired              -> 'Token has expired'
  MissingRequiredClaim -> names the exact claim ('Required RFC 9068 claim iss is missing', and per-claim variants for sub/client_id/jti/iat/exp)
  UnsupportedAlg       -> 'JWT alg is not supported by this resource server'

That is an authentication oracle. Probing with crafted tokens now reveals: whether the token parsed at all; whether the SIGNATURE verified as distinct from whether it EXPIRED (which tells an attacker a captured token is genuine but stale, or that a forgery is structurally correct and only the signature is wrong); the exact set of required claims, by enumeration; and which algorithms the resource server accepts. The signature-vs-expiry distinction is the most valuable of these to an attacker and the least necessary to a legitimate client.

This conflicts with SEC-6 (uniform auth errors) from PLAN §4-RS, which exists precisely to stop an unauthenticated party learning why their credential was refused.

HOW IT SURFACED: it is failing CI, not passing silently. crates/oraclemcp/tests/e2e_http_oauth.rs::binary_http_oauth_rejects_missing_invalid_and_insufficient_tokens asserts the header is exactly error="invalid_token" with NO error_description, and it fails on both Linux (cargo test job) and the Windows lane. THE TEST IS RIGHT AND THE CODE IS WRONG. Do not 'fix' this by updating the test to accept the description — that would bless the leak and is the single wrong outcome available here.

THE TENSION IS REAL, so resolve it rather than picking a side: B2a+B2b legitimately asks to make token errors diagnosable. Diagnosability belongs to the OPERATOR, not to the anonymous caller. The correct shape is a uniform client-facing response (error="invalid_token", no discriminating description) with the specific TokenError reason recorded in the audit/security trail where an operator can read it. That satisfies both requirements instead of trading one for the other.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Anonymous callers receive an identical WWW-Authenticate challenge regardless of WHY the token failed. A test must assert that two different failure modes (e.g. BadSignature vs Expired) produce byte-identical headers.
2. The specific reason is still recoverable by an operator from the audit/security trail, with a test proving it is recorded.
3. The existing e2e assertion stays as written; it is the contract.
4. If a description is kept for the Missing case only (no token presented leaks nothing, since the caller already knows), state that reasoning explicitly rather than leaving it implicit.

Found by the orchestrator on 2026-07-21 while triaging why oraclemcp CI stayed red after the clippy P0 cleared.

title: fuzz-build CI job is continue-on-error, so an uncompilable fuzz target stays hidden
description:
Observed 2026-09-24: crates/oraclemcp-guard/fuzz/fuzz_targets/grant_scope_match.rs (.15.5, landed 53c54411) fails to compile (E0618, a local binding shadows fn resolved()). ci.yml job 'fuzz targets compile (nightly)' reported it on 473aeb5b and 6ab809ad, but the job has continue-on-error: true, so main stayed green. The orchestrator workspace gate never builds fuzz crates, which sit outside the workspace, and the scheduled Fuzz Campaign only runs nightly. As a result a bead's 'fuzz target runs 60 s clean' acceptance criterion was claimed while the target could not compile.

Fix: make a fuzz-target compile error fail CI. Keep toolchain or installer churn from reddening CI by separating the steps: installing cargo-fuzz may stay tolerant (with bounded retry), but 'cargo fuzz build' of each crate must be a blocking step. Add a check that a planted compile error in a fuzz target fails the job.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: fuzz-build is blocking for compile errors; main CI shows red when any fuzz target fails to compile.
- [ ] Negative: a planted broken fuzz target (selftest or PR proof) makes the job fail.
- [ ] Toolchain or install failures are handled explicitly (bounded retry or a separate tolerant step), not by continue-on-error on the build step.
- [ ] No-claim: does not run fuzz campaigns in PR CI.
